meta.selection_policy: Significance 5; novelty, depth and exposition each ≥4; at least one of those three =5. Proof status is informational. Retain every paper above the target-size weighted-score cutoff. Allocate the remaining positions among equal-score papers to minimize Σ (selected_topic − N × reference_share)² / (N × reference_share), subject to eligibility and available papers. Within each topic, resolve equal-score ties by submission number.
meta.review_method: AI-assisted manuscript screening and scoped proof review; not official STOC decisions or formal correctness certificates.

topic_taxonomy.data_sublinear: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms

meta.topic_balance: Equal weight to the STOC 2026 initial accepted-paper topic proportions (212 papers) and the FOCS 2026 accepted-paper topic proportions (174 papers). No SODA data. The target proportion is a soft comparison, not an enforceable cap.
meta.acceptance_rate_note: 28% is the user-suggested working rate, not an officially verified STOC 2026 or FOCS 2026 rate. FOCS 2025 officially reports 137/546 = 25.09%; the comparison includes that lower-rate sensitivity. A secondary STOC 2026 report of 211/752 = 28.06% remains unverified and is not used as primary evidence.

review.title: Metric Self-Dual Completion and Optimal Additive Hardness for Quantum and Graph-State Distance
review.authors: Rafail Ostrovsky
review.summary: Deterministically embeds every binary code C of length m into a self-dual binary code of length Θ(H), H≥2m, preserving all embedded coset distances exactly by a factor 2 and making all other codewords heavier than H. review.prior_frontier: Claims prior additive hardness Θ(√N) for quantum distance and Θ(N^(1/3)) for graph-state distance; source good-code hardness and explicit dual-good construction still require independent source verification.

score_reasons.significance: Linear ambient size removes the polynomial loss in additive distance-hardness reductions and preserves every coset metric.
score_reasons.novelty: The K=M∩τ(C)⊥ surgery isolates short codewords while a prefix-sum conversion makes the host self-dual.
score_reasons.depth: The argument combines exact orthogonal-complement identities, a dual-good to self-dual transformation, and CSS/graph-state reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: Theorem 1 states four separate guarantees and Sections 3 and 5 give short algebraic constructions with recoverable inverses.

checked: Traced K⊥=M⊕τ(C), A=K⊕τ(C), half-dimension/self-orthogonality and exact coset-distance argument.
Checked the all-ones normalization inverse and prefix-sum self-duality and distance inequalities, including C=0 and w=0 cases.
Checked linear-length arithmetic from constant-ratio dual-good family and CSS rate/distance conversion.
remaining: Independently verify the precise explicit dual-good family in Shpilka/Guruswami and Austrin–Khot source hardness assumptions.
Read the full preliminary CSS and graph-state distance identities and source-hardness section.

review.summary: For unique-fixed-point Tarski families with antichain solutions and nonnegative adversary bounds, dimension multiplication by t amplifies hardness by Omega(t); width multiplication by m with dimension doubling gives Omega(log m). Consequences include Omega(k log^2 n), tight log^3 n at dimensions 8–10, polynomial-in-width bounds in high dimension and a superpolynomial exponential-width bound.

score_reasons.depth: Chain monotonicity and tensor adversary denominator control are substantive; the Perron-vector numerator gives t times the base norm.
score_reasons.exposition: Theorems state antichain and nonnegative-adversary hypotheses explicitly, and distinguish dimensional versus width costs.

checked: Screened chain constructor using downward closure; checked tensor-adversary numerator calculation against unit Perron vector.
remaining: Trace Lemma3.3 monotonicity cases, query-filter norm denominator and the staircase embedding.
Verify repeated-bootstrapping parameter arithmetic and applicability of ordered-search composition.

papers.authors: Vladimir Vovk

review.title: The universal measure of nonstochastic objects
review.authors: Vladimir Vovk
review.summary: In the structure-free setting, the universal measure of (α,β)-nonstochastic objects is Θ(τ(α)) when β is bounded by any fixed computable function of α; τ is the tail of the universal distribution and decreases slower than every computable decreasing rate. Probability-measure models exhibit a contrasting behavior.
review.prior_frontier: Prior standard abundance statements typically depend on a prescribed string-length or nested structure and feature exponential decay in α. The new scope is structure-free; the distinction must be retained. Historical priority claims were not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: A sharp qualitative reversal of how abundant nonstochastic objects are, with a matching two-sided characterization in the specified model.
score_reasons.novelty: The universal-tail characterization and divergent Kraft-mass deficiency principle go beyond a change in numerical constants.
score_reasons.depth: The proof links computable Markov kernels, complexity deficiencies, and universality through a succinct general lemma.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions and quantifiers are explicit, and Appendix A identifies dependency order; the proliferation of stochasticity variants makes the later omnibus results demanding.

checked: Traced Lemma 17: pushing the universal semimeasure through a computable kernel preserves domination up to a constant.
Traced Lemma 18: finite normalized approximants with Kraft mass ≥2^k give ≤2^(t−k) mass to K−F≤t; summing the universal mixture yields the τ(t) lower bound.
Checked Theorem 10: a witness Q with K(Q)≤α and deficiency≤β forces K(ω)−F(ω)≤α+cβ+O(1), then Lemma 18 and computable tail stability apply.

Traced both bounds of central Theorem 1: singleton witnesses give the upper bound; the plain/prefix deficiency comparison gives the lower bound via Theorem 10. The comparison can be recovered by encoding the plain-description deficit self-delimitingly, yielding d_plain≤2 d_prefix+O(1).
Checked the computable-g(α) and additive-constant handling using Lemma 3; this is not a uniform claim over arbitrary noncomputable growth of β.
remaining: The later omnibus results and the full collection of quasi-stochastic variants have not all been checked. No formal proof artifact was executed.

score_reasons.significance: Provides exact parallel and second-cut algorithms in a setting lacking submodularity.
score_reasons.novelty: MST/proxy-edge merge framework works on arbitrary vertex partitions and extends with ordered merging to second cuts.
score_reasons.depth: Triangle elimination and amortized merge analysis are substantial but comparatively elementary.

review.prior_frontier: New online-ordering model; leverages recent online vector balancing rather than improving the offline Steinitz constant. Prior signers and matching lower-bound regimes not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Gives tight deterministic behavior and a general reduction for a natural new online discrepancy problem, rather than settling the older offline Steinitz question.
score_reasons.novelty: Independent signer copies on a capacity tree convert sign discrepancy to irrevocable permutations.
score_reasons.depth: The technical point is conditioning on ancestor tapes while retaining a valid fixed-stream signer law and accounting for quota overrides.
score_reasons.exposition: The algorithm distinguishes proposed and actual routing signs and illustrates both quota correction and conditional composition.

checked: Read the capacity-routing algorithm and terminal-bound proof; checked that ancestors alone fix the stream at a node and the private tape remains independent.
Checked the override correction is bounded by signed-count imbalance and odd-capacity correction.
remaining: Finish subgaussian composition proof and check matching lower-bound regimes and invoked signers before selecting.

remaining: Audit all success-probability and multi-instance hybrid quantifiers in the conditional hardness reduction.
Verify concentration/anticoncentration, exact exponential constants, and cryptanalytic evidence for planted conjecture.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a well-defined open adaptivity problem while attaining minimax parameter dependence.
score_reasons.novelty: Dyadic challengers with randomized learning rates accumulate credit that controls the main learner’s rate changes.
score_reasons.depth: Requires stopped-epoch accounting, variance-sensitive importance estimates and a nonuniform prior over subroutines.
score_reasons.exposition: The comparator/adversary quantifiers and two within-round filtrations are explicit and useful.

checked: Verified E[Zt|Gt]=⟨qt−pt,ℓt⟩ under the stated sampling law and why pt≥qt/2 bounds credit overshoot.
Checked that fixing an oblivious comparator is used before conditioning on random epochs.
remaining: Audit stopped-epoch challenger guarantees, credit amortization and rate-doubling summation.

review.summary: A single adversarial-bandit algorithm adapts to unknown comparator switches S with expected Õ(√((S+1)KT)) regret against every oblivious loss table. It does not provide the impossible corresponding adaptive-adversary guarantee.
review.prior_frontier: Known-S switching bounds were optimal; unknown-S adaptation was open in the oblivious case and impossible in the cited adaptive model. Prior-source comparison remains to be checked.

checked: Traced conditional forward representation OPT(p)=minπ〈απ,p〉 and concavity-to-PF factor2 integration.

papers.authors: Marc Dufay, Roger Wattenhofer

review.title: Optimal Subcubic Byzantine Agreement with Plain PKI
review.authors: Marc Dufay, Roger Wattenhofer
review.summary: Deterministic synchronous Byzantine agreement with plain PKI tolerating t<n/2, O(n) rounds and total bit complexity O(κ^((√13−1)/2)n^((√13+1)/2)). Removes the need for threshold signatures for a subcubic protocol; the runtime proof assumes κ=polylog n.
review.prior_frontier: Previously optimal-resilience plain-signature deterministic protocols had cubic communication, while quadratic protocols used threshold signatures. Optimality in the title concerns resilience/rounds, not a matching lower bound for the 2.303 exponent.

score_reasons.significance: Breaks the cubic communication barrier while retaining full t<n/2 resilience under a weaker setup.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines proof gathering, validated dispersion, recursive group merging and fault-tolerant expanders.
score_reasons.depth: Recurrence balances proof-size costs and recursive calls; signatures remain long and cannot be treated as threshold aggregates.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear model motivation, but several terminology/exponent typos and a lengthy protocol dependency chain require careful verification.

checked: Read proof-gathering and validated-dispersion structure and the per-party recurrence and polylog-κ qualification.
remaining: Audit agreement/validity for all protocol compositions, fault-tolerant expander construction, recursion base regimes and total-bit accounting.
Overview line 119 says threshold signatures despite the plain-signature construction; appears a wording error, not yet a demonstrated model violation.

review.title: Exponential Quantum Advantage in Testing Fourier Dimensionality
review.authors: Kenny Chen
review.summary: Fourier-dimension testing for Boolean functions has O(k/sqrt(epsilon)) quantum queries and Omega(k) lower bound, versus softO(2^(k/2)/epsilon) classical upper bound matching prior exponential-k lower bound. Tolerant alpha*epsilon versus epsilon versions have softO(k/epsilon) quantum and softO(2^(k/2)/epsilon) classical queries; tolerant runtime may enumerate all k-subspaces.
review.prior_frontier: Improves prior classical roughly 2^k tester to 2^(k/2) and establishes natural exponential quantum query gap. Tolerant equality is in k dependence, not identical epsilon/log factors or runtime.

score_reasons.significance: Nearly settles classical query dependence and gives exponential quantum advantage for a previously studied property.
score_reasons.novelty: Fourier subspace growth plus amplification yields standard tester; tolerant extensions require stronger sketch/recovery arguments.
score_reasons.depth: Core quantum tester is concise; classical/tolerant matching bounds carry most technical novelty.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes query complexity from brute-force tolerant computation and states remaining epsilon gap.

checked: Read Fourier projection as conditional expectation on U-perp cosets; majority rounding connects distance with missing spectral mass.
Traced one-sided span-growth tester: every far instance has at least 2epsilon mass outside any k-subspace; capped amplification and O(k) trials suffice.
remaining: Quantum lower bound and full classical collision-based tester.
Tolerant tester conditions, tolerable alpha and uniform subspace sketch guarantees.

review.title: Online Random Sampling with Real Probabilities
review.authors: Thomas L. Draper, David G. Harris, Feras A. Saad

score_reasons.significance: Near-entropy random-bit use with logarithmic persistent space is a strong general-purpose sampling result.
score_reasons.novelty: The local uniform-state invariant permits both space savings and irrational/countable distribution support.
score_reasons.depth: Must preserve exact output laws while recycling randomness conditional on both output and state size.
score_reasons.exposition: The computational model and exclusions for oracle-internal space are stated clearly, with explicit sampling pseudocode.

checked: Checked that (Z+the binary expansion of fresh fair bits)/M is uniform on [0,1] when Z is uniform on {0,…,M−1}.
Confirmed that the space accounting excludes implementation-internal CDF-oracle space and retains accuracy/index efficiency assumptions.
remaining: Trace conditional uniformity after Recycle, entropy telescoping, finite expected termination and the matching space lower bound.

review.summary: Exact online sampling of discrete distributions with real-valued probabilities uses cumulative entropy plus O(log n) expected random bits and O(log n) persistent state, via a local uniform randomness reservoir. Handles irrational probabilities and countable support under specified CDF-oracle access.
review.prior_frontier: Replaces global arithmetic decoding with compact local recycling and extends rational bounded-denominator recycling. Runtime and temporary-space claims depend on stated oracle efficiency conventions.

score_reasons.depth: Interlocking envy, bundle-preservation and domination-count invariants are nontrivial but elementary.

checked: Traced domination-count progress under bundle permutation and bounded n² iterations.
Checked residual shrinkage geometric rate yields O(n²logn) Core calls per progress iteration.
remaining: Permute existence compactness argument, Repair preserving every old bundle, all query recurrence and degeneracies with zero-valued residue remain.

review.title: Deterministic Root-Finding over Finite Fields with Elliptic Curves
review.authors: Pierre-Jean Spaenlehauer
review.summary: Given certified elliptic-curve/twist preprocessing with largest group-order prime factor Ξ, deterministically finds roots of split separable degree-n polynomials over Fq in soft-O(Ξ²n log²q+n^ωlogq+n log³q) field operations. Efficient construction of sufficiently smooth preprocessing remains open.
review.prior_frontier: Replaces multiplicative-group smoothness with simultaneous smoothness of a curve and twist, avoiding GRH in the online phase; prior elliptic number-field approach used GRH. Does not prove unconditional deterministic polynomial-time finite-field factoring.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a new conditional route and certifiable field-specific preprocessing for a central problem, while the decisive preprocessing obstruction remains.
score_reasons.novelty: Lifts roots to curve/twist points and uses an elliptic Mignotte–Schnorr torsion-class recursion.
score_reasons.depth: Must represent split divisors, handle x-coordinate collisions after translation and certify group bases and smooth orders.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly separates online theorem, number-theoretic existence conjecture, and constructive open problem.

checked: Read the formal datum and complexity theorem; checked the Hasse-interval existence argument and twist-order relation.
Inspected translation formulas and the need to split colliding opposite points before interpolation.
remaining: Audit divisor translation, torsion recursion, Ξ² complexity and deterministic preprocessing verification.

review.title: An Algebraic Semantic Framework for Nondeterministic Computation
review.authors: Bojin Zheng, Jingwen Zheng, Weiwu Wang, Zhiying Huang
review.summary: Defines marked-input binary-branch machines with algebraic labels and claims polynomial equivalence to parameterized nondeterministic machines. Proves relabeling/interpretation invariance observations and restates separation as noneliminability/path sensitivity under additional uniform-depth condition. Explicitly does not prove P!=NP in this manuscript.
review.prior_frontier: No new complexity-class separation established here; stated separation belongs to companion work. Generator-independence is automaton isomorphism, not an arithmetic field isomorphism.

score_reasons.significance: The actual contribution is a model reformulation; the advertised relation to P versus NP supplies no proved separation or new quantitative bound.
score_reasons.novelty: Marked control semantics and reinterpretation of branch labels largely restate nondeterministic choice.
score_reasons.depth: Core inspected arguments are symbol simulation, normal forms and definition-level equivalences.
score_reasons.exposition: Frequent claims that standard witness encoding is impossible are unsupported by the finite-symbol simulation given in the same paper.

checked: Read branch-trigger/projection axioms and full parameterized equivalence proof.
Inspected separation-equivalence proof, which follows directly from definitions and leaves noneliminability conjectural.
remaining: Input-length and witness-parameter semantics need clarification: Lemma 5.11 passes to encoded <x,c>, while simulation marks input positions.
Projection axiom prohibits 0-to-1 creation but alone does not force 1-to-0 consumption, so one-use marker discussion requires an additional condition.
Lean artifact and companion separation claims not verified; no correctness certification is made.

papers.title: Separating $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{NP}$ under the Algebraic Semantic Framework
papers.authors: Bojin Zheng, Jingwen Zheng, Weiwu Wang

review.title: Separating $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{NP}$ under the Algebraic Semantic Framework
review.authors: Bojin Zheng, Jingwen Zheng, Weiwu Wang

score_reasons.significance: The claimed conclusion is confined to a custom model and its essential uniform-verifier argument has a substantive gap.
score_reasons.novelty: The generator count is imposed by the encoding/unfolding rules, so a new invariant alone does not establish computational hardness.
score_reasons.depth: Prime-root independence is standard; the missing step is justifying an infimum over all verifiers from a restricted encoding lemma.
score_reasons.exposition: The manuscript explicitly disclaims ordinary P≠NP, but its universal claims obscure the input-map restriction and parameter-count versus bit-length distinction.

checked: Read Definition 4.2: reading a marked cell creates a generator by definition, independently of transition choices.
Compared Theorem 4.17 on p.16, which uses marker-free input map ι0, with Lemma 6.3 on p.21, which explicitly requires marked map ιF.
Traced Theorem 6.5 on p.22: it applies that restricted lemma to any verifier before taking an infimum, without establishing that every verifier in the infimum uses ιF.
Verified the two-instance read-all-elements argument itself; it forces input reading, not nondeterministic choice under an unmarked map.
remaining: A valid central separation needs a single aligned verifier/input-map class, or a proof of the missing uniformity across the allowed encodings.
Lean sources and axioms were not audited; a checked restricted statement would not by itself repair the prose model mismatch.
issues: Essential quantifier/model gap: ιF-specific forced generator consumption is used as a lower bound over a verifier class whose zero-dimensional construction uses ι0.

review.desk_reject_reason: The central separation is not established by the supplied argument: Lemma 6.3 requires input map ιF (PDF p.21), while Theorem 6.5 drops that requirement when quantifying over all verifiers (p.22); the P-side zero-dimensional construction uses the different map ι0 (p.16). Reading every element does not force generator activation under ι0. This is an essential missing justification, not a claim that ordinary P equals NP.
review.summary: Claims Pcb≠NPcb in a custom algebraic-semantic machine model and explicitly disclaims a standard Boolean P≠NP theorem. The central dimension argument changes the permitted input-map condition between the zero-dimensional upper bound and universal lower bound.
review.prior_frontier: The paper introduces its own semantic dimension invariant and cites its earlier machine equivalences. It supplies no established separation for ordinary Turing-machine P and NP; the claimed Lean verification was not executed or independently inspected.

score_reasons.novelty: Anchor clique reduces arbitrary sketches to incidence sketches; distance-decaying ring weights support sharper leverage estimates.
score_reasons.depth: Routing decompositions, leverage score comparison and hard-distribution total variation are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Distinguishes sketch dimension from bit-space streaming and does not overclaim the latter.

checked: Checked parameter relation ℓ=Θ(b^4),n=2ℓb=Θ(t^5),nt=Θ(n^{6/5}).
Inspected conditioning on anchor set before applying incidence result to fixed reduced sketch.
remaining: Anchor-dimension reduction, routing norm bound, distribution positivity/weight ratio and TV-to-spectral separation need audit.

papers.authors: Ping Li, Vincent Y. F. Tan

review.title: Last-Iterate Stationarity of Muon with Finitely Many Newton-Schulz Iterations
review.authors: Ping Li, Vincent Y. F. Tan
review.summary: For Muon using a fixed finite number of Newton–Schulz steps, positive input stabilization and a sufficiently small constant step guarantee full-sequence deterministic stationarity. Under persistent unbiased bounded-variance noise, schedules η_t∼t^−p and 1−β_t∼t^−q with p>3/4 and 2(1−p)<q<2p−1 yield almost-sure and mean-square gradient convergence.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier analyses mainly controlled average/best iterates or idealized polar transforms; SoftMuon last-iterate results used additional assumptions. This is an optimizer-specific asymptotic result, not a competitive finite-time last-iterate rate.

score_reasons.significance: Addresses a practically used finite-iteration optimizer and explains failures of fixed hyperparameters, but its strongest guarantee is asymptotic stationarity.
score_reasons.novelty: Sector bounds for the finite quintic transform support a coupled descent/tracking potential and momentum filtering.
score_reasons.depth: Combines nonlinear spectral transform bounds with stochastic approximation and no-polynomial-rate examples.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states stabilization, momentum schedules and conservative versus local step thresholds.

checked: Checked Lyapunov coefficient arithmetic with λ=2η/[κ(1−β)] and η≤κ(1−β)/(4L).
Checked stochastic summability conditions p+q/2>1 and 2p−q>1 and the balanced q=2p/3 choice.
remaining: Audit finite-Newton–Schulz sector inequalities, stochastic uniform integrability and last-iterate upgrade, and counterexample constructions.

review.title: Paths and Intersections: Repelling Pairs
review.authors: Yu Chen, Pavlo Pylyavskyy, Zihan Tan
review.summary: For prescribed cyclic-order Kalmanson metrics and consistent terminal path structures in an OS graph, realizing nonnegative lengths exist iff metric-repelling terminal pairs have disjoint paths. Gives O(k^5) outerplanar metric recognition/construction, unbounded-size minimal nonouterplanar submetrics, and polynomial compact medial template for all edge-minimum OS realizations.
review.prior_frontier: Extends tree/cactus recognition and fixed-order OS four-point realizability; minimum edge count differs from NP-hard total-length optimal realization. All minimum graphs are represented compactly, not explicitly output in polynomial total time.

score_reasons.significance: New tractable inverse metric problems with structural characterization and minimum-realization template.
score_reasons.novelty: Repelling pairs separate combinatorial path compatibility from numerical length feasibility.
score_reasons.depth: Farkas dual flows, maximal path switching, cut dominance and medial arrangements support algorithms.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise nonnegative-length, cyclic-order and compact-output conditions prevent broad overinterpretation.

checked: Verified elementary repelling-pair necessity by switching shortest paths.
Read LP/Farkas proof roadmap and maximal-switching potential: crossing changes preserve metric sum under nonrepelling Kalmanson equalities.
remaining: Flow balance/integrality conversion and cut-dominance-to-uncrossing completion.
Outerplanar dynamic program, minimal forbidden submetrics and minimum-medial-template characterization.

review.title: Concentration Inequalities for Branching Random Walks with Applications to Phase Transitions in CSPs
review.authors: Changqing Liu, Bo Zhang
review.summary: Claims smooth conditional drift plus exponential increment moments yield dependent-process/branching concentration, then random3-SAT satisfiability lower4.0029 and mixed2+p threshold transitionp=1/2.
review.prior_frontier: Prior3-SAT lower3.51 and4-SAT7.91 cited; new probability foundation and applications not independently validated.

score_reasons.significance: Claimed random-CSP threshold improvements would be major, conditional on resolving foundational concentration proof.
score_reasons.novelty: Proposes smooth-drift extension and descendant-population reweighting rather than standard independence assumptions.
score_reasons.depth: Concentration-to-PDE closure involves difficult uniform conditioning and remainder estimates.
score_reasons.exposition: Theorem5.4 uses imprecise “domain where smooth”; proof interchanges conditional process laws without clearly stated sufficient-state assumptions.

checked: Inspected Theorem5.4 and induction/Taylor expansion pp14–16, rather than accepting broad abstract formulation.
remaining: Resolve whether conditional drift functions remain the same after conditioning on an earlier uj; establish uniform Lipschitz constants and remainders before using concentration; verify BRW negative association and CSP application.
issues: PDFpp15–16 condition the evolution on an earlier uj and then apply E[X_{n+1}|u_n]=µ_n(u_n) within that conditional law. For general dependent processes this requires a sufficient-state/Markov or appropriate conditional-drift hypothesis, not supplied by Doob–Dynkin alone. A precise justification is needed for the central theorem.

review.title: Arbitrarily Slow Polynomial Convergence of Fictitious Play
review.authors: Jacob Abernethy, John Lazarsfeld, Andre Wibisono
review.summary: For every k≥2 constructs a rational skew-symmetric zero-sum game on (k+1)²−5 actions per player whose simultaneous fictitious-play gap is Θ(t^−1/k). Both players take a prescribed common first action; every later best response is unique.
review.prior_frontier: Extends Wang’s fixed-game t^−1/3 obstruction to arbitrarily small polynomial exponents without adaptive tie-breaking. Daskalakis–Pan’s t^−1/n constructions allowed adversarial ties. Prior papers not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Eliminates every game-independent positive polynomial convergence exponent even with unique responses, materially clarifying a classical dynamic.
score_reasons.novelty: A recursive clock preserves the old payoff matrix and adds endpoint/reset actions to lower the exponent one step.
score_reasons.depth: Algebraic compatibility, positive representations and score restoration must be maintained across an unbounded hierarchy of fixed games.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit initialization and tie-breaking qualifications avoid claiming robustness to arbitrary starts; the long induction is carefully staged.

checked: Checked action recurrence m_(k+1)=m_k+2k+3 from m_2=4 gives (k+1)²−5.
Checked binomial-basis summation transfer Fτ, its triangular positive block, and the displayed k=2 examples.
remaining: Trace the full Definition 6.2 invariant, endpoint/reset feasibility, unique-response perturbation and all-time rather than phase-boundary gap bound. The 76-page construction has not been fully audited.

score_reasons.novelty: Reprogramming preserves broad query-norm support and connects low-entropy outputs to heavily queried correct answers.
score_reasons.depth: Requires a robust oracle-reprogramming/counting argument beyond the basic hybrid inequality.
score_reasons.exposition: The random-oracle qualification and conditioning on noticeable acceptance are clearly stated.

checked: Verified the inspected swapping/hybrid recurrence using unchanged initial state, unitary norm preservation and the total query norm on changed coordinates.
Checked that the min-entropy guarantee is conditioned on acceptance and holds with high probability over the random oracle.

papers.title: On the Hardness of 4-to-1 Games with Perfect Completeness
papers.authors: Yumou Fei, Dor Minzer, Shuo Wang

review.title: On the Hardness of 4-to-1 Games with Perfect Completeness
review.authors: Yumou Fei, Dor Minzer, Shuo Wang
review.summary: For every constant ε>0 there is a finite alphabet size r for which distinguishing value 1 from at most ε in 4-to-1 Label Cover is NP-hard. Through stated reductions this yields hardness of coloring 3-colorable graphs with any fixed number of colors, and of finding constant-density independent sets in 2-colorable 3-uniform hypergraphs.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript contrasts its perfect completeness with the established almost-perfect-completeness 2-to-1 theorem, and prior 3-colorable-versus-5-colorable hardness. Essential prior reduction hypotheses have not yet been independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Perfect completeness closes a major d-to-1 frontier and would settle constant-color hardness for 3-colorable graphs.
score_reasons.novelty: The quadratic outer PCP, local low-rank middle test, lazy repetition, and mixed Grassmann inner code overcome the completeness obstruction.
score_reasons.depth: The 116-page construction combines nonstandard agreement soundness with covering and zoom-in coordination.
score_reasons.exposition: The main quantifiers and distinction between perfect and almost-perfect completeness are explicit; the full composition is demanding.

checked: Checked Claim 2.5: the planted-coordinate distribution has density #{i:x_i∈Γ}/(tp), so Cauchy–Schwarz bounds its total variation by (1/2)√((1−p)/(tp)). This supports the stated O_p(t^−1/2) covering heuristic.
Separated the proved fixed-k coloring corollary from Remark 1.8’s tentative slowly growing-k formulation.
remaining: The 115-page reduction has a checked planted-coordinate density calculation and a careful separation of proved versus tentative coloring claims. The quadratic-PCP, local-rank and Grassmann-agreement composition remains unchecked; this large-proof exception does not certify the headline hardness theorem.
Audit the outer quadratic PCP, middle local-rank soundness, lazy-repetition covering parameters and inner Grassmann agreement/composition; verify all alphabet and reduction-size dependencies.
Trace the exact hypotheses of the cited reductions giving Corollaries 1.7–1.12.

More generally derives O(sqrt(log k/k)) TV distance from additive d^−k designs plus the circuit structure.
review.prior_frontier: Design moment convergence alone does not imply TV convergence; earlier evidence and low-moment bounds did not establish this density-level guarantee. Haar’s exact Beta(1,d−1) probability law differs from exponential Porter–Thomas by O(1/d).

score_reasons.significance: Supplies a rigorous distributional justification for a widely used random-circuit heuristic at polynomial depth.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines moment Fourier control, analytic continuation and smoothing with a local-gate inverse-moment bound.
score_reasons.depth: The low-frequency moment estimates must be bridged to all frequencies without treating finite moments as a TV guarantee.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes fixed-bitstring randomness over circuits, Haar Beta versus exponential law, and the open sublinear-depth/noise regimes.

checked: Checked Markov tail bound at 2k/d using additive d^−k design error and k!+1≤k^k for k≥2.
Checked the truncated-support Cauchy–Schwarz/Plancherel TV inequality and the conditional Beta(1,3) last-gate reduction to 3 E[R^−1].
remaining: Audit inverse-moment Theorem 6.1, the Hadamard three-circle step and smoothing support errors; verify the BH26 O(nk+log 1/ε) design dependency.

review.title: The Spectral Cost of Sharpness: Fourier Truncation, the Gibbs Bend, and the Computability of Classification
review.authors: Wenwei Li
review.summary: Claims a basis-independent ℓ1 threshold for uniform reconstruction of discontinuous classifiers, together with Fourier sharpness, computability and learning-cost consequences. Theorem 3.2(b), a central advertised generalization, is false under its stated uniformly bounded orthonormal-basis hypothesis.
review.prior_frontier: Fourier continuity and Bernstein/Gibbs phenomena are classical. The proposed generalization omits continuity of basis functions and also asserts an unsupported iff from a sufficiency statement.

score_reasons.significance: The central general theorem admits an elementary counterexample; surviving Fourier-specialized observations do not support its advertised general conclusion.
score_reasons.novelty: The purported basis-independent obstruction is invalid.
score_reasons.depth: Classical Fourier computations and continuity arguments are used, with a missing hypothesis in a central proof.
score_reasons.exposition: The theorem explicitly assumes only boundedness but its proof silently calls partial sums continuous.

checked: Read and checked Theorem 3.2 against its exact hypotheses.

Counterexample: take the Walsh orthonormal basis on [0,1] with Lebesgue measure, uniformly bounded by 1; let g be the first Rademacher function, equal to +1 on [0,1/2) and −1 on [1/2,1]. It has essential jump 2 but exactly one nonzero coefficient. Its weighted ℓ1 sum is 1, contradicting Theorem 3.2(b), and its finite partial sum reconstructs it exactly.
remaining: Other Fourier-specialized, computability, NTK and learning-complexity claims were not fully audited because this central general theorem is already false.
issues: Theorem 3.2(b) is contradicted by a single Rademacher function in the uniformly bounded Walsh basis: a jump-2 target has one nonzero coefficient and finite exact reconstruction. The proof assumes continuity absent from the hypotheses.

review.desk_reject_reason: Theorem 3.2(b) is contradicted by a single Rademacher function in the uniformly bounded Walsh basis: a jump-2 target has one nonzero coefficient and finite exact reconstruction. The proof assumes continuity absent from the hypotheses.

score_reasons.exposition: The short manuscript explains precisely why read-once structure avoids the usual algebra-to-Boolean obstacle.

checked: Verified the vertex-by-vertex ABP-to-multilinear-circuit simulation and its linear edge-size overhead.
Inspected why read-once structure preserves syntactic multilinearity on each source-to-sink path.
remaining: Trace the explicit evaluation dynamic program and check applicability of the imported lower bound over F₂.

review.summary: An explicit Boolean function requires Õ(n²) size in read-once parity branching programs, improving Õ(n^(3/2)), by transferring a syntactically multilinear algebraic lower bound and giving polynomial-time evaluation of the resulting Boolean function.
review.prior_frontier: Uses the Raz–Shpilka–Yehudayoff/Alon–Kumar–Volk multilinear lower bound; the new contribution is the Boolean transfer plus explicit evaluation, not a new unrestricted algebraic-circuit lower bound.

papers.title: Asymptotic Rank of Weighted Graph Tensors via Completely Positive Covers
papers.authors: Huanyi Zhou

review.title: Asymptotic Rank of Weighted Graph Tensors via Completely Positive Covers
review.authors: Huanyi Zhou
review.summary: Over every field, proves floor(n²/4)≤log₂ asymptotic-rank(GT₂(K_n))≤n²/4, with equality for even n; extends to weighted graph tensors via a copositive dual constrained by path triangle inequalities. Gives odd-cycle upper bound m−1+1/(m+1).
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript reports earlier uniform complete-graph edge exponents about .7723, versus n/[2(n−1)] here, tending to the optimal .5. It builds on recent polynomial-multiplication matrix-multiplication methods, whose dependencies still require external verification.

score_reasons.significance: Determines exact asymptotic ranks for every even complete graph and resolves a stated graph-tensor exponent question.
score_reasons.novelty: Extends shared-leg separation and spectral growth to arbitrary tensor order, then introduces a completely-positive-cover formulation for weighted graphs.
score_reasons.depth: The 80-page proof combines arbitrary-field asymptotic spectral duality, entropy inequalities, polynomial degenerations and conic duality.
score_reasons.exposition: The main inequalities and the passage from complete to weighted graphs are laid out clearly; essential recent dependencies are substantial.

checked: Verified the grouping step conditional on the complete-graph theorem: integer group sizes give ∑a_i a_j P_ij≤(∑a_i)²/4, extending to nonnegative reals by scaling/continuity.
Checked the even-n equality, n=2 edge case and edge-exponent limit from the two main inequalities.
remaining: Audit shared-leg separation, diagonal-growth bounds and field-independent spectral-duality hypotheses; these carry the main new upper bound.
Verify conic Slater conditions and path restrictions, and independently inspect the recent polynomial-multiplication dependencies.

papers.title: Almost-MMS allocations with small agent redundancy
papers.authors: Vadim Grinberg, Uriel Feige

review.title: Almost-MMS allocations with small agent redundancy
review.authors: Uriel Feige, Vadim Grinberg
review.summary: For any fixed ε>0 and ρ<1, sufficiently large additive instances with (1+ε)n agents contain n agents receiving at least ρ times their n-MMS. Also obtains exact 1-out-of-[n+O(log²n)] MMS for all n agents and almost-MMS with m≤(2−ε)n goods without redundant agents.
review.prior_frontier: Improves ordinal MMS surplus from O(sqrt(n)log n) to O(log²n); the unrestricted conjecture that n-agent approximate MMS tends to 1 remains open. Selection guarantee uses n-MMS, not the weaker original-population MMS.

score_reasons.significance: Makes almost-exact fairness possible with arbitrarily small fixed agent redundancy and sharply lowers the exact ordinal slack.
score_reasons.novelty: Ordered breakpoint profiles reduce feasibility to prefix loads; rounding and saved-item reserve intervals permit augmenting the selected population.
score_reasons.depth: Combines polylog-loss iterative rounding, valuation-type clustering, head/tail separation and a careful exchange construction.
score_reasons.exposition: Provides unusually explicit quantifiers and contrasts selectable-agent MMS with all-agent ordinal MMS; thresholds can be enormous.

checked: Checked breakpoint-prefix Hall feasibility and head-item value-rounding loss at most q/q².
Checked the basic-solution variable reduction (f+d)/2≤3f/4 and its O(q²log n) accumulated load error.
remaining: Audit reserved intervals, augmenting replacement steps, tail integration and the O(log²n) exact ordinal claim. The 63-page proof is not fully checked.

papers.title: 0.4633-Approximation for Online and Offline Non-Monotone DR-Submodular Maximization
papers.authors: Vaneet Aggarwal, Donglei Du

review.title: 0.4633-Approximation for Online and Offline Non-Monotone DR-Submodular Maximization
review.authors: Vaneet Aggarwal, Donglei Du
review.summary: Obtains coefficient 54440750000/117486474169>0.463378 for nonnegative C1 non-monotone DR-submodular functions on compact convex down-closed subsets of the unit cube; queries may lie anywhere in the cube. An objective-independent downward recovery map admits an upper-linearizing field estimated by one noisy gradient. Offline exact-oracle contraction removes gradient/smoothness parameters; matroid/fixed-knapsack set-function consequences use standard rounding.
review.prior_frontier: Improves manuscript-cited4/9 coefficient, compared with .401 uniform smooth offline guarantee and .47043868 oracle upper bound. Regularity/access conditions differ; historical bounds not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A material constant improvement for a broad continuous and discrete submodular class.
score_reasons.novelty: Piecewise exponential/linear-fractional recovery and cancellation of small/large coordinate comparisons produce the improved factor.
score_reasons.depth: Long analytical scalar inequalities, signed secants, one-query field sampling and scale-free contraction require substantial work.
score_reasons.exposition: Assumptions and tightness of this fixed map are clear, but the long field construction and cancellation tables are demanding.

checked: Checked downward feasibility of both recovery branches and explicit discontinuity at1-b.
Traced greedy affine lower normalizer via vertex submodularity and coordinatewise concavity, large-before-small order and telescoping restoration inequality.
Checked two-coordinate cut forces alpha=4b/(2b+1)^2 for the fixed map.
Read anchor/contraction argument removing scale dependence, including zero-width coordinate case.
remaining: Core scalar averaging inequality AppendixA and full signed-slack cancellation have not been audited; pp24-25 were partly viewed but not counted as fully inspected.
One-query estimator, regret proofs and discrete rounding/restrictions need verification.

review.title: Strongly explicit Ramanujan 2-lift towers via Hilbert modular forms
review.authors: Olga Kharlampovich, Igor Pak, Alina Vdovina

score_reasons.significance: Exact binary towers with sharp spectral bounds and local computation would be a strong explicit-expander advance.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses 2-adic arithmetic transformations and Hilbert modular forms to bridge two classical construction approaches.
score_reasons.depth: Depends on local-to-global quaternion arithmetic, Hecke identification and the correct automorphic Ramanujan theorem.
score_reasons.exposition: The main statement is precise, but the multigraph convention is essential and much of the proof demands specialist number theory.

checked: Confirmed that loops/multiple edges are explicitly allowed, necessary already at the smallest binary levels.
Inspected the order trace-pairing matrix and the claimed unit-discriminant argument; arithmetic identities have not yet all been recomputed.
remaining: Recompute the quaternion base data, verify compatible coordinate bijections at every level, trace the exact Hecke/Jacquet–Langlands/Blasius hypotheses, and check neighbor bit complexity.

review.summary: Claims strongly explicit connected nonbipartite Ramanujan 2-lift towers with exactly 2^n vertices and degree p+1 for primes p≡1 mod17; neighbors/lift bits cost O_p(n³) after fixed-p preprocessing. Graphs are labeled multigraphs permitting loops and half-loops.
review.prior_frontier: Combines arithmetic Ramanujan constructions and binary lift towers; the exact-order strong explicitness is the claimed advance. It is not an all-degree simple-graph construction.

papers.title: Exponential Sampling Lower Bounds for Polynomial Sources
papers.authors: Yan Zhong

review.title: Exponential Sampling Lower Bounds for Polynomial Sources
review.authors: Yan Zhong
review.summary: For each fixed degree d, every F₂ polynomial source of degree d and arbitrary seed length has overlap at most exp(−Ω_d(N)) with Ber(1/3)^N. Gives degree-independent flat targets at prescribed entropy, adjacent-degree hierarchies, and limited nonlinear-gate extensions; unrestricted AC⁰[⊕] remains open.
review.prior_frontier: Strengthens reported 1−o(1) statistical-distance results to exponentially small overlap and resolves the two stated 2026 questions. Those prior statements are quoted from the manuscript, not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Exponential separation against arbitrary-seed polynomial samplers answers explicit sampling-hardness questions with sharp exponential order.
score_reasons.novelty: Weighted affine cubes turn coordinate acceptance gaps into a product-distribution overlap bound without conditioning outside the source class.
score_reasons.depth: The framework combines Gowers-type cube averages, KL tensorization and algebraic collision constructions; stronger target results require additional machinery.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes fixed from growing degree, arbitrary seed length and restricted parity circuits from unrestricted AC⁰[⊕].

checked: Traced Lemma 2’s induction/Jensen cube bound.

Traced Theorem 3: reweight cubes by the common mass, bound pair-output KL by K log(1/overlap), tensorize coordinate tests and compare the squared empirical mean to the uniform acceptance gap. The final inequality has the stated 2/(m²K) coefficient.
remaining: Check the precise Khodabandeh–Shinkar acceptance-gap theorem and selection of K yielding c_d=δ_d^6.
Audit explicit entropy targets, adjacent-degree hierarchy, growing-degree sampler and nonlinear-gate extensions separately.

papers.title: Non-Malleable Affine Extractors with Small Error and Complexity Lower Bounds
papers.authors: Yan Zhong, Xin Li

review.title: Non-Malleable Affine Extractors with Small Error and Complexity Lower Bounds
review.authors: Xin Li, Yan Zhong
review.summary: Constructs non-malleable affine extractors with linear output and exponentially small error at every fixed positive entropy rate, including a fixed number of affine tamperings. At entropy C n/log n obtains n^(1−η) output and error 2^−n^(1−η). Applications include exponential correlation bounds for weakly read-once linear branching programs and explicit near-maximal bounded-depth Res(⊕) lower bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Previously negligible-error non-malleable affine extraction required entropy rate near 1. Also removes a log²N loss in a separate Res(⊕) size-depth tradeoff via parity condensation; the general unrestricted Res(⊕) lower-bound problem is not claimed solved.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial advance in explicit extraction across entropy rates, with consequences for several concrete lower-bound models.
score_reasons.novelty: Refines affine correlation breaking and majority amplification; affine sections convert non-malleability into weakly-read-once branching-program hardness.
score_reasons.depth: Requires quantitative entropy/error accounting under several correlated noninvertible tamperings and simultaneous gadget surjectivity for lifting.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates extractor-based applications from independent condensation and distinguishes bounded-depth proof lower bounds.

checked: Read formal extractor quantifiers, including fixed-point-free only on source support and noninvertible affine maps.
Checked that a nonuniform affine distribution is at least 1/2 from uniform and inspected the Fourier seed-guess correction and affine-section second-moment route.

Traced the good-block rank-budget lemma for jointly affine pairs: the first block with joint conditional rank>=kappa*l/2 leaves whole-input rank>=kappa*n/2, and at mostkappa*l/16 further affine fixings preserve selected-block rank>=3kappa*l/16.

Traced the nonlinear future-seed consistency step in Lemma3.11. It remains an indicator inside expectation rather than an illegitimate affine conditioning. On each good cell, fixing the kernel coordinates makes the pair affine in a uniform selected output W; Fourier expansion of the consistency indicator has total absolute coefficient1 and degree<=D.

Checked the resulting loss2^Qg(epsilon_g+2^-zeta_D*s_g), with no extra loss from the number of affine cells because their probabilities sum to1. Checked Parseval/Cauchy–Schwarz conversion and the low-entropy tampered-image case by conditioning on the whole affine image.
remaining: Large-proof exception:129 pages. The central conditioning/Fourier bookkeeping was traced conditional on the stated local condenser/correlation breaker and low-degree correlation bounds; these constructions are not fully verified.
Proposition3.7, Lemma3.8, all parameter hierarchies, multiple-tampering extension, sublinear-entropy regime and branching-program/resolution/lifting applications remain unchecked.

papers.title: A dichotomy theorem for approximating CSPs in random-order streams
papers.authors: Noah G. Singer, Madhur Tulsiani, Santhoshini Velusamy

review.title: A dichotomy theorem for approximating CSPs in random-order streams
review.authors: Noah G. Singer, Madhur Tulsiani, Santhoshini Velusamy
review.summary: For every finite-alphabet fixed-arity predicate family and gap beta<gamma, the basic LP characterizes single-pass random-order approximability: if LP solves the gap, O_epsilon(log^3 n) space solves the loosened gap; otherwise Omega_epsilon(n) space is needed even for O_epsilon(n) constraints at the tightened gap. Perfect completeness is retained when gamma=1.
review.prior_frontier: Previous random-order lower bounds were Omega(sqrt n) for one-wise-uniform predicate families; linear lower bounds and broad LP classifications were known in adversarial or multipass models. Literature not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A broad dichotomy with exponential space separation, including first claimed linear random-order CSP lower bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: Moves singleton-free Fourier analysis from edge to component blocks and couples it to random-hypergraph exponential moments; simulates regularization by weighted stream explorations.
score_reasons.depth: Both general lower bound and arbitrary-degree streaming LP algorithm require substantial new analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed model, overview and modular lemmas expose the major bottlenecks despite the85-page length.

checked: Traced weighted singleton-free level inequality from component-resampling hypercontractivity, multiplier domination, Parseval and p-1=(t-l)/(2s).
Checked complex-valued extension of positive resampling operator through pointwise absolute-value domination.
Read distinction between Poisson random instance and random presentation, and removal of nonzero-shift constraints to retain original predicate family.
remaining: Posterior induction Theorem5.10, random-hypergraph component bounds, communication hybrid and gap transfer not audited.
On-the-fly regularization, exploration importance weights and suffix-degree bias control not audited.
Essential cited hypercontractivity and LP local solver dependencies not independently checked.

score_reasons.depth: Needs distributional control across intermediate lattices, generalized birthday combination and paid worst-case sampling/precision costs.

checked: Verified the normalization stability inequality in Lemma 2.7.
Checked that the λ₁ guess is from a polynomial-size list and that correctness uses only a near-correct guess, while all guesses must be paid in the runtime.
remaining: Trace the gradient signal after coset aggregation, difference-tree distribution/independence lemmas, discrete-Gaussian generation and worst-case time/precision cap. The paper has 62 pages.

review.authors: Weitian Tong, Yao Xu
review.summary: Randomized always-feasible algorithms for unweighted nonpreemptive throughput maximization on any number of identical machines achieve expected ratios 17/13+ε in polynomial time and 21/17+ε in pseudopolynomial time, with integer binary-encoded time data.
review.prior_frontier: Improves manuscript-cited STOC 2026 ratios 4/3+ε and 5/4+ε. Polynomial versus pseudopolynomial dependence is explicitly distinguished; prior results are not independently checked yet.

score_reasons.significance: Improves two quantitative guarantees for a recognized throughput problem, though by modest constants.
score_reasons.novelty: Coordinates noncrossing boundary pairs through triple-consistent configuration marginals and exploits crossing-pair slot exchanges.
score_reasons.depth: Requires careful erasure accounting, dependent configuration sampling and projected pricing while retaining feasibility.
score_reasons.exposition: The source of duplicate losses, stronger LP, expected guarantee and machine-count reduction are carefully described.

checked: The final loss conversion is consistent: (c−8η)(1−3η)−η≥c−14η and the stated η ensures 1/(c−14η)<1/c+ε.
Checked why the large-machine theorem would remove fixed-m dependence once its stated hypotheses hold.
remaining: Audit crossing-exchange net gains, noncrossing joint sampling from local marginals, projected LP separation and configuration-copy implementation.
Trace the AGTW26 decomposition and ILM20 large-machine guarantee with binary time data.

review.title: Sample-Efficient Agnostic Multi-Distribution Learning Requires Polynomial Adaptivity
review.authors: Thomas Y. Chen
review.area: Learning theory; adaptive sampling lower bounds
review.summary: At VC dimension d=K+1 and accuracy ε=1/K, agnostic multi-distribution learning with per-instance expected near-optimal sample budget O((d+K)ε^−2 polylog K) needs soft-Ω(K^1/8) expected sampling rounds. Permits arbitrary computation, raw-sample reuse and randomized improper outputs.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier polynomial round lower bounds applied to an optimization abstraction; the open raw-sample question allowed global correlation search. Constant-accuracy logarithmic-round algorithms are not contradicted.

score_reasons.significance: Would resolve the unrestricted adaptivity question with a polynomial rather than logarithmic obstruction.
score_reasons.novelty: Encodes a statistical path in the minimax benchmark and compares whole adaptive experiments rather than assuming path following or full table recovery.
score_reasons.depth: Latent source order, retained pilots, stopping flags and one shared sample budget require delicate adaptive likelihood bookkeeping.
score_reasons.exposition: The assumptions and failure modes are explicit, but the main lower bound depends on a large appendix of interlocking comparison lemmas.

checked: Checked the deterministic-majority benchmark and telescoping extraction of endpoint correlation for randomized predictors.
Checked that N≳K sqrt(D)/(ε²R⁴ sqrt(log K)) with D=K yields the stated K^1/8/polylog round exponent at near-optimal samples.
remaining: Audit the exact-pool KL expansion, evolving-reference Lemma 4.2, retained-pilot martingale bound and expected-round truncation. The 104-page argument is not fully checked.

papers.authors: August Chen, Claudio Gentile, Haim Kaplan, Tomer Koren

review.title: Supervised Learning with Hidden Correspondences
review.authors: August Chen, Claudio Gentile, Haim Kaplan, Tomer Koren
review.summary: Hidden input-label correspondences lie in a fixed data-independent matching-covered bipartite graph G. Pseudo-label ERM obtains agnostic VC excess risk O(sqrt((d log(1/delta)+log(1/delta))/n_eff(G))) with n_eff=u^T L^dagger u. score_reasons.novelty: Minimum-norm weights unbiased for every hidden perfect matching become normalized electrical potentials; a uniform dependent-pair Hanson-Wright bound enables ERM.
score_reasons.depth: Uniform concentration, graph lower-bound construction and sample-dependent impossibility are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear examples and explicit data-independence and matching-covered preprocessing prevent overinterpreting the universal upper bound as per-graph lower optimality.

checked: Read unbiased-weight characterization and Laplacian expression; checked perfect-matching n and complete-bipartite1 endpoints.
Checked deterministic centering projection preserves Frobenius bound; covariance bias is controlled at same scale.
Read pair-index decoupling roadmap and pseudo-label affine-risk identity, allowing labels outside original range.
remaining: Full weight characterization proof, uniform Hanson-Wright argument and generalization complexity contraction not audited.
Prescribed-degree lower construction, data-dependent graph impossibility and SGD extension need verification.

checked: Verified Forrelation 1−2k/N when a sign vector differs in k coordinates from the Hadamard transform of a bent function.
Confirmed the lower bound counts both classical preprocessing and quantum oracle queries.

papers.title: Local Search with Correlated Randomness
papers.authors: Yunbei Xu

review.title: Local Search with Correlated Randomness
review.authors: Yunbei Xu
review.summary: Studies tape laws satisfying ν[w]≤D P[w]^s for every prefix. Closed-event worst-case probabilities equal min(1,D times the prefix-cover capacity). For a specified majority-satisfiable k-CNF local walk, identifies a sharp source threshold, cubic expected delay at threshold and linear delay above it; also gives restart, retry-order and noisy-search applications.
review.prior_frontier: Uses a classical tree-capacity identity, explicitly credited as such; novelty is algorithmic characterization and sharp critical-time bounds, not a new max-flow theorem. Not a SAT tractability breakthrough.

score_reasons.significance: Gives exact robustness thresholds and running-time transitions for concrete algorithms under a cumulative weak-randomness model.
score_reasons.novelty: Variable-depth prefix covers distinguish algorithms with identical independent-randomness stopping laws and quantify why shared-tape restarts may fail.
score_reasons.depth: Critical barriers and matching capped-recursion constructions yield nontrivial cubic-to-linear and cube-root-tail transitions.
score_reasons.exposition: The model and its limits are explicit, including that the k=3 strong promise is already tractable by 2-SAT.

checked: Checked the finite-depth capacity proof: a maximum subflow respecting prefix capacities extends to a probability law because child capacities sum to at least parent capacity.
Checked the barrier balance m versus T/m² gives the claimed cube-root exponent; this is conditional on the displayed strip estimate.
remaining: Verify extension from finite cylinders to arbitrary closed events, the capped-recursion lower bounds, all-source sharpness and matching delay construction.
Audit restart necessity/sufficiency and noisy-search reductions separately.

review.prior_frontier: Closes the O(ε^−4) versus Ω(ε^−2) uniform-sampling gap. Sparse relative bounds use O(ε^−2 n/d̄) samples; cut recovery still needs O(nε^−2) further weight queries.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a basic optimal sampling rate for a canonical dense-graph problem, with metric and sparse-relative extensions.
score_reasons.novelty: Minimax matching of fractional cuts under two vertex distributions reduces optimum comparison to a symmetrizable empirical-process bound.
score_reasons.depth: Handles the sample-dependent feasible region and cut choice, not just concentration of a fixed cut.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise weighted sampling and value-versus-solution distinctions; clean deterministic comparison lemma isolates the random step.

checked: Fully traced minimax Lemma 2.6 on symmetric compact convex domains and its 4Δ cut-value comparison.
Checked repeated sampled vertices can be coalesced without lowering cut value because there are no self-loops and all copies have identical external weights.
remaining: Audit symmetrization for the sample-dependent domain, kernel-moment bounds, importance-sampling lower bound and Max-r-Cut extension.

Checked multiplication correction p and automorphism correction tau(p)/p preserve logical representation.
Read security reduction with public p fixed before key generation and full-output centered-restoration inequality.
remaining: Cyclotomic-unit spanning dependency, bit complexity, rescaling appendix and RNS error guarantees not audited.

review.title: Temporal Aggregation: Maintaining Randomness against Adaptive Adversaries
review.authors: Bernhard Haeupler, Anton Paramonov

score_reasons.significance: A reusable adaptive-randomness maintenance theorem with multiple dynamic-graph applications has broad algorithmic value.
score_reasons.novelty: The temporal-selection attack isolates a different bias mechanism and motivates a generic repair principle.
score_reasons.depth: Requires coupling evolving objects to few fresh realizations and amortizing adversary-triggered resampling.
score_reasons.exposition: The concrete attack, static/dynamic distinction and application roadmap make the contribution unusually accessible.

checked: Recomputed the one-level attack probabilities: fresh simultaneous trials succeed with 37/64, whereas adaptive deletion and sequential sampling succeed with 3/4.
Confirmed that the attack samples each walk only once, distinguishing it from simple resample-until-hit selection.
remaining: Trace the recursive polynomial amplification, generic temporal aggregation theorem, and update/dilation/congestion accounting in applications.

review.summary: Temporal aggregation maintains random choices under adaptive updates with logarithmic load/resampling overhead, yielding adaptive dynamic expander routing and coloring applications. Identifies temporal-selection attacks against an earlier proactive-resampling analysis and supplies a repair framework.
review.prior_frontier: Builds on ESA 2022 proactive resampling and exhibits a gap in its claimed adaptive guarantee; the precise attack and repaired spanner comparison need independent checking before endorsing the correction claim.

papers.title: Integral saturation of adjacency-degree lattices
papers.authors: Zhipeng Lu

review.title: Integral saturation of adjacency-degree lattices
review.authors: Zhipeng Lu
review.summary: For G∼G(n,1/2), the integer module Z⟨A,D⟩1 equals Z^n with failure probability at most n^(−3/20+o(1)), simultaneously eliminating all prime obstructions. A fixed polynomial-size family of diameter≤7 caterpillars of order O(√(n log n)) identifies almost every graph among all finite simple graphs; no efficient decoder is claimed.
review.prior_frontier: Stronger than rational walk controllability and distinct from generalized-spectrum reconstruction: the degree operator is required and the conclusion is integral saturation. The manuscript cites prior AD moments and random-matrix estimates; these dependencies remain to be traced.

score_reasons.significance: Establishes a strong arithmetic rigidity property of random graphs and a constrained homomorphism-profile identification theorem.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses a common degree-difference denominator to reduce infinitely many prime obstructions to a bounded range, then tailored dependent-matrix estimates.
score_reasons.depth: The finite-prime analyses, conditional alternating forms and invariant-subspace counts are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully distinguishes identification from decoding and rational generation from all-prime saturation.

checked: Verified the mod-two adjacency-only obstruction using vanishing positive moments and isotropic dimension bounds.
Checked the final prime-union argument conditional on B.1/S1.1/S2.1/S3.1: prime divisors of degree differences are ≤n−1 and the stated failure bounds sum to n^(−3/20+o(1)).
remaining: Audit the integer-surjective cut construction giving Δ_G³ Z^n, all conditional prime estimates and their uniformity.
Verify the caterpillar-family count/order bound and integer-orthogonal rigidity argument.

papers.title: The Complexity of Single-Interaction Hamiltonians
papers.authors: Elad Hecker

review.title: The Complexity of Single-Interaction Hamiltonians
review.authors: Elad Hecker
review.summary: Claims QMA-completeness for a fixed unit-strength ordered two-qubit interaction h=Z⊗Z+X⊗Y−Y⊗X, using only the interaction graph as input. Also develops exact finite-interaction compilers, geometric 8-local hardness and several separately qualified stoquastic, precise and frustration-free consequences.
review.prior_frontier: Prior fixed two-qubit hardness allowed large variable weights. The main construction does not preserve bounded degree; geometric and size-dependent interactions are separate theorems.

score_reasons.significance: Removes both termwise type and coupling-strength freedoms at the smallest nontrivial locality.
score_reasons.novelty: Opposite orientations cancel exchange and create Ising penalties; defect-relative perturbation avoids a prohibitive global perturbation norm.
score_reasons.depth: Requires energetic enforcement of core sectors, balanced mediator simulation and exact spectral-window compilation.
score_reasons.exposition: Careful distinction between fixed and uniformly size-dependent interactions, but the 120-page scope and numerous secondary claims make auditing demanding.

checked: Checked h_uv+h_vu=2Z_uZ_v and that (h+3I)/4 is rank-three projector via eigenvalues 1,1,1,−3.
Checked incorrect core sectors have energy at least 4S−12MR while a valid sector has energy at most zero, so S>3MR excludes incorrect sectors.
remaining: Audit strong-from-weak effective XY approximation and defect-relative error bounds, source QMA-hardness assumptions and all compiler promises. Secondary qPCP/FF/stoquastic results are not yet traced.

papers.title: Limits of Finite-Sample Dependence Measures under Data Processing Inequality
papers.authors: Yuqing Kong

review.title: Limits of Finite-Sample Dependence Measures under Data Processing Inequality
review.authors: Yuqing Kong
review.area: Information theory / algebraic statistics / mechanism design
review.summary: For an independence-zero C1-extendable one-sided fixed-alphabet DPI functional on n-by-m distributions, any zero row forces value0; if n>m it vanishes everywhere. For n<=m, every nonzero polynomial such functional has degree at least2n and lies in the square of the maximal-minor ideal modulo total-mass1. Gram determinant attains2n. Dimension-changing DPI families all collapse. Gives sharp2n-task bounds for normalized nontrivial peer prediction under memoryless garbling.
review.prior_frontier: Squared-DMI supplied2n-task constructions; earlier binary low-degree results did not establish all-alphabet rigidity. Interior smoothness is insufficient; Shannon information evades boundary-C1 hypothesis.

score_reasons.significance: Sharp obstruction classifies when finite unbiased DPI scores and unequal-alphabet peer payments can exist.
score_reasons.novelty: Reversible split/merge at an unused state forces derivative equality; positivity promotes row-cone vanishing to second-order determinantal-ideal membership.
score_reasons.depth: Connects differential boundary argument to Schur charts and primary powers of generic maximal minors.
score_reasons.exposition: Exception hypotheses, one-sided versus dimension-changing models and memoryless-strategy limitations are explicit; core proof is concise.

checked: Traced zero-row proof: proportional splitting, two-sided transfer minimum, C1 boundary limit, all mass moved to one row; verified n=2 and additional-zero-entry cases.
Traced tall-case factorization U=T U_flat and dimension-changing reversible unused-state embedding.
Traced homogenization, positive open Schur chart, vanishing constant/linear q terms and saturation to I_n^2; no degree reduction via simplex relation.
Checked essential Bruns-Vetter Corollary9.18 in author-hosted book PDFpage122: powers of generic maximal-minor ideals are primary.
Checked Gram determinant sharpness by Cauchy-Binet and Hadamard |det T|<=1, plus degree/sample equivalence and peer-prediction reduction.
remaining: Supplementary restricted-deviation construction, family of admissible factors and coNP-hardness appendix not audited.
No formal verification; historical novelty claims attributed to manuscript.

review.title: Optimal Marginal Convergence for Transvection-Walk-Based Trapdoored Matrices over Large Fields
review.authors: Mark Braverman, Aayush Jain, Stephen Newman

score_reasons.significance: A uniform optimal mixing law across arbitrary entry subsets is a substantial random-walk result.
score_reasons.novelty: Skeleton-conditioned bounds support a stronger structural picture than unconditional mixing alone.
score_reasons.depth: Rational sections, collision-variety estimates, routing and rank minors require a lengthy algebraic/probabilistic argument.
score_reasons.exposition: The main theorem lists explicit field/time hypotheses, and the cryptographic assumptions are disclosed.

checked: Inspected the transmission-chain degree bound: a nonzero product of elementary matrices forces consecutive matching indices, enabling the union bound.
Confirmed the field-size threshold is exponential in n log n rather than a small-field result.
remaining: Trace geometric integrality of fibers, collision-count-to-TV transfer, target-schedule routing and worst-case lower bounds.

review.summary: Claims optimal Θ(|S|+n log(n/ε)) marginal mixing for any nonempty entry subset S in random transvection walks on SL_n(F_q), including typical row-pair-skeleton conditioning, for very large q≥(5000n)^(6n). Cryptographic trapdoored-matrix consequences assume structure-conditioned pseudorandomness.
review.prior_frontier: Closes the cited large-field transvection column/marginal mixing gap. The field-size restriction and conjectural cryptographic leap are essential; mixing is not itself pseudorandomness against computational attacks.

papers.title: Beating the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound at Alphabet Size 42
papers.authors: Gil Cohen, Tomer Manket

review.title: Beating the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound at Alphabet Size 42
review.authors: Gil Cohen, Tomer Manket
review.summary: Proves existence of nonlinear codes over alphabet 42 with rate at least 1−H₄₂(δ)+β for one uniform β>0 and every δ∈[.39,.48]. Alphabet restriction of AG codes, divisor-class averaging and expurgation improve the asymptotic Gilbert–Varshamov bound; no explicit construction is provided.
review.prior_frontier: Lowers the manuscript-reported threshold from alphabet 46 (Zinoviev–Litsyn, 1985) to 42. This is an existence frontier rather than an explicit-code or binary-GV result.

score_reasons.significance: Improves a decades-old threshold in a foundational rate-distance problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Controls surviving close pairs after alphabet restriction through divisor-class weight distributions and zeta functions.
score_reasons.depth: Requires AG-code counting and an optimized asymptotic expurgation estimate, with a delicate small numerical gain.
score_reasons.exposition: The statement, nonconstructive scope, proof overview and extensive background exposition are exceptionally clear.

checked: Recomputed F(.39)=0.0000531098733965 and F(.48)=0.000312486226023, and checked the exact integer inequality 90^6<49^7.
Traced concavity of F, admissible a_GV range and compactness argument producing a single t₀ and positive rate increment uniform on [.39,.48], conditional on Proposition 4.9.
remaining: Audit average truncated weight-enumerator estimates, class-number/zeta asymptotics, alphabet restriction and expurgation lemma and all AG tower hypotheses.
Numerical spot checks are not interval-arithmetic certificates for the full theorem; the analytic concavity reduction is what reduces the sign test to endpoints.

review.title: An $O(n^{0.1537})$-Coloring Algorithm for $3$-Colorable Graphs
review.authors: Kaisei Deguchi, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Hirotaka Yoneda, Masataka Yoneda
review.summary: Randomized polynomial-time O(n^0.1537)-coloring of every 3-colorable graph; a general vector-coloring independent-set framework first gives n^(1/6+o(1)), then band rounding and stronger constraints improve the exponent.
review.prior_frontier: Improves Bansal–Huang–Lee O(n^0.1954). This is approximate coloring, not exact 3-colorability or constant-color approximation; uses KTY24 dense-progress as a dependency.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial exponent improvement for a central long-standing approximation problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Nested cores turn failed Gaussian local-maximum rounds into geometric covers; Ehrhard-based lifting and band rounding strengthen sparse progress.
score_reasons.depth: Combines Gaussian convex geometry, recursive failure certificates, approximate SDP implementation and numerically certified inequalities.
score_reasons.exposition: States ordinary versus strict vector coloring separately and provides implementation and computational-verification appendices.

checked: Checked β=2/3 in Theorem 3 gives independent-set exponent 5/6 and dense-progress exponent 1/6.
Checked β=.692601 yields α=(1−β)/2=.1536995, leaving positive slack for the advertised .1537 exponent.
Traced Lemma 39 conversion of a neighborhood Gaussian tail into a large-measure convex set, conditioning on the transverse-selected neighbor.
remaining: Large-proof exception: 79 pages plus a numerical exponent certificate. The independent-set exponent conversion and neighborhood-to-convex-set lemma were checked, while the nested-core/lifting and certified computation remain substantive unverified components.
Audit nested-core probability estimates, Ehrhard lifting and final numerical certificate; verify KTY24 input requirements and approximate SDP robustness. The 79-page proof is not fully traced.

review.title: BQP⊆IP Does Not Relativize
review.authors: Adam Bouland, Andrew Huang, Anand Natarajan, Itay Shalit, Avishay Tal
review.area: Quantum and classical complexity / interactive proofs
review.summary: Constructs a classical oracle O with BQP^O not contained in IP^O by proving Forrelation fools polynomial-depth, polynomial-message Avg-Max circuits. Together with the separately cited relativizing BQP-in-MIP theorem, gives IP^O!=MIP^O. Does not rule out unrelativized IP or cryptographic verification.
review.prior_frontier: Addresses a longstanding open BQP-versus-IP oracle question; prior Forrelation lower bounds separated PH rather than full interactive proofs. IP-versus-MIP consequence uses a separate recent inclusion.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a foundational oracle-separation question and constrains black-box classical verification of quantum computation.
score_reasons.novelty: Convex softmax extensions of interactive acceptance functions and conditional Gaussian sign smoothing bypass Fourier-mass barriers.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines oracle normal forms, derivative bounds, shifted Gaussian interpolation and multiscale hybrids with precise dimension control.
score_reasons.exposition: A clear six-step overview and detailed core estimates make a difficult separation unusually traceable.

checked: Traced oracle-decision-tree affine max representation and softmax induction: error dLln2/lambda, gradient l1<=L and entrywise Hessian l1<=2lambda d L^2.

Traced central convex rounding lemma: condition on signs and correlated Gaussian component, use independent truncated Gaussians; checked density bound1/sigma+|mu|/sigma^2 and Gaussian max yields logarithmic dimension cost.
Traced shifted-coordinate tail fixing, Gaussian interpolation with no diagonal covariance contribution, and all dyadic independent-noise-removal hybrids.
Checked delta=N^(-1/8),lambda=1/delta,T=ceil(10ln(2N)) give poly(n)N^(-1/8); checked terminal sign-coupling error.

Traced AppendixA Forrelation advantage from orthogonality and Gaussian moments, then AppendixC random-oracle diagonalization. Other-length oracle blocks can be fixed since the circuit bound is uniform; choose spaced lengths beyond earlier query bounds.

Inspected Goldwasser-Sipser original public-coin conversion description; set-membership verification can use the same classical oracle, supporting applicability of the standard relativizing conversion.
remaining: Supplementary PRG consequences and BQP-intersection-NP versus prover-efficient IP AppendixD not fully audited.
The external recent BQP-in-MIP inclusion underlying the IP/MIP corollary was not independently checked.
No formal verification of the main separation.

papers.title: Random-Oracle Unitary Synthesis is Impossible
papers.authors: Andrew Huang, Akshar Ramkumar, John Wright

review.title: Random-Oracle Unitary Synthesis is Impossible
review.authors: Andrew Huang, Akshar Ramkumar, John Wright

score_reasons.significance: Separates random-oracle resources from worst-case structured queries in a fundamental synthesis task.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines a synthesis impossibility theorem with near-matching pseudorandom-unitary security constructions.
score_reasons.depth: Requires query-weight sensitivity, representation-theoretic design control and sharp adversary bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The manuscript explicitly distinguishes query efficiency from computational efficiency for its strongest upper bound.

checked: Traced the single-oracle-bit hybrid expansion and its factorization into matrices of forward/backward query amplitudes.
Checked the Frobenius-norm accounting that connects this factorization to the two query weights.
remaining: Audit the random-oracle synthesis coupling, representation-theoretic high-order design bounds and the PRU impossibility/construction transition.

review.summary: Superpolynomial query lower bound for synthesizing Haar-random unitaries from a random Boolean oracle; excludes scalable ROM pseudorandom unitaries beyond roughly N-query security while constructing query-efficient O(N)-secure designs. The strongest construction is not known computationally efficient.
review.prior_frontier: Contrasts with recent worst-case unitary synthesis using arbitrary classical function oracles and improves prior design-security levels. The model distinction is central; no contradiction to worst-case synthesis is claimed.
