papers.authors: Zvika Brakerski, Andrew Huang, Yael Tauman Kalai, Nicholas Spooner

review.title: Tight Post-Quantum Parallel Repetition for Private-Coin Arguments
review.authors: Zvika Brakerski, Andrew Huang, Yael Tauman Kalai, Nicholas Spooner
review.summary: Under the appropriate post-quantum FHE assumption, FHE-transformed polynomial-round private-coin arguments have k-fold threshold-repetition soundness at most the Binomial(k,ε) tail plus negligible error, including ε^k for all-accept. Gives a constant-round succinct QMA argument with negligible errors under post-quantum LWE.
review.prior_frontier: Previous encrypted parallel-repetition analyses addressed classical cheating provers and weaker bounds. The theorem concerns a transformed protocol, not arbitrary unmodified private-coin repetition.

score_reasons.significance: Obtains the optimal binomial soundness profile against entangled quantum cheating provers and a useful QMA consequence.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines a tighter correlation-reduction strategy with coherent ciphertext switching that preserves adversary entanglement.
score_reasons.depth: Requires QSVT/projector manipulation, cryptographic hybrids and a quantitative reduction through polynomially many rounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The transformed-protocol scope and classical-versus-quantum FHE requirements are explicit.

checked: Matched informal Theorem 1.1 to Corollary 5.3, including efficient ε, polynomial k,t and additive negligible error.
Inspected the final contradiction reduction and the explicit use of multiple initial-state advice copies; no claim of cloning an unknown state is made.
remaining: Trace the oracle distinguisher and coherent switching lemmas, success amplification cost and negligibility uniformly over all rounds.
Check the QMA succinct-argument composition and precise classical-friendly quantum FHE assumption from LWE.

papers.title: Sharp universal death of entanglement threshold for Pauli Hamiltonians
papers.authors: Bobak Kiani

review.title: Sharp universal death of entanglement threshold for Pauli Hamiltonians
review.authors: Bobak T. Kiani
review.summary: Determines the universal full-separability threshold for Pauli Hamiltonians with coefficient magnitudes ≤J and term-overlap degree Δ≥2: βJ≤arctanh(max_(0≤x≤1) x[(1−x)/(1+x)]^(Δ−1)). Gives commuting finite-tree entanglement witnesses above it, asymptotic constant 1/(2eΔ), and a classical product-state sampler a fixed distance below threshold.
review.prior_frontier: Improves earlier sufficient 1/(96Δ) scale to the exact degree-dependent boundary, with locality-independent overlap convention. Algorithm is polynomial for fixed Δ and fixed relative distance below threshold, not uniformly at the boundary.

score_reasons.significance: An exact universal entanglement transition, including matching witnesses, is a substantial sharpening of recent high-temperature quantum results.
score_reasons.novelty: A separable polymer expansion is governed by an independence/component polynomial; noncommutation is absorbed into corrected polymer weights.
score_reasons.depth: Requires simultaneous Pauli coefficient control, positivity at the tree fixed point, a partial-transpose obstruction and efficient approximate sampling.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly states the overlap graph, coefficient dependence and the gap between threshold separability and algorithmic interior.

checked: Checked optimization gives xΔ=sqrt((Δ−1)²+1)−(Δ−1), z2=(log 2)/4 and asymptotic 1/(2eΔ).
Traced the deletion-induction neighborhood count |N[γ]−{v}|≤(Δ−1)|γ| and the full-degree extra-factor handling.

Traced the entire main separability-threshold proof, Sections3–4. Inclusion-exclusion factors only over disjoint-support overlap components, so products of separable polymer corrections are legitimate. The different anticommutation-component factorization is used only for the Pauli norm, not for separability.

Checked the symmetrized-product cancellation induction: disconnected components factor; stars yield the alternating-position average; deleting any vertex of a connected nonstar leaves an anticommuting edge. Derived the 1/3 cancellation, the normalized cosh inclusion-exclusion identity, and the eta alpha^(|U|−1) bound.

Checked the red-first spanning-tree injection preserves anticommutation-component sizes. Traced both colored-tree generating functions, the scalar inequalities from 2bx=1−x², and the strict full-degree root bound.

Completed positivity induction including closed-neighborhood count b|gamma| versus b|gamma|+1, parent-before-child deletion ratios, and the strict inequality needed at Δ=2. Verified the weighted closed-neighborhood result by coefficient splitting and finite-dimensional closedness.

Traced the sharpness witness: two qubits per tree edge give commuting independent stabilizers with overlap graph exactly T; partial transpose produces (−1) per selected edge. The eigenvalue on the all-negative stabilizer sector equals the component polynomial. The b-ary recurrence x_{h+1}=s((1+x_h)/(1−x_h))^b crosses1 at finite height above the maximizing threshold, including exact-hit handling.
remaining: The main exact universal threshold and weighted sharp constant were audited. The efficient approximate product-state sampler of Section5, its truncation and finite-precision analysis, remain unverified and are not covered by this main-proof status.

Standard Pauli algebra, partial-transpose necessity for separability, and finite-dimensional compactness were used as established facts. No independent priority certification against all concurrent thermal-state results.

papers.title: Linear-Space Exact Distance Oracle for Minor-Free Graphs
papers.authors: Eunjin Oh

review.title: Linear-Space Exact Distance Oracle for Minor-Free Graphs
review.authors: Eunjin Oh
review.summary: For each fixed excluded minor H and constant epsilon>0, gives an O(n)-space exact distance oracle on weighted H-minor-free graphs with O(n^(1/2+epsilon)) query time. Also gives a space/query tradeoff roughly sigma versus n/sqrt(sigma), with polylogarithmic factors and substantial preprocessing; constants depend on H and epsilon. The new primitive partitions dense-distance pairs in a planar graph with one bounded-width vortex into Monge pairs and constant-middle-layer hourglasses.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript compares the linear-space result with planar exact oracles, the older Djidjev sigma-space/n^2/sigma tradeoff and VC-dimension approaches with nearquadratic space. Historical bounds not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Extends a fundamental planar-style exact linear-space distance bound to every fixed minor-free class.
score_reasons.novelty: The Monge/hourglass representation handles nonplanarity from bounded-width vortices while retaining efficient dense-distance relaxations.
score_reasons.depth: Combines graph-minor decompositions, shortest-path topology, recursive pair partitions and FR-Dijkstra machinery.
score_reasons.exposition: The structural lemmas give explicit vertex-participation and exact-distance invariants; decomposition and preprocessing assumptions are stated.

checked: Inspected the extended-boundary construction and why removing society-bag vertices separates the vortex into the appropriate sides.

Read Lemmas 22–28: separating or one-sided-touching paths yield constant-size bag hitting sets; free paths yield Monge inequalities; recursive partition halves a cardinality/product measure and bounds vertex participation.
remaining: Full correctness audit still needed: shortest-path tie-breaking/topological prerequisites, Lemma 7 special r-division, Appendix C partition proof, hourglass integration in shortest-path search, and reductions from multiple vortices/general clique sums.
Need independently verify graph-minor decomposition and FR-Dijkstra dependency hypotheses and all preprocessing/space accounting.

papers.authors: Shuchi Chawla, Dimitrios Christou

review.title: Stochastic Weighted Caching with Per-Request Predictions
review.authors: Shuchi Chawla, Dimitris Christou

score_reasons.significance: A constant guarantee resolves a natural combination of two previously insufficient information models.
score_reasons.novelty: Ex-ante covering relaxations, guarded eviction and ghost contraction supply a new route to the constant.
score_reasons.depth: The mandatory-admission partition and prediction-error charging are substantial technical obligations.
score_reasons.exposition: The one-hole example explains both the gain and the unequal-cost obstacle; continuous-time and discrete-time qualifications are explicit.

checked: Checked the qualified-miss amortization using disjoint hole intervals and the reason unqualified events are counted without conditioning on a prediction-revealing history.
Checked the ghost-versus-normal mass case split at the level of its stated relaxation and balance constraint.
remaining: The full ex-ante lower bound, quantitative partition constants giving 15.75, and erroneous-prediction analysis need a complete audit.

review.summary: Combines independent requests from a known distribution with per-request next-arrival predictions to obtain 15.75-competitive weighted caching and an error-sensitive O(min{1+E,log k}) bound.
review.prior_frontier: Each ingredient alone leaves a logarithmic barrier for weighted caching. The guarantee is an asymptotic expected cost-rate comparison; the discrete index-prediction transfer additionally assumes independence from the synthetic Poisson clock.

papers.title: Linear-size $\ell_1$ sparsifiers
papers.authors: Victor Reis, Thomas Rothvoss

review.title: Linear-size $\ell_1$ sparsifiers
review.authors: Victor Reis, Thomas Rothvoss
review.summary: Every real m×n matrix admits a nonnegative diagonal row rescaling with O(n/ε²) nonzero entries preserving its ℓ₁ norm on every vector within 1±ε. Equivalently, every n-dimensional zonotope has such a linear-size segment sparsifier. The ℓ₁ construction takes 2^m times polynomial time, not polynomial time.
review.prior_frontier: Removes Talagrand’s logarithmic factor O(n log n/ε²), answering the stated 1986 Schechtman question; matches the row-selection lower bound in the indicated ε regime.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a longstanding optimal-size ℓ₁ sparsification/zonotope approximation problem.
score_reasons.novelty: A separately convex leftover-volume function, hypercontractivity and symmetric-body volume bounds enable iterative support removal.
score_reasons.depth: Geometric volume and discrepancy tools replace independent sampling and yield the missing logarithm.
score_reasons.exposition: The existence/runtime distinction and equivalent formulations are clearly stated.

checked: Traced Theorem 26 conditional on Corollary 25 and Theorem 7: sign choice removes at least one quarter of supported segments and multiplicative errors sum geometrically to ε once support reaches Cn/ε².
Checked the stated exponential construction bottleneck is the zonotope containment oracle, not an asserted efficient ℓ₁ algorithm.

Traced the new zonotope anti-concentration argument on pages 7–12: Minkowski erosion by one segment has convex fiber-length volume, hence zonotope erosion is separately convex; separate Jensen plus degree-d scaling produces the positive-support bound. Applying Bonami hypercontractivity with p=1+rho² gives alpha≥rho^(2d(1+rho²)/(1−rho²)); the limit rho→1 is exp(−2d). Conditioning on absolute coordinates transfers this to the continuous cube.

Checked the erosion scaling identity and every coordinate section, including rank-deficient zonotopes handled in their span. Support functions justify cancellation of a common Minkowski summand, so all coordinate sections have relative volume≥exp(−2n).

Completed the symmetrizer argument on pages 12–15. In the dyadic coordinate partition, the sorted coefficients give the stated l2/l1 comparison; the inequality sqrt(uv)≤(5/4)(u+v)−u and m_(k+1)/m_k≥2/5 make the directional bounds telescope. The scaled Cartesian-product volumes give p·2^(−2m). A separating hyperplane then contradicts the existence of a large reflected intersection in the directional truncation. The needed existence follows directly from the manuscript’s averaging proof of Proposition23(A), so the stronger external assertion that the barycenter is suitable is not essential.

Checked the final sparsification: volume at least2^(−5m) gives a constant-scaled partial coloring via the explicitly stated external Reis–Rothvoss theorem; reversing its sign removes at least a quarter of the rows. Error parameters increase geometrically with shrinking support, and their sum is O(sqrt(c0/C)epsilon), yielding the required two-sided multiplicative error. The implementation uses exponential-time zonotope containment; no polynomial-time algorithm is inferred.
remaining: The main l1/zonotope theorem is traced. Bonami hypercontractivity and the Reis–Rothvoss constructive partial-coloring theorem are explicit imported interfaces, not re-proved. The separate PSD/spectral-sparsifier extension in Section7 and Banach-space historical consequences were not audited.

papers.title: Optimal Sparsification of Gaussian Processes
papers.authors: Shivam Nadimpalli

review.title: Optimal Sparsification of Gaussian Processes
review.authors: Shivam Nadimpalli
review.summary: Every bounded T⊂R^n has a shifted subprocess on exp(O(ε^−2)) points approximating sup_(t∈T) g·t in L2 to ε times Gaussian width. Matching exp(Ω(ε^−2)) lower bound permits arbitrary real shifts. Consequences improve norm juntas and Gaussian polyhedral approximation.
review.prior_frontier: Improves double-exponential shifted sparsification to optimal single-exponential dependence and strengthens L1 to L2. The subset restriction necessitates shifts; centered approximators use additional dimensions.

score_reasons.significance: An optimal dimension-free structural theorem with several learning and geometry consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Dynamically centered softmax interpolation resolves the circular dependence between cluster shifts and active regions.
score_reasons.depth: Brascamp–Lieb controls the conditional residual variance, while a radial slope argument gives the matching lower bound.
score_reasons.exposition: The core theorem is modular and transparent, including ODE existence, nonnegative shifts, bounded-set limits and sharpness.

checked: Traced Lemma 11 in full: continuity and global boundedness of the shift ODE by Gaussian integration by parts, Jensen on softmax weights and Hessian≥I for their conditional densities, giving L2 derivative ≤ net radius.
Checked Sudakov net cardinality, softmax truncation errors, nonnegative shifts from fixed representatives, and dense-subset limiting argument.

Traced matching lower bound: outside spherical caps every affine piece has radial slope ≤.9, forcing variance ≥1/(400n); exponentially small cap measure forces exponentially many pieces. Checked n=floor((κ/ε)²) and Gaussian-width rescaling.
Dependencies checked at theorem level: classical Sudakov minoration, Brascamp–Lieb variance bound, Peano existence, Gaussian integration by parts, chi variance and spherical cap estimates.
remaining: Secondary Lp, norm-junta, learning/testing and polyhedral-approximation consequences were not exhaustively audited. External classical proofs were not re-proved.

papers.title: Anchoring the Security of Invariant Quantum Money
papers.authors: Hans Schmiedel, Jiangshan Yu

review.title: Anchoring the Security of Invariant Quantum Money
review.authors: Hans Schmiedel, Jiangshan Yu
review.summary: For rapidly mixing invariant-money schemes, characterizes security as preparation hardness from classical (serial number, measured object) inputs plus an explicit coherent-to-measure-first transfer assumption. Proves path-finding permits orbit-state preparation under an efficiently superposable transitive group parameterization, and a serial-number-fixing fully black-box reduction barrier to deriving transfer from preparation hardness. Does not prove security from a standard assumption or show path-finding is insufficient by an oracle separation.
review.prior_frontier: Builds on invariant quantum money, knot/group-action proposals and knowledge-of-path assumptions. The preparation problem generalizes earlier component-superposition formulations; comparisons to the cited security constructions not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Clarifies necessary hardness and a concrete limitation of security reductions for a specialized quantum-money framework.
score_reasons.novelty: The useful additions are the exact measure-first equivalence, group-parameterization condition and serial-fixing barrier; the security decomposition includes a residual transfer assumption rather than replacing it with a standard problem.
score_reasons.depth: Uses spectral verification projection, coherent coset-fiber erasure and a polynomial-query hybrid barrier.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions clearly distinguish accepted weight, multiple orbits per serial number, average-case preparation and inefficient adversaries in the barrier.

checked: Traced Theorem 6.5: a successful measure-first forger gives a preparation algorithm by retaining one output, while independent repeated preparation has expected squared acceptance at least the square of average accepted weight.

Traced Theorems 6.7 and 6.9: transfer failure implies a nonnegligible forger; the controlled synthesis forger acts only on the accepted subspace, and an identity-oracle hybrid bounds a serial-fixing reduction advantage by polynomial times the square root of preparation advantage.
Inspected Proposition 4.4 and 4.7 coherent bijection/coset erasure; success requires orbit/group structure and appropriate section computation.
remaining: Initial screening only; no full audit of amplification with quantum path-finders, knot-model correspondence, NP-oracle preparation, or all design-condition results.

Checked the acceptance-probability convention for atoms and the explicit treatment of γ=0.

review.title: Hypergraph Recovery from Anonymous Projection Streams
review.authors: Siming Zhang, Shijie Chen, Zhehui Shen
review.summary: A one-pass randomized sketch recovers every edge crossing a cut of size <k in a simple r-uniform hypergraph from anonymous q-subset multiplicity counts, at sharp order q=min{r,1+ceil(log2 k)} and soft-O(nrk) bits. Also preserves all cuts truncated at k and gives sparse-difference reconciliation.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier hypergraph sketches received complete hyperedges; projection reconstruction results largely concerned random hypergraphs. Sharp observation threshold is proved for n≥2r and streams fixed independently of sketch randomness.

score_reasons.significance: Provides worst-case reconstruction of connectivity-critical interactions despite anonymous low-order observations, with matching identifiability order.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines low-Boolean-degree sparse recovery with membership/exclusion interpolation and safe clique-separator contractions.
score_reasons.depth: Must discover unknown small cuts without spending full reconstruction space and preserve all witnesses under adaptive contractions of a fixed cache.
score_reasons.exposition: Precisely separates anonymous multiplicity counts, simple uniform targets, oblivious streams, and synthetic weighted cut certificates.

checked: Traced the signed Boolean-moment separate-support induction and the q=2 boundary-sign base case.
Checked rational interpolation uniqueness from 2u evaluations of P′/P with distinct poles, including characteristic two, and the k(n−1) accepted-edge count through disjoint connectivity layers.

papers.title: Near-Quadratic Lower Bounds for Convex Optimization with Binary First-Order Queries
papers.authors: Jiachen Shen, Hui Zhong

review.title: Near-Quadratic Lower Bounds for Convex Optimization with Binary First-Order Queries
review.authors: Jiachen Shen, Hui Zhong
review.summary: For M-Lipschitz convex minimization on [-R,R]^d, one fixed canonical subgradient-selection chart forces every deterministic algorithm using arbitrary one-bit functions of local value/subgradient information to make Omega(d^2 log(MR/epsilon)/log^2(d+1)) queries for epsilon<=5e-8 MR/sqrt(d). At finer accuracies one log(d) denominator suffices. This is a deterministic fixed-chart result, not a randomized lower bound or a lower bound under every subgradient selection.
review.prior_frontier: Previous arbitrary binary first-order bounds had polynomially subquadratic dimension dependence and accuracy appearing separately; a recent exact-value nearquadratic bound had fixed accuracy. The manuscript reuses the exact-value hard matrix family and proves the multiplicative accuracy dependence. Historical comparisons not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Nearly resolves a stated dimension-times-accuracy lower-bound conjecture for local binary first-order oracles.
score_reasons.novelty: The product-row adversary and Brunn–Minkowski output forcing produce the previously missing multiplicative log(1/epsilon) factor.
score_reasons.depth: Handles arbitrary nonmeasurable binary query functions using outer measure while preserving a single predetermined canonical chart.
score_reasons.exposition: The core theorem is self-contained with explicit constants, model limitations, hard-family geometry and a stepwise volume argument.

checked: Traced the central Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 proof. The hard function is max_i(a x_i+<w_i,z>) plus a radial penalty, scaled to be 0.96M-Lipschitz in infinity norm. Identifying each matrix row via separated test points makes the fixed chart well-defined.

Verified nearest-point-in-convex-hull geometry: all simplex weights are positive, >=(1-Gamma^-2)/m; minimizer coordinates have magnitude >=3/(4 sqrt(m)); W^T x*=a z* and quadratic growth force proximity of any epsilon-optimal output. Radial projection does not increase the objective.

Verified the nonmeasurable-set point carefully: E -> outer_measure(P intersect E) is a finite measure on measurable E by Caratheodory additivity; hyperplanes have zero mass, so exact affine quantiles exist. Commitment keeps one row above the largest quantile and all others below it, losing <=4m in product volume, then the bit loses <=2.

Traced output forcing: the entire sum of independently varying rows weighted by output coordinates lies in a radius-r0 ball. At least m/2 coefficients have magnitude >=1/(2 sqrt(m)); taking closed convex hulls, Brunn–Minkowski and AM-GM bound product volume by initial_volume times theta^(m^2/2). Comparing potentials gives the core m^2 log(MR/(C sqrt(m) epsilon))/(4 log(8m)) bound.
Checked the stated constants and two accuracy regimes using m>=d/3, log(8m)<=3log(d+1), C=128*101^2 and C*c0/sqrt(2)<0.0462. No central substantive gap found.
remaining: Mixed-integer transfer theorem and the exact-value-plus-linear-measurement extension in Sections 4–5 have not been audited.
No claim of formal verification or independent validation of cited historical lower bounds.

score_reasons.exposition: Carefully states that energy assembly, retention and full-space readout are assumptions rather than automatic quantum conclusions.

checked: Checked link probability normalization/reversibility and child-parent consistency from common facet weights.
Traced terminal-gap recursion δτ=(1−θτ)min_i δτi and path-product bound using average squared-norm retention.
remaining: Audit the Gram-descent map and compatibility decomposition; no complete quantum instantiation was supplied to audit.

review.authors: Shiri Chechik, Inbal Haddad
review.summary: Gives oblivious-to-adaptive compilers for partially dynamic monotone properties with stable certificates: O(log n) parallel repetition preserves approximation for one-sided Monte Carlo primitives, and a two-primitive Las Vegas compiler preserves summed runtime at a two-step relaxation. Applications include decremental (1+o(1))-mincut with n^o(1) amortized updates and explicit cut, partially dynamic roughly 3/2 diameter, and incremental graph k-center/dominating sets. These are not general fully dynamic compilers.
review.prior_frontier: Generic differential-privacy reductions incurred polynomial overhead and primarily numerical outputs; the quoted recent fast mincut and diameter primitives were oblivious. Claimed clustering improvements include (4+epsilon) to (3+epsilon) oblivious incremental k-center. Historical and dependency bounds not yet independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Addresses adaptive robustness for several central dynamic graph problems while retaining fast update bounds and structural witnesses.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses irreversible stable outputs to hide randomness until a certificate can be frozen, rather than continuous noisy numerical release.
score_reasons.depth: Combines quantile-based repetition, oblivious primitives, multiscale coordination and a new incremental dominating-set sampling process.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit soundness, completeness, stability and runtime conditions make the compiler scope assessable; several application-specific obligations remain in appendices.

checked: Inspected Algorithm 2: copies freeze after their first valid certificate; a time budget aborts a copy; the wrapper outputs a fixed stored certificate once a quarter of copies are done.

Read the mincut threshold primitive and multiscale proof. A candidate cut is extracted and deterministically verified once per threshold, so the O(m) scan is amortized rather than incurred per update. Deletions preserve cut-certificate validity.
Read the incremental dominating-set roadmap: maintain approximate distances from samples of uncovered vertices, choose heavy-cover centers and resample once half the sample is covered.
remaining: Need full audit of the conditional-seed/runtime lemma, Appendix B repetition proof and simultaneous multiscale adaptive composition.
Need inspect essential mincut/SSSP dependency output interfaces, preprocessing/runtime guarantees, disconnected cases and clustering sample-adaptivity analysis.

review.summary: Characterizes almost-sure uniform generation of infinitely many new elements of an unknown infinite language over a countable universe under approximate DP: finite closure dimension and finite nested branching dimension are both necessary and sufficient. Sample upper bound is exponential in branching dimension; the lower bound is logarithm-iterated in it.
review.prior_frontier: Nonprivate generation is characterized by closure dimension alone. This introduces a distinct privacy obstruction and concerns information-theoretic generation, not a computationally efficient language model.

score_reasons.significance: Gives a complete combinatorial characterization for a new private-generation task.
score_reasons.novelty: Nested branching, iterated rank cores and robust-closure profiles isolate stable infinite outputs across neighboring datasets.
score_reasons.depth: Combines set-system structure with private selection and an interior-point lower-bound reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states almost-sure success, distinct-input requirement and the large quantitative gap.

checked: Traced Lemma 5.2’s deeper-tree contradiction proving the rank core remains infinite.
Checked Lemma 5.3 and the rank-decreasing/fixed-point dichotomy, giving at most 2^d possible rank profiles.
remaining: Audit the profile ordering, robust-closure interlacing on all datasets, private stable-block selection and randomized exclusion of input examples.
Trace the nested-tree reduction to interior point with δ≤1/(12n), and check measurability/model details for possibly uncountable classes.

score_reasons.depth: Combines structural-existence arguments, rooted minors and hierarchical recursion while avoiding explicit surface/torso decomposition.
score_reasons.exposition: Transparent depth/time tradeoff and external structural dependence; detailed overview identifies each technical obstruction.

checked: Checked the secret-guessing strategy finds a candidate set intersecting unknown apices, and its tree-distance potential decreases each iteration, hitting an apex within kd rounds.
Read exact runtime/depth theorem and distinction between structural existence in proof and structural construction in the algorithm.
remaining: Audit treewidth-oracle promise conditions, central-apex generalization, truncated quotients and log²³ accounting; verify Razborov decoder and polynomial GMST dependencies.

papers.authors: Zhangsong Li

review.title: Almost Sharp Equivalence between Approximate Message Passing and Low-Degree Polynomials
review.authors: Zhangsong Li
review.area: Average-case complexity; statistical estimation; approximate message passing
review.summary: For symmetric rank-one Gaussian matrix estimation Y=theta theta^T/sqrt(n)+W with fixed nonzero-mean sub-Gaussian iid prior, proves degree-D polynomial MMSE >= E Theta^2-q_AMP-sum_{g=1}^D([120K(D+1)]^60/n)^g. Thus growing degree D=o(n^(1/60)) cannot beat the limiting Bayes-AMP risk, and equality follows for D->infinity from existing fixed-degree AMP approximations. This is a restricted-polynomial lower bound, not general polynomial-time hardness, and excludes zero-mean priors.
review.prior_frontier: Montanari–Wein established constant-degree equivalence under corresponding prior assumptions. This manuscript supplies uniform growing-degree control. Cited AMP state evolution and polynomial approximation theorems not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Identifies the exact limiting risk for a substantially growing algebraic algorithm class in a canonical high-dimensional estimation problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses conditional cumulants with an AMP-calibrated auxiliary scalar channel, then averages out auxiliary randomness before a sharper Jensen bound.
score_reasons.depth: Requires connected multigraph expansions, rooted-tree summation, degree-two chain control and explicit excess-dependent estimates.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes nonzero-mean, fixed-prior, sub-Gaussian assumptions and unit/GOE diagonal normalization, with explicit remainder constants.

checked: Traced conditional-cumulant numerator identities, the two conditional-Jensen/Hermite denominator bounds, and the improvement from averaging cumulants conditional on theta.

Read the leaf-removal cumulant identity and traced the rooted-tree bound: posterior field derivatives yield product weights a_k; conditional Gaussian integration by parts and Bessel give sum s^k a_k/k!<=q_AMP, and an overcounted rooted-tree recurrence is bounded at the fixed point.
Checked why disconnected or root-absent graph cumulants vanish by conditional coordinate independence.
remaining: Main growing-degree assertion still requires audit of non-tree core reduction, long degree-two chain bounds, graph enumeration and the numerical exponent 60.
Need verify scalar fixed-point existence/stability and cited fixed-iteration AMP achievability under general sub-Gaussian priors; no correctness certification yet.

review.authors: Pankaj K. Agarwal, Benjamin Holmgren, Jack Stade

Also proves W[1]-hardness of reachability parameterized by k and instances requiring n^{Ω(k^{1/4})} piecewise-linear breakpoints.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the exponent under a robustness assumption; a concurrent robust-free (n/ε)^{O(k²)} approximation is explicitly acknowledged and also included independently in the appendix.

score_reasons.significance: Combines a faster robust approximation with a parameterized reachability obstruction and super-FPT output-complexity lower bound.
score_reasons.novelty: Hierarchical near-feasible plans and executable caravan surgeries synchronize robots without paying excessive waiting time.
score_reasons.depth: The long argument couples geometric discretization and surgeries with a separate reconfiguration-gadget reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Models and concurrent-work limitations are clear; the 91-page proof has substantial geometric bookkeeping.

checked: Checked the precise benchmark and additive ε exception for small optimal makespan; this is not an ordinary approximation to the unrobust optimum in n^{O(k)} time.
Inspected the surgery accounting: O(k³) events per Δ=Θ(k⁵/ε) interval and O(k²) repair cost per event give an O(ε) relative increase, subject to endpoint handling and constants.
remaining: Audit sampling and near-feasible-plan lemmas, global caravan event bound, collision-free local surgery, and endpoint cases.
Audit both reconfiguration reductions and parameter growth proving W[1]-hardness and the k^{1/4} breakpoint exponent.

review.authors: Thomas Depian, Robert Ganian, Jakob Greilhuber, Marlene Gründel, Simon Wietheger

score_reasons.significance: Turns a broad nonconstructive tractability principle into a uniform algorithm and resolves several concrete parameterized questions.
score_reasons.novelty: Positive pure-witness certificates complement obstruction certificates, allowing a computable search for a sufficient pruning threshold.
score_reasons.depth: Route-pattern consistency, Ramsey purification and multiplicity structures handle dense arbitrary-arity existential witness relations.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully separates decision linearity, witness output size, nonuniformity and absence of an explicit parameter bound.

checked: Checked normalization of abundant route indices preserves prefix equality and commutes with restriction to subtuples.
Read the pure-witness extension argument and why sufficiently large multiplicity structures preserve bounded obstructions before Ramsey purification.
remaining: Large-proof exception: 64-page uniform metatheorem. The route normalization/restriction compatibility and pure-witness extension were examined directly. Ramsey purification, effective cutoff and application encodings remain unverified, so this is not a complete theorem audit.
Audit full Ramsey purification, positive certificate completeness, computability of the global cutoff function and SNP encodings of applications. The 64-page metatheorem is not fully checked.

papers.authors: Sarita de Berg, Jacobus Conradi, Peter Kramer, André Nusser, Sampson Wong

review.title: A Sublinear Approximation Algorithm for Minimum Dilation Trees in the Plane
review.authors: Sarita de Berg, Jacobus Conradi, Peter Kramer, André Nusser, Sampson Wong
review.summary: For arbitrary n-point sets in the Euclidean plane, constructs a spanning tree whose maximum pairwise dilation is O(n^(14/15) log^3 n) times optimum, in O(n^5 log n) time. No bounded-spread or bounded-optimum assumption is needed. The ratio is sublinear in n; the running time is polynomial, not sublinear.
review.prior_frontier: The general-point-set benchmark was the MST with Theta(n) approximation, while known stronger algorithms assumed bounded spread or small optimum. The paper identifies Eppstein’s 1996 o(n)-approximation question as the motivation; historical attribution not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Breaks the linear approximation barrier for an established geometric spanning-tree problem with arbitrary spread.
score_reasons.novelty: Generalized circle and comb obstructions either certify large optimum or enforce a consistent hierarchy permitting a low-dilation tree.
score_reasons.depth: Uses weakly simple Delaunay supports, thin-polygon junction trees, interscale cutting, geometric packing and several simultaneous construction invariants.
score_reasons.exposition: The roadmap explains why naïve scale-by-scale connection fails and tracks the final exponent and polynomial runtime explicitly.

checked: Traced the circle obstruction: if every consecutive polygon-boundary pair had tree path shorter than 2R, those paths could be homotoped to boundary edges away from the enclosed disk center, contradicting contractibility of a closed walk in a tree.
Inspected junction-tree heavy-light spacing and Algorithm 1’s decreasing-scale cuts followed by increasing-scale connection.

Read the dilation induction and final arithmetic: locality confines paths to a radius O(Lambda^2 r log n) disk; packing controls finitely many large scales and n edges control the small-scale tail, yielding O(log^3 n max(n/Lambda,Lambda^14)); Lambda=max(6,n^(1/15)) balances them.
remaining: Central correctness still needs a full audit of comb obstructions, consistent junction sequences, good cuts and connectedness/locality/packedness invariants.
Need verify weakly simple degeneracies, compressed-scale properties and the geometric dependency hypotheses before certifying the main theorem.

review.summary: Constructs a strongly explicit constant-degree Kaufman–Oppenheim network family with deterministic polylogarithmic-round/local-computation self-routing for every permutation. review.prior_frontier: Earlier constant-degree fault-tolerant communication required global permutation preprocessing; this achieves routing from local information alone. The theorem is for the explicit network family, not arbitrary constant-degree expanders.

score_reasons.novelty: Robust product-set swap networks, algebraic voltage-lift coordinate routing and an iterative link-agreement compiler connect sorting to explicit HDXs.

checked: Traced the compiler’s final quantitative composition conditional on its simulation lemma: O(log(dT)) halvings reduce faults to |F|/(dT), and geometric input/output damage sums to O(|F|/d).
Checked that a constant overhead per compilation level preserves polylogarithmic complexity because the initial T is polylogarithmic and p is fixed.
remaining: Audit robust swap-network damage accounting, strongly explicit coordinate routing in the KO lift tower, and consistency/agreement under adaptive corrupted messages.
Verify the spectral/link hypotheses and that the same fault-set simulation supports repeated compiler composition.

checked: Checked the XOS set-intersection construction has expected intersection γ and union bound 2^(2γ)e^−2γ<1.

review.title: Learning vs. Optimizing Players in Budgeted Games
review.authors: Giannis Fikioris, Balasubramanian Sivan, Éva Tardos
review.area: Algorithmic game theory; online learning with budgets
review.summary: For repeated finite general games with bounded utility/cost matrices, null actions and full-information feedback of the learner’s utility/cost vector, gives a budget-feasible randomized learner with polynomial(T,n_L) per-round computation. Any adaptive optimizer earns at most the Budgeted Stackelberg benchmark times T plus O(sqrt(T)) with dimension/budget-rate factors; on piecewise iid intervals it obtains stochastic regret O(S n_L sqrt(T)/rho_L). A budgeted optimizer uses a two-phase benchmark and an additional inverse-budget factor. Does not promise adversarial no-regret or bandit feedback.
review.prior_frontier: Without budgets, swap regret controls manipulation. Prior budgeted-auction results used problem-specific pacing; this result covers general games with discontinuous mixed best responses. Cited prior benchmark/equilibrium results not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Extends non-manipulability and useful stochastic learning guarantees simultaneously to general budget-constrained games.
score_reasons.novelty: Separates response calibration from dual-weighted Lagrangian calibration, embedding continuous mixture weights as L2 step functions without exponentially many response buckets.
score_reasons.depth: Combines Hilbert-space calibration, budget LP duality, stochastic interval bounds and an explicit no-regret simulation for discontinuous forecast games.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states feedback, benchmark, null-action and budget-rate dependencies; distinguishes efficient polynomial computation from a practically cheap learner.

checked: Traced Theorem 4.2’s response-calibration reduction: group optimizer actions with the same observed utility/cost vector, bound their utility by a maximum of affine functions of the learner’s two-action mixture, extend to [-1,1], and apply the derivative/step-function inner product and Cauchy–Schwarz.
Read the four Lagrangian-calibration components and why lambda<=1/rho_L using the zero-cost null action.

Inspected the constructive forecast argument: response to an environment distribution f is the identical forecast f, making expected drift zero; projected gradient ascent yields a finite empirical forecast distribution without assuming continuity of the best-response map.
remaining: Budget feasibility and inactive-round concentration, full interval-regret proof, dynamic dictionary errors and budgeted-optimizer two-phase reduction still require audit.
Need check exact arithmetic/bit-complexity assumptions and polynomial forecast representation bound.

review.title: Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting
review.authors: Sofia de la Cerda, Aaron Potechin, Madhur Tulsiani, Jeff Xu
review.area: Random matrix theory; convex geometry; semidefinite programming
review.summary: Claims the sharp Gaussian centered-ellipsoid fitting threshold: for independent d-dimensional Gaussian points, a positive semidefinite fitting matrix exists with high probability for m<=(1-epsilon_d)d^2/4 and none exists for m>=(1+epsilon_d)d^2/4, with epsilon_d=1/poly(log log d). Gives explicit primal and dual witnesses via iterated spectral transformations and graph-matrix expansions. The model permits degenerate centered ellipsoids; the asymptotic slack is not optimized.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier cited results gave feasibility at c d^2 for unspecified small constant c and impossibility only beyond about d^2/2 by dimension counting. The d^2/4 conjecture is attributed to Saunderson–Chandrasekaran–Parrilo–Willsky; prior results have not been independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves both sides of a named sharp-threshold conjecture linking random geometry and SDP feasibility.
score_reasons.novelty: Replaces the identity-perturbation witness, which is insufficient near the threshold, with a nonlinear iterative construction and a corresponding dual refutation.
score_reasons.depth: Requires controlled inverse Gram expansions, free-independent graph-matrix shapes, semicircle polynomials and simultaneous truncation/error accounting.

checked: Inspected the precise Gaussian threshold and vanishing-slack qualification; the universality remark is not used in this screen’s main assessment.
Read the spectral map F(x)=max(2x,0), its semicircle normalization and the affine-correction iteration roadmap.
Traced the dual infeasibility criterion: Lambda=L*(y)>=0 with <Lambda,I-R><0 contradicts L(X)=1 and X>=0. Checked the objective calculation d-c_R*d/rho+o(delta*d) with c_R-rho=Theta(delta).

Read the final parameter balance D=t*=(log log d)^a, delta=D^-1/2, subpolynomial shape counts and the conditional conclusion that exact terminal correction o(delta) preserves the positive spectral floor.

papers.authors: Ashwin Nayak, Xingyu Zhou

review.title: Optimal Low-Rank Quantum State Tomography with Bounded-Sample Joint Measurements
review.authors: Ashwin Nayak, Xingyu Zhou

score_reasons.significance: A complete rank/block-size tradeoff settles several explicit tomography questions.
score_reasons.novelty: Support-varying uniform-spectrum ensembles and rank-sensitive Gaussian measurement analysis avoid a representation-theoretic route.
score_reasons.depth: Adaptive Fisher chain rules, van Trees localization and support/complement error control are substantial technical steps.
score_reasons.exposition: The measurement model, prior restrictions, concurrent results and matching parameter regimes are stated precisely.

checked: Checked the inverse-Lipschitz calculation for the projector chart: R_X has eigenvalues at least 16/17 and the correction term is at most one eighth of the trace-norm displacement.
Verified the displayed rate interpolates from dr^2/epsilon^2 at t=1 to dr/epsilon^2 at t=r^2, and inspected the exact adaptive-memory convention.
remaining: The Fisher trace bound for arbitrary joint POVMs, adaptive stopping/van Trees argument, and Gaussian estimator second-moment and complement analysis require full checking.

review.summary: Claims the optimal low-rank tomography sample rate Theta((dr/epsilon^2) max{1,r/sqrt(t)}) for measurements acting on at most t fresh copies, allowing classical adaptation and stopping between rounds.
review.prior_frontier: Closes rank-dependent adaptive and intermediate-block tradeoffs while recovering known full-rank bounds. The model retains only classical information between joint measurements; it is not a lower bound for arbitrary persistent quantum memory.

papers.title: Parallel Repetition for k-Player XOR Games
papers.authors: Mark Braverman, Dor Minzer

review.title: Parallel Repetition for k-Player XOR Games
review.authors: Mark Braverman, Dor Minzer
review.summary: Every fixed k-player XOR game over a prime field with classical value below one has exponentially decaying n-fold repeated value, with a game-dependent exponent and no restriction on the question distribution. States extension to all finite Abelian groups.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the reported earlier 3-player theorem by removing its no-integer-embedding assumption and allowing arbitrary k. Does not establish exponential repetition for all multiplayer games.

score_reasons.significance: Settles exponential parallel repetition for the full multiplayer XOR class, a major soundness-amplification frontier.
score_reasons.novelty: A BLR-style doubling transformation removes commuting embeddings, enabling ordered-contradiction Cauchy–Schwarz tensorization.
score_reasons.depth: Connects noncommutative perfect-game structure to a succinct but nontrivial tensorized analytic proof.
score_reasons.exposition: The main scope, classical value and group-dependent decay are explicit; key external noncommutative theorem requires careful tracing.

checked: Traced Claim 4.2’s lift from original strategies to the doubled game using ±α_i A_i and the common γ.
Checked the Fourier sum in Claim 4.1 conditional on Lemma 3.5: averaging (1−ε)^{number of nonzero characters} yields (1−ε(p−1)/p)^n.

Traced the BLR transformation and the complete no-commuting-embedding proof. On the cyclic subspace W, the D and E generators mutually commute across the two player copies, which transports the constraint from v to W. Varying one alpha makes E_i a representation of F_p; the constraints express each E_i using other players, forcing all E generators to commute. Since finitely many order-p generators act cyclically, W is finite dimensional and a joint eigenvector gives a forbidden perfect classical strategy.

Checked the direct proof of ordered-contradiction equivalence, rather than assuming the cited operator-algebra theorem: right multiplication defines the equivalence classes; left multiplication is well defined, bijective and commutes across players. The p distinct empty-word classes produce a nonzero phase-weighted vector with exactly the required eigenvalues.

Checked the gluing/lexicographic descent in Lemmas 3.3–3.4. Maximal reading sequences have a common noncrossing cancellation pairing. Copying the opening question to its paired closing position preserves a valid support challenge, cancels the second-copy words and preserves the nonzero signed right-hand side. At the first differing position both copies follow the smaller original reading sequence, so the finite integer potential strictly decreases.

Checked that the final zero-player game has two different right-hand sides: the inherited signs sum to zero from the last nonempty-player contradiction, while the signed right-hand side is nonzero. Thus every nontrivial prime-field character has expectation of modulus below one. Conditional Cauchy–Schwarz commutes with coordinate products; taking 2^T-th roots gives exponential decay in the number of nonzero Fourier coordinates.

Checked the final Fourier sum exactly: p^(−n) sum_a (1−epsilon)^|supp(a)| = (1−(p−1)epsilon/p)^n. The coordinatewise ±alpha strategy lifts every original winning tuple, establishing the claimed value comparison for all n.
remaining: The fully stated prime-field theorem is checked. The remark extending to arbitrary finite Abelian groups is not proved in detail in the manuscript and was not independently audited; Appendix A examples and historical priority were not checked.

review.title: Optimal Early-Stopping Broadcast via Exponential Information Gathering
review.authors: Giovanni Deligios, Fatima Elsheimy, Simon Holmgaard Kamp, Ivana Klasovita, Chen-Da Liu-Zhang, Julian Loss, Charalampos Papamanthou
review.summary: With plain PKI and strongly adaptive faults, early-stopping broadcast terminates in optimal min{f+2,t+1} rounds for t<n/2. For arbitrary t<n obtains 9f+7 rounds when f≥1. Both feasibility constructions use exponential communication/computation.
review.prior_frontier: Closes an exact round/termination gap in the honest-majority authenticated setting and achieves full resilience with linear actual-fault dependence; does not improve polynomial-communication protocols to these round bounds.

score_reasons.significance: Settles feasibility of optimal early stopping under authentication and removes a resilience restriction from linear-fault round bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: Conflict-cover stopping and consistent completion of missing signed reports replace honest-majority-at-every-EIG-node reasoning.
score_reasons.depth: Requires agreement between parties terminating at different depths and a separate transferable-evidence method without honest majority.
score_reasons.exposition: Makes exponential costs and decision-versus-termination distinctions explicit.

checked: Checked root threshold n−t−1 preserves validity and excludes at most t−1 faulty nonsenders when an honest party stops at round 2.
Read the conflict graph interpretation and leaf/internal-node consistency mechanism for later stopping parties.
remaining: Audit the complete output reconstruction, conflict-cover termination proof, strongly adaptive signature handling and the separate 9f+7 protocol.

papers.title: Solving Sparse SDPs in Sublinear Time: A Classical Algorithm Inspired by the Quantum OR Lemma
papers.authors: Fernando Brandao, Alexander Dalzell, Andras Gilyen, Francisca Vasconcelos

review.title: Solving Sparse SDPs in Sublinear Time: A Classical Algorithm Inspired by the Quantum OR Lemma
review.authors: Fernando G.S.L. Brandão, Alexander M. Dalzell, András Gilyén, Francisca Vasconcelos
review.summary: For sparse Hermitian SDPs with operator-norm-bounded data, strong duality and supplied primal trace/dual l1 bounds R,r, gives classical sparse-row-oracle solvers in soft-O(ns min{gamma^2,m,n/s} gamma^2.5+ms gamma^2), gamma=Rr/epsilon. In the bounded-radius constant-accuracy regime this is soft-O((n+m)s), with implicit approximate primal output and sparse dual descriptions. It removes the extra apparent quantum dimension speedup due to structured Gibbs-test reuse; it does not dequantize arbitrary unknown-state Quantum OR.
review.prior_frontier: Quoted classical solvers had soft-O(nm) dimension dependence versus quantum soft-O(sqrt(n)+sqrt(m)); low-rank/Frobenius-dependent dequantizations did not apply to generic full-rank sparse constraints. Historical bounds not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Achieves nearoptimal additive dimension dependence for an important generic sparse SDP model and narrows the dimensional quantum advantage to quadratic.
score_reasons.novelty: Classically reuses randomized Lanczos-filtered vectors across all sparse observables using an operator-norm-controlled shared-coordinate estimator, then makes both game players stochastic.
score_reasons.depth: Requires stable Gibbs-ratio estimates, Lanczos approximation, clipping, same-history coupling and high-probability regret analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully specifies sparse access, implicit output, radius/accuracy dependence and the limited sense in which Quantum OR is dequantized.

checked: Traced the coordinate estimator Z=Re((A psi)_I/psi_I) with I sampled from |psi_I|^2: cancellation gives unbiasedness and second moment <=||A psi||^2. Zero coordinates are never sampled, and clipping introduces bias <=R^2||A||^2/B.
Inspected the shared Gibbs estimator’s median-of-ratios construction and the game/target-value binary-search recovery, including epsilon/r constraint violation.
Read how the direct MMWU solver yields gamma^6.5 dependence and why the two-sided stochastic algorithm aims to improve this to gamma^4.5.
remaining: Need audit Lanczos relative-error conditions, unnormalized random-filter moment bounds, ratio estimator stability and the coupled stochastic regret proof.
Essential prior rank-one regret theorem, high-probability runtime/bit model and dimension lower-bound comparisons have not yet been checked.

review.title: PPAD Hardness from SIS
review.authors: Arka Rai Choudhuri
review.summary: Constructs average-case hard PPAD instances (indeed EOML/CLS) from either polynomially hard SIS with norm bound 2^{O(log³n)} plus a structured fine-grained average-case assumption, or SIS of norm and adversary-size scale 2^{n^{1/3}} alone. Uses unambiguous incrementally updatable SNARGs for succinct regular tree circuits.
review.prior_frontier: Prior cited LWE-based PPAD hardness required polynomial LWE plus fine-grained average-case hardness. This changes to SIS, which is not known to imply public-key encryption; it is not hardness from polynomial SIS alone.

score_reasons.significance: Broadens the cryptographic foundations of average-case total-search hardness to a different lattice assumption.
score_reasons.novelty: Mergeable functional commitments preserve uniqueness while supporting incremental proofs of exponentially large structured circuits.
score_reasons.depth: Requires tight norm growth, computation-time versus unambiguity-security separation and a multiscale hard-puzzle reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: The two assumptions and the need to recompute honest states within a security budget are carefully distinguished.

checked: Inspected the RSVL template and checked the parallel-puzzle clock invariant in Claim 4.1; polynomially many succinct components preserve polynomial successor/verifier size.
Verified that the fine-grained assumption is additional and the SIS-alone theorem uses subexponential hardness and specified larger norms.
remaining: Audit commitment merging, proof-state uniqueness, norm recurrences and all security-parameter changes.
Trace the false-positive reduction’s recomputation cost and the subexponential-SIS hard-computation instantiation.

review.title: Sharp Bounds on Ground State Energy of the SYK Model
review.authors: Arpon Basu, Pravesh K. Kothari, Siddhant Midha

review.prior_frontier: Closes an O(k) spectral-edge gap and confirms a physics prediction in the growing-k regime. Fixed-k sharp constants require separate work; the algorithm takes n^O(k), not uniformly polynomial time for growing k.

score_reasons.significance: Gives sharp spectral-edge information for a central random quantum model and calibrates quantum algorithms against its true optimum.
score_reasons.novelty: Represents all expected trace moments exactly by one deterministic twisted-bosonic operator, then compares its spectral behavior through Johnson-scheme structure.
score_reasons.depth: Must retain dependent chord-crossing correlations rather than assuming a q-deformed product heuristic, and control high moments and lower-tail witnesses.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully separates fixed versus growing locality and expectation versus concentration; the technical overview explains the failed heuristic.

checked: Checked normalized trace-moment upper-bound conversion with Hilbert dimension 2^(n/2).
Read exact chord dependence and Johnson-scheme matrix identity; inspected the Hilbert-valued Gaussian hypercontractive extension through scalar norm domination.
remaining: Audit the twisted-bosonic moment identity, Johnson eigenvalue bounds, lower bound test vector, sparse hypergraph concentration and algorithmic dependency.

review.title: Irreducibility for Topical Maps
review.authors: Brian Lins
review.summary: Organizes facial/graphical irreducibility, indecomposability, partial irreducibility and imperturbability for continuous order-preserving homogeneous maps of the nonnegative cone preserving its interior. Proves equivalences under multiplicative convexity or subadditivity, and translates boundary-signature and local uniqueness conditions into SAT instances. This supplies certification encodings, not a polynomial-time algorithm for arbitrary such maps.

score_reasons.depth: Uses cone boundary limits, multiplicative convexity, invariant faces and support-based eigenvector arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions, implication diagrams and concrete SAT clauses make the scope and stronger hypotheses easy to inspect.

checked: Traced Theorem 2.4: facial/graphical irreducibility imply indecomposability, multiplicative convexity turns finite singleton growth into finite subset growth, and subadditivity relates boundary support to divergence.

Inspected the SAT witness for non-imperturbability: nonzero x, y!=1, support(x) subset support(y), lower_signature(x)>=x and upper_signature(y)<=y. Tseitin transformation applies once formulas for signatures are supplied.
Read the scaling/comparison proof of sufficient uniqueness at a known eigenvector and the local-signature composition rules.
remaining: No full audit of all signature composition/representation assumptions or the recalled nonlinear Perron–Frobenius dependencies.
No solver experiments or generic efficient representation theorem claimed/verified.

review.title: The Authentication Complexity of Byzantine Consensus
review.authors: Kecheng Shi
review.summary: Characterizes directed initial public-key authentication graphs supporting synchronous Byzantine agreement via a three-set condition. For 2t<n≤3t, agreement needs Θ(min{n²,(n²/(n−2t))ln(en/(n−2t))}) bindings. Gives broadcast bounds and exact (n choose 2)−1 cost at t=n−1.
review.prior_frontier: Extends no-PKI/full-PKI resilience thresholds to arbitrary partially authenticated key tables; broadcast and agreement costs separate near n=2t+1. The cost counts initial bindings, not messages or authentication learned during execution.

score_reasons.significance: Determines a natural authentication resource tradeoff, including a tight agreement characterization and costs.
score_reasons.novelty: A three-set graph obstruction and setup-sensitive key propagation connect resilience to extremal directed graph design.
score_reasons.depth: Necessity simulations, efficient sufficiency and extremal constructions/lower bounds are all substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Models local key knowledge, designated keys, and agreement-versus-broadcast distinctions explicitly.

checked: Verified that the three-set condition is vacuous when n>3t and that the stated formula interpolates linear cost for a fixed fault fraction below one half and quadratic cost at r=O(log n).
Inspected the necessity simulation’s key assignment: absence of a signer verified in both A and B permits the two-view key splice.
remaining: Audit the full indistinguishability execution construction, three-set sufficiency with only local key tables, and polynomial computation/round bound.
Check extremal graph bounds, broadcast near-half construction and the exact maximum-resilience count.

checked: Checked the Metropolis good-set reduction: P(P/Q>M)=δ implies Q(bad)≤δ/M and acceptance at least (1−δ)/M on the good set.
Checked uniform first O(log n) signs cost a polynomial density ratio and that stored proposal choices must remain fixed across sampling and density evaluation.

score_reasons.novelty: Uses a resource-sensitive simulation definition and efficient fixed-channel realizations for two established protocols.
score_reasons.depth: Combines local wirings, PR-box equality computation, masking and bitwise equivocation over characteristic-two fields.

remaining: No full audit of the foundational channel-computability/timing definition, composition against arbitrary allowed verifier channels, or the cited local/entangled soundness and repetition dependencies.

review.title: SNARGs from any Witness Encryption, and More

score_reasons.novelty: Canonicalizes witnesses using NIZK and replaces universal EF correctness with local cryptographic proof steps.

score_reasons.depth: Matching lower bounds must realize moment measures by entire unitary ensembles; Fourier smoothing and entropy control add substantial analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly warns that the design hypothesis is stronger than standard design results and separates TV from Kolmogorov claims.

checked: Checked the two-regime equivalence min(√N/k,1/√k)=Theta(k^(-1/2)(1+k/N)^(-1/2)) and the atom-based Kolmogorov lower-bound mechanism.

remaining: Audit quadrature comparison, embedding into strong designs, relative-error transfer, TV smoothing and entropy estimates; verify the external strong-design theorem and parameter range.

review.summary: For finite metrics with instantaneous movement and maximum waiting time charged separately for each service batch, deterministic polynomial-time competitive ratios are 10 on lines, 12 on weighted trees and 20 on arbitrary metrics. Elective and automatic service have identical offline optima; blind-location service on a known finite line admits ratio 84. This is a changed delay objective, not an improvement for ordinary additive-delay service.
review.prior_frontier: Introduces a mobile-server extension of prior per-batch maximum-delay rooted aggregation. The manuscript contrasts additive-delay online service; those prior bounds were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Constant competitive algorithms on all finite metrics for a distinct batching objective are substantial specialist progress.
score_reasons.novelty: The ordered-window certificate and parity split account for server endpoints and offline rebatching.
score_reasons.depth: Core normalization and twofold movement charging are short; line and hidden-location implementations add geometry and amortization.
score_reasons.exposition: The definitions, normalization, certificate and MST nonmonotonicity example make the model and proof readable.

checked: Screening traced normalization: adjacent batches merge whenever the later earliest arrival precedes the first service, decreasing summed delay; this yields complete consecutive arrival blocks. Automatic simulation serves premature parked arrivals at zero delay.

Certificate proof charges interior arrival-window groups to batch delay and all other group spans to at most two traversals per movement segment. Tree endpoint augmentation and odd/even windows produce ratio 12. Running maximum terminal-MST/2 is bounded by final Steiner cost and gives phase cost at most five certificates, hence ratio 20.
remaining: The sharper line interval inequalities, full blind-feedback implementation, offline dynamic programs and lower bounds have not received a correctness audit.

checked: Checked quality-preserving normalization preserves all blocking comparisons and personal rank caps, but does not preserve unrelated edge rewards.
Traced Lemma 4.1: simultaneous wrong-active classes or two same-class own-active sources force a strict blocking pair; inspected why two boundary identities and delayed guards are retained.
remaining: Audit every batch transition and anonymous-token reconstruction, common-order interval completion, independent reward gap reductions and parameterized weighted history merging.

papers.title: Distributed Quantum Certification with Clifford Encoders
papers.authors: Hyunho Cha, Jungwoo Lee

review.title: Distributed Quantum Certification with Clifford Encoders
review.authors: Hyunho Cha, Jungwoo Lee
review.summary: Private-coin simultaneous quantum communication with one d-dimensional input copy per sender, r-dimensional quantum messages, no shared randomness/entanglement and no classical side channel admits optimal worst-case certification sample complexity Theta(d^3/(r^2 epsilon^2)). Fixed universal Clifford compressions suffice with at most 6d^2/r^2 settings. Rank-k reference upper bound is O(k^3/(min(r,k)^2 epsilon^2)), with a matching worst-case lower bound at each k>=2. Rank reduction itself is an arbitrary channel, not necessarily Clifford.
review.prior_frontier: Claims removal of sqrt(log d) sample and log d setting losses relative to CDSW26. Existing arbitrary-channel lower bound is cited, not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Closes logarithmic losses for a sharply specified communication model rather than changing the leading polynomial exponent.
score_reasons.novelty: Repairing ordinary subspace covers into symplectically nondegenerate covers achieves a fixed Clifford schedule at constant overhead.
score_reasons.depth: The finite-geometry expectation/repair argument and collective quadratic-distance estimator provide a substantive but relatively concise route.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit constants, arbitrary-channel versus Clifford distinctions and computational limitations are transparent.

checked: Screening traced E|rad(W)|<3 for uniformly placed subspaces and repair cost f(t)=2^(t/2)+1. One common GL coordinate change preserves coverage; linearity of expectation and Markov give <=6*2^(N-k) nondegenerate members. This coordinate change is only preprocessing, not a claimed Clifford.

Pauli-coordinate coverage yields sum ||Phi_i(T)||_2^2 >= (d/r)||T||_2^2. The swap-based U-statistic variance is <=4D/s+64/s^2; with s=ceil(128d/epsilon^2), independent blocks and Chebyshev give error <=7/32 and the 774 sample constant.
remaining: Ordinary-cover construction, rank-support leakage reduction and external lower-bound applicability are not fully audited. No polynomial-in-qubit-count construction or efficient collective referee measurement is claimed.

checked: Inspected the reduction from interlacing to the largest nontrivial root and removal of the trivial eigenvalue factor in the matching model.

review.title: An exponential separation between entanglement-assisted and unassisted one-way quantum communication
review.authors: Ryan Anselm, Srijita Kundu, Olivier Lalonde, Ashwin Nayak
review.summary: Exhibits total Boolean functions on n-bit inputs with O(log n) entanglement-assisted one-way classical communication, but Θ(n^{1/3}) unassisted one-way quantum and randomized communication at worst-case error 1/3. The upper bound uses Θ(n) shared EPR pairs; an entanglement-assisted SMP variant also exists.
review.prior_frontier: First claimed asymptotic entanglement advantage over unassisted quantum communication for total functions in the one-way setting; prior separations involved relations or restricted SMP partial functions.

score_reasons.significance: Establishes an exponential resource separation for total functions resolving a longstanding communication question.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines bounded-order subgroup membership with total shifted equality and noncommutative group representation lower bounds.
score_reasons.depth: Requires matrix-moment analysis and a precise Heisenberg-group instantiation supporting the quantum lower bound.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully separates totality, prior entanglement, one-way versus SMP models and the amount of shared entanglement.

checked: Verified shifted equality has no promise on no-instances, so the constructed function is total.

Traced final parameter conversion conditional on Theorems 5.2/6.1: input length Θ(2^{3r}), lower bound Ω(2^r), assisted cost Θ(r), and Θ(2^{3r}) EPR pairs; surjective decoding preserves the lower bound.
remaining: The 44-page communication separation has a checked total-function interpretation and final parameter reduction. Its subgroup protocol and matrix-moment lower bound remain essential unchecked components; this is a scoped large-proof exception.

Check padding for every input length and the SMP protocol/entanglement model separately.

review.title: Sounder, shorter, and simpler PCPs from HDX neighborhoods
review.authors: Yotam Dikstein, Irit Dinur, Max Hopkins, Noah G. Singer
review.summary: Two-query PCP/Label Cover reduction of size n(log n)^C and soundness ε>(log n)^(-a), with alphabet exp((1/ε)^C), from new fixed-dimensional neighborhood agreement tests of total length n poly(1/ε) and poly(1/ε)-size views.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier HDX constructions had quasi-linear exponents depending on fixed soundness and required fault-tolerant routing. The alphabet may dominate a downstream hardness reduction and is not claimed constant.

score_reasons.significance: Improves the length-versus-small-soundness frontier of a central PCP primitive, with wide hardness-of-approximation consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Neighborhood views replace growing-dimensional faces; dense cluster list matching handles exponentially longer lists and avoids fault-tolerant routing.
score_reasons.depth: Combines local list decoding, cluster-support sampling, triangle-consistent matchings, coboundary expansion and alphabet reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates PCP length and alphabet costs and supplies a detailed proof roadmap, although the 74-page dependency chain remains substantial.

checked: Checked the exact theorem range and retained the exp((1/ε)^C) alphabet cost.
Inspected why naive low-support pruning fails: per-function ε^481 support is below the ε^37 unexplained mass; clustered support restores the cross-list overlap needed for matching.

Traced the central cluster-core stabilization and two-way restriction argument (Lemma 4.3, Proposition 4.5, Lemma 3.7). A failed scale adds Omega(epsilon^12) genuinely new support; splitting indices modulo3 gives at most27 epsilon^-12 bad scales among400 epsilon^-24.

Checked the essential replacement of exponentially many cluster events by polynomially many disjoint exclusive-support events: m=O(epsilon^-443), individual additive error epsilon^481, aggregate O(epsilon^38)<=epsilon^37, failure O(lambda^2 epsilon^-1405); pairwise distance sampling contributes lambda^2 rho0^-2 epsilon^-886.

Checked both directions of cluster transfer: intersection epsilon^500 divided by list size yields Omega(epsilon^943)>epsilon^1000, diameter expands by at most7rho0, and unexplained passing mass plus discarded intersections fit the100 epsilon^37 support slack. Stability then returns to the selected core lists with O(rho0 epsilon^-24) distance.
remaining: Large-proof exception:73-page PCP/HDX development; the central clustered list-pruning proof was traced, but no end-to-end PCP correctness certification is claimed.
The upstream list-decoding and link-sampling lemmas, triangle consistency, KMS complex instantiation, routing, and final alphabet-reduction/length/error parameter chain remain unchecked.
The epsilon-dependent alphabet exponential in (1/epsilon)^C and sufficiently small epsilon/spectral expansion assumptions must be retained.

papers.title: Sublinear Copies Suffice for Fidelity Estimation with Pauli Measurements
papers.authors: Abhilash Dharmavarapu, Jayadev Acharya, Nengkun Yu, Yuhan Liu

review.title: Sublinear Copies Suffice for Fidelity Estimation with Pauli Measurements
review.authors: Jayadev Acharya, Abhilash Dharmavarapu, Yuhan Liu, Nengkun Yu
review.summary: Uniform independent full-weight Pauli-basis measurements estimate Tr(rho sigma) for every known target density matrix rho with O(d^a epsilon^-2 log(1/delta)) copies, a=lambda+(1-lambda)log_2(3)/2=0.967434151..., lambda=(1+sqrt(33))/8. The Pauli shadow norm squared is bounded by d^a ||rho||_2^2. Fidelity interpretation requires pure target. Distributed unknown-state estimation additionally has a (sqrt(7.5))^N/epsilon term, so the sublinear dependence applies only in the high-precision regime.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the stated general O(d/epsilon^2) Pauli measurement guarantee for all target states through a sharper analysis of the existing classical-shadows protocol. Prior-frontier history not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: A worst-case sublinear sample guarantee for every target under single-qubit Pauli measurements breaks the previously stated linear barrier.
score_reasons.novelty: Reduces the shadow second moment to a Pauli-compatibility graph and dominates its noise kernel by two-bit Boolean noise.
score_reasons.depth: Combines a precise PSD comparison, hypercontractivity and depolarizing-channel output-norm multiplicativity; the proof is compact but nontrivial.
score_reasons.exposition: The estimator and proof chain are explicit; some extracted notation is misleading, requiring rendered-page checks. High-precision restriction is explicit in the full distributed theorem.

checked: Traced unbiasedness by 3^(N-weight) basis multiplicities and the second-moment expansion over compatible Pauli pairs; Holder with exponents 2/(1+gamma),2/(1-gamma) gives the E_gamma/W_gamma split.

Verified the graph kernel C is PSD with eigenvalues 0,3/4,3/4,1; the exact two-dimensional principal-minor calculation yields p=(7-sqrt(33))/16 and BSC_p tensor BSC_p >= C. Tensorization applies because both matrices are PSD. A numerical independent eigenspectrum check corroborated the algebra (not a substitute for it).

At gamma=lambda, Boolean hypercontractivity on 2N bits gives E_lambda <=(4/3)^N 4^(N(lambda-1)/(1+lambda)) ||rho||_2^(4/(1+lambda)). Retaining this purity factor before the Holder power gives the asserted ||rho||_2^2 dependence.

Counted W_gamma by symmetric-difference support: (10/3)^N times weighted coefficient norm. King Theorem 3 applies at Schatten p=2 to the depolarizing channel with parameter 1/sqrt(5), whose one-qubit maximum purity is 3/5. Verified the original theorem and channel parameter range at arXiv quant-ph/0204172 PDF pp2,8.

Combining powers yields exponent 0.9674341512698683<0.9675, which justifies little-o(d^0.9675). Chebyshev and median amplification give the sample guarantee. Rendered PDF p3 confirms robust-certification thresholds are 1-epsilon/C versus 1-epsilon, not the overlapping thresholds produced by text extraction.
remaining: The secondary distributed-inner-product corollary imports the 7.5^N cross-shadow second-moment bound from HWX26; that external bound was not independently audited.
Prior-work chronology and practical classical postprocessing time are not verified. This is a main-proof mathematical check, not formal verification.
