papers.title: Ruling out Fast Approximation Algorithms for Clique, Biclique, Collinearity, and Arithmetic Progressions
papers.authors: Reina Itakura, Karthik C.S., Mayank Motwani, Gary Peng

review.title: Ruling out Fast Approximation Algorithms for Clique, Biclique, Collinearity, and Arithmetic Progressions
review.authors: Reina Itakura, Karthik C. S., Mayank Motwani, Gary Peng
review.summary: Under fixed 3-uniform hyperclique hypotheses, rules out near-linear algorithms for gap clique, biclique, planar collinearity and integer arithmetic-progression detection. Precise clique theorem uses b edge/triangle pieces of K_h and a b-hyperclique hypothesis, giving M^{b/(b−1)−ε}; biclique gives M^{2h/(2h−1)−ε}, collinearity N^{h/(h−1)−ε}.
review.prior_frontier: Provides gap-creation tools for constant-factor fine-grained approximation. Soundness excludes K₄ or four collinear points, so the original triangle/three-collinear soundness questions are not fully resolved.

score_reasons.significance: Establishes conditional superlinear barriers for four natural gap problems, with precise but modest exponent gaps.
score_reasons.novelty: A covering-disperser framework preserves local consistency while amplifying clique-style promises and supports geometric embeddings.
score_reasons.depth: Requires extremal set systems, sparse threshold graphs and deterministic collinearity-preserving projection.
score_reasons.exposition: The full theorem corrects the parameter shorthand in the abstract and explicitly states limitations of the gap amplification.

checked: Checked the biclique exponent conversion from M=O_h(n^{h−1/2}) to the h-hyperclique n^h threshold.
Inspected the high-dimensional collinearity map and the random-projection/no-new-collinearities argument; the formal deterministic construction remains unchecked.
remaining: Audit covering-disperser consistency, exact graph output sizes and the threshold-graph construction.

Check deterministic projection, polynomial coordinate bounds and arithmetic-progression transfer; independently assess only the stated hyperclique assumptions, not the paper’s commentary on other hypotheses.

papers.title: Hamiltonicity of mildly pseudorandom regular graphs
papers.authors: Alp Muyesser

review.title: Hamiltonicity of mildly pseudorandom regular graphs
review.authors: Alp Müyesser
review.summary: An (n,d,λ)-graph with λ≤(1−δ)d and d≥C δ^(-6)(log n)^3 is Hamiltonian. Uses random bipartite spectral inheritance, Haxell connections, constant-layer Hamilton routers and robust Hall matchings.
review.prior_frontier: Improves a recent much larger polylogarithmic degree threshold for mildly expanding regular graphs. The result is existential; the paper explicitly does not supply an algorithm under the same bound.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial quantitative simplification of Hamiltonicity in weak spectral expanders, including subconstant gaps.
score_reasons.novelty: Recombines spectral sampling and router methods rather than introducing the qualitative Hamiltonicity criterion.
score_reasons.depth: The probabilistic partition must simultaneously support vertex-disjoint routing and perfect matchings after reservoir redistribution.
score_reasons.exposition: Short and largely modular, but the final divisibility reduction is only sketched and prevents a complete verification here.

checked: Traced the two-step matrix Bernstein sampling calculation, conditioning binomial sampling on fixed size and the resulting spectral slack.

Traced Haxell connecting lemma via expander pruning, its multiplicity/degree bounds and all absolute-constant inequalities. Checked comparator pairing, short even-cycle packing and the robust Hall lemma.

Traced the main theorem conditional on the stated divisibility hypotheses: δ^4 d/log²n gives the required δ^(-2)log n sampled degree, and redistributed layers satisfy the robust Hall degree conditions.
remaining: The final theorem removes divisibility by an unspecified short-path contraction. It does not explain how contraction preserves the regular spectral input or how to arrange k divides n−|S| before the router S is known. This reduction needs a rigorous argument or an unequal-layer replacement.
Independently verify the external basic-router Proposition 4.4 and standard cited matrix/Haxell/Moore results.
issues: Proof of Theorem 1.3, PDF p.12: divisibility removal by short-path contraction is not justified for the regular spectral model, and k|(n−|S|) depends on a later router. This is an unclosed verification gap, not a demonstrated false theorem.
Minor repairable typo in comparator proof p.9: the first cycle matching should pair c0 with c1, not c2.

papers.title: Improved Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing and Worst-Case Optimal Polynomial Intersection
papers.authors: Yihang Sun, Mary Wootters

review.title: Improved Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing and Worst-Case Optimal Polynomial Intersection
review.authors: Yihang Sun, Mary Wootters
review.area: Coding theory, leakage-resilient cryptography and quantum algorithms
review.summary: Over prime fields and arbitrary distinct evaluation points, Shamir sharing of fixed rate R>1/2 tolerates any fixed b bits of local leakage; one-bit leakage is exponentially small for R>1/2-delta for an absolute delta>0, including arbitrary biases. For worst-case density-rho OPI lists supplied through coherent membership oracles, quantum poly(n,log p) time reaches SCL_rho(R)-epsilon and perfect satisfaction if R+rho>1. Separate existential discrepancy results extend beyond these algorithmic regimes; random evaluations require log p=n^Omega(1). An ordinary, unfolded OPI oracle separation uses vanishing 1/polylog(n) rate and quasipolynomial fields.
review.prior_frontier: Claims improvement from arbitrary-bias one-bit LLR rate 0.668 to below 1/2 and from Johnson-radius SCL_rho(1-sqrt(1-R)) to SCL_rho(R) for quantum OPI. Explicitly acknowledges concurrent similar LLR results by Nguyen and random-evaluation work by Hwang–Maji–Shkredov–Ye. Historical and new capacity list-recovery dependencies not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Breaks an identified leakage threshold and connects it to improved worst-case quantum algorithms and coding discrepancy guarantees.
score_reasons.novelty: A common centered Fourier framework, weighted dual-code thresholding and retained phases below rate 1/2 support several distinct advances.
score_reasons.depth: The 82-page argument combines capacity list recovery, MDS Gowers inequalities, conditioned quantum distributions, coherent preparation and a separate oracle-hardness encoding.
score_reasons.exposition: The phase diagrams and seven-step overview distinguish existential from algorithmic bounds and random from arbitrary evaluation points; numerous essential dependencies need careful checking.

checked: Traced Lemma 1.17 weighted Fourier thresholding: heavy lists have bounded size via L2 mass; dual list recovery controls heavy-agreement codewords by poly(n)*gamma^k. For the remaining words choose support T and sigma*n light positions, then two disjoint information sets of size t-k in the shortened MDS code. Cauchy–Schwarz and projection bijections give theta^(sigma n)(1+Gamma)^(t-k), and at most 3^n choices are absorbed by choosing theta. The requirement 2k-t=Omega(n) is used explicitly.

Traced Lemma 2.10: partition coordinates outside J into three blocks of size <=k-|J|, use kernel-invariance to apply Cauchy–Schwarz three times, and use MDS surjectivity to make all three increments independent and uniform on F_p^J. The resulting U3 norm factors as a product over J.

Read the elementary U3 gap for balanced sign functions: a nonzero Fourier coefficient bound c<1 and Parseval applied to f and multiplicative derivatives yield ||f||_U3^8 <=1-(1-c^2)^2(1-(1-2tau)^2)<1. Its prerequisite Fourier coefficient bound was not rederived.

Checked the balanced below-half composition: low supports <=floor((2-delta)k) are exponentially controlled by thresholding; high supports contribute entropy H2(5delta/2-delta^2) plus (1/2-3delta)log2(q), negative for sufficiently small fixed delta.
remaining: Full correctness is not established. The essential recent arbitrary-evaluation GRS capacity list-recovery/list-decoding theorems and the MPCSW21 test criterion have not been checked against their original sources.

Arbitrary-bias conditioning/Brascamp–Lieb Appendix A, the full OPI discrepancy and conditioned-DQI analysis, efficient coherent preparation/erasure of decoding lists, perfect-satisfaction truncation, random-evaluation universality and classical oracle-hardness encodings remain unchecked.
Only the specified central thresholding/MDS cancellation components were traced; their correctness does not establish all seven main result families.

review.title: Revisiting the XOR lemma

review.summary: Refutes the 1995 dream XOR lemma as stated: constructs a function with very small correlation against a chosen class while its even-fold XOR has unexpectedly large correlation with a quadratic polynomial. review.prior_frontier: Separates an impossible near-lossless conjecture from valid XOR lemmas; improves the stated γ² size loss to γ in an appropriate parameterization. This does not refute the standard XOR lemma.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a longstanding hardness-amplification conjecture negatively and improves a fundamental tool’s quantitative proof.
score_reasons.novelty: Fixed-point-free involutions in Maiorana–McFarland functions yield a quadratic XOR witness; randomized-threshold reconstruction avoids estimating two-copy correlation.
score_reasons.depth: A compact mix of matching concentration, Fourier structure and elementary amplification gives nontrivial bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The counterexample and positive results are clearly distinguished, though a displayed absolute-value bound needs a minor correction.

checked: Traced the quadratic witness for fπ(x,y)=x·π(y): averaging over x,x′ makes correlation exactly Pr[y′=π(y)]=2^{−n/2}.

review.title: Optimal Tolerant Testing of Lindbladian Dissipation
review.authors: Jinge Bao, Yiyi Cai, Zhong-Xia Shang
review.area: Quantum property testing and open-system dynamics
review.summary: For bounded-diamond-strength time-independent Lindbladians on n qubits with an arbitrary unknown Hamiltonian and a representation by traceless k-local jump operators (fixed k, unrestricted support overlap), tolerant testing of canonical-dissipator normalized Frobenius strength <=epsilon1 versus >=epsilon2 has optimal total forward-evolution time Theta_k(epsilon2/(epsilon2-epsilon1)^2), for epsilon2<=Lambda/sqrt(2). The model allows arbitrarily short memoryless calls, ancillas and joint measurements, and charges only summed interaction time.
review.prior_frontier: Extends Cai26 non-tolerant Theta(1/epsilon) testing to positive acceptance thresholds and removes bounded jump-overlap degree. Historical claims and prior theorem have not been independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the threshold dependence of tolerant dissipation testing without system-size dependence under constant locality.
score_reasons.novelty: Jump-state functional estimation retains information erased by Pauli twirling, with a support-discovery and aggregate-estimation method.
score_reasons.depth: The dimension-free candidate omission and U-statistic covariance bounds handle unknown, arbitrarily overlapping jump supports; state preparation and adaptive lower bounds add nontrivial analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: The cost model and locality assumptions are explicit, and the norm identity separates rate from structure clearly.

checked: Screening traced the claimed decomposition ||D||_F=Gamma*sqrt(1+h(sigma)) with h=Tr sigma^2+(d Tr sigma_R^2-1)/2 and the need to estimate the dimension-amplified marginal purity.

Read candidate discovery proof: pairwise unions of Bell/Pauli-vector supports yield <=16^k m^2 candidates. Positivity bounds local matrix entries by w(P)*p_Q, omitted paired labels cost exp(-mp_Q), and x exp(-mx)<=1/(em) yields expected lost squared coefficient mass O_k(1/m).

Read conditional U-statistic variance: sigma_R<=2^k I/d compares measurement moments to the maximally mixed state, giving covariance <=6^k I and variance O_k(1/N+m^2/N^2). With m=O_k(delta^-1), N=O_k(delta^-2), global purity SWAP tests complete the functional estimator.
remaining: Canonical norm identity and locality marginal bound, finite-time flagged-output approximation, two-stage rate test with fixed total time, copy lower bound and adaptive Poisson-record lower bound remain unaudited.
The interaction-time guarantee alone does not establish small query count or efficient total gate/measurement complexity.

review.title: When Masks Leak Their Weight: From Additive Sharing to Learning with Physical Rounding
review.authors: Aniruddha Biswas, Jihun Hwang, Hemanta K. Maji, Ilya D. Shkredov, Xiuyu Ye
review.summary: For additive sharing modulo N with |N−2^n|≤2^n/n, fixed k≥3 shares hide secrets against Hamming-weight leakage with advantage O_k(n^{−k/2+5/4}), even with the final share exposed. Two shares are insecure for every modulus. Gives batch-fixed masked LWPR simulation and sharper Mersenne estimates.
review.prior_frontier: Improves prior prime-exponent Mersenne bounds O_k(n^{−k/4+1}) requiring at least five shares; removes primality and extends near powers of two. The exponent’s k coefficient is tight, not every remaining power of n.

score_reasons.significance: Reduces the sharing threshold and broadens arithmetic scope for a concrete side-channel leakage model.
score_reasons.novelty: Bernoulli-doubling Fourier estimates replace exact rotation symmetry; transference controls near-dyadic boundary errors without a crude per-share union bound.
score_reasons.depth: Combines generating-function spectral analysis, matching lower bounds and composition-aware leakage simulation.
score_reasons.exposition: Precisely separates worst-case leakage, averaged sum leakage and fixed-before-preprocessing input batches.

checked: Checked the contraction/base-case exponent n^{−(k−2)/2}n^{1/4}=n^{−k/2+5/4}.
Checked that the stated transference terms are smaller powers n^{−k/2+3/4} and n^{−k/2+1/2}; for four shares the square-root composition term permits V=o(n).
remaining: Audit Bernoulli-orbit spectral estimate, generating-function integrals and transference lemma constants uniformly in the modulus.
Check lower-bound constructions and full LWPR simulation, especially preprocessing dependence and the stipulated nonadaptive batch inputs.

review.title: Learning quantum symmetries
review.authors: Isaac Holt, Sathyawageeswar Subramanian
review.summary: Extends state hidden-subgroup learning to normal cores and specified nonabelian group families; introduces projective anyonic symmetry learning through self-orthogonal-code linearisations. General formal algorithms depend inversely on a minimum asymmetry gap and require efficient QFT/controlled representations.
review.prior_frontier: Previous general StateHSP algorithms covered abelian groups. The normal-core sample count uses minimal quotient subgroups rather than all group elements. The advertised arbitrary mixed-state stabilizer corollary omits an essential gap dependence.

score_reasons.significance: The symmetry framework and projective-representation extension are substantial, but the unconditional mixed-state application is overstated.
score_reasons.novelty: Relates linearisation matrices to self-orthogonal codes and improves normal-core sampling through minimal subgroup obstructions.
score_reasons.depth: Uses nonabelian Fourier analysis, central extensions, code constructions and group-specific efficient implementations.
score_reasons.exposition: General theorems state gap/oracle assumptions, but the main application fails to carry them through and several elementary statements need qualification.

checked: Checked HSP-to-BoseSL using the graph state and right-regular action, and the linearisation cocycle cancellation condition M M^T=0.

Constructed an information-theoretic counterexample to Theorem 9.27 as stated: ρ=|0^n><0^n| and ση=(1−η)ρ+ηI/2^n have different exact stabilizers, but trace distance of T copies is at most Tη. No uniform poly(n)-time/copy algorithm distinguishes them for arbitrarily small η.
Theorem 9.17 explicitly includes 1/ε asymmetry-gap dependence, so its omission in Theorem 9.27 is substantive.
remaining: Determine a corrected gap-dependent stabilizer statement and audit the general normal-core and projective algorithms.
Check the claimed amplified minimum asymmetry gap in Theorem 9.17 and repair Lemma 9.6 to restrict row scalings to invertible operations.
issues: Theorem 9.27 is false as a uniform poly(n)-time exact-learning statement for arbitrary mixed states: arbitrarily near states can have different exact stabilizer groups. General gap-dependent results are not thereby refuted.
Lemma 9.6 says arbitrary scalar row multiplication preserves standard-form condition M*: multiplication by zero is an immediate counterexample; invertible scalars are needed.

review.title: When are bosonic Gaussian states classical to learn?
review.authors: Senrui Chen, Antonio Anna Mele, Francesco Anna Mele, John Preskill
review.summary: For n-mode Gaussian states with covariance Sigma >= (1/2+nu)I, single-copy, possibly adaptive tomography to epsilon trace distance has tight complexity Theta(n^2 epsilon^-2 min(n,1+nu^-1)); nonadaptive heterodyne measurements attain it. Cold passive states with covariance <=(1/2+O(1/n))I require Omega(n^3/epsilon^2), and k-copy blocks without retained quantum memory require Omega(n^3/(epsilon^2 min(sqrt(k),n))). Known covariance spectrum remains hard for nonadaptive measurements.
review.prior_frontier: Prior general heterodyne bound O(n^3/epsilon^2) and entangled Theta(n^2/epsilon^2) tomography are claimed. New contributions are the lower bounds and temperature-sensitive improvement. A concurrent finite-to-Gaussian reduction by Rubin is acknowledged; historical sources not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Gives a tight continuum between cubic and quadratic sample complexity, with a physical covariance promise and arbitrary single-copy POVM lower bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines a low-energy fugacity embedding and temperature-dependent posterior analysis with a one-sided relative-covariance trace-distance bound.
score_reasons.depth: Adaptive bosonic posterior anti-concentration uses symmetric-power moments and random block-cost control; the upper bound requires resolvent stability near the vacuum boundary.
score_reasons.exposition: Main statements clearly separate passive hard families, general warm states, block entanglement and no-memory constraints; applications are explicitly qualified.

checked: Screening read the fugacity embedding R=sigma/4, constant-mass single-photon recovery, exact simulator with expected <=4/9 input copies, and the claimed block-budget reduction; no proof of the simulator or variable-block dependency has yet been audited.

Traced the warm tomography estimator conditional on the stated trace-distance theorem: inflate centered empirical covariance C_hat/(1-zeta)-I/2 so it dominates the true quantum covariance and remains physical; outside the concentration event output a valid fallback state.

With C<=alpha_nu Sigma, alpha_nu=1+1/(1+2nu), gamma_nu=2nu/(1+2nu), relative covariance error <=2alpha_nu zeta sqrt(2n)/(1-zeta). The stated bound and separate mean error yield N=O((1+1/nu)n(n+log(1/delta))/epsilon^2), independent of displacement and maximum energy.
remaining: The essential one-sided resolvent/relative-entropy bound in Section 7.1, adaptive posterior likelihood and Jacobian estimates, finite-dimensional tomography dependency, exact Gaussian simulator and all lower-bound comparisons remain unaudited.
The completed upper-bound composition is conditional on those lemmas and should not be treated as a full correctness audit.

review.authors: Jiale Chen

review.summary: For polynomially bounded integer weights in general graphs, gives deterministic O(ε^{−2}) unweighted and O(ε^{−2}log(1/ε)) weighted semi-streaming passes; deterministic incremental total time O((mε^{−3}+nε^{−6})log³n); and improved decremental and deterministic weighted-to-bipartite dynamic reductions.

review.title: Local Leakage Resilience of Multiplication-friendly Shamir Secret Sharing
review.authors: Jihun Hwang, Hemanta K. Maji, Ilya D. Shkredov, Xiuyu Ye
review.summary: For Shamir degree d=floor(cm), every fixed 0<c<1/2, proves near-optimal (2/π)^((1−o(1))d) worst-case one-bit-per-share leakage advantage for almost all public evaluation tuples over sufficiently large prime fields; m is a small c-dependent power of field bit length.
review.prior_frontier: Independent recent results cross 1/2 by an absolute constant for every evaluation tuple and general p>m. This reaches every positive rate with almost-all tuples and much larger fields, not a uniform strengthening in every parameter.

score_reasons.significance: Reaches the full constant-rate multiplication-friendly range for a standard secret-sharing scheme with nearly sharp security exponent.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines higher-order Fourier/nilsequence structure with leakage-independent local Reed–Solomon certificates and a sharp one-coefficient bound.
score_reasons.depth: The 100-page argument must control adversarial leakage after public tuple selection, shortenings and field-size growth uniformly.
score_reasons.exposition: The tradeoff against all-tuples results is explicit and the proof overview identifies the uniform good-set requirement.

checked: Checked the Shamir-to-RS comparison Insec≤2Δ via Ps(X)=s+XQ(X) and affine leakage remapping.
Traced conditional shortening P=Pu+MJ Q: remaining coordinates are a lower-dimensional RS code under invertible affine maps, giving the 2^|J| factor in the few-perturbation bound.

Traced the sharp Fourier extremum by selecting positive projected pth roots of unity; its finite-field base tends to 2/π. Checked Markov exp(√m) loss remains o(d) and exceptional fraction negligible for m=n^u.
remaining: Large-proof exception: 99 pages using higher-order Fourier analysis. The RS reduction, conditional shortening and sharp one-bit Fourier extremum were traced, including the exceptional-tuple parameter loss. The nilsequence/local-constraint and Gowers-norm machinery remains unverified.
Audit periodic nilsequence approximation, local-constraint certificate and simultaneous good set, many-perturbation Gowers estimate, higher-order parameter exponents and the matching LSB strategy.

papers.title: Group Isomorphism: Depth-$2\frac{1}{2}$ Circuits and Lower Bounds
papers.authors: Joshua A. Grochow, Gülce Kardeş, Michael Levet

review.title: Group Isomorphism: Depth-$2\frac{1}{2}$ Circuits and Lower Bounds
review.authors: Joshua A. Grochow, Gülce Kardeş, Michael Levet
review.area: Circuit complexity and computational group theory
review.summary: Cayley-table Group Isomorphism has uniform quasipolynomial-size depth-3 circuits with polylogarithmic bottom fan-in (depth 2.5), using Sigma_2 polylog-time verification. Any CNF, or CNF-of-XORs, for promise GpI on valid groups needs n^Omega(log n) size, already for Abelian 2-groups; DNF exponential lower bound is for the total language including invalid-table rejection. Upper bound reduces depth at the cost of a larger unspecified quasipolynomial exponent and does not improve serial runtime.
review.prior_frontier: Claims first Boolean circuit lower bounds for GpI and improvement from uniform depth 3.5 size n^O(log n) to depth 2.5 with somewhat larger quasipolynomial size. Earlier generator-enumerator results applied to quasigroups; this method exploits group structure. Historical claims not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Establishes nontrivial circuit lower bounds for a natural algebraic isomorphism problem and an improved low-depth upper bound.
score_reasons.novelty: The rank-to-Abelian-group affine reduction and a rank-gap affine-subspace lemma complement a composition-series strategy that avoids the missing published Ree short presentation.
score_reasons.depth: Uniform finite-simple-group presentation machinery and extension cohomology make the upper bound substantial; the new rank-gap lower-bound lemma is short and structural.
score_reasons.exposition: Careful distinctions between total and promise problems, larger size versus smaller depth, and unpublished presentation dependencies improve reliability of the framing.

checked: Traced the affine reduction: (u,z)*(v,w)=(u+v,z+w+M(u coordinatewise v)) is associative by bilinearity, Abelian and exponent <=4. Its square subgroup has size 2^rank(M), giving group type Z4^rank(M) x Z2^(2k-2rank(M)); each Cayley-table bit is affine in one matrix row.

Traced the new rank-gap lemma (Theorem 5.16) over arbitrary fields. Normalize an invertible point to I; in the translation space every row-supported matrix has zero diagonal. If every row admits a nonzero such matrix, a shortest directed support cycle can be scaled to have a one-dimensional (-1)-eigenspace, contradiction. Thus some row-supported subspace vanishes.

For the inductive dimension bound, coordinate relabeling must conjugate by a permutation (rather than merely permute rows, as phrased locally); this preserves eigenspaces and gives the claimed WLOG. Delete a zero last column, use absence of last-row-only matrices for injectivity, and preserve nonzero eigenspace dimensions under projection. Dimension recurrence <=k+(k-1)+... gives k(k+1)/2.

Traced the CNF-of-XOR covering application: each falsifying set is affine and avoids corank one; sets covering full-rank matrices have <=2^(k(k+1)/2) points. |GL(k,2)|>=2^(k^2-k) yields >=2^(k^2/2-3k/2)=n^((log2 n)/8-3/4) clauses for n=2^(2k).

Read the CNF row-cube connectivity argument and count, but its external affine bounded-rank dimension theorem was not independently verified. DNF argument requires rejecting invalid tables and is not claimed here for promise GpI.
remaining: The upper bound remains unaudited: composition-series guessing, quantified verifier complexity, extension compatibility, Ree normal forms, and uniform PSU3/Suzuki presentations in Sections 4,6,7 require substantial additional checking.
The external bounded-rank affine-space theorem used by the ordinary CNF proof has not been checked in its original source.
The new CNF-of-XOR lower-bound chain was traced, but this does not verify the full upper-and-lower-bound manuscript.

review.title: Triangle-Freeness: Estimation Is as Easy as Testing
review.authors: Nick Kushnir, Asaf Shapira

score_reasons.significance: Settles the polynomial testing-versus-estimation relation for a central previously unresolved graph property.
score_reasons.novelty: Reinterprets GGR-style sampled updates as a short-label encoding of a penalized deletion optimum, avoiding regularity-based blowups.
score_reasons.depth: The edge-to-vertex compression and normalization-compatible dense-CSP reduction are the core technical insights.
score_reasons.exposition: The compact argument separates existence of good labels from the estimator, and clearly explains why arbitrary inconsistent labels cannot produce a false optimum.

checked: Traced Sections 2–5: deletion-plus-triangle penalty, exact ordered-triple score identity, short-label decoder, block update compression, subsampling and the removal/testing comparison.
Verified the color-sum partition puts a triangle's edges in different blocks, so simultaneous updates have the exact linear score difference in (3.3).

Checked the conditional Bernoulli mean absolute error bound and telescoping without independence between edges; label length is O((1+lambda)^2 eta^(-3)), and final labels reproduce each edge's last block decision.

Checked BHHS's primary-source Theorem 4.1, Section 3 normalization and Definition 8.1: the constructed payoffs have maximum one, full ordered-triple density, and use the required (n/N)^3/full-denominator sample normalization.
Verified the bounded sampled optimum, independent-sample amplification and polynomial query count; exhaustive label search does not imply efficient runtime.

Traced the random-blowup comparison holding the n-vertex tester's decision rule fixed: collision probability at most 1/6, triangle probability at least 1/3, and R_triangle<=81*18^6*T_triangle^6. Checked Goldreich–Trevisan Lemma 4.1 directly; random induced-subgraph sampling uses O(q) vertices.

Independently justified the final Omega(1/epsilon) testing lower bound by a randomly located clique of order Theta(sqrt(epsilon)*n) against the empty graph: along the all-zero query transcript, each query hits an edge with probability O(epsilon).
remaining: No formal proof artifact was run. The published BHHS subsampling and Goldreich–Trevisan canonicalization theorems were checked for applicability, rather than re-proving their full source papers. Historical priority was not exhaustively audited.

sources.detail: BHHS: payoff normalization and Theorem 4.1; density in PDF p.19

review.summary: Shows distance from triangle-freeness can be estimated with only a polynomial loss relative to its optimal testing query complexity: E_triangle(epsilon)<=poly(T_triangle(epsilon/8)).
review.prior_frontier: Improves the previous exponential testing-to-estimation transformation for triangle-freeness. This is a dense adjacency-query result, not a polynomial-in-1/epsilon tester or an efficient-running-time bound.

review.authors: Adithya Diddapur

score_reasons.significance: Almost closes deterministic space gap over a substantial approximation regime.
score_reasons.novelty: Message-adaptive graph compression replaces one-bit packed gadgets by linear-cost gadgets.
score_reasons.depth: Combines entropy compression with graph gadget packing and a distinct independent-set construction.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear separation between output search, randomization, and restricted beta range.

checked: Traced message-wise entropy subadditivity under the stated conditional product hypothesis (Proposition 2.3).

Checked single-gadget final arithmetic: clique at least n/4 versus output at most 3 log n gives n/(12 log n); selection A-prime=A uses only positive support, not a claimed high conditional probability.

Verify independent-set construction and insertion-only simulation.

papers.title: Quantum Cryptomania with Classical Communication without One-Way Functions
papers.authors: Mohammed Barhoush, Amit Behera

review.title: Quantum Cryptomania with Classical Communication without One-Way Functions
review.authors: Mohammed Barhoush, Amit Behera
review.summary: Constructs a real self-inverse unitary oracle with perfectly correct IND-CPA public-key encryption using classical keys/ciphertexts but no nearly deterministic quantum-computable one-way functions. Also constructs such encryption from efficiently verifiable one-way puzzles and quantum iO with classical descriptions.
review.prior_frontier: Extends separations beyond quantum minicrypt to classical-communication public-key encryption; the negative result is relativized/black-box and the positive construction assumes qiO rather than puzzles alone.

score_reasons.significance: Separates major quantum cryptographic primitives whose classical counterparts sit in a strict implication hierarchy.
score_reasons.novelty: Continuous interpolation of two sampling/decryption tables prevents deterministic evaluator extraction while retaining encryption security.
score_reasons.depth: Requires a distribution-preserving path barrier, oracle hybrid security and simultaneous diagonalization against candidate functions.
score_reasons.exposition: Distinguishes all-input and average-input determinism, sampled-input variants and the precise point-obfuscation security notion.

checked: Traced the barrier Proposition 5.4: independent endpoints land in distinct separated sets with probability g²−sum pi²; bounded-speed crossing spends at least δ/v in the gap; unchanged marginals turn average crossing time into gap mass.
Checked why the naive key-verification oracle would itself yield a sampled-input qOWF, motivating modification of oracle operations rather than table distributions alone.
remaining: Audit construction of distribution-preserving paths for the real self-inverse oracle, qPKE hybrid bounds, PSPACE-aided no-qOWF diagonalization and qiO suppression-lemma construction.

papers.title: Quantum Fair Exchange
papers.authors: Hao Chung, Yi Lee, Justin Raizes, Sri AravindaKrishnan Thyagarajan

review.title: Quantum Fair Exchange
review.authors: Hao Chung, Yi Lee, Justin Raizes, Sri AravindaKrishnan Thyagarajan
review.summary: Formalizes simulation-based exchange of publicly projectively verifiable quantum states with recovery on abort. A purely classical trusted third party cannot give perfect exact-state resilience when both accepting subspaces have dimension at least two; assuming computationally unclonable states, even negligible-error validity preservation is impossible. A trusted party limited online to receiving/storing/sending registers statistically realizes fair exchange using input-independent trusted quantum preprocessing, with no added computational assumption.
review.prior_frontier: Builds a new fair-exchange model requiring input recovery, stronger on abort than identifiable-abort MPC or prior token-exchange locking guarantees. Quantum storage alone without trusted preprocessing remains open; no general optimal-resource claim is proved.

score_reasons.significance: Separates classical mediation from restricted quantum custody for recovery-preserving exchange, a distinct security requirement for quantum assets.
score_reasons.novelty: Classical-memory forking yields a clean impossibility mechanism; the storage-only construction combines delegated trap checking, recovery and trusted preprocessing.
score_reasons.depth: Malicious evaluators/checkers, repeated state access and matching attack patterns in simulation require a substantial error-correcting and hybrid argument.
score_reasons.exposition: The technical model distinguishes exact-state information-theoretic resilience from computational valid-state preservation, although informal introductory wording should be read through that qualification.

checked: Traced computational impossibility Theorem 4.14: copy only the classical mediator state at a random cut and run disjoint honest continuations; neither party quantum state is copied or rewound. No-signalling gives the correct fail-stop marginals.

Endpoint acceptance is negligible at cut zero by retaining the unclonable challenge and producing a second accepted state, and near one at the end by completeness. Alternating sender rounds force sum_t |p0(t)-p1(t)|>=1-negl, giving disagreement probability >=1/(T+1)-negl under a uniform cut.

Apply output-verification failure bounds before conditioning on disagreement; independently randomize which party holds the identically distributed challenge. With probability >=1/(2(T+1))-negl the rejecting party is the challenge holder and both outputs pass its verifier. The initial generated-to-valid-state replacement costs O(sqrt(eta)), still negligible.

Read construction roadmap: one physical qubit per encoded block is released, hidden traps and fresh traps distinguish evaluator/checker fault patterns, two passes ensure an honest hidden pad refresh between adversarial accesses, and input-independent EPR/magic-state inventory supplies operations the mediator cannot perform.
remaining: The 64-page full construction and simulation remain unaudited: compilation, repeated-access twirling, trap error tails, identification probability, encoded recovery, delayed teleportation and adversarial output-pattern matching.
The BB84 exact-state impossibility is read at roadmap level, not fully checked; it requires exact recovery rather than just any valid output state.
Computational lower-bound reasoning was traced, but its underlying unclonable-state existence is an explicit assumption and no full protocol-correctness conclusion follows from this audit.

review.authors: Marek Eliáš, Gautam Kamath, Janardhan Kulkarni, George Z. Li, Jingcheng Liu, Sepideh Mahabadi, Pan Peng, Jakub Tarnawski, Hangyu Xu, Zongrui Zou
review.summary: For nonnegative weighted graphs with public vertices and edge-weight l1 adjacency, gives polynomial-time (epsilon,delta)-edge-DP synthetic graph release with simultaneous cut error gamma times the true cut plus O(n/(gamma epsilon) log^7(n/(delta beta gamma epsilon))). Polynomiality is in an exact real RAM with Gaussian/Laplace draws, not bit complexity. Gives a nearly matching additive lower bound and applications including 1.387-approximate private correlation clustering with nearly linear additive error; that application additionally needs capped release and a private clustering baseline.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript contrasts its near-linear additive error with prior polynomial-time n^(13/12+o(1)) error and prior inefficient near-linear release. Historical bounds and the application algorithms were not independently checked. The Lean repository is accessible, but its full compilation and statement-to-paper correspondence were not verified.

score_reasons.significance: Closes the computational gap for all-cut release to nearly linear additive error, with consequential optimization applications.
score_reasons.novelty: Fractional retirement connects Gaussian SDP witness privacy loss to retired edge mass; it adapts PREM rather than merely applying generic composition.
score_reasons.depth: Combines log-determinant optimizer stability, success-charged adaptive composition, MWU utility, numerical optimization and a substantial formal implementation.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise privacy and real-RAM assumptions, modular lemmas and explicit formalization scope; the 63-page analysis and large implementation require substantial checking.

checked: Traced Lemma 13: first-order optimality gives lambda||X0^-1/2(X1-X0)X1^-1/2||_F^2 bounded by the signed perturbation; the per-edge Cauchy-Schwarz estimate yields the weighted local stability bound. Its small-norm consequence gives the factor-two q_e comparison.

Traced the Gaussian likelihood calculation in Lemma 14: generalized eigenvalue logarithms are controlled by the relative Frobenius norm, and centered quadratic-form concentration gives the batch bound. The standard concentration inequality itself was not independently sourced.

Traced Lemma 16 in Appendix A, including the auxiliary common-history kernels, k delta-prime TV accumulation, and the supermartingale exp((sum privacy losses minus four times successful charges)/(4 ell-star)). Checked the failed-output term via exp(.35)<1.5 and the final two-sided DP transfer.

Traced Lemma 17: a common good Gaussian event controls densities under both inputs; conditioning doubles the likelihood bound, successful witnesses dominate local charges, and coordinatewise total retirement at most one bounds their sum. Checked epsilon and delta calibration with n^2 calls.

Read the public Lean repository README sections on theorem1_machine, statistical theorem, computational model and limitations. It distinguishes actual machine operation counts from older assigned-cost interfaces and does not claim bit complexity. No Lean build was run.
remaining: The full MWU/aggregation utility proof, approximate-SDP implementation accuracy and time, discrepancy lower bound, and application reductions were not traced.

The substantial Lean project was not compiled, its axiom audit was not run, and its complete formal statements were not compared with the manuscript. Formal correctness cannot be inferred from its README.

papers.title: A Sharp Dynamic Haussler Lemma
papers.authors: Shihao Shao, Dacheng Tao

review.title: A Sharp Dynamic Haussler Lemma
review.authors: Shihao Shao, Dacheng Tao
review.summary: For any [0,1]-valued class F with d=sfat_(epsilon/32)(F), constructs a single global family of deterministic causal experts of size at most (C/epsilon^p)^d, covering every length-T input sequence and every target in normalized l_p error epsilon. C is universal and independent of p and T; the experts are existential, with no computational efficiency claim. A fixed countable binary class of Littlestone dimension d requires more than (1/(2^(p+1)epsilon^p))^d experts on all sufficiently long horizons, even permitting arbitrary real-valued covering vectors.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript identifies open horizon-independent dynamic binary and integral sequential l2 covering questions, distinguishing earlier fractional covers. Those historical attributions were not independently checked. The new theorem is stronger than a separate cover chosen for each input tree.

score_reasons.significance: A sharp horizon-independent global covering theorem, with matching accuracy exponent, resolves a central structural question in online learning.
score_reasons.novelty: The shared-parent continuation routing removes the remaining logarithmic factor while preserving one causal family for every sequence.
score_reasons.depth: Interlocking adaptive sampling, partial SOA completion, buffered certificates, rank-sensitive capacity allocation and a perfect-information determinization argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully specifies the information order, distinguishes provisional and final predictions, and handles infinite classes and rank-zero cases; the long construction remains demanding.

checked: Traced separated-class reduction via Zorn, rank-zero singleton property, rank-decreasing centers without attained extrema, and sign-only correction schedules with repeated selected ordinals. Checked Q_d counts and the convolution identity used to remove pool multiplicity.

Traced the adaptive low-hit lemma through red/blue double sampling. Conditioning on the union preserves predictable inputs; partial SOA causal completion handles undefined labels, and 2^(-red ones)(3/2)^(blue ones) is a martingale. This controls all fixed master codes before selecting target-dependent witnesses.

Traced the master/replay analysis: union sampling or all-round master regime; coupling full pool vectors to union bits and an independent seed; buffered replay updates retain targets with 2 eta slack. A selected disagreement forces a master or replay correction, giving at most 2d hits. The joint exponential supermartingale uses only fresh coordinate independence, not independent replay histories.

Checked universal-constant parameter inequalities and that Good has probability above 15/16 against every deterministic adaptive input strategy with independent finite auxiliary seed. The union bounds charge fixed schedules and pool subsets, not an uncontrolled infinite target set.

Traced robust singleton identification and local packing: certificates separate identified targets by more than 2 eta on a pool, so rank-r subclasses have at most Q_r(m) identifications. Activation at k/2 pools and at least 3k/4 accurate replays imply more than k/4 eligible nonsingleton parents born before activation.

Traced causal child assignment, load supermartingale and capacities ceil(16 Q_(d-i)(m)/k+log(4P)). Parent eligibility persists after capacity exhaustion, preserving conditional routing probabilities. Counting yields 16Q_d(2m)+P(log(4P)+2), whose lower-rank overhead is absorbed by R.

Traced finite-depth perfect-information determinization, including infinite branching via choice, and verified that resulting expert predictions depend only on observed input prefixes. Checked p-general conversion using eta=epsilon/32 and R=16/epsilon^p.

Traced the fixed countable finite-field hyperplane lower bound: only false negatives and increasing affine span give Littlestone dimension at most d; the standard basis is shattered. Checked pairwise distances, q selection including q=2, periodic-prefix threshold and the real-valued triangle-inequality packing argument.
remaining: No efficient expert evaluation or numerical constants are claimed or verified. Historical novelty and the cited prior open questions were not independently checked. This is a mathematical audit of the main upper/lower arguments, not a formal proof certificate.

score_reasons.significance: A major accuracy improvement at the full high-temperature threshold of a central sampling model.

score_reasons.exposition: The introduction separates zero-field sampling, covariance results and the still-open inference consequence well; the short net-of-times reduction needs careful dependency checking.

Checked the distinction between weak Poincaré warm-start mixing and an unrestricted spectral-gap assertion, and the need to union bound across temperatures and localization times.
remaining: The central high-probability cumulant bounds, TAP Hessian lower bound, net-of-times uniformity and imported annealing/localization lemmas need a full audit before recommendation.

review.summary: For every fixed inverse temperature β<1, simulated annealing samples the zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model to arbitrary inverse-polynomial total-variation error with high probability over GOE disorder; each temperature stage uses O(N log N) Glauber steps.
review.prior_frontier: Previous algorithms reaching all β<1 achieved only slightly o(1) total-variation error. This strengthens accuracy to N^-a and develops high-probability weak Poincaré/covariance bounds. It does not establish the corresponding nonzero-field spiked-Wigner recovery claim.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate; full main-proof audit pending

papers.title: Is Randomness Necessary for Adaptive Data Analysis?
papers.authors: Edith Cohen, Haim Kaplan, Yishay Mansour, Shay Sapir, Uri Stemmer, Eliad Tsfadia

review.title: Is Randomness Necessary for Adaptive Data Analysis?
review.authors: Edith Cohen, Haim Kaplan, Yishay Mansour, Shay Sapir, Uri Stemmer, Eliad Tsfadia
review.summary: Every deterministic, even unbounded, mechanism on a domain of size 2^{O(n^2 log n)} is defeated with probability >=.9 by O(n log n) adaptive Boolean queries of error >.1 for a distribution uniform on 20n points. With b private random bits, O(n log n+b) queries suffice on a correspondingly larger domain. Analyst depends on mechanism.
review.prior_frontier: Randomized mechanisms support ~n^2 queries; earlier version had random-oracle or tower-domain qualifications. This version supplies a plain-model exponential-domain separation. Prior frontier not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves whether internal randomness is necessary for unrestricted adaptive data analysis.
score_reasons.novelty: Couples full query truth tables to force bit-natural behavior while controlling adaptive history density.
score_reasons.depth: Information-theoretic response profiles and adaptively selected maximal couplings go beyond ordinary natural-mechanism attacks.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states mechanism-dependent attacker, domain size, bounded-analyst distinction and limited-randomness extension.

checked: Verified Lemma 4.2 selected-query density bound: each of <=N+1 marginals conditions N fair bits, so any adaptive choice is dominated by (N+1)2^N times uniform. Multiplying conditional bounds yields the history domination for fixed dataset and locations.
Traced fixed-row/profile coupling and union over N*2^(N-1) row-pattern possibilities; conditioning-on-history danger is explicitly handled, not ignored.

Completed the main deterministic lower bound and limited-randomness extension on PDF pages 8–15. The common-point set has size at most5n/4, so its uniform mass under N=20n is below0.1. If neither endpoint already separates, a first majority threshold crossing, together with the fewer-than0.8 fraction of candidates containing the changed point, forces one of the two neighboring queries to eliminate at least0.1 of all surviving candidates. This uses only response bits, not equality of full answers.

Independently derived the probabilistic lemma: the total variation for bit u is E[X_u c_u(Y)]. At most2^d possible conditional-majority sign vectors occur; the standard exponential-moment bound for Rademacher sums gives expected maximum at most sqrt(2Md ln2), yielding the stated average-TV bound.

Checked the coupling construction for adaptive threshold patterns. Sequential disintegrations preserve all specified query marginals along the path. For a fixed row and other-row support pattern, comparing to a coupling that first fixes the other entire rows bounds disagreement by the mean conditional TV. Including all samples omitting the row makes the response profile independent of the hidden position. The union over N·2^(N−1) possibilities validly covers patterns selected as functions of the hidden locations.

Checked the history argument without assuming hidden locations remain independent after observation. For fixed locations and actual sample, each selected query has density at most (N+1)2^N relative to a uniform truth table, including failed couplings. Multiplying densities bounds every history. In the prescribed-history experiment, the current-round failure uses fresh coins independent of all earlier selection coins conditional on locations and sample, so multiplying the history bound by failure probability and summing over histories is justified.

Checked all parameter arithmetic and quantifiers: k=ceil(log_(10/9)(N^n))+1 eliminates every possible sample on success; M=ceil(2N^n(100kN2^N D^k)^2) makes total coupling failure≤1/200 and gives log|X|=O(n²log n). Averaging fixes a support distribution and an analyst with the required failure probability; the attacker may depend on the mechanism.

Checked the bounded-seed extension: track2^b sample–seed pairs, including all seeds in profiles, giving d=2^b(N−1)^n, k=O(nlog n+b), and log|X|=O(n²log n+nb). The common-point counting and conditional-history independence arguments remain valid with the seed fixed.
remaining: The main information-theoretic lower bound and bounded-private-randomness theorem are traced. The separate cryptographic deterministic upper bound in Appendix A and its PRG/extractor dependencies were not audited.

review.title: Spatial Mixing and Deterministic Approximate Counting of Multi-spin Systems beyond Bounded Degree Graphs
review.authors: Zhidan Li, Kuan Yang
review.summary: Develops rational marginal polytopes for deterministic FPTASes on positive multi-spin systems with polynomial-prefactor self-avoiding-walk growth D and Birkhoff contraction c satisfying Dc<1. For sparse G(n,d/n), counts q-colorings with high probability for fixed q≥(2+η)d.
review.prior_frontier: Improves random-graph coloring counting leading constant 3 to 2. Spatial mixing has a polynomial prefactor and is explicitly weaker than usual uniform SSM; fixed d,q and positive rational inputs are part of the guarantees.

score_reasons.significance: Improves deterministic counting in a prominent sparse random-graph regime and extends multi-spin correlation-decay algorithms beyond maximum-degree bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: Carries joint marginal constraints through rational polytopes and linear-fractional optimization instead of independent coordinate intervals.
score_reasons.depth: Must simultaneously bound contraction, recursion size, bit precision and permissive blocks around high-degree vertices.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly distinguishes polynomial-prefactor mixing from uniform SSM and gives a counterexample to conflating them.

checked: Traced the Hilbert-distance recursion into self-avoiding walks with weighted count Kn^α D(Dc)^R.
Checked the polytope-diameter recurrence, finite rounding contribution and logarithmic R/precision choices; positive ratio bounds ensure feasible coordinates stay positive.
remaining: Audit polytope containment and exact linear-fractional implementation, total recursive bit complexity, permissive-block feasibility and high-probability random-graph block/SAW bounds.

sources.detail: Positive-interaction theorem and non-uniform SSM warning

review.title: Rapid Mixing for Sampling Colorings of Random Graphs up to Tree Uniqueness Threshold
review.authors: Zhidan Li, Kuan Yang
review.summary: For every fixed eta>0, sufficiently large constant d and fixed integer q>=(1+eta)d, single-site Glauber dynamics for proper q-colorings of G(n,d/n) mixes in n^C(1+log(1/epsilon)) time with high probability, C depending on eta,d,q. It reaches the asymptotic regular-tree uniqueness benchmark despite unbounded maximum degree. Establishes O(log n) coupling and spectral independence uniformly over feasible pinnings, with matching logarithmic lower bounds.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript improves the previous Glauber requirement q>=(1.7632...+o_d(1))d. A prior non-MCMC sampler already reached (1+o_d(1))d but only instance-size-tied n^-Omega(1) error, not arbitrary-accuracy FPAUS. These historical bounds were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Improves the natural local sampler to the tree-uniqueness benchmark on a central sparse random-graph model.
score_reasons.novelty: A one-step buffer around high-degree vertices provides bounded and connected marginal supports, enabling logarithmic independence to yield polynomial mixing.
score_reasons.depth: Requires marked Galton-Watson message estimates, buffered percolation, entropy factorization and comparison back to single-site dynamics.
score_reasons.exposition: The theorem quantifiers and earlier fixed-accuracy limitation are clear; the extensive probabilistic message and buffer arguments are technically demanding.

checked: Traced list-coloring connectivity under an ordering with list size at least residual degree plus two: lift each recoloring after moving the deleted vertex away from its neighbors and the proposed color.

Checked the buffered extension and marginal-bound argument: high-degree vertices have no neighbors outside the buffer, its components are tree/unicyclic, and every neighbor of an unbuffered vertex has bounded degree. Local recoloring maps have at most q^(D+1) preimages. Conditional marginal supports are projections of connected list-coloring supports.

Checked the entropy assembly conditional on its cited factorization theorem and the unverified buffered percolation lemma: good blocks decompose into logarithmic components; bad-block probability is absorbed, yielding polynomial single-site tensorization.

Traced the full/marginal block-generator orthogonal decomposition, eigenvalue |U| on the orthogonal complement, logarithmic-component canonical-path relaxation bound, and the two comparison losses from block overlap and continuous-to-discrete time. The final chain is positive semidefinite and has minimum stationary mass at least q^-n.
remaining: The main O(log n) coupling-independence theorem, marked branching/message analysis and buffered percolation proof were not audited.
External entropy factorization and mixing comparison dependencies have not been checked against their primary sources. The inspected final assembly alone does not verify the full 52-page theorem.

review.title: Noncrossing is All You Need: Beyond Identical Delay Functions in Online Matching with Delays on General Metrics
review.authors: Yossi Azar, Junhao Gan, Shahar Lewkowicz, Xiao Sun, Seeun William Umboh

score_reasons.significance: Removes several substantial restrictions on a central online-with-delays problem.
score_reasons.novelty: The minimum-partition potential and comparison of virtual against consolidated instances extend beyond a routine HST application.
score_reasons.depth: Laminar forests, geometric counter chains and parity-sensitive charging form a substantial analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise model definitions, two failed algorithm attempts and a concrete greedy counterexample explain the obstacle effectively.

checked: Checked the concave-delay greedy counterexample and the exact value/derivative noncrossing requirements.

Verified that running-maximum continuity follows because arrivals can only decrease the optimal partition potential, and that geometrically decreasing equivalence-class chains permit two-stage pruning with loss at most four.
remaining: The complete aligned/misaligned charging proof, virtual-to-consolidated reduction, and HST competitive accounting remain unaudited.

review.summary: Extends online matching with delays to request-specific noncrossing delay functions, with nonclairvoyant deterministic O(1) competitiveness at one location and randomized O(log n log Δ+log²Δ) competitiveness on arbitrary metrics.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier constant/polylogarithmic guarantees required identical known linear or concave delays. The new class allows different functions but requires earlier requests to have no smaller accumulated delay and no larger derivative at every later time; this is not arbitrary heterogeneous delay.

papers.authors: Konstantin Zabarnyi

review.title: Designing Information in a Forest: Algorithmic Aspects
review.authors: Konstantin Zabarnyi
review.summary: Binary-state, binary-action persuasion under a directed-forest information hierarchy admits weakly polynomial exact optimization and succinct sampling for monotone symmetric utilities, and exact modular optimization. Supermodular optimization has no FPTAS even on disjoint 3-receiver chains; depth-h approximation factors are 1/(h+1) and (1-1/e)/(h+1) for super/submodular objectives.
review.prior_frontier: Private persuasion symmetric/supermodular tractability and earlier modular additive FPTAS are cited; forest nonmodular case is new. Prior literature not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Substantial tractability/hardness boundary for information hierarchies beyond fully private or public signals.
score_reasons.novelty: Exact posterior/count LP relaxation with recursive implementation and forest dynamic programming.
score_reasons.depth: Must implement exponentially supported signaling and enforce nested posterior consistency; hardness uses lexicographic scales.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise utility/state restrictions and succinct versus explicit support distinction.

checked: Traced relaxation constraints as posterior calibration and child-parent martingale equations. Recursive conditional sampling preserves unconditional node marginals and child adoption counts on a forest.
Checked stated approximation factors specialize to private-persuasion factors at depth zero.
remaining: Finish induction that every receiver posterior equals its promised value despite descendant observations; verify separation oracle and bit complexity.
Audit supermodular max-cut reduction, coefficient sizes/no-FPTAS gap, and general-DAG symmetric hardness.

review.title: Entropy Bounds for Local Coordination and Graph Amenability
review.authors: Ron Peretz, Dean Kraizberg
review.area: Distributed computation; information theory and coordination games
review.summary: Converts unbiased binary local coordination of disagreement cost ε to leader profiles with O(ε log(1/ε)) cost; constructs Ω(ε√log(1/ε)) separation, including equilibrium profiles. General real-valued outputs retain a sharp square-root loss.
review.prior_frontier: Improves a recent O(√ε) conversion and refutes a constant-factor conjecture for binary profiles, leaving a √log versus log gap. Applies to arbitrary information skeletons as well as graph neighborhoods.

score_reasons.significance: Substantial specialist progress on the geometry of locally generated correlation and leader coordination.
score_reasons.novelty: Mutual-information increments replace Shapley influences; weighted-majority hyperplane geometry produces the nonconstant lower separation.
score_reasons.depth: Upper bound is concise, while the uniform-over-leaders lower construction requires geometric and concentration arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: States the residual logarithmic gap and binary/unrestricted distinction clearly.

checked: Fully traced the entropy upper bound: pair-information increments dominate individual increments, their masses give conditional entropies h(p), and triangle inequality gives TV≤h(p).

Checked independent sources ensure support on each allowed information set; grand coupling plus Jensen yields a deterministic leader realization with cost≤2h(Ibin/2). Verified the displayed two-source example attains the TV bound.
remaining: Audit majority-arrangement lower bound and uniform concentration, equilibrium implementation, real-output cycle lower bound and the external grand-coupling theorem if selected.

sources.detail: Main upper theorem and real-output comparison

papers.title: $\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}$
papers.authors: Rishabh Batra

review.title: $\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}$
review.authors: Rishabh Batra
review.summary: Proves that uniform efficient EFI pairs exist iff uniform expanding single-copy pure-state pseudorandom generators exist. Honest generators need no advice; security remains against nonuniform QPT adversaries with quantum advice. The construction keeps a purification, obtains local prefix witnesses with an entropy surplus, randomizes the start of a repeated source, extracts each column, then masks every discarded qubit to retain pure fixed-key outputs. Does not establish many-copy PRS.
review.prior_frontier: The cited prior equivalence required O(log lambda) bits of classical advice to select the extraction length. Removing this yields a uniform EFI meta-complexity characterization via a prior theorem. The prior meta-complexity equivalence was not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Removes honest-generator nonuniformity from a foundational equivalence at the minimal end of quantum cryptography.
score_reasons.novelty: Fixes source entropy by retaining purification and uses compatible local prefix witnesses rather than an unavailable global high-entropy replacement.
score_reasons.depth: Handles quantum conditional entropy with negative summands, a random-start construction, backwards extraction hybrids and explicit key accounting.
score_reasons.exposition: Short, modular proof carefully separates single-copy security, honest uniformity, quantum advice, local witness consistency and pure outputs.

checked: Traced correlated-flag indistinguishability and its Holevo surplus from Helstrom guessing plus Fano. Purification and an explicit flag give source entropy exactly one; replacing only the flag prefix adds the surplus while preserving the exact preceding marginal.

Traced random-start windows, including the truncated first source copy: strong subadditivity increases conditional entropy when past systems are omitted; each shift permutes source coordinates. Prefix witnesses need not be jointly consistent, but each has exactly the true previous-prefix marginal.

Checked the AEP calibration t=2^16 M^2(lambda+4), negligible smoothing 2^-lambda/12, H_min>=7t/(4M), and extraction length t/2+3t/(4M). Consulted Tomamichel thesis Theorem 6.4/Corollary 6.5 (PDF 105–106): for one-qubit A, 4 log(2 sqrt(2)+1)<10 is dimension-independent in B.

Checked extraction against Dupuis et al. Theorem 3.1 (PDF 9): partial-trace Choi conditional min-entropy is t-2ell; trace distance halves the trace-norm bound. With smoothing epsilon/12 and ell<=(t+k)/2-log(1/epsilon), the two contributions total at most epsilon. The proof uses second moments, hence an exact Clifford two-design suffices.

Checked efficient finite binary-seed Clifford sampling by modulo indexing, with bias at most 2^(-lambda^2); Koenig–Smolin primary source PDF 1–2 confirms polynomial indexing and circuit synthesis. Raw seed bits are output, canceling their entire length from stretch.

Traced the backwards retained-column hybrid using witness equality on the original past, polynomial tensor hybrids against quantum-advice distinguishers, and Pauli masking of all unused qubits. Computed n-r=N(2ell-t)-Mt-Lt=(M-3/2)t>0 for M>=4. Reverse direction follows from rank at most 2^r versus output dimension 2^n.
remaining: Standard EFI amplification is used as an existing result; its full repetition proof was not re-proved. The secondary meta-complexity corollary depends on the cited earlier characterization, not independently audited. No many-copy security or formal proof certificate is asserted.
