papers.authors: Oded Lachish, Amit Levi, Ilan Newman

review.title: Testability of General Graphs with Weak Query Oracles
review.authors: Oded Lachish, Amit Levi, Ilan Newman

score_reasons.significance: A broad structural account of exactly how weak graph access limits testability.
score_reasons.novelty: The combination of degeneracy reduction, oracle separations and induced-freeness lower bounds is substantive.
score_reasons.depth: Several complementary tester and indistinguishability arguments must be coordinated across models.
score_reasons.exposition: Useful conceptual organization, but informal/formal numbering and typographical errors make the theorem dependencies less polished.

checked: Checked the blow-up transversal counting: deleting all H copies requires at least |E|/e_H edges, while high-girth regular graphs are H-free.
Checked the fresh-label collision mechanism and q²/t indistinguishability scale under random relabeling, including matching isolated-vertex counts.
remaining: Tree testers, the full finite-family degeneracy transfer, induced-freeness case analysis, and the imported characterization require further checking. Lower-bound construction size and all model-separation constants have not been fully audited.

review.summary: Characterizes one-sided testability in a weak general-graph oracle with random-edge and random-neighbor access, separates degree/count-strengthened models, and proves polynomial lower bounds for cyclic forbidden subgraphs even with two-sided error.
review.prior_frontier: Extends bounded-degeneracy characterization techniques to arbitrary graphs under deliberately weak access. For fixed H, acyclic freeness is testable while cyclic freeness is not; the finite-family characterization imports the bounded-degeneracy result and is not always an explicit decidable criterion.

papers.title: Optimal Online Stochastic Matching
papers.authors: Paul Duetting, Michal Feldman, Mathieu Molina

review.title: Optimal Online Stochastic Matching
review.authors: Paul Dütting, Michal Feldman, Mathieu Molina
review.summary: Known-law unweighted online bipartite matching has optimal competitive ratio 1-exp(1-e), approximately .8206, for Poisson and finite i.i.d. arrivals, with a polynomial-time guarantee; unknown arrival laws are strictly worse.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript cites a .716 algorithmic guarantee. Independently verified Chierichetti–Giacchini–Panconesi–Vattani, ICALP2025 Definition8 and Theorems9,14,15: the known-i.i.d. hard distribution has offline optimum (1-o(1))n and online ratio at most 1-exp(1-e). The new result matches this upper bound in both known-law models.

score_reasons.significance: Claims to close a long-standing constant gap for a central online matching model.
score_reasons.novelty: Exact Poisson-exponential offline correspondence via supermodular chain distributions, plus posterior-allocation potential.
score_reasons.depth: Combines a novel benchmark duality, continuous stochastic control, finite-i.i.d. transfer and efficient implementation.
score_reasons.exposition: The complete proof explains the exact benchmark transfer, finite-count correction and drift cancellation clearly; all new central arguments and ancillary weighted/unknown-law claims were checked.

checked: PDF pp. 8–14,33–35: checked work/completion identity by the infinite-demand coupling x_i=min(Z_i,B_i), with B_i independent of Z_i; coverage-polymatroid max-flow characterization; matching/completion hazard coupling and reverse conditional-history construction. Checked both offline min-cut deficiencies and the supermodular excursion order-complex contraction A→A union B via decreasing-size deletion. This yields the exact alternating chain identity, not an unsupported equality of all joint distributions.

PDF pp. 12–14: verified the nested-set count/waiting-time law and common independent Pois(a) shift; conditional on integer maximum Poisson deficiency, exponential deficiency is a sum of that many independent mean-one exponentials. Integrating gives exact equality of expected offline optima. The chain nesting requirement and zero-deficiency boundary are respected.

PDF pp. 14–19,36: checked posterior-allocation policy feasibility and residual independent exponentials under adaptive nonanticipating service, x_i+1-s_i=E[Z_i-Y_i|F_t]≥0. Independently differentiated q(t,h)=1-exp(-(h+1)(exp(1-t)-1)), its PDE and sensitivity bound. Computed completion jumps and deterministic work drift, justified bounded-trajectory Dynkin integration, and derived the coordinatewise factor 1-exp(1-e).

PDF pp. 19–25: checked the exact finite-i.i.d. transfer. Keeping n and the service rule fixed while varying the hidden Poisson count, scaling all work/capacities by a/n preserves routing probabilities. Entire power-series coefficients give n arrivals versus n-1 uniform work points, with n(n-1)!=n!. Greedy polymatroid augmentation preserves past allocation and reaches the offline optimum in the exponential comparison. Repeating the coefficient argument from each history gives E[Y_i-x_i|F]≤R/N, including N=1 and R=0, without assuming independent fixed job demands for the binomial process.

PDF pp. 25–27,36–39: checked greedy bounded-rate ODE construction and posterior-total comparison. Verified ell(t)x_i<R using t(exp(1-t)-1)<1-t. Recomputed the binomial-process generator: completion rate (N-1)s_i/R, other-job jumps cancel R differentiation, and the remaining coefficient is (1+ell)w_i. The exact drift includes the nonnegative w_i ell x_i/N term. Verified N=1 separately and terminal dominated convergence, yielding the ratio for every m,n.

PDF pp. 27–31,39–42: checked the balanced rational flow rule and its central comparison lemma: minimum-rate neighbors receive all positive type flow; weights decreasing in those rates support every feasible allocation; the scalar product inequality with a_i=w((s_i-c)+) proves the weighted drift comparison. Both Poisson and binomial potentials therefore give the same ratio with rates depending only on the unmatched set.

PDF pp. 40–42: checked the strict initial surplus kappa=2^-18 m^-3, tight lower rate level sets, common excess-drift lower bound, binomial correction sign for t≤1/(4max(1,C)), both weight estimates, the r tau^3/512 integral estimate, no-completion probability, and C≤2m versus C>2m regimes. Verified capped exact-rational rejection sampling uses O(log m) trials and loses at most kappa E[OPT]/2 by conditioning on the full arrival sequence, so the worst-case polynomial per-arrival algorithm retains the exact constant. Rational convex QP has polynomial input/solution bit size, at most m+1 updates; Poisson total arrivals are unbounded, so the claim is preprocessing/per-arrival time, not worst-case total run time.

PDF pp. 43–53: checked the complete weighted offline duality extension. LP dual prices cap at W; integer-weight residual prices are affine on each standard cube-chain simplex. Along a face, coordinates increase once and each residual type price decreases by at most one, producing nested count/waiting-time increments. Checked equality of expected simplex maxima and the Euler sublevel deformation retraction giving min g=sum(-1)^dim max_sigma g. Finite sums, rational scaling and integrable real-weight approximation justify the full equality. Also checked continuous random-weight truncation and support-function equality of compact downward-closed expected allocation regions.

PDF pp. 53–59: checked the complete unknown-law strict-gap construction. The posterior hidden set is uniform on unseen vertices; universal arrivals are independent of unseen-count U. Recomputed mean U/m, pairwise covariance O_s(1/m), E[1/U] asymptotics and two dominated/reverse-Fatou limits proving integral I=o(1-s), uniformly over policies. Verified convexity differential comparison with s x(t/s), integrating factor, strict concavity loss of order 1-s, fixed-H averaging, and O(sqrt n) Poisson/fixed-count transfer. Offline near-perfect matching follows from the cited hard distribution and monotone replacement of restricted neighborhoods by universal ones.

Independently fetched the official ICALP2025 primary PDF, stored as dep_CGPV25.pdf: verified Definition8 on p.10, Theorem9 on p.11 and Theorems14–15 on p.13. It has exactly the 1/[d(d-1)] with-replacement neighborhood law used here, a near-perfect offline matching and the claimed upper ratio even for known i.i.d. laws. Poissonizing the fixed-count benchmark changes it by at most E|Pois(n)-n|=O(sqrt n), which suffices for both uses.
remaining: This is an independent mathematical audit, not a formal verification. The linked Lean repository was not downloaded or executed, and no claim is made about its axiom/dependency closure.

Standard external max-flow/LP/convex-QP, polymatroid augmentation, stochastic compensator/Dynkin and Euler-characteristic facts were applied with their hypotheses checked; their full general proofs and the ICALP2025 hard-instance proof were not independently reproved.
The .716 historical algorithmic baseline and secondary background citations were not independently reconstructed; the exact optimality upper bound used by the new theorem was verified.

sources.detail: Complete central proof and appendices through PDF p.59 checked; PDF author order preserved.
Official primary source: hard distribution, online bound, and near-perfect offline benchmark, pp.10–13.

papers.title: Separating QMA from QCIP with a Classical Oracle, or, the Power of Quantum Proofs over Classical Interaction for Quantum Verifiers
papers.authors: Alper Cakan

review.title: Separating QMA from QCIP with a Classical Oracle, or, the Power of Quantum Proofs over Classical Interaction for Quantum Verifiers
review.authors: Alper Çakan
review.summary: Builds a classical oracle and unary language in QMA outside QCIP, allowing polynomially many classical-message interactions with a quantum verifier. Also constructs a sampleable gap and derives cryptographic black-box barriers; an IP-versus-MIP consequence uses an external relativized containment.
review.prior_frontier: Recent classical-oracle QMA–QCMA separations still admitted AM protocols. This separates quantum witnesses from arbitrary polynomial classical interaction in the oracle setting; unrelativized QCIP contains QMA via PSPACE.

score_reasons.significance: Strengthens a central quantum-proof separation to all polynomial-round classical interaction and bears on longstanding oracle questions for interactive proofs.
score_reasons.novelty: Contractive simultaneous incompressibility supports verifier-only classical-query simulation against an unbounded prover.
score_reasons.depth: Combines codeword/hash structure, independent marking, interactive simulation, cheating provers and fixed-oracle diagonalization.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states the oracle nature and distinguishes the concurrent BQP-versus-IP result; full 87-page verification is substantial.

checked: Checked why earlier code-intersection oracle instances admit an AM attack and how independently marked NO instances prevent that particular test.

Traced the incompressibility parameter application: s=c+t ceil(log M), t=c+λ², and γ=ceil(λ/12) eventually give s+8λ²≤γt; Markov upgrades expected failure to simultaneous-over-provers simulation for most oracles.

Traced the classical-query simulator hybrid, including the fresh-register estimator, conditional private-state identity, geometric stopping/reset union bound and per-query4theta squared-norm error. The prover reply rule depends only on fixed oracle and transcript, so conditioning on estimator samples does not further disturb the private verifier state.

Checked the cutoff encoding/decoding argument: full transcript plus t successful trial indices, replay with shared estimation tapes and no oracle, recovers every newly marked input; union over all transcripts makes the bound uniform over prover strategies.

Checked finite randomness: rounding each of at mostM+r algebraic sampling distributions to2^-krand probabilities adds at most(M+r)L2^-krand<=epsilon/3; exact decoder and rounded simulator are kept distinct. This is query efficiency with unrestricted local computation, not a polynomial-time classical simulation.
remaining: Large-proof exception:86-page oracle separation. The new verifier-only simulation argument was traced, but its oracle-family incompressibility bound and the full separation are not certified.
QMA witness soundness under independent marking, contractive incompressibility, public-coin cheating prover, fixed-oracle diagonalization and sampleable-gap construction remain unchecked.
The external ANTV26 containment extension from BQP to QMA underlying the IP/MIP corollary still needs independent verification.

papers.title: One Polynomial Field for Every Euler Step and the Flow: Polynomial Dynamics for PTIME and PSPACE
papers.authors: Olivier Bournez

review.title: One Polynomial Field for Every Euler Step and the Flow: Polynomial Dynamics for PTIME and PSPACE
review.authors: Olivier Bournez
review.summary: Compiles each halting deterministic machine into one fixed rational polynomial field and initialization whose unit-step Euler map, every variable Euler mesh with steps in (0,1] and divergent sum, and continuous flow share the logical configuration trace at their own internal clock sections. Scale h=2^-s with s linear in space plus log time permits drift noise h^(2K), physical time O(s(T+s)) and O(s) fractional bits at unit step. Compact bounded-active-state semantics characterize P by polynomial time and PSPACE by eventual correctness robust to every permitted perturbation, without a supplied stabilization horizon.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier polynomial dynamics characterizations treated discrete or continuous executions separately; the claimed new point is one common field with unit step independent of horizon. Historical comparison is manuscript-reported and not independently checked. Exact frozen parameters and scale-dependent shrinking noise are essential, and this is not invariance of arbitrary polynomial fields.

score_reasons.significance: Substantial unification of discrete and continuous analog complexity with explicit precision/space guarantees, but primarily a specialist realization theorem.
score_reasons.novelty: The same internal polynomial clock and field work for every admissible mesh, using interval gains instead of multiplying worst one-step errors.
score_reasons.depth: The 93-page proof combines robust overlapping gates, comparator cones, stack-height telescoping, forced Euler limits and common safety certificates.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully explains exact parameters, shrinking disturbance budgets, distinct section times and nonpractical constants, with a useful separation of theorem and compiler obligations.

checked: Inspected the compiler interface and analytic roadmap: local defect Delta=(1+log(1/epsilon))(epsilon^(1/4)+nu), error B Gamma T Delta, and interval stack gain O(1/h). The K/4>c+2 condition pays for time h^-c and two inverse-scale factors.

Traced Proposition 40 soundness: deterministic rounding to b=ceil(r)s+3 bits is an allowed disturbed execution; its finite compact state set has 2^O(s) states, so a state after that many updates lies on the eventual cycle and must carry the correct answer. Fixed-degree exact polynomial evaluation and the counter use O(s) space.

Inspected weighted-grid estimates, convex-lock update control, clock and cut-separation hypotheses, and the common-certificate Euler-limit argument for measurable forcing. These are not a verification of the compiler.
remaining: The central robust polynomial clock/comparator construction, local cycle invariant, full stack normal form and common polynomial safety-certificate existence proof are not audited. Full verification of the 93-page realization would require checking these interdependent analytic lemmas.

papers.title: Canonical Graph Decompositions via Local Separations
papers.authors: Raphael W. Jacobs, Paul Knappe, Jan Kurkofka

review.title: Canonical Graph Decompositions via Local Separations
review.authors: Raphael W. Jacobs, Paul Knappe, Jan Kurkofka

score_reasons.significance: Makes an important structural decomposition accessible algorithmically.
score_reasons.novelty: Local bottlenecks and a replacement for globally ordered nested separations provide genuinely new structural language.
score_reasons.depth: Extensive lifting, crossing, displacement and folding arguments connect finite data to infinite-cover tangles.
score_reasons.exposition: The introduction carefully explains the local/global obstacle and scope, though the substantial technical dependencies require considerable reader effort.

checked: Checked why an always-halting algorithm with a one-way 'order too large' certificate does not decide the threshold: it can also output a decomposition above the guaranteed threshold.
Traced the stated construction dependencies and verified the connected-path justification in the global crossing criterion.
remaining: The key lifting/projection and unique-crossing correspondence, nested-set construction, and full graph-decomposition reconstruction need a targeted long-proof audit. The separate efficient algorithm is outside this submission's proved results.

review.area: Structural graph theory and canonical decompositions
review.summary: Constructs canonical graph-decompositions from finite local separations, replacing an inherently infinite-cover construction. The always-halting algorithm either outputs a decomposition or certifies that the requested order exceeds the guaranteed locality threshold.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier canonical local-connectivity decompositions were defined through usually infinite coverings. This paper supplies a finite combinatorial construction; the polynomial-time/FPT bounds displayed as Theorem B are announced in separate work, not proved here. It does not decide the stated undecidable threshold predicate.

papers.title: Optimal PRGs for Low-Degree Polynomials over Polynomial-Size Fields
papers.authors: Gil Cohen, Noam Goldgraber

review.title: Optimal PRGs for Low-Degree Polynomials over Polynomial-Size Fields
review.authors: Gil Cohen, Noam Goldgraber
review.summary: Explicit PRG for degree-d n-variate polynomials over any-characteristic F_q, with q>=C(d log d)^4/epsilon^2, statistical error epsilon and seed O(d log n+log q). A conditional trace reduction converts optimal generators at q approximately d^delta into binary-field seed O(d^{1/(1-delta)} log n).
review.prior_frontier: Prior optimal seeds required field exponential in d or dependent on n, with characteristic limitations. Binary-field generators are incomparable; prior comparison not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Achieves optimal seed at polynomial field size without characteristic restrictions.
score_reasons.novelty: Polynomial-valued hitting sets suppress exponentially many bad factors; Hensel lifting replaces large-characteristic machinery.
score_reasons.depth: Irreducibility preservation and algebraic decompositions with precise error accounting.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates proved large-field construction from conditional small-field route.

checked: Traced final statistical-distance argument conditional on Proposition 5.1 and indecomposable equidistribution: bad restrictions <=2cd/q, degree <=4d log d, and triangle inequality recover epsilon.
Checked trace reduction degree dq/2, requiring q >= (dq/2)^delta, hence degree O(d^{1/(1-delta)}).
Seed bookkeeping: ell=O(log(1+d/log q)); ell log q=O(d+log q), so extra field samples fit stated seed (with usual n>=2 convention).
remaining: Audit PHSG construction and seed bounds, Hensel bad-locus Lemma 3.8, Gauss/indecomposability equivalences and external equidistribution theorem.
Handle small d,n and exact uniform sampling from non-power-of-two seed spaces in the explicit PRG definition.

papers.title: From Block Orthogonality to Decidability in Complex-Weighted Counting CSP
papers.authors: Chenghua Liu, Boning Meng

review.title: From Block Orthogonality to Decidability in Complex-Weighted Counting CSP
review.authors: Chenghua Liu, Boning Meng
review.summary: Gives a total exact decision procedure for Cai–Chen complex algebraic-weight #CSP tractability over any finite domain, proves block orthogonality alone implies the type-partition and Mal’tsev conditions, and extends to occurrence-multiple #CSPd.
review.prior_frontier: Cai–Chen supplied a dichotomy with an infinite-family criterion whose decidability was open. This gives termination, not an efficient polynomial-time meta-classifier; exact algebraic input encoding is essential.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves effectivity of a broad weighted counting dichotomy and simplifies its structural criterion.
score_reasons.novelty: Compresses bad row witnesses to arity q²+1 and converts universal polynomial identities into finite tensor-character isomorphism tests.
score_reasons.depth: Must handle complex cancellation, purification, roots of unity, pinned isomorphism and construction of a common Mal’tsev operation.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates finite termination from complexity and documents replacing a faulty simple-instance dependency with an all-instance theorem.

checked: Traced finite certificate disjunction-to-polynomial conversion: choosing one violated equation per certificate produces a nonzero product iff every certificate fails.
Checked multiplicative-character linear independence by subtracting the relation at a glued instance, and the tensor realization of monomials including conjugates and constant degree.
Inspected the pinned isomorphism statement and its twin condition; the paper explicitly notes a counterexample to a prior simple-instance strengthening.
remaining: Audit purification invariance and witness compression, the full pinned isomorphism proof, Skolem–Mahler–Lech cancellation control, common Mal’tsev construction and degree-restricted gadgets.

papers.title: Fatness and Flatness
papers.authors: Arnold Filtser, Hung Le, Nikolas Mählmann, Marcin Pilipczuk, Michał Pilipczuk

review.title: Fatness and Flatness
review.authors: Arnold Filtser, Hung Le, Nikolas Mählmann, Marcin Pilipczuk, Michał Pilipczuk
review.summary: Characterizes hereditary induced-shallow-minor-free classes equivalently by fat-shallow-minor exclusion, drill-flatness and exclusion of large induced subdivided cliques/webs. Gives a quantitative improvement step yielding fixed-radius ball deletion and polynomial overhead. Extends drill-flatness to length spaces excluding shallow delta-fat clique minors, with drill radius at least 25 sqrt(alpha delta), and derives bounded large-scale epsilon-scatter dimension. Consequently NORM k-CLUSTERING admits an FPT approximation with (1+epsilon)OPT plus O(delta/epsilon^2)||1||; not a pure multiplicative EPAS at arbitrarily small scales.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the nowhere-dense/uniform-quasi-wideness characterization and prior minor-free scatter-dimension methods to induced/fat minors. The fat-minor quasi-isometry conjecture is reported false, so the structural extension is not a consequence of it. Prior-result novelty not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A useful structural equivalence covering substantially broader graph classes, with a concrete first general clustering consequence for fat-minor-free metrics.
score_reasons.novelty: Replaces small vertex deletion by bounded-radius drilling and obtains an extremal proof of scatteredness improvement without the older branching-index machinery.
score_reasons.depth: Coordinates induced models, Ramsey extraction, length-space separation around enlarged holes and metric coarsening.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes hereditary hypotheses, metric scale dependence and unavoidable additive error; quantitative proofs are long but organized.

checked: Read the induced scatteredness-improvement proof: either a large local ball or a larger scattered subset exists, or many short paths with mutually nonadjacent middle segments produce an induced subdivided shallow clique. Inspected its iterative drilling and radius-37 bookkeeping.

Checked the final coarsening reduction: snap clients and facilities to a maximal r0-scattered net, preserving the client multiset and changing costs by at most 2r0||1|| each way. Small-radius scatters then have order at most two; a prior bounded-scatter algorithm yields total additive (4+2epsilon)r0||1||.
Checked the parameter substitution alpha=2r, beta=epsilon*r/3 and r>=11250 delta/epsilon^2, which meets the metric drill-radius requirement.
remaining: The full hereditary equivalence (notably Ramsey extraction), length-space fat-model construction and iterative enlarged-hole proof, and the external scatter-based clustering algorithm were not audited.

papers.authors: Kegong Shi, Hongfei Sun

review.title: Robust Exact Realization of Pairwise Boolean Statistics
review.authors: Kegong Shi, Hongfei Sun

score_reasons.significance: A substantive exact-rounding theorem for a specialized but natural marginal-realization problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Hierarchical rectangle exchanges and robust reserve geometry address coupled pairwise residuals.
score_reasons.depth: Uniform correction, matrix concentration, constructive discrepancy and lattice constraints must all align.
score_reasons.exposition: The explicit model, promise, runtime encoding and carefully limited sharpness claims are helpful.

checked: Verified the four-row switch changes only cross-pair counts by (u−v)(w−z), preserving total and singleton counts.
Checked the dimension-sum recurrence for O(n² log n) reserves and the counting lower bound L≥m log2(2t+1).
remaining: Uniform correction-ball concentration after forbidden-row conditioning, support-function feasibility, constructive discrepancy rounder and collision/restart bit complexity remain to be audited.

review.summary: Shows exact realization of integer total/singleton/pairwise Boolean counts sufficiently deep inside the fractional zonotope, even after forbidding a constant fraction of cube rows. Uses O(n² log n) reserved rows and a Las Vegas algorithm polynomial in the explicit table size 2^n.
review.prior_frontier: General discrepancy provides approximate rounding, while this result repairs to exact specified pairwise statistics under a quantitative interior promise. Runtime is polynomial in the exponential table length, not in the number n of Boolean coordinates; tightness is for reserve information/freedom, not the minimum sufficient depth.

papers.authors: Hongyi Chen, Tianyi Zhang

review.title: Nearly Optimal Sparse Navigable Graphs in General Metrics
review.authors: Hongyi Chen, Tianyi Zhang
review.summary: Randomized O(n^2 log^2 n)-time construction of an alpha-navigable directed graph for any metric and alpha>=1, with O(log n) times optimal edges, separately per source; handles distance ties and has no aspect-ratio dependence.
review.prior_frontier: Prior exact-alpha logarithmic approximation ~min(n OPT_alpha,n^2.5); near-quadratic existed only at alpha=1 with distinct distances. Claimed lower bounds match up to logs; not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves near-quadratic construction across the full navigability parameter range.
score_reasons.novelty: Couples set-cover instances via common metric pivots and sampled coverage proposals.
score_reasons.depth: Frequency pruning plus adaptive validation avoids constructing all cubic incidences.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear distinction between exact-alpha and bicriteria guarantees and explicit ties.

checked: Verified each-source set-cover decomposition and OPT=sum of source optima.

Checked pivot logic: an uncovered target has d(s,t)/alpha <= distance to nearest pivot; all covering intermediate points lie strictly before that pivot, hence sampled order statistics bound its residual frequency.
Traced standard greedy maximum-coverage shrinkage and treatment n<=1.
remaining: Audit shared-list data structure, sample uniformity after adaptive filtering, stagewise failure union and O(n^2 log^2 n) amortization.

papers.title: The Computational Complexity of Concurrent Stochastic Games: Exact Value and Approximation
papers.authors: Ali Asadi, Krishnendu Chatterjee

review.title: The Computational Complexity of Concurrent Stochastic Games: Exact Value and Approximation
review.authors: Ali Asadi, Krishnendu Chatterjee
review.area: Algorithmic game theory; stochastic games and real complexity
review.summary: For finite concurrent zero-sum stochastic games with limit-average or reachability objectives, value approximation lies in TFNP and its gap decision in NP∩coNP. Exact threshold decision lies in ∃R∩co-∃R and is PosSLP-hard even with deterministic transitions and two actions per player.
review.prior_frontier: Improves TFNP[NP] approximation verification and PSPACE exact upper bounds; strengthens SQRT-SUM hardness. Does not provide a polynomial-time value algorithm.

score_reasons.significance: Advances both approximate and exact complexity classifications for a central stochastic-game model.
score_reasons.novelty: Succinct signed power-series numbers and convex/concave value transformations yield polynomial certificates despite doubly exponentially small strategy probabilities.
score_reasons.depth: Needs exact symbolic comparison, shrinking Bellman intervals, delicate small-gap representations and arithmetic-circuit simulation.
score_reasons.exposition: Explains why ordinary fixed-point precision and floating-point strategies fail, and keeps search, promise and exact decision statements separate.

checked: Traced the convex transform argument: nondecreasing convex f≤identity converts the Bellman equality/inequality into L≤Ψ(L), with action quantifiers correct for maximizing and minimizing MDPs.
Checked the witness verifier uses only constant-degree products of succinct power-series entries and exact comparisons, rather than iterating a near-undiscounted Bellman map.
Read the exact-threshold separation strategy using shifted thresholds and repeated-squaring encodings of tiny constants.
remaining: Audit existence of polynomial-size convex increments and lower bounds on distinct value gaps, symbolic arithmetic complexity, perturbation of strategies, multiplication gadget and algebraic threshold separation.

papers.title: The Multiple Unicast Conjecture is False
papers.authors: Mark Braverman, Zhongtian He

review.title: The Multiple Unicast Conjecture is False
review.authors: Mark Braverman, Zhongtian He
review.summary: Refutes the undirected multiple-unicast conjecture with a causal linear code over F9: a 182-vertex subgraph of the PG(2,9) incidence graph has 735 unit-capacity edges and 157 independent sessions of rate one, while every fractional multicommodity flow has common rate at most 147/157. The code has a fixed chronological vertex order and each physical edge transmits exactly one symbol per execution, so pipelining achieves the stated rate. A prior amplification theorem gives an unbounded polylogarithmic gap. A separate 166-session construction concerns nondeterministic certificates only.
review.prior_frontier: The Li–Li conjecture ruled out any coding advantage for undirected multiple unicast. The manuscript explicitly acknowledges concurrent refutations via Fourier circuits and a reversible-circuit approach; this result supplies a small explicit finite-field example, not sole-priority ownership. The amplification theorem was checked in its primary source.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a long-standing central conjecture with implications for conditional computational lower bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: An explicit projective-plane/Reed–Solomon construction with a causal orientation realizes a new coding/routing separation; it is independent of the concurrent circuit routes.
score_reasons.depth: The decisive finite construction combines self-dual local quartic codes, a 166-dimensional compatible subspace and an orientation balanced by two nine-edge correction sets.
score_reasons.exposition: Nineteen pages give every graph and schedule datum, a short algebraic dimension proof, and a clear separation of nondeterministic and causal models.

checked: Traced the projective-plane graph and local homogeneous quartic codes, including the Frobenius twist at line vertices. Five evaluations determine every local codeword; the characteristic-three power sums prove local self-orthogonality independent of representative scaling.

Traced the dimension argument: 166 retained bidegree-(4,4) monomials evaluate compatibly. Vanishing finite evaluations imply a degree-52 polynomial h(Z cross Z^9,Z^3) vanishes on 91 distinct projective lines, so it is zero. The excluded monomial divisibilities make all substituted leading terms distinct, forcing independence.

Checked the causal proof: oriented candidate in/out-degrees equal five; C-outdegree equals J-indegree. Each vertex has exactly five already available values. Zero C-values remove at most nine dimensions; restriction to the 157 B-edges is injective by chronological zero-input induction, hence bijective. Interpolation computes the unique compatible extension.

Independently reconstructed F9 arithmetic and the entire graph from the manuscript, extracted all 175 deleted edges and the 182-vertex permutation, and verified every orientation constraint. Independently simulated all 157 basis-message vectors through all 182 interpolation systems: every decoded vector equals its corresponding basis vector. Verified 735 physical edges, 157 sessions, 166 distinct dimension-proof leading terms and the projective-plane absence of four-cycles. Script audits/audit286.py; results audits/audit286-result.json.

Checked throughput and routing arithmetic: the fixed acyclic execution pipelines at one symbol per physical edge per time slot; each deleted-edge demand has graph distance at least five, so total load is at least 785r and r<=735/785=147/157.
Consulted Braverman–Garg–Schvartzman ITCS 2017 Theorem 1 and its common undirected throughput model: any fixed gap above one yields an infinite family with polylogarithmic coding advantage.
remaining: The older amplification theorem was checked for applicability, not re-proved. Concurrent priority claims and the separate circuit constructions were not audited. The independent finite verifier supports the exact construction but is not a formal proof certificate.

papers.title: Bayesian Optimal Stopping: Invincible Prophets and Achievable Philosophers
papers.authors: Alireza AmaniHamedani, Ali Aouad, Senem Isik, Thomas Kesselheim, Amin Saberi

review.title: Bayesian Optimal Stopping: Invincible Prophets and Achievable Philosophers
review.authors: Alireza AmaniHamedani, Ali Aouad, Senem Isik, Thomas Kesselheim, Amin Saberi

score_reasons.significance: A useful unification and strong approximation guarantee for learning-sensitive stopping policies.
score_reasons.novelty: The coupled improvement of an algorithm and its dual martingale is more substantial than applying a fixed threshold rule.
score_reasons.depth: Repeated updates and importance-weighted estimation require delicate multiplicative error control.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper explicitly distinguishes its benchmarks, access models and the almost-polynomial versus PTAS guarantees.

checked: Checked the 1/q threshold density normalization, base/surplus layer-cake calculation and bounded optional-stopping use in the single primal-improvement step.
Verified that the general runtime and value-oracle assumptions are materially stronger qualifications than the abstract phrase 'achievable philosopher' alone suggests.
remaining: Validity and progress of all dual updates, rare-event Monte Carlo control, full runtime recurrence and the finite-K prophet lower bounds need further audit.

review.summary: Approximates the Bayes-optimal stopping policy through iterative primal/dual martingale improvement, while showing that prophet competitiveness approaches worst-case limits as the number of hidden worlds grows.
review.prior_frontier: Separates computational approximation of the online optimum from information-theoretic comparison with the offline prophet. The general scheme has an input-size exponent involving log*|I| and is not a PTAS; IID and bounded-world independent cases obtain a PTAS. The correlated model assumes conditional probability and conditional maximum-value oracles, stronger than sampling access.

papers.title: Unitary Complexity in Polynomial Space
papers.authors: William Kretschmer, Ewin Tang

review.title: Unitary Complexity in Polynomial Space
review.authors: William Kretschmer, Ewin Tang
review.summary: Under robust clean/projective unitary-class definitions, unitaryPSPACE equals polynomial-space entrywise approximability. Every such unitary either has no efficient synthesis relative to any classical oracle, or admits one using NEXP witness-bit oracles. Quantum commitments imply synthesis hardness or BPP != NEXP.
review.prior_frontier: Builds on quantum/classical polynomial-space equivalence and state/column synthesis. Stated synthesis resolution by another manuscript is explicitly not assumed; low-error overhead matters. Prior dependencies not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Links a major quantum cryptography foundation to classical separations and clarifies unitary-space classes.
score_reasons.novelty: NEXP witness truth tables replace arbitrary helpful classical oracles, with canonical phase/garbage distinctions.
score_reasons.depth: Space-efficient matrix synthesis, clean ancilla extensions and relativized witness extraction.
score_reasons.exposition: Careful phase, garbage, oracle and low-error qualifications prevent inflated consequences.

checked: Traced central witness-verifier reduction on pp.35–36 conditional on entrywise characterization: truth table size exponential, entry precision gamma=delta/(2 sqrt(2^(n+a))), column error <=3delta, operator error <=6delta sqrt(2^n)=epsilon.
Checked NC=NP padding/witness circuit recursion has polynomial space even with exponentially long oracle truth-table input.
remaining: Audit entrywise characterization, column-to-unitary external synthesis dependency, clean-extension Lemmas 5.3/5.7, phase conventions and cryptographic EFI reduction.
Do not assume the outside claimed unitary-synthesis result; it is not verified here.

papers.title: A Deterministic Near-Linear Time Approximation Algorithm for Restricted Shortest Paths in Directed Graphs
papers.authors: Vikrant Ashvinkumar

review.title: A Deterministic Near-Linear Time Approximation Algorithm for Restricted Shortest Paths in Directed Graphs
review.authors: Vikrant Ashvinkumar
review.summary: Deterministic bicriteria (1+ε,1+ε) single-source restricted shortest paths in soft-O(m log(nW)/ε^9), with a compact witness representation and deterministic path retrieval. Fixed k-resource extension has ε^(-(4k+1)) dependence.
review.prior_frontier: Improves randomized sub-mn directed algorithms to near-linear dependence on graph size, bypassing the hopset approach. Depends logarithmically on length aspect ratio W and initially uses exact real arithmetic; strongly polynomial single-source remains open.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the graph-size dependence of a fundamental bicriteria routing problem up to logarithms and aspect-ratio dependence.
score_reasons.novelty: Independent multi-tick Poisson clocks turn resource feasibility into an adaptive escape-probability DP; exponential potentials derandomize actual path retrieval.
score_reasons.depth: The core proof combines label-setting monotonicity, adaptive-clock concentration and a conditional-expectation witness construction without heavy machinery.
score_reasons.exposition: The 14-page argument is compact and self-contained, with separate completeness, soundness and deterministic witness proofs.

checked: Traced all of the main positive-weight exact-real argument. Higher tick states are finalized first; initializing to artificial-tick transitions ensures DP(v,i,j)≤higher-state values, making every edge relaxation at least the popped predecessor value and validating the Dijkstra label-setting invariant.
Checked completeness from two Poisson upper tails and soundness by coupling adaptive accumulated resource use to independent Poisson processes; artificial ticks only hasten explosion.

Traced deterministic potential: expected exponential terms remain fixed under edge traversal, artificial ticks decrease them, and a potential below one forces a nonexploding successor. At termination an overbudget resource would make its term at least one because q=Theta(ε^-2).

Checked termination via tick increases or earlier extraction order, q^2 layers times q^2 relaxation work and geometric length guesses give ε^-9. Zero-weight edges can use deterministic zero ticks; zero objective optima require a preliminary zero-length-subgraph shortest-cost computation.
remaining: The stated word-RAM implementation relies on a brief probability-truncation claim; a fully explicit precision/error proof was not supplied or independently completed. The fixed-k extension is a short sketch, not separately audited in detail.

The exact-real model must support the specified Poisson probabilities/exponentials; this audit certifies the mathematical DP and real-arithmetic complexity, not a complete finite-precision implementation.

papers.title: Optimal testing of fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states
papers.authors: Vishnu Iyer, Bryan O'Gorman, Ojas Parekh, Kevin Thompson, Andrew Zhao

review.title: Optimal testing of fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states
review.authors: Vishnu Iyer, Bryan O’Gorman, Ojas Parekh, Kevin Thompson, Andrew Zhao
review.summary: Gives optimal Theta(epsilon^-2) copy complexity for testing whether an unknown pure state is fermionic Gaussian (with fixed parity), a Slater determinant, bosonic Gaussian, zero-mean bosonic Gaussian, or coherent, independent of mode count and, for bosons, energy. Constant-copy base tests use two copies except general bosonic Gaussian states, which use three. Tolerant testing requires epsilon2>beta epsilon1 for a class-dependent constant beta>1; this is not an arbitrary-gap tolerant tester.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier bounds quoted in the manuscript depend polynomially on modes and, for bosons, energy; the previous fermionic bound is soft-O(n/epsilon^2). Historical comparisons were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Eliminates all mode and energy dependence in copy complexity for five physically important pure-state classes.
score_reasons.novelty: A common spectral-gap-to-distance theorem turns algebraic tests into robust optimal testers.
score_reasons.depth: The general Lojasiewicz argument and class-specific spin, unitary, metaplectic and Jacobi representation calculations are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: The common framework and explicit optical tests clarify the result, although the 91-page proof requires substantial specialized reading and contains an isolated coefficient typo.

checked: Traced the general projector argument: decompose rejection amplitude by the number of factors orthogonal to psi, symmetrize onto m copies, and use T^2>=Delta T to obtain ||grad r||^2>=4r(c0-c1r). The combinatorial coefficient ratios yield c0=(m(m-1)Delta-k(k-1))/(m-k) and c1=m+k-1.

Traced the gradient-flow distance conversion and Bernoulli testing reduction, including the necessary multiplicative tolerant gap. Checked the general-boson substitution k=3,m=7,Delta=7/45 gives alpha=2/135, agreeing with Theorem 6.1.
Checked the fixed-parity convention in the fermionic preliminaries and the idealized general-boson implementation: a Gaussian mode transformation followed by exact Fock-number comparison.
remaining: The class-specific representation decompositions and spectral gaps, the lower-bound hard-state constructions, infinite-Fock-space analytic details and implementation resource costs have not been fully audited. Copy complexity does not itself bound precision or photon-counting implementation cost.
issues: Minor verified coefficient typo: page 23, Eq. (3.13), prints -7r, while Lemma 3.2 requires -(m+k-1)r=-9r for k=3,m=7. The same line’s c-prime=(7Delta-1)/6 and the general formula used on pages 27–28 and 63 use the correct coefficient, so this does not presently invalidate the stated testing bound. Visual PDF inspection confirmed the typo.

review.summary: Bounded-error randomized value-oracle SFM requires Omega(n log n) worst-case expected queries; even deciding whether any prescribed set is a minimizer has this lower bound. Earlier CGJS hard family instead admits Theta(n log log n) randomized queries.

score_reasons.novelty: Layered functions suppress good-set leakage and hide a bit in one special set.

score_reasons.exposition: Precise expected-query/error conventions and clear explanation why old hard family fails.

checked: Checked decision-to-search reduction uses at most two extra value queries and preserves error.

Confirmed layer arithmetic n=2k^2: Omega(k) large layers times Omega(k log k) yields Omega(n log n), provided stop-layer aggregation is valid; proof explicitly avoids naively charging multi-layer queries repeatedly.
remaining: Audit submodularity with single-point slack, randomized one-layer Lemma 3.1, simulation/stop-layer direct-sum and expected-time conversion.
Verify reduction to arbitrary prescribed set and CGJS HiddenPermutation equivalence.

review.summary: For independent costs in [c,cbar], unrestricted-bid first-price procurement has worst-case PoA R=cbar/c; restricting bids to that interval gives tight 1+e^-2(R−1). An optimized deterministic cap with outside-option cost cbar achieves sqrt(R)/e+O(1), order-optimal among regular phantom mechanisms.
review.prior_frontier: Transfers the tight value-auction welfare bound of Jin–Lu via reflection, and contrasts it with unbounded-bid mixed equilibria. Prior theorem and phantom-class novelty not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Sharp cost-sensitive guarantees clarify a common auction model, but the main bounded-bid result is an affine transfer of an existing welfare theorem.
score_reasons.novelty: The heterogeneous heavy-tail equilibrium and interval-only phantom-cap comparison supply the principal new ingredients.
score_reasons.depth: Equilibrium survival functions and cap optimization are elementary; the general phantom lower bound needs additional regularity analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates cost bounds, bid bounds and outside-option costs, with explicit equilibrium and information assumptions.

checked: Traced the heavy-tail mixed equilibrium: opponents survival product makes utility constant, and scaled bids become identically distributed as L grows.
Checked balancing 1+e^-2(T−1) and R/T gives the displayed positive quadratic root and sqrt(R)/e leading term.
remaining: Verify regular-phantom lower bound, tie handling and the value-auction dependency; no full main-proof audit.

papers.title: The Hard-Core Model on Bipartite Spectral Expanders: Counting and Sampling at All Fugacities
papers.authors: Ijay Narang, Will Perkins

review.title: The Hard-Core Model on Bipartite Spectral Expanders: Counting and Sampling at All Fugacities
review.authors: Ijay Narang, Will Perkins
review.summary: For fixed degree Delta and spectral bound sigma on a regular bipartite biadjacency matrix, gives an FPRAS and approximate sampler for lambda<=(1-xi)/sigma. A high-fugacity FPTAS applies when log(1+lambda)>=C sigma^2/(Delta^2-sigma^2) log(eDelta). These cover every fugacity if sigma<=c(Delta^2/log(eDelta))^(1/3), giving an efficiently checkable all-fugacity certificate for sufficiently high-degree random regular bipartite graphs. Degree and slack are fixed parameters; this is not a uniform polynomial-in-Delta algorithm.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier all-fugacity random-regular results used additional random-instance expansion properties rather than a single efficiently checkable spectral certificate. The manuscript cites those algorithms and external spectral-mixing/long-range-order criteria; their priority and proofs were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A deterministic spectral certificate extends tractable counting beyond the usual uniqueness regime and certifies instances previously handled only with high probability.
score_reasons.novelty: Discrete quadratic localization cancels the exceptional bipartite rank-one direction in a dependency matrix, then reconstructs the original law by an exact positive Gaussian mixture.
score_reasons.depth: Combines all-pinnings mixing bounds with phase concentration and a scale-sensitive polymer expansion.
score_reasons.exposition: The two fugacity regimes, precise thresholds and algebraic cancellation are presented clearly in 33 pages.

checked: Read the exact dependency-matrix computation: same-side entries q-1 and opposite-side q^-1-1 minus adjacency/q cancel the Delta J/n direction. Weighted congruence bounds the remaining term by t sigma/sqrt(q).

Checked the discrete Gaussian mixture identity by integer translation and the truncation tail bound using |imbalance|<=n and successive mass ratio at most exp(-Delta). Small n<Delta/xi is explicitly enumerated for fixed Delta, avoiding q=0.
Read Tanner expansion, polymer weight decay and the Kotecky–Preiss connected-set estimate.
remaining: The external dependency-matrix mixing theorem and Hadas–Peled phase-concentration criterion, full annealing/mixture implementation and complete phase-overlap error bounds still need correctness auditing.

review.summary: Positive additive valuations need not admit a Pareto-optimal EFX allocation: explicit four-agent/eight-good counterexample. For every alpha>2/3, four agents and nine positive-valued goods suffice to rule out Pareto-optimal alpha-EFX. Does not disprove existence of EFX alone.

score_reasons.novelty: Small symmetric positive-valued examples expose unavoidable trading improvements.

score_reasons.exposition: Transparent valuation tables, three-case proof and explicit dominating allocations.

checked: Traced Theorem 1: large goods must be singleton bundles; dihedral symmetry and utility totals reduce to three profiles; verified explicit dominating allocations in Figures 2–3.

Independent exhaustive enumeration of all 65,536 complete allocations found 168 EFX allocations, each Pareto dominated; none Pareto-optimal EFX. Script/results retained in audits/check296.py and check296.json.

remaining: Appendix A nondegenerate perturbation was read but not exhaustively checked; main two theorems are independent of it.

checked: Traced strategy description counting: O(q+c) moves, poly(n)-support approximations, O(n)^(O(q+c)) histories and adaptive hybrid error.
Checked importance-weighted compression normalization: pi/p≤n, expected sampled sum m, Hoeffding gives exp(−Omega(m epsilon²/n²)).

papers.title: Dimension Reduction and Coresets for Min-Sum k-Clustering
papers.authors: Asaf Dallal, Robert Krauthgamer

review.title: Dimension Reduction and Coresets for Min-Sum k-Clustering
review.authors: Asaf Dallal, Robert Krauthgamer
review.summary: For Euclidean min-sum k-clustering, a Gaussian projection to O(epsilon^-2(ddim log(1/epsilon)+log k+log log n)) dimensions preserves every partition cost with probability at least 4/5; alternatively O(epsilon^-2(log(1/epsilon)+log k+log aspect-ratio)) dimensions suffice. Metric doubling inputs admit a movement-based coreset of size epsilon^-O(ddim) k log n with nearest-neighbor movement, built near-linearly in n for fixed other parameters. Separate lower bounds require dependence on doubling dimension and epsilon^-2 log log n for Gaussian maps, and log n for movement coresets. Streaming results use three insertion-only passes or O(log n) dynamic passes and do not promise polynomial downstream optimization time.
review.prior_frontier: Previously the generic JL O(epsilon^-2 log n) bound was the available oblivious projection guarantee. Earlier min-sum coresets modify distances and have a different, incomparable preservation definition. Prior results were read through the manuscript comparison, not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Supplies two standard compact representations for a clustering objective that lacks the usual center-based structure.
score_reasons.novelty: Reference-cluster orientation and density-adaptive movement pay for cluster-cardinality-weighted pair errors rather than ordinary center distances.
score_reasons.depth: The projection proof, density packing and bootstrap for a constant-factor reference solution require distinct nontrivial arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise for-all-partitions guarantees and explicit streaming-pass and running-time caveats make the result assessable.

checked: Read the sparse-distortion-graph/reference-partition proof roadmap and the distinction between movement-based and prior modified-metric coresets.

Checked the density movement charge: rho(x)<=gamma_m(x)+OPT_hat/(km^2); multiplying by cluster cardinality and summing yields an additive OPT_hat/k per cluster. Triangle inequality doubles this bound and summing at most k clusters gives relative error. Singleton movement is addressed separately using nearest-neighbor distance.
Read the annular-reference bootstrap recurrence alpha_(t+1)<=O(rho)+alpha_t/2 and its explicit near-linear-in-n rather than uniform-in-all-parameters complexity.
remaining: The full distortion-graph/net projection proof, density-ring packing cardinality, lower-bound constructions, weighted bicriteria dependency and streaming implementations still need a correctness audit.

review.title: The Complexity of Choosing Parity Projections
review.authors: Karthik Sheshadri, Nicholas Smirnov
review.summary: For signed 2CNF, finding a nonempty cube of size <=k with identically-one parity derivative takes 2^{O(k^2)} poly(length) and has exponential kernel. Identically-zero counterpart has arbitrary computable coW[1] gap hardness even positive essential-variable instances with a supplied zero cube. Both unrestricted problems are Sigma_2^{parity P}-complete on positive 2CNF, with approximation/width refinements.
review.prior_frontier: Extends earlier fixed-k circuit coNP complexity and parity monomial prediction; FPT result is specifically 2CNF, not general circuits. Prior frontier not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Rich representation-sensitive classification of a cryptanalytic parity projection search problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Crown parity lifting encodes maximal monomials into positive 2CNF; sum-one versus sum-zero parameterization diverges.
score_reasons.depth: Combines symmetry/type compression, parity counting reductions and structural-width dynamic programming.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise table resolves an abstract ambiguity: FPT bound is for 2CNF, not arbitrary succinct Boolean functions.

checked: Fully traced Theorem 3.1 FPT algorithm: certificate hits every clause; maximal matching gives <=2k cover; outside variables have <=16^{2k} types; k representatives/type suffice by formula automorphism. Enumerating <=k subsets yields 2^{O(k^2)}.
Traced Lemma 3.2 checking candidate: parity sum of <=2^k products tested by reachable-row linear spans over F2, dimension <=2^k+1.
remaining: Audit crown lifting, zero-cube arbitrary-gap reduction, kernel deletion and binary-language dichotomy.
Width/round lower bounds and claimed assumptions require independent verification; no reliance here on manuscript claim that ETH was refuted.

review.title: Strong Lower Bounds for Weak Epsilon-Nets
review.authors: Sujoy Bhore, Reilly Browne, Da Wei Zheng
review.area: Discrete geometry; epsilon nets and piercing
review.summary: Proves f_3(r)=Omega(r^(3/2)) for weak 1/r nets of convex sets, and f_d(r)=Omega(r^gamma_d), gamma_d=0.5 floor((sqrt(8d+25)−1)/2), via shifted grid quadratic lifts. Gives corresponding fractional-piercing gaps and Hadwiger–Debrunner lower bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Claims the first polynomial-superlinear lower bounds in fixed d≥3, improving r log^(d−1)r; the exponent grows like sqrt(d/2), not d/2. Prior literature frontier not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: If the stated prior frontier is accurate, breaks a longstanding geometric lower-bound barrier already in dimension three.
score_reasons.novelty: A rational vertical shift forces five grid incidences of a quadratic to imply a square; moment matrices extend the construction to higher-dimensional flats.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines interpolation integrality, PSD rank-one convexity and a dimension-sensitive incidence charging argument.
score_reasons.exposition: The compact construction and 3D warm-up are effective; the singular Gaussian-elimination and shifted-intercept notation need explicit clarification.

checked: Traced the 4D variance reconstruction and per-line incidence charge; verified the 3D shift tau=1/(9q^5) visually.
Checked the five-root lemma: cleared interpolation denominators ≤q³, nonzero integer discrepancy forced below 8/9, then a degree-four polynomial vanishes at five roots.
Traced general Lemma 2: Gram range fixes the span, each k-flat contains ≤q^k grid points and belongs to ≤q^(s−k) hyperplanes, and at most four flats suffice.
Justified singular elimination through the Gram kernel; use h=b+tau as the intercept coordinate. Checked constant, square and nonsquare quadratic cases and the ≤4q^s replacement budget.
Checked rank-one PSD lift implies convex position on a nonzero-intercept hyperplane, incidence demand gives Omega(q^(s+2)), and dimension inversion yields gamma_d.
remaining: External prior-frontier claims and referenced standard fractional-piercing/Hadwiger–Debrunner equivalences were not independently re-proved.
resolved_notes: Expository clarification: the elimination variable for the last-coordinate offset must be h=b+tau; singular free coefficients vanish on the Gram range and hence do not change its intersection flat. This supplies the justification omitted in the short Gaussian-elimination sentence.

papers.title: Competitive Random-Order Correlation k-Clustering

review.title: Competitive Random-Order Correlation k-Clustering
review.authors: Mahsa Derakhshan, Andisheh Ghasemi, Rajmohan Rajaraman, Omer Wasim, Tegan Wilson
review.summary: For disagreement-minimizing correlation clustering with at most k clusters, converts an unconstrained alpha-approximation to a 1+2alpha+O(epsilon) approximation, hence 3.97+O(epsilon) using the cited 1.485 algorithm. In random-order irrevocable vertex arrivals, Balanced Pivot is O(log^4 n)-competitive in expectation for all graphs; Uniform Pivot is O(log^3 n) for disjoint cliques. Lower bounds are Omega(log k) for arbitrary online algorithms and Omega(log^2 k) for algorithms never splitting disjoint cliques, on n=O(k log k) instances.
review.prior_frontier: Previously constant-k PTAS algorithms were exponential in k, and random-order unconstrained Pivot achieved factor three; the imposed cluster cap changes the online behavior fundamentally. Prior-frontier claims were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Provides both a general-k offline constant approximation and polylogarithmic random-order guarantees with genuine logarithmic lower bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: A least-current-load modification of Pivot is analyzed via projected final loads, fixed optimal almost-cliques and random stopping-time decompositions.
score_reasons.depth: The analysis handles strong correlations between the kth-pivot time, unseen vertices and eventual cluster sizes; the 58-page development is technically substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: The lower-bound distinction between arbitrary and non-splitting algorithms is explicit, and the proof overview explains the new dependencies.

checked: Read the reduction through a disjoint-clique instance and the matching-order a(I)s(I) offline bounds.

Read the hard instance of k-1 cliques of order log k and two singleton vertices: OPT=1, unseen cliques remain indistinguishable from singletons at early arrivals. Full information-theoretic symmetry argument remains to be audited.

Checked the projected-load inequality and Lemma 7.9 conditioning: once a pivot arrives, its eventual captured-neighbor set is fixed, so remaining arrivals into that set are hypergeometric. Read the no-early-pivot hazard bound in Lemma 7.10.

The manuscript claims Lean verification but explicitly assumes Chernoff/hypergeometric concentration, negative association facts and Pivot’s factor-three guarantee; no independent Lean build or correspondence audit has been performed.
remaining: Complete stopping-time cost summations, the lower-bound indistinguishability proof, the disjoint-clique PTAS and the claimed formalization still require auditing.

review.title: The Power and Limits of Money Burning in Bilateral Trade
review.authors: Moshe Babaioff, Noam Nisan, Ariel Shaulker

score_reasons.significance: A sharp and counterintuitive separation in a foundational mechanism-design setting.
score_reasons.novelty: Identifies randomized weak budget balance as substantially stronger than distributions over posted prices.
score_reasons.depth: The construction and impossibility depend on compatible allocation/payment inequalities and carefully chosen distributions.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions, benchmark distinctions and complementary positive/negative results are clearly presented.

checked: Derived the payment identities from individual rationality, weak budget balance and the single-parameter incentive characterization, including zero payments without trade.
Checked the disjoint-interval limitation for randomized strongly budget-balanced posted prices and the separation's need for truthfulness in expectation over internal randomness.
remaining: The full grid mechanism's budget balance and surplus calculations, independent distributions and first-best impossibility constructions require audit.

review.summary: Shows that randomized truthful-in-expectation DSIC mechanisms may benefit both traders by arbitrarily large factors through money burning, yet cannot achieve constant approximation to first-best gains from trade under independent values.

papers.title: The Exact Communication Threshold for Parallel Repetition
papers.authors: Daiki Suruga

review.title: The Exact Communication Threshold for Parallel Repetition
review.authors: Daiki Suruga
review.summary: For every finite total two-player relation and arbitrary fixed input distribution, any worst-case communication rate strictly below zero-error internal information complexity yields exponentially small success on all n independent instances. Claims matching global-error amortized rates for distributional and randomized communication, with unrestricted rounds.
review.prior_frontier: Strengthens earlier small-rate/direct-product or fixed-round converses to exact information threshold; matching achievability invokes BR11 and Sur26. Prior dependencies not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Exact unrestricted-round strong-converse threshold is a substantial communication-complexity characterization.
score_reasons.novelty: Single-coordinate conditioning preserves coefficient one on communication rate, followed by KL-controlled protocol reconstruction.
score_reasons.depth: Information budget, local transcript simulation, zero-message coupling and near-zero-error continuity require careful interplay.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear difference between worst-case communication, expected communication and global versus per-coordinate error.

checked: Verified proposed local sampling is a valid protocol because each conditional uses only sender input and preceding transcript.

Traced entropy comparison conditional on product identity (37): constructing Q^n as backwards conditionals gives sum coordinate divergences =D(Q||P)-D(Q||Q^n), hence <=log(1/p), and Pinsker transfers error.

Completed the conditioned-coordinate extraction. Greedy conditioning adds at most log(1/p)/(−log(1−epsilon)) successful coordinates. Appending their outputs restores the rectangle factorization needed after conditioning: at an unselected coordinate the remaining prefix/suffix densities separate into an Alice factor and a Bob factor. Chain rules give averaged information at most R+O(log(1/p)/n) with coefficient exactly one on R.

Checked the new likelihood-ratio identity on pages17–19 in detail. The product of local single-coordinate simulation laws telescopes across adjacent coordinates: odd messages at i pair with even messages at i+1, while the boundary-message factors equal one because the original protocol is deterministic. The remaining input terms telescope too. The constructed backwards-sampled Q_n is a normalized distribution, and taking the logarithm gives sum_i D(q_i||P_i)=D(Q||P)−D(Q||Q_n)≤log(1/p). This justifies the crucial 1/n divergence bound without assuming the conditioned transcript is a valid protocol.

Checked the zero-message correlated sampler and finite-randomness implementation in Appendix C. Rejection sampling gives disagreement≤2TV/(1+TV); the finite joint distribution of all outputs replaces the infinite random sequence exactly. Comparing each party’s sample to the joint-input sample and applying Pinsker gives the stated square-root information error. This also proves zero information cost equals the zero-message optimal error.

Completed Appendix B’s zero-error continuity proof for total relations. The full-support mixture permits simultaneous bounded rectangle factors; thresholding each factor isolates a high-probability rectangle on which fixed local outputs must be valid. Rare fallback exchanges all inputs. The probability of fallback is O(epsilon^(1/16)) and its extra conditional entropy tends uniformly to zero, independently of the original protocol.

Checked public mixing of the low-error and zero-message protocols to achieve information cost exactly R. The inequality (a+b)sqrt(R+a)/(R+a+b)≤sqrt(a)+b/sqrt(R), together with the entropy continuity bound, gives the explicit positive-rate exponent; the constants2^(−28),5 and24 leave strict slack. Fixing all coins first extends the deterministic analysis to every randomized protocol with the same worst-case communication bound.
remaining: The new strong converse and continuity proof are traced. The matching achievability and randomized amortization conclusions use external Braverman–Rao compression, Suruga2026 achievability and the information-complexity minimax identity; these external results were not independently re-proved.

review.title: A Quadratic Bogolyubov Theorem and Quantum Worst-Case to Average-Case Reductions
review.authors: Davi Castro-Silva, Alexander Golovnev, Tom Gur, Julia Wolf
review.summary: A quadratic Bogolyubov theorem over F2 yields a bounded-complexity nonempty quadratic variety with seven-point correction from any positive-density set. An implicit quantum quadratic Goldreich–Levin algorithm gives worst-to-average reduction for quadratic maps in soft-O_alpha,delta(T+n^(5/2)) time with coefficient-oracle access.
review.prior_frontier: Extends additive-combinatorial linear-map reductions to quadratic structure; naive monomial lifting fails to preserve the uniform input distribution. This is not black-box correction from the average-case algorithm alone. Prior comparisons not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Links a new structural additive-combinatorics theorem with a uniform worst-to-average reduction for a natural nonlinear computation class.
score_reasons.novelty: Implicit quadratic correlator oracles avoid learning an explicit n²-size description, while sparse-shift tessellation handles inputs outside the variety.
score_reasons.depth: Requires characteristic-two local inverse/counting lemmas, stabilizer bootstrapping, and careful quantum verification and oracle-error composition.
score_reasons.exposition: The overview separates local correction, coefficient verification and sparse shifts; the 75-page proof has substantial prerequisite machinery.

checked: Read the formal algorithmic Bogolyubov theorem and its density-increment/rank-refinement implementation.
Traced sparse-shift support shrinking conditional on Warning’s theorem: root density q^-dr beats the Chernoff bad-support mass and O(q log n) rounds give constant support.
Checked that correcting Q(x+s) uses the sparse cross terms in O(|s|n²), and that verification requires separate access to Q coefficients.
remaining: Audit local U3 counting/inverse theorem in characteristic two, implicit QGL and complete quantum error/time composition.
Handle the small-n base case in Algorithm 3 by finding a root directly, rather than returning the initialization 1^n; this is an inexpensive repair within q^O(dr) cost.
issues: Two apparent local presentation defects: Algorithm 3 needs a base-case root search when n<20drq³, and the seven-point sampler on p16 should check nonempty subsets S⊆[3], not the empty subset. These do not by themselves refute the structural or complexity theorem.

papers.title: Thinning and Sprinkling: Robust Vertex Sampling and Almost Hamiltonicity
papers.authors: Micha Christoph, Zach Hunter, Benny Sudakov

review.title: Thinning and Sprinkling: Robust Vertex Sampling and Almost Hamiltonicity
review.authors: Micha Christoph, Zach Hunter, Benny Sudakov
review.summary: Develops thinning–sprinkling for vertex sampling. A p-random induced subgraph of a t-tough graph is Omega(p^2 t)-tough when p^2 t=omega(log n); a connected d-regular vertex-transitive graph remains (1-epsilon)-tough when p^2d=omega(log n). Applications give almost-spanning cycles for toughness omega(log^3 n), vertex-transitive degree omega(log^3 n log log n), and nearly regular lambda-expanders with lambda d=omega(log^3 n) and d=omega(log^3 n log log n). Also finds spanning bipartite Omega(k)-connected subgraphs for connectivity k=omega(log n). These are asymptotic almost-Hamiltonicity results, not proofs of full Hamiltonicity or the constant-toughness conjecture.
review.prior_frontier: The sharp Omega(p^2 k) connectivity sampling theorem is explicitly an existing result with a new proof. Claimed new almost-cycle bounds improve the known general tough/vertex-transitive guarantees and lower the standard sublinear-expander degree threshold from roughly log^70 n to omega(log^5 n). Historical bounds were not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Makes substantial progress on classical long-cycle questions under polylogarithmic structural assumptions.
score_reasons.novelty: A reusable nested-sampling argument turns failure witnesses into seeded components and destroys those components with independent sprinkling.
score_reasons.depth: The framework covers several connectivity notions and supports a reservoir-merging construction, including specialized vertex-transitive structure.
score_reasons.exposition: A compact 31-page manuscript clearly separates the re-proved classical sampling theorem from new robustness and almost-cycle applications.

checked: Traced the toughness thinning lemma: a failure with k components survives removal of its small witness and retention of k seeds with probability exponential in k p^2 t.

Traced the sprinkling mechanism: maximal short-path packing yields kt/2 candidate paths; unexplored seed endpoints remain independent, giving constant success probability per round. More than k log_2 n successful growth rounds contradict the representative doubling lemma, and a final independent sprinkling merges components with exponentially small failure.
Read the Gallai A-path reservoir lemma and path-merging scheme; one endpoint per current path ensures disjoint joining paths reduce the number of forest components without creating premature cycles.
remaining: The representative-doubling lemma, reservoir construction and full parameter allocation, specialized vertex-transitive/expander arguments and algorithmic extraction remain to be audited.

review.authors: Lars Rohwedder

score_reasons.exposition: Excellent progression from failed simple approaches to a compact, explicit algorithm and self-contained proof.

checked: Traced the full main theorem. Verified the deterministic ancestor ordering by conditional expectation, its exact hypergeometric conditional probabilities and O(log² n) simultaneous path-intersection bound.
Checked the recursion's path feasibility, fixed root paths and marginal objectives. Verified Lemma 5's prefix/suffix induction, the (1−λ) loss from threshold crossing, and α_d=(c log² n)^d/λ.

Verified the per-vertex recursion-tree threshold-mass argument: at most n² nonleaf calls per depth, depth O(log n/λ), and λ=2^-Θ(√(log n log log n)) yields polynomial total work and the stated approximation.

review.authors: Giannis Fikioris, Balasubramanian Sivan, Éva Tardos

review.title: Cryptographic Conditions for Efficient Testing of Distributions and Quantum States
review.authors: Bruno Cavalar, Eli Goldin, Matthew Gray, Taiga Hiroka, Min-Hsiu Hsieh, Tomoyuki Morimae
review.summary: Studies verification against time-bounded uniform samplers producing arbitrarily correlated samples: soundness concerns the random-coordinate marginal and gives acceptance at most 1-epsilon+n^-c when its distance from the target is at least epsilon. It does not certify iid sampling or closeness of the entire tuple. Polynomially many samples suffice with potentially inefficient verification. Every PPT target is efficiently verifiable with classical security iff infinitely-often OWFs do not exist. Quantum-target verification follows from no infinitely-often one-way puzzles and implies no infinitely-often QEFID; mixed-state verification lies between absence of weak nonuniform EFI and absence of EFI. These quantum implications are not asserted equivalences.
review.prior_frontier: Classical unrestricted identity testing has exponential sample complexity in bit length; the improvement changes the adversary/sampler model and builds on Aaronson’s Kolmogorov-complexity sampling verifier. Prior exact characterizations and external probability-estimation results were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Connects a carefully restricted but meaningful verification task to minimal cryptographic assumptions, including correlated quantum outputs.
score_reasons.novelty: Time-bounded universal-distribution complexity gives the classical construction; quantum verification needs additional techniques because one-sided classical probability estimation does not transfer.
score_reasons.depth: Several reductions span metacomplexity, minimal quantum cryptography and state verification in a 90-page development.
score_reasons.exposition: The precise marginal and uniformity qualifications are present, but the introductory identity-testing language and breadth require careful reading to avoid stronger interpretations.

checked: Read the exact adaptive/selective definitions, order of quantifiers, inverse-accuracy dependence and the prohibition on nonuniform adversaries. A repeated identical uniform sample is intentionally accepted under the marginal notion.

Read the classical proof construction using one-sided estimation of the target product probability and average-case estimation of conditional uK^t; acceptance compares their log probabilities with a log-squared slack.
Read the distinction between classical iff and the two quantum implication chains, including infinitely-often and weak/nonuniform qualifiers.
remaining: The complete likelihood-ratio soundness argument, parameter choice in conditional complexity estimation, all quantum minimax/cryptographic reductions and primary-source dependencies still need correctness audits.

review.title: Tight Bounds for Tusnády's Problem in the Plane
review.authors: Zhewei Wei
review.summary: Planar axis-parallel rectangle discrepancy is Theta(log^{3/2} n): independent uniform points have, with probability >=1-exp(-An), anchored discrepancy >=c_A(log_2 n)^{3/2} for every coloring. Resolves plane only; construction is probabilistic.
review.prior_frontier: Prior Omega(log n) versus O(log^{3/2} n). Matching upper bound directly verified in Nikolov, arXiv:1701.05532v2, Theorem 1 (PDF p.2); general rectangles follow from four anchored rectangles.

score_reasons.significance: Closes a longstanding central geometric discrepancy problem at the previously upper-bound exponent.
score_reasons.novelty: Finite-point oscillation recursion and digit revelation obtain exponentially strong simultaneous-coloring lower bounds.
score_reasons.depth: Subtle conditional gains, scale choice and uniform exponential concentration, despite short elementary presentation.
score_reasons.exposition: Complete transparent proof with explicit constants, small-n fallback and self-contained probability lemmas.

checked: Traced deterministic vertical comparison and child-average identity: deviations are independent symmetric jumps conditional on revealed heights/prefixes; midpoint offset gains survive arbitrary fixed shifts.
Verified moments and Holder proof in Fact 2.2; uniform digit jumps have variance (b^2-1)/(12b^2) and fourth moment <=3 variance^2, giving stated gain constant.
Traced good-event bound: bad transitions concentrate >=n/2 points in area <=3/b; union over at most 2^M regions gives (48/b)^{n/2}, common to every coloring.
Traced one-digit sensitivity <=1/M using shift-invariant oscillation, conditional martingale MGF, fluctuation tail exp(-lambda^2 M^2/(2hn)), and union over 2^n fixed colorings.
Checked h maximal with b^-5 h b^{h-1}<=n: exponent hM/(2048b^3)>bn/4096; selected b absorbs coloring entropy and exp(-An). M>n case has claimed threshold<1 and singleton anchored rectangle suffices.
Verified external matching upper statement directly in Nikolov Theorem 1; no unresolved substantive gap found in new lower-bound proof.
remaining: Advertised Lean formalization was not downloaded/built; this is a mathematical reading audit, not formal certification.
No explicit deterministic construction or higher-dimensional result is claimed.

sources.detail: Nikolov Theorem 1: fixed d >=2 upper O_d(log^{d-1/2} n), checked directly.

review.title: Persuasion by Parts
