review.title: Efficient thermalization of one-dimensional noncommuting Hamiltonians via system-bath interactions with $\Theta(n)$ ancilla qubits
review.authors: Zhiyan Ding, Bowen Li, Ruizhe Zhang
review.summary: For bounded nearest-neighbor noncommuting Hamiltonians on a one-dimensional chain with fixed local dimension and fixed inverse temperature beta>0, gives a parallel system-bath Gibbs sampler with trace-norm error epsilon from every initial state in expected total Hamiltonian evolution time soft-O(n/epsilon). It uses (4^q-1)n resettable bath qubits for q qubits per site, randomized frequencies and interaction times, and coupling alpha^2=Theta(epsilon/n). The output guarantee is for the state averaged over fresh randomness. Complexity is total evolution time, not a complete finite-precision gate count.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript improves a cited soft-O(n^6/epsilon) single-ancilla system-bath guarantee by using a linear-size parallel bath and sharper analysis. Lindbladian samplers already had soft-O(n) size dependence and better logarithmic accuracy dependence; this is a hardware/model-specific improvement, not a universal Gibbs-sampling breakthrough. Sources were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Closes most of a large system-size gap between physically simpler bath interactions and Lindbladian-based preparation for one-dimensional chains.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses Gibbs-weighted channel estimates, centered local moments and randomized dephasing to control an extensive Lamb shift without making it a small global perturbation.
score_reasons.depth: The 91-page proof combines Dyson term matching, complex-time locality, weighted fourth moments, approximate fixed points and enhanced dissipation.
score_reasons.exposition: The algorithm and resource measure are precise, but the critical improvement depends on several long analytic estimates and external one-dimensional functional inequalities.

checked: Read the concrete bath architecture, probability laws and main parameter choices. The constant local dimension and fixed beta restrictions are essential.

Traced the final perturbation arithmetic: O(n alpha^4) one-round error is absorbed into an Omega(alpha^2) contraction; an O(n alpha^4) stationarity defect yields O(n alpha^2) bias, requiring alpha^2=Theta(epsilon/n).
Read the strengthened dissipation step explaining why a mere weighted spectral-gap bound, with exponentially bad initial norm, would be insufficient for the near-linear result.
remaining: Full locality/Dyson comparison, the centered-moment theorem, positivity and cancellation of the approximate stationary state, Lamb-shift contraction and applicability of the cited enhanced-dissipation theorem still require detailed correctness audits.

review.title: The Greedy Superstring Conjecture Is False
review.authors: Nikolai Chukhin, Rishikesh Gajjala, Juha Harviainen, Alexander S. Kulikov, Ivan Mihajlin, Hiroki Shibata, Alexander V. Smal

score_reasons.significance: Resolving a nearly four-decade conjecture and tightening both sides would be exceptionally consequential.
score_reasons.novelty: The explicit gap-word obstruction and Lyndon/Rauzy counting argument provide different new mechanisms for the lower and upper bounds.
score_reasons.depth: Detailed overlap classification and combinatorics on words support several interconnected results.
score_reasons.exposition: The main claims and distinction among GREEDY, MGREEDY and TGREEDY are clear; the long construction requires careful table checking.

checked: Traced the complete new cycle-cover argument on pp.10–14: distinct minimal Lyndon edges can be deleted from the Rauzy multigraph without disconnecting it; summing the substring-count inequalities gives O−W≤OPT. Checked tightness and the MGREEDY/TGREEDY consequences.

Traced the complete binary lower-bound construction on pp.14–22: all gap-word overlap cases, substring containment in H, four prescribed greedy stages, lengths, and the r→∞ ratio. Independently recomputed every live overlap for 24 instances (r=1,…,8 and three P choices) with audit316.py; all passed. Finite tests supplement the parameterized argument.

Traced the length-three upper bound on pp.23–33, including open-trail counting, loop absorption, zero-contribution bundles, endpoint attachments, isolated-loop charging, and the closed-connector free=2 case. Checked both fixed-length lower-bound families through p.34.

Checked primary dependencies: Mucha Lemma2.5 for primitive/non-equivalent cycle strings; Blum et al. Claims2–6 and Theorem10 for periodicity/cycle covers; Englert–Matsakis–Veselý (ISAAC2023) AppendixA.1 for the 2OPT+oc−wc transfer; Nikolaev arXiv:2102.05579 Theorem4 for tie-breaking invariance. The length-(o+1) periodic-window inclusion follows because each window starts within one prefix segment and fits inside that segment’s input string.
remaining: Manual proof check, not formal certification. The finite test suite is not exhaustive over parameters. Nikolaev’s transformation need not preserve fixed string length; the manuscript correctly qualifies its fixed-length lower bounds by existence of a tie-breaking run. The general approximation theorem for SCS and its concurrent factor-two result are separate from this greedy lower bound.

review.summary: Claims a binary-string family with greedy superstring ratio tending to 12/5, refuting the factor-two Greedy Conjecture; also improves the greedy upper bound to three and proves sharp or improved bounds for fixed-length strings.
review.prior_frontier: The old general greedy interval was lower bound two and upper bound about 3.396. This submission claims [2.4,3]. Its greedy lower bound is distinct from the best approximation algorithm for SCS, including the acknowledged concurrent factor-two announcement.
review.recommendation: Strong shortlist candidate after independent central-proof checks, including the requester-authored submission under the same standard.

score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes infinite class from finite, contextual from noncontextual, and beta scaling.

Read the anchor cancellation, transpose-kernel necessity and forward/transpose interpolation roadmap.

papers.title: Integral 2 × 3 × 3 Tensor Isomorphism is in BQP
papers.authors: Thomas Huffstutler

review.title: Integral 2 × 3 × 3 Tensor Isomorphism is in BQP
review.authors: Thomas Huffstutler
review.summary: Proves BQP membership for isomorphism of binary-encoded integral 2x3x3 tensors under GL2(Z)xGL3(Z)xGL3(Z), including repeated-root and identically singular determinant pencils. Regular tensors reduce to compatible balanced-module principality plus a row-lattice test; singular pencils split by least polynomial-kernel degree. The quadratic-kernel branch reduces to fourteen degree-at-most-two congruences in four variables, decidable classically in polynomial time given modulus factorization. Fixed-format polynomial congruence feasibility is also stated for arbitrary fixed variable/equation/degree counts. Faithful padding embeds the known real-quadratic-principality obstruction.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the cited BQP result for integral 2x2x2 tensors; existing arithmetic orbit decidability did not give polynomial bit complexity. Complex SLOCC equivalence is a different, easier base-field problem and is not the novelty here. Prior sources were not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Adds the next small integral tensor format, including all degenerate inputs, to the quantum polynomial-time arithmetic-isomorphism landscape.
score_reasons.novelty: Compatibility is retained through an endomorphism order and row lattices rather than testing the two modules independently; singular quadratic kernels yield a fixed congruence formulation.
score_reasons.depth: Combines integral module structure, matrix-pencil degeneracies, arithmetic principality and p-adic/finite-field quantifier elimination.
score_reasons.exposition: The complete case split and distinction between decision and construction are explicit; the main dependency burden is concentrated in identifiable arithmetic results.

checked: Read the regular criterion H=E Q0 plus full row lattice, which forces det Q0=+-1; equal slice determinants then force the companion map to be unimodular. Principality alone is correctly not claimed sufficient.
Traced the quadratic-kernel congruence reduction and global determinant-sign requirement. Surjectivity of SL2(Z)->SL2(Z/NZ) is the cited lifting input; no huge witness has to be output.

Read the fixed-format congruence proof: CRT; one fixed p-adic formula; Pas elimination outside fixed exceptional primes; Presburger and finite-field formula reductions; univariate root existence via gcd(g,t^p-t); fixed-prime Macintyre power tests. Polynomial bit complexity depends critically on those uniform fixed-formula dependency statements.
remaining: The exact Pas/Kiefe/Macintyre statements and their uniform applicability, BHJ principality hypotheses, the pure-cube infinite-stabilizer case and linear-kernel compatible-algebra decomposition need independent correctness audits.

review.title: Efficient Quantum State Identity Testing
review.authors: Shih-Han Hung, Ming-Hsien Tsai
review.summary: For fixed epsilon in (0,1/4), distinguish n pure states with all pairwise fidelities >=1-epsilon from existence of one pair <=epsilon. Schur/Jucys-Murphy measurement uses O(log(n/delta)) copies per state, with matching lower bound for delta bounded away from 1/2. Parallel destructive swap tests have constant quantum depth and an extra log(2/delta) factor.
review.prior_frontier: Relaxes earlier identical-or-orthogonal promises; earlier one-copy permutation test fails robust completeness. Prior optimality results not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Optimal sample dependence for a meaningful robust quantum identity promise.
score_reasons.novelty: Jointly measures commuting Jucys-Murphy sums in forward and reverse order to aggregate the fidelity for every state.
score_reasons.depth: Representation-theoretic estimator plus unknown-coordinate mixed-state lower bound.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit purity, epsilon range, per-state sample count and quantum-depth versus classical postprocessing conventions.

checked: Traced random-matching no-bad-edge probability (a-1)(b-1)/((n-1)(n-3))<=1/3; odd n duplication preserves promises.
Verified fidelity-sum bound using spectral norm of two rank-one projectors, and Hoeffding range [-(n-1),n-1] yields logarithmic copies once normalized.
Checked Helstrom delta lower bound epsilon^m<=4delta(1-delta), and phase-averaged product state diagonalizes into binomial weights.
remaining: Verify Schur transform/Jucys-Murphy spectral correspondence and corrected gate-count dependencies.
Finish chi-square lower-bound calculation and asymptotic log(n/delta) combination, including adaptive/unequal copy accounting if claimed.
Constant depth refers to quantum gates plus unrestricted classical postprocessing, not full bounded-fanin computational depth.

review.title: Learning the structure of open quantum systems
review.authors: Laura Lewis, Ewin Tang, John Wright
review.summary: Learns unknown-structure constant-local Lindbladians in B1 error epsilon using O(g d² log n/epsilon²) evolution time and constant-scale time resolution, with nonadaptive ancilla-free Pauli experiments. Lower bound Omega(g d²/(epsilon² log d)) holds even for adaptive entangled experiments. Also learns Hamiltonian structure from high-temperature Gibbs states.
review.prior_frontier: Generalizes Hamiltonian structure-learning capabilities to irreversible dynamics; parameterwise optimality is claimed, not a matching joint multiplicative lower bound. Approximate degree depends on the target error. Prior comparisons not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Addresses structure learning with physically simple measurements and resolves the extra ambiguity caused by dissipative terms.
score_reasons.novelty: Thresholded inversion of local Fourier confusion avoids the polynomial-n norm loss of direct inversion; a moment-matched dissipative family supplies lower bounds.
score_reasons.depth: Combines B1 stability, nonlinear evolution remainder control and information-theoretic lower bounds against general quantum access.
score_reasons.exposition: The formal norms and approximation degree are explicit, with a useful caution about individual versus simultaneous parameter optimality.

checked: Verified the first-order cancellation in the lower-bound star construction: a=−2 sum u_i, b_i=1, c_i=i u_i cancels the coherent contribution.
Read why inverse time evolution is unavailable and why rounding before and after inversion is needed to maintain degree O(d).
Checked the formal upper and lower norm/model distinctions and the footnote limiting optimality.
remaining: Audit the B1 inverse bound, rounded-iteration invariant, evolution error estimate, moment-matched channel distinguishability and Gibbs-state extension.

papers.title: Optimal High Probability Bounds for Random Order Online Sorting
papers.authors: Mingyu Kang, Chenglin Fan

review.title: Optimal High Probability Bounds for Random Order Online Sorting
review.authors: Chenglin Fan, Mingyu Kang
review.summary: For every fixed multiset of n real numbers arriving in uniform random order, gives one comparison-based algorithm placing each value irrevocably in exactly n output cells with competitive ratio O(log n) and an exponential tail above that scale. It uses O(n log n) comparisons/word operations and O(n) auxiliary words. For every randomized measurable algorithm, some fixed distinct input forces Omega(log n) ratio with probability 1-exp(-Omega(sqrt(n))). The upper bound extends to arbitrary unknown iid laws, including atoms and without moment assumptions.
review.prior_frontier: Cited prior work gave O(log n) expected cost for known uniform inputs and O(log^2 n), with announced log^(3/2) refinement, high-probability guarantees for arbitrary random-order inputs. This closes both the random-order worst-case scale and a strong lower-tail version. Prior publications were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Determines the worst-case competitive scale with high probability in the strict no-extra-output-space model.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines empirical partitions with hierarchical overflow routing, reverse exposure of growing prefixes, and geometric charging of persistent partition errors.
score_reasons.depth: The proof must control adaptive capacity reallocation and correlated phases rather than merely union-bound bucket overflow.
score_reasons.exposition: Exact resource, tie-breaking, tail and input-distribution statements are clear, and the lower-bound proof is particularly transparent.

checked: Traced transfer from a fixed numerical cut under iid uniform samples to a rank cut by conditioning on the binomial mode, costing only an n+1 moment factor. The metric ratio is a convex combination of crossing counts, so Jensen transfers the exponential tail without independence assumptions.
Checked independent random priorities for repeated values: priorities assigned to occurrences are independent of their arrival permutation; zero numerical gaps create zero weights.

Traced the lower bound: with i suffix values, at most 2i occupied anchors border vacancies. At scale 1/(100i), conditional concentration gives at least 4i/5 proximity components and at most i/10 anchor-near values. Every completion has at least i/2 long edges. Integrating disjoint threshold bands over doubling suffix sizes from sqrt(n) to n/4 gives Omega(log n), with exp(-Omega(sqrt(n))) failure.
remaining: The central empirical-partition overflow and persistent-error exponential-moment lemmas, full integer capacity schedule, implementation and extraction of the deterministic hard input still need a complete audit.

score_reasons.novelty: Acceptance-level inverse parameterization exposes convex perspective and a dual certificate.
score_reasons.depth: Infinite-dimensional optimization plus equilibrium uniqueness and numerical certification.

review.title: A Spectral Theory of Local-to-Global Leakage
review.authors: Rei Ueno
review.summary: For independent uniform shares over a finite abelian group, expresses global chi-square mutual information as a diagonal product of local Fourier energies, or local energies times a spectral-alignment probability. Constructs equal-local-information channels with different exponential global decay and automorphism-weighted exact cancellation.
review.prior_frontier: Refines magnitude-only information bounds with spectral alignment; the central diagonal Fourier identity is a direct convolution/Parseval calculation. It does not invalidate upper bounds based only on local MI, only exact characterizations or tightness claims. Prior conjecture attribution not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Useful structural clarification for additive masking, but limited to a specific independent-channel sharing model and largely elementary spectral structure.
score_reasons.novelty: The alignment interpretation, permutation-invariant separation and automorphism cancellation organize information that scalar leakage measures discard.
score_reasons.depth: Core factorization is straightforward Fourier analysis; realizability and character-order refinements add technical content.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates chi-square and Shannon quantities but rhetoric about magnitude-only bounds can obscure the difference between bounds and exact asymptotics.

checked: Traced the posterior convolution/Parseval factorization and the Renyi-entropy interpretation under identical channels.
Checked LSB versus MSB on Z_(2^l): parity leakage persists, while half-interval Fourier modes have magnitude below one.
Read the full-support input-permutation construction and automorphism-induced frequency permutation.
remaining: Verify realizability constraints, uniform worst-case expansion for Shannon MI, quotient-spectrum Mobius bounds and exact-cancellation construction.

papers.title: Linear Set Reconciliation with $O(d)$ Additive Redundancy
papers.authors: Tianren Liu, Rui Xu, Tong Yang, Kangyang Zhou

review.title: Linear Set Reconciliation with $O(d)$ Additive Redundancy
review.authors: Tianren Liu, Rui Xu, Tong Yang, Kangyang Zhou
review.summary: Constructs a public-coin F2-linear sketch recovering each fixed weight-at-most-d vector with failure at most 2^-lambda, using L(n,d)+O(d)+lambda polylog(n) bits, polylog(n) updates and d exp(O((log log n)^2)) worst-case decoding. For n<=2^polylog(d) and lambda<=d^(1-c), this gives L(n,d)+O(d) space and d^(1+o(1)) decoding. Guarantees are for inputs fixed before randomness, not simultaneous correction of all d-error patterns. The word-RAM model assumes constant-time public random permutation/inverse, random coefficient and precomputed expander-table access; their storage and preprocessing are excluded.
review.prior_frontier: Algebraic sketches use about d log n bits and peeling constructions approach the counting bound with fixed multiplicative slack. This eliminates that multiplicative slack at the cost of subpolynomial decoding overhead and a public preprocessing model. The compared primary constructions were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Approaches the information-theoretic bit count with fast updates and nearly linear decoding in an important parameter regime.
score_reasons.novelty: Sequential column recovery turns known row-prefix uncertainty into decoder-only hints, retaining coefficient one on hinted bits while contracting the remaining error-location cost.
score_reasons.depth: The recursive charge analysis, entropy bounds for row loads and random-scaled first-error positions are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: The full theorem distinguishes additive confidence overhead, fixed-input success and preprocessing assumptions, though the headline alone hides these qualifications.

checked: Read the hinted recovery definition and recursive potential X+alpha h_N(Y), including the extra waiting bits that make unknown-location costs contract geometrically.
Read the top-level entropy accounting: total expected abstentions is at most d*w; random nonzero field scaling makes the first wrong bit geometric, yielding O(d) total error-location charge.
Checked the final asymptotic substitution and dense/small-instance branches: direct storage handles d>=n/2, and the lambda polylog(n) term covers the deterministic small regime.
remaining: Recursive concentration with adaptive hints, precise charge margins and recursion-tree size, worst-case decoding implementation and the external deterministic sparse-recovery/expander guarantees still require auditing.

papers.authors: Jonas Conneryd

review.title: Random ($\log{n}$)-CNF Formulas Are Hard for Depth-$2$ Frege with Modular Gates
review.authors: Jonas Conneryd
review.area: Proof complexity / random CNF lower bounds
review.summary: For random signed k-CNF with M=n*2^k clauses, omega(1)<=k<=O(log n), proves with high probability unsatisfiability and polynomial-calculus degree greater than n/2-4n/sqrt(k) over every field. Extending Pang’s tradeoff to arbitrary fixed inference rules gives exp(Omega_p(sqrt(k)*log n)) lower bounds for depth-two AC0[p]-Frege, for prime p. A degree upper bound n/2-n ln(k)/(2k)+O(n/k) limits this formula family as a route to full constant-depth modular Frege lower bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Builds on the recently cited common-multiplier tradeoff rather than proving full AC0[p]-Frege lower bounds. Prior random-CNF bounds in restricted resolution systems handle constant width, so those and this growing-width result are formally incomparable. The recent external breakthrough claims were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Obtains superpolynomial lower bounds for actual CNF refutations in a stronger depth-two modular Frege setting and identifies a quantitative limitation of the family.
score_reasons.novelty: A matching-deficiency closure supports a near-n/2 pseudo-reduction; the accompanying support-covering upper bound sharpens the methodological picture.
score_reasons.depth: Requires careful local-ideal compatibility, random expansion and a modular Frege-to-degree tradeoff with fixed-rule-set control.
score_reasons.exposition: The manuscript clearly attributes the tradeoff and closure machinery and distinguishes depth two, growing width and unrestricted depth.

checked: Traced closure monotonicity, absorption and Hall-based extension: extra clauses can be satisfied without changing the monomial/closure variables, so their reduction operators agree. This yields the multiplication-compatible pseudo-reduction.

Checked the random-formula estimates read: a union bound gives unsatisfiability at M=n*2^k; small clause-set neighborhood failure decays from (e^2 2^k (j/n)^(k-2))^j, and medium sets exploit support fraction below 1/2 by Theta(1/sqrt(k)).
Read the precise depth-two tradeoff rather than inferring a bound for full AC0[p]-Frege.
remaining: The construction/existence lemma for the maximal deficiency closure, all quotient-ring reduction details, the complete tradeoff proof and polynomial-calculus upper-bound construction still need correctness audits.

review.summary: Studies reachability of supplied lean resolution refutations under local replacements with unary size and width bounds. Trading reachability remains PSPACE-hard at budgets arbitrarily close to twice the endpoint size from below, whereas locality at least three connects any two proofs at endpoint-sum+6 when no empty input clause exists (frozen proofs additionally need matching inventories). A separate minimal-Horn construction stays disconnected with a 17/16 size allowance.

checked: Traced all internal main-proof steps. Verified strong-component nesting, cut-count union bound, contraction edge budget and the identity that lifting is the original Ising law conditioned on monochromatic contracted blocks.
Verified the even-subgraph lifting identity by incidence-matrix rank, including all parity boundary classes and Z_B≤Z_0.
Checked the cycle-switch cancellation and injective (S,U,a) encoding: the syndrome endpoints recover the starting edge, giving the local covariance bound without a path-length loss.
Verified both terms in the total-covariance decomposition, the 2n−2 possible two-defect boundaries, and the inequalities comparing ρ=p/(2−p) with heat-bath variances.
Checked monotonicity of extremal-chain densities, geometric bias contraction, coupling-to-TV conversion and the dynamic-connectivity runtime, including parallel-edge counters.
Verified external theorem applicability in primary sources: Benczúr–Karger Definition 6.3/Theorem 6.5, Karger Corollary A.7, and Wulff-Nilsen's deterministic dynamic-connectivity bounds.

review.summary: For fixed m identical machines, minimizes total weight of tardy jobs in soft-O_m(n+d_max^(m+1)) time and O_m(n+d_max^m) value space; reconstructs a schedule using soft-O_m(d_max^(m+1)) extra space. score_reasons.novelty: Canonical completion intervals extend knapsack item filtering to distinct due dates.

Batched updates use only previous-job DP values, preserving 0/1 inclusion. Canonical optimal schedule gives one inequality and predecessor schedule reconstruction the other.

Independent implementation compared canonical and unrestricted DP on 1200 fixed-seed instances with 1–3 machines, at most 9 jobs, due dates <=8, including ties; all agree. Saved check354.py and check354.json.
remaining: Historical priority and claimed conditional lower bound are not independently verified; they are not dependencies of the algorithm.

review.title: All Unitaries Have Constant Depth Quantum Circuits
review.authors: Barak Nehoran, Joseph Slote, Henry Yuen
review.area: Quantum circuit complexity and unitary synthesis
review.summary: Every n-qubit unitary has a clean exact circuit of one- and two-qubit gates of depth O(n), using 2^{O(n)} ancillas and unitary-dependent arbitrary rotations. Allowing exponentially large quantum fan-out yields constant depth. A fixed synthesis algorithm uses three queries to a target-dependent diagonal phase oracle on O(N loglog(N/epsilon)) qubits (six classical queries after phase computation), N=2^n, with operator-norm approximation. These are nonuniform depth/space tradeoffs, not efficient-size compilation or black-box Hamiltonian fast-forwarding.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript contrasts Rosenthal’s previous general depth 2^{n/2} upper bound, a folklore two-query classical-oracle construction with N^2-bit query input, and a one-query lower bound for o(N)-bit oracle inputs. Prior sources not yet independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the general unitary parallelization question with optimal linear bounded-fan-in depth at exponential space.
score_reasons.novelty: Connects quadratic-phase synthesis, single-excitation harmonic oscillator encodings and exact correction by block encoding.
score_reasons.depth: Requires uniform operator-norm discretization in exponentially many modes, exact shallow Fourier operations, and a clean exact-implementation upgrade.
score_reasons.exposition: The resource model and distinction between query input length and truth-table size are explicit; the analytic discretization is substantial.

checked: Read exact circuit/oracle models and reduction through real symmetric traceless involutions. Traced the Gaussian/Fresnel calculation giving the continuous encoded matrix element -i S_yx; the regularization caveat is explicitly stated.
Checked Theorem 5.1 uses error epsilon^2, so applying epsilon/sqrt(2) in the clean-isometry conversion is consistent.

Traced exact boosting: A near U by delta<=1/(10sqrt(N)) implies B=UA^{-1}/2 has absolute row/column sums <=1/2+sqrt(N)delta/[2(1-delta)]<=5/9. Row/column isometries with distinct padding flags give R^dagger S=B. Disjoint ancillas make the product block BA=U/2; one round -QFQ^dagger FQ has block U and hence no leakage. Fan-out replacement gives O(n) depth at the stated exponential width.
remaining: The 49-page argument has not been fully audited: verify all Poisson-summation/tail bounds and operator-norm control for arbitrary superpositions in Sections 5.2.3–5.2.4.
Check exact shallow QFT phase decoding and clean indexed-state preparation, including applicability of the cited Rosenthal and Takahashi–Tani results.
Check formal circuit size/uniformity conventions, lower bound and all ancillary workspace bookkeeping.

review.summary: Gives polynomial-time average-case reductions among noisy planted k-XOR and Tensor PCA preserving approximately independent target laws in total variation. Also gives 5-to-4 XOR and 7-to-4 Tensor PCA reductions, sparse-regime order reductions and k-sparse LWE variants. Hardness is conditional and parameter-scale based; canonical density rho=0 does not directly imply every denser problem.

remaining: Audit total-variation Gaussianization, sparse-Gram CLT, repeated-index completion, densification interpolation and recovery lifting.

review.prior_frontier: Primarily a conceptual synthesis and application of established pseudorandomness, coding and Vadhan–Zheng pseudoentropy tools; it does not give an efficient training algorithm or explain worst-case NP-hard optimization. A two-sided learning extension has O(t*+K^4 Delta_min^{-2} log T).

review.title: Near-optimal incoherent tomography of low-rank quantum channels
review.authors: Kean Chen, Aadil Oufkir
review.summary: For channels with input/output dimensions d1,d2 and Kraus rank at most r, adaptive incoherent diamond-norm tomography uses O(d1 d2 r^2 log(2d1)/epsilon^2) queries. If positive Choi eigenvalues are Omega(d1/r), nonadaptive tomography needs Theta(d1 d2 r^2/epsilon^2). Lower bound covers arbitrary adaptive single-use experiments with fresh entangled reference but no inter-query quantum memory; formal lower theorem assumes d2>=2, d1<=r d2, r<=d1 d2, d1 d2 r>=12 and sufficiently small constant epsilon. No computational restriction on measurements or postprocessing.
review.prior_frontier: Extends previously understood rank-one and full-rank incoherent channel tomography. Coherent away-from-boundary complexity is Theta(d1 d2 r/epsilon^2), whereas the rank-r incoherent cost has an extra r up to logs; manuscript acknowledges independent adaptive state-tomography lower bounds. Prior results not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Nearly characterizes the full rank-dependent cost of channel tomography without quantum memory in operational diamond distance.
score_reasons.novelty: Adaptive input conditioning through a regularized complementary-channel quantity and an all-feasible-ranks local hard family overcome two distinct obstructions.
score_reasons.depth: Combines Haar directional moments, Nyström estimation, operator-convex log-inverse maps, matrix updates and adaptive Fisher-information lower bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise access model and feasible-dimension conditions are explicit, although proof dependencies span several substantial matrix estimates.

checked: Traced the operator-convexity lemma: [Phi(Q^-1)]^-1 is operator concave by a constrained quadratic minimum; log monotonicity/concavity then makes log Phi(Q^-1) operator convex.

Checked the input-selection potential: trace budget<=3r, Golden–Thompson normalizer<=15r/4, multiplicative-estimate loss4/3, and T>=log_2 d1 yield H_s(average input)<=9r. Final fresh estimator and nearest-channel projection give diamond error<=22rs<epsilon.
Read the local normalized Kraus construction, uniform one-query Fisher trace<=16D/r and the adaptive-information/Fano deduction, including formal epsilon and Dr restrictions.
remaining: Audit complement-block flattening, full two-batch directional concentration, prior small-ball geometry and truncated-Gaussian log-Sobolev applicability.
Essential cited estimator and matrix concentration dependencies have not all been checked from primary sources.

checked: Traced the full central argument. Verified that the enhanced first-violated-row oracle leaves independent convex Gaussian restrictions, and that separating-query stopping preserves this product structure.

Checked the localization-to-short-residual lemma: determinant signs equal residual-coordinate signs; covariance bounds put both signs in a narrow strip, and logconcavity supplies linear central mass against the Gaussian quadratic small-ball probability.
Verified entropy normalization by a common invertible map and independent Gaussian radial replacement, the approximate isotropy infimum argument, and entropy loss under random orthogonal projection.
Checked both branches of the dimension induction, including the high-entropy-row deletion compensation and the product bound for the potential 2ν+4d0 K/d².

review.title: New Lower Bounds for Private PAC Learning
review.authors: Prathamesh Dharangutte, Amartya Sanyal
review.summary: Introduces Independent Class Packing, summing private constant-accuracy costs of independently embeddable classes, and proves an additive lower-bound framework for improper realizable approximate-DP PAC learning. Obtains multiplicative d log* N bounds for boxes/halfspaces, k log*(N/k) for interval unions, and parameter-range-specific d log(1/delta) for subspaces. Constructs equal-VC/equal-Littlestone classes with different private sample complexities.
review.prior_frontier: Strengthens general additive VC+log*LDim bounds on several natural classes; ICP is defined using component private sample complexity, not yet an intrinsic universally characterizing combinatorial invariant. Prior bounds not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Clarifies why two standard dimensions cannot determine private learning costs and closes several natural-class bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: Independent hard-instance packing gives additive private costs instead of taking a logarithm after dimension addition.
score_reasons.depth: Uses minimax hard databases, privacy amplification and careful padding/confidence reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states the component-cost dependence and limitations of its upper characterization.

checked: Verified geometric threshold packings for boxes, halfspaces and interval unions realize arbitrary independent prefixes.
Lemma 6 conditional subclass reduction uses disjoint private training/validation data; two 3/4-success candidates fail jointly with probability 1/16 and private selection contributes 3/16.
Checked 24 ln 64<100, giving stated 101/(epsilon alpha_0) overhead.
remaining: Uniform minimax hard-distribution lemma, empirical-to-population privacy conversion and full ICP parameter ranges.
Stronger threshold lower bound at delta<=c/m and tight subspace/equal-dimension separation proofs.

review.title: Convex optimization on moment polytopes: Hadamard mirror descent and efficient algorithms for quantum functionals and other tensor parameters
review.authors: M. Levent Doğan, Keiya Sakabe, Michael Walter
review.summary: Hadamard mirror descent minimizes holonomy-invariant convex objectives over gradients with O(1/k) convergence; applications give polynomial real-arithmetic iteration bounds for quantum functionals and related moment-polytope tensor parameters. General arbitrary convex objectives are not covered.
review.prior_frontier: Prior Hirai flow and norm descent results were qualitative or restricted to semistable inputs; first general quantum-functional polynomial iteration claim is manuscript-reported. Finite-precision Turing analysis is explicitly deferred to future work on PDF p12.

score_reasons.significance: Makes previously implicit tensor-spectrum quantities algorithmically accessible in exact arithmetic.
score_reasons.novelty: A dual mirror-descent framework on Hadamard manifolds plus an entropy step-size inequality extends beyond ordinary tensor scaling.
score_reasons.depth: Combines Busemann potentials, dual smoothness, invariant theory/capacity bounds and quantum relative entropy.
score_reasons.exposition: General assumptions and limitations are stated carefully, including the deferred finite-precision analysis.

checked: Traced Lemmas 5.3-5.4 and Theorem 5.5: geodesic convexity, endpoint Busemann inequality and parallel-transport-invariant convexity yield a telescoping shifted-function potential and O(1/k).
Checked Proposition 5.9 cancellation establishing relative-smoothness implies the step-size condition, and Proposition 5.11 smoothness/dual-smoothness composition.
Checked matrix/vector update equivalence under polar decomposition and K-equivariance.
Traced Theorem 7.5 entropy inequality using pinching by the spectral projections of Z, relative-entropy data processing under partial trace, and weighted cancellation.
remaining: Finite capacity bounds and full passage from asymptotic directions to moment-polytope minimizers, all tensor-parameter applications and external invariant-theory dependencies remain unchecked.

review.title: Faster Minimum k-Cut II: Improved Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms for Weighted Graphs
review.authors: Trevor Vaughn
review.summary: For fixed k>=3, weighted Minimum k-Cut has randomized k^{O(k^2)} n^{k-1} log^2 n time and deterministic k^{O(k^2)} n^{k-1} polylog(n) time after O(m) parallel-edge aggregation. Assumes positive integer capacities with polynomially bounded total capacity; auxiliary weights have polynomial bit complexity. In particular weighted 3-cut becomes near-quadratic. Does not claim an unconditional matching lower bound.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript previous algorithm: randomized n^{k-2}(m+n)(log n)^{O(k^2)}, dense exponent k; prior deterministic exponent k+O(1). It explicitly notes the older Max-Weight Clique conditional barrier has been refuted in the stated bounded-weight regime. Prior sources not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Improves the dense exponent by one for general fixed-k weighted cuts and matches it deterministically, with a near-quadratic 3-cut base case.
score_reasons.novelty: Batched residual-tree completion, constant-size repair-edge nets and constructive light-cut overflow replace per-candidate minimum-cut work and nonconstructive truncation.
score_reasons.depth: Requires a structural crossing-pattern classification, reusable 2-respecting optimization and two different derandomization regimes.

checked: Traced the (2,3,3) repair argument: local optimality bounds a strict-small fragment boundary by three times its same-side repair capacity; combining with other-side boundary<5lambda/6 yields repair capacity>lambda/18 and fraction>1/10.

Read inherited boundary complexity and shared residual optimizer: residual subtree boundaries lie in delta_T(A) plus one edge, so constant-many original DFS intervals provide constant-time cut-value queries from one capacity matrix. Full GMW optimizer applicability remains unchecked.

Traced the constructive overflow recursion and potential |V|-k; then the truncation argument with U*=jB/2<=lambda_j recovers an optimum whenever a light optimum side is discarded. Read the invocation-count/exponent calculation.
remaining: Audit all good-tree crossing patterns and the oracle form of the GMW 2-respecting optimizer, including auxiliary edges.
Check sunflower/Venn certificates, random-tree probabilities, deterministic skeleton construction, special 4-cut contraction branch and BSS sparsifier dependencies.
Verify runtime logarithms and bit-complexity model throughout the full algorithm.

review.title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness

review.summary: For fixed q, Delta and beta strictly below tree uniqueness, Potts Glauber mixes in n polylog n and Swendsen-Wang in O(log n) on almost every random Delta-regular graph. On lattice cubes/tori below beta_c, inverse spectral gap is n^{1+o(1)}, giving mixing n^{2+o(1)}. A shattering/escape dichotomy avoids uniform correlation decay under arbitrary pinnings.
review.prior_frontier: Potts sampling via random-cluster dynamics was already near-linear on random regular graphs, but polynomial Glauber mixing throughout uniqueness was open for q>=3; lattice all-dimension uniqueness mixing and an optimal comparison conjecture are claimed advances. Prior results not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves sharp-temperature mixing questions for fundamental dynamics in two central graph families.

review.title: Unconditional Quantum PAC Learning Advantage in the Large Error Regime
review.authors: Igor C. Oliveira
review.summary: A polynomial-time quantum learner using one uniform quantum random example of an arbitrary Boolean function outputs an O(n^2)-size classical hypothesis with agreement >=1/2+10^-3 2^{-n/2} and success >=0.53. O(1/eta) samples boost advantage to Omega(2^{-n/2}/sqrt(eta)) and success1-eta. Padding yields an unconditional quantum/classical polynomial-time separation for constructive n^{omega(1)}2^{-n/2}<=lambda(n)<=n^{-omega(1)}, with classical membership-query learners failing even at advantage lambda/n^k and success1/n^k. Efficiently computable target concepts require subexponentially secure OWFs; the unconditional class is unrestricted.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier Fourier sampling achieved this tiny advantage only with success at most1/2 after orientation, and classical zero-query randomized hypotheses can also succeed below1/2. The result improves success/robustness, not practical inverse-polynomial weak learning; the latter robust separation would imply NP not subset BPP under the cited agnostic-learning theorem.

score_reasons.significance: Establishes an unconditional robust learning separation with classical output hypotheses, while locating the precise large-error regime.
score_reasons.novelty: Interference with a known reference branch samples quadratic hypotheses proportionally to (1+normalized correlation)^2, retaining correlation sign.
score_reasons.depth: The moment method supplies both a >1/2 single-sample guarantee and pairwise independence needed for majority amplification and padding.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear distinctions between agreement and learner success, quantum-example access and membership queries, and conditional efficient-concept variants.

Traced pointwise mean1/sqrt(N) and pairwise product1/N, hence pairwise independent correctness signs. Independent repetition and odd majority preserve pairwise independence across inputs, so correlation variance<=1/N; Chebyshev yields failure O(1/m) at advantage Omega(sqrt(m/N)).
Read padding argument and classical unseen-label symmetry lower bound; the stronger padded lower-tail lemma remains unchecked.

Verify cited small-error agnostic-learning implication and majority-bias bound from primary sources.

review.summary: For a discrete mixture of arbitrarily many (possibly infinitely many) separated identity-covariance Gaussians in R^n, estimates mass near a candidate center in exp(O(n^{1/3} log^{4/3}(1/epsilon_w)/epsilon_d^{4/3})) time and samples. Matching lower bound uses separation Delta in place of epsilon_d, matching when epsilon_d=Theta(Delta)<=1. Recovers all components of weight >=2epsilon_w with location/weight errors and no spurious unmatched outputs; for fixed parameters its cost is exp(O(n^{1/3})), while the full recovery bound also includes n^{O(k)} and doubly exponential k terms, k=log^2(1/epsilon_w)/epsilon_d^2. review.summary: For extendable families of real-valued matrices defined by a fixed measurable local predicate, one-sided constant-query testability is equivalent to both packing amplification of edge-disjoint local violations and stability of completing sparse-hole partial matrices. Recovers metric-family distinctions and O(epsilon^-2) ultrametric/tree-pseudometric testers. For fixed C>2, nonadaptive metric testing on entries[1,C] has sharp one-/two-sided complexity F: n^2 for epsilon<=n^-2; n/sqrt(epsilon) to n^-1; sqrt(n)/epsilon to n^-1/2; (n/epsilon)^{2/3} above that. Adaptive two-sided lower bound is Omega(sqrt(n/log n)), including fixed small proximity.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript removes logarithmic losses in recent ultrametric/tree bounds and strengthens a previous n^{2/3-o(1)} nonadaptive one-sided lower bound at vanishing proximity to sharp constant-proximity two-sided bounds. review.summary: Approximating finite-dimensional quantum value of tilted XOR games with binary answers is RE-complete at a constant additive gap around 3/4. One distinguished Alice question has a forced answer; the remaining predicates are XOR. Includes exact-value and succinct-input distinctions.

resolved_notes: PDF p27 omits factor 4 before the last triple product and writes +1 instead of -I in the second squared norm. Re-expanding the four odd-parity projectors gives the corrected identity and the same 15028 epsilon bound.

review.title: Quantum circuit compilation with constant overhead
review.authors: Chenyi Zhang, Xinyu Tan, Robin Kothari, David Gosset, Craig Gidney
review.summary: Every G-gate circuit of arbitrary one-/two-qubit gates, including adaptive circuits with at most G gates on each branch, admits inverse-polynomial diamond-error compilation into an adaptive {H,T,CNOT} circuit with O(G) worst-case gates. The constant depends on the fixed error exponent. Dyadic rotations admit O(G+log(1/epsilon)) gates for arbitrary precision; an n-qubit phase-gradient state admits O(n) unitary gates at error 2^-n. Classical feedforward and ancillary resource states are allowed.
review.prior_frontier: Independent per-gate synthesis costs O(G log(G/epsilon)); the paper removes that logarithmic overhead for inverse-polynomial error by amortizing resources across gates. It improves previous expected O(n log n) phase-gradient preparation. Cited synthesis bounds not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Removes a ubiquitous compilation overhead for arbitrary circuits in a clearly specified adaptive model.
score_reasons.novelty: A reusable catalyst plus consumable bank converts phase halving and injection into a globally amortized protocol; base-B angle encoding handles every fixed precision exponent.
score_reasons.depth: Requires a worst-case tail bound and a separate linear-cost highly accurate resource-state construction.
score_reasons.exposition: Precisely distinguishes worst-case gates, adaptive operations, precision exponents and special dyadic compilation.

checked: Traced the resource-bank alternation H<=I and binomial recursion termination bound, yielding O(G+log(1/epsilon)) worst-case calls after cutoff.

remaining: Audit phase-gradient LCU preparation, exact amplitude-amplification error, gadget identities and lower-bound counting argument.
Verify synthesis dependencies and the precise treatment of classical control cost, which is not claimed as quantum gate cost.

checked: Traced Theorem 11 completely: S=1+x+2x^2-x^3+2x^4+x^5 has nonnegative square/cube, P=(1+x)S, and normalized dyadic multiplicities p=P(2)^-1*(1,2,2,4,4,4,8,16,32,32,32,64), q=(1,2)/3 give exact tensor factorizations for 2 and 3 copies.
One-copy factorization would pair entries in ratio 1:2; multiplicity recurrence t_e=c_e-t_(e-1) gives t_3=-1. Every n>=2 is 2a+3b.

Justified local pure-state conversion criterion directly via local Stinespring isometries: pure output factors from its environment, so input Schmidt spectrum must equal output spectrum tensor an environment spectrum; converse is rearrangement and discarding. Compactness of finite-dimensional local channel sets makes nonattainment of exact conversion a strict value gap.
Traced Proposition 8: shared reduced question state of the second game simulates product strategy for first, and accepting both is bounded by accepting first alone.
remaining: Audit scope is the central one-round game theorem and one-round entangled-value monotonicity. Multi-round QMIP/channel-capacity equivalences, teleportation reduction, and zero-error capacity consequences have not been traced.

review.title: Strongly Log-Concave Measures and Lattices
review.authors: Brayden Letwin, Victor Reis, Thomas Rothvoss
review.area: Geometry of numbers and lattice probability
review.summary: If every sublattice of the dual of a full-rank lattice Lambda has determinant at least one, there exists an even smooth positive density that is (2pi/e)-strongly log-concave and uniform modulo Lambda. Conversely such a lift forces weak dual stability up to universal dilation. Consequences include covering radius at most sqrt(2e/pi) times Gaussian expected gauge, flatness O(n sqrt(log n)), and subspace flatness O(log^{3/2} n). These are existence/geometric statements, not efficient sampling algorithms.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript improves flatness O(n log n) and subspace-flatness O(log^3 n), or O(log^{5/2} n) after recent geometric inputs. It offers a new route to reverse Minkowski rather than claiming the sharp logarithmic improvement there originates here. Prior works not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A structural lattice lift yields improved bounds for both major flatness constants and transfers analytic inequalities to flat tori.
score_reasons.novelty: Optimizes log Gaussian lattice mass divided by covariance trace, permitting a singular optimizer and inductive product lifts.

papers.authors: Xi Chen, Ruiquan Gao, Yuhao Li, Aviad Rubinstein, Mihalis Yannakakis

review.title: Tarski Fixed Points in Quasi-FPT Queries
review.authors: Xi Chen, Ruiquan Gao, Yuhao Li, Aviad Rubinstein, Mihalis Yannakakis
review.summary: For monotone functions on [n]^k, gives deterministic O(5^k (log n)^ceil(log2 k)) query upper bound and Las Vegas worst-case expected lower bound Omega((log n/polylog k)^floor(log4(6k+4))), even for unique fixed points. Arbitrary computation between oracle queries is free.
review.prior_frontier: Improves prior log^O(k)n upper and roughly k log^2n lower bounds; claims first superpolynomial query lower bound. Does not imply equivalent running-time bounds for explicit parity/stochastic games.

score_reasons.significance: Nearly characterizes dimension dependence of a central total-search oracle problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Safe-function antipodal elimination and recursively amplified unique fixed-point instances give new upper/lower frameworks.
score_reasons.depth: Maintains monotonicity and uniqueness while hiding binary-search information through recursive boxes.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise deterministic versus Las Vegas definitions and explanation of failed constructions make scope clear.

checked: Verified lower-bound dimension recurrence k_l=2(4^l-1)/3 and l=floor(log4(6k+4))-1; side padding m=floor(n^(1/l)) gives denominator O(l^4) in log n.
Checked postfixed points are closed under joins and prefixed points under meets using monotonicity.
Read sign-coordinate doubling used to avoid the explicit monotonicity violation of naive amplification.

Completed the new upper-bound proof on pages6–14: universal postfixed/prefixed joins/meets bound every safe fixed point on every slice; candidate sets are monotone under new queries. The median construction creates antipodal sets each incident to at least2^(−k) of the bad pairs. Solving the slice on the smaller coordinate part minus one eliminates one whole set, including the asymmetric strict inequality in the last coordinate. Coordinate separation finishes in dimension k−1. Summing this last recurrence over k gives O(k2^k log n) times the half-dimensional cost.

Checked Appendix A’s exact exponent recurrence e(r)=ceil(log2((r+3)/3)), including1+e(floor(r/2)−1)=e(r). The factor r2^r5^(floor(r/2)−1−r) tends to zero, giving the stated5^k factor and exponent at mostceil(log2 k). This is query complexity with unbounded between-query computation, not an efficient runtime implementation.

Completed the new lower-bound construction and amplification on pages16–25 conditional on Lemma13. Complemented copies place all possible inner fixed points on one antichain; the0/1 sign functions remain monotone. Opposite one-sided increments with swapped sign coordinates force a=b=t*. Every outer query reveals at most four inner evaluations; the comparison bits remain hidden until an inner fixed point is queried.

Checked the adaptive inner-query accounting in Lemma17. The event that an inner instance is first touched is independent of that instance before its first query, so conditioning on that event permits the induction bound; this supplies the implicit justification for Pr(E_t prime and N_t≥1)≤epsilon Pr(N_t≥1)≤epsilon E N_t. Heavy queried instances are bounded by total queries/q, and Markov plus the conditional comparison decision tree gives success≤m^(−1/2)+qepsilon/3. The dimension/side-length recurrences and the stated induction exponents then work.

Fetched the primary EPRY20 manuscript (arXiv1909.03210) and examined its Section4, PDF pages14–17. Its stated and proved lower bound uses expected binary-search costs. I did not find the explicit polynomially small success guarantee at depth c(log m)² that this submission requires as Lemma13.
remaining: Substantive large-proof exception: the29-page submission’s new upper-bound and amplification arguments are traced, but the essential strengthened base-case tail in Lemma13 still needs a derivation from the46-page EPRY source or another primary theorem. An expected lower bound alone does not imply this tail. Therefore the full lower-bound theorem is not certified here.
The exact safe-function equivalence imported from CLY23/CLY26 is used as an external interface; its complete proof was not re-audited.
issues: Lemma13 imports a stronger probability bound than the cited source explicitly states. The submission notes this in a footnote but does not provide its tail derivation. This is an unresolved dependency check, not a counterexample to the claimed bound.

papers.title: Online Matching with Arbitrary Stochastic Rewards
papers.authors: Rajan Udwani

review.title: Online Matching with Arbitrary Stochastic Rewards
review.authors: Rajan Udwani
review.summary: Perturbed Greedy achieves at least 0.5915 unweighted and 0.5314 vertex-weighted competitive ratios for online matching with arbitrary independent edge success probabilities, against an adaptive offline benchmark that knows all probabilities but cannot see unprobed outcomes.
review.prior_frontier: Breaks the 1/2 barrier for arbitrary probabilities in both versions; equal-probability, small-probability and different benchmarks had stronger prior guarantees. Earlier bounds were not independently re-proved.

score_reasons.significance: Improves a longstanding general-probability barrier under the strong adaptive offline benchmark.
score_reasons.novelty: Counterfactual release arrivals and auxiliary charges repair sample-path comparisons that fail for stochastic outcomes.
score_reasons.depth: Uses per-resource primal-dual targets, a correlated-outcome coupling, release charging and a weighted deletion influence induction.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully distinguishes independent and equivalent correlated models; constants are supported by an explicit finite-grid prescription.

checked: Verified independence-to-common-threshold coupling for any non-anticipative policy probing each arrival at most once; OPT membership in a chosen resource probe set is independent of that arrival threshold.
Traced unweighted sample-path availability inclusion, maximal demand, last-release argument and resampled auxiliary charge preserving expectation.
Traced weighted influence lemma Q(A\j)>=(1-kappa_j)Q(A) and two cases in the product-potential induction; checked kappa_j<1 in the nontrivial case and sigma_Lambda<=kappa_j.
Traced weighted release proof and Lemma 7 integral minimization including flat perturbation bands and the limit Lambda=infinity.

Reproduced the 16000-interval numerical checks for headline rows. Unweighted alpha1=0.591658671 and grid lower bound=0.591690654; weighted alpha1=0.531640134 and grid lower bound=0.531670228. Quadrature error estimates <5e-9, well below reported margins.
remaining: Numerical reproduction uses adaptive double-precision quadrature with error estimates, not formal interval arithmetic. Intermediate weight-ratio rows, auxiliary impossibility results and related-work completeness were not audited.

papers.title: Geometry-Dependent Online and Offline Approximation for Non-Monotone DR-Submodular Maximization
papers.authors: Vaneet Aggarwal, Yiyang Lu

review.title: Geometry-Dependent Online and Offline Approximation for Non-Monotone DR-Submodular Maximization
review.authors: Vaneet Aggarwal, Yiyang Lu
review.summary: For nonnegative continuously differentiable DR-submodular objectives on the entire cube and compact convex down-closed feasible K containing a supplied zeta*1, achieves alpha(zeta)=1/2-(1-2zeta)_+^2/[2(3-2zeta)^2], including 4/9 at zero and 1/2 at zeta>=1/2. One post-action gradient query on the cube and one projection give O(sqrt(T)) expected alpha-regret; value-only variants and offline conversions follow. Polynomial exact value-plus-full-gradient queries cannot beat about 0.4704 at zeta=0. Queries may be outside K.
review.prior_frontier: Claims improvement over 0.401 online/offline achievable ratios and oracle upper bounds about 0.477 continuous/0.478 cardinality-constrained set functions. These prior comparisons and the rounding transfers have not been independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A meaningful constant advance with a geometric interpolation and matching qualitative half-diagonal threshold.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses a rational action map and ordered lower/upper coordinate paths for an upper-linearizable field, plus a four-component symmetry gap.
score_reasons.depth: Proof must handle signed increments, unbiased field estimates and exact-gradient indistinguishability in the lower bound.
score_reasons.exposition: The access model is explicit, but the 100-page treatment is lengthy and many secondary polynomial-objective refinements complicate auditing.

checked: Traced Lemma 4.1: coordinatewise DR comparisons, comparator telescoping and summation by parts with ordered mu_i=x_i(1-x_i)/c yield coefficient 1+c+1/(4c).
Traced feasibility x/(c+x)<=c*x+(1-c)^2 and convexity/down-closedness, yielding the 4/9-to-1/2 action guarantee.
remaining: Audit stochastic field variance and regret reductions, four-component hardness and exact-gradient smoothing, and the discrete rounding/query-budget transfers.
Verify the degree-two/three refinements and stronger value-only statements separately.

papers.title: Single-or-Sample: Online Fair Allocation for Combinatorial Agents
papers.authors: Shuchi Chawla, Zhiyi Huang, Pooja Kulkarni, Ruta Mehta, Parnian Shahkar

review.title: Single-or-Sample: Online Fair Allocation for Combinatorial Agents
review.authors: Shuchi Chawla, Zhiyi Huang, Pooja Kulkarni, Ruta Mehta, Parnian Shahkar

score_reasons.significance: A meaningful advance for simultaneous fairness under irrevocable online decisions.
score_reasons.novelty: The Single-or-Sample design and adaptive upper-cylinder/MGF analysis provide reusable ideas.
score_reasons.depth: Combines randomized allocation, bucketing, exponential potentials, and valuation-specific concentration and lower bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper states the oblivious-adversary restriction and oracle assumptions; the long appendices organize the probabilistic machinery well.

checked: Checked the binary-additive first-agent lower-bound construction: requiring two items and hiding the later common valued set produces a quadratic-in-c failure event.
Checked Appendix B's adaptive bucketing induction, composition of upper-cylinder bounds across rounds, weighted MGF expansion, and predictable-charge supermartingale stopping argument.
remaining: Audit the main submodular potential calculation, special-round handling, XOS deficit concentration, and efficient oracle implementation.
Check all lower-bound regimes and simultaneous-success constants; the positive results do not cover adaptive adversaries.

review.summary: Single-or-Sample gives every submodular agent a 1/24-MMS allocation simultaneously with probability at least 0.423, against an oblivious arrival adversary. For XOS agents it gives c-MMS with probability 1-O(c) for c up to 1/(4 log n), with complementary impossibility results. The XOS log n versus log log n threshold gap remains.
review.prior_frontier: Online combinatorial fair allocation had no comparable simultaneous constant-factor submodular MMS guarantee. The new analysis handles adaptive sampling without replacement without incorrectly asserting pairwise negative dependence; XOS guarantees and lower bounds concern distinct parameter regimes.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate for the final pool; the core probabilistic tool passed a targeted check, but the full allocation proof remains to be audited.

papers.title: Group Action and Spin Representation Lead to a Holant* Complexity Dichotomy on Domain Size 3
papers.authors: Jin-Yi Cai, Jin Soo Ihm

review.title: Group Action and Spin Representation Lead to a Holant* Complexity Dichotomy on Domain Size 3
review.authors: Jin-Yi Cai, Jin Soo Ihm
review.summary: Gives a decidable polynomial-time versus #P-hard classification for domain-three Holant* with complex-valued symmetric signatures and all unary signatures freely available; high-arity signatures and binary matrix closures require a common compatibility criterion. This is not unrestricted domain-three Holant without free unaries.
review.prior_frontier: Extends single complex ternary signature and real-valued multi-signature dichotomies to complex-valued families; finite-generation decidability uses external matrix-semigroup Zariski-closure machinery. Prior results not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a substantial higher-domain counting-classification gap.
score_reasons.novelty: Spin representation, frames/shells and annihilators expose complex isotropic interactions absent over the reals.
score_reasons.depth: Long classification combines group action, algebraic geometry, gadget hardness and matrix-semigroup decidability.
score_reasons.exposition: Extended overview explains representative cases and points to the full proof; complete case verification remains extensive.

checked: Checked generalized orthogonal invariance: M^T A M=A preserves edge contractions under tensor basis change.

Traced compatible rank-two signature algorithm: after removable edges, a starting local tensor choice uniquely propagates across a connected component; W-type expansion vanishes by excess u occurrences when a ternary vertex exists.
Identified binary multiplicative-closure quantifier as essential rather than pairwise compatibility alone.
remaining: The 111-page Holant dichotomy has concrete checks of orthogonal invariance and a rank-two tractable case. Its full group/spin parameterization and exhaustive hardness classification remain unchecked; this is a large-proof exception.
Complete tractability criterion and all hardness cases in full 111-page submission.
Spin/group parameterization, Boolean bipartite dichotomy, annihilator degeneracies and applicability/effectivity of semigroup Zariski closure.

papers.title: Polynomially larger deletion codes by linear hashing of substring counts
papers.authors: Eyal En Gad

review.title: Polynomially larger deletion codes by linear hashing of substring counts
review.authors: Eyal En Gad
review.summary: For every fixed t>=2 and fixed alphabet q, there exist length-n codes correcting any t insertions, deletions and substitutions with redundancy (2t-1)log_q n+O_t(log_q log_q n). The same leading coefficient holds for t bounded substring replacements; no efficient encoder/decoder is claimed.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the classical greedy/Levenshtein leading coefficient 2t to 2t-1; for two deletions this is 3 versus the sphere-packing lower coefficient 2. Prior-code optimality claims were not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Polynomial increase in fixed-error deletion-code size after a longstanding leading-coefficient barrier.
score_reasons.novelty: Random linear hashes of substring spectra plus odd-cycle removal exploit relations between local edit differences.
score_reasons.depth: Combines local de Bruijn geometry, bounded independent witnesses and a recursive reconstruction count.
score_reasons.exposition: Proof cleanly separates exceptional nonseparated edits, witness extraction, counting and final code selection.

checked: Checked k-unique-word density including overlapping windows, parity-spectrum injectivity for equal-length partners and single-edit shared-source lemma.
Traced local bubbles and separated edit coverage, including 2tb position shifts, margins, disjoint source intervals and nonzero signed supports.

Traced odd-walk witness extraction: first nontrivial linear dependence or large rule block; block closure preserves generating order, independent reductions and c<=(2t-1)R+1, with extra component only R>L.
Traced recursive reconstruction count: one root position per support component, three overlapping windows per bubble, earlier-rule recursion and at most b extra letters per transfer.
Checked hash independence, witness survival Q^-R, absorption n<=q^R for large blocks, sum_R>=2 4^-R=1/12 and final independent-label-class code size >=q^n/(8Q).
remaining: No efficient construction or decoding algorithm follows. Earlier-code frontier and the claimed historical novelty were not independently established; this audit concerns the supplied existential theorem.

sources.detail: Final union bound and code selection

papers.title: Thin-shell stability and heat-adjoint hypercontractivity: logconcave sampling with sesteric complexity from a cold start
papers.authors: Yunbum Kook, Santosh S. Vempala

review.title: Thin-shell stability and heat-adjoint hypercontractivity: logconcave sampling with sesteric complexity from a cold start
review.authors: Yunbum Kook, Santosh S. Vempala
review.summary: For general logconcave densities given by a zeroth-order evaluation oracle and a standardized inner ball in a constant-measure ground set, constructs finite-q Renyi-warm starts in soft-O(n^{2.5}+sqrt(q)*n^2 min{R sqrt(L),R^{3/2} Lambda^{1/4}}) expected queries. Near-isotropic instances give soft-O(sqrt(q)*n^{2.5}). New Gaussian-tilt thin-shell stability and heat-adjoint hypercontractivity provide balanced Renyi warm-to-output guarantees. This is oracle-query complexity, not total bit complexity; centering/inner-ball assumptions matter.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the stated soft-O(n^{2.75}) cold-start bound and matches an abstract Speedy-walk iteration exponent with an implementable query algorithm. Thin-shell inputs use recent established results cited in the manuscript, not independently checked here.

score_reasons.significance: Improves the exponent for a basic general sampling task while strengthening the output metric.
score_reasons.novelty: Controls total spectral gains/losses and moving means under quadratic tilts rather than relying on false covariance-operator stability; uses heat-adjoint hypercontractivity for annealing.
score_reasons.depth: Combines new analytic stability with restart/rejection bias control, order-preserving annealing and an exponential lift for general densities.
score_reasons.exposition: Formal statements expose the warmness orders, inner-ball normalization and expected query cost; technical dependencies are separated.

checked: Traced the heat-flow Lq derivative inequality and the choice (q(t)-1)/(p-1)=1+t/C_LSI.

Read the centered tilt proof: integrated quadratic variance equals spectral loss minus gain and mean square; Cauchy–Schwarz and anisotropic thin-shell control bound spectral log-derivative energy, giving loss<=16s tr(M^2) and uniform variance<=336 tr(M^2).
remaining: Verify the anisotropic thin-shell and spectral perturbation inputs, shifted-mean extension, restart conditioning and actual annealing/exponential-lift complexity.
Check the exact centering needed when simplifying the R,L-dependent bound to the near-isotropic headline.

papers.title: Testing State and Unitary Designs
papers.authors: Akinori Kawachi, Yoshifumi Nakata, Yuki Takeuchi

review.title: Testing State and Unitary Designs
review.authors: Akinori Kawachi, Yoshifumi Nakata, Yuki Takeuchi

score_reasons.significance: A broad and quantitatively substantial treatment of operational design testing.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines sample reuse, rank/collision lower bounds, and coherent estimation to separate access resources.
score_reasons.depth: The 120-page treatment contains substantial representation-theoretic, moment, and quantum-query analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Resource tables and explicit access models are helpful; the number of regimes makes careful theorem-by-theorem qualification necessary.

checked: Checked the state empirical-frame-potential variance: disjoint pairs are independent, shared-index covariance is bounded by theta/D+theta^(3/2), and vanishes in the exact-design case.
Traced Theorem 4.11's SWAP-test batching, Chebyshev/Hoeffding thresholds, constants, and sample versus total-query accounting.
Inspected the symmetric-space dimension/rank setup and the state lower bound's reduction to the rank-collision lemma.
remaining: Audit the general rank-collision lemma and epsilon-tight finite-design lower bounds.

Audit unitary random-list moments, small-range query reduction, frame-potential estimators, and their imported quantum-query lower bounds. The checked state branch does not certify these separate results.

review.summary: Studies state- and unitary-design testing with independent sampled preparation/oracle processes. For fixed t and constant distance, state-design testing has sample complexity Theta_t(d^(t/2)); unitary results distinguish sample count, queries per sampled process, and total coherent query cost. Additional frame-potential estimators and lower bounds cover controlled/inverse access regimes.
review.prior_frontier: Design certification usually focused on moments or frame potentials without a unified separation of independent samples and reusable oracle queries. The state dimension exponent is matched; several epsilon dependences and unitary sample/query tradeoffs remain unmatched.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate, subject to a targeted large-proof audit across its principal independent branches; not yet correctness-cleared.

papers.title: No Truly Sublogarithmic-Round Algorithm for Distributed MIS in the LOCAL Model
papers.authors: Seri Khoury, Aaron Schild

review.title: No Truly Sublogarithmic-Round Algorithm for Distributed MIS in the LOCAL Model
review.authors: Seri Khoury, Aaron Schild
review.summary: Proves randomized LOCAL MIS requires Omega(log n/log log n) rounds for any fixed positive global success probability, even with IDs [n], exact n and constant-factor maximum degree knowledge. Hard graphs blow up a degree-Theta(log n) high-girth skeleton into polynomial-size cliques joined by dense random bipartite edges.
review.prior_frontier: Improves prior Omega(sqrt(log n)) lower bound toward classical O(log n) upper; leaves a log log n factor. Sources and full proof not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Nearly closes a decades-old worst-case distributed MIS complexity gap.
score_reasons.novelty: Dense clique blowups and conditional-resampling entropy bounds overcome limitations of locally treelike hard graphs.
score_reasons.depth: Requires overlapping-view information budgets, truncation accounting and reduction to exact finite LOCAL identifiers.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit global-success theorem and separate warmups clarify how the stronger final entropy estimate is used.

checked: Traced final occupancy algebra conditional on Lemma 9.2/Proposition 10.3: p<=rb+sqrt((76rp/D)log(emr/p)), m<=D^4,r<=D,p>=1/D gives p<=4732r log D/D.
Read single-layer resampling KL calculation conditional on branch-independence lemma; entropy symmetry is averaged over inner views, not falsely imposed pointwise.
Verified crude ID extraction uses disjoint matrix quadrants for pairwise independent labels; exact [n] IDs require separate appendix.

Traced the new multi-layer entropy argument (Lemmas 7.1–7.3): conditional independence is used only for raw disjoint edge-variable extensions A,B given F_h; I((Z_u,Z_v);A,B|F_h) dominates the two marginal informations. Branch equality is averaged over inner views. Summing the increments gives D J_t/2 >= (D-1)H_t+K, with J_R=2K from independent private draws, and hence the scalar coincidence lower bound via KL/Hellinger.

Checked random-matrix and shortlist concentration (Lemmas 5.1–5.3,8.1–8.5): sequential distinct sampling bounds each coordinate probability by P(x)/tail; density >=1/4 gives tail-product <=4 conflict. Independent eligibility indicators plus Markov on shared-output capture losses give 3t/4, not an unjustified independence assertion. With h=floor(nu/8), M=1000ell, 16e/1000<1/2 and D^3 2^{-h}/(h-1)<1/(8D), the fixed-list contradiction is quantitative.

Traced conditional truncation Proposition 8.6, including deleted-coordinate mass <=1/m, f=(tau_Y-2/D)_+/2, weighted average branch failure <=delta*mu, and the entropy lower bound for E[f_u f_v]. Constants give tau <=2100 log(D)/D+6sqrt(w). Kept/deleted conflicts are disjoint subsets; intermediate positive conflicts arise only in resampling.

Traced the central first-failure partition (Lemma 10.2/Proposition 10.3) rather than assuming independence of deletions: nested views and tower conditioning identify each resampled stage with original surviving coordinates; each later deleted part has zero conflict and a previous m-coordinate shortlist conditional on V_j. Direct multi-layer KL comparison bounds its conflict by 2tau_j log(em/tau_j)/D; mass partition and entropy give S<=2p log(emr/p)/D without an extra r.

Checked finite LOCAL reduction and Appendix A: disjoint oriented P×Q matrix blocks yield independent tentative IDs with point probabilities <=2/n; graph-ID correlation is allowed. Fixing identifier-indexed private tapes yields a symmetric T+3 rule; legal exact-[n] completion preserves all repair neighborhoods and is independent of tapes. External domination union bound is over all choices before selecting the MIS. Checked the maximal-edge switching proof of a D-regular girth-g skeleton and parameter choices D=floor(log n/4), k~e^D, N even~n/k: local-ID collision o(1), external-domination n*gamma=o(1), and skeleton size dominates D^{2T+6}.
remaining: No independent implementation or mechanized proof check was performed. Historical priority and comparisons to earlier LOCAL lower bounds were not independently audited; the new occupancy theorem and exact-ID reduction were checked mathematically.

papers.title: Certifying Capacity and Gaps of the Rank-Dependent Gain-Sharing Framework for Ranking
papers.authors: Pan Xu

review.title: Certifying Capacity and Gaps of the Rank-Dependent Gain-Sharing Framework for Ranking
review.authors: Pan Xu
review.area: Online matching / limits of primal-dual analyses
review.summary: Computes exact degree-two Ranking competitiveness and limitations of rank-dependent gain sharing; online degree<=2 has actual ratio about .7177 versus monotone-certificate .7149, and 2-regular graphs have 119/144 versus 3/4. Proves positive gaps even for arbitrary measurable splits, and regular-graph competitiveness tends to 1-1/e.
review.prior_frontier: Prior analyses recover 1-1/e without degree restrictions and gave weaker upper bounds on Ranking for regular graphs. The manuscript distinguishes optimizing a split from changing the algorithm; comparison claims not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Quantifies an analysis barrier and sharpens the actual performance of a canonical online algorithm under degree restrictions.
score_reasons.novelty: Separates monotonicity loss from limitations persisting over all measurable rank-only charge splits.
score_reasons.depth: Uses rooted order-state safety events, positive kernel mixtures, exact function optimization and regular graph approximations.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise framework distinctions, but 95 pages and several interlocking exact/asymptotic results make the contribution costly to verify.

checked: Checked positive-mixture upper-bound identity; it uses Dirac measures and requires no minimax interchange.
Traced rooted order-state invariant: an arrival with overlapping witness sets kills both positive safety events; disjoint states merge with opposite root comparisons.
Checked monomial conditional safety profile via linear-extension counts and preservation of the disjoint-or-mutually-exclusive invariant.
remaining: Exact quartic/filtered-root minimization, actual degree-two competitive lower bound, regular-instance constants, all-measurable protocol barriers and large-degree asymptotics remain unaudited.

papers.title: Improved NP-Hardness of Approximation for Max-3-Cut and for Max-k-Cut with Small k
papers.authors: Ziang Ni

review.title: Improved NP-Hardness of Approximation for Max-3-Cut and for Max-k-Cut with Small k
review.authors: Ziang Ni
review.summary: Proves unconditional NP-hardness of approximating weighted Max-3-Cut beyond 27/29+epsilon, via a completeness/soundness gap 29/30 versus 9/10. Gives 45/47 for Max-4-Cut, 33/34 for Max-5-Cut and improvements through k=20. The main reduction lacks perfect completeness; separate known-reduction refinements give 82/85 on 4-colorable graphs. An LP-certified barrier limits the specified black-box 3Lin gadget framework, not all hardness reductions.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the 16/17 general Max-3-Cut NP-hardness bound, while that prior bound still remains for 3-colorable graphs. Prior sources and rational barrier certificate not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Improves a longstanding unconditional constant for a basic cut problem and several small-k cases.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines an equation and its negation to avoid color-reference gadgets, with a generalized soundness criterion.
score_reasons.depth: The core 3-cut proof is short; broader soundness and universal gadget barrier add depth.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly distinguishes general versus colorable graphs, NP versus UGC hardness and the scope of the gadget barrier.

checked: Traced the E/N gadget values for the three color-equality patterns and the family (2E,N,N). Completeness gives 58/3 out of weight20; soundness charges both sigma and -sigma to get18, producing27/29.
remaining: Verify the balanced role-separated form of Hastad’s theorem, generalized Fourier soundness criterion, extra-color gadget arithmetic and exact LP certificates.
