papers.title: Product Expansion of Random Codes via Analytic Techniques
papers.authors: Eshan Chattopadhyay, Noam Ringach, Nicholas Spooner

review.title: Product Expansion of Random Codes via Analytic Techniques
review.authors: Eshan Chattopadhyay, Noam Ringach, Nicholas Spooner

score_reasons.significance: Product expansion is central to modern locally testable and quantum-code constructions; a new route and symmetric witnesses are consequential.
score_reasons.novelty: The Rademacher/sparse-Gram-to-finite-field approach and cyclic symmetry construction are distinctive.
score_reasons.depth: Requires nontrivial sparse random-matrix moments, Wigner-word counting, polynomial transfer, and algebraic interpolation.
score_reasons.exposition: The two-part organization and explicit field-size/rate restrictions help, although 103 pages and large constants make verification demanding.

checked: Checked the elementary sparse-plane setup and normalized Rademacher operator-norm estimate via Gaussian symmetrization.
Checked the sparse tensor Gram trace expansion, diagonal exclusion, bijection to non-left-backtracking bipartite walks, and even-edge criterion for a nonzero Rademacher expectation.
remaining: Audit the decisive sparse Wigner-word equivalence-class count and the resulting operator-norm parameters.
Audit the real-to-prime-field transfer, field-size bookkeeping, and Part II cyclic Reed-Solomon/interpolation construction. No binary or explicit-construction consequence has been verified.

review.summary: Proves product expansion of random codes over sufficiently large growing prime fields using real analytic estimates and finite-field transfer, and constructs product-expanding rate-1/2 MDS pairs invariant under a common cyclic action. These are existential large-field statements; they do not prove binary expansion or an explicit qLTC construction.
review.prior_frontier: Prior random-code product-expansion arguments depended on more elaborate coding machinery. This supplies an analytic route at arbitrary rates bounded away from 0 and 1, plus same-length symmetric witnesses complementing concurrent algebraic constructions.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate for a focused large-proof audit; the elementary reductions checked so far do not establish its central counting and transfer steps.

papers.title: Stable Movement for Nondual Lipschitz Convex Optimization: Efficiency and Nearly Optimal Oracle Rates
papers.authors: David Martinez-Rubio, Cristóbal Guzmán

review.title: Stable Movement for Nondual Lipschitz Convex Optimization: Efficiency and Nearly Optimal Oracle Rates
review.authors: David Martínez-Rubio, Cristóbal Guzmán
review.summary: For fixed 1≤p≤min(q,2), q>1, gives a polynomial-time real-arithmetic randomized algorithm using T first-order queries with high-probability error Õ_p,q(GR/T^(1/p−(1/q−1/2)_+)) over RB_p. Stable nested-body selectors attain matching high-dimensional movement rates; includes Õ(GR/T) for p=1,q=2. Polynomial degree can depend on p,q; no bit-complexity or Hölder-smooth theorem is claimed here.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript identifies Bullins et al. (also submission #69) as already attaining these oracle rates with exponential computation, and seeks computational efficiency; older randomized lower bounds are extended. Historical lower-bound dependencies not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the efficient nonsmooth nondual-geometry oracle frontier, including the simplex/Euclidean-Lipschitz case.
score_reasons.novelty: The optimization-to-chasing reduction and mixed-norm Gaussian selector turn oracle-optimal but computationally inefficient strategies into efficient ones.
score_reasons.depth: Head-tail lifting, stable selectors, approximate-center control and polynomial implementation require several interacting geometric arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: The modular bundle algorithm and exact real-arithmetic qualifications make the source of the improvement clear.

checked: Checked the deep-cut bound Γ/(2G), geometric phase contraction, and the resulting T≈(GR/ε)^(1/ρ) arithmetic conditional on the movement bound.

Checked the elementary head-tail exponents and p=1,q=2 specialization.
remaining: Audit the mixed-norm selector movement theorem and its sampling concentration under adaptive requests.
Trace the ellipsoid/inner-ball feasibility and approximation guarantees giving polynomial computation, including finite precision if claiming more than real arithmetic.
Verify randomized optimization lower-bound reduction and cited chasing/lower-bound dependencies.

score_reasons.novelty: Combines Gaussian convex-order domination with forced moves toward the smaller endpoint and a backward ternary witness tree.
score_reasons.depth: A compact convex-functional selection theorem supports the new tail argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Self-contained central proof and explicit implementation limitation; constants and exceptional parameter range are transparent.

checked: Traced one-dimensional convex transform: interior equal-height case loses at most H on a length-eight interval and gains H/2 on its complement; boundary case uses (z-25)_+<=z^2/100.
Checked high-dimensional transform convexity by partial minimization, isotropic Gaussian conditioning, and compatibility of forced moves outside endpoint gap 27.
Traced finite affine separation and compact finite-intersection argument establishing a simultaneous admissible selection for all convex test functions.
Traced algorithm law recursion and receiver gap<=29; backward slack gains using integer increments, leaf threshold D^2/80 and input-only witness count 2T*3^ceil(D^2/80).
Verified subgaussian union-bound exponent, D>=300 inequality and final rounding of the high-probability threshold; sign reversal preserves receiving gap.
remaining: The existence proof does not furnish a polynomial-time sampler/selection algorithm. Historical optimality comparison and cited conjecture attribution were not independently audited.

Traced local acyclic replacement and coordinate-projection decoding even with cycles/self-loops in the source generalized circuit.
remaining: Audit all three auction constructions, exact no-slack conditions and FIXP membership dependencies.
Verify the cited restricted squaring-basis completeness result.

score_reasons.significance: A complete classification for a central counting model would close a major structural gap.

score_reasons.depth: The proof combines gadget interpolation, finite-dimensional real algebras, polynomial factorization, and classification of Hamming/Doob intersection arrays.

checked: Checked the mixed-derivative identity giving CD/n from log(exp_entrywise(sC) exp_entrywise(tD)), using zero row and column sums and finite-dimensional closure.

Verify the composable realizability/interpolation framework, centering, and local analytic homomorphism construction.
Audit affine factorization, distance-regular classification and hardness gadgets, plus the zero-entry/rank-deficient extension and real-number computational convention.

review.summary: Classifies planar graph-homomorphism partition functions for every fixed symmetric nonnegative real matrix: general-graph tractability, planar-only tractability via holographic FKT, or planar #P-hardness. review.summary: Characterizes finite commutative aperiodic monoid product queries by Theta(min(n,sqrt(n beta))) with full alphabet, where beta is product breadth. Gives breadth-sensitive stably ordered algorithms and improves general N-element aperiodic products to sqrt(n) log^{O((N log N)^(1/3))}(n); query returns a full element and multiplication table is known.
review.prior_frontier: Quantifies the Aaronson–Grier–Schaeffer star-free upper bound beyond fixed monoid size. Product breadth coincides with the classical small Davenport constant in the commutative case. Claimed Lean formalizations were not executed.

score_reasons.significance: Provides structural rather than fixed-algebra bounds and a substantial size-dependent exponent improvement.
score_reasons.novelty: Backward essential width with depth-dependent adversary weights removes the logarithmic loss; regular-class representations control general monoids.
score_reasons.depth: Uses adversary duals, monoid ideal structure, matrix representations and nilpotent radical recovery.
score_reasons.exposition: Careful input-alphabet and query-model qualifications, with an extensive 103-page algebraic development.

checked: Traced essential-width adversary proof: first differing state gives the sole nonzero query contribution; random-order hazard <=B/t and weights sqrt(t/B),sqrt(B/t) yield 16sqrt(nB).
Checked commutative aperiodicity gives J-triviality; every deletion-essential position belongs to every preserving subword.
Traced the matching lower-bound biregular adversary graph; identity in the permitted alphabet is essential for padding and stated tightness.
Screened general-monoid regular-class/radical strategy and size/dimension tradeoff; distinguished it from the fully traced commutative result.
remaining: Stable-order algorithm, breadth versus aperiodicity index, full cube-root N exponent, nilpotent lifting and bounded-depth Dyck parameter conversion remain unaudited. Lean source/build and formalization scope not verified.

papers.title: Tree Equivalence of Higher-Order Recursion Schemes Is Undecidable
papers.authors: Mingkun Xiao, Yixuan Sun

review.title: Tree Equivalence of Higher-Order Recursion Schemes Is Undecidable
review.authors: Mingkun Xiao, Yixuan Sun
review.summary: Tree equality for deterministic higher-order recursion schemes is Pi^0_1-complete, already for safe productive schemes of order at most four over one nullary and one binary symbol. The lower bound reduces nonhalting of deterministic two-counter machines. The general upper bound includes nonproductive schemes with bottom labels. Related lambda-Y equivalence transfers do not claim preservation of the same order/safety restriction.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves the stated longstanding higher-order tree-equivalence question; known decidable MSO model checking and nondeterministic pushdown bisimilarity results do not settle it. Prior-model correspondence claims not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a fundamental equivalence question with strong fixed-order and fixed-alphabet restrictions.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses signed polynomial guard weights and a shift recurrence at fixed simple types, then compares two varying unary observations to detect cancellation.
score_reasons.depth: Must enforce safety despite unbounded polynomial degree, preserve productivity and prove full higher-type representation adequacy.
score_reasons.exposition: The manuscript explicitly explains the unsafe naive encoding and supplies a type/operand audit and precise transfer limitations.

checked: Traced the first-error invariant: Z_m(c) kills false-zero tests while c kills false-positive tests, and zero persists after invalid prefixes.

Read the fixed-type shift update Z_{m+1}(x)=(x-1)Z_m(x-1), source control compiler and operand safety table. Read why logical relations over arbitrary functional arguments are required for numeral reuse.

Traced the entire first-error reduction: legal counters after m instructions lie in [0,m]; Z_m(x)=product_{j=1}^m(x-j) is nonzero at0 and zero at every possible false-zero counter. A false positive at0 multiplies by0, and later illegal negative counters cannot restore a zero signed weight. Zero-start machine initialization and the inc-A/dec-A jump gadget preserve counters and out-of-range halting targets.

Checked fixed-type polynomial implementation algebraically: C_{m+1}(u,v)=(u,v+1) tensor C_m(u,v+1) has difference (u-v-1)Z_m(u-v-1)=Z_{m+1}(u-v). Both components stay natural even for negative virtual counter differences. State rules use the old counter/polynomial in guard multiplication and advance the polynomial on every branch; no hidden unbounded step-register or type growth is used.

Completed the order/safety audit of the actual expanded rules. C=o->o, N=C->C, P=N->N->N have orders1,2,3; polynomial updates and state symbols have order4. All types and their application suffixes are homogeneous. Every nonground operand has order at most each free parameter order; in particular Next p q has order3 with only order3 parameters, while p u (Succ v) is order2 with order2/3 parameters. The order3 prefix p u is in function position, not an operand, under the stated safety definition.

Traced the higher-type logical-relation proof rather than checking numerals only at observation arguments. Num requires correct iteration for every related function and ground map; Mul applies the first numeral to the function realized by the second, establishing m*n iterations. Pol_m quantifies over arbitrary numeral representations, so shifted arguments and all later composed arithmetic remain reusable. Induction yields Reg_m on every candidate, without legality assumptions.

Checked productivity and both directions of operational correspondence at all finite addresses. State roots expose b immediately; halt observations terminate because the selected component realizes a finite numeral, including invalid zero-weight branches. Any first discrepancy must enter child0 of a genuine halt; unequal unary chain lengths imply nonzero signed weight and therefore a legal source halt. The fixed binary contexts are injectively decodable (source children at1 or10/110/111), preserve substitution, order and safety, and keep all outputs productive.

Traced the direct upper bound fully. Finite domains are all monotone function tables over {0<1}; simultaneous iteration stops only when the complete nonterminal environment stabilizes. A typed logical relation proves each finite semantic approximant operationally sound, and fixed-point substitution makes every actual head unfolding denotation-preserving, giving exact head convergence. The total reader distinguishes a present bottom node from an absent child, computes exact finite prefixes, and expresses equality plus productivity as a universal computable predicate even for invalid input codes. This establishes the claimed Pi^0_1 upper bound rather than merely semideciding positive observations.

Checked the paper-level consequences ruling out complete effective equality certificates and computable disagreement-depth bounds by dovetailing/finite-prefix comparison on the productive compiler outputs.
remaining: The supplementary Rocq artifact at Zenodo was not downloaded or compiled; no independent machine-checked status is claimed. The external HORS-to-pushdown and lambda-Y equivalence translations underlying Corollaries7.1–7.2, and the cited source-machine universality proof, were not independently re-proved. The main fixed-order safe productive HORS reduction and general finite-semantics upper bound were checked directly.

review.authors: Hongyi Chen, Shuyan Fan, Tianyi Zhang

score_reasons.significance: The first polynomial improvement in this important adaptive dynamic graph regime is substantial.
score_reasons.novelty: Candidate maintenance and information-restricted probabilistic games offer new tools for adaptive sampling analysis.
score_reasons.depth: The main challenge is coupling dynamic invariants and amortization with exactly what the output leaks about hidden samples.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper explains the old bottleneck and states adversary/update assumptions; the 62-page data-structure specification is necessarily involved.

checked: Checked geometric skipping as independent Bernoulli sampling.
Checked the membership-query game: unrevealed live bits remain independent, reveal-and-delete coins cannot be reused, and the first no answer stops accumulation of known sampled elements.
Checked the emptiness-query game: fixing the all-nonempty history fixes its operations, Harris controls empty events, and an unconditional binomial tail suffices for sample size despite conditioning.
remaining: Verify that the actual MIS update process and all adversary-visible outputs expose only the permitted game information.
Audit migration thresholds, candidate rebuilding, failure union bounds, and amortized m^(5/8) operation counts.

review.title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part I: Glauber Dynamics
review.authors: Aniket Das, Tselil Schramm
review.summary: For fixed tensor order k≥3, signed-hypercube Gaussian tensor PCA at λ≥C_k N^((k−2)/4) admits polynomial-time strong recovery from uniform initialization using high-temperature Glauber trajectory averaging followed by low-temperature dynamics. Odd k uses the averaged spin vector; general k uses an augmented second moment and its top eigenvector. Averaging is polynomially long, not near-input-linear, and this does not lower the general algorithmic SNR threshold.
review.prior_frontier: Prior cold-start local methods required λ roughly N^((k−2)/2), while global spectral/SoS methods reached N^((k−2)/4). The manuscript explicitly augments the dynamics by annealing and averaging, so fixed-temperature conjectures are not directly contradicted. Historical threshold claims not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Closes a substantial local-versus-global algorithm gap for a central planted inference model.
score_reasons.novelty: Ergodic differential recovery and reverse planting supply informative warm starts from the local chain itself.
score_reasons.depth: Controlling disorder correlated with the whole trajectory, adaptive contiguity and recovery dynamics is technically extensive.
score_reasons.exposition: The model normalization, cold-start qualification, even-order modification and runtime gap are clearly stated.

checked: Traced Theorem 4.1: Boolean integration by parts, signed-permutation symmetry, Gaussian linearity and trace covariance yield u_H=λσ_N²x*+ζ with iid variance σ_N²≈N^(-(k−1)/2); even k vanishes by spin flip.
Traced Corollary 4.3: sign rounding gives iid biased Rademachers with mean Θ(min(λσ_N,1)), hence N^(-1/4) correlation at threshold and exp(−Ω(√N)) failure.
Checked why raw odd-order averages cannot be used for even k, and distinguished the eigenvector postprocessing in Algorithm 2.
remaining: The 79-page tensor-PCA algorithm has a traced Gaussian reduction and sign-rounding calculation. Reverse planting, adaptive contiguity and ergodic approximation are the essential unverified steps from this ideal statistic to an actual algorithm; this is a large-proof exception.
Audit ergodic-average approximation and its time/uniformity estimates.
Audit reverse planting, adaptive contiguity and correlated-disorder control, which are central to the main recovery theorem.
Trace the even-order second-moment extension and finite-operation simulation bounds; this screening is not a full 80-page proof audit.

review.title: Fair Team Contracts

review.summary: For a new swap-based fairness notion in binary-effort team contracts, optimal submodular contracts have shares max(incentive threshold, common floor). Fairness is within the hired team, relative to a common pure equilibrium after each swap, with effort-favoring ties.
review.prior_frontier: Related work studies unconstrained team contracts and equal-share contracts; this paper changes the fairness benchmark, so its approximation is not a direct improvement of those guarantees. Prior literature not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial treatment of a precisely defined new fairness constraint, rather than a resolution of an established general contracting barrier.
score_reasons.novelty: The endogenous floor and tight equal-share comparison give a structural explanation for permitted pay differences.
score_reasons.depth: Combines equilibrium response, XOS additive transfer, discretized optimization and submodular greedy/pruning.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions clarify the existential equilibrium comparison and continued payment to agents who cease effort.

checked: Traced unique post-swap equilibrium: all agents whose shares do not fall remain active by submodularity; only the decreased-share agent can exit.
Checked fairness inequalities for unequal shares and the floor L*=max_i threshold_i*f(S\i)/f(S).
Checked monotonic ordering of fair shares by incentive thresholds and why max(L*,threshold_i) satisfies the strict dropout condition for unequal shares.
remaining: Additive FPTAS/NP-hardness, tight cubic-root constant, transfer to submodular rewards and 0.249 numerical/algorithmic analysis remain unaudited. The fixed-team structural theorem implicitly requires an incentivizable team.

review.title: Faster enumeration of primes
review.authors: David Harvey

score_reasons.significance: A near-output-linear Las Vegas bound for enumerating primes is a major algorithmic advance on a classical task.
score_reasons.novelty: The generating-function, compressed block multiplication, and correction of dense exceptional intervals form a new approach.
score_reasons.depth: The 108-page proof combines arithmetic in quadratic rings, fast transforms, coding-style reconstruction, sieve estimates and deterministic certification.
score_reasons.exposition: The exposition carefully separates rigorous, randomized and conjectural claims, gives a useful roadmap, and candidly identifies memory and practicality limitations.

checked: Traced the parity generating-function identity through quadratic-ring ideal counts and the split/inert Euler products modulo 4.
Checked the sparse compression map's Vandermonde injectivity rationale and the explicit restriction that core candidates are guaranteed only on low-weight intervals.
Inspected the randomized permutation implementation and impostor-counting setup; distinguished final prime-counting certification from the conjecture asserting that failure never occurs.
remaining: This 108-page paper has genuine prior checks of the parity identity, compression injectivity and randomized certification framework. The claimed fast prime-enumeration runtime requires numerous arithmetic, sieve and data-movement estimates not covered by those checks; selection is explicitly a large-proof exception.
Audit the main fast compression/decompression and sliced/block polynomial arithmetic, including Turing-machine data movement.

Audit exceptional-interval sieve estimates, randomized impostor probability, square-primality repair, final certification, and the two rigorous parameter optimizations. The elementary identity check alone does not certify the runtime theorem.

review.summary: Gives prime enumeration in N(log N)^(1/2)(log log N)^(1+o(1)) deterministic bit operations and expected N(log log N)^(2+o(1)) Las Vegas time. These are multitape-Turing asymptotic results, with roughly linear space and no practical implementation claim.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the best previous prime-enumeration bit bounds by a positive power of log N, using fast polynomial arithmetic and sparse-vector compression instead of explicitly processing all sieve incidences. The rigorous randomized theorem is distinct from the faster heuristic theorem.
review.recommendation: Exceptional candidate for a targeted large-proof audit, based on the rigorous theorems rather than the heuristic speedup.

papers.authors: Junho Hwang

review.title: Tight Bounds for Randomized Generalized k-Server on Uniform Metrics
review.authors: Junho Hwang
review.summary: Randomized generalized k-server on uniform metrics has tight Theta(k log k) competitive ratio against oblivious inputs, and weighted uniform metrics have exp(Theta(k)) ratio via a 20^k algorithm. Unit-weight upper bound is (k+1)ln(2k) with no additive term, even for infinite spaces.
review.prior_frontier: Improves O(k^2 log k) versus Omega(k) to matching order for unit weights, and exp(O(k^2)) to exp(O(k)) for weighted spaces. Prior lower-bound dependencies were not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Closes both randomized competitive-ratio orders for a central generalized server model.
score_reasons.novelty: Exact coupling to decaying configuration weights and a planted permutation-constraint lower bound address different sides of the gap.
score_reasons.depth: Weighted multilevel simulations and random-CSP component geometry accompany a particularly simple unweighted potential.
score_reasons.exposition: Makes obliviousness, arbitrary weights and cardinalities explicit; state-distribution tracking is not an efficient implementation claim.

checked: Fully traced unit-weight upper bound: lazification by Hamming potential, half-mass distributed among k repairs, and half-resampling preserve normalized weights.
Checked expected movement <=(k+1) log(Phi_old/Phi_new), offline surviving weight >=(2k)^(-OPT) and telescoping with common initial configuration.
Screened lower-bound component separation and weighted-level recurrence, keeping them distinct from the checked upper bound.

Traced the complete new unit-weight lower bound. Conditioned permutation-constraint acceptance has exact pair probability D_d/(k-1)^d; the second-moment bound and first-moment forbidden-distance/support estimates yield a fixed good system with exponentially many solutions.

Recomputed the delicate numeric exponents for delta=.04,eta=.08,beta=.77,alpha=.9: G1 endpoints -0.0118795,-0.00412578; G2 endpoints -0.00185246,-0.00898846; G3 -1.17315578. All exceed the claimed asymptotic negativity margin1/600. The final leading constant .1*.77*(.77-.08)=.05313>1/20.

Checked component confinement and posterior accounting: each component varies in<eta*k coordinates and has<2^k solutions; fixed hidden permutation remains uniform on survivors; inverse survivor-count expectation bounds the chance of sharing its component. Confinement depends on the algorithm distribution and prior requests, not realized algorithm coins, so the adversary is oblivious.

Traced the weighted20^k upper bound end to end: maximal coupling of normalized expert weights charges at most2Delta times log mass loss; survivor expert is fixed by the request parser independently of its randomness; c_l=3c_(l-1)+4log(d_l-1)+2 <=10*5^(l-1).

Checked coordinate-specific demand conservation, contamination recursion and hard-multiphase selection. At mostm/16 phases contaminated by server l and<m/8 by larger servers leave enough good phases; the l=2 adjacent-witness argument covers m=2,3 separately. Every completed k-phase costs OPT at leastv_k/2^k.

Checked arbitrary weights: integer-ratio rounding gives w_i<=v_i<=2^(i-1)w_i, dummy unrequested points retract without extra cost, zero cheapest weight is trivial, and composing factors gives exactly20^k OPT+10^k w_k. No polynomial-time implementation is claimed.
remaining: The external Omega(2^k) weighted k-server lower bound used to label the result tight up to the exponential base was checked for model compatibility on the official ESA2021 source, not re-proved.

Main-proof-checked covers the three new main bounds; all bounds are for an oblivious adversary. Algorithms maintain potentially enormous supports and the weighted phase construction can have huge k-dependent state.

sources.detail: Primary prior exponential weighted-k-server lower-bound model verified.

papers.title: A Bulow--Klemperer Theorem for Bundling and Improved Approximation Bounds for Simple Auctions
papers.authors: Yichen Huang

review.title: A Bulow--Klemperer Theorem for Bundling and Improved Approximation Bounds for Simple Auctions
review.authors: Yichen Huang
review.summary: For one additive bidder with independent nonnegative regular item values of finite monopoly revenue, optimal revenue is at most the reserve-free grand-bundle second-price revenue from two iid bidders, itself at most twice optimal one-bidder bundling; factor2 is tight. For arbitrary independent items, REV<=SREV+(pi^2/6)BREV, giving factor<2.645; a separate bounded-value construction exceeds2.11. Exact recovery by the better of optimal separate/bundle auctions can require Omega(log m) bidders without regularity.
review.prior_frontier: Improves prior constants5.2 and concurrent3.52/3 for arbitrary independent items, and stated48-approximate two-bidder/18-approximate bundling regular-item bounds to exact competition and tight factor2. Prior and concurrent sources not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Gives an exact multidimensional Bulow–Klemperer statement and substantially narrows the basic simple-versus-optimal revenue ratio.
score_reasons.novelty: Charges threshold variation or cumulative entropy of total value minus utility to unallocated value, avoiding the usual core-tail decomposition.
score_reasons.depth: Combines quantile regularity, entropy tensorization, unbounded-menu limits and carefully designed lower examples.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear separation of independence, regularity, original bidder count and approximate versus exact competition.

checked: Traced regular scalar inequality q(1-q)(-vprime)<=v and coordinate replacement tensorization of absolute variation, yielding REV<=BSPA2 for bounded residual menus.
Traced cumulative-entropy tensorization and normalized one-item payments, yielding REV<=J(total)+SREV; read the equal-revenue-tail extremal reduction for the pi^2/6 bound.

Team audit completed the regular-quantile and unbounded-menu steps. Concave R gives v=R/q locally absolutely continuous, while bounded Lipschitz residual g removes endpoint terms; nondifferentiable g points matter only on quantile plateaux where v-prime=0. Adding the bundle at price M gives p_M>=min(p,M) and bounded residual w<=M, so limiting the finite-residual inequality avoids subtracting infinite expectations.

Team audit traced normalized coordinate payments p_j=z*x_j-[u(z)-u(0)]>=0, their one-item revenue bound E p_j<=r_j, cumulative-entropy tensorization, and the extremal scalar integral giving pi^2/6. Independently checked Appendix B: the entropy chain identity plus convexity (second derivative/Cauchy–Schwarz) and product independence prove the tensorization used on threshold indicators.

Team audit checked the tight regular example and lower-bound completion: the concentrated harmonic block has variance <=2c^2/(N H_N^2), remaining mean tends to zero, and REV(X+E)<=(sqrt(REV(X))+sqrt(E E))^2 controls the perturbation. Rare huge values contribute only the quantified O(d*W_max/M) excess beyond max(REV(W),d). The compound-Poisson intensity is positive with mass log16 and mean23/48; independent splitting and the multiple-jump bound hold uniformly over prices, and capping at1/2 preserves the chosen seed-price sale and shifted-revenue upper bound.

Independently traced all Appendix C quantitative inequalities. The Laplace identity follows by integrating exp(-ux) over u and Tonelli, and the two rate pairs reproduce the specified zero-inflated exponential components. The e^(1/2)<33/20 rational series bound implies seed revenue >7/50. For shifted bundle prices psi(0)=9, psi-prime(0)=-105, psi-double-prime>=750 gives the positive quadratic 375(t-7/50)^2+33/20. For separate prices, convex trapezoid integration and the exponential-integral majorant yield eta(t); chi-triple-prime>0 gives chi>=3/560-9t/280+t^2/15>0, hence the all-price 9/80 bound.

Team audit checked the logarithmic-competition construction: the rare powers have tail <=2^(1-j), yielding scalar revenue<=4. Concentration separates the one-bidder benchmark E C+2.5n from bundle k-bidder revenue <=E C+4k+sqrt(2n)<E C+1.5n, and separate k-bidder revenue<=5kn<E C. The item-count bound 5n<=exp(20k) and zero-padding give the stated logarithmic lower bound.

Independently checked Appendix A auction reductions: a uniformly positioned real bidder among simulated iid bidders retains 1/k expected payments in a truthful one-bidder mechanism; fixing independent Y and subtracting y_i times allocation preserves utility and IR, with total subtraction at most max_i y_i. These justify the bundle bidder-sampling and component bounds used in the construction.
remaining: Standard single-item revenue characterization, convex-utility characterization of truthful mechanisms, and cited prior/concurrent frontier comparisons were used through their stated interfaces rather than independently re-proved. This is a mathematical team audit, not a mechanized verification or implementation.

papers.title: Batched Updates for Dynamic Single-Source Shortest Paths on Directed Graphs with Nonnegative Edge Weights
papers.authors: Yuhan Chen, Zanbo Zhang, Jun Liang

review.title: Batched Updates for Dynamic Single-Source Shortest Paths on Directed Graphs with Nonnegative Edge Weights
review.authors: Yuhan Chen, Jun Liang, Zanbo Zhang

score_reasons.significance: Potentially useful implementation-level batching improvement, but limited established asymptotic advance for a flagship theory venue.
score_reasons.novelty: Two-phase propagation and deferred queue coverage refine known affected-area ideas rather than establish a new dynamic complexity frontier.
score_reasons.depth: Zero-weight ties, delayed eligibility, and safe commitment require careful invariant reasoning.
score_reasons.exposition: The distinctions between scheduled and true affected work are commendably explicit, although dense state rules and residual anonymous headers reduce readability.

checked: Traced finite path-witness preservation, deferred queue coverage, and the shortest-path-boundary argument for safe distance commitment.
Checked the monotone-legal-key reasoning behind one full repair per incoming container and the operation-count interpretation of the stated complexity.
remaining: Audit output-parent acyclicity on zero-weight cycles and all initialization/parallel-edge cases.
Check exact integer priority-queue assumptions and compare novelty with the cited affected-area algorithms. No general scheduled-to-true-affected-set reduction is available.

review.summary: Proposes a two-visit propagation/commitment scheme for mixed batched nonnegative SSSP updates. The bound is O(k+examined_records+scheduled_vertices log scheduled_vertices), or a log-log queue term under polynomial integer-key assumptions. The stronger bound in terms of genuinely changed vertices is explicitly conditional on scheduled-work control.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier affected-area dynamic SSSP frameworks already reuse old shortest-path structure under heterogeneous modifications. The contribution is a specific batching discipline and local-container analysis; the unrestricted worst-case bound remains comparable to recomputation, and no general true-affected-set improvement is proved.
review.recommendation: Below the current top-400 standard on significance and novelty; not a desk reject merely for being incremental. Full correctness has not been certified.

papers.title: Low-Rank Denoising for Predict-then-Optimize
papers.authors: Henry Aldridge-Krawciw, Irene Aldridge

review.title: Low-Rank Denoising for Predict-then-Optimize
review.authors: Henry Aldridge-Krawciw, Irene Aldridge
review.summary: Analyzes projecting a noisy averaged cost vector onto a low-rank signal subspace before shortest-path optimization. Gives exact bias/variance MSE, optimal projector onto positive eigenvalues of Σ_c−D/m, incoherence-dependent replication savings, bounded independent-coordinate-noise margin bounds, and a learned-subspace bound under exact low rank and homoscedastic sub-Gaussian noise. MSE optimality is not regret optimality.
review.prior_frontier: Uses standard PCA projection, Ky Fan eigenvalue optimization, Hoeffding and Davis–Kahan bounds; comparison is primarily to plain averaging and a synthetic SPO+ benchmark, not an established unresolved computational frontier.

score_reasons.significance: Useful specialist clarification of when projection helps a one-shot decision problem, but limited general algorithmic advance.
score_reasons.novelty: The exact noise-aware projector and crossover formula synthesize familiar bias/variance principles.
score_reasons.depth: Central mathematical results follow by orthogonal decomposition, spectral variational principles and standard concentration.
score_reasons.exposition: Assumptions and experimental limitations are explicit, although some table references and boundary wording need polishing.

checked: Traced the orthogonal decomposition and Ky Fan optimization, including Loewner monotonicity of the optimal rank in m.
Checked the Hoeffding coordinate bound using Σ_j Π_ej²=Π_ee and the margin implication; it requires the stated bounded, independent coordinate noise.
Checked learned-subspace error reduction to a Davis–Kahan sine-angle term, conditional on the cited covariance concentration.
remaining: External covariance concentration constants and sample-centering adjustment not independently verified.
Experiments and code were not reproduced; projector/rank selection performance is not implied by the MSE theorem.

papers.title: Structural Origins of Cubic Complexity in Pebble Motion
papers.authors: Tadashi Sakuma, Tomoki Nakamigawa

review.title: Structural Origins of Cubic Complexity in Pebble Motion
review.authors: Tomoki Nakamigawa, Tadashi Sakuma
review.summary: Sequential labeled pebble motion on trees admits O(nN+n^2 log(1+min(n,k))) moves, where k is maximum isthmus size; hence O(N^2 log N) worst-case. Further cycle-length/diameter bounds and a unique giant biconnected-core description restrict feasible graph families with cubic worst-case motion.
review.prior_frontier: Classical general-graph bound is Theta(N^3); claimed first subcubic tree bound lies within logarithmic factor of quadratic lower bound. Earlier feasibility/decomposition theorem is crucial and was not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Separates tree motion from the classical cubic general-graph regime and links move complexity to structural obstructions.
score_reasons.novelty: A movable blank workspace and interface presentation/transcription mechanism organize the reconfiguration.
score_reasons.depth: An 87-page chain of local routing, centroid decomposition, workspace repairs and global structural consequences.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed pseudocode and model distinctions, but some broad overview claims require reading several later invariants and feasibility reductions.

checked: Checked distinction between feasible particular configurations and all-configuration feasible puzzles; extending to every feasible tree instance invokes the classical decomposition.
Checked stage-count arithmetic O((N/b)^2*b^2 log b) and more refined nN+n^2 log(1+min(n,k)) target.
Inspected permanent/temporary subtree states and explicit boundary-vertex repair in CutOff; traced cycle repair overhead multiplication O(k min(CL,n)D)*O(n/k).
Verified general graph runtime assumes shortest through-vertex cycles supplied, while the move bound excludes their preprocessing cost.
remaining: Local routing primitive, workspace invariant throughout extraction, feasibility of boundary repairs, structural necessity and sharp lower-bound examples remain unaudited. The supplied algorithms are sequential total-motion results, not parallel MAPF makespan claims.

papers.title: Proximity Gaps for Gabidulin Codes and Applications
papers.authors: Songsong Li, Chaoping Xing, Chen Yuan, Ruiqi Zhu

review.title: Proximity Gaps for Gabidulin Codes and Applications
review.authors: Songsong Li, Chaoping Xing, Chen Yuan, Ruiqi Zhu
review.summary: An F_{q^m}-linear rank-metric [n,k,d] code has correlated line proximity up to radius(d-1)/(3n), error q^{floor(delta*n)+1-m}. Gabidulin codes improve the radius to(d-1)/(2n), error at most10q^{n-1-m}. Explicit families show failure at d/(2n) and match the error dependence up to constants. A Ligero-style transparent extractable commitment for q-linearized polynomials has soft-O(lambda*k) prover and soft-O(lambda*sqrt(k)) verifier/proof costs measured in extension-field operations.
review.prior_frontier: Establishes rank-metric analogues of known Hamming/RS proximity gaps, with tight boundary examples and a new structured-polynomial commitment application. Prior Hamming bounds and security dependencies not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Extends a central proof-system soundness tool to rank-metric codes with quantitative tightness.
score_reasons.novelty: Globalizes rank-metric Berlekamp–Welch systems over a rational-function field, then replaces commutative division by coefficient recurrences.
score_reasons.depth: Must control Frobenius degree growth and correlated error support, with separate algebraic counterexamples and cryptographic composition.
score_reasons.exposition: Distinguishes common rank support from the weaker all-or-few property and states field-operation complexity; the error may be vacuous unless the extension is large enough.

checked: Traced specialization solvability to rational-function solvability by augmented-minor degree <=sigma_e, then Cramer denominator degree bounds.
Read uniqueness-based composition identities and the triangular Frobenius recurrence modulo the good-parameter polynomial.
remaining: Audit denominator clearing through the recurrence, the final shared-rank conclusion, both tightness constructions and all IOPP/PCS extraction assumptions.

papers.title: On Proximity Gaps for One-Point Algebraic Geometric Codes
papers.authors: Songsong Li, Chaoping Xing, Chen Yuan, Ruiqi Zhu

review.title: On Proximity Gaps for One-Point Algebraic Geometric Codes
review.authors: Songsong Li, Chaoping Xing, Chen Yuan, Ruiqi Zhu

score_reasons.significance: A useful extension for algebraic proof-system soundness, especially fixed-field long codes.
score_reasons.novelty: Auxiliary nonspecial divisors and error-incidence counting replace a divisibility lemma that does not directly transfer from Reed-Solomon codes.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines Riemann-Roch interpolation, parameter counting, and explicit AG-tower obstructions.
score_reasons.exposition: The abstract and theorem statements distinguish designed distance, slack, mutual agreement, and field/length dependence clearly.

checked: Traced the complete central half-distance argument in Theorem 3.1: finite bad-point sets construct an auxiliary divisor over a finite extension, dimension counting yields A nonzero, and the zero Riemann-Roch space forces B_z=A_z f_z.
Checked the error-incidence averaging, interpolation on ell+1 parameters, descent of the final coefficients to the original field, treatment of A_z=0, and final w(a-ell)<=ae count.
remaining: Audit the separate Johnson-radius mutual-agreement branch and both Garcia-Stichtenoth counterexamples, including tower asymptotics.
Verify all theorem-to-soundness parameter substitutions and imported algebraic-geometry facts before overall acceptance.

review.summary: Extends polynomial-curve correlated agreement to one-point AG codes up to half the designed distance without an extra genus penalty. With constant slack the soundness is O(ell(ell+1)/(epsilon q)) independently of block length. A distinct mutual-agreement theorem reaches a Johnson-type radius with length-dependent soundness, and tower counterexamples limit stronger extrapolations.
review.prior_frontier: Reed-Solomon proximity-gap theory is constrained by length at most the field size. Good AG towers permit unbounded length over a fixed field; the paper gives the half-distance soundness needed for that advantage while documenting obstacles above half distance.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate. Its principal half-distance proof passes a targeted check; the independent positive and negative branches remain unverified.

papers.title: List Size of Random Linear Codes: Optimality and the Limits of Average-Radius List Decoding
papers.authors: Chen Yuan, Ruiqi Zhu

review.title: List Size of Random Linear Codes: Optimality and the Limits of Average-Radius List Decoding
review.authors: Chen Yuan, Ruiqi Zhu
review.area: Coding theory; random linear list decoding
review.summary: For fixed prime power q and radius p<1−1/q, random linear codes at rate 1−h_q(p)−ε have list size h_q(p)/ε+O_p,q(1). Average-radius list decoding behaves differently: its necessary leading constant is at least p(1+h_q′(p)), exceeding h_q(p) when q^p(1−p)>1; stronger constructions make it grow as (log λ/(eλ)+o_q(1))q/log q for p=1−λ/q. Limits are fixed p,q then ε→0 and n large.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves the cited GLM+22 leading-constant conjecture for ordinary list decoding and refutes its average-radius version. Independent concurrent ordinary-list result of Silas is acknowledged; prior bounds/citations not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Determines a sharp list-size constant and separates two central coding notions previously conjectured to agree.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines affine bad-list counting with entropy-rich constructions that reveal an alphabet-dependent average-radius obstruction.
score_reasons.depth: The hard components are multiple ball-intersection constraints and uniform entropy estimates over every linear projection.
score_reasons.exposition: Order of limits, independent work, and differing upper/lower models are clearly specified.

checked: Traced Lemma 3.4 increasing-support chain induction by choosing a largest coordinate fiber and adding a point outside it.
Independently checked p(1+h_q′(p))−h_q(p)=p+log_q(1−p), including positivity for sufficiently small p when q≥3.
Checked the affine-dimension union-bound roadmap conditional on the sharper |N(A)| counting estimate and the random-code subspace probability.
remaining: Audit Lemma 3.5 change of variables, ball intersections and the constant additive term in the upper bound.
Audit all linear-projection entropy bounds and the random-code containment theorem used for the lower bound.
Check the multi-shift optimization producing q/log q and cited baseline/concurrent results.

papers.title: How Much Can Approximate Equilibria Change the Social Cost of Selfish Routing?
papers.authors: Yu Cheng, Tianle Jiang

review.title: How Much Can Approximate Equilibria Change the Social Cost of Selfish Routing?
review.authors: Yu Cheng, Tianle Jiang
review.summary: For degree-d polynomial latencies with nonnegative coefficients, exact bounds compare every multiplicative epsilon-equilibrium to an exact equilibrium: both relative increase and decrease are sqrt(d epsilon)+O_d(epsilon) in general games; on single-commodity series-parallel depth-h networks the reduction is h epsilon+O(epsilon^2), while increase is epsilon.
review.prior_frontier: Classical approximate PoA compares against social optimum and does not approach one as epsilon vanishes; prior series-parallel 1+epsilon upper bound is reused. Historical tightness claims not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Quantifies stability of equilibrium social cost and isolates a genuine topology-dependent square-root versus linear distinction.
score_reasons.novelty: A common intermediate-cost parameter unifies lower bounds, while a latency-polynomial dual handles upper bounds.
score_reasons.depth: Sharp analytic optimization and matching multi-population/network constructions are needed beyond standard smoothness.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly separates exact-equilibrium comparison from PoA and defines depth as maximum path length.

checked: Traced variational inequalities and decomposition C(f)-C(fprime)=T-R, including R>=D>=0.
Checked polynomial scaling, Jensen with zero padding, and mu_d(T/C)<=D/C<=epsilon(1-T/C); derivative gives minimizer d/(d+1).
Checked small-epsilon expansion rho_d=sqrt(d epsilon)+O(epsilon) and the cyclic-resource construction attaining the lower-bound relation.
Inspected the upper-bound Lagrangian sign and reduction of monomial constraints to a game-independent program.
remaining: Full upper-bound dual solution and transitions between its three regimes, series-parallel induction, topology-specific tight examples and monotone-latency extension remain unaudited.

papers.title: The Complexity of Private Signaling in Nonatomic Routing Games
papers.authors: Yu Cheng, Tianle Jiang

review.title: The Complexity of Private Signaling in Nonatomic Routing Games
review.authors: Yu Cheng, Tianle Jiang
review.summary: For single-commodity Bayesian nonatomic routing with maximum simple-path length d and L-Lipschitz latency functions, computes a private recommendation scheme with social cost <=exact-IC OPT+epsilon and conditional deviation gain<=epsilon in time poly(states)*n^{O(d+d^3 L/epsilon)}. No bicriteria FPTAS exists even for parallel linear latencies with coefficients in[0,1]; removing either bounded d or bounded L precludes a bicriteria PTAS unless P=NP.
review.prior_frontier: Addresses the stated open computational problem for private signaling beyond constant-size parallel networks. Prior public-signaling hardness is a different benchmark. Prior sources not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Gives nearly matching approximation classifications for a natural private-information routing problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Preserves path marginals while controlling every arc in rounding, and pins dual multipliers with auxiliary states to turn hard separation into hard optimization.
score_reasons.depth: Conditional incentives require errors proportional to recommendation probability; hardness needs more than a separation-oracle observation.
score_reasons.exposition: Bicriteria additive scope, rational encoding and both bounded parameters are explicit.

checked: Traced cancellation of recommendation probability using marginal-preserving flow rounding and outcome-wise O(d^2 L/k) path-latency perturbations.

Read the dependent Beck–Fiala rounding: release rows with <=2d fractional paths, retain total mass, and use a nonzero nullspace direction because (2d+1)|W|<=d|F|; endpoints preserve marginals in expectation.
remaining: Audit the completed rounding deviation argument and all dual-pinning hardness constructions/gap tolerances.
Verify finite-dimensional strong-duality reduction and exact latency-input assumptions throughout.

review.title: The Complexity of Distributed Minimum Weight Cycle Approximation
review.authors: Yi-Jun Chang, Yanyu Chen, Dipan Dey, Yonggang Jiang, Gopinath Mishra, Hung Thuan Nguyen, Mingyang Yang

score_reasons.significance: A substantial characterization of a basic distributed graph problem across approximation regimes.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses shifted low-diameter decompositions as cycle-capture primitives, with a short/long-hop split to reduce congestion.
score_reasons.depth: Approximate-distance robustness and reconstruction of a potentially missed antipodal segment are technically meaningful.
score_reasons.exposition: The parameter ranges and conditional lower bounds are explicit, including the restricted sense in which upper and lower bounds match.

checked: Checked the truncated-shift union bound and why capture places a center within delta_max-d of the cycle.
Traced the non-tree-edge cycle approximation and Proposition 4.5's safe-capture inequality along visible segments; at most one segment can contain the antipodal obstruction.
remaining: Audit the approximate-SSSP implementation, missing-segment recovery, congestion accounting and optimized exponents.
Audit communication lower-bound gadgets and their girth assumptions; the upper bound is for undirected weighted graphs, whereas the lower bound also covers directed unweighted graphs.

review.summary: Establishes a continuous approximation/round tradeoff for undirected weighted minimum-weight cycle in CONGEST: (k+1)-approximation in O-tilde(n^((k+1)/(2k+1))+n^(1/k)+D). Conditional girth-based lower bounds nearly match at integer k; parallel and broadcast-congested-clique variants follow.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier CONGEST algorithms gave about 2-approximation in n^(2/3)+D rounds, with weaker square-root lower bounds for larger ratios. This paper improves rounds when accepting a larger ratio, rather than improving the 2-approximation guarantee. General lower bounds assume the Erdos girth conjecture.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate pending full algorithmic and lower-bound audit.

papers.title: A Counting and Sampling Lovász Local Lemma
papers.authors: Hongyang Liu, Chunyang Wang, Yitong Yin, Yiyao Zhang, Can Zhou

review.title: A Counting and Sampling Lovász Local Lemma
review.authors: Hongyang Liu, Chunyang Wang, Yitong Yin, Yiyao Zhang, Can Zhou
review.area: Approximate counting; exact sampling; Lovász local lemma
review.summary: For arbitrary finite-domain CSPs with evaluation access, explicit scopes, and 4e p(D+1)²≤1, gives deterministic approximate counting in (nD/ε)^O(kD log q), randomized counting in Õ(poly(k,D,q)(n/ε)²), and exactly uniform sampling in expected Õ(n+kmD²) time with O(m) oracle evaluations. Thus fixed-local-parameter counting/sampling reaches the pD² scale, not the weaker satisfiability pD scale.
review.prior_frontier: General-CSP prior algorithms are cited at roughly pD^5≲1, with subclass refinements; pD² hardness is claimed tight up to constants under NP≠RP. Those prior algorithms and the hardness reduction have not yet been independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A counting/sampling analogue of the LLL at the conjectured general-CSP exponent is a major general result.
score_reasons.novelty: Canonical two-tree regrouping of inclusion-exclusion exposes a distance-two expansion with the correct pD² scale.
score_reasons.depth: Requires correlation decay, efficient local evaluation, randomized counting and an exact sampling implementation with bit costs.
score_reasons.exposition: Oracle assumptions and expected-versus-worst-case runtime distinctions are explicit.

checked: Fully traced canonical Tree(D) construction and inversion: equal accepted/rejected histories characterize preimages as T plus arbitrary free constraints.
Traced the pointwise inclusion-exclusion regrouping and telescoping probability ratio in Lemma 3.5.
Checked the initial conditional-marginal bound r≤1.2p and the β^|T| term using disjoint scopes, LLL conditioning, and |R|≤D²|T|.

Completed the deterministic estimator audit: final rejected distance-two vertices separate T plus free^(1)(T) from all remaining free constraints, so the coefficient requires only O(kD|T|) variables. Checked telescoping product sensitivity, the beta/alpha decay constants, budget decrement by |T|, stability in [-2p,2p], and convolution error <=4(0.9)^L. The final constraint-product error and parameter-dependent exponent follow with L=O(log(m/epsilon)); it is not a uniform-exponent deterministic FPTAS.

Traced the randomized estimator and its reciprocal recursion through Lemmas 5.4–5.7. Selected scopes are disjoint even though rejected local experiments overlap; independent reciprocal factors cancel rejected (1-p_b) probabilities. The zero-terminated series is integrable by E|Y|<=sqrt(EY^2)<1, with second moment (1+r)/[(1-r)(1-M)]. Strict subfamily induction avoids circularity. The Cayley rooted-tree count and Lagrange-inversion identity at x=3pD^2 bound E R^2<=3p_root. Expected recursive offspring <1/8, followed by independent product-estimator variance and explicit cost truncation, gives the randomized counting bound.

Traced the exact sampler measure transport, not merely its scalar marginal identity. Pointwise inclusion-exclusion gives equal-mass parity terms; Route toggles a selectable violated constraint with no later violated vertex at distance <=2. Coupled canonical executions preserve the ordered violated transcript and the toggle set, giving a reversible parity exchange at identical point mass 1/Z. The exceptional singleton maps the violation measure to its odd root term.

Checked insertion/deletion renewal algebra for Algorithm 4. Insertion entered with mu_minus returns (1-r)mu_plus/2 and continues (1+r)mu_minus/2. For deletion, direct return is independent of X with probability (1-r)/2; the aggregate entering measure 2mu_minus/(1-r) solves the renewal equation starting from mu_plus. Strictly smaller recursive families and support preservation justify the transport, including saved proposal assignments independent of recursive removals.

Checked weighted proposal factor cancellation: local experiments violate with probability 2p_c/(1+p_c); two recursive parity proposals give (1-r) times the final-check pass probability. Per-tree reciprocal acceptance factors cancel local and rejected factors exactly, preserving the conditional E_T assignment law. Bounds p(D+1)^2<=1/(4e), H<9/8, and the rooted-tree moments give <0.97 direct proposal offspring; update recursive offspring <1/4. Grouping calls by family/sign preserves proportional input laws, which is needed for expected near-linear cost.

Independently traced ReciprocalTest: Coin has u=2(1-B)/(2-B); contracted -1/+2 walk has theta=u^2/(1-u+u^2)<9/40. Its Galton–Watson PGF G=1-theta+theta*z*G^3 and survival 1/(2N) give acceptance 1/(2B). Re-derived expected O-call expression using pre-change survival 1/j; the harmonic integral bounds M<74/25 and yields at most 3/B calls. No unsupported numerical simulation is used as proof.

Checked the Appendix A parameter substitution p=A^-2, D<=2 floor(eA), and monotone-clause self-reduction from approximate sampling to counting; the imported BGG+19 hardness theorem itself is retained as an external dependency.
remaining: External LLL conditional-probability theorem, connected-set enumeration implementation, and BGG+19 hardness theorem were used through their stated interfaces rather than independently re-proved. No executable sampler or mechanized proof was built; detailed machine-level implementation is not audited.

review.authors: Yin Liu

score_reasons.significance: Completes a natural strict counting model beyond real/rational restrictions.
score_reasons.novelty: The contribution is preserving the cubic bipartite interface through interpolation, absorption and exceptional group-orbit cases, rather than inventing matrix-group methods themselves.

checked: Checked the exact real intersection of the complex tractable families.

Confirmed why arbitrary grouping is legal here without planarity, and why three exceptional projective directions obstruct naive complex absorption.
remaining: Audit the full finite/infinite projective-order exhaustion, singular boundaries, and legal gadget substitutions.
Obtain and run the supplied rational certificate verifier, and verify imported binary hardness interfaces. The checked absorption lemma alone does not certify the dichotomy.

review.summary: Classifies exact Holant(f|=3) for complex algebraic symmetric Boolean ternary f on strictly cubic bipartite multigraphs with no freely supplied auxiliary signatures. Checked geometric-scale arithmetic ε/(2a_j)=16δ_j n and the final strictly positive separation for r≤n,δ_j≤1/4.

review.title: Settling the Sample Complexity of Rényi Entropy Estimation
review.authors: Qisheng Wang
review.summary: Determines, for fixed noninteger alpha>0, sufficiently large alphabet d and sufficiently small error epsilon, Renyi-entropy sample complexity Theta(d^max(1/alpha,1)/(epsilon^(1/alpha) log d)+d^abs(1-1/alpha)/epsilon^2). Constants depend on alpha and are not uniform near integer orders.
review.prior_frontier: The introduction compares earlier almost-matching alphabet-exponent lower bounds and upper bounds with restricted error dependence. The claimed simultaneous sharp epsilon and logarithmic dependence is new; older papers not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a basic distribution-estimation complexity across all fixed noninteger entropy orders.
score_reasons.novelty: A moment-matching construction with controlled low moments and large alpha-moment ratio supplies the missing sharp lower bound.
score_reasons.depth: Combines signed interpolation weights, Poissonized indistinguishability and bias-corrected Taylor/polynomial estimators.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise fixed-alpha and large-d qualifications are available in the formal results; the exposition separates the two lower-bound mechanisms.

checked: Checked the signed Lagrange-weight identity annihilating low-degree moments and the geometric-node exponent separating the two alpha moments.
Inspected controlled first, second, alpha and twice-alpha moments in Lemma 3.1.
Checked the aggregation from per-coordinate variance to relative mean-square error and the resulting two sample-complexity terms.

Completed the signed-interpolation construction: alternating Lagrange weights annihilate moments through K+r−1; the geometric-node exponent isolates the alpha moment while first, second and twice-alpha moments remain bounded. Checked r=ceil(2alpha)+3, the fractional-distance choice of eta, factorial tail estimates and normalization bounds.

Traced the normalized hard priors, including the residual mass split over s coordinates, the fallback event, the exact entropy-center separation, Chebyshev concentration, and the comparison of the dependent Poisson experiment with independent coordinate mixtures via conditional KL. The alpha>1 dominance regime implies the concentration requirement; outside it the second lower-bound term suffices.

Checked moment-matching Poisson indistinguishability with K=ceil(4 log(ed)) and n=O(1/(tK)); the residual-coordinate error is O(sqrt(n m t²)), within the stated constants. This yields the first sample term for fixed noninteger alpha.

Completed all estimator regimes in Lemma4.2: falling-factorial unbiased polynomial estimates, truncation tails, large-probability Taylor bias, exact Poisson-polynomial variance identity, and misclassification tails. Summed the independent coordinate errors and checked the Renyi power-sum inequalities, clipping and logarithm conversion giving both upper-bound terms.

Independently checked the parametric lower bound with a rare mass a and perturbation t=Theta(a epsilon): entropy separation is Theta(t/a) and squared Hellinger distance Theta(t²/a). For alpha<1 spread rare mass over d−1 coordinates with a=(d−1)^{−(1−alpha)/alpha}; for alpha>1 put mass a=(d−1)^{−(alpha−1)/alpha} on a single coordinate. This yields d^{abs(1−1/alpha)}/epsilon². The alpha<1 construction is also explicitly given in #451 AppendixA.
remaining: Established polynomial-approximation and moment-matching Poisson-TV lemmas are imported; their hypotheses and use were checked, not their original proofs. Standard constant-factor Poissonization/de-Poissonization is used.

The checked theorem is for each fixed noninteger alpha>0, sufficiently large d and sufficiently small epsilon; constants are not uniform as alpha approaches an integer. Integer-order and quantum-copy extensions are not claimed by this audit.

review.summary: In comparison search on n ordered elements, knowing the first n^{1-delta} exact moments can still leave an Omega(log n) worst-case approximation ratio to distribution-aware optimal search, for every fixed delta>0. papers.authors: yang zhou, Mingsheng Wang

review.title: Almost-Linear Modular Composition over Arbitrary Commutative Rings
review.authors: Yang Zhou, Mingsheng Wang
review.summary: Claims a deterministic division-free algorithm computing g(a) mod monic f of degree n over every commutative ring with identity in n·2^O(√log n) ring operations, including preprocessing. General arbitrary monic moduli and arbitrary inputs are covered; finite-field bit complexity and special modulus X^n were already almost linear.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript compares against expected O(n^1.43) arbitrary-field algebraic complexity and faster generic-input bounds, distinguishing existing bit-model and X^n results. Exact prior exponents and application reductions remain to be checked.

score_reasons.significance: Almost-linear general-modulus composition would resolve a major basic algebraic algorithm bottleneck.
score_reasons.novelty: Deformed product bases plus transposed previously prepared basis changes avoid constructing a dense power matrix or hiding preprocessing.
score_reasons.depth: The argument combines multi-index convolution, noncircular two-pass preparation, nilpotent deformation and precision-recursive linear solving.
score_reasons.exposition: Short modular lemmas expose the preprocessing cost and division-free ring model clearly.

checked: Traced digit encoding, monic padding, and extraction of the t^(L−1) coefficient; all deformation bases equal the monomial basis modulo t.
Traced the coefficient-extraction pairing: the reversed Hankel matrix is unit triangular Toeplitz, hence invertible over rings with zero divisors as well.
Checked the selected-coefficient Kronecker substitution: both γ and α+η stay in the encoded box, preventing aliasing at the queried positions.

Traced Hensel residual recursion and its total precision per level; checked the block preparation formula M(α+β)=(E_v^T H e_β)_α and the order of transposed maps, which only invokes previously prepared changes.
Checked the total Õ(NL4^m) bound and balanced m≈√log N substitution, conditional on the arithmetic/transposition primitives.

Traced the complete division-free modular-composition construction on PDF pages 2–9 and Appendix A. Padding a monic modulus to power-of-two degree preserves the required reduction; the balanced mixed-radix substitution and extraction of coefficient t^(L−1) recover precisely g(a) modulo the padded polynomial.

Checked every basis transition: halving digit j replaces its high half by the next power-of-X block; both bases reduce to the standard monomial basis modulo t. The Gram matrix is consequently invertible modulo every t precision even over rings with zero divisors.

Checked the coefficient-of-X^(N−1) pairing. Its Hankel matrix becomes unit triangular Toeplitz after column reversal, so its inverse uses only unit constant-term power-series inversion. Moment arrays have 3·2^m N entries. The mixed convolution queries remain within the encoded box, so larger intermediate exponents cannot alias a queried coefficient.

Checked Hensel solving at precisions floor(q/2) and ceil(q/2): division by a power of t is coefficient shifting, and total precision per recursion level is q. This gives the claimed near-linear precision cost without division by nonunits. Reversal of t coefficients correctly turns the transposed R-linear map into the adjoint over R[t]/t^q.

Checked the preparation order: E_v=T_2 T_4 ... T_v uses only earlier transition tables; each enlarged moment block is E_v^T H times one explicitly computed basis element. Thus table construction is not circular. The 3·2^m blocks, 2^m convolution factor and O(log N) transitions yield soft-O(4^m N L), with L≤m·2^ceil(log2(N)/m). Setting m=ceil(sqrt(log2 N)) gives n·2^O(sqrt(log n)).

Checked the imported arithmetic interface against Cantor–Kaltofen, Acta Informatica 28 (1991), pp. 693–694: their primary paper explicitly supplies a division-free bilinear straight-line algorithm over arbitrary algebras, using integer linear maps and coprime-scaling Bezout recombination. This supports the manuscript’s fixed-input multiplication transposition. Unit-series Newton inversion and reversed monic division also require no forbidden division, including characteristic two.
remaining: Arithmetic operation bounds are checked; no implementation or bit-complexity claim was verified. Cantor–Kaltofen multiplication is an explicitly verified external theorem interface, not re-proved here.

review.title: The Information-Theoretic Limits of Hiding Among Decoys in the Shuffle Model
review.authors: Pengcheng Su, Haibo Cheng, Ping Wang
review.summary: For a fixed d-symbol alphabet, releasing one genuine message plus n-1 uniformly shuffled decoys has optimal prior-independent worst-case mutual information Theta_d(1/n) for iid or heterogeneous independent decoys, Theta_d(1/n^2) for correlated message-oblivious decoys, and exactly max{log(d/n),0} for message-dependent decoys. review.area: Circuit complexity; approximate counting; space-bounded randomness
review.summary: Logspace-uniform positive semi-unbounded arithmetic circuits of depth K admit a downward multiplicative (1−2^−t) floating-point approximation in Boolean depth O(K+(log n/log log n)log(2+t/K)). Repeated variables/tautologies are allowed. The theorem is asymptotic beyond a parameter-dependent n threshold and does not cover arbitrary exponentially small epsilon or small k.

score_reasons.significance: Replaces a parameter-dependent exponent by near-quadratic n dependence at an important high-density random-SAT scale.

score_reasons.depth: Requires an executable recursive rejection-repair sampler, marginal coins and a nontrivial interacting-core variance/exploration argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Formal theorem states the large k cutoff, occurrence model and accuracy range;74 pages of coupled subroutines require extensive checking.

remaining: Audit the simultaneous random-formula root estimates, acceptance-probability bounds, recursive Bernoulli factories and global restart errors.
Verify polymer convergence, core spectral-gap proof and the final bit-complexity/error budget yielding the near-quadratic exponent.

review.title: Optimal and Verifiable Quantum Advantages in Communication Complexity
review.authors: Ryan Anselm, Michelle Ding, Dar Gilboa, Sabee Grewal

score_reasons.significance: Optimal separations for total search, with a distinct efficiently verifiable branch, are major complexity results.
score_reasons.novelty: The bulk-Fourier-mass condition preserves totality while supporting an optimal classical lower bound; hierarchy-restricted separations sharpen the role of magic.
score_reasons.depth: Uses entropy/coupling arguments, spectral-mass stability and structured communication lower bounds across several regimes.
score_reasons.exposition: The resource comparison table explicitly separates communication, gates, totality, verification and classical interaction, preventing several easy overclaims.

checked: Checked totality and the 3/4 quantum success guarantee from excluding at most 1/8 Fourier mass at each spectral extreme.
Traced the sequential maximal coupling/entropy-deficiency bound and the unbiased sampled-inner-product variance calculation.
Checked the uniform pairwise Gaussian-limit argument for Fourier mass concentration and the Parseval coupling step controlling unstable coefficients.
remaining: Audit the complete rectangle/two-way classical lower bound and quantitative window probabilities.
Audit the affine verifiable variant and all Clifford-hierarchy separations, including their access/gate assumptions. The targeted coupling checks do not certify those branches.

review.summary: Gives an optimal n-qubit one-way versus Omega(2^n)-bit randomized two-way separation for a total search relation, Pelagic Fourier Fishing. An efficiently verifiable variant retains the exponential gap against classical one-way protocols. Clifford-hierarchy restricted variants give optimal n versus Omega_d(n^d) gaps, including a quadratic stabilizer-only separation.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier total-relation separations and Fourier-fishing query lower bounds fell short of the optimal exponential communication or linear truth-table query scale. The strongest two-way lower bound and efficient verification belong to different variants; arbitrary phase-state preparation can require exponentially many gates.
review.recommendation: High-priority candidate for a targeted large-proof audit; distinguish the different communication and verification guarantees in any shortlist.

Verify FIXP membership, source generalized-circuit completeness and full distance-approximation reduction.

Paging reduction prediction availability, inherited cache-trajectory bound and extension to general delay functions.

remaining: Verify exact hypotheses of external directed sparse regularity and one-sided inheritance results and the quoted approximate-king lower bound.
Complete small-n and epsilon bookkeeping, including the two-tournament corollary.

review.title: Fine-Grained Complexity Across the Computational Phase Transition
review.authors: Zhe Ju, Jingcheng Liu, Yitong Yin

score_reasons.significance: Quantifies a major algorithmic phase transition and relates its exponent to general computational hardness.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines marginal-response control, integrated spectral stability and near-critical phase gadgets with a robust parameter-sequence reduction.
score_reasons.depth: The 119-page analysis spans critical tree recursions, covariance, annealing, gadget fluctuations and fine-grained reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: The distinction between degree-uniform upper bounds, fixed-degree lower bounds and SAT implications is carefully stated; the extensive dependencies require substantial review.

checked: Traced the integrated spectral-stability calculation: clipping the subcritical divergence at sqrt(n/d) gives the logarithmic critical term, and integrating the supercritical linear response yields n delta^2/d.
Checked the response-to-covariance proof's small-support exponential-moment bound, signed-sum symmetrization, and sorted-coordinate decomposition/Cauchy-Schwarz extension to arbitrary real vectors.
remaining: Audit the decisive hard-core marginal-response estimate and the imported spectral-stability-to-mixing theorem.
Audit annealing variance/runtime, phase-gadget moment asymptotics, mixing bottlenecks and the uniformity/size parameters of the SAT reduction.

review.summary: Claims a near-critical hard-core mixing transition governed by exp(Theta(n delta^2/d)) times polynomial factors, with degree-uniform upper bounds and fixed-degree lower bounds. A robust SAT reduction transfers fixed power savings along specified inverse-polynomial distances above uniqueness; it is a conditional speedup implication, not an unconditional lower bound for all algorithms.
review.prior_frontier: Known uniqueness thresholds separated polynomial tractability from hardness at fixed distance, but did not resolve the vanishing-distance exponential scale. The paper also improves critical Glauber mixing through O(sqrt(n/d)) spectral independence and tailored annealing.
review.recommendation: Exceptional candidate if its long near-critical and gadget analyses survive a targeted large-proof audit; not yet correctness-cleared.

review.title: Finding and Certifying Weighted Minimum Cuts with Cut Queries
review.authors: Troy Lee
review.summary: For undirected graphs with arbitrary nonnegative real weights, gives O(n log²n) cut-query certificates of exact global mincut and a deterministic O(n^(3/2)log³n(loglog n)²) query algorithm, also capable of reporting all mincut shores. Counts oracle calls only; exact arithmetic and offline computation are unrestricted. Certificates permit competing graphs with new positive edges on the same vertex set.
review.prior_frontier: Prior deterministic subquadratic query algorithms handled simple unweighted graphs, while weighted inputs had the trivial quadratic upper bound. The certificate bound also limits approximate-cut-dimension lower-bound methods. Prior results and attribution remain unaudited.

score_reasons.significance: Breaks quadratic deterministic queries for arbitrary weighted mincut and establishes near-linear certificates.
score_reasons.novelty: Tree-encoded saturated flows certify max-flow values with O(n) queries; a weak skeleton replaces full deterministic sparsification.
score_reasons.depth: Combines dual flow structure, terminal halving, tree packing and weighted two-respecting-cut search.
score_reasons.exposition: The nondeterministic certificate versus algorithm distinction and unrestricted offline computation are carefully stated.

checked: Traced the O(n)-flow certificate mechanism conditional on min-cost-flow duality: distinct-power costs rule out zero-cost cycles, component potential shifts extend the tight forest, and singleton/tree-pair/outgoing-set queries recover capacities and divergences.
Checked consistent graphs may introduce edges because every non-tree pair already has a prescribed saturation direction.
Traced Lemma 16’s induction on a partition, using minimum crossing length, nonnegative residual lengths and crossing weight at least kλ/2.
remaining: Audit full flow-dual construction, isolating-cut certificates and terminal-halving theorem.
Audit weak-skeleton construction and total weighted deterministic query bound, including zero-mincut inputs.
Verify tree-family coverage and two-respecting-cut oracle adaptation. The advertised Lean library has not been built or checked.

review.authors: Maxime Flin, Mohsen Ghaffari, Magnús M. Halldórsson, Yannic Maus, Alexandre Nolin
review.summary: Solves the variable LLL in randomized poly(log log n) LOCAL rounds with arbitrary inverse-polynomial failure probability under p*d^1000<1. Nodes know polynomial size, degree and probability upper bounds; message size and local computation are unrestricted.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the stated general O-tilde(log n) round bound under polynomial slack to within a polynomial of the Omega(log log n) lower bound. Earlier fast results applied to constant degree or exponential slack; cited corrected shattering and decomposition primitives remain to be independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Closes an exponential gap in a central distributed primitive with broad consequences for locally checkable problems.
score_reasons.novelty: A dangerous-event helper LLL quadratically amplifies the probability exponent while expanding dependency radius only by a constant.
score_reasons.depth: The short argument couples conditional retraction, bounded local independence, ruling sets and exponential-criterion repair.
score_reasons.exposition: The main proof is compact and explicit about constants, conditional success and the unrestricted LOCAL model.

checked: Traced all new amplification steps: dangerous-event probability d^(-19lambda/32), helper degree d^23, and exponent lambda^2/700.
Checked erased-variable locality, preservation of unviolated untouched events, repair degree at most floor(lambda/16) and its exponential criterion.
Checked recursion depth O(log log log n), radius cost 23^L and conditional failure union bound.
Read the appended ruling-set refinement and exponential-criterion reduction; bounded-degree MIS and shattering are external dependencies.

Audit revisited all new amplification and repair steps, including fixed-set retracted marginals, joint independence, lambda²/700 arithmetic, repair dependency distance11, arbitrary-successful-helper conditioning, and the 23^L round recurrence.

Checked the primary corrected shattering paper arXiv:2606.27847: Corollary1, constant-degree LLL Theorem1, and repaired MIS Theorem7 have the needed forms. Independently reconstructed the relevant one-shot shattering bound by growing a separated set connected at distance4 inside a large affected component; its membership events depend on disjoint variable sets, permitting the tree-count union bound.
