papers.authors: Emmanuela Orsini, Arpita Patra

review.title: From Degree Three to Degree Two: Statistical Randomized Encodings for All Functions
review.authors: Emmanuela Orsini, Arpita Patra
review.summary: Every Boolean function has statistical randomized encodings of degree two jointly in original input and independent uniform random bits, with correctness and privacy errors <=2^-lambda and complexity polynomial in mod-2 branching-program size plus lambda. Locality-three decomposable encodings and locality-three OWFs from uniform-NC1 OWFs follow. Multiparty effective-degree-two encodings protect every static semi-honest coalition, allowing arbitrary local preprocessing. This permits negligible correctness error; it is not a perfectly correct statistical encoding nor unconditional polynomial overhead in circuit size.
review.prior_frontier: Prior general perfect encodings degree three/locality four; quadratic multiparty constructions for >=4 parties protected at most floor(2k/3) corruptions. Sources and downstream reductions not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the degree-two and locality-three statistical-encoding questions with multiple cryptographic consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Pairs two different recursive linear secret-sharing access structures so exposed rank-encoding shares lose reconstructibility doubly exponentially in depth.
score_reasons.depth: Coupled reconstruction probabilities, parity conditioning and degree-preserving composition give a substantial algebraic/privacy mechanism.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly distinguishes statistical correctness from perfect correctness and branching-program efficiency from circuit efficiency; discusses why naive OWF transfer fails.

checked: Checked det[[1,0,c],[a,1,0],[0,b,d]]=abc+d and rank at least two; multiplication by uniform h-by-3 matrix is quadratic, with rank-test error <=7*2^-h and rank-two leakage only through c and ac.
Traced the sharing product identity sum_i a_i c_i=ac and independent additive sharing that makes leaf outcomes uniform conditional on their parity.

Read linear-image/coset privacy dichotomy and reconstruction access composition. Checked recurrences p_next=2p^2-p^4, q_next(0)=((beta(q0)+beta(q1))/2)^2, q_next(1)=(q0+q1-q0*q1)^2, and privacy hybrids costing <=2p+2max(q0,q1).
The degree-three composition masks individual monomials with zero-sum masks; per-copy error set at lambda+ceil(log M) makes total <=2^-lambda.
remaining: Large-proof exception (54 pages). The determinant gadget, sharing algebra and amplification/privacy recurrences were checked. The remaining recursive simulation and external degree-reduction chain are substantial; this is not full clearance of statistical encoding for all functions or of its one-way-function corollary.
Independently evaluate depth-four numerical seeds and all parameter/complexity constants; read complete formal hybrid proof.
Trace essential perfect degree-three/locality reductions and the distributional-to-ordinary OWF reduction; ordinary one-wayness does not follow directly from an encoding with correctness errors.
Audit multiparty, client-server and circuit-efficient variants, including coalition simulators and computational assumptions.

review.title: Short Non-Interactive Proofs for Time-Space Computations
review.authors: Ryan Williams, Zoe Xi

score_reasons.significance: A broadly applicable faster noninteractive verification theorem with significant complexity consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Integer quadratic constraints and sparse subset-sum tensor encodings combine to reduce both message and verifier costs.
score_reasons.depth: The soundness proof must recover integral witnesses from nearby tensor codewords while preserving fine-grained prover/verifier bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The full theorem exposes input length, space, randomness and prover costs; the central trace argument is presented in detail.

checked: Checked the integer NAND and unit-vector constraint logic in the inspected encoding passage.
Traced the trace theorem conditional on the tensor-code lemmas: nearby integral source recovery, nonzero trace discrepancy, bad-anchor counting, and the final non-codeword line-test case.
Checked the message-count decomposition by support sizes and the stated rectangular-product substitutions in the verifier runtime.
remaining: Audit the subset-sum code construction, tensor testing/integral recovery lemmas, and all chunk/input-lookup constraints.
Verify bit-size safeguards, randomness-efficient amplification, rectangular multiplication imports, honest-prover construction and the lower-bound applications.

review.summary: Constructs noninteractive Merlin-Arthur proofs for time-T, subpolynomial-space computations with T^(3/4+o(1)) message length and verification time. Honest-prover time is T^(1/2+omega/4+o(1)), becoming near-linear only if omega=2. Applications include unrestricted-depth circuit counting, QBF verification and MA time-space lower bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Prior specialized QBF verification had exponent 4/5 and known stronger circuit-counting protocols imposed depth restrictions. This provides a general small-space simulation; the theorem's input-size factors matter when T is not superpolynomial.
review.recommendation: High-priority candidate for full central-proof verification; the trace structure is promising but its coding and arithmetic prerequisites remain essential.

papers.authors: Mark Bun, Mandar Juvekar

review.title: UPPcc is Not Closed Under Intersection
review.authors: Mark Bun, Mandar Juvekar
review.summary: Constructs explicit bounded-integer-halfspace matrices with sign rank Θ(d) whose disjoint-input two-fold conjunction has sign rank 2^Θ(d), with 2^Θ(d²) rows/columns. Consequently O(log n) unbounded-error communication can rise to Ω(√n), proving UPP^cc is not intersection-closed. This does not contradict intersection closure of PP or PP^cc.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier cited examples only raised O(log n) to Θ(log²n), remaining inside UPP^cc. Resolves a longstanding closure question; external historical and sign-rank characterization references not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a basic longstanding closure question for unbounded-error communication complexity.
score_reasons.novelty: Continuous spherical symmetrization and robust average-margin bounds convert approximate orthant sign-representation obstructions into explicit finite sign-rank lower bounds.
score_reasons.depth: Gegenbauer derivative estimates, robust polynomial coefficient control and boundary-sensitive discretization are substantial interacting components.
score_reasons.exposition: The technical overview clearly explains why exact continuous sign arguments alone fail under discretization.

checked: Verified ordinary halfspace sign-rank upper bound d+1 and n=Θ(d²) parameter conversion.
Checked the lowest homogeneous term parity obstruction to exact orthant sign representation.
Traced the conditional robust-margin roadmap: rescale at ρ=2^−KD, control low-degree coefficients, then approximate at half degree.
Checked the Legendre-basis coefficient argument through orthogonality and |λ′_θ|≤3^|θ|∫|p|, conditional on the stated classical Legendre facts.
remaining: The 47-page sign-rank separation has checks of its exact parity obstruction and coefficient-control mechanism. Smoothing, rational approximation and finite discretization remain substantial unchecked parts; this is a large-proof exception.
Audit spherical smoothing/derivative theorem and constants.
Audit the approximate-sign polynomial coefficient lemma and its rational-approximation dependencies.
Trace finite integer discretization, boundary mass, Forster/generalized-margin theorem and exact explicitness.

Catalytic space is polynomial and must be restored; ordinary workspace is logarithmic.

score_reasons.novelty: Uses algebraic rank-improvement certificates and a Pfaffian threshold-or-matching dichotomy to free recoverable catalytic bits.

checked: Checked the threshold-or-matching proof: if no edge splits the first nonzero Pfaffian coefficient, coefficient sums at each vertex force degree exactly one in the extracted edge set.
Traced deletion/recovery of a threshold weight from all other weights, and accumulation of free catalytic space before falling back to an ordinary algorithm.
Checked that restoring the deleted weight uses a polynomial independent of that weight.
remaining: Maximum-rank assignment construction and restoration in Section 3.1.
Catalytic rank/Pfaffian/interpolation implementations and field/bit-length assumptions.
Mixed-matrix and matrix-space approximation results.

papers.authors: Tomer Ezra, Tamar Garbuz

review.title: Fair Share Allocations for Almost All Agents
review.authors: Tomer Ezra, Tamar Garbuz
review.summary: Additive nonnegative valuations admit 1-out-of-(n+O(sqrt(n log n))) MMS allocations. More generally exact AnyPrice Share is attainable when total entitlement <=1-epsilon and each entitlement <=epsilon^2/(2048 log(8/epsilon)). With total entitlement one and cap epsilon^3/(262144 log(16/epsilon)), ex-ante proportionality coexists either with each agent obtaining full APS with probability >=1-epsilon or with every outcome giving APS at entitlement (1-epsilon)b_i. The former probability is individual, not simultaneous; a necessary entitlement cap is O(epsilon), leaving a gap.
review.prior_frontier: Prior general ordinal MMS denominator 4 ceil(n/3), and full MMS for a prescribed constant fraction of agents; manuscript cites 7/9 multiplicative MMS separately. Prior claims not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Replaces linear extra MMS bundles with sublinear slack and serves almost all agents at their full benchmark.
score_reasons.novelty: Configuration LP with entitlement-threshold rank bounds isolates a small-total-entitlement fractional set, served by a reserve.
score_reasons.depth: Combines bucket cutoffs, fractional extreme-point rank, tail rounding and marginal-preserving joint sampling.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear distinction between ex-ante and ex-post guarantees and individual versus joint success; several technical bucket constructions require careful tracing.

checked: Traced the configuration-LP feasible solution from APS certificates conditioned on avoiding the first q items; inflation <=1/(1-qc) is absorbed by entitlement slack.

Read fractional-agent threshold argument: all late tail constraints have a common row direction, so at most h(z)<=2+2q log(1/z) agents of entitlement >=z can remain fractional at a vertex. Integration bounds their total entitlement by 1/(2q).
Verified reserve assignment: sorted every-qth goods retain >=1/q total value, fractional share 2q*b_i gives value >=2, and singleton-capped faithful rounding loses <=1.

Read complete joint-sampling Lemma 4.1: k fractional variables give <=k/2 agent equalities and <k/2 heavy-coordinate constraints; endpoint martingale splitting preserves marginals, while a released coordinate has absolute contribution <=2xi.
remaining: Audit APS certificate/ordering reduction, bucket cutoffs and exact tail-realization Lemma 2.1.
Trace ex-ante proportional allocation construction, the asymptotic substitutions, polynomial implementation qualifications and lower-bound examples.

review.authors: Ethan X. Fang, Shengtao Guo, Junwei Lu, Yuan Yao

score_reasons.significance: The first unconditional exponential-base improvement for arbitrary-cost bipartite TSP is a substantial exact-algorithm result.
score_reasons.novelty: The optimal-tour assignment lemma combines a Brouwer fixed point with Hamiltonian-cycle parity, enabling an unusual geometric state enumeration.
score_reasons.depth: The proof is short but uses delicate assignment-neighbor structure and counting to preserve an optimal tour in a restricted dynamic program.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper cleanly separates structural lemmas, enumeration, dynamic programming and symbolic perturbations; optional geometric background is marked.

checked: Traced the fixed-point price argument: a positive residual creates a cubic-on-one-side bipartite supergraph with a cheaper second Hamiltonian cycle, contradicting optimality.
Checked the compatible-set coverage exchange, generating-function count and negative derivative at alpha>3/7; at alpha=1/2 the minimizing z=sqrt(2) gives sqrt(1+2sqrt(2)).
Checked block-by-block admission of an optimal tour in the restricted Held-Karp recurrence and lexicographic perturbation preserving arbitrary original costs and absent edges.
remaining: Verify the imported neighboring-assignment spanning-tree theorem and the exact Thomason parity interface.
Audit the definition of compatibility/coloring forests and all enumeration boundary cases; an independent small-instance implementation would be useful before acceptance.

review.area: Exact graph algorithms and combinatorial optimization
review.summary: Gives deterministic minimum-cost Hamiltonian cycle below base 2 for graphs with an independent set of size alpha n, alpha>3/7. For bipartite graphs the bound is O-star(1.956636^n), with arbitrary real costs accessed through additions/comparisons. It does not give this improvement for unrestricted weighted TSP.
review.prior_frontier: The classical Held-Karp O-star(2^n) bound remained the unconditional baseline for arbitrary-cost bipartite TSP. The paper restricts dynamic-programming states using canonical minimum-cost assignments induced by a product-of-simplices triangulation.
review.recommendation: High-priority candidate for full verification; most new arguments have been traced, with the structural import and finite-instance validation still pending.

review.title: Quantum Lazy Sampling and Path Recording for Any Group
review.authors: Ben Foxman, Alex Lombardi, Fermi Ma, Barak Nehoran, John Wright
review.summary: Develops exact path-recording simulation for Haar-random elements of any compact group represented in U(N), with O(t log N) recording qubits after t queries. Efficient updates require efficient compatible representation-theoretic transforms; the general formula alone is not an efficient algorithm. Applies the framework to permutation-times-Clifford pseudorandom unitaries.
review.prior_frontier: Generalizes ad hoc random-function/unitary/permutation recorders and removes approximation error in the mathematical simulator. Tableau recording already existed in Grinko-Yoshida; the paper explicitly acknowledges concurrent path-recording development there. The new commutant update and PC application are distinct contributions.

score_reasons.significance: A broadly reusable exact framework for analyzing random quantum oracles with a simpler cryptographic construction as a substantial application.
score_reasons.novelty: Expresses path updates through commutant symmetrization and representation-dependent reweighting.
score_reasons.depth: Requires a careful equivalence among group-function, tableau and path Hilbert spaces, followed by partition-algebra pseudorandomness analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper states reachability and efficiency qualifications explicitly, but its 122 pages make a complete audit substantial.

checked: Inspected the legal-path projector and inverse reweighting restriction.
Traced the main intertwining argument: appending matrix coefficients in the group-function representation, transporting through the partial isometry and inducting over adaptive queries.
Checked that the paper makes no unconditional efficient-update claim for arbitrary compact groups.
remaining: Large-proof exception:122-page representation-theoretic oracle framework. The central adaptive intertwining induction was traced, conditional on the stated Schur normalization and legal-path identities; those identities, all oracle variants and cryptographic applications remain unchecked.
Derivation of the Schur normalization identity and all commutant formulas.
Mixed forward/inverse/conjugate query implementations and efficient Clebsch-Gordan dependencies.
The complete PC pseudorandom-unitary proof and quantitative security parameters.

review.title: Approximate Covering and Packing in Polymatroids
review.authors: Kristóf Bérczi, Karthekeyan Chandrasekaran, Chandra Chekuri, Siyue Liu, R. Ravi
review.summary: For integer monotone normalized submodular f with singleton values <=d, independent sets mean f(I)=sum_{e in I}f(e), not arbitrary integer points of a polymatroid polytope. A cover with (2d-1)chi_circle(f)-(2d-2) sets is constructible in exponential time; a value-oracle polynomial algorithm uses (4d-2)chi_circle(f). Polynomially packs floor(kappa_circle(f)/d) disjoint generators, where generator B satisfies f(B)=f(E). The intersection of d loopless matroids is a special case.
review.prior_frontier: Prior matroid-intersection covering bound 2d-1 was nonconstructive, and a recent polynomial factor d(d-1) was known; general polymatroid generator packing had O(log f(E)) rather than solely d dependence. O(d) packing leaves the proposed O(log d) objective open. Prior sources not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Closes the quadratic-versus-linear algorithmic covering factor and gives the first singleton-bound-only general packing factor.
score_reasons.novelty: Historical superlevel-set potential makes polymatroid push-relabel work despite multielement blocking; induced-matroid packing is a distinct short reduction.
score_reasons.depth: Augmentation validity, integer marginal deficits and level-history accounting are substantial combinatorial arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions and exponential versus polynomial guarantees are explicit, with separate algorithms and proofs.

checked: Read the complete push-relabel potential analysis: descending-level greedy blocking gives p(B)<=sum_t[f(a)-f(a|S_j^{>t})] by telescoping and integral loss >=1 for each rejected item.

Traced push potential increment <=d*p(a)-p(B)<=(2d-1)DeltaC and last-relabel lower bound Phi>=(2d-1)sum_{a relabeled}p(a), using k>=(4d-2)chi_circle. Thus uncovered level mass <=n, every level <=n and <=n^2 pushes/relabels.
Read generator packing reduction: r_f(S)=min_{T subset S}(f(T)+|S-T|), and kappa_circle/d inequalities imply |E-S|>=floor(kappa_circle/d)*(r_f(E)-r_f(S)), enabling disjoint matroid bases.
remaining: Verify induced-matroid rank/generator lemmas and precise external matroid-union applicability.
Audit exponential local-search exchange invariants and construction of chi_circle, including degenerate rank-zero cases.

review.title: Online Algorithms Cannot Find Isolated Perceptron Solutions
review.authors: Shuangping Li, Gabe Schoenbach

score_reasons.significance: A broad structural obstruction to online solution finding at every positive density.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses uniqueness of suffix completions and exchangeability instead of a direct overlap-gap argument.
score_reasons.depth: Combines harmonic telescoping with uniform Gaussian approximation and anti-concentration.
score_reasons.exposition: The model and separation from stability barriers are clearly explained.

checked: Traced nested prefix-completion events, uniqueness below isolation radius, and exchangeability of the next-column error.
Checked the weighted telescoping argument yielding a suffix length with small conditional failure probability.
remaining: Uniform signed-Gaussian covariance and high-dimensional CLT estimates in the appendix.
Thin-shell anti-concentration, random-seed measurability, and the full interval generalization.

review.summary: For every fixed positive constraint density, an online algorithm that irrevocably assigns binary perceptron coordinates cannot find an h-isolated Gaussian solution with nonvanishing probability when h is omega(log^4 n). The online algorithm may have unlimited computation. A well-separated interval generalization is also claimed.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier stable-algorithm barriers operate in a different computational model and at specific density thresholds. This is a density-independent barrier for online assignments, not a lower bound against arbitrary polynomial-time algorithms.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate; central probability estimates still need a full audit.

review.summary: Deterministic low-rank tensor reconstruction in k^{O(k²)}poly(n,d,τ) time over R/C for tensors admitting a rank-k rational-coefficient representation of known bit bound τ; over finite fields the output and minimal rank are over the algebraic closure, represented in a bounded extension. Here n is the sum of dimensions and d the order.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier reconstruction bound cited as k^{O(k^16)}, or k^{O(k^6)} with a newer polynomial-system solver. These baseline derivations are manuscript claims, not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Substantially improves the rank dependence for a central reconstruction problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Projection and rank structure shrink the polynomial-system unknown count to O(k²).
score_reasons.depth: Combines identity testing, depth-three circuit rank bounds, low-degree reconstruction and exact algebraic solvers.
score_reasons.exposition: The field and representation assumptions are explicit; PDF rendering was needed to preserve algebraic-closure overbars.

checked: Verified on rendered PDF page 4 that the finite-field theorem concerns algebraic-closure rank, not rank over the base field.
Traced the simultaneous-nonvanishing hitting-set argument by bounding the product of subset-sum polynomial degrees.
Checked the low-rank case variable/equation count: fewer than 9k² coefficient unknowns and k^{O(k)} equations of degree O(k).
remaining: Audit the central rank theorem and projection-extension reconstruction.
Verify exact polynomial-system solver complexity, finite extension bounds and bit complexity.

review.title: Quantum Lower Bounds for Collision Problems
review.authors: Pan Peng, Jingyu Wu
review.summary: For fixed k>=2 and exactly k-to-one strings of length n over every feasible alphabet q>=n/k, proves adaptive quantum finding complexity Theta_k(n^((2^(k-1)-1)/(2^k-1))) and one-round complexity Theta_k(n^(1-1/k)). Nonadaptive injective-versus-k-to-one testing needs Omega(epsilon*sqrt(n/k)) queries for q>=n. One-round queries may be arbitrarily entangled.
review.prior_frontier: Transfers the optimal random-function multicollision exponent to exact balanced inputs, where conditioning a random-function proof does not work. Resolves the stated Koiran-Landes-Portier-Yao one-round testing question. External optimal upper bounds and historical question were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Settles the exact-promise adaptive and nonadaptive complexities of a central family of collision tasks.
score_reasons.novelty: Domain-harmonic projection controls permutation-recording error while preserving bucket occupancy, enabling exact-promise lower bounds.
score_reasons.depth: Combines representation-theoretic encodings, compression commutators, collision-growth recurrence and one-round state comparison.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper clearly distinguishes promise, alphabet and access models, but 80 pages contain several independent delicate arguments.

checked: Checked the two-coordinate reflection commutator calculation and the assigned-position sum giving range-harmonic leakage O(sqrt(t)/n), with n outside the square root.
Traced how the encoded-component comparison plus this leakage yields projected single-query O((t+1)/n) error.
Checked contraction-based accumulation to O(T(T+1)/n) without renormalizing the projected process.
Read the exclusion of inverse-permutation evaluation and why one-round lower bounds require a separate direct analysis.
remaining: Spectral-gap/frame-normalization identities used by the encoding and exact conditional decompression.
Full collision-growth and successful-output verification bounds.
Nonadaptive occupancy and decision-state comparison arguments, plus upper-bound dependencies.

papers.title: P vs NP, a Resolution
papers.authors: Mihail Saslis

review.title: P vs NP, a Resolution
review.authors: Mihail A. Saslis
review.summary: Claims a deterministic O(n_A^2*n_B+e_A*n_A*n_B) algorithm for unrestricted subgraph isomorphism, hence P=NP, via cycle/tree decompositions and a greedy conflict graph of component embeddings. The final clone-selection subroutine is not complete: it can reject a positive instance without trying another clone in the same host component.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript purports to settle P versus NP. The established NP-completeness reduction is not the contested step; the claimed complete polynomial algorithm fails.

score_reasons.significance: No valid resolution follows because the central decision algorithm can reject a yes-instance.
score_reasons.novelty: Cycle decomposition and greedy clone elimination are not supplied with a sound new completeness argument.
score_reasons.depth: The correctness induction assumes compatible component embeddings without proving that its greedy choices retain them.
score_reasons.exposition: Essential choices are unspecified and the running-time discussion treats input-dependent component counts as constants.

checked: Inspected the B_ISOMORPHIC_A procedure, especially step 5 on PDF page 11, and the completeness induction on PDF page 12.

Constructed and enumerated a connected cactus host with cycles abc, adef, bghi, cjkl, jmn; pattern B is disjoint C3 plus C4. Its only triangle vertex sets are abc,jmn and its only square sets are adef,bghi,cjkl.

The clone-conflict graph has edges X1-Y1,X1-Y2,X1-Y3,X2-Y3 and no isolated vertices. With the permitted smallest-delta tie choosing C3 and clone abc, deleting its conflicts removes all square candidates; delta_C3=1 makes step 5 exit instead of trying clone jmn. Yet jmn and adef give a valid embedding, even an induced one. Executable enumeration and trace are saved in audits/audit488.py and audit488.json.
remaining: A full executable implementation is not supplied and the decomposition pseudocode is ambiguous; the counterexample grants the final stage the correct complete clone lists, so completeness already fails under that favorable assumption.
issues: PDF 11, B_ISOMORPHIC_A step 5 incorrectly conflates having only one host connected component with having only one embedding choice inside that component. The explicitly described valid clone choice can lead to premature rejection.
PDF 12 completeness induction does not show that separately existing embeddings can be chosen disjointly by the proposed greedy routine.

review.desk_reject_reason: Demonstrable failure of the central algorithm: the cactus instance and allowed execution described in the audit reject C3 disjoint-union C4 despite the disjoint embedding jmn plus adef. Step 5 (PDF11) provides no alternative-clone search when delta=1.

review.title: Newton Steps are Faster for Linear Complementarity Problems
review.authors: Haoyuan Ma, László Végh, Adrian Vladu

score_reasons.significance: Improves a longstanding conditioning dependence for a substantial LCP class.
score_reasons.novelty: Local diagonal weights separate Newton convergence from the global handicap.
score_reasons.depth: Requires spectral-radius structure, stability of extremal path weights, and two-step progress analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: The overview explains both the new norm and the dimension-versus-handicap tradeoff.

checked: Recomputed Newton centrality error as the coordinatewise square of the resolvent action.
Traced quadratic contraction in the Rump norm conditional on weight bounds and stability; verified the small-neighborhood constants in Proposition 5.8.
remaining: Proofs of Rump-weight boundedness and stability, including the primary Rump theorem.
The sharper two-Newton-step n^(9/8) progress bound and initialization/bit-complexity reductions.
The separate coNP-completeness and handicap-approximation hardness claims.

review.summary: For sufficient-matrix linear complementarity, claims an interior-point iteration bound with handicap dependence improved to its square root, at a dimension cost: min{sqrt(n)(1+kappa), n^(9/8)sqrt(1+kappa)} up to logarithmic factors. Develops a resolvent-norm characterization and locally stable Rump weights.
review.prior_frontier: Classical sufficient-LCP iteration bounds depend linearly on 1+kappa. The new tradeoff improves that dependence; it does not make general LCP polynomial-time or give a strongly polynomial algorithm.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate; the new weight-stability machinery and final progress bound remain unaudited.

papers.title: QMA has perfect completeness
papers.authors: Sabee Grewal, Dorian Rudolph

review.title: QMA has perfect completeness
review.authors: Sabee Grewal, Dorian Rudolph
review.summary: Proves QMA=QMA₁ with exact Hadamard–Toffoli verification. A polynomial-bit rational diagonal entry of a power of the acceptance operator closes a finite nonunitary history into an exact cycle; a global kernel test gives perfect completeness and constant soundness. The construction depends on verifier arithmetic and does not relativize to arbitrary quantum oracles.
review.prior_frontier: Settles the longstanding perfect-completeness question for QMA. Prior nearly-perfect/infinite-counter approaches are discussed; primary Takeuchi exact-gate dependency independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a foundational complexity-class equality and upgrades several QMA₁-completeness results.
score_reasons.novelty: The rational diagonal-power certificate avoids needing an exact eigenvalue and permits an exact finite cyclic history.
score_reasons.depth: The proof is unusually short but its combination of arithmetic control, nonunitary history and exact rational block encoding is substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: The complete central proof makes the contraction argument, certificate sizes and gate implementation transparent.

checked: Traced Lemma 3.1 realification: acceptance spectra duplicate, the new real-coordinate qubit may be part of the witness, and paired Hadamards preserve the acceptance operator.
Independently realized the real controlled-phase gate as a controlled real rotation using Toffoli and controlled-Z with paired-Hadamard spectator; verified dyadic denominator 2^{2g}.
Checked ℓ=O(m), diagonal trace pigeonhole Γz>2, exact rational bit size, cyclic fixed point and NO-case norm bound ||C||≤2/3 for every allowed certificate.
Traced both block-encoding gadgets and the branch counts a,2a,b, with V and V† applied unconditionally; verified no controlled-V assumption is needed.
Checked certificate rescaling, M/8≤a≤M/4, all branch ranges fit, and rejection probability ≥1/576 for arbitrary witnesses after measuring the certificate.
Checked constant soundness amplification against entangled repeated witnesses via tensor-product accepting operators.
Read Takeuchi arXiv:2312.16433 Appendix B and checked its exact |000⟩→|100⟩ gate algebra; this supplies clean |1⟩ ancillas for exact X/CNOT from Hadamard–Toffoli.
remaining: Quantum-3-SAT and clique-homology corollaries were not independently traced through their external completeness reductions.
The forward-only in-place-permutation oracle corollary depends on MPR26 controlled-query/history reductions and was not independently audited.
This is a mathematical main-proof check, not formal verification or circuit execution.

review.title: Constant-Round Massively Parallel Algorithms for Approximate MSTs in Metric Spaces
review.authors: Eunjin Oh, Hyeonjun Shin
review.area: Massively parallel algorithms; metric spanning trees
review.summary: Fully scalable randomized MPC constructs a (1+epsilon)-MST in an explicitly represented n-point metric in O(log(1/(sigma*epsilon))/sigma^2) rounds, n^sigma local and soft-O(n^2) total space. Euclidean coordinates in arbitrary d give O(sigma^-4) approximation in O(sigma^-2) rounds and O(nd+n^(1+sigma)) total space. Doubling dimension <=c sigma log n gives O(sigma^-1) approximation in O(ddim/sigma^4) rounds with soft-O(n^(1+sigma))*2^O(ddim) space. Actual trees and corresponding approximate TSP tours, not only cost estimates, are produced with high probability.
review.prior_frontier: Removes the log log n additive term for general metrics and log log n log log log n rounds for high-dimensional Euclidean MST; lower-bound optimality in epsilon is conditional on the 1-vs-2-cycles conjecture. Doubling result increases dimension range while weakening 1+epsilon approximation. Prior sources not independently traced.

score_reasons.significance: Constant-round construction of high-dimensional approximate metric MSTs addresses a central MPC bottleneck with near-input-size space.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses truncated local Prim plus forest cutting and merging rather than global threshold-graph connectivity.
score_reasons.depth: Weighted contractions obey a relaxed triangle inequality; local forest identification, root-cost control and memory-efficient merging must work together.
score_reasons.exposition: Input representation, dimension, local-space and approximation tradeoffs are stated clearly; proofs are spread across metric-specific constructions.

checked: Traced truncated-Prim Lemma 4.1: outside-neighborhood separation >2tau and total current weight <tau force the next global-Prim edge to stay inside, with consistent tie breaking.

Read first-stage forest orientation and root-cost proof: choosing highest-priority maximum-weight vertex within cost radius prevents two-way edges; root-to-minimum-cost paths are interior-disjoint and charge root cost to tree weight.

Inspected the exponential-clock fragment labeling used to cut long rooted paths, and read the contraction iteration: O(1/sigma) calls with epsilon/(2L) error reduce to a graph fitting one machine and multiply cost by <=exp(epsilon/2)<=1+epsilon.
remaining: Audit the random fragment-cut probability/cost bounds, forest-merging concentration and full MPC storage/communication accounting.
Trace geometric consistent-hashing dependencies, unbounded-spread reduction and the TSP traversal construction.

review.title: On ZLIP: Combinatorial Structures and Reduction to √n-ZSVP
review.authors: Shengmao Jiang
review.summary: Studies orbit sampling in lattices isometric to Z^n, with an explicit nonzero fourth-moment criterion for recovery and flat-shell counting. Separately, under a stated finite Gram-randomization implementation assumption, reduces ZLIP to Gamma(N)-ZSVP in padded dimension N when n Gamma(N)^2/N<=1/4, covering fixed powers Gamma(N)<=C N^alpha with alpha<1/2. It does not establish the exact square-root endpoint suggested by the title.
review.prior_frontier: Extends established orbit-learning and Gram-randomization methods to broader profiles and padding reductions. The shell-sampling route additionally assumes a supplied finite relative local estimate; these conditional hypotheses are not algorithmically established in this manuscript.

score_reasons.significance: Offers useful structural and conditional reductions for a special lattice-isomorphism problem, with material implementation assumptions.
score_reasons.novelty: The primitive singleton-projection test is a clean new use of padding, while recovery and randomization foundations are inherited.
score_reasons.depth: Combines fourth moments, shell combinatorics, invariant sampling and exact integer-coordinate arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: The formal theorem and conclusion are careful about assumptions and the excluded endpoint; the title is less precise.

checked: Traced the padding success bound from uniform support within an orbit, using a union bound to obtain probability at least 3n/(4N).
Checked gcd invariance under unimodular maps and exact unit-norm acceptance iff projection retains a single hidden coordinate.
Checked finite-total-variation loss, polynomial padded dimension for fixed alpha<1/2, and the exact-uniform sampler after full basis recovery.
Read the explicit counterexample at Gamma(N)=sqrt(N): all-ones orbit projections never pass when n>=2.
remaining: Finite Gram-randomization assumption is taken as a hypothesis, not proved here.
Full fourth-moment learning, local-limit shell sampler and quantitative flat-shell combinatorics.
Cited ZLIP-to-exact-ZSVP reduction and related-work priority.

sources.detail: Excluded square-root endpoint and exact-uniform postprocessing

papers.title: Discrepancy for Random Linear Codes
papers.authors: Dean Doron, Tal Leonov, Jonathan Mosheiff, Henrique Navas, Nicolas Resch, João Ribeiro

review.title: Discrepancy for Random Linear Codes
review.authors: Dean Doron, Tal Leonov, Jonathan Mosheiff, Henrique Navas, Nicolas Resch, João Ribeiro
review.summary: Random linear codes have nearly exact intersections with all translates of any fixed normalized nonnegative test above its infinity-norm capacity parameter, over arbitrary finite fields, with exponential relative-error bounds. A second theorem handles large families of Fourier-concentrated tests. Consequences include near-uniform counts in every Hamming ball above list-decoding capacity, and prime-field rectangle/erasure list-recovery under moderate field growth; these counts are exponential, not efficient decoding or constant-list results below capacity. A local-leakage application supplies linear ramp secret sharing at any fixed linear reconstruction threshold with O(n/log n) gap for polynomial-size prime fields in the stated growth regime.
review.prior_frontier: Prior above-capacity results mainly gave weaker covering guarantees; leakage-resilient linear schemes were restricted to reconstruction thresholds above n/2. The paper compares against unstructured random codes. Prior results and secret-sharing reductions not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Broad discrepancy guarantees for random linear codes connect above-capacity coding and previously unavailable secret-sharing thresholds.
score_reasons.novelty: Self-convolution controls the variance of each newly added random generator; repeated smoothing yields failure probabilities strong enough for huge test families.
score_reasons.depth: Multistage smoothness and Fourier concentration analyses are substantial, with delicate growth restrictions on alphabet and family size.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed theorem bounds distinguish translate families over all fields from rectangle applications over primes; high technical load but clear organization.

checked: Traced self-convolution F_f=f*reflected(f): Fourier coefficients are |fhat|^2, translations disappear, and alpha-Fourier concentration squares.

Read complete one-generator variance lemma: dual-code indicators are pairwise independent off scalar lines; collinear contributions and AM-GM give Var(delta_new)<=((q-1)/q)^2 delta_{C,F_f}, with mean delta/q.
Read initial trajectory classification and proof that a first smoothness failure without increasing steps requires many bad steps, using the multiplier 1/q+t/(4qk).
Checked the dual-typical Markov union bound and Fourier-weight enumerator bound gamma*q^-i*((1+(q-1)alpha)^n-1).
remaining: Finish quadratic-in-t bad-step tail, monotonicity failure control and repeated-smoothing parameter induction; these are essential to uniform-family guarantees.
Verify all probability regimes near rate one, prime-field rectangle Fourier bounds and ramp secret-sharing leakage conversion.

review.title: Trading Time, Space, and Alternations: General Plasticity for Algorithms from Hardness of Range Avoidance
review.authors: Zeyong Li, Roei Tell

score_reasons.significance: Offers a general connection between avoidance hardness and algorithmic resource tradeoffs.
score_reasons.novelty: Turns failure to avoid ranges into short encodings of accepting PCP witnesses.
score_reasons.depth: Combines witness compression, padding, persistent-randomness verifiers and derandomization equivalences.
score_reasons.exposition: The assumptions and average-case versus worst-case guarantees are stated with useful detail.

checked: Traced the compressed PCP-witness verifier: hardness forces an accepting proof into a range, while repeated tests preserve worst-case soundness.
Checked the public-coin conversion union bound over short messages, padded input distribution and space accounting with reusable randomness.
remaining: Audit the PCP construction and all hardness quantifiers.
Check the persistent-randomness derandomization equivalence, alternating-time consequence and worst-case exponential-time corollary.

review.summary: Connects average-case hardness of low-space indexed Range Avoidance to general time-space and alternation simulations. Under the additional persistent-randomness derandomization assumption prBP*L=prL, obtains subpolynomial-space average-case simulations; stronger hardness assumptions yield alternation collapse consequences.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the conceptual time-space plasticity suggested by recent square-root-space simulation results, but the principal new general simulations are conditional and average-case. Persistent two-way access to randomness is a separate resource requiring an explicit assumption.
review.recommendation: Strong conditional-complexity candidate; do not present the simulations as unconditional or worst-case polynomial-time results.

review.title: Polynomial Swap Coboundary Expansion with Applications to LTCs and PCPs
review.authors: Yotam Dikstein, Izhar Oppenheim, Inga Valentiner-Branth
review.summary: For suitable KMS complexes of sufficiently large dimension and field size polynomial in r, proves r-swap coboundary expansion Ω(r^−34) with permutation coefficients Sym_m for m below the field characteristic. Vertex degrees remain bounded independently of the number of vertices. Supplies a stronger ingredient for forthcoming sparse-code tests and improves the parameter dependence of an older succinct-PCP construction.
review.prior_frontier: Previous bounds on related bounded-degree complexes were exp(−O(sqrt(r))); even inverse-exponential bounds were not known for the particular KMS family. The paper explicitly acknowledges a newer PCP construction with better parameters than its PCP application.

score_reasons.significance: A polynomial rather than subexponential local-to-global loss is an important quantitative structural advance.
score_reasons.novelty: A product decomposition of group-relation fillings reduces the problem to small-factor Dehn functions.
score_reasons.depth: Requires probabilistic color geometry, group presentations, cone fillings and several local-to-global expansion reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: The overview explains the decomposition and carefully distinguishes proved structure from forthcoming applications.

checked: Checked the permutation-coefficient characteristic restriction and bounded-degree quantifiers.
Traced the combinatorial part of link connectedness/simple connectedness: disjoint color sets leave any given pair of root indices uncovered by another color set.
Verified the colored-join isomorphism including empty restricted faces.
Checked the stated Dehn decomposition formula and how polynomial-length sorting would yield polynomial overhead, conditional on allowed subgroup commutations.
remaining: Audit the actual subgroup commutation/decomposition lemma, direct factor filling bounds and random nice-color probability.
Verify all external presentation, vanishing-cohomology and local-to-global hypotheses.
Trace the r^−34 arithmetic and PCP substitution; the forthcoming LTC result is not proved here.

review.title: Randomness-Efficient Robust Locally Testable Codes in the Low-Acceptance Regime from HDXs
review.authors: Inbar Ben Yaacov, Yotam Dikstein, Siqi Liu
review.summary: Proves low-acceptance robust local testability for KMS codes with constant-in-blocklength query count q=exp(poly(1/epsilon)) and q*2^rand=N*poly(1/epsilon), over sufficiently large prime fields. Also proves low-acceptance axis-parallel hyperplane testing for high-order tensor codes with very strong relative-distance assumptions. The KMS rate is not constant; low-acceptance c^3-LTCs remain open.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier KMS-code results supplied high-acceptance testability. This preserves sparse local views while reaching low acceptance; the tensor test itself is classical, with a new low-acceptance guarantee. Historical comparisons and HDX input theorems not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A major step toward randomness-efficient low-soundness coding and PCP building blocks, without resolving the constant-rate low-acceptance LTC problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Synchronizes competing local codeword lists through permutation-valued cocycles and then uses high-acceptance agreement testing to reach an actual global codeword.
score_reasons.depth: Combines list stability/pruning, spectral and coboundary expansion, agreement testing and quantitative trickling down.
score_reasons.exposition: The 87-page manuscript distinguishes robust local agreement from simple test acceptance and clearly states rate and distance limitations.

checked: Checked the final high-acceptance-to-low-acceptance implication: most selected local codewords agree with one global codeword and retain epsilon/3 local agreement.
Traced the permutation cocycle cancellation on triples and the union-bound constants from list restriction bijections.
Checked selection via a coboundary potential and the final 1-alpha edge-consistency estimate.
remaining: List-stability and pruning proof feeding the cocycle construction.
KMS/tensor expansion parameters, explicit rank/field bounds, local-testability trickling and Appendix C divisibility removal.
No independent construction or decoding implementation was tested.

papers.title: Geometry Of The Subset Sum Problem - Part I
papers.authors: Srinivas Bollepalli

review.title: Geometry Of The Subset Sum Problem - Part I
review.authors: Srinivas Balaji Bollepalli
review.summary: Claims polynomial-time exact decision and counting for arbitrary integer Subset Sum by constructing/refining a geometric path DAG, and hence P=NP and FP=#P. The polynomial-size proof relies on an invalid path-count formula and an unsupported worst-case growth argument; no valid general polynomial bound is established.
review.prior_frontier: The claimed complexity-class collapses would be fundamental, but they depend on the new DAG-size bound, not on the standard dynamic-programming fact that paths in an already small DAG can be counted. No independent claim of P not equal NP is made by this review.

score_reasons.significance: The stated breakthrough is unsupported once the essential path-count and growth bounds fail.
score_reasons.novelty: The geometric encoding may be a useful representation, but the claimed compression is not proved.
score_reasons.depth: The product inequality conflates arc-count ratios with path multiplication, and the peak-growth argument uses typical-expectation language for a worst-case theorem.
score_reasons.exposition: Many internal references are unresolved question marks, and key global bounds are sketches rather than complete arguments.

checked: Read definitions of the configuration graph, point counts gamma_i, completed layered graph J and arc growth factor alpha_i.

Algebraically checked Proposition 9.30: gamma_1*product_{i=1}^{j-1}alpha_i telescopes to gamma_{j-1}*gamma_j, an adjacent-layer edge count, while the true number of paths in complete layered J is product_{i=1}^r gamma_i. For layer sizes 1,2,2,2 the asserted formula gives 4 but the actual path count is 8.

Traced the dependency from this formula to Product Inequality 9.32, maximal gamma bound 9.33, and polynomial graph-size conclusions in Section10. The substitution of a geometric progression as the worst case in 9.33 is also not justified.

Read Theorem10.1: after a logarithmic number of refinements it asserts zero paths are separated and roughly as many nodes are removed as added, using statements about what one can expect in general; it gives no worst-case argument establishing that invariant.
remaining: The small layered-graph example refutes the combinatorial identity used in the proof, not an explicitly reconstructed original Subset Sum execution. No claim is made that it itself disproves every possible SSP-specific bound.
A valid bound for graph refinement on all subset-sum instances, replacing these essential steps, would be required before the complexity conclusions could be evaluated.
issues: Proposition9.30 (PDF72) is not a valid path-count identity: its product telescopes to adjacent-layer edge counts, whereas complete-layered paths multiply all intermediate layer sizes. Theorem9.32 explicitly relies on it.
Theorem9.33 (PDF73) assumes without justification that the extremal point-count sequence is a geometric progression.
Theorem10.1 (PDF83) replaces required worst-case refinement analysis with expectations and unquantified claims about surviving nodes.

review.desk_reject_reason: Missing valid proof of the essential polynomial DAG-size bound: Proposition9.30 has an explicit elementary path-count error, and Theorems9.33/10.1 do not supply a replacement worst-case bound. Consequently the advertised P=NP and FP=#P conclusions are not established.

review.authors: Henry Fleischmann, Sagnik Mukhopadhyay, Swagato Sanyal
review.summary: Zero-error randomized outgoing-cut-query algorithms for s–t reachability in unweighted directed graphs use Õ(n^{9/5}) queries in a simple version and Õ(n^{5/3}) in a refinement, in expectation and with high probability. Checked the query balancing T=n^{4/5} and n^{2/3} yields the claimed exponents conditional on the averaging and flow lemmas.

Trace the explicit flow-recovery query bound and general-digraph extension.

review.title: Directed Global Minimum Cut in Almost-Linear Time
review.authors: Henry Fleischmann, Jason Li, Thatchaphol Saranurak, Benyu Wang
review.summary: Computes directed global minimum cut with high probability using maximum-flow instances of total size O-tilde(m), plus O-tilde(m) additional time. For polynomially bounded positive integral weights this gives m^(1+o(1)) time. The key is marginal contraction of a random arborescence without constructing an approximate arborescence packing.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the previous m^(1+o(1))*min(sqrt(n),n/m^(1/3)) exact bound. Independently checked the stated near-linear flow-rounding and two-arborescence primitives and the rooted constant-factor approximation theorem in their primary sources.

score_reasons.significance: Settles almost-linear exact complexity for a fundamental directed cut problem.
score_reasons.novelty: An auxiliary matching-flow construction gives expectation-preserving support mixing, bypassing explicit approximate packing.
score_reasons.depth: The main contribution is a short structural coupling: Hall feasibility, preservation of all previously one-respected cuts, flow rounding and two-tree decomposition.
score_reasons.exposition: The full argument is unusually compact, with the fractional vector limitation and why capacity violations after rounding are harmless explicitly explained.

checked: Traced the full novel proof: Hall matching between any arborescence and fundamental paths in the fixed tree supplies a feasible auxiliary flow.

Checked that one-respected cut S induces connected T[S], hence h(SxS)<=|S|-1 and its incoming h mass is at least one. Demand-preserving rounding retains this guarantee even if individual capacities are exceeded.
Checked heavy-light/segment-tree compression, integral total 2n-2 support, two-arborescence partition, and E[1_Tnew|T]<=(1_T+q)/2.
Verified t=ceil(log_2(16n)) contractions give expected mincut crossings <3/2, hence probability >1/2 of one crossing, and logarithmic amplification/recovery fits total O-tilde(m) flow size.
Verified primary-source statements for Kang-Payor rounding, Tarjan two-arborescence complexity, Quanrud rooted approximation and the cited one-respecting cut recovery formulation.
remaining: External maximum-flow, cut-recovery, arborescence-decomposition and approximation algorithms were used as established black boxes, not re-proved in full.
Second-mincut and arboricity application reductions were not audited.
Implementation details for zero-connectivity inputs are routine reachability preprocessing rather than the positive-lambda core analyzed.

sources.detail: Kang-Payor Sections 2.2 and 3.3: integral-demand and expectation-preserving flow rounding.
Tarjan primary publication abstract: directed rooted two-tree algorithm in O(m alpha(m,n)).
Quanrud Theorem 1.1: rooted (1+epsilon) cut approximation in O(log^4(n)/epsilon) flows.
Appendix A restates Cen et al. Theorem 2.7 cut recovery with polylogarithmic flows.

papers.title: The list size of random linear and LDPC codes at capacity
papers.authors: Shashwat Silas

review.title: The list size of random linear and LDPC codes at capacity
review.authors: Shashwat Silas
review.area: Coding theory; random linear and LDPC codes
review.summary: For fixed prime power q and fixed radius 0<rho<1-1/q, sufficiently small fixed epsilon yields random-linear-code list size floor(h_q(rho)/epsilon) or one greater with high probability as block length grows. Outside an exponentially tiny fractional-part window it equals the ceiling. Also proves threshold-rate equivalence, up to arbitrary prescribed slack for sufficiently large fixed odd check size, between the Gallager-type LDPC ensemble and random linear codes for a precisely defined class of convex local properties. This is combinatorial list size, not efficient list decoding, and does not assert equality for every fixed small LDPC check size.
review.prior_frontier: Prior q>=3 list size only known up to a constant factor, binary case within three adjacent integers; concurrent work obtains the h_q(rho)/epsilon+O(1) bound. Prior local-property transfer to LDPC was one direction. Sources not independently traced.

score_reasons.significance: Sharp list-size concentration across every finite alphabet and a general LDPC threshold converse substantially resolve two coding questions.
score_reasons.novelty: An entropy-deficit theorem for many sparse linear combinations supplies the sharp leading constant; small-subgraph conditioning supports the LDPC converse.
score_reasons.depth: General-position versus small-support structure, Gibbs variational bounds, sunflower arguments and dependent-code second moments are technically substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states fixed parameters, near-integer exception and the exact three convexity/rounding assumptions on LDPC local properties.

checked: Traced conversion of a clustered bad type to k sparse coordinates and m-k pairwise nonproportional sparse combinations, including quotient by the all-ones direction and threshold denominator k-1.
Verified threshold lower-bound case split: one combination gives constant entropy deficit gamma*, while many give (k-1)h+eta, choosing eta=h/L and N0 polynomial in log L.
Read Gibbs variational single-combination deficit D_q(rho||rho(1+kappa)); Fourier expansion establishes approximate multiplicativity for combinations in W-general position with error q^T*kappa^W.
Checked the greedy general-position dichotomy: failure to extend T vectors places all combinations in a dimension <=T-1 subspace plus low-support vectors.
remaining: Audit full small-support/sunflower entropy theorem, exact extremal bad-type quotient analysis and near-integer parameter arithmetic.
Trace external random-linear-code threshold theorem and all LDPC second-moment/small-subgraph conditioning arguments, including parity-compatible rounding hypotheses.

papers.title: The Polynomial-Time Low-Degree Conjecture is False
papers.authors: Songtao Mao

review.title: The Polynomial-Time Low-Degree Conjecture is False
review.authors: Songtao Mao
review.summary: For every fixed r>=3, constructs vertex-permutation-invariant simple-graph distributions P_n matching G(n,1/2) exactly on every set of Theta((log n)^(r-1)) edges, yet a uniform deterministic O(n^2)-time rank test strongly distinguishes after any fixed resampling rate epsilon in [0,epsilon_r], for some sufficiently small positive epsilon_r. The sampler is nonuniform with polynomial advice; uniform polynomial-time sampling remains open. Thus the stated symmetric, uniform-null, noisy polynomial-time low-degree conjecture fails without an additional hypothesis.
review.prior_frontier: Previous symmetric Boolean examples had zero advantage through polynomial degree but only quasipolynomial-time noisy distinguishers; other polynomial examples violated uniform-null, symmetry or robust-noise assumptions. The exact original conjecture and cited Reed–Muller dependencies remain to be independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A counterexample within the stated standard binary symmetric noisy setting changes the scope of a widely used hardness heuristic.
score_reasons.novelty: Monomial-lifting plus rank exposes Reed–Muller structure in surviving clean columns without locating hidden evaluation labels.
score_reasons.depth: Constructs a low-bias polynomial subspace, high-girth evaluation vectors and alternating-form graph law; combines these with random-puncturing rank bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: Main theorem states the small-noise interval and sampler nonuniformity explicitly, and the rank proof is detailed and compact.

checked: Traced the low-bias subspace averaging argument conditional on BEHL12 and the evaluation-vector union bound: short zero-sum probability <=2^-K+eta^w gives L*2^(-3K/4)+exp(n eta)-1=o(1).
Traced exact edge independence: <=D edges use <=2D<=L independent endpoint vectors; uniform alternating forms restrict surjectively to their span. Random permutation preserves the marginals.

Read the complete rank separation argument conditional on BHSS22: null monomial-lift columns are full rank; planted clean columns number n^(1/2-a lambda+o(1)) but span dimension <=sum_{j<=rs}binom(m,j)=n^(b h2(r sigma/b)+o(1)), strictly smaller. Other columns add at most one rank each.
Checked parameter existence, Chernoff clean-column count and Gaussian-elimination time n^(1+alpha+o(1))=o(n^2), with 1/2<alpha<1.

Verified all three critical external hypotheses directly in primary sources. Hopkins thesis Conjecture2.2.4 assumes fixed-arity vertex symmetry, product null, superlogarithmic almost independence and fixed resampling noise; it does not assume a uniformly polynomial-time sampler. BEHL primary ECCC TR08-080 revision1 Lemma2 supplies the absolute-bias tail for degree <=(1-epsilon)m; choosing epsilon=1/2 validates Lemma2.1. BHSS primary ECCC TR22-075 Theorem1.1 gives independent evaluation columns for a uniform distinct subset of size (1-delta) times the code dimension and degree <gamma_0 times the number of variables. The manuscript conditions on distinct null columns and enlarges uniformly to half the code dimension, which correctly matches that sampling model.

Rechecked the full main Theorem1.2 chain on pp8–15: the low-bias subspace and short-dependence union bound; alternating-form restriction surjectivity; clean-column binomial count after independent resampling; rank-deficit bound despite arbitrarily corrupted other columns; rational parameter choices and n^(1+alpha+o(1)) arithmetic cost for alpha<1. The advice is used only to sample the alternative; the rank distinguisher is a single uniform algorithm independent of noise rate and advice.
remaining: No unresolved issue in the principal graph-valued counterexample was found. The optional explicit trace-subspace construction and the Gaussian/tensor extensions in Section4 were not fully audited; uniform polynomial-time sampling remains explicitly open, and stronger conjectures imposing that condition are not refuted.

papers.title: Robust quantum state certification and uncertainty principles for total influence
papers.authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Jerry Li, Joe Slote

review.title: Robust quantum state certification and uncertainty principles for total influence
review.authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Jerry Li, Joseph Slote
review.summary: For all but exponentially few Haar-random target states, gives constant-robustness certification using nonadaptive single-qubit Pauli measurements with O(ε^−2 log(1/δ)) copies, or O(ε^−1 log(1/δ)) with one adaptive final measurement per copy. Assumes oracle access to target amplitudes in standard and Hadamard bases; generally this is not an efficiently implementable classical description. Proves a weighted total-influence uncertainty principle.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier single-qubit tests had robustness degrading with n or log n; prior constant-robustness tests needed log n-qubit measurements. Concurrent work also achieves constant robustness with a different many-basis test.

score_reasons.significance: Removes dimension-dependent robustness loss under very restricted measurements, with meaningful information-theoretic limits.
score_reasons.novelty: A two-basis test is analyzed through a weighted influence uncertainty principle rather than a single-chain spectral gap.
score_reasons.depth: The weighted random-measure concentration and good/bad subspace decomposition are extensive technical contributions.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper clearly discloses its amplitude-oracle limitation and separates adaptive and nonadaptive copy dependence.

checked: Traced the reduction from the certification acceptance operator to a constant spectral gap on the target-orthogonal subspace.
Checked the sharp unweighted influence bound by diagonalizing the one-qubit matrix HDH+D, with minimum eigenvalue 1−1/sqrt(2).
Verified the role of orthogonality in the weighted theorem and the two-basis amplitude access model.
Checked that nonadaptive shadow estimation has ε^−2 dependence, whereas ε^−1 optimality is asserted only for the adaptive version.
remaining: Audit the 50-plus-page weighted concentration/subspace argument and uniformity over all orthogonal states.
Trace finite-precision oracle implementation and all ε/δ regimes in the amplification corollary.
Concurrent-work claims and external certification lower bounds not independently verified.

review.title: Gain-Sharing Optimization in Randomized Primal--Dual Analysis: Structure and Certification

score_reasons.novelty: Replaces searching particular gain functions with a least-profile comparison principle and certified shooting formulation.

checked: Checked the unique minimizing-load equation from strict monotonicity of e^(−ℓ)(1−f(ℓ)) and the envelope derivative.

Traced the regularity bootstrap: uniform Lipschitz bounds for the maximum yield absolute continuity, fixing an interior maximizer yields the derivative, and monotonicity gives a unique continuous minimizing load.
Checked that a sup-norm residual below 1/5000 implies the displayed score error below 10^−4 for η=0.66.
remaining: Audit canonical LP reduction, lossless restrictions, full least-profile comparison/existence, and the actual interval-arithmetic certificate data; numerical enclosures not independently recomputed.

papers.title: Overcoming the Randomness-Utility Trade-off in Answering Differentially Private Linear Queries
papers.authors: Surendra Ghentiyala, Pritish Kamath, Ravi Kumar, Pasin Manurangsi

review.title: Overcoming the Randomness-Utility Trade-off in Answering Differentially Private Linear Queries
review.authors: Surendra Ghentiyala, Pritish Kamath, Ravi Kumar, Pasin Manurangsi
review.area: Differential privacy; randomness complexity; convex geometry
review.summary: For d-dimensional queries with sensitivity one in a norm induced by a compact symmetric convex body, a pure epsilon-DP mechanism has expected norm error O(d/epsilon) and uses O(log d) independent random bits in expectation. The general optimal-error construction need not be computationally efficient. For l_infinity and epsilon<=log d, an efficient mechanism achieves expected error O(d log d/epsilon) with the same expected randomness. Randomness optimality is established against prior lower bounds only in the high-privacy regime epsilon<=1/d.
review.prior_frontier: Previous O(log d)-random-bit mechanisms had roughly quadratic-in-d error; Laplace-level error generally needed Omega(d) random bits. Manuscript uses known entropy-to-expected-randomness conversion and compares with recent private/public randomness variants; prior sources not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Removes a previously apparent utility/randomness tradeoff for pure-DP linear query answering, with a practical-model distinction for efficient implementation.
score_reasons.novelty: Exponential sampling by distance to a cell, combined with one partition secluded at all scales, improves both tail and entropy bounds.
score_reasons.depth: Torus random covering, simultaneous multiscale cell bounds and entropy control provide a substantial geometric argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates expected error/random bits, inefficient existence and efficient logarithmic-error overhead; limitations are prominent.

checked: Read multiscale partition existence: an eta-net of a norm torus has exp(O(d log d)) anchors; lambda=Theta(d log d) random center intensity covers all anchors and bounds every radius 1/ell neighborhood by O(d log d*exp(d/ell)) via Chernoff and union bounds. John transformation preserves norm distances.
Verified cell-distance sensitivity <=1 by triangle inequality and hence pure-DP exponential mechanism; cell distance, rather than representative distance, supplies a unit-mass normalization term.
Read shell-tail and entropy argument: Z=ceil(d*distance/rho) has E Z=O(log d), near-shell log cell count O(log d+Z), far-shell count dominated by exponential tail; H(P)<=H(Z)+H(P|Z)=O(log d).
remaining: Audit exact sampling computational model and entropy-to-random-bits dependency; real-valued query computation and arbitrary convex-body access are separate costs.
Read full explicit l_infinity partition, efficient enumeration/rejection sampler, and epsilon/running-time dependence. Claimed Lean artifact was not built.

review.authors: Dimitrios Myrisiotis

Exact continuous uniform risk instead uses an explicitly defined rational-weight counting class; binary-gap and unbounded-loss qualifications matter.
review.prior_frontier: Extends prescribed-architecture and permutation-training hardness to freely chosen architectures with fixed numerical inventories. Most headline complexity classes reflect new model classifications rather than stronger general learning lower bounds.

score_reasons.novelty: Sparse disagreement witnesses yield a polynomial universal separating set for constant caps; occurrence-placement and moment-cancellation gadgets handle harder variants.
score_reasons.depth: Many reductions require excluding all alternative inventory placements, with a particularly long Boolean-case appendix.
score_reasons.exposition: Assumptions and promise gaps are carefully stated, but 110 pages and numerous models make full assessment demanding.

remaining: All hardness reductions, particularly the extensive architecture-placement converse, require audit.
Continuous exact rational integration and Gaussian counting classifications/dependencies not checked.

review.title: Adaptive Steps and Certificates for Semi-Streaming Shortest Paths
review.authors: Sarwan Ali
review.summary: For connected undirected positively weighted graphs, modifies sampled multiplicative-weights semi-streaming SSSP by retaining shortest-path trees and small violator sets. score_reasons.significance: Adds certifiable instance-adaptive stopping to an important streaming primitive while leaving the worst-case round frontier unchanged.
score_reasons.novelty: Tree retention and permanent violators turn per-edge jump histories into a rigorous stretch certificate and bulk Bellman–Ford progress.
score_reasons.depth: Proofs combine sampled constraint-weight control, spanning-tree union bounds and explicit multiplicative-weight failure counts.
score_reasons.exposition: The resource accounting includes retained trees and violators, and the appendix exposes the constants and standing assumptions.

checked: Verified retained-tree distance monotonicity and exactness when no edge violates a triangle inequality.
Traced the window certificate by telescoping a true shortest path and averaging edge-relative excess.
Checked the fixed-tree sampling union bound, at-most-one bulk violation per edge, failure-count bound and the displayed 11k²/ε round arithmetic.
remaining: Check streaming implementation and initialization assumptions, all refined instance bounds and experimental reproducibility; no independent verification of the external spanner routine.

review.title: A Numerical Refinement of an Exact Discrete Fourier Transform Bound

review.summary: Refines the certified exact-complex-arithmetic DFT saving to delta=0.0030201659, giving work O(n(log n)^(1-delta)) for all integer lengths. Improvement beyond the previous certificate parameter is 5.9e-9; uses the same circuit and Fourier reduction with tighter rational moment estimates and tensor power 11640 instead of 7760. Model supplies an exact canonical root of unity and allows unbounded-magnitude complex scalars, with charged preparation and polynomially bounded integer words; this is not a bit-complexity FFT claim.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier circuit certificate allowed any saving below C0=0.00302016, even though an earlier displayed final theorem used 0.0030103. Checked exponent-slack logic delta<beta<C: inherited polyloglog overhead is absorbed by the fixed positive beta-delta gap.

review.summary: For continuous-time bipartite matching with independent Poisson arrivals and hidden exponential patience, approximating optimal long-run reward within a sufficiently small constant relative error is NP-hard when both sides have finite patience, and also when suppliers have finite patience and customers zero patience. Hardness already uses unit rewards and unit abandonment rates. Policy-computation consequences require efficiently executable policies and polynomial mixing/settling conditions; they do not rule out all policy representations. If either side has infinite patience, a flow formulation is exact.

review.title: Provable Recovery from Integer Quotients: Improved Bounds for Nonlinear Hidden Number Problems
review.authors: Taehun Kang, Changmin Lee
review.summary: Improves provable unrevealed-bit exponents to 1/2−ε for modular inversion HNP, 1/5−ε for elliptic-curve HNP, and 1/3−ε for hidden multipliers. For each fixed secret, under specified random-shift/multiplier models, returns all consistent secrets in expected poly(log p) bit time and is uniquely correct with high probability. Arbitrary valid inputs have exact correctness but no polynomial worst-case time guarantee.
review.prior_frontier: Prior cited exponents are 1/3,1/6,1/5 respectively. Elliptic-curve query subgroups must have size at least p/polylog p, with changed accepted-tuple sampling. Historical baselines not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Improves rigorous leakage thresholds for three established nonlinear HNP variants.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses nonzero integer quotients of reduced polynomial values and targeted dual-lattice tail bounds rather than requiring small values to vanish over integers.
score_reasons.depth: Problem-specific counting and elliptic-curve pole cancellations are substantial beyond the common search framework.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper distinguishes every-input correctness from distributional expected cost and states sampling changes explicitly.

checked: Checked that invertible integer basis change preserving px₁ gives x₁=Σα_j(h_j/p), with original-constraint reconstruction preventing spurious congruence solutions.
Traced interval subdivision completeness and the direct-scan cap concept.
Traced the paired LLL primal/dual length bound using size-reduction and Gram–Schmidt inequalities.
Checked the conditional EC counting exponent X^{5N−6}/M^{N−2} and limit (N−2)/(5N−6)→1/5, given its pole-count claims.
remaining: Audit all target-dual tail bounds, integer interval complexity and MIHNP/HNPHM parameter arithmetic.
Verify elliptic-curve identities, anchor pole counts and acceptance-conditioning probability.
Trace uniqueness and reconstruction expected-time guarantees under each exact sampling model.

papers.title: Fast Provable Algorithms for Approximate CVP and Exact SVP on Random \(q\)-ary Lattices
papers.authors: Jiseung Kim, Junhyuk Kwon, Changmin Lee, JeongHwan Lee

review.title: Fast Provable Algorithms for Approximate CVP and Exact SVP on Random \(q\)-ary Lattices
review.authors: Jiseung Kim, Junhyuk Kwon, Changmin Lee, JeongHwan Lee
review.summary: For random q-ary Euclidean lattices with density δ=m log2(q)/n≤1, gives 5/3-CVP in time 2^(0.2668n+o(n)) and exact SVP in 2^(0.2741n+o(n)); for 1<δ≤1.5, exponents are 0.56 and 0.468. For all but 2^−Ω(n^(2/3)) matrices, CVP succeeds simultaneously for every rational target under a common random tape. Includes an original-GPV parameter-regime forgery application.
review.prior_frontier: Compares with general-lattice exact SVP exponent 0.5, exact CVP exponent 1, and heuristic sieving exponent 0.2925. These are distribution-restricted results, not worst-case lattice breakthroughs or an attack on all current lattice signatures. External prior exponents not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Substantial provable exponential improvements for a cryptographically central random lattice distribution, including target choices depending on the matrix.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines representation-based modular searches with a symmetrized finite-group amplification that upgrades average to every right-hand side and controls the conditional output mean.
score_reasons.depth: The 117-page argument must handle composite moduli, dependent shortest vectors, exact ball enumeration, list cutoffs and rigorously certified exponent optimization.
score_reasons.exposition: Quantifier and density qualifications are explicit, but the large analytic and numerical appendix makes the headline constants costly to verify.

checked: Traced Lemma 4.4: sign symmetrization makes the unconditional mean zero; ±1 determinants give pairwise-uniform finite-group shifts; two Markov steps and independent added columns control every right-hand side.
Checked the correction-vector averaging inequality and why a simultaneous event for finitely many congruence values covers every rational target, including adaptive choices of target.
remaining: Large-proof exception:117 pages. The exact simultaneous all-target modular-correction argument was traced, including sign symmetry, determinant-based pairwise uniformity and the two Markov steps. This does not verify the lattice algorithm, conditioning and numerical exponent certificates end to end.

Audit recursive representation-search inclusion bounds with full matrix conditioning, composite-modulus collisions, exact-search cost, shortest-vector dependence and all certified exponent tables; GPV parameter/security application not independently checked.

papers.authors: Yuval Efron, Jovan Komatovic, Ling Ren

review.title: Byzantine Broadcast in $\widetilde{O}(n^2)$ Communication
review.authors: Yuval Efron, Jovan Komatovic, Ling Ren
review.summary: Deterministic synchronous authenticated single-bit Byzantine broadcast tolerating any t<n adaptive corruptions with O(n² log⁴n·λ) communication by correct parties and O(t) rounds, using a PKI, signatures and binding vector commitments with λ>log n. Cryptographic primitives are idealized; this is not unauthenticated broadcast or a long-message amortization theorem.
review.prior_frontier: Dolev–Strong gives optimal resilience and O(t) rounds but cubic signature-bit cost; the manuscript claims the first near-quadratic communication at this resilience. Prior protocol and lower-bound sources not independently traced.

score_reasons.significance: Near-quadratic authenticated broadcast with an arbitrary dishonest majority resolves a fundamental communication gap.
score_reasons.novelty: An efficient signature-retrieval primitive combines adaptive demand scaling, sparse consistency graphs and a splitting protocol.
score_reasons.depth: The communication argument must charge honest senders even against a dishonest receiver that equivocates.
score_reasons.exposition: Compact explicit pseudocode and separately stated safety, delivery and cost invariants.

checked: Checked the sparse comparison-graph cut property and its probabilistic construction in the overview.

Traced Claim 15: binding bounds each common-request group by 2n/c; comparison edges prohibit two large disjoint unions, forcing fewer than 3n/c surviving honest senders. Charging the previous scale controls even senders rejected in the current scale.

Traced Claims 16–19 completely: sorting by claimed left counts maintains enough unclaimed values per group, yields distinct leaves outside the receiver’s known set, preserves honest senders, and uses O(log²n) bits per virtual sender.

Completed the broadcast/retrieval composition (PDF pp.7–14). Checked why a correct member of an unconvinced receiver's sender set has M_i signatures, why no correct party is permanently blamed, and why acceptance propagates within one epoch. The final t+1-signature test has a correct signer; the early certificate case uses fewer than E simultaneous correct senders and only two adjacent certificate steps.

Traced Ladder progress and charging: at each completed scale either the surviving sender count quarters or the receiver acquires at least c times that count. With x_s=2^s|P_s|, x_{s+1}<=x_s/2+2a_s implies sum x_s<=2|P|+4|V\A|. This controls malicious withholding, the partial final scale and the receiver's total cost across epochs. Verified last-scale resolution, honest-sender numerical checks, all Bisect pseudocode invariants, and the comparison-graph sender charging. Summing over two bits/two sender epochs yields the stated O(n^2 log^4 n lambda) correct-party communication.

Checked the model qualifications: ideal valid signatures and valid commitment openings, synchronous authenticated channels, communication only of parties remaining correct, and unrestricted deterministic local preprocessing for the existential comparison graphs. Adaptively corrupted parties are part of the global faulty set in the proof. The power-of-two n assumption is explicit; the round count is more precisely O(t+1), including t=0.
remaining: No substantive issue found in the central protocol proof for its stated ideal-primitive model. Concrete computational-security composition and efficient construction of comparison graphs are not claimed by this audit. The manuscript states that arbitrary n can be handled by modifying constants; its alternative padding-with-crashes explanation alone need not preserve O(t) for very small t, so the reviewed pseudocode scope is power-of-two n. Historical lower bounds were not independently reproved.
