review.title: A Proof of the Most Informative Boolean Function Conjecture
review.authors: Zijie Chen, Amin Gohari, Adel Javanmard, Honghao Lin, Vahab Mirrokni, Chandra Nair, David Woodruff

score_reasons.significance: A resolution of a major longstanding information-theoretic conjecture.
score_reasons.novelty: Hybrid balanced/entropy-deficit potentials and new global lower bounds address the previously failing boundary regimes.
score_reasons.depth: A large analytic and computer-assisted proof with a substantial accompanying formalization.
score_reasons.exposition: The short main development explains the architecture well; the 276-page proof and large certificate system remain difficult to independently reproduce.

checked: Verified the cube induction, entropy-production normalization and differential-inequality deduction of the final information bound, conditional on the local Bellman theorem.
Traced the mean-centered entropy-deficit bound, parent-branch maximum argument and stated coverage of same-side/opposite-side mean regimes.

Inspected the public Lean statement: finite uniform cube, independent BSC kernel, Shannon mutual information and all p in [0,1]. The final build target checks theorem type and standard axioms; this inspection is not a build.
Read the formalization's manuscript-deviation log, including replacement certificates and independently re-proved regional obligations.
remaining: Large-proof exception: did not independently verify every analytic regional inequality or replay all interval certificates.
Did not build or kernel-replay the 45,500-module Lean project. Its repository reports roughly 1,200 CPU-hours and about 300 GB for a full build.
Reported build results and axiom checks are author-provided evidence, not a verification performed in this review.

sources.detail: Formalization repository and stated resource requirements; not independently built.

review.summary: Claims a computer-assisted proof of the full Courtade–Kumar most-informative Boolean function conjecture: I(g(X);Y) <= 1-H_2(p), in every dimension for every Boolean function and crossover probability. A hybrid Bellman inequality handles biased functions, with analytic boundary arguments and certified compact-region inequalities.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves the full conjecture beyond previous partial regimes if the complete analytic/certificate chain is valid. The paper explicitly repairs a false earlier sufficient Bellman comparison rather than assuming it.
review.recommendation: Exceptional-result candidate with an explicit large-proof audit limitation; no claim of independent end-to-end formal verification.

review.title: A Deterministic O(log m)-Competitive Algorithm for Online Minimum Cost Bipartite Matching with Delays
review.authors: Tung-Wei Kuo
review.area: Online algorithms; bipartite matching with delays
review.summary: Proves the existing deterministic VRM algorithm is O(log m)-competitive in every metric for online bipartite matching with delays, without knowing the metric or m: at γ=2 the bound is 24+18 ln m. A non-bipartite extension gives 28+24 ln m using minimum-weight matching to implement augmenting paths.
review.prior_frontier: Prior deterministic general-metric bipartite bound cited as O(m^{0.59}); logarithmic non-bipartite performance is concurrent with #482. This paper closes the bipartite case left outside that framework.

score_reasons.significance: A polynomial-to-logarithmic deterministic improvement for the general-metric bipartite problem is major.
score_reasons.novelty: The key new analysis charges waiting continuously to a fixed optimum rather than charging geometric augmentation scales.
score_reasons.depth: A compact but effective combination of time-augmented metric, alternating-path ages and harmonic integration; non-bipartite implementation needs a careful cycle invariant.
score_reasons.exposition: All central steps and constants are exposed in a short chain of lemmas.

checked: Traced the complete bipartite algorithm and stable-time invariant; finite event count and eventual matching hold after the last arrival.
Independently checked OPT equals minimum matching cost in the time-augmented metric by matching each offline pair at its later arrival.
Traced the augmenting-length telescope and ALG≤(2+2γ/(γ−1))WR.
Traced edge-disjoint optimal paths, unarrived-terminal charges and the D*≥age(v)/(γ+1) inequality.

Checked the harmonic charge envelope min(1,(γ+1)D(e)/(t−b_e)), finite support, integration and 24+18 ln m constant. If OPT=0, the stable-time age inequality precludes any positive waiting; no division is needed.
Traced Appendix A shortest-distance dual potentials proving no negative cycles after augmentations.
Traced the non-bipartite perfect-matching reduction and negative-cycle invariant edge by edge, the doubled charging rate and 28+24 ln m constant.
remaining: No numerical implementation or formal verification performed.
Historical competitive-ratio baselines and identity with the earlier named VRM algorithm were not independently checked; the paper defines a self-contained algorithm analyzed here.

papers.title: Second-Best Trade Is Half Efficient in Multidimensional Markets
papers.authors: Dirk Bergemann, Yang Cai, Kangning Wang, Jinzhao Wu, Renzhe Xu

review.title: Second-Best Trade Is Half Efficient in Multidimensional Markets
review.authors: Dirk Bergemann, Yang Cai, Kangning Wang, Jinzhao Wu, Renzhe Xu
review.area: Algorithmic mechanism design; gains from trade
review.summary: For finite-support additive multidimensional buyers and sellers with independent agents but arbitrary within-agent correlation and arbitrary downward-closed trade feasibility, proves existence of a Bayesian-IC, interim-IR, reportwise strongly budget-balanced mechanism attaining at least half of first-best gains from trade.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the tight bilateral and concurrent single-dimensional half guarantees to coupled multidimensional feasibility. It is an existence theorem, not an efficient mechanism construction or a dominant-strategy/ex-post-IR guarantee. Prior tightness source not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A sharp universal guarantee in a broad multidimensional two-sided market class where optimal mechanisms lack a structural characterization.
score_reasons.novelty: Bounds every feasible mechanism-design dual through stopped Markov chains and antithetic clocks, rather than constructing a particular dual/mechanism.
score_reasons.depth: The key step preserves only one density factor per market side using downward-closed allocation thinning, coupled to strong duality and payment normalization.
score_reasons.exposition: States the incentive, support, correlation and budget-balance distinctions clearly and presents a compact probabilistic overview.

checked: Checked the recovery resolvent identity and prior-density differential inequality in the proof overview.
Traced Lemma 7.1 exactly: the acceptance coin has mean 1/K and is independent of the terminal type, thinning preserves feasibility and loses one factor per side irrespective of the number of agents.
Checked the final reduction from the dual objective and antithetic exponential-clock moment to the half guarantee.

Traced the complete main half-efficiency proof and appendices A.1–A.3: finite feasible bounded LP, signed-to-nonnegative transfer normalization, common-pool reportwise strong budget balance, and exact partial-Lagrangian coefficients/attainment.

Checked the payment normalization edge cases: minimum buyer utility plus each reported payment is nonnegative by incentive compatibility and nonnegative true values; seller receipts minus minimum utility remain nonnegative; rebating surplus to one seller preserves incentives and participation; the zero-total pool has identically zero payments.

Recomputed the Markov generator and flow direction: off-diagonal rate alpha(vprime,v)/((1+tau)f(v)), fA=(tau f-alpha(v,bottom))/(1+tau), hence f exp(tA)<=exp(kappa t)f. The exponential resolvent recovers every coordinate of each full type.

Checked convexity of maximum feasible surplus, conditioning on shared clocks, the exact thinning coin independence from the terminal profile, downward-closed feasibility, and sequential loss of one density factor per market side rather than per agent.

Checked the antithetic exponential clocks and beta-integral bound pointwise: u^(-k)(1-u)^(-k)<u^(-k)+(1-u)^(-k) for 0<=k<1; integral <2/(1-k). Thus every finite useful dual is at least half first best and attained LP duality proves the stated mechanism existence.
remaining: The established external bilateral-trade tightness example attributed to Liu–Qin–Ren–Wang Theorem 6.2 was not independently re-proved; main-proof-checked covers the new half-efficiency theorem, not that external lower bound.
The theorem is for finite type supports, independence across agents, additive nonnegative values/costs, BIC and interim IR; no polynomial-time construction or ex-post IR claim is inferred.

papers.title: Optimal $e^{(\gamma+o(1))n}$-Approximation of the Permanent of Positive Semidefinite Matrices
papers.authors: Nima Anari, Farzam Ebrahimnejad

review.title: Optimal $e^{(\gamma+o(1))n}$-Approximation of the Permanent of Positive Semidefinite Matrices
review.authors: Nima Anari, Farzam Ebrahimnejad
review.summary: For rational Hermitian positive-semidefinite A, gives a deterministic polynomial-time exp((γ+ε)n)-approximation to per(A), where γ is Euler’s constant and ε>0. The exact real-arithmetic relaxation satisfies exp(−γn) exp Φ(A)≤per(A)≤exp Φ(A), with Φ maximizing Σlog(vᵢ†Xvᵢ)+log det X−tr X+d over positive-definite X for A=VV†. Entries may be complex; no entrywise nonnegativity assumption.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript improves exp((γ+0.9999)n)-type approximation to the exp((γ+o(1))n) threshold and cites hardness below exp((γ−ε)n); hardness source not independently traced.

score_reasons.significance: Closes the leading exponential constant for approximating PSD permanents, subject to the cited hardness.
score_reasons.novelty: Entropy-corrected covariance optimization removes an entire exp(n)-scale loss.
score_reasons.depth: A short but substantive synthesis of the Gaussian Wick identity, Gibbs variational formula and maximum entropy; numerical implementation deserves separate scrutiny.
score_reasons.exposition: The central sandwich has a particularly transparent, modular proof and separates exact and finite-precision formulations.

checked: Traced the main exact sandwich: per(A) is a Gaussian product moment; arbitrary trial distributions are upper-bounded using Jensen and the complex-Gaussian maximum-entropy bound at their second moment; a CN(0,X) trial loses exactly γ per linear form.
Checked finiteness, positive second-moment matrix, the covariance/pseudocovariance entropy argument and existence of an interior maximizer.
Verified stationary normalization tr X*=n+d; the same first-order equation also gives X*≥I. Zero diagonal is handled separately.
Checked that an additive εn/2 underestimate of Φ, exponentiated after adding εn/2, yields the stated one-sided approximation sandwich.

Rechecked Theorems7–9 and resolved the weak-optimization concern using the stationarity identity: X*>=I and tr X*=n+d, so one can optimize on tr X=n+d, I/2<=X<=2nI. After normalizing nonzero rows of V, the objective gradient has polynomial norm (at most 2n+3 in operator norm) throughout this body, and each quadratic form is bounded below by 1/2. A relative row-factor error eta therefore changes each logarithm by O(n eta), uniformly on the body; polynomially many bits, depending on log(1/epsilon), suffice. Rational LDL factorization followed by sufficiently accurate square roots supplies such a factor, avoiding unstable rank decisions by numerical threshold alone. The manuscript gives standard weak-optimization references rather than these explicit constants, but this check finds no substantive finite-precision obstruction.

Checked the cited hardness statement in primary ENOG24 arXiv:2404.10959 Theorem1.2: every fixed positive epsilon, Hermitian PSD matrices, NP-hardness within exp((gamma-epsilon)n). It matches the class and one-sided approximation convention; deterministic optimality uses P!=NP.
remaining: No unresolved central proof issue found. The review traced the new entropic sandwich and the algorithmic precision reduction; it uses standard polynomial-time weak convex optimization and rational linear algebra as established results. The previous hardness proof itself was not reproved.

review.authors: Prabhanjan Ananth, Seyoon Ragavan, Amit Sahai

score_reasons.significance: Removes a central efficiency/security limitation of a foundational unclonable primitive.
score_reasons.novelty: Pauli spectral balance and an agreement-sensitive operator filter yield a sharp simple construction.
score_reasons.depth: The security proof combines noncommutative norm bounds and a Schur-complement argument.
score_reasons.exposition: A particularly transparent proof, explicit efficient implementation and two routes to the key norm estimate.

checked: Checked perfect correctness and uniform parity-constrained eigenstate preparation with local Cliffords.
Re-derived the Choi-state expression for joint guessing success, including transpose and normalization factors.
Verified the Pauli symplectic character norm and block-factorization product bound ||E_B E_C|| <= d/(d^2-1).
Checked operator order in the inserted agreement powers, convergence and normalization of the resolvent filter series.
Verified the positivity proof for +/- (E_B-E_C) <= D, the Schur-complement quadratic sandwich and the top-eigenvector cancellation giving t^2 <= ||E_B F E_C||.
Combined the estimates to recover exactly 1/2 + (1/2)sqrt(2^n/(4^n-1)). No gap found in the main theorem.

Checked the primary Broadbent–Culf–Rochette lower-bound statement, Corollary 22 in the fetched arXiv version, giving Omega(d^(-1/2)) advantage for perfectly correct ciphertext dimension d. The manuscript uses different version numbering.
remaining: No formal Lean execution was performed; the mathematical central proof was checked directly.
qsiO application reductions and the separate alternative conditional-overlap proof were not fully audited.

sources.detail: Primary lower-bound statement, fetched version Corollary 22.

review.summary: Constructs efficient one-time private-key unclonable encryption of a single bit with perfect correctness and optimal-order information-theoretic advantage O(2^(-n/2)). Encrypts as a random eigenstate of a nonidentity n-qubit Pauli; encryption uses local Cliffords and decryption local Pauli measurements.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier unconditional constructions sacrificed either efficient operations or negligible advantage. This merged construction achieves both and matches the known dimension-dependent lower-bound order. Applications to copy protection still require qsiO and one-way-function assumptions; this is not unconditional public-key or reusable encryption.
review.recommendation: Strong acceptance candidate; central construction and security proof checked, pending global ranking.

papers.authors: Seyoon Ragavan, Noah Shutty

review.title: Quantum Algorithms for OPI Variants Beyond Locality and Classical Decodability
review.authors: Seyoon Ragavan, Noah Shutty
review.summary: Extends Regev/DQI code-intersection algorithms in two directions: quantum decoding based on a small Schur square finds full-support kernel vectors when dist(C⊥)log_q(q−1)≥2n+s₂+2; a classical algorithm requires the stronger cubic-product condition dist(C⊥)≥n+s₃. Separately, histogram constraints yield quantum algorithms and random-oracle separations. Prime-field Reed–Muller intermediate regimes are candidates for advantage, not established plain-model separations.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier non-dequantized applications used efficient classical decoders and product constraints. The formerly proposed random-matrix m≈n² advantage is acknowledged as classically matched; the new structured quantum regime has m≤n^{2−Ω(1)}.

score_reasons.significance: Broadens a significant quantum-algorithm paradigm beyond two major restrictions.
score_reasons.novelty: Quantum unambiguous symbol measurements plus Schur-square relinearization, and stability-based Fourier analysis for global histograms, are distinctive contributions.
score_reasons.depth: Combines coding product spaces, coherent decoding, quantitative reduction errors and occupancy local-limit analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: The distinction between candidate advantage, classical competitors and proved oracle separation is clear.

checked: Traced Lemma 7.3 linear relaxation and the union bound over Δv and shortened-square Δw: each nonzero coordinate contributes at most 1/(q−1).
Checked the extra |C⊥| factor in the Regev reduction is reflected in the condition 2n+s₂, rather than n+s₂.
Read coherent implementation and precision scaling: exponentially small operator error needs only polynomial logarithmic precision.
Verified extension fields have an additional classical route and are not claimed as the central advantage candidate.
remaining: Audit quantum decoding reduction and unambiguous-state implementation in full.
Trace Reed–Muller puncturing/distance parameters, classical cubic-product algorithm and histogram stability.
Audit random-oracle hardness and its exact oracle model.

review.title: Catalytic Tree Evaluation from Matching Vectors
review.authors: Alexandra Henzinger, Edward Pyne, Seyoon Ragavan
review.summary: For every fixed ε>0, solves TreeEval in O(log n) free space, 2^O((log n)^ε) catalytic space and polynomial time. A generic matching-vector/decoder construction gives additional tradeoffs and a multitape-time-T simulation using O(√T) free space, 2^O(T^ε) catalytic space and 2^O(√T) time.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the previous polynomial catalytic tape at logarithmic free space; does not put TreeEval in ordinary logspace or remove the catalytic tape from the time-space simulation. Small-dimension matching-vector implications are explicitly conditional. Prior algorithm bounds not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Subpolynomial catalytic memory suffices for a central tree-evaluation problem with polynomial time and logarithmic clean workspace.
score_reasons.novelty: Connects matching-vector PIR and decoding identities to masked register computation, exposing vector dimension and decoder sparsity as separate resources.
score_reasons.depth: Must preserve arbitrary tape contents exactly while recursively recycling scratch space; composite-modulus decoders and uniform matching-vector generation are essential.
score_reasons.exposition: The positional-register oracle interface is unusually precise, and the comparison table distinguishes ordinary and catalytic space.

checked: Traced the four-query inner-product extraction with register swaps and exact inverse updates.
Verified the one-level decoder cancellation: the score sum vanishes only for the two correct labels, all wrong candidates cancel for arbitrary masked contents, and the true candidate contributes one.
Checked the retained-state accounting across recursive oracle calls and the distinction between temporary scratch and per-depth state.
remaining: Large-proof exception:42-page recursive catalytic construction with nontrivial matching-vector dependencies. The central arbitrary-content mask cancellation, reversible inner-product extraction and retained-state accounting were traced; complete recursive restoration, uniform decoder construction and final parameter chain remain unverified.

Verify the complete recursive readout/restoration, tape-to-ring representation, uniform composite matching-vector/decoder constructions, parameter substitutions and external time-to-TreeEval reduction.

papers.title: Good Quantum Locally Testable Codes from Lossless Cubical Complexes
papers.authors: Itay Cohen, Itai Leigh, Assaf Reiner, Amnon Ta-Shma, Elad Tzalik

review.title: Good Quantum Locally Testable Codes from Lossless Cubical Complexes
review.authors: Itay Cohen, Itai Leigh, Assaf Reiner, Amnon Ta-Shma, Elad Tzalik
review.summary: A conditional construction: sufficiently imbalanced four-dimensional decorated cubical complexes whose directional graphs are two-sided lossless yield quantum LDPC codes with constant rate, relative distance and local-testability soundness. Such complexes are not constructed. The main unconditional implication is a local-to-global theorem for robust small-set coboundary expansion of Boolean-level complexes in arbitrary dimension; there are no nontrivial local component codes.
review.prior_frontier: Generalizes the two-dimensional lossless approach of Lin–Hsieh. The manuscript distinguishes concurrent spectral/local-code qLTC constructions from its conditional geometric route; those sources not independently audited here.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a structural route to good qLTCs and a dimension-independent expansion theorem, with the missing input construction clearly substantial.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses cochains on Boolean-cube level vertices and decomposes terminal-link overlap into same-type collisions and light squares.
score_reasons.depth: Controlling cancellation in higher dimensions and proving robust local-to-global expansion are nontrivial new ingredients.
score_reasons.exposition: The abstract states conditionality clearly, and the proof separates link expansion, excess propagation and coding consequences.

checked: Read the precise qLTC hypothesis: X and its reversal satisfy the expansion theorem; stretch factors μ1,μ2≥4 and μ3,μ4≤1/4. Checked bounded check and qubit degrees from directional degrees.

Traced recursive excess Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 4.4: different-type heavy children with a heavy square completion share a terminal; all other extra terminals are charged to same-type or light-square terms, then normalized double counting propagates excess.
The paper explicitly says its natural Ramanujan-bigraph candidate is not two-sided lossless; no unconditional existence claim is credited.
remaining: Full link expansion, quantitative same-type/light-square bounds, parameter choices, code dimension/distance/soundness, and linear-time decoding proof remain unaudited.
Existence of the requisite lossless cubical complexes remains an open hypothesis, not a verified component.

score_reasons.significance: A complete classification connecting stability to two classical CSP properties.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses critical obstructions and coupling-sensitive approximation reductions.
score_reasons.depth: Requires both structural/algebraic classification and stable rounding arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: The separate computational and information-theoretic claims are clearly stated.

checked: Verified the disagreement-component splicing lemma for two single-constraint deletions.
Checked Wasserstein triangle inequalities through double-deletion instances and the cubic path-distance sum producing linear sensitivity.
remaining: Audit the large-diameter critical-obstruction construction and classification imports.
Check both approximate-solving directions, stable Horn/bijunctive algorithms and affine reductions.

review.summary: Classifies every finite Boolean CSP language by stability under deletion of a random constraint. Exact solving has constant average sensitivity exactly for finite-duality languages, otherwise linear; approximate solving has O(epsilon^(-1) log n) sensitivity exactly for bounded-width languages, otherwise linear for some constant error.

review.summary: For finite-horizon two-player uninformed Markov games with unknown fixed transitions/losses and unobserved opponent actions, achieves high-probability empirical Nash-value regret soft-O(H^{3/2}S√(AK)) against arbitrary adaptively chosen episode-wise Markov opponent policies. The opponent can see the learner’s committed policy but not future randomness. Computationally inefficient: the candidate value grid is exponential in the state count. This is not general external regret; the benchmark agrees with it only for a fixed opponent.
review.prior_frontier: Prior worst-case empirical Nash-value regret was soft-O(K^{2/3}); √K was known under restricted nonstationarity. K and A dependence is optimal up to logs, but H/S gaps remain. Prior sources not independently traced.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the statistical √K rate question under a useful hidden-opponent feedback model.
score_reasons.novelty: Coordinates global candidate weighting with state-dependent policy mixing through a robust drift–cost optimization.

score_reasons.exposition: Clearly defines the stronger empirical Nash benchmark and admits exponential computation rather than implying an efficient learner.

checked: Traced Lemma B.5: Bellman minimization over capped distributions; a minimum weighted candidate pool is feasible because c≥2λ and λ≤1/(2S); optimizing over pools bounds the positive residual mass by c per state, leading to cS total drift plus cost.
Checked Lemma B.6’s bandit substitution: for a normalized pool, quadratic-over-mixture costs collapse to at most 2λ(A+1)/pool mass, including zero-probability action convention.
Read the exponential value grid and the exact empirical benchmark based on per-state maxima over the realized opponent policies.
remaining: OMD stability, implicit-exploration high-probability bounds, comparator discretization, final regret arithmetic and the old-method lower bound remain unaudited.
Conic finite-precision computational estimates and the cited MDP lower bound are not independently verified.

The two-round protocol does not itself have a runtime bound, and fixed-distribution protocols leave communication/runtime unrestricted. Prior work not independently checked.

score_reasons.novelty: Uses joint priors over hypotheses and pointwise noise profiles, not a fixed noise model, and turns minimax distinguishability into a common verifier test.
score_reasons.depth: Requires empirical distribution transfer, stochastic-label rerandomization, bounded-space implementation and distinct class-specific lower bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully separates labeled/unlabeled resources and protocol rounds/runtime, though the accuracy-level dimension changes require attention.

papers.title: Combinatorial limitations of list-decoding Reed-Solomon codes
papers.authors: Omar Alrabiah, Rohan Goyal, Venkatesan Guruswami

review.title: Combinatorial limitations of list-decoding Reed-Solomon codes
review.authors: Omar Alrabiah, Rohan Goyal, Venkatesan Guruswami
review.area: Coding theory and Reed–Solomon list decoding
review.summary: For full-length RS codes over F_{q^{4t}}, rates q^{-2} and (1−q^{-1})² admit n^{Ω_q(log n)} lists at radius 1−√R+O_q(n^{-1/4}). Over infinitely many prime fields, explicit words have n nearby codewords at constant rate about 2/(3m) and radius about 1−1/m for m≡2 mod3; amplification gives arbitrary fixed polynomial list sizes at rate Θ(1/ℓ), constant gap Ω(1/ℓ²) below capacity. Thus prime-field constant-list capacity conjectures fail, while polynomial-list capacity remains compatible.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier extension-field superpolynomial examples had vanishing rate; prime-field polynomial-list examples had vanishing gap. The manuscript also distinguishes concurrent characteristic-two low-rate results. Prior and concurrent sources not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Sharp combinatorial barriers at constant rates substantially constrain universal RS decoding and refute a prime-field constant-list conjecture.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses proper quadratic forms for the Johnson-radius barrier and low-degree images of multiplicative subgroups for the prime-field barrier.
score_reasons.depth: The prime-field coefficient and moment construction is elegant; extension-field families and list amplification are deeper additional components.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise field, rate and list-size distinctions prevent conflating the two negative results.

checked: Traced prime-field coefficient cancellation: invariance under subgroup scaling forces weighted coefficient monomials to have degree divisible by subgroup size, eliminating the highest t/d coefficients.
Verified shifted cubes f_a(x)=(x+a)³−a³ are permutations when p≡2 mod3; the (t+1)/3 moment of f_a(H) recovers a, hence gives p distinct error polynomials and exact n−t disagreements.
Checked dimension k=2(t+1)/3 and the compatible prime congruences in Theorem 1.2; read amplification via products and the expected pairwise-overlap bound from a quadratic equation in the shift.

Traced the complete extension-field construction (pp9–17): polarization and the degree<2n/q identity Q^q−Q=(X^n−X)L_Q; translation invariance forces the quotient constant, then its linear coefficient forces zero. Properness and complete splitting identify all level-set multiplicities, including zeros shared by Q/L_Q.

Checked Lemma3.8 in both characteristics: the norm-trace quadratic has nondegenerate polar form; prescribed isotropic U has a unique monic degree-q^t linearized P with image U^perp. Kernel(P)=q^t and P^{-1}(U)=q^{2t} force full splitting and exact degree q^{3t} of L_Q. Counted zero vectors in successive orthogonal complements and divided by possible kernels to obtain at least q^{t²}/2 distinct forms.

Checked both rate constructions and collision multiplicity: low-rate codeword determines Q up to F_q^*, high-rate disagreement level set Q=1 fixes its normalization. The error quotients are polynomials, degree cancellations give the exact strict RS degree bounds, and root counts give the stated O_q(n^{-1/4}) excess over Johnson.

Completed prime-field amplification pp18–21: the pair-overlap equation has at most two shifts because the subgroup element is nonzero; expectation at most t/12 and Markov retain half the subsets with overlap at most t/6. Degree K=(ell−1)t+2(t+1)/3 leaves a Theta(t) agreement surplus, yielding Theta(1/ell) rate and Omega(1/ell²) capacity gap.

Checked higher-moment injectivity: the coefficient at X^t is C_r a^{3r+1}; clearing denominators produces an integer M_r congruent to (−1)^{3r+1} modulo m, so nonzero for all sufficiently large admissible primes. Vandermonde on the distinct cubes recovers the symmetric difference except possibly zero; equal set cardinalities remove that exception. Dirichlet congruences are coprime. Minor displayed congruence/averaging shorthand does not change these derived inequalities.
remaining: All central new constructions and counting arguments checked. Historical/concurrent comparison and exact wording of externally cited conjectures have not been independently verified; the result is a combinatorial limitation for specified full-length fields, not a refutation of polynomial-list capacity in general.

score_reasons.significance: An algorithmic capacity theorem for Reed–Solomon codes would be a major coding-theory advance.
score_reasons.novelty: A constrained derivative interpolation space and multiplicity constraints provide the central new route.

checked: Checked local substitution: the error polynomial has T-adic order d, and the coefficient constraints force every interpolated summand to have order at least m.
Checked the interpolant's degree-after-substitution bound and the basic monomial-space construction.

Completed the central interpolation audit. Hasse inversion makes E_P have T-adic order d; weighted local coefficient annihilation therefore gives multiplicity m at each agreement. The global weighted-degree cutoff is strictly below mA, so A agreeing points force the differential polynomial to vanish identically.

Checked the local-rank improvement: after Y0=y+TU, all monomials lie in V with U-degree≤T-degree and weighted derivative degree≤W+T-degree. The kernel spaces T^r E^{h_r}U^aY1^bY^c stay inside V modulo T^m. Their lowest T-coefficients are (U−Y1)^{h_r} times nonzero polynomials, which proves both the stated dimension and independence across r. The rank-nullity sum is at most m³/d times Lambda(W+m).

Checked weighted-simplex volume bounds and the centroid/Markov lower bound on the cardinality of the truncated lattice set B. Independently made the O_theta(1) step explicit: with L=log(ed), C=1+theta/2 and d≥3, (d−1)(d³+binom(d,2))/floor(Cd⁴/L)≤L/C. Thus the additive logarithmic term is at most log((4+3theta)/theta)+1; condition(21) makes it smaller than theta(1−theta)log(d)/18.

Checked the exponent comparison 2/(2+theta)+theta(1−theta)/18 < (5−theta)/(5+theta), and hence local rank<|B|m³ d^{−2theta/(5+theta)}. The interpolation-dimension lower bound beats n times this quantity under the displayed epsilon restriction.

Resolved two omitted rounding/reduction details without changing the algorithm: the true ratio A/(k−1)≥1/(1−theta) supplies an extra theta²m/(1−theta)>1 that absorbs the ceiling in |c|. For k below floor((1−theta)epsilon n), the interpolation space for that maximal dimension is contained in the actual lower-k space; all local constraints are identical. Thus proving existence at maximal k extends to the claimed smaller k, despite the proof abruptly assuming equality.

Verified the primary Kopparty2015 Theorem4.3 in Theory of Computing11(5), p160: for prime q, degree bound k−1<q makes its floor((k−1)/q) term zero, degree-per-Y below q and weighted degree below q² yield at most q^{4d+6} roots in q^{O(d+1)} time. Checked the stated field bound implies both degree hypotheses, including the harmless ceiling slack for d and A.

Checked enumeration of interpolation monomials and linear constraints in q^{O(epsilon^{−12/theta})}. Checked the all-rate reduction: enlarge message degree only by a parameter-dependent constant, pad the evaluation set and received word to N≈k/((1−theta)eta), retain at least the original agreement count, apply the low-rate algorithm, and prune by original degree/agreement. For bounded exceptional n exhaustive enumeration has constant parameter-dependent exponent.
remaining: The external nonlinear differential-equation solver was verified in its primary theorem statement and exact prime-field specialization, not re-proved. Historical priority and separate cryptographic/proximity-gap applications are not part of this audit.

The verified result retains prime characteristic, arbitrary distinct evaluation points, the sufficiently large linear-in-blocklength field requirement at fixed rate/slack, and runtime polynomial in q with parameter-dependent exponent. It is not polynomial in log q and is not an extension-field theorem.
resolved_notes: The dimension-count proof writes a floor where B was defined with a ceiling. The stronger unused rate slack absorbs the extra1 as detailed in the audit; this is an editorial proof gap with a direct repair.

The interpolation proof abruptly sets k=floor((1−theta)epsilon n) although the statement permits smaller k. The monotonic containment of the maximal-k interpolation space in the actual space repairs this missing reduction.

sources.detail: Primary nonlinear differential-equation solver, exact prime-field hypotheses and cardinality/runtime bounds verified

review.summary: Gives polynomial-time list decoding of Reed–Solomon codes up to capacity over prime fields with arbitrary evaluation points and sufficiently large linear-in-blocklength field size. The low-rate derivative-interpolation theorem combines with a rate reduction to obtain constant-rate guarantees.
review.prior_frontier: Addresses the longstanding algorithmic capacity barrier for ordinary Reed–Solomon codes. Runtime is polynomial in q for fixed accuracy/rate parameters, not polynomial in log q; prime-field and field-size hypotheses must be retained.

Traced the new support lemma: setting variables outside a monomial support to zero inserts rank-one dead-layer projectors; two dead layers factor the cyclic trace, so a log-partition monomial spanning layers0,k needs degree>=min(k,M-k)+1.

Checked the reflected-log combination, Borel–Carathéodory modulus estimate and maximum-modulus argument giving(128 Cstar/(epsilon*h)) exp(-epsilon*h*dk), conditional on the finite-Trotter multivariate zero-free theorem.

review.title: Hitting sets From Derivations: Waring Rank and Noncommutative ABPs
review.authors: Shubham Bhardwaj, Foram Lakhani, Partha Mukhopadhyay, Ramprasad Saptharishi, Pratik Shastri, Amit Kumar Sinhababu

score_reasons.significance: Polynomial hitting sets for these algebraic models are a major advance.
score_reasons.novelty: Distinct-pole derivations and a controlled Wronskian give an unusually concrete generator.
score_reasons.depth: The argument connects differential algebra, derivative-closed spaces, and finite matrix realizations.
score_reasons.exposition: Elementary self-contained lemmas make the core mechanism unusually accessible; AI provenance is disclosed and does not substitute for mathematical evidence.

checked: Verified the distinct-simple-pole obstruction to nonconstant derivation constants in the commutative polynomial ring.
Checked x-independence of the derivative-closed Wronskian by triangular column differentiation, its unitriangular translation factorization, and the O(nr squared) rational degree bound.

Completed both main proofs in Sections2–5. The injectivity argument normalizes a highest-degree coefficient and applies the intertwining operator; minimal degree/number of top words forces a constant, contradicting a nonzero kernel element. The proof uses only linearity and the intertwining identity, so also works for the non-Leibniz left-derivative operator.

Checked the pole argument coefficientwise in arbitrary characteristic-zero fields: rational derivatives have zero residue at each distinct rational pole, forcing the top homogeneous partials or word coefficients to vanish. No analytic logarithm branch is needed.

Checked the commutative Wronskian denominator Q^m and numerator degree m(n−1), giving determinant numerator/denominator degree≤nr². Injectivity plus the ordinary characteristic-zero Wronskian criterion gives nonzero determinant. Vanishing order B=nr²+r would force its last column, hence numerator, to have order at least nr²+1, a contradiction.

Checked the ncABP factorization independently: F=I+M+...+M^d, left derivative partial_i F=M_iF, and rows R_{m+1}=R_m'+R_m sum_i b_i M_i. Applying the F(t)-linear map Psi entrywise is legitimate because R has scalar entries; Psi(F) remains unitriangular, so its determinant is1. Minimal homogeneous ABP prefix polynomials are linearly independent by the standard same-layer elimination argument; different layers have distinct degrees.

Checked the explicit finite matrix realization: on monomials t^a, the integration operator has entry (-1)^{b-a-1}i^{b-a}/b from column a to row b>a. It strictly raises t-adic order, so quotienting by t^B commutes with every word evaluation. Numerators and denominators have polynomial bit length for B=ns²+s, and nonzero Psi(f) is witnessed by applying f(T_1,...,T_n) to1.

Checked the polynomial evaluation hitting set from the commutative generator and the nonhomogeneous reduction: homogenization gives size O(s³), hence dimension O(ns⁶); a nonzero entry of the scaling polynomial has degree≤s−1 for an s-vertex acyclic ABP. Thus s distinct scalars suffice. The displayed construction uses s+1 scalars, a harmless count mismatch that can be removed with the stricter degree bound.
remaining: The ordinary formal-power-series Wronskian criterion and standard ABP homogenization were treated as established dependencies; their uses and a direct minimal-ABP basis argument were checked. The optional alternative classical-source AppendixA proof was not needed for, or included in, this audit.

Priority is a separate issue: page2 explicitly calls the proof technically identical to the contemporaneous OpenAI release, while claiming the authors obtained it independently beforehand. This audit verifies the presented mathematics, not that temporal/novelty assertion.
resolved_notes: Corollary1.3 says at most s evaluation tuples but the displayed set {0,...,s} has s+1. Since a size-s acyclic ABP has degree at most s−1, using {0,...,s−1} repairs this without changing the theorem or complexity.

review.summary: Constructs polynomial-size hitting sets in characteristic zero for polynomials with bounded partial-derivative dimension, including powering circuits, and for noncommutative algebraic branching programs using matrix substitutions. The generator uses truncated logarithms and a formal-derivation Wronskian.
review.prior_frontier: A black-box derandomization advance for restricted algebraic models; does not derandomize general commutative arithmetic circuits. The manuscript explicitly discusses contemporaneous independently reported noncommutative ABP results.
review.recommendation: Highest-priority proof-audit candidate; assess the overlapping contemporaneous results explicitly.

review.title: Testing Implies Distance Estimation with Polynomial Loss
review.authors: Gaia Carenini, Cameron Seth
review.summary: Every isomorphism-closed dense graph property with q(ε)-query testing admits additive-ε distance estimation using poly(max{1,q(cε)},1/ε) queries, for an absolute c>0. The tester may be adaptive/two-sided; computation can be exhaustive and the original input size remains available to the sampled predicate.
review.prior_frontier: Replaces earlier tower/exponential conversion losses with polynomial query overhead for general graph properties, not only hereditary properties. Uses the recent polynomial-arity dense-CSP subsampling theorem of Bernasconi et al.; its exact hypotheses and normalization were independently checked in the primary manuscript.

score_reasons.significance: A general polynomial testing-to-distance-estimation conversion resolves a broad quantitative obstacle in dense graph testing.
score_reasons.novelty: Derivative tests of the canonical rejection rule plus clipped weak regularity yield short vertex labels without a regularity tower.
score_reasons.depth: The key work is matching weighted rounding, role-dependent endpoint labels, CSP normalization and a sampling theorem polynomial in arity and log alphabet.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions carefully preserve original n in the tester, distinguish query from running-time complexity, and expose normalization factors.

checked: Traced the complete main reduction: amplified canonical tester; exact multiaffine rounding; cost+2·rejection penalty within O(τ) of distance; derivative counting lemma with separate endpoint roles; clipped-potential boosting with O(γ^−2) steps.
Checked that arbitrary labels still decode legal weighted graphs, that their bit length is O(s²γ^−2), and that the s-ary bounded CSP satisfies OPT=a_n(1−M̃/3) with a_n=(n)_s/n^s.

Verified the cited dense-CSP Theorem 3.3 and Definition 2.1 in arXiv:2608.00203v1: bounded predicates, ordered distinct variables, n^−s normalization, polynomial dependence on arity and log alphabet, sampling without replacement.

Checked the final inversion a_n≥1/2, Chebyshev repetition T≥432/ε², rational exhaustive optimization and small-n fallback. Empty P_n is decidable by finite enumeration; with a tester family, exact membership follows by choosing proximity below one edge edit and enumerating its finite randomness.
remaining: The main theorem is checked conditional on the cited CSP sampling theorem, whose statement/hypotheses were verified rather than re-proving its full argument. The natural/hereditary query lower bounds in Corollary 1 were not independently audited.

review.summary: For stochastic knapsack with upfront inspection/execution costs and multi-choice items, characterizes limited-adaptivity gaps through inverse ROI α: Θ(1+α) for fixed nonadaptive/batch policies, Θ(√(1+α)) for stopping-adaptive policies, and constant approximation with fixed-order adaptive skipping. review.prior_frontier: Ordinary stochastic knapsack has constant adaptivity gap without these costs. The mixed-sign utility model separates stopping from skipping and demands fuller size-distribution information. Integer/rational sizes underlie polynomial implementation; continuous distributions are treated with resource augmentation. Prior results not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A natural hybrid model produces a sharp hierarchy of policy complexity with an economic parameter explaining the losses.
score_reasons.novelty: Inverse ROI captures the cost of failed attempts and yields distinct linear, square-root and constant adaptivity regimes.
score_reasons.depth: Combines moment-matched lower bounds, multi-choice time-indexed LP rounding and stopping-policy arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: The policy classes and mixed-sign objective are explicit; introductory O(α) shorthand needs the harmless 1+α convention at small α.

checked: Traced the adaptive-policy LP upper bound using the last attempted item and truncated sizes; independence of each unobserved item size from its insertion event is essential.
Checked per-item rounding selects at most one mode/time and yields x/8 attempted mass for t>0; nonnegative LP coefficients avoid reversing the utility inequality.

Identified a repairable boundary omission in Lemma 5.3: its displayed Markov division by t does not cover t=0. For integer T≥1, the t=1 LP constraint instead bounds the expected number of positive-size selected predecessors by 1/2, giving the same probability bound.
remaining: Audit compact LP approximation, all moment-matching and adaptivity-gap lower bounds, stopping-policy analysis and the Pandora’s-box transfer; explicitly insert the t=0 boundary argument and treat degenerate T=0 separately if allowed.
issues: Repairable omission: Lemma 5.3 divides by t although t=0 is permitted. The integer-time t=1 capacity constraint supplies the missing case when T≥1; this does not establish a fatal flaw.

review.summary: Over every field, every specified one-sided factor of a degree-D polynomial computed by a size-s noncommutative circuit has size O(sD³), and every factor in f=agb has size O(sD⁶). score_reasons.significance: Settles a basic structural closure problem for several noncommutative complexity classes with strong representation-preserving bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: A cofactor-specific linear extraction automaton cancels shorter suffixes, and its one-copying-state structure yields quadratic formula size.
score_reasons.depth: The proof is concise but structurally powerful: noncommutative cancellation, triangular matrix substitution and Boolean-sum compatibility all matter.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully distinguishes nonuniform arithmetic size from factor discovery and bit length, with explicit bijections and size recurrences.

checked: Fully traced the central extraction identity: pair every reset path on rv with the uniquely corresponding shorter-suffix path by deleting/inserting its last reset block; only the no-reset path remains. Checked empty suffix, scalar cofactor and positive-characteristic cancellation.

Verified ε-transition elimination and matrix substitution at every gate; O(b³) gates per original multiplication and reversal give O(sD³)/O(sD⁶). Degree additivity follows from the unique maximum-length word cut.
Traced the formula recursion F(U,z)=pV·F(W,z)+F(V,CWz): CW is scalar, so only one recursive call occurs per original node and the extra unchanged subtree copies sum to O(s²).

Traced VNP closure using x↦Mx,z↦zI before Boolean specialization; specialization commutes with the fixed map, and linearity moves it through the Boolean sum even though individual summands need not share the factor.

papers.title: The Strong Secretary Conjecture is True for Linear Matroids

review.title: The Strong Secretary Conjecture is True for Linear Matroids
review.authors: Kristóf Bérczi, Shaddin Dughmi, Vasilis Livanos, José A. Soto, Victor Verdugo

score_reasons.significance: An optimal guarantee for a central longstanding online-selection problem.
score_reasons.novelty: The single-element invariant/uncrossing proof overlaps an acknowledged concurrent result and is superseded in scope by the general-matroid theorem. The auxiliary-vector and polymatroid-marginal extension to optimal XOS/group arrivals is a substantial distinct contribution.
score_reasons.depth: A compact but powerful LP feasibility argument with representation issues at the boundary.
score_reasons.exposition: Readable separation of the invariant, chain reduction and acceptance analysis.

checked: Traced minimax uncrossing: supermodularity and squared-dimension tie-breaking force a chain-supported dual optimum.
Checked the safest-state greedy assignment, the dimension identity and the sum over OPT(X) establishing every chain constraint.
Verified the harmonic acceptance probability with k=floor(n/e), including the finite-n inequality.

Completed the recursive online construction: every subset distribution is computed deterministically from only that subset's revealed vectors and relative weight order. New subsets are processed by size, so all predecessor distributions exist even for unrealized prefixes. Uniform last arrival and fresh randomization yield exactly the recursively defined span law. Rational finite-LP solutions preserve rational probabilities and feasibility.

Rechecked the whole LP-feasibility proof: compact minimax, dimension-square tie breaking, nested safest-state acceptance, and the dimension-increment identities establish all chain constraints; modularity and independent OPT then imply every subspace constraint. Verified k=floor(n/e) and the finite-n harmonic inequality; n≤2 is handled separately.

Checked infinite-field signatures: there are finitely many possible integer dimensions and intersections with spans of subsets of observed elements. Equal signatures have identical constraints and secondary objectives, so representative-based uncrossing still works. This is an existence argument ignoring effective signature enumeration, as the manuscript states.

Independently justified finite-field specialization for a finite linear matroid: take the finitely generated coefficient ring together with inverses of the product of nonzero basis determinants, then specialize to a finite residue field. Vanishing minors stay zero and the chosen nonzero minors stay nonzero. In the known-matroid model exhaustive enumeration of finite fields/matrices eventually finds a matching representation.

Completed the XOS/group extension. Contracting the current span gives matroid ranks r_W(D)=|D|−dim(W∩span D). The weighted Minkowski sum of independence polytopes has rank E r_W; this can also be seen directly by adding their greedy support functions. The invariant therefore places alpha times the all-ones vector in that sum, giving simultaneously feasible subset marginals.

Checked the new auxiliary-vector construction for every chain: extend the independent bundle B by nested sets D_j in L_j to bases of span(B)+L_j. Applying the marginal lemma to B∪D_s gives selected auxiliary vectors in L_j independent modulo the kept span; discarding them bounds expected intersection by (1−alpha)dim L_j+alpha dim(span B∩L_j). The offline bundles span a direct sum, so averaging gives the maintained invariant and uncrossing completes allocation-LP feasibility.

Checked XOS value analysis using a fixed supporting additive clause and unconditional element marginals; restricting the global allocation to a random prefix yields i/n of its expected value. Harmonic summation gives1/e. For groups, every element of the fixed global greedy optimum stays in each prefix optimum containing its group, giving per-element1/e; unit-demand optima may be chosen singleton. Overlapping eligibility sets do not duplicate assignments because independence modulo the old span forbids previously assigned elements.

Checked the modular-flat extension algebraically and the reduction from an unavailable extension to a finite LP over deterministic ordinal policies of the known matroid. The classification of fully modular extendable matroids is an external statement not needed for the linear/XOS results.
remaining: The external classification of fully modular extendable matroids, its examples and historical priority were not independently checked. The main linear-matroid theorem and XOS/group/agent extension proofs were traced.

No polynomial-time implementation is claimed. Infinite-field online representation is qualified as an existence result ignoring computational issues; finite-field and known finite-matroid searches are finite but can be enormous.

review.summary: Proves optimal1/e per-element secretary guarantees for linear matroids, with unbounded computation and online access to a representation. Its distinctive extensions give1/e expected welfare for XOS agent arrivals and1/e per-element guarantees for group arrivals on linear matroids, using feasible bundle marginals and auxiliary subspaces.
review.prior_frontier: The paper explicitly acknowledges a concurrent same-invariant LP proof for known linear matroids and Huang's stronger1/e expected-polynomial-time result for arbitrary matroids under single-element arrivals. Thus the single-element headline is no longer a unique frontier. The new optimal XOS/group-arrival extensions are separate contributions not implied by those single-element algorithms.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate on its verified XOS/group-arrival extensions and alternative structural method; assess alongside the acknowledged stronger concurrent single-element result.

papers.authors: Quang Dao, Scott Kominers, Justin Thaler, Kai Zhe Zheng

review.title: Cube-Root Soundness Is Optimal for the Line–versus–Point Test
review.authors: Quang Dao, Scott Duke Kominers, Justin Thaler, Kai Zhe Zheng
review.summary: The line-versus-point test over every finite field and dimension m≥2 guarantees degree-d global agreement at least acceptance−O((d/q)^{1/3}). Explicit cubic-extension examples show the exponent 1/3 is optimal, including fixed degree; higher-degree construction is given in dimension ≥3.
review.prior_frontier: Improves reported soundness exponents 1/48 in higher dimensions and 1/7 in dimension two; separates this test from stronger plane-versus-plane soundness. Historical and formalization claims not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Identifies the optimal field/degree exponent for a foundational low-degree test used in PCP constructions.
score_reasons.novelty: Simple-root uniqueness propagates one local polynomial throughout an incidence component, and subfield geometry supplies matching obstruction.
score_reasons.depth: Weighted interpolation, resultants, Hensel lifting, spectral incidence bounds and dimension bootstrapping combine in a compact argument.
score_reasons.exposition: The upper/lower quantifiers, extension-field regime and limits of the matching exponent are clearly stated.

checked: Traced the squarefree interpolation/pruning mechanism and the two-line derivative argument forcing simple roots.
Traced the resultant bound on exceptional line graphs, conditional on standard resultant facts.
Traced propagation through the connected incidence component once a local Hensel lift is given; inspected the explicit line-family injectivity/count in the lower construction.

Completed the bivariate upper bound on pages11–17. The weighted monomial count exceeds q², squarefree reduction preserves all zeros and weighted degree, and a generic derivative direction exists because the number of irreducible factors is below q. Resultants bound the exceptional line graphs by D(D−1); low-degree pruning costs at most k/q+k/(q+1). Two distinct incident directions at every remaining point force A_Z nonzero, giving simple roots.

Independently checked the local lifting interface: homogeneous coefficients of the formal implicit solution are determined uniquely degree by degree by the nonzero constant A_Z. Restriction to each incident line commutes with truncation. More than D incident lines force the substituted polynomial of degree≤D to vanish identically, and one-variable simple-root uniqueness propagates the resulting degree-d polynomial throughout the component. Incidence mixing and minimum degree give both component densities at least k/(4q).

Checked higher-dimensional bootstrapping on pages17–20: line sampling in a random plane has variance O(1/q); outside the good plane set, balancing constant labels limits accidental global agreement to2d/q. Point-conditioned plane mixing gives plane–plane acceptance≥beta²/4−(d+1)/q. The imported Bhangale–Richelson plane–plane theorem then yields Omega(beta²) good planes, and plane–point mixing recovers Omega(beta) point agreement. The primary ECCC2025/126 and SODA2026 source confirms the needed Omega(d/q) threshold and Omega(acceptance) conclusion.

Checked the additive upgrade on pages20–22. Replacing removed values by X_1^(d+1) creates at most2d/q agreement with any target polynomial. Each iteration removes at least c0 delta/2 fresh points; assigning each line to its first matching polynomial creates disjoint point and line families. Cauchy–Schwarz sums their mixing errors to q^(−1/2), rather than a factor times list length, proving acceptance minus O((d/q)^(1/3)).

Completed the lower construction on pages22–26. Distinct F_s-independent pairs parameterize distinct lines. The F_s-linear map z↦z^s+alpha z has either one or s preimages; counting partitions gives exactly one label with s² votes at independent-coordinate points. Scaling shows f(tx)^s=C_x t^(s−1), whose nonzero polynomial difference with a degree-d target has at most ds roots. Multiplying by a monic degree-(d−1) polynomial in a third coordinate gives the stated acceptance; the coefficient of Z^(d−1) of a total-degree-d target is affine, which reduces exceptional fibers to the degree-one planar bound. Projection extends to all m≥3, with only O(q^(−3)) extra lines. Fixed-degree planar and higher-dimensional examples rule out every larger exponent.
remaining: The manuscript’s new proofs and the stated imported plane-test interface were traced. The external plane–plane theorem and Grassmann eigenvalue estimates were not re-proved. The claimed Lean formalization was not downloaded or compiled, so no independent machine-check certification is made.

papers.title: Pairwise Exchanges of Freely Replicable Goods with Negative Externalities

review.title: Pairwise Exchanges of Freely Replicable Goods with Negative Externalities
review.authors: Shangyuan Yang, Kirthevasan Kandasamy

score_reasons.novelty: Matching structure organizes the feasible round proposals and protocol.

score_reasons.exposition: Definitions and departures from conventional rationality and stability are explained explicitly.

checked: Checked the iff characterization of myopic incentive compatibility: a negative-gain proposal is rejectable, overlapping receiving slots create a beneficial rejection, and disjoint slots make gains additive.
Verified the matching interpretation and why repeated copying of initially owned goods is allowed while receiving slots can fill only once.
remaining: Full participation-IR alternating-path argument, equilibrium impossibility examples, and bundle/cycle hardness reductions not audited.

review.summary: Models pairwise exchanges of replicable goods with additive negative externalities. Characterizes myopically incentive-compatible proposal sets by matchings, supplies a maximum-sharing protocol, and proves impossibility results for stronger incentive and efficiency combinations.
review.prior_frontier: Extends exchange models to replicable goods with negative externalities, using a deliberately weaker roundwise incentive notion and participation-based individual rationality. review.recommendation: Solid specialist contribution; below the strongest current shortlist tier pending global calibration.

review.summary: A deterministic adaptive-adversary framework for decremental weighted undirected graphs maintains path-reporting neighborhood covers with approximation 2^{1/poly(ε)} and total time O(n+m^{1+O(ε)}2^{1/poly(ε)}), together with emulators, approximate balls and deterministic padded decompositions. It recovers several near-best distance algorithms and new decremental tree covers.
review.prior_frontier: Neighborhood-cover tradeoff improves prior log-log-dependent approximation; several other algorithms match or nearly match prior bounds with modular simplification. Unlike one predecessor, the general neighborhood cover does not guarantee restricted cluster insertions.

score_reasons.significance: A broadly reusable deterministic toolkit can simplify many central dynamic-distance algorithms and improves a key cover tradeoff.
score_reasons.novelty: Shelled emulators and a single structural property isolate monotone ES-tree correctness from construction details.
score_reasons.depth: The simultaneous induction over emulators/covers/balls and adaptive dynamic update analysis are extensive.
score_reasons.exposition: Black-box interfaces and explicit prior-feature comparison are helpful despite a 140-page overall development.

checked: Inspected the weak approximate-ball update invariant: an emulator witness on a shortest source path preserves the additive/multiplicative estimate when a regular vertex estimate rises.
Checked quantized estimate-increase charging and the geometric phase-size accounting for restricted-to-general cluster maintenance.
remaining: Emulator structural property construction, full cover/cluster algorithms, all scale and sparsity parameter composition, padded decomposition and application reductions not audited.

review.title: Constant-Time Dynamic Edge Coloring via Dynamic Splitting and LLL
review.authors: Mohsen Ghaffari, Sijin Peng
review.summary: Maintains a proper (1+ε)Δ edge coloring of simple graphs under insertions/deletions in poly(1/ε) worst-case expected update time against an oblivious adversary, for a fixed maximum-degree bound Δ≥soft-O(1/ε²). Removes every n-dependent requirement on Δ. Develops dynamic LLL and bottom-up degree splitting as intermediate tools.
review.prior_frontier: Prior constant-update BCPS algorithm required Δ≥(log n/ε⁴)^Θ(log(1/ε)/ε). This is expected per-update time, not deterministic or high-probability worst-case time, and not an adaptive-adversary guarantee. Prior bound checked only as quoted in the manuscript.

score_reasons.significance: Answers the stated constant-time near-optimal edge-coloring degree-threshold question and produces reusable dynamic splitting machinery.
score_reasons.novelty: Bottom-up failure discovery bypasses the logarithmic cost of checking every splitting level after each update.
score_reasons.depth: Maintaining implicit transcripts across levels requires a joint shattering witness analysis and palette-change couplings to prevent repeated polynomial losses.
score_reasons.exposition: The theorem makes fixed Δ, simple graphs and oblivious updates explicit; the intricate transcript invariants require careful extended reading.

checked: Inspected the transcript-repair invariants and induction distinguishing explicit dirty sets from implicit endpoint-only changes.

Checked the conditional critical-failure bound: after fixing earlier levels and the updated edge, remaining incident edge choices are independent; category Chernoff and sign Hoeffding give exp(−Ω(U/log⁶U)).
Checked constant expected leaf adjacency lookup using independent routing and hashing: collision probability 2^−R·2^R/Δ=1/Δ, under the oblivious-update model.
remaining: Audit the joint multi-level witness/component-size lemma, complete repair cost sum, dynamic LLL resampling coupling and final ε palette/degree accounting.

checked: Traced the signed-permutation invariance-test energy formula and its intended antisymmetric encoding, conditional on overlap and concentration lemmas.

remaining: The 57-page oracle separation has traced signed-permutation and peeling-sign identities. Completion normalization, compressed-oracle control and witness elimination remain essential unverified steps; this is a large-proof exception.
Completion-map normalization/intertwining and error bounds, compressed-oracle dependency, imperfect block-size estimates, trace-power witness elimination and final diagonalization not audited.

review.title: Lotteries Protect Single-Item Sellers from Monopolist Intermediaries
review.authors: Jingyi Liu, Aviad Rubinstein, Ertem Nusret Tas, Matt Weinberg, Qianfan Zhang
review.summary: For a single-item seller facing a revenue-maximizing monopolist intermediary, two-option lottery menus recover a constant fraction of direct-sale optimal revenue for one bidder or iid bidders satisfying the stated tail condition. For heterogeneous α-strongly regular bidders the optimal ratio is Θ(√α); arbitrary heterogeneous distributions allow only Θ(1/n). Positive randomization results require the intermediary to be message-independent; message-dependent access eliminates this benefit.
review.prior_frontier: Closes the cited ABGP22 deterministic-seller question with an α^(1/(1−α)) guarantee relative to anonymous pricing, tight for one bidder; lotteries give a qualitatively larger guarantee. Prior comparison quoted from the manuscript, not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Identifies a sharp revenue-protection effect and its distributional and information boundaries in a substantive intermediary model.
score_reasons.novelty: The contrast between message-independent and message-dependent intermediary auctions and the √α frontier provide new mechanism-design structure.
score_reasons.depth: Combines virtual-value transformations, two-point menu design and adversarial heterogeneous constructions.
score_reasons.exposition: Model assumptions and negative results are explicit, although the limiting quarter-revenue construction needs careful tie-breaking treatment.

checked: Checked that access values are utilities from the seller menu only under message independence; permitting message-conditioned allocation changes the optimization problem.

Traced the one-bidder two-price proof: the threshold p has pS(p)=OPT/2, utility beyond p cannot maximize intermediary revenue, and the (1−ε)p half-price branch yields (1−ε)OPT/4; inspected the terminal-atom treatment and seller-adverse tie-breaking assumptions.
Checked the power-law regular example and the α→1 limit of the deterministic guarantee.
remaining: Audit exact limiting/attainment details for the quarter bound, iid reduction, heterogeneous √α upper/lower bounds and message-dependent impossibility theorem.

review.summary: For G≤S_n and char(F) not dividing |G|, any structurally G-symmetric circuit for n×n matrix multiplication has at least n²N/2 wires, where N is the sum of dimensions of distinct irreducible constituents of the permutation representation. Checked the rigidification step directly by bottom-up quotienting gates with identical operator/weighted-child multisets: an input-fixing automorphism then fixes every quotient gate; G-actions descend and product count does not increase.
Verified Reynolds averaging uses the characteristic hypothesis, and abelian regular representations are multiplicity-free over any semisimple base field; checked the binary-tree subgroup embedding.

review.title: Optimal partition rank bounds for the determinant and other multilinear polynomials
review.authors: Neil Krishnan, Guy Moshkovitz
review.summary: Over every field, an n-variable-block set-multilinear polynomial whose permutation monomials all have nonzero coefficients has partition rank at least n for odd n and n−1 for even n. These bounds are attained by the determinant. Also gives characteristic-two elementary-multisymmetric examples with partition rank d or d−1 but bounded analytic rank.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the manuscript’s quoted log₂n+1 and recent n−n^c lower bounds to exact parity-dependent determinant rank. The earlier bounds and priority were not independently checked; the theorem applies to the specified permutation-supported multilinear class.

score_reasons.significance: Determines an exact basic explicit tensor invariant over every characteristic and supplies a new route to partition-rank lower bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: Complex degree varieties extracted from graded modules allow characteristic-free polynomial identities despite the original coefficient field.
score_reasons.depth: Uses Koszul matrix factorizations, regraded resolutions, K-polynomials and a permutation anti-concentration theorem.
score_reasons.exposition: The parity distinction and field independence are clear, though the central degree-variety containment is a substantial algebraic dependency.

checked: Checked the Koszul factorization from a partition decomposition and the polarization identity that covers the relevant degree variety by r subset-sum hyperplanes; factorials are taken over C, not the original field.
Traced the even-dimensional determinant upper bound through pf(XKXᵀ)=det(X) and the first-row Pfaffian expansion, conditional on the standard minor-summation identity.
Checked the final root-of-unity orbit and union-bound arithmetic giving n versus n−1, and the generic-real-projection reduction for the permutation concentration lemma.

Completed the new degree-variety argument: the cokernel of the degree-relation matrix has K-polynomial q_ab and is annihilated by a power of D. Independently reconstructed the omitted initial-module Hilbert-function preservation by Gaussian elimination in each finite row-degree component; leading column-degree forms span an equal-dimensional associated graded space. Bihomogeneity of D preserves annihilation.

Checked the essential specialization step: localizing the finite free resolution at the annihilating polynomial gives a bounded free resolution of zero, hence a split contractible complex; specialization at a point where that polynomial is nonzero preserves the contraction. Regrading can have infinite-dimensional graded pieces, but the resolution-defined Laurent K-polynomial remains valid. Agreement of the permutation-matrix point with row-minus-permuted-column grading gives Q(z,z_sigma^{-1})=0.

Traced the integer K-polynomial lift into the intersection ideal J and the permutation averaging argument. Symmetric polynomials of degree at most r have only their constant value on e1=...=er=0; this yields E_r subset X_r(D) over C independently of the original coefficient characteristic.

Rechecked the full Koszul matrix recursion, complementary factorization KK*=fI, degree shifts and transpose orientation. Polarization is evaluated over C, so its factorial causes no small-characteristic obstruction. This converts partition decompositions into the subset-sum hyperplane cover.

Verified Pawlowski primary paper arXiv:2002.08535 Theorem1.1 has exactly the parity-dependent permutation-orbit bound used here. Checked the generic real projection, translation and subtraction of a constant vector that reduce complex affine constraints to that result. The root-of-unity orbit and strict union bound give n for odd n and n−1 for even n.

Checked the determinant upper bound for even n≥4 via pf(XKX^T)=pf(K)det(X) and Pfaffian first-row expansion. Each summand separates rows {1,i} from their complement. Alternating rather than merely skew-symmetric matrices makes the identity valid also in characteristic two; odd n uses Laplace expansion.
remaining: The main determinant and permutation-supported partition-rank theorem was traced. The elementary-multisymmetric analytic-rank applications and incidental rank-invariant remarks were not independently audited.

Pawlowski’s sharp external anti-concentration theorem was verified in the primary statement, not re-proved. Standard finite graded free resolutions and the classical Pfaffian minor-summation identity were used as established dependencies.

review.summary: For K≤N binary-phase states in an N-dimensional Hilbert space, a T-query adversary with S qubits of oracle-dependent advice recovers the sampled key from one copy with probability O((1+T²+√(S(T+1)))/K). score_reasons.significance: Quantifies a major communication-versus-preprocessing advantage of fully quantum primitives and unifies several oracle lower bounds.

checked: Fully traced Theorem 5.2: the advice optimum is the expected norm of a positive operator; its 2t-th trace moment becomes repeated applications on an initially empty Fourier database, growing by at most 2T+2 each time.

Verified the exact primary external theorem JRS2018 arXiv:1509.07127v3 Theorem2.1, Remark2.2 and stabilization Remark2.4: the beta_0-averaged rotated Petz map, with the half-rotation parameter, has the stated root-fidelity bound and depends only on reference state and channel.

Spectator-reference powers cancel to the support projection even on correlated inputs. Tracing the recovered quantum register leaves an effect linear in the unnormalized classical block, so every stochastic coarse label is a postprocessing of the SAME fine-label POVM.

Checked normalization, stationarity and detailed balance of the averaged kernel; the latter uses the even rotation density and u↦−u, rather than an unjustified commutation of states. Conditional mutual information telescopes to at most log k. Fuchs–van de Graaf and Cauchy–Schwarz yield the selected-reward bound sqrt(log k/N), valid for every analysis-only coarse label.

Checked the signed-loss minimax step in full. For each adversarial law on (state,observable,sign), choose its state marginal as prior and its conditional law as coarse label. Detailed balance converts the reward bound into the required expected signed bias. All responses live in the same compact convex grid-output POVM space with budget fixed first; minimax therefore supplies one POVM controlling every finite-state signed bias.

Checked the net extension using the operator B_j=sum_z z_j N_z, which is an effect: bias is (N+1)-Lipschitz in trace distance. A finite net of radius epsilon/[4(N+1)] yields a state-uniform bias guarantee without a union bound over the net. Independent repetitions and Hoeffding give the valid epsilon^−4 intermediate bound.

Completed the geometric refinement to epsilon^−2: majority block observables are effects on k=Theta(epsilon_s^−2) copies and have expectation at most1/8 or at least7/8 outside a quarter-error interval. Constant-accuracy simultaneous estimates select a half-error shift and reduce every error by3/4. Fresh copies make the guarantees valid conditional on adaptive history; delta_s=(delta/4)(3/4)^(S−1−s) sums below delta. The weighted geometric sum of block costs is O(epsilon^−2 log(2M)log(2M/delta)).
remaining: The sequential ordinary-PGM alternative in Sections2.2–3 and its external quadratic-minimax comparison were not needed for the verified recovery-measurement proof and were not audited in full. AppendixC is likewise auxiliary.

The primary universal-recovery theorem was checked for its exact statement and applicability, not re-proved. Standard minimax, quantum entropy, fidelity and concentration theorems are imported. This is a sample-complexity existence theorem; no efficient construction or implementation of the minimax POVM is established.

review.authors: Jesko Dujmovic, Daniel Wichs
review.summary: Exponentially hard injective one-way functions yield public-coin interactive NP arguments with communication/rounds O-tilde(T^theta) and verifier time O-tilde(|x|+T^theta), for an assumption-dependent theta<1. Interactive vector commitments recursively amplify constant-factor compression. This is neither polylogarithmic succinctness nor a construction from ordinary polynomial-hardness OWFs.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier succinct interactive NP arguments relied on collision-resistant or multicollision-resistant hashing. The manuscript supplies a different stronger-hardness OWF route; prior-separation scope not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Changes the assumption basis for a central succinct verification primitive.
score_reasons.novelty: Interactive recursion with delayed local message extraction replaces static Merkle hashing.

checked: Traced the selective interval binding composition proof, including outer-opening disagreement hybrids.
Checked continuation-sampling failure p(1-p)^Q<=1/(Q+1), fresh public-coin preservation of the real execution, and a single outer-binding reduction for differing sampled/real openings.
Checked total bound bind_inner(t_epsilon)+2c bind_outer(t_epsilon)+epsilon with capped runtime O(c^2(t+V+d)/epsilon).

Completed the new composition theorem on PDF pages15–20. Equalizing the two revealed inner-message restrictions costs c outer-binding attacks. For extraction, each saved prefix is continued independently Q=ceil(c/epsilon) times with a fixed adversary tape; p(1−p)^Q≤1/(Q+1) bounds a missed successful continuation. Different extracted and real restrictions yield one outer-binding attack for the whole capped sampler, with no spurious extra Q loss. Public-coin independence preserves the real execution law although extracted messages are sent before subsequent inner challenges.

Checked the base commitment parameter conversion on pages12–14 against the stated Haitner–Reingold interface. Polynomial hashing into5n bits is injective on all2^n image points except with probability≤2^(−2n), even when inputs depend on the public seed. A reduction independent of the image/set/relation averages over seeds, uses Jensen on the squared attack success, and has time poly(n)2^v 2^(delta n/2)≤2^(delta n). The choices v,ell yield sender length≤(1−zeta/8)n and binding error≤2^(−zeta n/5).

Checked shared-challenge parallel blocks and local interval verification: a disputed interval touches at most ceil(L/n)+1 blocks and a chosen block can be relayed before commitment. Recursive lengths satisfy M_(j−1)≤M_j dtilde/lambda+lambda; an opening touches at most two blocks at every node because2dtilde≤lambda. Communication is bounded by gamma^(k+1)N+O(lambda ell^k).

Checked recursive security budgets: beta_j≤eta+2ell beta_(j−1)+epsilon0 with epsilon0=ell epsilon/(2(2ell)^k); the total time inflation has logarithm O(log(N+t)+k²+k log(1/epsilon)+log lambda). Setting lambda=D(log N)^3 and epsilon=2^(−(log N)^2) covers every polynomial-time attack for all sufficiently large N; k=floor(log(N/lambda)/log(ell/gamma)) gives theta=log ell/log(ell/gamma)<1 and the advertised succinctness.

Checked the stated PCP-combination arithmetic and selective-position loss: fresh PCP randomness follows the completed interactive commitment; only the response phase is rewound. A guessed position loses N, and O(N/xi) capped rewindings remain polynomial for inverse-polynomial xi. Polylogarithmic repetition and local openings preserve soft-O(T^theta) communication and soft-O(|x|+T^theta) verifier time, conditional on the explicitly imported PCP and Kilian soundness interfaces.
remaining: All new vector-commitment construction and composition proofs are traced. The exact journal-version Haitner–Reingold reduction, Mie/BSGH PCP interfaces, and Chiesa et al. strict-time Kilian reduction remain imported dependencies; the entire external proofs were not audited. The historical black-box separation comparisons were not checked.
resolved_notes: The arbitrary-depth receiver-time bound on PDF page23 omits the cost of reading the sender transcript: it should include s_k. At the final balanced depth chosen on page25, s_k=O(lambda ell^k), so this omission does not alter the claimed final verifier bound.

Budgeted-orienteering conversion, expected-budget qualification, running time and oracle bit complexity.
