review.summary: Reconstructs every unknown n-bit string from exp(p^(−7/3)(log₂n)^c) deletion-channel traces for an absolute c and retention p>0. Pairwise distinguishing is quasipolynomial time, but unrestricted reconstruction uses exponential candidate enumeration in this paper.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the earlier exp(soft-O(n^(1/5))) worst-case upper bound and bypasses local-SQ barriers using globally separated polylog-order statistics. Later quasipolynomial-time reconstruction and n^Ω(log log n) lower bounds mentioned in related work are not this manuscript’s theorems.

score_reasons.significance: A major improvement to worst-case trace reconstruction sample complexity after a longstanding exponential gap.
score_reasons.novelty: Repeated zooming around the first discrepancy combines robust bispectrum identification, multiple-trace simulation and controlled binomial deconvolution.
score_reasons.depth: Maintains support, Fourier decay, statistical order and retention probability through O(log log n) scale increases.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed overview explains why global statistics escape known barriers and explicitly separates sample and running-time claims.

checked: Verified the exact three-trace simulation: condition three independent retention coins on a nonempty retained subset, starting with retention P=1−(1−p)^3. Checked the product-statistic coefficients and min/max shift support bounds.
Checked the generating function and the radius/angle dichotomy arithmetic, including the wraparound branch that loses at least p/4 in modulus.

Traced the final induction bookkeeping conditional on Proposition 37: b=O(log log n), initial retention 3^−b min(p,1/4), order growth 3^b, and initial window p_base^−6 give the stated p^−7/3 exponent and quasipolynomial sample bound.
remaining: Large-proof exception:49-page reconstruction induction. The exact three-trace simulation, generating-function geometry and final parameter bookkeeping were traced. The robust bispectrum/deconvolution and complete induction-step argument remain unchecked; this is not end-to-end validation of the quasipolynomial bound.
Audit robust three-point/bispectrum lemma, abrupt-start Fourier bound, binomial deconvolution and the complete Proposition 37 induction step; verify pairwise-testing-to-reconstruction dependency.

papers.authors: Jean Rosemond Dora, Ladislav Hluchý

review.title: RHELIOS: Adversarially Robust Online Convex Optimization with Optimal Adaptive Regret in Banach Spaces
review.authors: Jean Rosemond Dora, Ladislav Hluchý

score_reasons.significance: The headline upper bound fails under the explicit equation-based implementation tested here.
score_reasons.novelty: The text does not substantiate a new valid regret mechanism beyond standard mirror descent.
score_reasons.depth: The essential path-variation and corruption inequalities are asserted rather than derived.
score_reasons.exposition: Algorithm 1 omits the next dual-state assignment, Eq. 12 is not equivalent to Eq. 10, and lower-bound formulas use incompatible corruption scalings.

checked: Implemented the charitable Eq. 10 interpretation with R(w)=w^2/2, K=[-1,1], alpha=1, no corruption, and eta=1/sqrt(T(1+V)). For even N, take T=N^3 and N alternating linear-gradient blocks of length N^2; the comparator is the minimizing endpoint, with V=2(N-1).

The recurrence d_(t+1)=-eta*g_t-2*eta*d_t has block slope -eta*g/(1+2eta). Projection stays inactive for this family. Alternating blocks make the learner's signed linear loss O(N), while the comparator's linear loss is -T and switching cost is 4(N-1); regret is T-O(N), versus the claimed O(N^2).
Direct calculations for N=8,16,32,64,128 give regret/claimed-scale approximately 5.55,11.34,22.73,45.39,90.67, consistent with the analytic contradiction.
remaining: No corrected algorithm or corrected theorem is supplied or inferred by this review.
issues: Theorem 4.1 fails for the natural Eq. 10 update and an allowed constant step size specified by Eq. 13, already for uncorrupted Euclidean linear losses.

The three algorithmic subroutines do not specify a consistent composite update; Eq. 12 is a different proximal rule, and arbitrary Banach squared-norm gradients cannot generally be replaced by 2(w_t-w_(t-1)).

review.desk_reject_reason: Concrete failure of the headline upper bound under its displayed update, together with inconsistent algorithm definitions and missing essential inequalities; this is a mathematical assessment, not an inference about authorship.
review.summary: Claims an optimal dynamic-regret algorithm in arbitrary Banach spaces with corruption and switching costs. The stated update and learning-rate rule do not establish the advertised bound, and a simple uncorrupted one-dimensional family defeats the natural reading of the algorithm.
review.prior_frontier: Dynamic regret with path variation is a well-developed online-optimization problem. A new optimality claim requires a valid algorithm and quantitative potential analysis; the manuscript supplies incompatible updates and only a telescoping assertion.

Structural implication from large submodular width to clique-embedding power, depending on Marx machinery.
Counting/core-class consequences and quasipolynomial decomposition computation.

Checked loop closure through translation groups and simultaneous ordered-point transporters, conditional on the supplied actual scaffold and explicitly polynomial local grids.

review.title: Facility Location with Customer Incompatibilities
review.authors: Zachary Friggstad, Pengfei Wu
review.summary: Metric facility location with one common client matroid at every facility admits a (1+√2+ε)-approximation for uniform opening costs. For a common partition matroid and arbitrary opening costs, gives (15+ε). Algorithms use polynomially many independence-oracle queries and rational-cost local search. Facility-specific matroids already encode Set Cover, even with common partition blocks but varying group capacities.
review.prior_frontier: Extends uniform-capacity facility location to client matroids; differs from matroid median, where a matroid restricts facilities rather than assigned clients. General nonuniform costs with an arbitrary common matroid are not claimed. Prior approximations/hardness sources not independently traced.

score_reasons.significance: Constant-factor algorithms for a substantially broader incompatibility model with a clear hardness boundary.
score_reasons.novelty: A matroid-exchange compression of local assignments controls excess opened facilities; partition costs use a bounded-congestion mapping.
score_reasons.depth: Compression must preserve independence while transferring clients along paths that can revisit facilities.
score_reasons.exposition: Proof structure is readable but the local-search pseudocode reverses its update assignment and calls rank submodularity supermodularity; displayed inequalities use the intended direction.

checked: Traced the common-matroid connection-cost supermodularity via dual potentials and rank layer-cake identities, and telescoping deletion costs to F(S\P)≤2C*.

Traced the compression chain: move each client to its prescribed optimum-image facility, displace outside the target independent set via a fundamental circuit, and never displace a previously fixed client. Minimum-cost injection cycles show W cannot increase; tie-breaking forces P inside the injection image.
Checked uniform-cost rescaling λ=1/√2 combines C≤C*+F*/λ and F≤2λC*+F* to give 1+√2.
remaining: The nonuniform partition-matroid bounded-congestion construction and full 15-factor analysis are not audited.
Full dual-integrality setup, polynomial local-search implementation, and hardness reductions/source assumptions remain to be checked.

Finite-precision model and essential cited matrix-multiplication/SDP dependencies need primary-source checks.

Permutation-cover upper bound and polynomial-factor formulation for all residues of n.

review.summary: Using only each agent’s ordinal ranking of n items in an unknown common metric, constructs a randomized one-sided perfect matching with expected distortion O(n^{log_4 3}), the first sublinear bound. remaining: Large-proof exception (93 pages). The new cluster-completion flow construction and randomized radius supermartingale, together with their parameter optimization conditional on the prefix bound, were traced. Separate mechanism families, lower bounds and cited derandomization require further verification.
External RSD prefix bound and deterministic reduction remain unverified; fractional-to-integral output and implementation details need checking.
RSD branching/pruning lower bound, PS upper/lower analysis, coordinated merging and truthful-mechanism lower bounds remain unaudited.

Sampled-calibration conversion, approachability guarantees and implementation/runtime details.

review.summary: Conditional randomized polynomial-time 2^{O((log* n)²)} approximation for vertex guarding simple polygons. review.title: Optimal Contention Resolution from Samples

review.summary: For independent unknown Bernoulli activations under a cardinality constraint, characterizes samples needed for optimal online contention resolution: one sample achieves random-order optimum 1-e^-k k^k/k!; zero suffices when k>=5. For adversarial fixed order k=1, two samples attain optimal 1/2, one cannot; for fixed k>=2, no constant sample count attains the full-information optimum.

score_reasons.exposition: Precisely separates random/adversarial order and exact optimum from asymptotic near-optimality.

remaining: Random-order optimal ratios for general k and zero-sample boundary k=5.
Single-sample impossibility and finite-sample impossibility for k>=2.
Reduction from sum p_i<=k to the equality version used by some schemes, and all arrival-order restrictions.

review.title: The Sample Complexity of Multicalibration with an ERM Oracle
review.authors: Princewill Okoroafor
review.summary: Learns ordinary multicalibration with soft-O(d/ε³) samples and polynomial weighted-ERM calls, versus prior ε^{-7}-type oracle bounds. For soft-Ω(1/ε)≤d≤poly(1/ε), matching lower bound applies to black-box ERM access with hidden classes and polynomially many calls, not to explicitly represented computational problems. Deterministic predictor output requires a computable total order and stored sample inputs. Swap multicalibration has statistical Θ̃(d/ε³) complexity but this paper’s oracle-efficient swap upper bound is only Õ(d/ε⁴). Ordinary-error estimation is NP-hard even with efficient ERM, unlike swap estimation.
review.prior_frontier: Enumeration achieves Õ(ε^{-3}+dε^{-2}) ordinary calibration, showing an oracle-access sample price. The paper distinguishes that statistical bound from efficient ERM and from swap guarantees. Prior sources not independently audited.

review.summary: Constructs explicit two-sided lossless bipartite expanders with full-rank binary adjacency and a free finite 2-group action. remaining: Arithmetic congruence-quotient Ramanujan proof, distinct-witness verification, preservation of lossless expansion, balanced-product rank inheritance and final code parameter choices remain unaudited.
Thermal lifetime is an external conditional consequence; its dynamical assumptions and transfer have not been verified.

review.title: On Brouwer's Laplacian conjecture
review.authors: Pravesh K. Kothari, Stefan Tudose
review.summary: Proves Brouwer’s Laplacian conjecture for every finite simple graph: the sum of the largest k Laplacian eigenvalues is at most m+binom(k+1,2). Establishes an implication cycle with the Grone–Merris–Bai majorization theorem through centered split-graph nuclear norms and a projection routing inequality.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript describes earlier special cases and approximate bounds. The essential pre-existing Grone–Merris–Bai theorem was checked against Hua Bai’s primary arXiv text 0911.2172v4 and has exactly the required finite-simple-graph majorization scope.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a prominent general spectral graph inequality rather than another special case or asymptotic relaxation.
score_reasons.novelty: The split-graph nuclear-norm bound and level-cut routing inequality reveal a new link between two classical spectral bounds.
score_reasons.depth: A concentrated chain of projection identities and cut inequalities replaces broad structural case analyses.
score_reasons.exposition: Short, complete and modular proof; an isolated summation-index typo does not affect the preceding identity or argument.

checked: Traced all implications on PDF pages 3–8. Grone–Merris bounds excess split-graph eigenvalues above clique size; the trace identity then gives ||LH−rC||*≤r(n−r).

Verified P²=P, P1=0 projection identity and N=CMC=C−2P, so ||N||≤1. For each level cut, the constructed split graph gives Σcut v+Σcross|Mij|=−tr((L−rC)N). Nuclear/operator norm duality and telescoping yield the full routing inequality.
Checked Cauchy–Schwarz converts routing to the quadratic residual bound; the scalar positive-part identity and diagonal-variance identity then imply Brouwer’s bound, including k=n.
Traced the reverse Brouwer-to-split-trace-to-Grone–Merris argument, complement/rank reduction and its degree-sequence minimization.

Primary dependency scope verified at https://arxiv.org/html/0911.2172v4. Numerical sanity checks for 1,050 random centered projections validated the key identities and inequalities; artifacts audits/audit696.py and audit696.json.
remaining: Bai’s established theorem is used as an external theorem; its full original proof was not re-proved. This is a main-proof check, not formal verification.
resolved_notes: PDF page 4 final display writes a sum of min(d_i,k) up to k; the immediately preceding correct identity requires summing over all n vertices. This is a local index typo; the proof establishes the n-term identity.

review.summary: For every fixed ε>0, a deterministic algorithm approximates any nonnegative n×n permanent within (1+ε)^n in n^{O(ε^{-2} log³(2/ε))} arithmetic operations. Rational inputs have polynomially bounded intermediate bit lengths. This is exponential-factor approximation, not an FPTAS.
review.prior_frontier: The paper improves a previous constant exponential base near √2; it also acknowledges an independent exp(o(n))-factor polynomial-time result. Those prior algorithm claims were not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Arbitrarily small constant exponential bases address a central deterministic counting frontier.
score_reasons.novelty: Balanced monomer-dimer entropy and a convex correction to analytic polynomial approximations give a distinctive route.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines entropy interpolation, bipartite matching correlation, complex resolvent derivative estimates and numerical convex optimization.
score_reasons.exposition: The theorem distinguishes arithmetic and bit complexity, with explicit approximation parameters; the numerical appendix needs separate checking.

checked: Traced attainment of balanced vertex fields modulo the bipartite gauge and the alternating-path injection proving the required negative monomer correlation.
Traced the upper entropy interpolation, including its compactness limit at t=1.
Checked the signed-derivative Hessian row-sum argument and the β∑w convexity/error correction.
Checked support-preserving rounding, bounded-gauge minimizers, and the final α,η,δ choices giving the advertised multiplicative error.

Completed the lower entropy inequality via independent thinning of a permanent-weighted perfect matching. The selected left coordinates recover the partial matching; entropy chain rule and reduced conditioning give expected restricted entropy >=tH(sigma), while expected log edge weight scales by t.

Checked the full path-tree and complex derivative argument pp14–20: Schur complements match the monomer-ratio recursion; bipartite symmetry replaces the resolvent by (I+sB²)^{-1}; disjoint child-row supports give norm(B)<=2sqrtK. The Möbius image has Re(s)>−1/(8K), giving inverse norm<=2 and inductive nonvanishing for every induced subgraph. Signed log-weight derivatives have norm<=sqrtK; Cauchy coefficient bounds and row-sign choice yield the claimed weighted Hessian domination and convex correction.

Checked Appendix A implementation pp24–30. Constraint-violating steps use log degree and have separation log(5/4); feasible steps use the surrogate gradient. The common minimizer is strictly degree-feasible, gradient norm and dyadic errors preserve a h eta/2 squared-distance decrease, forcing an acceptable iterate within the specified T. All recorded values are feasible upper estimates.

Checked explicit coefficient/denominator bounds, exponential Taylor truncation, dyadic gradient rounding and fixed-denominator iterates. Their precision parameters are polynomial in n,p,m; polynomial enumeration costs n^{O(m)} and the gauge-bound box remains polynomial in these quantities. Exact preprocessing cases n<=1, absent perfect matching and unsupported edges are handled.

Verified the primary LSW paper Section3.1/Theorem3.1 and proof of Theorem3.4: polynomial arithmetic scaling puts a heaviest generalized diagonal at row maxima, with polynomial bit growth. Subsequent upward rounding changes permanent by at most n n! 2^{-p}; perB>=1 converts this to the stated relative bound. Checked the final entropy/rounding budgets and exponent m=O(epsilon^{-2}log³(2/epsilon)).
remaining: Central approximation algorithm, analytic estimate and numerical implementation checked. Historical/concurrent superiority comparisons were not independently checked. The result is an exponential-factor approximation for each fixed epsilon, not an FPTAS or exact permanent computation. Established LSW scaling is used with its verified scope, not reproved in full.

review.title: Fast Odd-Permutation Sums in Characteristic Two and Shortest Even Directed Cycles
review.authors: Boxuan Chen, Bin Cui, Hanqing Li, Xupeng Miao, Haoze Wang
review.summary: Computes the sum of odd-permutation monomials and all its first derivatives for any matrix over a characteristic-two field deterministically in O(n^ω) field operations, for fixed ω>2. Gives randomized shortest even directed-cycle length and full shortest-cycle arc support in soft-O(n^ω ℓ), and a witness in soft-O(n^ω ℓ+n²ℓ²), where ℓ is the optimum length; success probability 1−O(n⁻³).
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript compares prior characteristic-four/permanent-based shortest-even-cycle costs soft-O(n^(ω+3)) for length and soft-O(n^(ω+4)) for extraction, with new worst-case soft-O(n^(ω+1)) and soft-O(n⁴). Those historical bounds were not independently rederived.

score_reasons.significance: Removes two polynomial factors from a difficult parity-constrained directed-cycle problem and computes all optimum-support arcs.
score_reasons.novelty: Binary-interval trace aggregation plus a fixed Boolean border handles the odd-permutation polynomial, its gradient and singular matrices directly in characteristic two.
score_reasons.depth: The argument integrates complementary minors, rank-sensitive borders, ring arithmetic and incremental row restrictions without introducing new extraction randomness.
score_reasons.exposition: Precisely separates success-event, expected and unconditional runtimes, and explains why the retained diagonal entries make every ring inversion legal.

checked: Traced the complementary-minor identity and binary interval-tree trace aggregation; the depth cost is n^ω times a convergent sum of (2d+1)2^(−(ω−2)d).
Checked the fixed-border polynomial identity for corank ≤3 and the zero-gradient argument for corank ≥4; differentiation keeps the border fixed rather than differentiating the rank computation.
Verified the invertible gradient formula G=ΔBCB+(Φ+Δ)B, including the characteristic-two diagonal identity (CB)pp=1.

Traced the lowest even coefficient and arc derivatives, the (m+1)ℓ/q union bound, the geometrically increasing truncation precision, and invertibility of every Schur complement over the truncated ring.

Checked extraction forcing: the initial deleted diagonal forces the path, occupied columns prohibit internal repetition, and a nonzero coefficient has a nonzero extension. The two fixed borders and zero-constant row updates make every Sherman–Morrison denominator a unit.
Verified the ℓ−1 extensions, soft-O(n²ℓ²) maintenance cost, absence handling and exceptional-event contribution to expected runtime.
remaining: Standard fast rank-revealing linear algebra and soft-linear polynomial multiplication/inversion are used as established algorithmic primitives; their implementations and prior-work historical comparisons were not independently audited.

papers.authors: Yang S. Hu, William Kuszmaul, Jingxun Liang, Stefan Walzer, Huacheng Yu, Renfei Zhou

review.title: Quadratic Probing Insertions Are $\epsilon^{-(1+o(1))}$ Time
review.authors: Yang S. Hu, William Kuszmaul, Jingxun Liang, Stefan Walzer, Huacheng Yu, Renfei Zhou
review.summary: Quadratic probing with independent uniform key hashes, prime table size n, insertion-only workload and ε>1/√log n has expected next-insertion cost ε^{-(1+o(1))} at load 1−ε. A fallback scans the table after the quadratic sequence. The result does not establish the exact O(1/ε) conjecture or a bounded-independence implementation.
review.prior_frontier: Previously constant insertion cost was proved only at small loads (up to 37.61%); an all-load bound O(ε^{-2} log n) retained n-dependence. These historical comparisons are manuscript claims, not independently rechecked.

score_reasons.significance: A near-tight analysis resolves the major qualitative question for a basic decades-old hash-table rule.
score_reasons.novelty: Poissonized positive association, vacancy covariance mass and sparse square-difference multiplicities bypass witness-tree limitations.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines a custom associated-variable tail bound with divisor and modular-hyperbola estimates.
score_reasons.exposition: The model, high-load range and difference from the exact conjecture are stated clearly.

checked: Traced occupied-set monotonicity and the finite-layer Harris argument converging to Poissonized positive association.
Checked translation invariance, Var((n−N)+)≤Var(N), total covariance ≤1, and how nonnegative covariances imply the R(k) bound.
Checked the divisor-factorization argument for k≤√n and the rectangle reduction to the cited modular-hyperbola estimate.

Completed the custom association tail proof and independently justified the convex-order input for Bernoulli variables: replacing one coordinate by an independent copy changes E phi(sum) by Cov(X_i,phi(S+1)-phi(S)), nonnegative under association and convexity; iterate. The truncated quadratic comparison then contributes exactly 8d/mu^2, and Chernoff supplies the exponential term.

Checked the arithmetic dependencies in primary arXiv:1103.2879 Theorem13 for the fixed rectangle actually used, and arXiv:1110.4689 Lemma3.1/Remark3.2 for f(x)=x and full auxiliary interval. In the latter specialization distinct shifts give independent square classes by their distinct simple roots, so the shifted curve is irreducible. Restricting y to [0,k) with k<=n/2 makes the point-to-square correspondence injective. The displayed degree/Weil error is sqrt(n) exp(O(|J| log log n)), uniform for the needed slowly growing |J|.

Traced the covering and final tail summation on pp13–15: |J|=ceil(2n log(1/epsilon)/k) is o(log n/loglog n) under epsilon>1/sqrt(log n); inclusion-exclusion yields union size >(1-epsilon)n. The n^0.76 bridge and the remaining harmonic tail are lower-order or O(1/epsilon), leaving only the divisor-bound range to contribute epsilon^(-1-o(1)). Prime table size, insertion-only workload, fully independent uniform hashes and the fallback scan within2n probes are essential.
remaining: No substantive issue found in the central Theorem1.1 proof under its stated parameter regime. The review does not extend it to composite table sizes, arbitrary limited-independence hashing, unrestricted smaller epsilon, or the informal deletion/rebuilding remark. Historical priority claims and primary number-theory theorems were not reproved beyond checking their applied specialization.

review.title: Private PCPs from Product Expansion

review.area: PCPs; coding theory; quantum fault tolerance
review.summary: Constructs private PCPs for CircuitSAT of length n log n exp(O(k log k)) and O(kN^(1/k)) queries, with perfect completeness, inverse-polylog fractional privacy at k=2, and constant soundness gap for fixed k. The k=2 construction is unconditional; k>2 relies on the explicitly unverified product-expansion conjecture. Its key theorem proves two-dimensional product expansion for Reed–Solomon codes on coprime-order multiplicative subgroups of a prime field, with comparable subgroup sizes and rates bounded away from one.
review.prior_frontier: Crosses the prior sum-of-rates-below-one restriction for this structured RS pair. The manuscript distinguishes subsequent qLTC/zero-knowledge-PCP works and its own X-error-only fault tolerance; it does not establish quantum PCP or full quantum fault tolerance. Historical comparisons are manuscript claims.

score_reasons.significance: Produces unconditional square-root-query private PCPs and a concrete high-rate product-expansion theorem underlying several quantum-code directions.
score_reasons.novelty: Coprime subgroup geometry defeats the diagonal privacy attack and permits multiplication-compatible tensor codes beyond the old rate barrier.
score_reasons.depth: Combines algebraic-curve gcd estimates, tensor-code privacy/robustness and a private robust circuit construction.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly labels higher-dimensional expansion as conjectural, including the unverified candidate proof, and distinguishes privacy from an efficient zero-knowledge simulator.

Checked the divisibility contradiction at t≤c h³/N, cancellation of mixed factors with multiplicity, and the univariate interpolation completion.
Checked the interpolation error-locator construction and both weight regimes giving ρ=Ω(ε⁶/K³), including preservation under coordinate scaling.
Confirmed that the stated high-dimensional guarantees remain conditional, and that the quantum interpretation protects against X errors rather than arbitrary quantum faults.
remaining: Verify the exact positive-characteristic hypotheses of the external Corvaja–Zannier theorem.
Audit the collective product-expansion/relative robust-testing reductions, private robust circuit, soundness composition and final PCP parameter accounting.

review.title: An Efficient Black-Box Reduction from Online Learning to Multicalibration, and a New Route to Φ-Regret Minimization
review.authors: Gabriele Farina, Juan Carlos Perdomo
review.summary: Black-box reduction gives distribution-valued high-dimensional H-multicalibration error at most external regret over H plus EVI errors; a converse obtains EVI solutions from multicalibration. A best-response reduction then bounds distribution-valued Φ-regret by calibration against tests σ(p)−φ(σ(p)). Efficient instantiations require bounded tests and evaluable operators on well-bounded convex bodies with appropriate oracles.

score_reasons.significance: A general computational connection unifies useful forecasting and decision-making guarantees.
score_reasons.novelty: Expected variational inequalities isolate the optimization primitive and calibrating only induced deviations makes the reduction fine-grained.
score_reasons.depth: The central inequalities are short, with substantial consequences depending on EVI algorithms and online-learning instantiations.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions explicitly distinguish distributions from single actions and state the required geometric/oracle conditions.

Checked the converse by best responses and averaging forecast distributions, and Theorem 5’s best-response nonpositivity argument.
Confirmed that the nonlinear Φ-regret notion permits distributions; single-point coalescing is justified only for linear deviations.
remaining: The efficient EVI theorem and well-bounded-body oracle dependencies remain unchecked.
Delayed/censored observation algorithms, omniprediction rates, ECE guarantees and RKHS/linear-swap corollaries have not received a correctness audit.

papers.authors: Xiongxin Yang

review.title: $0/1$-Polytopes with Exponentially Small Edge Expansion
review.authors: Xiongxin Yang
review.summary: Constructs full-dimensional 0/1-polytopes in dimension 4n+1 whose graph edge expansion is at most 4n β^n/(1−β^n), where β=(1+√6)²/12<1. Thus general 0/1-polytopes can have exponentially small expansion, disproving both the Mihail–Vazirani bound h≥1 and any universal inverse-polynomial lower bound.
review.prior_frontier: The long-standing Mihail–Vazirani conjecture asserted expansion at least one for all 0/1-polytopes. The result concerns the unrestricted class and does not refute expansion theorems for special classes such as matroid polytopes.

score_reasons.significance: An explicit exponentially small-expansion family overturns a central conjectural property of 0/1-polytopes.
score_reasons.novelty: The Cayley construction pairs two unequal product layers and cuts along cross-edge connected components, eliminating all cross-layer boundary edges.
score_reasons.depth: The exact five-pair block compatibility calculation and binomial diagonal estimate convert a geometric construction into an exponentially sparse cut.
score_reasons.exposition: The self-contained first proof and separate general two-layer cut formulation make the critical construction readily checkable.

checked: Traced full dimensionality and the exposed-edge criterion for the Cayley sum of C^n×D^n and D^n×C^n, with C={00,01,10,11} and D={00,01,10}.
Checked the five compatible block pairs, invariance of active-block supports along cross edges, and the 12^n vertices in each layer.
Verified the cut |I|<|J|, cancellation of all cross-edge boundary, its size 12^n−Σr binom(n,r)²6^r, and the exact diagonal-boundary count Σr binom(n,r)²6^r[4(n−r)+5r/3].
Recomputed the binomial bound Σr binom(n,r)²6^r≤(1+√6)^(2n), giving β≈0.9915816238. At n=1000 the displayed expansion upper bound is approximately 0.85236<1, in dimension 4001.
Traced the alternate general two-layer majority-component cut and its Hellinger-overlap specialization.
remaining: No formal proof-assistant verification or complete computer enumeration of the polytope graph was performed; the analytic construction and estimates were checked directly.

review.authors: Sinan Oral, Supartha Podder

score_reasons.significance: A strong exact-quantum oracle separation against two major classical classes.
score_reasons.novelty: Exact-count repair preserving classical indistinguishability is the central new mechanism.
score_reasons.depth: Convex smoothing, Gaussian replacement and restriction bounds make a substantial 58-page proof.
score_reasons.exposition: The stages and exact gate/query conventions are clearly separated.

checked: Verified the three-query exact amplitude-amplification calculation for success probabilities 3/4 and 1/4.
Checked the repaired-count divisibility and three-stage integer balancing conditional on the stated bin scales.
Traced the product-sign versus fixed-slice coupling, both conditional means, the two-sided Jensen comparison for convex tests and the O(1/M) fluctuation estimate.

papers.title: Tensor Decomposition Beyond the Spectral Threshold
papers.authors: Agastya Vibhuti Jha, Davide Mazzali, Jeff Xu

review.title: Tensor Decomposition Beyond the Spectral Threshold
review.authors: Agastya Vibhuti Jha, Davide Mazzali, Jeff Xu
review.area: Average-case tensor decomposition and sum of squares
review.summary: For random independent Rademacher components and tensor order k in {3,4}, claims approximate decomposition in n^{O-tilde(ell)} time up to rank m=o-tilde(n^{k/2} ell^{k/2-1}), for ell=o-tilde(n). Recovery is high correlation up to permutation and, for even order, signs; not exact or arbitrary-tensor decomposition.
review.prior_frontier: Polynomial-time algorithms stop near rank n^{k/2}; analogous subexponential tradeoffs existed for tensor PCA and random CSP refutation but not decomposition.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial time-rank tradeoff for a canonical inference task, if the stated implementation and proof gaps are repaired.
score_reasons.novelty: Joint sharp signal/noise bounds aim to recover a unit additive advantage above a much larger fourth-order noise baseline.
score_reasons.depth: Kikuchi lifts, correlated polynomial random matrices and SoS rounding span a substantial technical proof.
score_reasons.exposition: The conceptual overview is strong, but explicit algorithm acceptance and central lemma statements do not agree with their claimed use.

checked: Checked the fourth-order background expectation mu=(3n^2-2n)/n^4 and why a unit excess over m*mu is needed.
Compared the formal algorithm to the noisy SoS constraint and read the high-moment rounding reduction.
Visually verified Lemma 6.4 on PDF page 34; for m=1 and x=v1 its normalized spider polynomials satisfy s4=s8=1, contradicting the displayed o(1) bound.
remaining: Repair and verify the stopping/acceptance rule for rounded fourth-order candidates; a success probability for a trial does not justify accepting the first candidate passing a weak test.
Audit the full sharp matrix bounds and their SoS certificates after correcting the lemma statement.
Verify all rounding/bit-complexity and complete-component recovery guarantees; the cited ancillary low-degree lower-bound certificate was not checked.
issues: PDF 34 Lemma 6.4 omits the necessary constant 1: 2s4-s8<=o(1) is false already for one planted component. The subsequent argument only needs <=1+o(1), suggesting a repairable statement error.

PDF 31 Algorithm step 2 tests <T,vhat^tensor k>>=1-epsilon, while the fourth-order SoS constraint on the same page needs 1+m*mu-o(1). Uncorrelated vectors can exceed the former threshold above the spectral rank; the proof does not show that the first accepted BKS output has high planted correlation. This is a missing guarantee, not a demonstrated failure distribution for that sampler.

PDF 34 derives an O(1/n) noise bound for all m<=n^3 from moments of size m^{t/2}/n^{2t}; this calculation only supports a larger o(1) threshold near m=n^3. The weaker o(1) estimate needed by the argument may be repairable.

papers.title: Reed--Muller Codes are Optimal Binary Linear 3-Query LCCs
papers.authors: Oliver Janzer, Peter Manohar

review.title: Reed--Muller Codes are Optimal Binary Linear 3-Query LCCs
review.authors: Oliver Janzer, Peter Manohar
review.summary: Proves that a binary linear (3,δ,ε)-locally correctable code with ε<1/2 has block length n≥2^(Ω(δ⁷√k)). Thus constant-radius binary linear 3-query LCCs match the Reed–Muller exponent up to constants; the theorem does not cover nonlinear codes or merely locally decodable codes.
review.prior_frontier: Removes the remaining logarithmic loss from the prior Alrabiah–Guruswami lower bound, stated as 2^(Ω(√(k/log k))). Previously the matching √k exponent was known for design LCCs. Historical comparisons were read in the paper rather than independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Settles the optimal asymptotic exponent for binary linear 3-query local correction.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses a unique-colour cycle directly in a chain Kikuchi graph, avoiding the rainbow-cycle bottleneck and replacing earlier near-regular pruning with mixing and Eulerian expansion decomposition.
score_reasons.depth: Combines hypergraph-chain constraints, directed Eulerian expansion, random-walk colour distributions and a quotient-space iteration.
score_reasons.exposition: The overview explicitly identifies the two irregularities in prior arguments and the linearity/design boundaries.

checked: Checked the parity contradiction for an odd-coloured Kikuchi cycle using independent colour vectors.

Traced the new Eulerian expanding-subgraph decomposition conditional on the stated short-cycle fact: remove cycles to retain ≥δ²n²/2 edges, retain short cycles, and delete entire crossing cycles with total loss ≤δ²n²/8.
Verified the quotient-space iteration: each iteration removes ≥δ²n/8 nonzero coordinates and contributes O(δ^−12 log²n), giving k=O(δ^−14 log²n) and the stated δ⁷√k exponent.

Traced the full new LCC lower-bound proof: quotient iteration, Eulerian short-cycle expander extraction, lazy tuple completion, chain Kikuchi graph, local colour-variance pruning and random-matrix mixing.

Independently checked Lemma5.7: centre the columns of X, use R=2M-I column-stochastic with doubly stochastic mean; Jensen bounds the quadratic R term, and the symmetric-mean spectral gap bounds the cross term. Right multiplication contracts expected column variance by1-lambda2 even though individual M need not be doubly stochastic; independence justifies reverse-order induction.

Checked colour-variance normalization: each right vertex has2^r edges per colour, left degrees are2^r times conditional-walk coordinates, so V=4^r/(2(m+1)) times the pairwise squared distribution difference. Taking r=C n^2/(lambda^2 m^2)log m meets the pruning threshold.

Checked the pruning constants: at mostk/10 bad colours per vertex, Cauchy–Schwarz removes at most10/(9sqrt(10))<1/2 of the edges; deleting vertices of current degree<=original degree/6 costs at most|E|/3, leaving minimum colour degree>=k/60. The unique-colour-cycle induction then forces exponentially many graph vertices.

Checked the decomposition counts: cycle removal yields>=delta^2 n^2/2 Eulerian edges; short cycles of length<=24/delta^2 retain>=delta^2 n^2/4; deleting whole crossing cycles loses<=delta^2 n^2/8. Thus one piece has at leastdelta^2 n/8 vertices and cut densitydelta^4/96. Each quotient step costs O(delta^-12 log^2 n), and at most8/delta^2 steps give k=O(delta^-14 log^2 n).

Verified essential external statements against their primary texts: Kothari–Manohar arXiv:2311.00558 Definition2.3/Fact2.4 give the doubled-length padded normal form with delta/6; Huang–Ma–Shapira–Sudakov–Yuster Corollary1.3 gives the6|V|^2/|E| short directed cycle for simple Eulerian digraphs.
remaining: Established Cheeger inequality and the cited normal-form/short-cycle theorems were checked for applicability, not re-proved from scratch.

The main result is for binary linear3-query locally correctable codes, not general nonlinear codes or merely locally decodable codes. Constant correction radius and the explicit delta^7 dependence must be retained.
resolved_notes: Minor degenerate-case qualifications in auxiliary statements: Lemma5.3 needs a nonempty edge set (otherwise its conclusion fails for arbitrary unused colour palettes); its actual Kikuchi application is nonempty. Lemma4.1 should use log(2m), or assume m>=2, to include a singleton empty-transition instance. The main asymptotic proof can handle bounded-small n separately, so these do not obstruct the stated asymptotic main lower bound.

sources.detail: Definition2.3/Fact2.4 primary LCC normal-form statement checked.
Corollary1.3 short directed-cycle statement and proof hypothesis checked.

review.summary: Every Eulerian directed graph admits an O(n epsilon^-2)-edge reweighted Eulerian spectral sparsifier constructible in polynomial time. With polynomially bounded weight ratio, a nearly linear-time algorithm constructs O(n epsilon^-2 log n) edges with high probability.
review.prior_frontier: Previously fast Eulerian sparsification lost an extra logarithm compared with undirected sampling, and the best existential bound was also superlinear by logarithmic factors.

score_reasons.novelty: Nested effective-resistance certificates reuse heavier edges across lighter scales without accumulating a logarithmic loss.

checked: Read the scale-wise nested-partition construction and traced its concave regularized-volume potential.
Checked the total cut inequality C <= (1/20)(4.5m+1.5C), implying C<m/2.
Checked geometric summation of per-edge certificate weights across dyadic scales.
remaining: Full strong effective-resistance partition lemma and nearly linear construction.
Variance/degree-correction analysis giving linear-sized existence and fast n log n sparsifiers.
Resolve minor pseudocode indexing/exposition inconsistencies: the displayed loop goes from light to heavy, while the immediately following prose says heavy to light; its proof uses light to heavy.

review.title: Exact Agreement Expansion up to the Top via Non-polarity
review.authors: Tali Kaufman, Huy Tuan Pham
review.summary: Proves exact agreement for arbitrary finite-alphabet assignments on N-element top sets tested on n-element subfaces: equal inclusion probability ρ=n/N, a hypergeometric-type variance upper bound and conditioned singleton-walk gap γ imply soundness at most 8/γ+64(1−ρ)/(ργ²). Applications include all matroid bases with soundness O(k²/[h(k−h)]) and sparse Grassmannian posets; no higher layers are required.
review.prior_frontier: Prior general results required extra layers, two-sided expansion or additional link agreement hypotheses; prior matroid applications treated truncations or special linear matroids. The Grassmannian bound is generally O(q^(k−h)), improving to O(q) only under the additional local restricted-distance promise.

score_reasons.significance: Extends exact local-to-global consistency to top faces under weaker spectral assumptions, including bases of every matroid.
score_reasons.novelty: Regularized first-error exposure yields an exact-agreement estimate from one-sided singleton-link expansion without a two-sided or above-top structure.
score_reasons.depth: The central proof connects a spectral Dirichlet lower bound with a variance-controlled Hellinger comparison of local witness distributions.
score_reasons.exposition: The abstract framework states inclusion, variance, stationarity and gap assumptions explicitly and separates exact from approximate agreement.

checked: Fully traced Theorem 7: each non-majority label has mass ≤1/2, so its regularized indicator has variance at least half its second moment; summing spectral inequalities gives E≥ργV.
Checked the first-error distribution on a test face, its norm bound ≤ρ, and equality of witness distributions on every accepting pair.
Verified the pointwise square-root comparison, use of Var(Z)≤ρ(1−ρ)m, conditional-independence factor two, and the resulting E≤4ρτ+4(1−ρ)V/a.
Checked a=8(1−ρ)/(ργ), the integer-error bound V≥Pr[m>0]/(1+a), and exact soundness 8/γ+64(1−ρ)/(ργ²).
Traced the test-face deviation corollary and average-Hamming variant.
remaining: The main abstract theorem is checked; application-specific local-to-global walk bounds for matroids and Grassmannians remain external dependencies to verify.
The stronger local-distance theorem and companion LTC construction were not fully audited.

score_reasons.depth: The new combinatorics is compact but carefully maintains copy uniqueness, capacities and a decreasing polynomial potential through altered trees.
score_reasons.exposition: The complete intermediate proof, diagrams and explicit handling of private copy edges make the argument unusually transparent.

checked: Traced four-copy objective-preserving reduction conditional on the cited +2 congestion rounding; private capacity-one leaf edges prevent counting duplicate requests in one colour class.
Checked the packing lemma: at merge termination total load is at least 4q−1, contradicting load ≤4u+2 when q≥u+1.

Traced star contraction and the eleven-colour induction, then ten-colour bin relocation: ≥5 removed crossing paths and ≤1 newly crossing path decrease load by ≥4, while restoration adds at most one of each colour.
Verified the termination potential |E|+Σ|Path(f)| drops by at least three per relocation and polynomial representation does not scale with numerical capacities.

Checked the cited Edwards–Girão–van den Heuvel–Kang–Puleo–Sereni Theorem 9 against its original statement: Δ≤6 and k=10−Δ≥4 satisfy the line-graph degree condition and exclude both exceptions. The common-vertex/palette-permutation case is valid.

Precise local-tree coupling, graph cutoff and seeded-completion estimates.

remaining: Verify every local minimal-cover configuration, especially Y-wire and crossing gadgets, using the actual figures or finite enumeration.
Audit the transversal-CNOT construction, logical-effect interpretation claims and approximation appendices; verify the reused color-code gadgets from the cited recent work.

score_reasons.depth: The measure comparison is elegant but requires a precise finite-field GIP cylinder bound and explicit multiplicative codes.
score_reasons.exposition: The total-input encoding, one-sided error and fixed-player dependence are clearly presented.

checked: Traced the constant-cost coordinate protocol and the use of W’s distance.
Checked that fixing correction codewords and replacing factors by information-set coordinates preserves cylinder intersections and conditional uniform measure.
Verified that accepting inputs have density q^{-dim W}, while the cited GIP bound yields q^{-4k dim V} per cylinder, and checked the displayed parameter comparison.

Completed the main proof through Appendix A. For q a power of four in [(32k)^2,(64k)^2], Riemann–Roch with pole degrees 8r/sqrt(q)-1 and r/4-1 gives dim V>=6r/sqrt(q), dim W<=r/4, product closure V^{*k} subset W and distance(W)>=3r/4. Checked explicit rational evaluation points and their nonzero trace denominators in the second Garcia–Stichtenoth tower.

Checked the cited primary BDPW finite-field discrepancy bound (Theory of Computing 6, Fact 4.11): q=2^m, p=k and length ell dim V yield cylinder measure at most q^{-4k dim V} when ell=2^{k+2}k. Fixing corrections and passing to information sets preserves uniform conditional measure and the cylinder property; accepting density q^{-dim W} then gives communication >(r/8-1)log q.

Checked the explicitness dependency in the author-uploaded primary Shum et al. 2001 paper: Section IV-A and Theorem 7 construct one-point AG generator matrices in polynomial length for the second GS tower in even characteristic. The manuscript uses precisely this case and fixed alphabet. Riemann–Roch, genus and multiplicative pole-divisor applications were checked; the cited AG algorithm itself is an established dependency, not reproved here.

Filled the padding argument: n_j=Theta_k(r_j), r_{j+1}=sqrt(q)r_j, so consecutive available lengths differ by a bounded k-dependent factor. Ignore suffix bits above the largest suitable level; explicit level selection and generator construction remain polynomial, and the linear lower bound survives.
remaining: Central new construction and separation argument checked. Prior best explicit/nonconstructive comparison and the internal proof of the established AG generator algorithm were not independently reproved. Constants depend on fixed k; no ordinary language-class BPP-versus-NP separation is asserted.

remaining: The full low-eigenvalue block estimate, high-eigenvalue projected de Finetti dependency, soundness constant-1/4 argument and efficient symmetry measurements remain unaudited.

review.summary: Establishes last-iterate convergence for carefully damped exact simultaneous best responses in Bayesian second-price pacing/throttling models. The resulting rate is instance-dependent geometric convergence, not a uniform polynomial-round or sample-based guarantee.

The informal O(n log(1/ε)) statement must be read with the formal constants: the explicit τ_min can be extremely small in n and budget/support ratios.

score_reasons.depth: The analysis handles zero initial multipliers, caps and weakly binding budgets, then couples conditional-equilibrium regularity to a global descent argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Formal assumptions and rate constants are detailed, but unresolved cross-references and the much cleaner informal rate obscure substantial quantitative restrictions.

checked: Checked the response-floor argument from s_i(a)≤a/4 and finite entry into the positive invariant box.

Checked the spending-Jacobian representation, upper-triangular −s_i relation after endpoint sorting, and Euler homogeneity identity giving the P-matrix conditions.
Verified that the formal convergence envelope depends on θ=1−aτ_min/2 and a potentially enormous entry time, so it is not a uniform efficient convergence claim.
remaining: Verify the quantitative conditional-equilibrium and triangular-potential bounds, external univalence theorem, and the separate throttling analysis.
No robustness to estimated responses, asynchronous updates or delays is established by the checked pacing theorem.

review.prior_frontier: The stated best algorithmic ratio is 0.504, while 1−1/e was the conjectured optimum; this result proves a strict upper separation without identifying the optimum.

Checked the potential ALG+(N/e)average(max(r−1/12,0)), all first/middle/final phase bounds and the exact baseline integral.

Handled the terminal-removal caveat by replacing Lemma 3’s equality with an upper-bound inequality, since removing the final residual capped budget only lowers potential; all subsequent upper bounds remain valid. Padding by inactive advertisers handles N not divisible by the construction’s fixed modulus.
remaining: No unresolved substantive gap found in the main upper-bound argument; this is not a formal verification. The appendix’s independent exposition of the classical bound and historical prior bounds were not audited.
issues: Nonfatal formulation issue in Lemma 3: deleting the final advertiser need not preserve the average for an arbitrary algorithm that declines its last positive payment. The resulting potential drop is nonpositive, so replacing equality by ≤ suffices, or assume the last allocation is optimal without loss.

review.summary: Proves that every Boolean function on an arbitrary finite product alphabet has a coalition of O_epsilon(n/sqrt(log n)) coordinates forcing some fixed output with probability at least 1-epsilon. Verified the acknowledged subsequent stronger bound on the arXiv abstract of 2610.03086.
remaining: No formal proof-assistant verification.

Traced the good-subfamily extraction, majority preservation of witness avoidance, coverage and global/local candidate bounds, including infinite candidate sets handled via finite subsets.
Verified neighboring-sample maps in both directions: outputs agree on the shorter sample, rank rises for missing outputs, and at most two version spaces give preimages ≤[4(d+1)]^t.
Checked the candidate count, empirical-loss bound, LDim(U)=d and VC generalization yielding the main sample bound.
Traced the separate subspace-span map with B=1 and codimension rank, privacy on arbitrary samples, realizable no-false-positive utility and cancellation of d inside log(en/d).

review.title: An $O(1)$ Bound for the KLS Constant
review.authors: Zhao Song, Xinzhi Zhang
review.area: High-dimensional convex geometry and KLS conjecture
review.summary: Claims a dimension-independent Poincare constant for every isotropic log-concave probability measure, and hence a constant reciprocal Cheeger bound resolving KLS, including nonsmooth and bounded-support measures.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript compares against the prior (log n)^{1/4} reciprocal-Cheeger bound. This is a claimed resolution whose central polynomial-to-functional-inequality step has not yet been audited here.

score_reasons.significance: Would resolve a central conjecture with major consequences for concentration and convex-body sampling.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines stochastic localization of Appell pairings with repeated normalized differentiation to exploit all polynomial degrees.
score_reasons.depth: Variance/integral double induction and a dimension-free higher-order Bochner argument form a demanding long proof.
score_reasons.exposition: The overview exposes the two main bottlenecks and gives explicit normalization constants, but the main conclusion requires a complete specialist audit.

checked: Complete new polynomial-variance route, PDF pp. 13–15,21–37,64–70: checked Appell centering, differentiation/expansion and affine covariance; generating-function differentiation under linear tilts; duality between polynomial variance and Appell-pairing operator norm; uniform finite fixed-dimension coefficients from log-concave marginal tails and smooth approximation. Checked compact-support removal by moments through degree 2k.

Checked normalized stochastic localization in detail, pp. 24–31 and Appendix A.1/A.5: local parameter-SDE existence, density-ratio Ito cancellation, covariance noise S_i, sum S_i²≤8I from the external quadratic-form bound, log-det non-explosion and covariance positivity, E Gamma_t=e^(−t)I, covariance-normalized Appell drift, all inverse-covariance tensor-slot cross-variations. Recomputed exact energy drift −kG_k−2<R_k,N_k>+G_(k+1)−2 sum<W_i,V_i>+(P+Q)/2, leading to the stated (12k²+k) bound. Checked localization-energy integrability and vanishing terminal expectations before integration, rather than assuming the martingale term has mean zero.

Checked the complete double induction, pp. 31–37: I_1=Var f, the exact degree-one identity yields sqrt(I_2)≤sqrt(V)+sqrt(8V), hence I_2<16V; normalization by 256^k(k!)² gives v_k≤1/(64k²), i_k≤1/(1024k^4). Verified the convolution factorial cancellation, finite-supremum quadratic inequality, k=3 boundary inequality and advancement of both coefficient and integral estimates. This proves c_k≤16^k/(8k), with constants independent of dimension.

Complete operator/domain and iteration setup, pp. 17–21,38–45: checked compact resolvent through the confining Schrodinger form, identification of spectral gap with the locally-Lipschitz Poincare constant, graph-core cutoff/mollification and extended Bochner identity, domain preservation under inverse square roots, normalized-gradient/second-normalization recurrences, nonnegative energy drop chi, cumulative a V_N+X_N≤lambda P_N, and a≤lambda². Checked polynomial pairings by integration by parts, including why the recurrence controls only a permutation average.

Complete tensor-recovery machinery, pp. 46–55 and Appendix A.6: checked subset-incidence raising/lowering decomposition and exact squared singular values binom(q−j,s−j)binom(N−s−j,q−s), their minimum, and the tensor block-recovery coefficient. Verified normalization-error identity ||grad z_r||²=chi_r/beta_(r+1), adjacent derivative-slot swaps, propagation with fixed normalization scalars (without incorrectly commuting derivatives and inverse H), insertion-sort symmetrization bound, full-pairing comparison and dyadic factorial telescoping.

Complete cumulative-loss/curvature argument, pp. 56–63: checked convolution-kernel l1/l2 bound, startup dyadic-degree accounting, epsilon/L0/p*/R parameter inequalities, low-degree and high-degree tail splits, sqrt(lambda)W<1/4 and absorption of errors using X_N≤lambda P_N. Verified first-crossing bootstrap for normalization factors through ceil(lambda/a), contradiction between retained variance and energy loss, and final curvature bound uniform in dyadic degree. Taking degree to infinity at fixed positive curvature and then regular approximation yields CP≤2^85.

Primary dependency checks: official arXiv:2607.24164v1 Theorem 1.2 gives exactly Var(X^T B X)≤2 E||grad(X^T B X)||²=8 tr(B²) for every symmetric B and isotropic log-concave law. Checked Klartag 2023 Lemma 2.1 directly in the author PDF: arbitrarily close covariance and Poincare lower approximation by a smooth strongly log-concave measure with bounded Hessian; whitening preserves the required regularity. The external Cheeger/Poincare comparison is consistent with the same primary Letwin source.
remaining: This is an independent mathematical audit of the complete central new proof, not machine verification or a claim of community acceptance. The external Letwin quadratic-form theorem and Klartag regular-approximation theorem were checked for precise statements and applicability, not re-proved in full. Standard stochastic-calculus, elliptic-regularity and spectral theorems remain imported background.

The proof establishes a dimension-free universal constant (explicitly CP≤2^85); it does not optimize that constant or provide a new implemented convex-body sampler. Expository historical/application claims were not all independently re-audited.

Read the separate n-1 corruption simulation using adaptively well-formed functionality randomness.

score_reasons.significance: Provides the first polynomial-degree abelian Cayley local spectral expanders at arbitrary fixed link quality in dimension two.
score_reasons.novelty: Algebraic-curve evaluation directions simultaneously avoid hyperplanes and support exponentially many independent maximal-minor functions affine along those directions.
score_reasons.depth: The construction balances binary kernel dimension with real link spectra, using field traces, tensor evaluation injectivity and Riemann–Roch spaces.

checked: Checked the trace embedding into the binary kernel and the separation argument excluding row-space words of weight one or two.
Traced the categorical-product link spectrum using additive characters, including the negative eigenvalue bound and connectivity.

Verified the binomial minor count and exponent comparison log₂(27/4)>8/3, yielding exponential kernel dimension and polynomial Cayley degree for fixed field.
remaining: Verify the Garcia–Stichtenoth tower parameters, Riemann–Roch dimensions, exact explicit-construction runtime and quotient-complex simplicity/face accounting.
Audit the separate weighted graph-product construction and its negative-spectrum estimate, and trace the cited geometric-integrality dependency.

review.title: AQUI-GuaRD: Algorithmic Safety and Concentration Bounds for Constrained Control under Adversarial PDE Dynamics
review.authors: Jean Rosemond Dora, Ladislav Hluchý
review.summary: Proposes a PDE-constrained reinforcement-learning framework with quadratic-program safety projection, exponential violation tails, VC-based sample bounds, NP-hardness and dynamic regret. The central safety and complexity claims are only sketches and lack the hypotheses and constructions needed to establish them.
review.prior_frontier: Combines existing barrier certificates, Galerkin approximation and martingale tools; the manuscript does not provide a verifiable derivation of its advertised new joint guarantees.

score_reasons.significance: Safety under uncertain PDE dynamics is important, but the stated guarantee is not established by this submission.
score_reasons.novelty: No precise new theorem is supported beyond invoking standard tools in a proposed pipeline.
score_reasons.depth: The required exponential supermartingale estimate, hard-instance construction and regret reduction are absent.
score_reasons.exposition: The manuscript repeatedly calls sketches rigorous but leaves core objects, constants and assumptions unspecified.

checked: Inspected all nine pages and rendered page 5 to verify Eq. (7): P(sup M_t≥ε)≤E[M_0^+]/ε is asserted for a martingale error process. This is false as stated: M_0=0 and M_1=±1 with equal probability gives 1/2≤0 at ε=1.

The compensated exponential process in Theorem 6.1 is not shown nonnegative, and no exponential initial-moment or quadratic-variation bound yielding e^{-ακ} is established. A lower ellipticity bound alone does not provide the claimed variance upper control.

Theorem 8.1 gives no actual polynomial-size reduction/gadgets or completeness/soundness argument; Theorem 8.5 does not establish the claimed relation from conductivity variation to comparator variation.
remaining: Substantial new hypotheses and complete proofs are required for the safety, sample-complexity, hardness and regret claims; these cannot be treated as a routine omitted technical appendix.
issues: The displayed Eq. (7) martingale bound is false under the stated assumptions; the proposed process is not shown to meet the missing nonnegativity condition.
Theorem 6.1’s e^{-ακ} dependence is asserted without the needed quantitative stochastic estimate; Theorems 6.3/6.4 and 8.1/8.5 contain no complete lower-bound, reduction or regret proofs.

review.desk_reject_reason: Essential mathematical proofs are missing. PDF page 5 uses a false-as-stated maximal inequality in the main safety proof, while pages 6–7 merely assert Fano packings, a 3-SAT reduction and a drift-to-regret relation without constructing them. This is manuscript-grounded proof insufficiency, not a judgment about the application area.

checked: Traced universal-state domination, the history-conditioned relative-entropy telescoping, fidelity-to-trace-distance step and Markov bound O(s/(mε²)), conditional on the recovery-map theorem.

papers.authors: Zimo Sheng, Mingyu Xiao

review.title: A Near-Linear Element-Kernel for d-Hitting Set
review.authors: Zimo Sheng, Mingyu Xiao
review.summary: For fixed d≥3, gives a randomized one-sided-error d-Hitting Set kernel with O_d(k log³k) elements, O_d(k^d log^(2d−2)k) sets and parameter O_d(k log³k), in expected polynomial time. Separately gives a deterministic O_d(k^(7/4) log^(3/2)k)-element kernel. Output elements re-encode assignments and need not be original elements.
review.prior_frontier: The stated prior element bound was O(k^(d−1)); the result does not beat the known k^(d−ε) bit-compression barrier because it retains many sets. Historical priority was not independently rechecked.

score_reasons.significance: Almost linearizes the universe size for every fixed hyperedge rank, breaking the quadratic rank-three frontier.
score_reasons.novelty: Shared address tables encode a small hitting set while conditional checks preserve clause width d and avoid a separate variable per input element.
score_reasons.depth: Two-level separation, cardinality circuits and bounded-width distributive expansion balance element and set complexity; deterministic hashing requires a further parameter tradeoff.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly distinguishes universe size, output parameter, bit size, one-sided error and non-subinstance kernels.

checked: Traced the random separation bound: B≈k/log k, bucket capacity O(log k), O(log k) candidate second-level hashes, and success at least49/64.
Checked the shared-table injection invariant and both directions of the satisfiability/hitting-set equivalence, including local choices that differ from the selected bucket hashes.
Verified clause width≤d, t^(d−1)L^(d−1) clauses per input set, O(k+Btq₂L) variables and resulting randomized bounds.
Checked the stated pair-variable d-CNF-to-hitting-set conversion and parameter inflation.

Traced both complete re-encoding constructions. The balanced binary-counter circuit has O(N) gates because sum_j N(j+1)/2^(j+1)=O(N); Tseitin constraints preserve width3. A maximal packing supplies a directly represented element in every set, which is essential to keeping later clauses at width d.

Rechecked randomized one-sided correctness: fixed-solution bucket overflow <=1/8, t independent second-level candidates fail any bucket <=1/8, success>=49/64>3/4. Shared-table addresses permit at most one decoded element per active cell. Conditional checks for unselected local hash choices are automatically true; distributing the OR of conjunctions uses only L^(d-1)t^(d-1) clauses per set.

Traced deterministic Lemma5.1: the polynomial two-evaluation/linear-combination family has B^3 functions, pair collision count B(B-z)+Bz^2, yielding total squared bucket deviation <=(a^2+1)(k/B)^2 when B<=sqrt(k). Therefore some hash has every load at mostceil((a+2)k/B).

Traced the self-contained Beneš permutation-network induction and evaluation-table completeness/soundness. Distinct stored polynomials have at most r-1 agreements; an unhit set of at most d elements can falsely match at most db(r-1)<q evaluation points, so one mandatory clause fails.

Checked q=Theta_d(b), Bq rows times O_d(b log^2 k) gates, hence N=O_d(kB^3+(k^2/B)log^2 k); balancing B=Theta(k^(1/4)sqrt(log k)) yields k^(7/4)log^(3/2)k elements and k^(d+3/2)log k sets. The final variable-pair reduction has parameter N and does not preserve input k.

Checked the preliminary kernel statement directly against van Bevern arXiv:1112.2310 Theorem2 and its deletion-based final step: O_d(k^(d-1)) vertices, O_d(k^d) edges in polynomial time, with unchanged target hitting-set size.
remaining: The established preliminary kernel is used as an external theorem; its full original matching/crown proof was not re-proved.

Main-proof-checked covers Theorems1.1–1.2. The ancillary subhypergraph-kernel lower bound relies on the cited Dell–van Melkebeek compression theorem, whose exact hypotheses were not independently audited.

The near-linear result is randomized with one-sided error in expected polynomial time; both constructions re-encode the universe and increase the output parameter. They are not parameter-preserving or bit-sparsification kernels.

sources.detail: Primary preliminary-kernel dependency; Theorem2 and final deletion construction checked.

papers.authors: Kean Chen, Aadil Oufkir

review.title: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the near-boundary regime
review.authors: Kean Chen, Aadil Oufkir
review.summary: Characterizes coherent channel-tomography query complexity near the dimension boundary: for Kraus rank at most r and dilation ratio tau=rd2/d1>1, diamond error epsilon already requires Theta(rd1d2/epsilon^2), while tau=1 permits Heisenberg scaling. Choi trace error has the gradual transition Theta(d1^2/epsilon + min{(tau-1)d1^2,(tau-1)^2d1^2d2^2}/epsilon^2). Upper bounds use parallel queries; lower bounds allow sequential adaptive coherent protocols. Exact lower-bound statements require sufficiently small universal epsilon; no efficient implementation is claimed.
review.prior_frontier: Prior work settled the boundary and constant-distance regime but left shrinking tau-1 unresolved; previous diamond lower bounds lost a squared tau-1 factor.

score_reasons.significance: Completes the parameter regime of a central quantum learning problem and distinguishes two genuinely different phase transitions.
score_reasons.novelty: Range-versus-basis averaging and low-rank Kraus reshaping remove the near-boundary loss.
score_reasons.depth: Combines Schur–Weyl block comparison, Grassmannian packing, and separate estimator error components.
score_reasons.exposition: Forty pages state the coherent model and small-error ranges explicitly; algorithmic implementation remains an open problem.

checked: Checked Lemma3.2 error conversion: reshaped out-of-image error has rank at most min(r,alpha*d2); operator norm of reshaped isometry is at most sqrt(d2), giving the stated nuclear-norm cross-term bound and normalized Choi error.

Traced Lemma5.9 diamond separation: Weyl twirling chooses an output unitary whose overlap with the fixed isometry block is large; a two-branch entangled input exposes the off-diagonal cross term, and pinching gives diamond distance >= ||P-Q||op/sqrt(8).
Read the comb domination and Schur dimension-ratio roadmap; near-boundary lower theorem explicitly assumes epsilon<=1/(8e^(3/2)sqrt(8)) for diamond and <=10^-12 for Choi.
remaining: Covariant estimator moment bounds, complete comb block domination, good-set construction and packing volumes have not been audited. The cited dilation-reduction theorem has not been independently checked.

score_reasons.depth: Bridges labeled and unlabeled chains, spectral comparison, continuous intertwining and representation of symmetric twirling by a classical partition chain.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly marks symmetric-subspace and nonadaptive restrictions and separates the small-particle and very-large-particle arguments.

Checked reverse edge-partition construction and the invariant that equal mass on current parts is maintained except at split events.
remaining: Large-proof exception:79-page interacting-particle/quantum-development. The beta-binomial projection, two local coupling rules and reverse partition invariant were traced. The covariance comparison, global coupling estimates and quantum/cryptographic consequences remain unchecked.
Trace the full covariance contraction and two-particle spectral comparison.
Finish large-t discrepancy/low-mass probability bounds and continuous intertwining; audit the symmetric-twirling identification and cryptographic reduction.

papers.title: Autoregressive Distribution Learning and Universal Compression
papers.authors: Shuichi Hirahara, Mikito Nanashima

review.title: Autoregressive Distribution Learning and Universal Compression
review.authors: Shuichi Hirahara, Mikito Nanashima
review.summary: Shows polynomial-time autoregressive distribution learning is equivalent to universal compression and entropy estimation of uniformly random prefixes. For prefix-closed distribution classes this is equivalent to evaluator learning and compression even without efficient decoding. The entropy estimator has completeness on the target class but soundness on every distribution; compression redundancy is m^(1-gamma) for fixed gamma>0. Additional generator-learning equivalence is for the full class of P/poly-samplable distributions.
review.prior_frontier: Autoregressive learning readily implies compression; the converse fails generally under one-way functions. Random-prefix compression provides an exact characterization rather than asserting equivalence for arbitrary full-sample compression.

score_reasons.significance: Connects efficient next-symbol prediction with fundamental compression and entropy tasks through an exact class-level characterization.
score_reasons.novelty: Uniform random truncation resolves the one-way-function obstruction and identifies a robust prefix-closed equivalence.
score_reasons.depth: The hard direction combines multi-sample entropy distinguishers, a hybrid reduction and constructive conditional pseudoentropy prediction.
score_reasons.exposition: The definitions distinguish arbitrary-distribution soundness, efficient encoding versus decoding, and restrictions on generator equivalence.

checked: Checked compression-to-entropy construction: prefix-free lengths obey Kraft; cap against a trivial code; average independent bounded code lengths; KL nonnegativity gives universal soundness and Hoeffding gives high probability.

Traced the central hybrid reduction: replacing only the next symbol preserves the context marginal, raises full entropy by conditional entropy, and loses a factor r in the gap tester advantage. Choosing r polynomial in target accuracy invokes the constructive prediction lemma.

Read the exact claim that Vadhan–Zheng Algorithm2 is uniform at every length and can select entropy-ball radii without knowing conditional entropy. This external dependence is essential, not independently certified here.
remaining: Large-proof exception (55 pages). The compression-to-entropy and next-symbol hybrid reductions were traced. The constructive oracle theorem, all-length uniformity and the remaining equivalences form a separate unresolved verification workload; no complete equivalence theorem clearance is implied.

Verify Vadhan–Zheng constructive oracle and quantifier compatibility in the primary source; finish chain-rule high-probability conversion, deterministic compression derandomization, evaluator and generator equivalences.

Learning hardness concerns two-hidden-layer ReLU networks and specified classically evaluable improper hypotheses, not quantum-query PRF security.

score_reasons.significance: A worst-case-lattice foundation for fixed-parameter TC0 post-quantum pseudorandomness would be a substantial advance.

Checked the final clipping/conditioning argument assuming the Fourier and moment bounds: clipping changes endpoint mass by E|W-V|; conditioning on the charge hyperplane of mass1/q costs O(q); bounded rejection needs O(q log1/delta) trials.
Read the fixed-family versus fixed-accuracy distinction: each inverse-polynomial accuracy order has its own polynomial-time calibration sampler, but q,d and rounding map stay fixed.
remaining: Large-proof exception (137 pages). The algebraic LAR reduction, conditional invertibility and final clipping/conditioning/rejection estimates were checked. review.title: Time/Space Hardness from Lattice Problems
review.authors: Damiano Abram, Giulio Malavolta, Lawrence Roy
review.summary: From the specified Decomposed SIS hardness assumption constructs correlation-intractable functions yielding average-case memory hardness and sequentiality, hence P!=L, P!=NC, and a proper uniform NC hierarchy. The assumption is a structured/extended SIS variant with parameter-specific extension width and short-solution bound beta<q; it is not claimed from ordinary SIS or ordinary worst-case SVP. Homomorphic lattice encodings support iteration without fixing a depth cap or bootstrapping.
review.prior_frontier: Sequential and memory-hard primitives previously largely relied on dedicated resource assumptions. This derives them from a one-wayness assumption against unrestricted polynomial-time algorithms, with a related SuperSVP foundation rather than standard lattice hardness.

score_reasons.significance: Connects conventional average-case hardness with qualitative separations inside P and an entire NC hierarchy.
score_reasons.novelty: A composable read primitive avoids depth-driven encoding growth and permits a diagonal correlation-intractability argument.
score_reasons.depth: The reduction must preserve exact key distributions, bounded corrections and a guaranteed nonzero SIS witness.
score_reasons.exposition: Thirty pages separate public fast iteration from O(T)-time correction extraction and specify the precise structured assumption.

checked: Traced the new homomorphic-read assembly: balanced matrix products, concatenation before normalization, and affine-coefficient propagation produce a correction recurrence polynomial in the encoded length per squaring level, rather than per simulated time step.

Checked the space-CI extraction algebra: programmed W and U_h hide the selected computation; combine output coordinates, subtract the hash identity, and obtain extended-SIS vector (H,K,-1), so nonzeroness is unconditional.

Checked diagonalization on the hash key itself and the NC hierarchy argument: T=log^(j+1)lambda exceeds NCj depth while public evaluation lies in NC^(j+rho+1); an adjacent-level collapse gives a contradiction.

Extended the audit through the exact homomorphic-read construction and time-CI proof (pp13–26). The balanced affine product reads a Boolean encoded address; concatenate summand programs before normalization, assemble n² matrix entries with e_r e_s^T, and add the old table correction at f(alpha). This establishes the new invariant conditional on normalization and multi-hop evaluation Theorems4.3–4.5. The balanced depth gives multiplicative correction growth per logarithmic read layer, and repeated squaring gives the stated logT-layer recurrence rather than T-layer growth.

Checked affine-mask propagation and both CI reductions: uniform auxiliary matrices plus G^{-1} program exactly uniform key bits, independently conditional on the base key. The space construction shifts only h=ceil(log2T) to G+U_h and relies on fixed halting configurations; the depth construction programs every routing bit and NAND/copy selector, then propagates every mask. Combining designated output coordinates and subtracting the hash equation yields (H,K,-1), guaranteeing a nonzero bounded vector without an unjustified nonzero-error assertion.

Checked bounded-depth layering, public parallel evaluation and the hierarchy contradiction: fixed-key field lengths and kappa=ceil(loglambda)^2 dominate any polynomial circuit width; T_j=log^{j+1}lambda dominates the hypothesized NC^j depth. The public evaluation has depth T_j polylogN, and the standard adjacent-level collapse yields strict NC hierarchy only under the stated parameter-specific ExtDSIS assumptions.

Final dependency availability check: bibliography p27 identifies Tree Encodings I/II only by title and year; PDF has no external URI annotations. Roy's author page identifies ePrint2026/741 and2026/1140, and their official ePrint records confirm the exact revised titles and September18 versions. The supplied manuscript states precise imported interfaces in Lemmas4.1–4.3/Theorems4.4–4.5, but gives no proofs for them. Theorems1.1–1.3 assume Decomposed SIS hardness and treat the encoding interfaces as established results, rather than additional conjectural hypotheses.

score_reasons.significance: Completes a major general-graph counting-complexity classification if the extensive remaining cases hold.
score_reasons.novelty: Conserved Hamming imbalance creates mountain signatures; binary transfer groups and matching-product reconstruction handle the remaining height cases.

score_reasons.exposition: The paper distinguishes direct gadgets from Turing simulation and exact algebraic recognition from fixed-signature evaluation, but checking all dependencies is substantial.

checked: Traced mountain construction F.5.2 conditional on the endpoint-preserving self-loop dependency: positive zero-sum combinations turn Bézout coefficients nonnegative, yielding both signs of the gcd.

Checked the explicit EXACT4_3/EXACT4_1 example explaining that reduction-versus-gadget distinction.
Inspected preservation of two-sidedness, factor closure and whole-set basis changes; read the height-one transfer-group and contraction-pencil roadmap.
