review.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent
review.authors: Yuhan Ye, Kaizhao Liu
review.summary: For smooth convex objectives and any predetermined nonnegative gradient-descent stepsize schedule, proves worst-case error n^(-p_sil-o(1)), p_sil=log2(1+sqrt2), matching the silver exponent. Also matches the anytime exponent 2p_sil/(1+p_sil) up to o(1), meaning infinitely many bad horizons for a single infinite schedule. The hard objective and dimension may depend on the schedule; this is not a lower bound for adaptive stepsizes or accelerated methods.
review.prior_frontier: Best nonnegative-schedule lower exponents were about1.4500 finite-horizon and1.1837 anytime, compared with silver upper exponents1.2716 and1.1195.

score_reasons.significance: Determines the optimal polynomial acceleration exponent available from nonnegative predetermined GD stepsizes.
score_reasons.novelty: Bends a local trajectory to reduce the checkpoint-transfer denominator coefficient toward one.
score_reasons.depth: Combines convex projection geometry and Moreau interpolation with an extremal recursive checkpoint analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: The model restrictions and anytime quantifiers are explicit, with a 33-page construction and appendices.

checked: Traced the local Moreau-envelope construction: a finite convex hull of selected arc slopes has the same projection at the constructed trajectory points; scaling its support function realizes the prescribed gradients with Lipschitz constant one.
Checked the backward arc projection criterion and the slope-potential telescoping bound A(sigma)=sigma+sqrt(1+sigma^2), which bounds unwanted second-coordinate drift independently of gap length.
Read the chained transfer ratio (b-2)/(c(a+s)) and activation conditions; each coordinate occurs in at most two half-scaled components, explaining global smoothness.
remaining: Complete backward-trajectory coordinate inequalities, inactive-region verification, checkpoint extremal recursion, quantitative a-versus-exponent balance and anytime horizon argument remain to audit.

review.authors: Tomohiro Koana, Soh Kumabe

score_reasons.significance: Breaks a longstanding general directed Hamiltonicity exponential-base barrier.
score_reasons.novelty: Nonuniform random arc duplication/deletion preserves a nonzero grouped path polynomial with probability (49/50)^(n−1), enabling cheap group isolation.
score_reasons.depth: Combines a sharp polynomial cancellation lemma with randomized linear-system enumeration and weighted determinant sums.
score_reasons.exposition: Short, complete arguments expose both success probability and enumeration cost, including conversion to one-sided error.

checked: Traced the entire new argument: Lemma 6 leading-monomial rank bound, induction giving survival (1−δ)^(n−1), and isolation over group tuples with odd counts.
Checked weighted Matrix–Tree inclusion–exclusion, including arbitrary added arcs from t: surviving trees have every internal vertex non-leaf and hence t as their unique leaf.
Verified OR-to-random-XOR sampling probability, expected one solution for fixed coefficients over R, cutoff and coverage bounds; n≥4 union-bound arithmetic holds.
Checked (15/8)(50/49)=375/196<1.9133, error amplification across exponentially many trials and self-reduction to a checked cycle.

Reviewed the exact standard isolation-lemma application (N group elements and weights 1..2N); its per-element critical-weight union bound gives 1/2. Primary BKK17 source inspected for the Laplacian framework.
80 independently generated weighted digraph tests on n=3..6 verified the determinant inclusion–exclusion identity with extra t-arcs; saved check811.py. These are sanity checks, not the proof.
remaining: No formal verification or full implementation benchmark; standard Matrix–Tree and polynomial-time determinant algorithms used as established dependencies rather than re-proving their general theory.

review.authors: Chaoqiang Fu, Daofeng Li, Yifan Su
review.summary: For persistent faulty pair identities with total fault budget s=Θ(n), near-optimal continuous rank estimation costs Θ(min{n²,n log n+nh}), while public certification at precision τ costs Θ(min{n²,n log n+nh+n/τ}); h faults may be selected online. Accuracy is squared rank error just above an explicit complete-table threshold U. Public guarantees hold for every compatible ranking.
review.prior_frontier: Separates actual estimation from version-space certification, extending persistent-fault sorting beyond compatible-set completion. This is neither independent random comparison noise nor repeated fresh comparisons; outputs are continuous rank estimates.

score_reasons.significance: Gives a sharp quantitative distinction between being accurate and publicly certifying accuracy under persistent adversarial faults.
score_reasons.novelty: Separates the costs of order resolution, online support selection and public precision while preserving the leading complete-information error.
score_reasons.depth: Uses inverse-distance sampling with a uniform faulty-flow bound, compatible-reference certificates and relocation lower bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The model states when identities and replies are chosen, cache semantics, hard budgets and continuous-output qualifications explicitly.

checked: Checked uniform faulty-coefficient Lemma3.2 via symmetrization, scalar contraction and E||sum ξa_ex_e||≤sqrt(sum E a_e²||x_e||²), producing4sqrt(V_E).
Traced score-correction decomposition into sampling noise, adversarial flow and short-distance residual conditional on warm history.
Verified projection nonexpansiveness, (1+3δ/16)²≤1+δ and the harmonic-query/abort accounting for fixed supports, conditional on the warm-order guarantee.
remaining: Audit warm-order construction, complete-information extremal lower bound, online excess-weight extension and public certificate/relocation matching bounds.

review.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent: The Strongly Convex Case
review.authors: Kaizhao Liu, Yuhan Ye
review.summary: For smooth strongly convex functions of condition number kappa and any predetermined nonnegative GD schedule, proves iteration complexity Omega(kappa^(1/p_sil-o(1))*log(1/epsilon)) for either squared distance or relative objective error. More explicitly the gap to silver is exp(O(sqrt(log kappa)))*log kappa. Schedules may depend on kappa and the finite horizon, but not on observed gradients; dimensions are unrestricted.
review.prior_frontier: The classical sqrt(kappa)*log(1/epsilon) lower bound for broader first-order methods did not establish optimality of silver-step GD. The authors earlier proved the corresponding convex exponent but quadratic contraction prevents a direct transfer.

score_reasons.significance: Matches the polynomial condition-number exponent and epsilon dependence for predetermined-step strongly convex GD.
score_reasons.novelty: Repairs excessive accumulated unselected steps and bridges between repair and bending components to retain the lower-bound chain.
score_reasons.depth: Controls both multiplicative excess and threshold ratios while counting overlap of repair intervals.
score_reasons.exposition: The 47-page manuscript clearly states nonnegative stepsizes and distinguishes general first-order algorithms and quadratic objectives.

checked: Checked Lemma5.1 conditional assembly: maximizing-checkpoint inequalities bound cumulative quadratic-contraction loss below1/2; multiplying bridge and bending ratios retains at least one eighth of the score and a bounded final threshold/excess ratio.

Checked Lemma5.2 repair overlap: if the next last checkpoint were inside the previous repair interval, the new total mass would be at most two residual tails, contradicting its S0 threshold. Thus each index appears at most twice; concavity bounds total logarithmic repair loss.
Traced the two simultaneous induction estimates in LemmaC.1 ensuring either a dominant step or two sizable steps with intervening mass below both.
remaining: The bending, repair and bridge local-function constructions, all repair quantitative constants, recursive checkpoint bound and global parameter optimization remain unaudited. The separate conversion for relative objective error also remains.

review.title: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II

review.area: Quantum nonlocality; graph coloring; hardness reductions
review.summary: For every d≥4, ε>0 and context radius k, constructs a d-to-1 game of classical value<ε with a perfect finite-dimensional k-compatible quantum strategy. score_reasons.significance: Would resolve the basic boundedness question for the quantum chromatic gap, already at the smallest possible quantum color count.
score_reasons.novelty: Stretched magic-square wires create arbitrarily large commuting neighborhoods, enabling quantum completeness to survive a classical PCP/hardness reduction chain.
score_reasons.depth: Combines local projector algebra, tensor repetition, multilayer Kneser hypergraphs and the intricate Fei–Minzer–Wang reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly separates classical soundness from quantum completeness and tracks context radius and finite-dimensionality through the chain.

Traced FMW quantum completeness and context preservation conditional on the stated support geometry: nearby questions yield nearby vertices in each register.

review.title: Splay trees are almost dynamically optimal
review.authors: Petr Chmel, Bernhard Haeupler, Richard Hladík, Michal Koucký, Antti Roeyskoe, Václav Rozhoň, Ondřej Sladký, Robert E. Tarjan
review.summary: Proves splay-tree access cost O((OPT+n)*log log n*(log log log n)^2) from any initial splay tree, against the offline dynamic BST optimum. Also proves the split conjecture within the same polyloglog factor. This is a first sublogarithmic competitive bound for splay trees, not constant-factor dynamic optimality; the additive n factor is essential for arbitrary initialization.
review.prior_frontier: Other BSTs such as Tango achieved O(log log n) competitiveness, but splay trees themselves had only O(log n) despite four decades of partial optimality results.

score_reasons.significance: Major progress on a central long-standing data-structure conjecture for the original natural algorithm.
score_reasons.novelty: Charges directly to a normalized offline tree using lazy intervals, rather than the non-tight interleave lower bound.
score_reasons.depth: Adapts pairing-heap amortization while controlling rank changes from offline rotations and zig-zag bends.
score_reasons.exposition: The 78-page proof has a useful warm-up explicitly labeled informal and precise additive/model guarantees, but several substantial dependencies require audit.

checked: Read exact Theorem1 including arbitrary initialization and additive n; identified the required normal form: ribless logarithmic-depth comparator and rotations at constant depth, with constant-factor overhead.

Traced Lemmas20–24 conditional on earlier structural invariants: a transferred shrinking interval cannot acquire new bends; all but six heap-children in an unbroken interval are hit by internal zig-zigs, giving geometric shrinkage. Important boundary pairings per interval are O(log G), hence paid operations u+O(ell log G+cost(T*)).
Checked why riblessness bounds the depth difference between a key and its neighboring null leaves, needed to charge zig-zags.
remaining: Large-proof exception (78 pages). The local interval-shrinkage/pairing charge and the riblessness depth comparison were traced under their stated structural invariants. Comparator normalization, global invariant maintenance and the final potential cancellation are still necessary for almost dynamic optimality and are not certified.

The comparator-normalization theorem, full lazy-interval operation invariants, pairing-heap interface and bad-pairing bound, zig-zag accounting, final potential balance and split extension all need a full audit. The informal static warm-up is not treated as proof clearance.

checked: Traced all construction and decoder arguments, including equal-length interval edit-distance contraction using paired alignment columns with indices ν≤iν,jν≤ν+δ.

score_reasons.novelty: A common convex duality organizes simultaneous search for hard operators and rounding functions, then separates heuristic search from rigorous certification.
score_reasons.depth: The certification reduces dimension-independent Gaussian optimization to moment inequalities, semidefinite bounds, interpolation errors and thousands of finite checks.
score_reasons.exposition: Search, exact decimals, theorem endpoints and unproved heuristic estimates are clearly distinguished; the numerical proof burden is large.

Verified convexity of Φ makes endpoint interval checks sufficient, and the finite-sign reduction uses convexity and positive interpolation weights.
Read the exact degree21 operator and32-component upper-rounding construction and the stated numerical certification interfaces.
remaining: Large computational-proof exception: obtain, inspect and independently rerun the RealGrothendieck interval/PSD certificates, all interval coverage and tail inequalities, and the upper-rounding Hermite coefficient/tail bounds.
Audit asymptotic graded-Gaussian compactness and matrix discretization dependencies in full. Neither numerical endpoint nor the≈1.779 heuristic is independently certified by this review.

papers.title: A Quadratic Lower Bound for Noncommutative Circuits
papers.authors: Sophus Valentin Willumsgaard, Pratik Shastri

review.title: A Quadratic Lower Bound for Noncommutative Circuits
review.authors: Pratik Shastri, Sophus Valentin Willumsgaard
review.summary: Proves an optimal Omega(n*d) product-gate lower bound for arbitrary fan-in-two noncommutative circuits computing the degree-2d palindrome polynomial in 2n variables, without homogeneity or syntactic-degree restrictions. Thus d=n gives a quadratic lower bound. The same argument applies to any degree-2d polynomial in n variables whose middle coefficient matrix has full rank. A functional-ring corollary additionally invokes a transfer theorem.
review.prior_frontier: The general explicit linear-degree bound had long been Omega(n log n); concurrent work gave Omega(n^1.5). Earlier quadratic bounds required homogeneous circuits.

score_reasons.significance: Breaks a long-standing general noncommutative circuit lower-bound barrier and gives the tight size for an explicit family.
score_reasons.novelty: Projecting the coefficient-spanning set after expanding constant terms removes the syntactic-degree restriction.
score_reasons.depth: The central insight is a small ordered-subset spanning family rather than a bound on the raw number of circuit paths.
score_reasons.exposition: Ten pages contain the complete elementary main proof with no computational certificate or large technical appendix.

checked: Checked coefficient-span induction even when internal gates are not XY-separated: (ab)_XY=a_X*b_XY+(a_XY-a_X)*b_Y. Coefficients of nonempty Y words in the second term remain linear combinations of a-side coefficients.

Checked the path characterization and ordered-subset counting. Each path contributes products of X-only left siblings at right-branch product gates; expand each into constant and positive-degree parts. Degree-d projection kills every term using more than d positive-degree factors. A topological ordering fixes the product order for each gate subset, so at most sum_{k<=d} binom(S,k) spanning vectors remain, regardless of syntactic degree or sharing. Scalar edge weights do not change spans.

Compared this with the n^d independent palindrome coefficients. For d<=S/2, the binomial estimate yields S>=nd/(2e). For d>S/2, the sharper immediate bound n^d<=2^S implies n<4 and S>=d log2(n), giving Omega(nd) uniformly for n>=2.

Checked the one-variable-set extension by substituting x_i+y_i: coefficients of Y-words of length d, then projection onto X-degree d, reproduce the full-rank middle matrix. The substitution adds only n sum gates and no product gates.
remaining: The functional lower bound over a free noncommutative ring uses Raz2026 transfer theorem; that external theorem was not re-proved or source-checked in this audit. The symbolic main result is self-contained.

review.title: A polynomial scaling window for random k-SAT and a proof of the satisfiability conjecture
review.authors: Gaia Carenini
review.summary: For every fixed k≥3, the random signed k-SAT unsatisfiability hitting time has variance O_k(n^(1+2/k)), giving O_k,η(n^(1/2+1/k)) scaling windows and existence of a limiting threshold density α_k. Does not identify the numerical threshold or give an efficient SAT algorithm.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the author’s n/log n window bound and extends threshold existence beyond the previous sufficiently-large-k theorem; primary Aldous variance inequality and Perkins Proposition 14 formulation of the Abbe–Montanari criterion were inspected.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves limiting-threshold existence for every fixed k≥3 and gives polynomial window control.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses forced-variable hazards, a Poisson shorter-clause interpolation, concave occupation potential and structured-cover variance inequality.
score_reasons.depth: A compact but powerful combination of exact deletion identities and probabilistic interpolation replaces cluster analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully distinguishes terminal selection bias, fresh continuation lifetime, window width and threshold convergence; the argument is unusually explicit.

checked: Traced the full new argument. Verified ρ_j=binom(ℓ,j)/(2^j binom(n,j)) and the necessary finite-size additive term in the shorter-clause comparison.
Checked Poisson derivative/Jensen interpolation, minimization cv^(k/(k−1))−av≥−A a^k, submultiplicative survival giving Q(t,0)≤t/r, and t=r^(1/k).
Verified the concave potential telescopes using E[r_next]=r−1; independent Poisson splitting after deleting one variable yields the exact 2q(1−q) forced-variable identity.
Checked early-time occupation O(n^(1/k)), exponentially small late tail, and terminal weighting ρ_k r≤a_n^(1/k)ℓ/(2n), giving O(n^(2/k)) terminal lifetime.

Verified Aldous 1991 Theorem 1(b) in the author-hosted original: Var(T)≤κ ET E[c(terminal set)]. Checked Perkins Proposition 14 and the original Abbe–Montanari model/quantitative concentration framework.
Traced transfer through Poisson clause counts, collisions O(n^(2−k)) without replacement, quantile estimates and fixed-density convergence; polynomial error away from the limiting threshold follows.
remaining: The published Aldous covering proof and Abbe–Montanari interpolation theory were not reproved in full; their exact stated results are used. No formal verification or numerical determination of α_k.

review.title: Expanding Codes with Polynomial Stretch

review.prior_frontier: Improves the cited unconditional quasipolynomial-stretch/polylog-arity construction to polynomial stretch and constant arity, with randomized construction and fixed expansion loss. Does not attack uniformly random hypergraph kXOR/Goldreich conjectures.

score_reasons.significance: Refutes expansion-only hardness at the cryptographically important simultaneous constant-locality, polynomial-stretch and constant-noise regime.
score_reasons.novelty: Growing-field affine-flat indicators retain binary algebraic structure while layered hashing supplies expansion; a rank test replaces error decoding.
score_reasons.depth: Combines generalized Reed–Muller duality, erasure-capacity analysis, concentration and combinatorial expansion with separate cryptographic reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates the unconditional construction, random-versus-designed graphs and conjectural encryption consequences.

checked: Checked exact row weight after hashing within layers and binary-span containment in the generalized Reed–Muller subfield subcode.
Traced M(y)=Vdiag(y)Vᵀ: product-degree orthogonality annihilates codewords; each corrupted coordinate changes rank by at most1.
Verified Sylvester rank lower bound2rank(V_S)−|S|, rate proximity to1/2 via binomial anti-concentration and McDiarmid separation with constant threshold slack, conditional on the erasure theorem.
remaining: Substantive partial-proof exception:36-page algebraic/cryptographic construction. The binary-code span and rank distinguisher were traced, including all stated rank/probability arithmetic. The growing-alphabet applicability of the external erasure theorem is an essential dependency still to verify; expansion, low-degree hardness and PKE claims are not certified.
Verify the cited doubly transitive erasure theorem uniformly over growing field size, not just fixed alphabet.
Audit affine/hash expansion union bounds, XOR-MAJ reduction, planted-hypergraph low-degree analysis and conditional PKE security.

review.title: Online Correlated Exponential Clocks
review.authors: Zhiyi Huang, Kalen Patton, Peilin Yang, Jiahao Zhao
review.summary: Introduces online correlated exponential clocks with exact exponential marginals and negative association, yielding a common first-age Poisson generator for Display Ads0.556, AdWords0.530, and squared-load balancing4.69. Previous ratios were0.5368,0.504,4.9843. Fractional inputs must be fixed independently of generator randomness; this is not a guarantee for arbitrary adaptive feedback to the random rounding.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier improved online dependent-rounding schemes were application-specific; the new generator and interface transfer negative-correlation gains across reward and cost settings.

score_reasons.significance: Substantial simultaneous constant improvements for three established online allocation problems.
score_reasons.novelty: A problem-independent exponential-race interface and first-Poisson-age coupling unify previously separate rounding analyses.
score_reasons.depth: Negative association is proved through disjoint certificates and BKR, then age-measure potentials and covariance savings drive the constants.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions clearly isolate independence assumptions and the common lambda=4.5 generator; numerical verification remains necessary for the advertised constants.

checked: Traced the first-age negative-association proof: capped discrete cell priorities have disjoint occupied-cell/preceding-empty-cell certificates; BKR bounds increasing-event intersections. Interval first ages are monotone functions of disjoint priority blocks, and the limit passes to Poisson time.
Checked randomized probability integral transform at the zero-age atom gives uniform U and Exp(x) clocks; all coordinate maps are nonincreasing, preserving negative association.

Checked the fresh-competitor reduction conditional on one resource clock vector: competitor minima yield a negatively associated allocated set with the same marginals as fresh independent competitors, so the cited submodular-dominance theorem applies.
remaining: The submodular-dominance and BKR primary dependencies were not independently checked; age-measure primal-dual arguments, covariance estimate and certified numerical calculations establishing all three ratios remain unaudited.

Continuity alone is not asserted sufficient.
review.prior_frontier: Replaces the ACT’s existential chromatic-subdivision criterion by a direct PL-map condition; the renaming dichotomy is a new proof of an existing result, not a new dichotomy.

score_reasons.depth: Requires carefully compatible local subdivisions, carrier constraints and chain-map realization for renaming.
score_reasons.exposition: Roadmap and invariant proofs are explicit, though the realization and counterexample appendices need specialist scrutiny.

checked: Traced the shallow-simplex refinement: dimension noncollapse permits colors, push-down reduces nonminimal violations, and descending shattering creates neither higher shallow simplices nor violated edges.
Checked the barycentric-support argument for new vertices having the intended output carrier and why previously handled faces should remain unchanged.
remaining: Finish the compatibility induction and carrier-preserving decision map, audit the ACT/PL assumptions and finite-complex scope, and verify renaming chain-map realization and the continuous-map counterexample.

review.title: Extending Tardos's Theorem to Separable Convex Quadratic Programming
review.authors: Bin Cui, Hanqing Li, Xupeng Miao
review.summary: Extends Tardos operation bounds to continuous separable convex quadratic programs Ax=b,x≥0 with integer A and arbitrary rational linear costs and nonnegative diagonal quadratic weights. Exact primal–dual optimum or infeasibility/unboundedness certificates use poly(r,m,encoding(A)) rational operations, independent of b,c,q lengths, with polynomial intermediate encodings.
review.prior_frontier: Extends coefficient-independent separable quadratic network-flow algorithms to arbitrary integer equality matrices. Strong polynomiality follows for structurally bounded-entry matrices, including an explicit multicommodity aggregate-quadratic-flow formulation; not for arbitrary nonseparable PSD objectives.

score_reasons.significance: A broad Tardos-type extension with exact strongly polynomial multicommodity convex-flow consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Objective compression plus two-sided continuous/integer proximity yields a local near-optimum solver; a circuit-based scale drives coordinate revelation.
score_reasons.depth: The covering and progress bounds control positive curvature and flat directions separately without numeric cost dependence.
score_reasons.exposition: The proof is concise but complete, and explicitly checks zero weights, unboundedness, exact certificates and reconstruction of bounded encodings.

checked: Traced the separable exchange and two-sided proximity proofs using conformal primitive circuits and nearest opposite-type optima.
Verified inward box rounding preserves integer points, Frank–Tardos feature differences have norm≤mR²+2mR, and unit-coordinate tests preserve nonnegative curvature and zeros.
Checked the shared-integer-optimum argument and scalingδ=ε/(2mG), giving a feasible point withinε of a relaxed optimum.
Traced both circuit scale inequalities: negative external directions bounded byα_F, positive-curvature recession directions byV_F, and flat redundant directions excluded by nearest-optimum choice.
Checked progress E_F≤mκρ_F, local radiusκE_F, accuracyE_F/(4mκ), strict addition of a zero-slack coordinate, and termination after≤m calls.

Verified zero-scale recovery, rational KKT certificates, infeasible/unbounded preprocessing, and the multicommodity lift. All LP matrices keep q in objectives/bounds rather than structural coefficients.
Checked bit-size reconstruction from original data and F each iteration, avoiding recursive coefficient-size growth.
remaining: Standard Tardos LP, Frank–Tardos compression and exact rational convex-QP algorithms are applied as established interfaces rather than reimplemented.
No general nonseparable quadratic extension is proved or implied.

review.title: Exhaustive Search Is Hard to Beat in Constant Depth for Hyperclique and Orthogonal Vectors
review.authors: Nikolai Chukhin
review.summary: Proves constant-depth De Morgan circuit gate lower bounds m^Omega(ell) for polynomial-size r-uniform hypercliques (ell<=m^(1/h-epsilon)), nearly exhaustive-search exponents for growing subpolynomial ell, and n^Omega(k) clique bounds through k<=n^(1/(h-1)-epsilon). Derives n^(k-epsilon) gates for fixed-k OV in sufficiently large polylogarithmic dimension and k-Dominating Set, plus Omega(n^2) wires for depth-three2-OV with dimension at least(1+eta)log n. These are restricted-circuit lower bounds, not unrestricted running-time conjectures.
review.prior_frontier: Prior clique/hyperclique lower bounds covered constant-size patterns and OV bounds needed polynomial dimension; depth-three near-quadratic OV wire hardness was an explicit open question.

score_reasons.significance: Extends exhaustive-search hardness to polynomial pattern sizes and proves the restricted-circuit OV conjecture at much smaller dimension.
score_reasons.novelty: Dense planted structures are analyzed through Fourier tails and monomial spanning rather than sparse switching lemmas.
score_reasons.depth: The gate-prefix argument controls all prefixes with one Fourier mass budget, while edge-cover derivatives handle dense random hypergraphs.
score_reasons.exposition: Thirty-five pages state depth, dimension, gate-versus-wire and growing-pattern restrictions carefully.

checked: Checked biased Fourier-tail transfer from the uniform theorem: two independent p-biased samples per coordinate yield random literal restrictions; Fourier square mass thins by Bin(|S|,1/2), retaining at least half the high-degree mass.

Traced the new spanning-event bound: an edge cover J witnesses a nonzero derivative; integer-valued gate-prefix differences satisfy sum_i d_i^2<=1 pointwise. Parseval and random embedding turn low-degree cover counts into(eD/m)^v while isolating the high Fourier tail.

Checked the k-OV-to-Dominating-Set projection: k+1 twins per color/coordinate force exactly one clique vertex of each color, and coordinate domination is orthogonality. Read the depth-three random row restriction and expected O(dW) formula-size bound.
remaining: Dense-planted uniqueness, full union-bound parameter optimization, one-layer saving for graph clique, the external hyperclique-to-OV reduction, and final depth-three formula counting remain unaudited. Background remarks about unrelated announced SETH claims were not verified or used.

review.title: Quantum group codes for non-Clifford logic: enhanced decoding, addressability and parallelizability

review.summary: Constructs non-LDPC quantum group-code families over fixed q=t^4 (t>4 a power of two): full addressability with [[n,Theta(n/log n),Theta(n)]], or linear rate/distance with orbit-wise addressability across Theta(log n) orbits. score_reasons.novelty: Combines free group-module structure with AG lifts to parallelize orbit-wise logical gates.

review.title: Tree Covers for Directed Graphs: Distance Oracles, Routing Schemes and Spanners
review.authors: Shiri Chechik, Gur Lifshitz
review.summary: Constructs directed k-strong tree covers of expected overlap O(k*n^(1/k)): for each ordered pair, a tree-pair gives distance(u,v)+(k-1)*roundtrip(u,v). Different directions may use different tree-pairs, yielding a(2k-1)-roundtrip spanner with O(k*n^(1+1/k)) edges. Provides path-reporting oracles and routing; O(log log k) query oracles use(2k-2)-strong stretch, not the base k-strong stretch. General k>=4 construction is expected soft-O(min(mn,n^2.5)).
review.prior_frontier: Prior directed covers used geometric distance scales and extra logarithmic weight-range factors; roundtrip spanners retained an extra log n edge factor. The result realizes a TZ-type hierarchy inside the directed graph.

score_reasons.significance: Extends a foundational structural distance framework to directed graphs with matching stretch/overlap tradeoffs and multiple algorithmic consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Expanded strict clusters separate connectivity from membership thresholds without a distance-scale decomposition.
score_reasons.depth: The two-level radius hierarchy preserves directed walk connectivity while still admitting geometric sampling bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: Fifty-three pages distinguish strong directional stretch, roundtrip stretch, expected overlap, and query-time/stretch tradeoffs.

checked: Traced the strong-stretch proof: choose maximal level i with R_i(x)<=(i+delta(x))*r, where delta distinguishes the forward and return paths. Maximality retains the full cycle in the larger strict cluster and the needed u-v walk in the expanded cluster; routing through its center costs at most dist(u,v)+i*r.

Checked the expected-overlap argument conditional on A_i,A_(i+2),...: candidate centers have a fixed distance ordering and each is independently retained in A_(i+1) with probability p/(1+p)=Theta(n^-1/k); eligible centers precede the first success.
Confirmed tree-pairs may have one missing reachability direction at some vertices, and cover guarantees are per ordered pair rather than one common tree for both directions.
remaining: Strict-cluster pruning lemma and zero/infinite-distance boundary conventions, faster construction algorithm, O(log log k) query search, routing and prioritized/sourcewise extensions remain unaudited.

review.title: Separating ClonableQMA and QCMA Relative to a Classical Oracle
review.authors: Alper Cakan, Kai-Min Chung, Wei-Hsiang Hung, Tzu-Yi Yang
review.summary: Constructs a classical oracle separating ClonableQMA from QCMA and clonable quantum advice from classical polynomial advice. Honest witnesses can be cloned in polynomial time with fidelity1-negligible, yet no efficient classical witness/advice replaces them. The result is relativized and concerns a locked classical XOR oracle, not unrestricted simulation or an unconditional class separation. Also constructs noninteractive quantum fire, without the stronger interactive/key-fire guarantees of other work.
review.prior_frontier: A quantum-oracle ClonableQMA/QCMA separation was known; recent classical-oracle QMA/QCMA separations relied on unclonable witnesses. This removes unclonability as a necessary mechanism in the classical-oracle setting.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a precise open oracle question about the source of quantum-proof advantage.
score_reasons.novelty: Self-encrypted hash access lets a code-intersection witness unlock and reproduce itself while blocking classical advice.
score_reasons.depth: Coherent successful-output uncomputation and query extraction must coexist under a restricted interface.
score_reasons.exposition: The model and cryptographic limitations are explicit, and the proof isolates good-code properties inherited from prior work.

checked: Checked the cloning hybrid: for every challenge, YZ failure weight<=2^-lambda gives one hash extraction Euclidean/trace error<=sqrt(2)*2^(-lambda/2); polynomially many calls preserve and decouple the seed. Repeated measurement yields both hash-preimage states because their densities are at least inverse polynomial.

Traced the QCMA guesser: guess a classical witness, simulate only accumulated valid pairs and guessed bits without querying the hidden hash, measure a uniformly chosen query, and use the acceptance-gap hybrid to obtain a fresh valid pair with probability>=1/(36Q^2), followed by a1/2 hash-bit guess.
Checked the final contradiction between(72Q^2)^(-L) extraction success and the code/hash combinatorial upper bound2^t*(1-lambda^-4)^(nL/2), taking L>=max(t,lambda) and n>=lambda^5.
remaining: The good-code existence and multi-pair combinatorial bound, complete promise-verifier soundness, oracle diagonalization across lengths and advice/quantum-fire extensions remain unaudited.

review.title: Some Observations in Logical Clocks in Distributed Systems
review.authors: Dharmendra Prasad Mahato
review.summary: Argues that logical-clock increments cannot all be 1 because processors have different physical speeds, and proposes reception updates that increment every transmitted vector component. The central premise confuses logical timestamps with physical durations; its vector update violates its own Theorem 5.2.
review.prior_frontier: Lamport 1978 requires strictly increasing local timestamps and receipt timestamps greater than the transmitted timestamp, not physically calibrated increments. Verified IR1/IR2 on PDF3 of the author-hosted original.

score_reasons.significance: No valid new synchronization theorem is established.
score_reasons.novelty: Numerically different legal clock assignments do not demonstrate an error in logical-clock semantics.
score_reasons.depth: Examples and elementary timestamp arithmetic, with an incorrect vector update.
score_reasons.exposition: Equations are explicit enough to expose the model mismatch, but the interpretation of clock correctness is mistaken.

checked: Directly compared the scalar-clock claims with Lamport IR1/IR2: incrementing by 1 respects both conditions regardless of physical processor speed.

Two-process counterexample to Eq.9 and Theorem 5.2: start at (0,0), P1 sends with vector (1,0); P2 increments its local coordinate and applies max componentwise with transmitted vector plus 1, obtaining (2,1). P1 has C1[1]=1<C2[1]=2.
remaining: Matrix-clock discussion was not audited after the central scalar/vector claims failed.
issues: PDF2 and PDF7 assert that unequal physical speeds invalidate uniform logical increments; this is false in the defined logical-clock model.
PDF9 Eq.9 increases remote vector components and contradicts Theorem 5.2 in one message exchange.

review.desk_reject_reason: Fundamental logical/physical-clock model mismatch (PDF2,7), and explicit one-message counterexample to the proposed vector update and Theorem 5.2 (PDF9).

sources.detail: Primary original IR1/IR2 and Clock Condition checked.

review.title: Resolving the Worst-Case Complexity of Linear Secret Sharing
review.authors: Oded Nir
review.summary: Every n-party monotone access structure has linear secret sharing over any finite field with maximum share 2^{ceil(n/2)−1}+1 field elements. Also claims nonlinear exponent0.494, quadratic exponent0.4994 and an almost-all 2^{n/2−o(n)} monotone-span-program lower bound simultaneously over every field.
review.prior_frontier: Closes the worst-case linear exponent at1/2, versus the cited previous0.7563 upper bound and fixed-field counting lower bound. Improves general nonlinear upper exponent0.585 to0.494. Independent checking here covers the main linear construction, not the sharper nonlinear or all-fields lower bounds.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the asymptotic worst-case complexity of a central information-theoretic cryptographic primitive.
score_reasons.novelty: A two-sided common-pad construction gives the optimal linear exponent with a particularly simple coalition-privacy invariant.
score_reasons.depth: The linear theorem is elementary once the construction is found; the upslice optimization, nonlinear separation and field-uniform lower bound add substantial separate machinery.
score_reasons.exposition: The main construction and privacy proof are unusually explicit, with exact per-party counts and a clear separation of the auxiliary improvements.

checked: Completely traced Construction3.1 and Theorem3.2: authorized C∪D reconstructs m_C, and every nonzero masking pad has T not containing D, so some member of D obtains it.

Checked privacy for an unauthorized coalition: incomplete additive sharings have independent uniform views, while every remaining secret-dependent share has the same coefficient on the undisclosed uniform padω_D. Translation ofω_D gives identical distributions for all secrets.

Verified per-party counts2^{|L|−1} and2^{|R|−1}+1, balanced partition arithmetic and the trivial one-party endpoint. Construction uses only additive operations, consistent with the finite-abelian-group extension.
remaining: Independently verify cited matching counting lower bounds.
Audit partitioned-upslice covering, numerical exponent0.494, quadratic compilation and the simultaneous-all-fields monotone-span-program lower bound.

sources.detail: Exact main theorem and share-count convention

review.title: Model Checking for Metric Extensions of Monadic Second-Order Logic
review.authors: Dibyayan Chakraborty, Sebastian Ordyniak, Sebastian Siebertz
review.summary: CMSO2 with shortest-path and equal-distance-on-geodesic-cycle predicates admits decision, additive optimization and exact counting FPT in formula length plus bag-connected treewidth; CMSO1 has the corresponding theorem for cliquewidth plus cycle-basis length. Restricted positive packing/covering templates also allow numerical distance thresholds outside the parameter. Unrestricted distance comparison has sharply different hardness boundaries.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript compares Courcelle-style theorems and earlier dedicated bag-connected-treewidth Geodetic Set algorithms; prior results not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Extends general logical algorithms to graph-metric problems beyond ordinary treewidth tractability.
score_reasons.novelty: Finite cyclic certificates make shortest paths definable using bounded cycle-basis length.
score_reasons.depth: Combines logical translations, structural width equivalences, numerical-threshold DP and hardness boundaries.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise distinctions among predicates and width parameters; long 70-page treatment.

checked: Traced Lemma 3.3: subtract a spanning-tree potential, divide nonzero integer defects by their gcd, and reduce modulo two; a binary cycle basis forces the odd-defect set to meet every cycle evenly, contradicted by a fundamental cycle containing its single non-tree defect.

Traced Lemma 3.4 and Theorem 3.5: modulus M>=3 exceeding cycle-basis length forces each bounded increment basis-cycle sum to be zero, yields a global integer 1-Lipschitz lift, and certifies a shortest path whose labels increase by one.
Checked the isometric-path partition application: each selected component is induced shortest, hence component count equals |V|-|F| and splitting yields every larger feasible count.
remaining: Full MSO translation, EqGC construction, counting multiplicities and width-decomposition dependencies remain unchecked.
Numerical-threshold DP, model-theoretic characterizations and unrestricted-distance hardness reductions require further verification.

review.title: Identifying bubble-like subgraphs in linear-time via a unified SPQR-tree framework
review.authors: Francisco Sena, Aleksandr Politov, Corentin Moumard, Massimo Cairo, Romeo Rizzi, Manuel Cáceres, Sebastian Schmidt, Juha Harviainen, Alexandru I. Tomescu
review.summary: A unified SPQR framework identifies superbubbles and ultrabubbles and computes a linear-size representation of all snarls in linear time. Snarls can be quadratic in number: the output represents clique-like families of endpoint pairs plus individually listed pairs. Also obtains linear-time feedback-arc identification for tipless bidirected graphs.
review.prior_frontier: Improves quadratic snarl/ultrabubble algorithms to linear time; superbubbles already had linear algorithms, now unified. The bidirected interpretation preserves vertex-side signs while connectivity and SPQR refer to the underlying undirected graph.

score_reasons.significance: A sharp algorithmic improvement for pangenome graph decomposition with a reusable structural framework.
score_reasons.novelty: Sign-cut decomposition and simultaneous two-sided SPQR summaries replace repeated per-separation acyclicity checks.
score_reasons.depth: Requires full S/P/R-node classification, boundary-sign handling and feedback-arc characterization in bidirected graphs.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly handles the quadratic-output obstruction through an O(n)-size representation, though the 60-page case analysis is substantial.

checked: Checked the equivalence between deleting inner edges of the biedged graph and vertex-side splitting in the bidirected graph.
Traced the dangling-block obstruction: a mixed-sign incident block retains a u–u′ path after splitting, preventing separability independently of the other endpoint.
Read sign-cut localization/minimality and the final representation theorem; checked that all pairs of tips are represented implicitly rather than enumerated.
remaining: Audit every SPQR reporting case and converse completeness, including sign-cut minimality dependencies.
Verify ultrabubble acyclicity/feedback-arc routines and total linear-time charging; the general-graph conditional feedback-arc lower bound remains unchecked.

review.title: Contextual Search and Bilateral Trade with a Trace-Square-Root Potential
review.authors: Romain Cosson, Federico Fusco, Anupam Gupta, Stefano Leonardi, Renato Paes Leme, Matteo Russo
review.summary: Tight horizon-independent O(sqrt(d)) expected total loss for contextual search and one-bit contextual bilateral trade with fixed unknown unit-ball vectors and adaptive unit contexts. Known-prior counterparts are bounded by trace-square-root covariance, allowing dependent seller/buyer priors with finite second moments. Search has explicit O(d^2) arithmetic and memory per round; worst-case trade uses an existential finite minimax lottery.
review.prior_frontier: Claims prior contextual-search O(d log d), one-bit trade O(d 6^d), and matching Omega(sqrt(d)) lower bounds; external lower-bound sources not checked.

score_reasons.significance: Closes dimension dependence in two established noiseless one-bit learning problems.
score_reasons.novelty: Trace-square-root directional comparison and dual quadratic proxy potential replace geometric uncertainty-set machinery.
score_reasons.depth: Explicit rank-one search update plus a separate discontinuous-payoff minimax trade argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Clean model and algorithm distinctions, with detailed scalar and matrix calculations.

checked: Checked gap-function affine representation: with T=sqrt(Sigma), M=(T-R)^2, the PSD slope R^-1-xx^T/||Rx|| and reverse triangle inequality give the claimed infimum; singular matrices follow by regularization.

Traced the complete contextual-search scalar potential calculation, including equality thresholds, and its matrix rank-one lift: Sherman-Morrison gives Delta Phi=(r/a)Delta phi with r/a>=1; R remains positive definite and initial potential <=2sqrt(d), yielding 12sqrt(d) expected total loss.
Traced one-bit posterior-standard-deviation contraction to 23/24 through the same scalar potential.

Inspected the trade minimax obstruction: raw payoffs are discontinuous, and the proof introduces a common shift/shrink of both valuations followed by bounded-density price smoothing; finite-support rounding requires compact successor-state support.
remaining: The 37-page paper contains a separate bilateral-trade branch: trade-or-information inequality and the complete smoothing/minimax limit proof remain unchecked; only its setup and initial regularization have been inspected.
Bayesian adaptive-context measurability and all lower-bound dependencies have not been exhaustively audited. Search arithmetic complexity is real-arithmetic, not a bit-complexity guarantee.

review.title: Pfaffian Recognition is in coRP
review.authors: Priyanshu Pant, Ranveer Singh
review.summary: Randomized polynomial-time recognition of general Pfaffian graphs (coRP), via a characteristic-two polynomial selecting perfect matchings with the wrong Pfaffian sign; O(|V|³) field operations per orientation-testing trial and a witness self-reduction. Also characterizes non-Pfaffian orientations of matching-covered graphs by a cut reversal making the orientation strongly connected.
review.prior_frontier: Previously quoted general recognition was coNP via Vazirani–Yannakakis, with deterministic algorithms in special graph classes. Verified the original 1989 Theorem 3.1 reduction (author-hosted PDF6–7); deterministic general recognition remains open.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves randomized recognition of a longstanding general graph class central to exact counting.
score_reasons.novelty: Wrong-sign coefficient extraction by determinants of two- and four-vertex-deleted minors is a simple new algebraic route.
score_reasons.depth: Main proof is short but combines crossing parity, characteristic-two identities, and inverse-minor acceleration effectively.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions, rejection direction, field size, singular evaluations, and witness recovery are transparent.

checked: Traced all new steps of Theorem 1.1: crossing-plus-reversal sign formula; distinct wrong-sign monomials; determinant/minor expansion giving their parity coefficient; degree 2n Schwartz–Zippel bound over q≥4n.
Verified the exact Vazirani–Yannakakis orientation-construction dependency in its original PDF6–7.
Checked Jacobi reduction and the prefix-sum computation of the crossing sum in O(|V|³); rejecting only nonsingular nonzero evaluations and q≥8n gives failure probability at most 1/2.
Checked witness self-reduction preserves a nonzero polynomial evaluation and returns a disjoint wrong-sign perfect matching.
Traced cut-switching along the even conformal cycle and odd ears, and the positive-circulation singular-matrix converse of the structural result.
remaining: The classical matching-covered ear-decomposition theorem used by the secondary structural result was not rederived or checked against the full book proof.
Published Pfaffian/determinant theory and deterministic perfect-matching algorithms are treated as standard dependencies; no formal verification or implementation claim.

review.summary: For additive nonnegative indivisible chores without payments, gives polynomial-time truthful-in-expectation, ex-ante envy-free mechanisms with ex-post1.97-MMS. Two agents admit optimal4/3; three admit3/2 with8/7 lower bound; general lower bound at least13/12.

score_reasons.exposition: The ex-ante/ex-post distinctions, complete-allocation/no-payment model and the limits of increasing nomination count are stated clearly.

checked: Traced Theorem3.5 conditional on the decomposition lemma: only the negative nominated-cost term depends on an agent’s report, and nominating the largest k costs establishes truthfulness and ex-ante EF.
Verified the sorted-block cost inequality and the necessary nonnegative coefficient n−2k−1; checked the equal-cost counterexample when k>n/2.
Checked why averaging intermediate fractional allocations to1/n and marginal-preserving rounding yields report-independent expected costs, without claiming independence of item assignments.
remaining: Audit nomination decomposition Lemma3.4, the one-hard/multiple-hard-agent1.97 constructions and all numerical inequalities.
Trace the optimal two-agent construction and lower-bound incentive cycles;1.875 refinement not audited.

review.title: Maximizing Unobserved Welfare: Logarithmic Regret from Purchases
review.authors: Xin Cheng, Yixin Tao, Yidan Xing
review.summary: For iid unknown buyer types with concave utilities satisfying radial curvature at known scale W, a purchase-feedback-only pricing/production policy achieves O(mW log(T+1)) welfare regret versus an aggregate-capacity offline optimum, while delivering every optimal purchase on every path. Known continuous convex nondecreasing production cost is paid in advance, unit per-round capacities and inventory carryover apply. Curvature means lambda -> u(lambda x)-W log(lambda) is convex; bounded expenditure alone instead permits Omega(T^1/4) regret.
review.prior_frontier: Compares prior online Fisher-market and purchase-feedback welfare bounds, often polynomial regret or known-distribution log regret; not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Logarithmic regret with unobserved welfare, unknown distributions and exact inventory feasibility substantially strengthens this model.
score_reasons.novelty: Radial purchase-support inequality and coupled inventory/history Gibbs potentials accommodate non-strict and non-differentiable utilities.
score_reasons.depth: Forgetting errors must be charged back to accumulated demand gaps while controlling terminal unsold stock.
score_reasons.exposition: Extensive overview identifies necessary curvature and separate pathwise versus expected guarantees.

checked: Inspected radial-curvature logarithmic support inequality and nonnegative decomposition of demand gap into surrogate error plus a-1-log(a).
Checked production optimality argument: logarithmic inventory normalizer has positive-definite covariance Hessian and diverges at the boundary; directional optimality yields c(q)+c*(pI)=pI.q.

Traced Lemma 4.3 conditional on its centered log-concave-survival moment bound: negative quadratic record correction absorbs the exponential fluctuation term when kappa*gamma>=80, leaving (-1/4+8/kappa)d^2<=0.
Checked aggregate-regret decomposition includes terminal inventory value and the stated forgetting/terminal estimates suffice to absorb half the loss.
remaining: Centered-moment Lemma C.1, full forgetting and terminal estimates, safe-delivery proof and lower-bound reduction not checked.
Algorithm invokes multivariate Gibbs integrals and optimization; no efficient implementation guarantee was verified.

review.summary: Gives a one-round one-way quantum-LOCAL algorithm for directed cycles with20,000 colors and arbitrary local errorε using O(log1/ε) qubits. With known n and ε=n^{-10}, classical reductions yield four-round3-coloring and constant-round bounded-degree coloring, MIS and maximal matching with high probability, and collapse classical O(log*n)-round LCLs to quantum O(1).
review.prior_frontier: Addresses the long-standing natural quantum-LOCAL advantage question: these tasks needΘ(log*n) classical rounds. No initial inter-node entanglement is assumed; nodes prepare local EPR pairs and send one register. Local computation/message size are unrestricted by LOCAL, and the finite algorithm has small nonzero error.

review.title: Cryptography from Dream Compression
review.authors: Liyan Chen, Abhishek Jain, Jiatu Li, Lawrence Roy
review.summary: Under quasi-polynomial-modulus LWE, prBPP=prP, and a new short-advice unprovability assumption for retraction WPHP in APX1 augmented by those axioms, constructs effective SNARKs and ordinary nonadaptively sound SNARGs for NP. Effective extraction means that the selected theory cannot prove a suitable extractor failure; it is not standard real-world knowledge soundness. Introduces effectively extractable hashes and reverse-mathematics equivalences for elementary PRG/CRH-to-OWF facts.
review.prior_frontier: Alternative to prior obfuscation/propositional-proof approaches; the logical assumption is new and stronger than plain unprovability, not a standard LWE-only construction. Prior claims not externally verified.

score_reasons.significance: A distinctive conditional route to NP succinct arguments and a useful separation between effective extraction and actual soundness.
score_reasons.novelty: Encrypted dream-compression Merkle hashing converts provable extraction failure into a forbidden retraction-WPHP witness.
score_reasons.depth: Requires precise bounded-arithmetic formalizations, malicious FHE correctness and short-advice parameter accounting.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly discloses unusual assumptions and security limitations, despite substantial foundational overhead.

checked: Read Assumptions 1 and 2 quantifiers: almost-everywhere/nonuniform proof witnesses, a fixed circuit-size exponent, and small tautological advice are materially stronger than simple unprovability.

Traced Lemma 5.14 conditional on PV-provable malicious evaluation correctness: a verified Merkle path either matches decrypted/decompressed root extraction at every level or gives z with D(C(z))!=z. The induction is Sigma^b_1 and invokes Buss witnessing.

Traced Theorem 5.12 reduction from a provable effective-extractor failure to a retraction-WPHP refuter via compression stretching and a witnessed path defect. The short-advice case pigeonholes n into powers of lambda and ensures trapdoor space dominates circuit descriptions.
remaining: Malicious FHE construction and APX1 security formalizations, witnessing/translation dependencies, Fiat-Shamir correlation-intractability composition and nonadaptive soundness proof remain unchecked.
No independent evidence establishing the new logical assumption; reverse-mathematics equivalences not audited.

Checked simultaneous batching preserves quantifier order and falsity because universal choices for separate batches use disjoint variables.
remaining: Audit repeated squishing size/alternation bounds and conversion to size-two backdoors.
Trace affine and2-CNF elimination, Horn hardness, enhanced detection and all density-hypothesis reductions.

Extends a recent k-median tapered-rounding framework by separating taper strength c=0.85 from potential coefficient kappa=8, with a new squared-cost comparison inequality certified by interval arithmetic plus a local zero-slack argument.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript states prior polynomial ratio 4.9+epsilon, with 1+8/e+epsilon previously only FPT in k. Relies materially on a recent OpenAI k-median framework; neither that source nor the computational archive has yet been independently audited here.

score_reasons.significance: If verified, closes the approximation threshold for a major general-metric clustering objective.
score_reasons.novelty: Squared taper/potential separation and exact zero-slack certificate extend rather than replace the previous rounding framework.
score_reasons.depth: Includes drift normalization, two derandomizations, certificate quantifiers and pseudo-approximation removal.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly distinguishes computer-certified ingredients, trusted arithmetic and manual dependencies.

checked: Checked coverage hardness metric: incidence distance 1, nonincidence 3, same-side distance 2 satisfy triangle inequalities; squared cost is n+8 times uncovered count.
Traced squared cap averaging: split by (1-y)/(1-w_i), use d_h<=d_i+(1-lambda*q_hi)N_i, and q^3<=q^2 to bound the squared radius term.
Checked normalized radius hypotheses and taper error using lambda<=1/2, |lambda-hat-lambda|<=zeta, E D=1, E sqrt(D)<=1; resulting error bound 120*zeta is supported by the displayed estimates.

Checked local zero-slack polynomial expansion -2u²-2v²-2uv(u+v)-u²v² and its negative quadratic bound for |u|,|v|<=1/16. Young-inequality final coefficient is negative conditional on the six certified derivative bounds.
Read certificate quantifier structure: alpha fixed per (x,omega) cell; beta may depend on row (D,s) but not (q,Z). Exact box tiling and delegated local region are essential.
remaining: External supplementary certificate, checker, derivative bounds and claimed Lean implication have NOT been run or verified.

Full inherited k-median structural lemmas, grid preparation, batch drift, deterministic conditional-expectation construction and additive-budget removal remain to be checked before correctness clearance.
The 56-page combined analytic/computational proof is a substantial audit; inspected local steps do not establish the headline theorem.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the polynomial probe complexity of a canonical greedy algorithm and establishes a genuinely adaptive obstruction.
score_reasons.novelty: An elimination-time weighted moment controls a recursively explored set despite early stopping; a distinct hidden-clique coupling supplies the universal lower bound.
score_reasons.depth: Requires exponential-moment inequalities, weighted integral elimination and adaptive transcript comparison beyond local neighborhood counting.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully specifies zero-error/stateless consistency and fixed-vertex expectation versus all-vertex tail guarantees.

papers.title: P vs NP proof
papers.authors: Gergő Czuczor

review.title: P vs NP proof
review.authors: Gergő Czuczor
review.summary: Claims P!=NP by splitting a time-hierarchy computation into allegedly hard bounded-length subproblems and summing their costs over exponentially many candidate inputs. The essential implication from a particular machine’s simulation time to a lower bound for all decision algorithms is invalid.
review.prior_frontier: Purports to settle P versus NP; this review identifies a fatal gap in the proposed proof and does not assert the opposite complexity-class equality.

score_reasons.significance: The headline conclusion is not established by the central lower-bound argument.
score_reasons.novelty: No valid new complexity separation survives the unsupported simulation/direct-sum step.
score_reasons.depth: Time hierarchy is used as if it supplied per-segment and per-input lower bounds, which it does not.
score_reasons.exposition: Input sizes, constants and language-level quantifiers are conflated in the final proof.

checked: Read full proposed separation Section3.7 (PDF17–19), including the time-hierarchy setup and bounded-halting alternatives.

The step at PDF17 lines420–429 splits one slow execution into k machines and declares each problem to require c+1 steps. Neither a worst-case language lower bound nor a machine executing c+1 transitions implies this: a machine can wait c+1 steps and accept every input while its language is decided immediately. Changing an intermediate state to accepting does not preserve hardness of the original language.

PDF18 lines451–454 and PDF18–19 lines463–468 further infer a k*c lower bound for an existential/no-witness question by summing alleged individual costs. No direct-sum theorem or oracle restriction is supplied; an arbitrary decision algorithm need not simulate every candidate.

Section3.4 switches to deterministic bounded halting with a specified input; for unary k this is directly polynomial-time simulable, so its NP-completeness does not follow from the earlier existential-input variant.
remaining: A new language-level lower-bound argument would be required; repairing presentation alone cannot justify the claimed P!=NP proof.
issues: PDF17 lines420–429 infer k independent hard decision problems from segments of a slow computation without justification; simulation length is not a lower bound on language-decision complexity.
PDF18–19 infer an existential bounded-halting lower bound by summing candidate costs, with no direct-sum theorem or restriction forcing simulation.

review.desk_reject_reason: Fatal missing argument in the central separation proof: time hierarchy gives no per-segment hardness and no k-fold direct-sum bound (PDF17–19). A deliberately delayed machine for the trivial all-input language illustrates why execution length cannot certify the asserted decision lower bounds.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a coherent security foundation for dynamic numerical precision rather than merely a faster discrete implementation.
score_reasons.novelty: Separates consistency, approximate collision resistance and precision-sensitive binding; base shifting avoids linear kernel collisions.
score_reasons.depth: Combines continuous lattice reductions, discontinuous digit maps, noisy binding and statistical hiding.

checked: Read dynamic precision quantifiers: honest opening for lV<=lP; binding only for separation at least 2^-lV, with approximate hash collision threshold f(l) and consistency error g(l).
Traced base-shifting difference estimate: first differing base-b digit yields B^-k times a nonzero integer vector plus infinity-norm tail <b/B.

Traced Proposition5.25 collision-to-CSIS-prime extraction conditional on its hardness reduction: first differing digit has Euclidean norm <=b sqrt(m), matrix tail <=mb/B in the stated coordinate norm, and B>20mnb plus precision error makes an approximate collision imply a small nonzero integer image.
Inspected simple hash-to-commitment binding reduction and noted that the native-real hash needs a different hiding construction; that proof is not established by the simple reduction.
remaining: Worst-case-to-average-case CSIS/CSIS-prime reductions, finite sampling/arithmetic error handling, hiding conversion, CLWE statistical binding and Sigma protocol not audited.
Real-arithmetic efficiency and continuity impossibility require exact model qualification; this is not a succinct evaluation-proof or real polynomial-commitment construction.

review.title: Optimal compression with quantum retrieval
review.authors: Shyam Dhamapurkar, Mohit Garg, Manaswi Paraashar, Jaikumar Radhakrishnan
review.area: Quantum query complexity; succinct data structures
review.summary: Exact quantum retrieval from a classical encoding of an m-bit string of weight at most n uses O(n^(1−1/t)m^(1/t)log(m/n)^(1−1/t)) bits adaptively; parallel t-query retrieval uses O(t n^(2−2/t)m^(1/t)log(m/n)^(1−1/t)). For constant n the latter improves to O(t 2^n m^(1/t)). This is the nonuniform bit-probe model, with free graph-dependent computation, not an efficient encoder or gate-complexity result.
review.prior_frontier: The RSV space–probe inequality sum_{i≤n} binom(m,i)≤sum_{i≤nt}binom(s,i), verified in the original Theorem 1 (PDF p8), gives the quoted Ω(t n^(1−1/t)m^(1/t)) regime t≤log(m/n). Prior quantum upper bounds did not achieve these exponents for general parameters.

score_reasons.significance: Nearly closes the exact quantum sparse-membership space–probe frontier, including a polynomial separation from classical retrieval.
score_reasons.novelty: Routing sparse blocks by matchings and decoding stored routing labels by Bernstein–Vazirani gives the near-optimal general tradeoff.
score_reasons.depth: The new proof combines elementary probabilistic expanders, exact quantum primitives, and carefully optimized recursive space bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The algorithms and recursive costs are unusually accessible; two nonadaptive graph descriptions need the local qualifications recorded below.

checked: Traced both random-graph existence arguments, including the Hall union bound and private-neighborhood hypergeometric tail.
Checked the adaptive matching routing, Hadamard encoding of routing labels, and the recurrence with p=((m/n)/log(m/n))^(1/t), including small-density and large-t regimes.

Checked the parallel occupancy-bit/Deutsch–Jozsa construction using private neighbors within each column and its recursively compressed first table. The column-wise property suffices for all encodable sparse inputs.
Traced the constant-n coordinate construction, whose stored membership patterns cost 2^n, and the resulting t m^(1/t) dependence.
Verified the exact external lower-bound inequality in Radhakrishnan–Sen–Venkatesh, quant-ph/0007021, Theorem 1 PDF p8; this comparison is not a new lower bound.
remaining: No formal verification; gate efficiency and constructive graph generation are outside the stated model. Nonadaptive integer padding is suppressed in the manuscript and has not been optimized for exact constants.
issues: PDF p8 states a stronger universal private-neighbor condition for every subset of size n(m/m1) than the column-copy graph on p9 supplies. The encoding only needs unions of at most n nonempty rows, for which each column contains at most n points and Lemma 4 applies. The proof should state this restricted property.

The sets B_a on p8 must be chosen inside the private neighborhoods, not merely pairwise disjoint subsets of neighbors; the preceding private-neighbor guarantee supplies these directly. These are repairable specification issues, not counterexamples to the space bounds.

review.title: Secret Sharing Despite Non-Extractable Randomness
review.authors: Divesh Aggarwal
review.summary: For every b≥2, constructs perfect two-out-of-two sharing of b bits using a b+2-bit key sampled from a class of flat sources of min-entropy at least b, although every deterministic bit extractor has statistical error at least 1/6 on some source. Gives two-out-of-n and r-out-of-r extensions with exact non-extractability thresholds 1/(4n−2) and 1/(2(2^r−1)). No leakage-resilience or non-malleability is asserted.
review.prior_frontier: Bosley–Dodis explicitly ask in Section 5 whether two-out-of-two sharing requires extractable randomness; verified in their author-hosted original PDF p16. Prior single-bit separations and positive extraction results for stronger leakage/non-malleability requirements leave the present long-message basic-sharing case open.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a foundational long-standing question separating the randomness needed for ordinary secrecy from encryption.
score_reasons.novelty: An explicit odd-block construction gives near-minimal key length and sharp extraction obstruction, rather than an entropy-amplification variant of the single-bit example.
score_reasons.depth: The central proof is short but structurally insightful: affine sharing identities and odd-cardinality discrepancy; the threshold extensions need additional linear algebra.
score_reasons.exposition: The construction and the exact distinction from stronger privacy notions are clear and independently checkable.

checked: Traced the two-out-of-two construction over F_(2^b): left/right tags and central affine pair reconstruct for every key; each marginal is message-independent for every source T. Checked key length and flat-source support size 2^(b+1)−|T|.
For an arbitrary ±1 extractor, v_i=h(C_i)−h(L_i)−h(R_i) is nonzero odd; choosing positive v_i gives source/complement signed-sum difference at least 2^b and combined support 3·2^b, proving TV≥1/6.
Checked the two-out-of-n decoder, per-share multiplicities, odd gadget size 2n−1, and balanced-index matching upper bound.

Checked r-out-of-r pads, linearly independent γ_i and nonzero subset sums, bijectivity of the pad map seen by each r−1 coalition, and odd/even activation-family cancellation; traced the sharp bias calculation.
Verified the precise historical question in Bosley–Dodis, Section 5, author-hosted enc-ext.pdf, PDF p16. The new construction itself does not require an unverified external theorem.
remaining: No formal machine check. The separate Appendix A criticism of a 2025 result is not part of this correctness endorsement and was not audited.

review.title: Efficient Stable Word-RAM Simulation by Population Protocols
review.authors: Leszek Gąsieniec, Tytus Grodzicki, Grzegorz Stachowiak
review.summary: Simulates every fixed P-program: word-RAM time/register count polynomial in w, w=Theta(log n), with unary input/output counts and modular signed w-bit arithmetic. Uses polylog(n) states and silently stabilizes correctly with probability1 in O(w²(TR*w+TRAM+TP)) expected and high-probability parallel time. Needs population large enough for counts, weights and one agent per register bit, prescribed word length/time/register bounds, and program initialization/halting for all partial retry inputs.

score_reasons.significance: General simulation framework provides systematic efficient stable computation beyond isolated semilinear examples.
score_reasons.novelty: Anomaly-detecting fast simulation is coupled to rank-tagged universal silent backup.

checked: Read exact resource and population parameters: n_w=C((TR+TP+1)2^w+rho-prime*w), with constant free-agent fraction and known w.

Traced rank backup uniqueness: equal-rank duel increases winner rank; rank r requires at least2^(r-1) initial leaders, and two leaders cannot both reach the final maximum rank without forcing a later increase. Final simulation uses fresh rank unavailable to earlier leaders.

Inspected persistent terminal check: unread lower-rank immutable inputs trigger output erasure and retry; input counts persist while working registers are rewritten before first read. Once all inputs counted, checking causes no state changes, enabling silence.
Checked expected-time composition conditional on polynomial all-reachable-state failure-detection/backup bound D(n): choose anomaly probability n^-eta so fast bound+n^-eta D(n) stays polylogarithmic.
remaining: Full MC-plus communication/clock/anomaly detection, register bit operations, conversion correctness and uniform polynomial residual-time bound D(n) remain unaudited.
Backup time O(n²w), state product accounting and every lower-rank reclamation interaction still need verification.

review.summary: Claims an O(n^6 m) algorithm for general 3SAT via checking-tree pair compatibility, repeated 2SAT subproblems, and a final-leaf combination rule. The claimed polynomial correctness is not established by this review; a stated Algorithm 1 output invariant is false on an explicit small example.
review.prior_frontier: No accepted polynomial algorithm for general 3SAT is used as prior work. The manuscript proposes a new proof of P=NP; this review scores the substantiated material rather than assigning significance for the unverified headline.

score_reasons.significance: No verified complexity-class resolution or independent useful theorem is established.
score_reasons.novelty: The checking-tree terminology and leaf-repair proposal are specific, but their global extension claims are unproved and include a false invariant.
score_reasons.depth: The construction is elaborate; elaboration does not establish the crucial bounded-recalculation argument.
score_reasons.exposition: The central properties are stated in long informal case discussions, making algorithmic state and quantifiers difficult to reconstruct.

checked: Read the exact good/standard checking-tree definitions, Algorithm 1, main Algorithm 3, and claimed O(n^6 m) accounting.

Checked the Algorithm 1 output assertion on a valid good-tree deletion: original clauses (x∨y∨z), (¬x∨p∨t), (¬y∨q∨t), (¬z∨r∨t); all nondirect pairs extend to a legal original path. Delete t. Algorithm 1 retains one 3-unit layer and three 2-unit layers; every remaining 3-layer unit has useful paths, and all cross-3-layer consistency tests are vacuous. Yet the legal 2SAT path (¬x,¬y,¬z) is incompatible with every unit of (x∨y∨z), contradicting p32 Step 8 that every 2SAT path is useful for some unit of each 3-unit layer. Finite enumeration confirms the premises.
Read the later key-part-path and correct-chosen-unit claims that purport to avoid exponential combination.
remaining: This counterexample disproves the stated universal output invariant, not by itself a complete execution of the final algorithm. A corrected invariant and a precise proof that the final-leaf procedure preserves an extendible solution are required.
The assertion that identical literals need only one recalculation irrespective of different states is not justified by the runtime proof.
issues: Demonstrably false Algorithm 1 Step 8 invariant on PDF p32; pairwise useful-unit information does not imply that each entire 2SAT path extends through a 3-unit layer.
PDF pp20–22 and p31 rely on informal global compatibility/final-leaf assertions without an established replacement for the failed extension invariant.

review.title: SNARGs for Oracle-Aided Circuits (or, Non-Interactive Proofs for AI Oversight)
review.authors: Liyan Chen, Abhishek Jain, Jiatu Li, Omer Paneth

score_reasons.significance: A substantial extension of succinct verification with potentially useful oracle-query savings.
score_reasons.novelty: Connects robustness proofs, correlation-intractable sampling and uniform non-membership proofs.
score_reasons.depth: Security depends on sophisticated proof-complexity formalizations and cryptographic reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: The main assumptions are stated, but long appendix dependencies make the informal headline insufficient for assessment.

checked: Checked transcript-language construction and completeness, and how sampled oracle answers are incorporated into the verifier.
Traced Lemma 5.4's key-distribution switch and reduction to EF-SNARG soundness, conditional on the stated primitive theorems.

Checked Lemma 6.1's robustness-to-emptiness implication: a false accepting transcript differs on more than an epsilon fraction; statistical correlation intractability forces a sampled discrepancy contradicting the checked opening.
remaining: 96-page proof exception: the witness-encryption route, low-depth list recovery, weak-theory formalization and primitive constructions have not been fully verified.
This is non-adaptive soundness for efficient representable oracles, not a guarantee for unrestricted human/oracle behavior.

review.summary: Constructs non-adaptively sound SNARGs for robust oracle-aided circuits in the efficient-oracle model, using LWE plus witness encryption/SNARG assumptions with Extended Frege correctness proofs; short robustness proofs allow an LWE-only route.
review.prior_frontier: Improves non-adaptive arguments of proximity previously requiring subexponential iO, and extends to robust oracle computations. CRS size depends on the oracle's polynomial-size representation; removing that dependence needs an additional bounded-arithmetic unprovability assumption.

papers.title: Graphon Colourings and Limits of Graph Partitions
papers.authors: Svante Janson, Tiffany Y. Y. Lo, Colin McDiarmid, Anda Skeja, Fiona Skerman

review.title: Graphon Colourings and Limits of Graph Partitions
review.authors: Svante Janson, Tiffany Y. Y. Lo, Colin McDiarmid, Anda Skeja, Fiona Skerman
review.summary: Develops pure and mixed finite-colour graphon limits, equivalence/purification and compactness. Proves Cheeger convergence for cut-convergent graph sequences with uniform linear minimum degree, and modularity convergence at positive limiting edge density. Fixed-colour mixed modularity optima are attained, but a finite colouring need not attain unrestricted modularity. Usual coloured cut distance is insufficient for mixed-colouring equivalence.
review.prior_frontier: Extends earlier pure-colouring and graphon-modularity work to a unified mixed framework and supplies convergence theorems with explicit nondegeneracy conditions. Some blow-up identities were known and are identified as such in the manuscript; the full graphon literature was not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Substantial structural consolidation and new convergence results for widely used partition functionals, with necessary hypotheses made explicit.
score_reasons.novelty: Mixed colourings preserve graphon equivalence and expose why naive coloured cut-distance formulations fail.
score_reasons.depth: Combines measure-theoretic representation and weak-star compactness with uniform denominator and rounding estimates over 85 pages.
score_reasons.exposition: The main restrictions and counterexamples are clearly summarized; several repeated statements and one repairable constant error need attention.

checked: Read the fixed-colour cut-norm/weak-star topology, quotient claim, and counterexample to cut-distance characterization for mixed colourings.
Traced Cheeger denominator lemma: H≤1/2 and degree≥c force colour mass≥c/2 and denominator≥c²/2.
Checked pullback invariance through conditional expectation and the stated 4δ_square/c² stability result.
Inspected modularity blow-up comparison and fixed-colour continuity proof.
remaining: Full purification/common-pullback representation, quotient compactness, finite-to-continuum rounding, unrestricted-colour approximation, and non-attainment construction remain unaudited.
issues: PDF p67 Eq. (5.111) omits a factor 2: constant graphons W1=1, W2=0.9 with an all-one colour give product difference 0.19>cut difference 0.1. The standard 2·cut bound repairs the argument and still yields (2κ+4)δ≤4κδ for κ≥2, so the displayed final continuity estimate is unaffected.
