review.title: Fully tolerant product state testing and closest product state learning
review.authors: Zongbo Bao, Jonas Helsen, Tuyen Nguyen
review.summary: For arbitrary mixed n-qudit states and fixed thresholds a>b, tests whether maximum pure-product fidelity is≥a or≤b using2^{softO((a−b)^{-5})}log(1/δ) copies independent ofn,d. Also gives an additiveε agnostic product learner with2^{softO(ε^{-8})}(nd)² polylog(nd/δ) copies and fixed-degree polynomial system-size runtime.
review.prior_frontier: Extends dimension-independent non-tolerant product testing to all tolerant thresholds; improves previousn^{poly(1/ε)} learning to FPT in inverse accuracy. Does not provide polynomial dependence on1/ε or efficient full-state tomography.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves whether full tolerance preserves constant-copy product-state testing and materially improves agnostic learning parameter dependence.
score_reasons.novelty: Randomly groups subsystems while controlling optimal product fidelity, then uses blockwise high-eigenvalue projection to remove growing local dimensions.
score_reasons.depth: Requires an operator-valued parity occupancy bound, optimal-vector refinement, k-copy symmetric tests and a separate measure-and-prepare learning reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully distinguishes maximum product overlap from generic state distance and makes the exponential accuracy dependence explicit.

checked: Traced the random-coloring operator bound in simultaneous swap eigenspaces: parity occupancy is bounded using the even-step hypercube return probability and the exact six-ball count.
Verified q≥13 suffices for(15q²−30q+16)/q⁴≤1/q, with s=2 and4 handled separately.
Checked block refinement through the top eigenvector of the conditional marginal, positivity of tensor powers, and telescoping squared-fidelity loss using the cited two-copy pure-state inequality.
Read the spectral projection theorem and identified its rank factors and threshold choice as the remaining bridge to the tester.
remaining: Audit the blockwise spectral projection bound, k/accuracy parameter arithmetic and implementation of symmetric tests.
Independently verify the cited sharp product-test bound and trace the agnostic learning, measure-and-prepare channel and qudit high-fidelity subroutine.

review.summary: Every time-T space-S deterministic computation has information-theoretically sound IP with poly(T,S,σ) prover and 2^{O(sqrt(log T))} S² poly(σ,log S) verifier; hence doubly efficient verification for polynomial space and T=n^{O(log n)}. Direct batching of deterministic computation replaces general unambiguous-IP batching.
review.prior_frontier: Prior time regime n^{O(sqrt(log n/log log n))} attributed to BGHK25; concurrent Rothblum construction has the same efficiency and related arguments. Neither full PSPACE doubly efficiency nor computational soundness alone is claimed.

score_reasons.significance: Extends a central doubly-efficient IP frontier to a substantially larger quasipolynomial regime.
score_reasons.novelty: Direct transition batching uses uniquely decoding checksums with row-proximity reductions.
score_reasons.depth: Nontrivial recursion keeps succinct predicates and soundness under both time and batch reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Formal resource bounds and concurrent-work scope are clearly stated.

checked: Traced soundness split: committed checksum determines at most one midpoint matrix in the d-row ball; valid boundaries and transitions force the deterministic true matrix. A failed auxiliary predicate excludes that matrix, making IPP input far.
Checked recurrence ε(t,k)≤ε(t,k↓)+ε(t/λ,kλ)+2^{-σloc}; k=1 gives verifier 2^{O(sqrt(log T))}S².
remaining: Full row-IPP construction and distance-preserving GKR dependency; recursion-size/field-size arithmetic and predicate representation circuits.
Verify history-conditioning in soundness against the exact protocol and all parameter bounds in Appendix B.

review.title: Approximating two-terminal network reliability

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a classic counting problem on unrestricted graphs.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses conditional DFS snapshots and a prediction martingale rather than the earlier annealing/Markov-chain approach.
score_reasons.depth: A surprisingly clean polynomial-time existence proof precedes a much more involved speedup.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates the simple FPRAS from the optimized algorithm and states the complement distinction clearly.

checked: Checked the full central existence proof for Algorithm S on pp.7-14: last-resolved-ancestor DFS decomposition, conditioning on an outgoing open arc, pool-weight cancellation including empty pools, and unbiased prediction martingales.

Checked Harris's inequality use bounding conditional reachability by q_w/q_v, the maximizing-edge bound on Phi, the second-moment recurrence for the aggregate prediction, orthogonality of martingale increments, and final Chebyshev bound.
The audited algorithm takes O(n^4 m^2/(epsilon^2 delta)) arithmetic operations and already establishes an FPRAS at constant failure probability.
remaining: The much faster advertised runtimes, undirected sparsification improvement, #BIS hardness, and full bit-complexity implementation were not independently audited. The complete manuscript is 58 pages.

review.summary: Gives the first FPRAS for two-terminal reliability on general directed and undirected graphs, with further near-nm and near-quadratic running-time claims respectively; complementary unreliability is shown #BIS-hard.

review.title: Constrained Directed Separation: Algorithms and Classifications
review.authors: Jedrzej Olkowski, M. S. Ramanujan
review.summary: For every fixed decidable hereditary digraph class H, finds a size≤k directed s–t separator inducing H, including minimum nonnegative binary-weight optimization, in 2^O(k^4 log k)n^O(1)+2^O(k²)τ_H(k). Fixed demand patterns are FPT for all H exactly when set-to-set; every other pattern is W[1]-hard already for independent deletion sets. For proper hereditary constraints on underlying graphs, bounded independence number gives the other tractable case. A matching co-solution-degeneracy dichotomy is proved.
review.prior_frontier: Directed independent s–t separator was open, unlike undirected hereditary separation via treewidth reduction. The paper supplies an alternative to an unavailable general directed torso theorem; original flow-augmentation and dichotomy dependencies have not all been checked.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the directed independent-separator case within broad hereditary and demand-pattern classifications.
score_reasons.novelty: Ordered minimum-cut representations turn input arcs into increasing chains inside staircase windows, enabling sparse conflict covering and min–max-closed CSP optimization.
score_reasons.depth: The proof coordinates directed flow augmentation, chain geometry, hereditary enumeration, hardness gadgets, and global co-solution sparsity.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions distinguish induced constraints on deleted vertices from properties of the remainder, and fixed versus parameterized pattern assumptions.

checked: Read exact theorem and parameter quantifiers, including fixed H and fixed demand patterns and dependence on the H membership algorithm.
Traced the connector criterion for valid cuts and the chain lemma: each input arc excludes a southeast or northwest quadrant, forcing active marked points to be coordinatewise comparable.
Checked Chain CSP soundness/completeness using a covering family of small independent sets, then intersecting windows with required chains to preserve min–max closure.
Checked representation completeness for minimal separators once the stated flow-augmentation theorem is assumed.
remaining: Original directed flow-augmentation theorem and weighted min–max CSP optimization need source checks.
The conflict-degeneracy proof, all non-set-to-set hardness gadgets, proper-hereditary classification, and global co-solution union sparsity require audit.

review.summary: Claims a locally uniform explicit Airy-series limiting satisfiability profile for random2-SAT at m=n+xn^{2/3}, matching the independent-clause model, together with conditional backbone and unconditional spine laws on then^{2/3} scale and cubic-kernel/path-length geometry.

score_reasons.significance: Would settle a long-standing critical-window limit and characterize several associated forcing/geometric observables.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines mirror-orbit SCC enumeration with pure-literal-core excess domination to justify summing fixed-excess Airy limits.
score_reasons.depth: Uniform contour control, supercritical core concentration, marked explorations and joint kernel/length laws require extensive independent arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: The two limit operations and the precise external concentration uniformity are exposed; the breadth makes a complete verification substantial.

checked: Traced order-independence and clause-monotonicity of the pure literal core; its occurrence-degree formula makes excessX monotone.
Checked R≤X on satisfiable formulas after suppression: P−ℓ=2X−E_cross and3ℓ≤2E_cross implyP≤2X, while mirror pairing givesP=2R.

Verified the supercritical monotone-coupling tail argument withσ_k proportional(k/n)^{1/3}, then the exponential-moment/truncated-series dominated convergence. These are conditional on the stated uniform Kim concentration estimate and fixed-excess limits.
remaining: Check the interpretation and uniform constants in Kim’s external concentration theorem at boundedσn^{1/3}; the manuscript explicitly supplies a sequential-uniformity argument that needs source verification.
Audit exact signed-kernel enumeration, zero-free contour domain, all Airy asymptotics and tail coefficients.
Trace backbone/spine explorations, moment identities and joint path-length/Dirichlet laws; no numerical evaluation or full143-page proof certification performed.

review.title: Counting over Unbreakable Decompositions: A Single-Exponential Parameterized Algorithm for Minimum Bisection
review.authors: Aditya Anand, Evangelos Kipouridis, Karol Węgrzycki
review.summary: Deterministic 2^{O(k)} n^{O(1)} algorithm counts every vertex subset by size and edge-cut size j≤k, yielding minimum bisection in single-exponential parameter time. Builds a compact decomposition with adhesions ≤2k and (3k,k)-edge-unbreakable bags inside each subtree; this does not provide lean vertex-separation decompositions.
review.prior_frontier: Previous minimum-bisection bound 2^{O(k log k)} n^{O(1)}. New edge-unbreakable construction and logarithmic partition-function dynamic programming both remove the exponent loss. Prior historical bounds read from manuscript.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the single-exponential parameterized running-time question for a classical global-cut problem, with exact counting.
score_reasons.novelty: Connected-support cancellation and sink-based enumeration replace expensive color coding.
score_reasons.depth: Algebraic DP, bit-complexity control and new edge-unbreakable decomposition fit together tightly.
score_reasons.exposition: Full concise proof separates the essential edge-cut limitation from stronger unresolved lean-decomposition questions.

checked: Traced Section 4 counting DP: disjoint edge decomposition and marker variables; nilpotence of (x,z); logarithm/Möbius support extraction. Nonzero monomial support yields connected Y with |Y∩β|≤3k and |δY|≤k, via factorization across disconnected supports.

Checked sink enumeration: an important cut of order ≤k+q−1 contains candidate Y and bounds reachable bag vertices, yielding ≤8^{k+q} candidate supersets. Complement reconstruction uses |β|>2q, avoiding double counting; small bags are explicitly handled.

Traced decomposition loop: positive excess found by additive edge-boundaries over components; important-cut domination preserves positive excess. Menger paths inject newly added separator vertices in old components into old boundary vertices, preserving adhesion ≤2k. Strict bag shrink and disjoint nonempty own-bag vertices prove termination and ≤n nodes.

Checked nilpotent arithmetic polynomial bit lengths, k=0/disconnected cases, and clique forcing in search self-reduction. Standard important edge-cut enumeration and Menger used with their stated applicable hypotheses.
remaining: No independent implementation or formal verification; standard important-cut enumeration theorem and formal-power-series identities accepted as cited standard dependencies.

review.title: A Width Hierarchy of Monotone Algebraic Branching Programs
review.authors: Julian Dörfler, Alexander Rogovskyy
review.summary: Proves an infinite strict constant-width monotone ABP hierarchy, with depth at least (k/(w−1))^((floor(n^(1/(w−2)))−1)/2) for support-equivalent iterated k×k matrix multiplication when 3≤w<k. Gives depth/width formula comparisons and sharp bounded-multiplication-depth monotone formula bounds, including permanent. The restrictions are nonnegative real coefficients and monotone computation; this is not an unrestricted matrix-multiplication algorithm or lower bound.
review.prior_frontier: Contrasts with nonmonotone constant-width collapse to width 3 and refines known monotone formula/circuit separations. General constant-width monotone ABP strictness was not previously established according to the manuscript; prior work not exhaustively rechecked.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the internal width hierarchy of a basic restricted algebraic model and gives quantitative superconstant-width tradeoffs.
score_reasons.novelty: A support-density width-reduction lemma coupled with densification preserves enough iterated-product structure to iterate the reduction.
score_reasons.depth: The proof uses structural constant paths, support counting, recursive projections and a generalized Snir framework.
score_reasons.exposition: The monotone restrictions and hierarchy relations are explicit, with diagrams explaining decomposition and projection.

checked: Read the exact monotone model and hierarchy/theorem statements.
Checked the rectangular closure of the iterated-product support and inspected width-2 compression through constant components.

Traced the high-support decomposition: absent a constant prefix/suffix node in a layer, each node covers at most k^(n−2) monomials; distinguished constant paths yield fewer than d² width-(w−1) pieces.
Checked the densification counting argument over block endpoint sequences and the projected support fraction α^(m/n).
remaining: Need verify the simplifying transformations without width/depth loss, complete final recurrence and boundary cases, and the formula/permanent lower-bound framework and matching constructions.

Verified monomial lifting gives nonnegative integer energy≥1 on every violated active assignment; a retained-row Gram boundG≤W+I/(4D) then rules out any new satisfying assignment.

The central capturing/selector-degree duality was fully traced, including Boolean interpolation and parity degree, and the nonnegative-energy/Gram preservation calculation checked. Audit the INDEX reduction’s signed sketch combinations and legality/length of strict-turnstile simulations.
Inspect the external general-stream-to-sketch equivalence and the full active-row sparsification algorithm, including decoding workspace and regularizer removal.

review.summary: Deterministic fully dynamic weighted set cover under element insertions/deletions maintains O(log n) approximation with O(log² n) worst-case set recourse and O(f polylog(fn)) worst-case update time, for polynomially bounded cost ratio C. For general costs, recourse/time include polylog C; approximation does not. Sets and costs are fixed; f is element frequency.
review.prior_frontier: Previous nontrivial worst-case recourse results covered unweighted set cover, while their weighted extensions paid polynomial C. Earlier weighted low-recourse bounds were amortized, not worst-case. Comparison is based on the manuscript references.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the weighted worst-case recourse obstacle while preserving efficient worst-case updates and logarithmic approximation.
score_reasons.novelty: Coordinates nested background recomputations with a foreground cover, freezing rules, suspension, and priority-dependent swapping.
score_reasons.depth: The central charging argument limits how often deleted elements delay threads; complete synchronization and deamortization require lengthy invariant analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: The decremental showcase explains the weighted obstacle well, though the full 75-page implementation and general-cost qualifier need careful reading.

checked: Read Theorem 1.1 and its polynomial-cost-ratio footnote and dynamic update model.
Inspected the decremental thread-length proof: dead elements can be charged by at most two later runs of a fixed-index thread because their foreground level decreases at most once.
Checked how active-time sums and sufficiently many work units per update bound suspended thread age, and read the extended-background-cover approximation strategy.
remaining: Full fully dynamic insertion handling, removal of the showcase freezing assumption, worst-case update implementation, and complete foreground/background approximation proofs require audit.

papers.title: On Clifford hierarchy testing and near-extremizers of noncommutative uniformity norms
papers.authors: Zongbo Bao, Jop Briët, Davi Castro-Silva, Philippe van Dordrecht, Jonas Helsen

review.title: On Clifford hierarchy testing and near-extremizers of noncommutative uniformity norms
review.authors: Zongbo (Bob) Bao, Jop Briët, Davi Castro-Silva, Philippe van Dordrecht, Jonas Helsen
review.summary: For prime local dimension d, the fourth Pauli uniformity norm has a dimension-independent near-extremizer inverse theorem: normalized trace fidelity to Clifford-hierarchy level 3 is ≥1−L(1−||U||P4). With access to U and U*, this yields a tolerant 1−ε versus 1−Cε tester using O(1/ε) queries and efficient gates. Higher levels and the small-correlation inverse theorem remain open.
review.prior_frontier: Bu–Gu–Jaffe proposed a uniformity-norm tester but the robust level-3 analysis was open; earlier inverse theorems covered stabilizer/Clifford levels. This is the 99% regime, not fully tolerant arbitrary-fidelity testing.

score_reasons.significance: Closes the next natural hierarchy-testing case beyond Clifford gates.
score_reasons.novelty: Repairs approximately multiplicative Pauli-derivative data via scalar cocycles and an exact Heisenberg representation.
score_reasons.depth: Inductive separation, density extension, representation characters and inverse Fourier bound work together.
score_reasons.exposition: Short complete argument with explicit higher-level group-closure barrier and inverse-access limitation.

checked: Traced Theorem 19: ≥2/3 good derivatives extend to all h by A+A=F_d^{2n}; group closure holds only for P^(k−2), k≤4. Product error ≤6sqrt(2δ) and separation force scalar phase defects.

The bounded phase cocycle lifts mod 2π to a real cocycle; averaging gives a coboundary. Corrected representation has central character τ^p and vanishing noncentral traces, hence is unitarily equivalent to the Weyl representation. P² Fourier identity then integrates derivatives and gives fidelity loss 24 C_(k−1) ε.

Checked ε_k=24^{-k}, C_k=24^{k−1} satisfy separation and phase-lift inequalities for k≤4. The real-part bound suffices in the derivative overlap line on p11, despite its unnecessary equality to absolute value.

Tester probability follows recursive swap tests; near-one fidelity separates ||U||P4^16 at 1−16ε versus 1−18ε for ε≤.04. Direct sampling O(ε^{-2}); standard amplitude estimation on coherent circuit and inverse reduces queries to O(ε^{-1}).
remaining: Not formal verification; standard equality-of-characters representation theorem and amplitude-estimation theorem accepted as dependencies. No higher-level or inverse-free claims checked or established.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the computational classification of a basic market model.

checked: Checked Proposition 4.1 completely: positivity and payment balance make the derivative of the price curve feasible; local Lipschitzness justifies replacing that curve by its tangent; coordinatewise remainder control yields the epsilon-KKT inequalities.

papers.title: Flexible rigidity: Compiling generic trusted-preparation protocols into sequential device-independent protocols
papers.authors: Amir Arqand, Srijita Kundu, Ernest Y.-Z. Tan

review.title: Flexible rigidity: Compiling generic trusted-preparation protocols into sequential device-independent protocols
review.authors: Amir Arqand, Srijita Kundu, Ernest Y.-Z. Tan
review.summary: A generic sequential compiler turns trusted-preparation protocols into device-independent ones at any fixed rate below 1/2 with constant noise tolerance. Requires an entanglement-based realization, measurement-dependent self-testing isometries, and exponentially small bad-event probability under sufficiently small depolarizing noise. Applications include search-secure uncloneable encryption, one-bit decision security, point-function copy protection, and blind randomness expansion; interaction is linear in the security parameter and devices are not assumed safely reusable across protocol instances.
review.prior_frontier: Previous trace-distance/fidelity multi-copy rigidity cannot directly deliver this constant-noise constant-rate event-security transfer; prior general DI applications used parallel repetition. The advance is a Rényi-divergence comparison framework, not removal of all device or protocol assumptions.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a reusable security compiler for cryptographic tasks beyond ordinary entropy-based key generation.
score_reasons.novelty: Sequential Rényi comparison bounds transfer exponentially rare bad events multiplicatively while tolerating constant local noise.
score_reasons.depth: Requires channel-level divergence inequalities, testing-constrained comparison exponents, depolarized-state estimates, and several cryptographic reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: Postulates and rate/noise quantifiers are explicit; the 80-page argument has substantial dependency and application bookkeeping.

checked: Read the precise informal postulates and order of rate/noise/security quantifiers.

Traced the sequential comparison theorem from its one-round divergence lemma: tilted classical transcript blocks, empirical-frequency constraint, minimization over the tilt, and the α/(α−1)log(1/p_accept) normalization term.
Checked depolarized pure-state comparison via purification, Schmidt decomposition, concavity of t^(1/α), and a bound independent of retained-memory dimension.
Checked why the acceptance-probability penalty cancels when converting conditional divergence to Pr[accept and bad].
remaining: Critical one-round channel lemma, comparison-exponent duality, rigidity-to-compiler specialization, and each cryptographic security reduction remain unaudited.
No claim here of security for devices reused across independent protocol instances, or constant-round interaction.

review.title: Planted Dense Subgraph Conjectures Are Equivalent
review.authors: Shuichi Hirahara, Nobutaka Shimizu
review.summary: For each fixed rational 0<q<p≤1, polynomial-time conjectures for planted dense subgraphs are equivalent across fixed/binomial planted size, search/decision, and inverse-polynomial through exponentially-high success. Decision advantage only a constant factor above edge counting suffices. The exponent α in k=N^(1/2−α) may change across reductions.
review.prior_frontier: Extends fixed-size planted-clique equivalences beyond the earlier k≪N^(1/3) range and handles p<1 without clique structure; fixed/binomial equivalence answers the cited Bresler–Jiang question. Prior sources not independently audited; not an assertion for vanishing p−q.

score_reasons.significance: Unifies commonly used average-case hardness conjectures and identifies edge counting as conditionally optimal even at tiny advantage.
score_reasons.novelty: Resampling nonneighbors and geometrically thinning makes vertex-membership score means telescope for general dense subgraphs.
score_reasons.depth: Combines fixed-size amplification, low-vertex-degree analysis, conditional random-coordinate concentration and search-to-decision reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly states fixed densities, advice scope and changing planted-size exponents, avoiding an unjustified same-parameter equivalence.

checked: Traced Lemmas 7.1–7.3: binomial tail ≥1/2, output planted membership probabilities (1−p)Kt/N or (1−q)Kt/N, conditional edge independence, telescoping μ0−μ1 and γ/(4L) gap including p=1.

Checked Lemma 7.5 random-coordinate encoding: only membership bits and edges within S∪{v} matter, their maximum inclusion probability is n/((N−1)L(1−θ)), giving the stated concentration conditional on cited Lemma 7.4.
remaining: The 55-page equivalence still needs full amplification and low-degree proofs, source verification of the random-coordinate concentration theorem, threshold-estimation error and all reduction parameter/advice quantifiers.

review.title: Structured Quantum Hardness from Unstructured Assumptions
review.authors: Xiao Liang, Takashi Yamakawa, Chak Fai Yung
review.summary: Assuming UP is not contained in BQP, almost every random oracle O satisfies NP^O∩coNP^O not contained in BQP^O. Establishes unbounded-honest-prover postquantum NIZK proofs in QROM via strong dense pseudorandom hashing; also rules out fully black-box quantum reductions of hard NP∩coNP languages to postquantum injective OWFs and iO.

score_reasons.novelty: Whole-transcript PRHF interface removes oracle-dependent advice from the NIZK reduction.

Complete almost-sure separation and universal-decision-oracle black-box impossibility, including iO hybrids and all cited dependencies.

review.title: Random Garbage Creates Exponential Quantum Query Separations
review.authors: Khaled Elbassioni, Rishikesh Gajjala, Saurabh Ray
review.summary: A Boolean promise property of injective functions f(x)=(h(x),x,r_x), with h permutation or Simon and one fixed tag table, has at most n+2 XOR queries versus Θ(√N) forward-erasing queries, N=2^n. A permutation embedding, permitting every completion and no inverse oracle, gives O(log L) XOR versus Θ(L^(1/4)) forward in-place queries on L=4N². Lower bounds permit coherent bypass. These are promise/function properties, not total Boolean functions or ordinary space lower bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Addresses Aaronson’s erasing-versus-standard oracle question by a tagged Simon construction and extends to fixed-dimension classical permutations. The precise historical question and recent comparator papers remain external checks; this review applies the same eligibility criteria as for other submissions.

score_reasons.significance: An exponential oracle-interface separation for Boolean properties, with a fixed-dimensional permutation version and matching forward bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: Positive local recorded-sector contributions handle adaptive queries to a fixed random table; reverse coupling and a coherent-block contraction control unknown permutation completions.
score_reasons.depth: The injective case is compact, but the permutation proof requires joint Gram identities, norm control and locality beyond branchwise reasoning.
score_reasons.exposition: Models, randomness fixed across calls, every-completion promises, and limitations are stated explicitly.

checked: Read exact query/promise models and matching Simon-sampling and birthday upper-bound arguments.

Traced the generic local-recording comparison: contractions give near-unit trace; positive sector weights control exceptional restriction mass without assuming the adaptively recorded set is independent of h.
Checked reverse coupling by counting the unique (P,W) pair yielding each reference permutation, making it independent of hidden data.
Inspected the whole coherent i-block completed-square contraction calculation and recorded-sector locality, including the compact variant where the candidate index is not publicly readable.
Checked compact dimension L=4N² and final error term 16T√(N/L)=8T/√N.
remaining: Full signed-query simulation, hybrid disagreement bound, macro basis actions, Gram identities, and the injective contraction/sector induction must be independently audited end-to-end before selection.
This screening is not a correctness endorsement of the author’s own submission.

review.title: Hardness of Approximation for Polynomial Optimization over Sphere for Linear Programming Relaxation Hierarchy
review.authors: Mrinalkanti Ghosh
review.summary: For even fixed degree d and 2d|q≤n, each prescribed instance-independent family of ≤n^(Cq) valid degree-q spherical polynomial tests admits high-probability random harmonic powered-objective LP gaps Ω((n/q)^(d/2−1/2)/sqrt(q log n)). Polynomial feasible-point lifts are covered; arbitrary extended formulations, adaptive tests and SoS lower bounds are not.
review.prior_frontier: Contrasts the LP bound with powered SoS upper factor O_d((n/q)^(d/2−1)); obtains an LP/SDP ratio Ω(sqrt(n)/(q sqrt(log n))). Random-tensor SoS lower bounds concern a different hierarchy and are not improved by this theorem.

score_reasons.significance: Provides quantitative limits on a broad prescribed family of polynomial LP relaxations with a meaningful LP-versus-SDP separation.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses the top harmonic of a powered objective as a signed calibration direction and isotropic complex restriction to retain trace-free energy.
score_reasons.depth: Requires spherical covariance, hypercontractivity and deterministic harmonic-power energy estimates.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully distinguishes powered objectives, fixed test families, restricted lifts and the non-SoS scope.

checked: Checked signed-functional normalization and sphere identities, orthogonality objective gain α||F||², degree-r covariance scaling and feasibility union-bound structure conditional on the harmonic/hypercontractive lemmas.
Verified factorial/root arithmetic converts H^(1/(2r))sqrt(r/s) to (n/q)^(d/2)/sqrt(log n), and division by O(sqrt(n)) yields the claimed q factor.
remaining: Audit deterministic isotropic-restriction energy in Appendix A.6, spherical hypercontractivity and reproducing-kernel normalizations; verify the cited SoS comparison and lift reduction.

review.title: The Critical Window for Sampling and Learning-to-Sample in Spin Systems
review.authors: Shuchang Liu, Bingsheng Zhang, Kui Ren
review.summary: For fixed finite rational symmetric single-site GHS law with first nonquadratic rate-function term κm^{2p}>0, τ=1/Var and d_p=(p−1)/p: PSD spin systems J≤τ(1+δ)I admit TV sampling in poly(N,B,η^{-1}) exp(Oρ(Nδ^{p/(p−1)})). Under bilinear-group CDH, bounded-width zero-field instances at excess N^{−d_p+ε} remain hard for fresh-sample generation or k→k+1 amplification with polynomial training samples. Binary p=2 gives exponent 1/2; tricritical spin-one weights 1:4:1 give 2/3.
review.prior_frontier: Extends fixed-supercritical binary learning-to-sample hardness to a near-critical exponent matching parameter-only sampling, up to N^ε versus logarithms. Claims concern this GHS family and CDH, not all spin systems or exact threshold constants.

score_reasons.significance: Relates data-assisted computational hardness to critical exponents for a broad spin family.
score_reasons.novelty: Complete-cloud reduction and scalar convexification tie both directions to the rate-function type.
score_reasons.depth: Combines convex sampling, phase concentration and signature-based amplification hardness.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise bit-length, zero-field and joint-TV definitions; some universal headline language requires the stated GHS scope.

Checked moment integration-by-parts bound independent of external field, small quadratic regularization TV bound, and O(sqrt N)-Lipschitz accept-and-sample kernel converting W2 error to TV.
Read cloud concentration passage: exponential tilting normalizes each phase; sum of squared relative magnetization deviations absorbs interaction mismatch with Young’s inequality.
remaining: Complete bit-precision and LMC complexity implementation; full cloud lifting/spectral norm construction and independent-training-sample simulation.
Signature/CDH reduction, near-one TV hardness and zero-field gadget quantifiers.

Checked both runtime regimes. For k>d^2, grouping into Theta(sqrt(dk)) blocks and enumerating local nets gives exp(O_epsilon(sqrt(dk) log(dk))) within d^{O_epsilon(k)}.

papers.title: Optimal Alternating Regret for Online Learning and Games
papers.authors: Yixin Tao, Weiqiang Zheng

review.title: Optimal Alternating Regret for Online Learning and Games
review.authors: Yixin Tao, Weiqiang Zheng
review.summary: Alternation-aware Hedge achieves at most 8log d alternating regret for simplex OLO for every horizon, with Ω(log d) lower bound for T≥d−1. For bounded continuous convex losses on compact convex domains, minimax alternating regret is Θ(d log(1+T/d)) for d≥2,T≥16. Gives O(log d/T) averaged NE/CCE rates in two-player games. Alternating regret uses f_(t−1)+f_t, with f_(t−1) already known; the continuous algorithm requires integrals/optimization and is not asserted to be polynomial-time for arbitrary domains.
review.prior_frontier: Improves prior T^(1/3)-type alternating-regret guarantees to horizon-independent simplex bounds and logarithmic general convex bounds. Concurrent higher-order optimism papers also attain O(1/T) CCE in broader multiplayer settings; the manuscript distinguishes its stronger adversarial alternating-regret guarantee.

score_reasons.significance: Determines sharp alternating-regret complexity and removes the time logarithm from a natural two-player CCE learning dynamic.
score_reasons.novelty: A centered quadratic correction to exponential weights creates a concave one-step potential with an exact stationary point; the convex-domain rare-loss construction proves matching lower bounds.
score_reasons.depth: The new core is relatively short and elementary, with a subtle functional extension and a carefully scaled multiblock lower bound.
score_reasons.exposition: Exact regret notion, timing, lower-bound regimes and concurrent work are clear, and all new central proofs are self-contained.

checked: Checked unique centering maximizer via F″=4β²Var−2β<0, normalization/nonnegativity of x_i=p_i(1−ξ_i/2), and the full finite-dimensional potential proof.
Checked Hessian negativity of the one-step log-sum-exp functional for β=η/4,η≤1/8, the stationary point z=−ξ, and deduction R_i≤8log d.
Checked adaptive expert-elimination lower bound summing 2/(d+1−t), with horizon restriction T≥d−1.

Traced the continuous functional Hessian argument using bounded directional derivatives and Jensen; checked the KL variational inequality and contraction of the domain around any comparator, giving 8d log(1/δ)+4Tδ.
Traced the rare/common convex losses, block rotations, expected learner cost Kν, endpoint comparator cost≤10Kν², and horizon padding; verified the independent 2D-block extension and both T/d regimes.
Checked the two-player averaging connection by pairing (x_t,y_t) and (x_(t+1),y_t): each player’s alternating regret bounds its deviation sum up to endpoint constants.
remaining: No formal machine verification or finite-precision implementation audit. The continuous-domain result is an information-theoretic online algorithm, not a general efficient integration method.

review.title: Learning Positive Linear Combinations of ReLUs in Fully Polynomial Time
review.authors: Ilias Diakonikolas, Jelena Diakonikolas, Puqian Wang, Nikos Zarifis
review.summary: First claimed poly(d,k,1/ε)-time and sample PAC learner for positive combinations of k arbitrary ReLUs under standard Gaussian inputs, with relative L2 error and no weight-conditioning assumption. Improper hypothesis is a linear function plus ≤k positive absolute-value terms; realizable labels are the main theorem.
review.prior_frontier: Prior algorithms were quasipolynomial in k or exponential in 1/ε; the result removes both obstructions for positive coefficients and Gaussian marginals, not signed coefficients or arbitrary distributions. Prior bounds not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a natural longstanding polynomial-time learnability question for one-hidden-layer networks.
score_reasons.novelty: Boosts list-decodable coarse direction recovery through Gaussian localization, tangent-space updates and pruning, with implicit Hermite filtering for polynomial coarse recovery.
score_reasons.depth: The main chain combines high-order implicit tensor computation, robust direction covers and optimization/sample error control.

score_reasons.significance: Addresses two central online-selection problems with rank-one-optimal headline ratios.
score_reasons.novelty: Reversible reference-state updates and the half-sampling invariant are strikingly economical ideas.
score_reasons.depth: The short proofs are conceptually sharp; the optimal secretary implementation adds a substantial distributional framework.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit update-after-rejection rules, tie handling and snapshot conditioning make the audited arguments clear.

checked: Checked the entire factor-four secretary proof: greedy one-element sensitivity, feasibility, reversible configuration bijection, exact counting of sample/order pairs, snapshot independence and the displaced-element ordering argument.

Checked the entire factor-two single-sample prophet proof: conditioning on unordered value pairs, both snapshot-induction cases, the four-row exchange table, independence of previous acceptances, and the final joint distribution/expected-value identity.
Confirmed that all secretary queries concern already observed elements and that the prophet construction uses the known matroid with O(n^2) queries.

review.title: Deterministic Fault-Tolerant Connectivity Oracles with Subqadratic Space
review.authors: Merav Parter, Elad Tzalik
review.area: Graph data structures and lower bounds
review.summary: Deterministic edge-failure connectivity encodings use Õ(n min{f^{2/5},n^{3/4}}) bits for simple undirected graphs, with exponential decoding; claimed lower bounds are Ω̃(n^{3/2}) and Ω̃(n f^{1/4}). Queries must list actual edges by endpoints, without edge labels. Polynomial preprocessing costs n^{o(1)} additional space. A separate Õ(n√f)-space construction has Õ(f) query time.
review.prior_frontier: Prior unrestricted deterministic space was quadratic, versus Õ(n) randomized space with per-query success. The bounded-fault deterministic frontier was Õ(n√f); this does not become a fast-query improvement at the smaller new space.

score_reasons.significance: First subquadratic deterministic encoding for arbitrary failure sets and polynomial randomization separation.
score_reasons.novelty: Cut-matrix symmetry amplification and short mask hierarchies provide a new information-compression mechanism.
score_reasons.depth: Combines expander geometry, sparsification, and a nontrivial positivity-based encoding lower bound.
score_reasons.exposition: Model and exponential decoding are explicit; several typos and minor cut-enumeration presentation details remain.

checked: Traced Lemmas 4.2–4.5: symmetry forces equal expander neighborhoods, hence every nonempty symmetric cut has >3t²/4 edges; subtracting genuine failed edges leaves a symmetric internal contribution. Balancing t²≈εf with t≈ε^{-2} yields f^{2/5}.

Checked the mask-hierarchy backward decoder: when the next surviving cut is empty, b is within D of f_{i+1}−r_i, and the >2D amplification gap decides emptiness. Mask identifiers allow failed-edge membership without storing the graphs.
Read the planted bipartite cut coupling and its symmetry; the desired n^{3/2}/log n bound reduces to positivity at p≈1/(√n log n).
remaining: The 56-page fault-tolerance result has traced cut-symmetry and mask-decoding mechanisms. The mask construction, analytic positive-semidefinite theorem and final connectivity transfer remain substantial unchecked parts; this is a large-proof exception.

Mask-family construction, analytic PSD theorem, connectivity/component lower-bound transfer, and fast-query construction require a full audit; external expander and sparsification dependencies not independently checked.

Audit global multiscale error and work charging, WSPC exchange proof, hidden-pair query lower bound/doubling calculation and comparison-tree output multiplicity; Euclidean BCP integration remains unchecked.

papers.authors: Jean Rosemond Dora, Ladislav Hluchý

review.title: Cryptographic Guarantees for Distributed Training Under Malicious Adversaries
review.authors: Jean Rosemond Dora, Ladislav Hluchý
review.summary: Claims verifiable homomorphic gradient accumulation, maliciously secure private training for α<1/3, asymptotic nonconvex convergence and an optimal universal 1/3 threshold. The concrete commitment and convergence argument do not establish these claims.
review.prior_frontier: Describes KZG commitments and standard noisy-SGD descent as a new unified primitive; claimed universal synchronous threshold is not supported by a valid indistinguishability argument. No independently verified improvement established.

score_reasons.significance: Central guarantees fail under the stated construction/assumptions, so the advertised training security and convergence are not established.
score_reasons.novelty: The specified single-base random blinding destroys binding to the unblinded gradient rather than providing the claimed new primitive.
score_reasons.depth: Proofs invoke extraction or indistinguishability without the required construction, and the descent calculation drops adversarial bias.
score_reasons.exposition: Algorithms omit a gradient-validity relation/opening construction and use an unavailable set of malicious workers in verification.

checked: Checked Algorithm 2: C̃=g^(P(τ)+r). For any nonzero constant c with r−c≠0, the pair (P+c,r−c) gives the identical commitment. Thus this formula cannot bind the original gradient polynomial as claimed.

Checked equations (21) and (23): they replace the aggregate cross term by ||∇F||², although only honest gradients are assumed unbiased. Counterexample to the stated smoothness/bounded-MSE inference: F(w)=w²/2, g̃(w)=w+b, w1=−b gives all iterates −b and average squared gradient b²; MSE=b² is bounded, while η=T^−1/2 makes the claimed bound O(b²/√T).
The verification routine supplies no SNARK relation that would exclude this bias, and its check of total malicious weight presumes knowledge of which workers are malicious.
remaining: A replacement binding construction and explicit valid-gradient proof system, adversarial bias control and a different lower-bound proof are necessary before the main claims can be reconsidered.
issues: Original-gradient binding fails for the stated randomized commitment.
Theorem 8.1 uses an unjustified zero-bias step; bounded MSE alone does not imply its vanishing gradient bound.

review.desk_reject_reason: Concrete commitment equivocation P→P+c,r→r−c invalidates original-gradient binding, and the principal convergence proof is false under bounded aggregate MSE without unbiasedness; explicit quadratic biased-gradient counterexample above.

sources.detail: Algorithm 2 constant-shift equivocation; Algorithm 3 lacks a validity relation
Equation (21) improperly substitutes an unbiased aggregate

score_reasons.exposition: Carefully contrasts distribution-free bounds with smoother-design prior results; headline rates retain polynomial gaps.

review.summary: Unconditional polynomial-query attacks tolerate inverse-polynomial valid agreement in two restricted QROM key-agreement models: arbitrary classical-query/classical-message prefixes followed by quantum final stages, or constant-round classical communication with one classical-query party and one quantum-query party. review.prior_frontier: Prior general quantum-query impossibility required perfect correctness; unrestricted imperfectly complete QCCC key agreement remains open. The two restrictions are essential and are not an unconditional attack on arbitrary imperfectly complete QROM protocols.

score_reasons.novelty: Connects order clauses, shift graphs and tropical feasibility.
score_reasons.depth: Several long structural and algorithmic reductions across 94 pages.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions and intermediate reductions are explicit, though the scope is demanding.

checked: Traced the injective order-uniform discrete-clause argument: maximal-clique values give a hitting cover, functional classes are independent, and common refinement handles a union of discrete clauses.
Checked why cyclic clauses give no edges on order-uniform tuples and why a single consistent path component induces a shift-graph homomorphism.
remaining: The 94-page proof is a large-proof exception: the preprocessing, general projection lemma, tropical feasibility duality, interval representations, full obstruction theorem and reverse algorithmic encoding remain unchecked.

review.summary: Develops chi-boundedness and fractional-colouring structure for set-defined graph classes, including polynomial chi-bounds whenever chi-bounded, shift-graph obstructions for nearly full classes, and algorithmic links to tropical feasibility. These are restricted definability results, not the general Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript organizes formerly separate set-defined examples into a structural and algorithmic classification; its claims about the prior general frontier were not independently exhaustively checked.

papers.title: Rapid mixing of Gibbs samplers via quantum Dobrushin–Shlosman conditions
papers.authors: Cambyse Rouzé, Daniel Stilck França

review.title: Rapid mixing of Gibbs samplers via quantum Dobrushin–Shlosman conditions
review.authors: Cambyse Rouzé, Daniel Stilck França
review.area: Quantum Gibbs sampling and mathematical physics
review.summary: Constructs QBP-dressed finite-block Gibbs-preserving KMS channels. Claims logarithmic trace-norm mixing for all fixed-temperature finite-range spin chains, uniform in on-site field norms and single-exponential in βJ_interaction; stability around interacting DS references; and weakly quartic-interacting Fermi–Hubbard systems at fixed hopping and effective-potential spread. Nearly linear gate preparation requires bounded local input terms.
review.prior_frontier: Other recent all-temperature chain samplers already obtain logarithmic mixing; new distinctions are field-uniform normalized temperature bounds, a classical-to-quantum block criterion, and weak-interaction fermionic regimes. The result does not cover arbitrary-temperature higher-dimensional interacting models.

score_reasons.significance: Strong quantitative and physical-model extensions of rapid quantum thermalization.
score_reasons.novelty: Adjustable block/time QBP updates and a completed first/last-jump expansion give field-uniform influence control.
score_reasons.depth: Requires clustering, locality, KMS completion, quantum transport, and fermionic stability estimates.
score_reasons.exposition: Comparative scope is unusually explicit, though the 106-page proof has extensive analytic dependencies.

checked: Traced the weighted DS contraction from an admissible W₁ decomposition and Poissonization of the averaged channel.
Read the new localized influence argument: interior partial-trace-zero inputs kill every jump term, leaving an exponentially decaying no-jump map.

For boundary inputs, the completed channel J_T+R_I N_T permits a trace-contractivity cap. The first/last-jump identity, Gibbs clustering, and marginal cancellation yield min{1,M⁸ζ_u f(v)} before summing distances.
remaining: Field-uniform clustering and its temperature constants, QBP/KMS algebra and locality, complete influence summation, reference stability, fermionic derivation, and implementation error accounting require a substantial full audit.

review.title: Edit Distance Approximation: Subquadratic Factor Three and Monge Approximation Schemes
review.authors: Egor Gorbachev
review.summary: Randomized factor-three edit-distance approximations in soft-O(N^(11/6)) unit-cost and soft-O(N^(40/21)) metric-weighted time; a Monge sparsification theorem with soft-O(n log W/√ε) core supports (1+ε) bounded/dynamic weighted algorithms. Nonmetric weights have fine-grained/query hardness even on small alphabets.
review.prior_frontier: Author explicitly acknowledges a later near-linear (1+ε) unit-cost claim supersedes that component; weighted algorithms and Monge theorem remain separate contributions. Previously factor 3+ε in truly subquadratic time; cited superseding result and prior bounds not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a broad weighted-alignment toolkit and sharp model boundaries, beyond the separately superseded unit-cost approximation factor.
score_reasons.novelty: Repairing centers removes approximation slack; recursively coupling density rows/columns yields a sparse Monge core while preserving multiplicative entry accuracy.
score_reasons.depth: Combines Monge algebra, geometric sparsification, dynamic hierarchies, exact alignment repairs and several fine-grained reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes metric, symmetric-only and quasimetric settings, and openly identifies the superseded unit-cost component.

checked: Traced central Monge sparsification Lemmas 7.5–7.7: ordered interval coupling gives r+c−1 entries and maximal lower-left quadrant mass; only the leaf containing a quadrant corner changes its sum.

Verified the lower-left sparsity count by removing r leftmost elements per row, and recursive square classes: at most 2/ε earlier squares per mass class gives O(n/(ℓ√ε)) divided squares and O(n log n log(2+K)/√ε) core.

Checked additive ε max(1,Aij) error and zero preservation convert to multiplicative error using the stated nonnegative decomposition with disjoint supports; min-plus approximation preserves a shared factor rather than multiplying it.
remaining: Audit the cited general-to-simple Monge decomposition and complete oracle construction, center selection/repair runtime, weighted alignment composition and dynamic persistence, and nonmetric OV reductions. No claim that all 80 pages or the superseding paper have been verified.

papers.authors: Xiongxin Yang

review.title: Glauber Dynamics for Sampling Colorings: Rapid Mixing above $(1+1/\mathrm{e})\Delta$ via Hidden Hard-Core Models
review.authors: Xiongxin Yang
review.summary: For every fixed γ>0 and sufficiently large Δ, heat-bath Glauber dynamics for proper q-colorings of any maximum-degree-Δ graph has spectral gap Ωγ(1/n) when q≥(1+1/e+γ)Δ, and mixing Oγ(n(n log q+log 1/ε)). Uniform in growing Δ,q; no girth assumption.
review.prior_frontier: Prior general-graph threshold quoted as 1.7408Δ (Li–Oveis Gharan), following 1.809Δ and 11/6. The conjectured Δ+2 threshold remains open; bounded-degree n log n corollary uses additional spectral-independence dependencies.

score_reasons.significance: Large constant improvement for general-graph coloring Glauber mixing.
score_reasons.novelty: Ghost colors expose hidden hard-core models; resolvent smoothing separates mean from variance rather than incorrectly transferring conditional spectral gaps.
score_reasons.depth: Bochner rectangles, background perturbation and hidden-chain energy comparisons are delicate.
score_reasons.exposition: Good explanation of the conditional-mean obstruction and exact threshold source.

checked: Checked single-vertex and nonadjacent-pair expansions, and four-corner identity w(M+αdu)(M+βdv)=w(2M+αdu+βdv)²/4−w(αdu−βdv)²/4.
Traced lifting Lemma18: averaging hidden Dirichlet form equals single-color form; Jensen gives smoothed mean-part bound, not full variance.
Checked activity perturbation Lemma23: one background recoloring changes only neighbor activities, density ratio bounded by (1+1/(q−Δ−1))^Δ and operator difference by 4Δ/(q−Δ)³ times local energy.
Read resolvent comparison roadmap; hidden activities≤1/(q−Δ−1) fall below the hard-core uniqueness scale e/Δ.

Completed the central chain on PDF pp. 6–29: summed single-color identity; nonadjacent commuting projections; four-corner rectangle identity and its negative error; mixed second-difference estimate; mean/variance split; the ghost-color lift; resolvent contraction; invariant background-recoloring measure; activity-ratio and generator perturbation bounds; and the final two Bochner comparisons. In Lemma 24 the adjacent ghost-color dependence is handled by enlarging the recoloring set before averaging, not by an invalid independence assumption. In Lemma 20 the weighted recoloring involution is used before dropping its indicator. The constants 16, 38, 622 and the O_gamma(1/Delta) absorption are consistent; the final gap is theta_gamma/(96n).

Verified the essential heterogeneous hard-core extension against CFYZ primary arXiv:2105.15005, Definition 1.8, Theorem 1.9, Lemma 8.4 and Section 8.3. Complete spectral independence survives decreasing the fugacity separately at every vertex. After scaling all fugacities by 1/25, their maximum is below 1/(2Delta), so the same pinned path coupling gives gap at least 1/(2n); the boosting theorem then supplies a constant continuous-time gap. This validates the manuscript footnote without assuming that a uniform-fugacity theorem automatically covers heterogeneous activities.

Checked scope: all graphs of maximum degree at most Delta, fixed positive gamma and sufficiently large Delta; q >= (1+1/e+gamma)Delta. This is for the uniform proper-coloring model, not the general list-coloring guarantee of catalogue #1074. The n^2 log q mixing estimate follows from uniform stationary measure and the proved spectral gap.
remaining: No unresolved step in the central Theorem 1 proof was found. The primary spectral-independence theorem itself is used as an established external theorem, not reproved; historical priority claims and an extension to lists are not certified.

score_reasons.novelty: Fault-tolerant charging and randomized refresh survive adaptive updates.

checked: Traced Lemma 4.5's incorrect-singleton charging: correct-neighbour level charges have bounded multiplicity, while the alternative per-level bad-degree charge sums over logarithmically many levels.
Checked Lemma 4.8's outgoing-agreeing-edge charges to disjoint singleton edges and the epsilon/tau loss.

review.title: Near-Logarithmic Inapproximability of Parameterized Set Cover
review.authors: Bingkai Lin, Xin Zheng
review.summary: W[1]-hardness of approximating k-Set Cover within Ω(log ρ/(k² log log ρ)) for n sets and universe at most ρ log n, k^{Ω(k²)}≤ρ≤n^{O(1)}. Gives randomized k-OV-based fine-grained hardness, a randomized Turing universe–gap equivalence in the specified parameter range, and primal/dual VC-dimension bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Previous factor was (log n)^{1/O(k)}. Near-logarithmic W[1]-hardness was independently and almost simultaneously obtained by Guruswami–Ren and Karthik; this manuscript adds universe-size quantification and related tradeoffs.

score_reasons.significance: Major near-logarithmic approximation barrier in a central parameterized problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Simple local acceptance gadgets plus linear separators sharpen universe control; independent headline results temper exclusivity.
score_reasons.depth: Nontrivial coding/self-reduction and VC-dimension analyses extend the core reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit parameter ranges and independent work acknowledgement make the scope clear.

checked: Verified the h-local acceptance family: rejector Y is a universe element, selected σ covers it exactly when σ is outside Y; a rejecting selection of size≤h leaves itself uncovered.
Traced the vector-sum-to-label-cover reduction: at most (h/k)^k nonzero tuple sums are simultaneously separated by one linear hash, while linearity preserves YES tuples.
Checked the size composition m(kp)^h≤2^{O(kh log h)}log n and h≈logρ/(k log logρ), giving the k² denominator in the approximation factor.
remaining: Explicit linear-separator construction, source vector-sum hardness, randomized list-recovery/self-reductions, reverse Turing reduction and VC bounds require full audit.

review.title: Abelian embeddings make useful promises: approximation of detrivialised equations
review.authors: Tamio-Vesa Nakajima, Zephyr Verwimp, Stanislav Živný
review.summary: For each prime p≥5, equations x+y+z=0 mod p promised nonconstant on each triple admit polynomial-time four-color nonmonochromatic assignments, whereas three-color decision is NP-hard. Extends to finite Abelian groups without 2/3 torsion when the three-color promise is defined; introduces an Abelian-embedding singleton reduction.
review.prior_frontier: p=2,3 were tractable even with two target colors. Gives a tractable natural family not solved by fixed consistency or BLP+AIP; hardness lies outside reconfigurable-relation frameworks. Prior classifications not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Classifies a natural qualitative relaxation of linear equations and establishes a useful tractability mechanism beyond standard relaxations.
score_reasons.novelty: Peeling nonzero supports of group solutions uses a rounding that permanently satisfies all incident constraints.
score_reasons.depth: Hardness requires additive rigidity of binary polymorphisms and minion reductions, alongside torsion-sensitive rounding.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates undefined two-color promises and the finite-group qualification explicitly; the algorithm has a concrete worked example.

checked: Traced singleton reduction: any nonzero support contains at least two colors in every intersected equation, so assignments outside it cannot invalidate that constraint; failure to find any prescribed nonzero value forces the promised solution into q−1(0).
Checked four interval colors on Zp and lowest-nonzero-digit/product extensions, and the subgroup injective reduction.
Checked the two displayed tableaux in Theorem 4.19 force exactly one essential-first-coordinate minor, conditional on binary rigidity Theorem 4.18.
remaining: Audit full additive-combinatorial rigidity in Appendix E, p=5 hardness, minion source theorem and lower bounds against consistency/BLP+AIP.

papers.title: Beyond light cones: State preparation complexity in quantum spin glasses
papers.authors: Omar Al-Ghattas, David Gamarnik, Bobak T. Kiani

review.title: Beyond light cones: State preparation complexity in quantum spin glasses
review.authors: Omar Al-Ghattas, David Gamarnik, Bobak T. Kiani
review.summary: For dense Gaussian quantum p-spin Hamiltonians, a state family with effective weight-p Pauli-profile entropy O(n²) stays Ω(√n) below the optimum for sufficiently large fixed p (depending on the entropy constant). Subquadratic entropy gives o(√n) advantage over any conditioning benchmark, including product states. Implies Ω(n²/log n) arbitrary one/two-qubit gate lower bounds even with unlimited discardable ancillas; depth-width, MPS, magic-hierarchy and Clifford+T consequences have separate parameters.
review.prior_frontier: Claims substantially stronger resource lower bounds than previous light-cone bounds for quantum spin glasses; unrestricted ground-energy benchmark imported from ACKK25 and product-state limit from Bha26. Prior citations not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Nearly quadratic circuit-size energy obstructions with unrestricted discarded workspace are substantial.
score_reasons.novelty: Local-profile metric entropy, conditioned product approximations, and convex residual projections unify distinct resource bounds.
score_reasons.depth: De Finetti conditioning, Gaussian process bounds, ancilla reductions and stabilizer resource estimates span a long argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit conditioning benchmark and order of limits clarify precisely what the entropy theorem implies.

checked: Lemma 2.6 residual projection onto the closed convex benchmark-profile set is nonexpansive; covers transfer with a factor for all excluded subsets. The decomposition pays twice the hit-interaction norm and Dudley bounds the residual width.

Lemma 2.5 block diagonal Gaussian series has variance at most 3^p p m*/n and logarithmic dimension O(n), giving O(3^(p/2) sqrt(p m*)). Pauli Parseval in Corollary 2.4 gives the crucial 2^p rather than 3^p approximation factor.
Final quadratic comparison optimizes alpha=sqrt(L) p (2/3)^(p/2); resulting L^(1/4)p6^(p/4) is negligible against 3^(p/2)/p as p grows. Subquadratic comparison takes n first then alpha to zero.
remaining: Full quantitative nonsymmetric de Finetti/conditioning proof and its cited input.
Entropy bounds and arbitrary-ancilla reduction for each circuit/resource family; quadratic-size construction and magic/stabilizer applications.
Independent verification of imported unrestricted ground-state lower bound.

score_reasons.exposition: The proof states its stronger whole-neighbourhood oracle and the amplification dependencies.

checked: Traced the complete central greedy-colouring lower bound in Section 3 and Appendix A: high-girth small-independence graphs, exponential tree size forced by a greedy label, and transcript-preserving edge deletion.
Checked the whole-adjacency-list oracle footnote, which preserves degrees and ordered replies by keeping complete queried stars.
Verified the common-core/disjoint-neighbourhood packing and conditional independent-copy amplification, including the improper partial-colouring case.
Checked the Yao/Markov reduction, epsilon-fraction intersections and the appendix random-graph bounds.

review.title: Minimum Sum-of-Radii Clustering with Strong and Weak Oracles
review.authors: Zachary Friggstad, Mahya Jamshidian, Ali Vakilian
review.summary: Polynomial-time O(1)-approximation for minimum sum-of-radii using O(k log n log log n/(1/2−δ)^3) exact point queries and all persistent noisy distances, with independent pair corruption at constant δ<1/2 and a known polynomial aspect-ratio bound. The factor is stated below 270. Proves Ω(k log n) expected point queries for high-probability MSR and k-center approximation in the stated k range.
review.prior_frontier: Prior MSR constant approximation had exponential dependence on k in both running time and strong queries; previous general point-query lower bounds were Ω(k), with stronger bounds only for row-local algorithms.

score_reasons.significance: Removes exponential parameter dependence and almost matches query lower bounds in a substantive oracle model.
score_reasons.novelty: Packing-LP-guided sampling detects small inexpensive clusters; repair handles adversarial corrupted values.
score_reasons.depth: Adaptive witness concentration and LP rounding/repair are carefully interdependent.
score_reasons.exposition: Model, aspect ratio, success probabilities, and large constant approximation are disclosed.

checked: Checked Lemma 3.3 uniform corruption bound: disjoint W,M of sizes h,h/2 use independent cross edges, with failure exp(−h²/36) dominating n^{2h}.

Checked Lemma 3.4 union bound over entire strong-query sequences: for a fixed sequence witness sets depend only on the true metric, while distinct outside points use disjoint incident edge sets. This avoids conditioning on adaptively chosen witnesses.
Verified median-plus-radius estimate d(s,x)≤md(x,s)≤d(s,x)+2r_s outside corrupted witnesses and the λ/h cap’s λ/2 exceptional weight bound.
remaining: LP progress, candidate merging, fresh-witness repair, compression to k centers, guess search, general-δ extension, and non-row-local lower bound require a full audit.

review.title: Sources of Complexity in Multi-Agent Combinatorial Contracts
review.authors: Tomer Ezra, Michal Feldman, Mathieu Molina, Maya Schlesinger
review.summary: Separates three sources of multi-agent combinatorial-contract hardness already with two agents: superpolynomially many critical contracts, searching a small family, and equilibrium selection. Gives a tight O(√n) demand/value-query approximation for monotone subadditive rewards.
review.prior_frontier: Improves subadditive O(n) approximation to the cited Ω(√n) frontier; supermodular no-finite-factor and weighted-matroid-rank no-PTAS results isolate small-team hardness. Prior bounds not independently audited; demand access and principal-favorable equilibrium selection are part of the model.

score_reasons.significance: Explains why small teams remain hard through distinct structural obstacles and closes a subadditive approximation gap.
score_reasons.novelty: Critical contract vectors distinguish enumeration from equilibrium selection; uniform small-block payments balance concentrated and distributed reward.
score_reasons.depth: Combines strategic lattice arguments, oracle/NP hardness constructions and subadditive potential analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Results table cleanly separates reward classes, computational versus query barriers and fixed versus growing numbers of agents.

checked: Verified induced utilities are supermodular and have increasing differences; monotonicity makes greatest equilibrium principal-optimal when total share≤1.

Traced low-share block lemma: equilibrium cost≤αi f(Si); either a single-agent 3/4 contract gives f(Si)/12 or block potentials sum to ≥7f(SR)/8, with ≤ceil√n blocks and ≤1/4 total block payment. Constant accounting yields the stated 1/(1536√n) low-share bound.
remaining: Complete high-share case/source single-agent theorem and all three hardness constructions, critical-contract search algorithm and equilibrium enumeration remain unaudited.

review.title: NP-hardness of additive approximation for generalized Turán problems
review.authors: Yihan Chen, Jialin He, Xihe Li, Jie Ma, Tianying Xie
review.summary: For each fixed counted graph T with an edge, proves NP-hardness of additive n^(v(T)-epsilon) approximation of maximum T-copies in an F-free subgraph in these regimes: bipartite T and no F embeds into a blow-up of T; complete multipartite T under the same obstruction; or arbitrary T with min chromatic number(F) at least chi(T)+2. Both spanning and arbitrary-subgraph conventions and infinite fixed forbidden families are addressed.
review.prior_frontier: Extends Alon-Shikhelman-style conjectured dichotomy beyond K2 and earlier clique/3-connected special cases; concurrent clique/finite-family result is acknowledged. Historical claims not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves large structural cases of generalized Turán approximation hardness.
score_reasons.novelty: Iterated leaf additions isolate an edge term in homomorphism counts, with rooted extensions for nonbipartite targets.
score_reasons.depth: Lexicographic polynomial weighting, random transversals and blow-up error control interact nontrivially.
score_reasons.exposition: Reduction states exact computable baseline, signal and rounding tolerances, distinguishing spanning conventions.

checked: Lemma 4.6 weight choice di=v(T)+3+v(T) sum_{j>i} dj makes a lexicographically inferior monomial smaller by n^(-v(T)-3), enough to absorb all homomorphism factors.

Lemma 4.7 edge-terminal quotient lifts retain an original T-edge mapped into a G-cluster edge; at most B^v(T) d_J(u,v) lifts. Summing orientations and isolated vertices produces S E[e(R_J)], with other terms bounded by the full blow-up.
Roadmap converts forbidden-F0 counting into E[K_k(R_J)] = O(n^(k-eta) B^-eta), then uses exact integer rounding of cut_{k-1}(G).
remaining: Lexicographically maximal quotient Lemma 4.5, source-instance Lemma 3.4 and complete blow-up parameter arithmetic.
Rooted-extension proofs for multipartite/arbitrary counted graphs, plus finite/infinite forbidden-family hypotheses.

review.authors: Martin G. Herold, Evangelos Kipouridis, Dániel Marx, Joachim Spoerhase
review.summary: Unified randomized EPAS for cluster-aware distance-mapping objectives in metrics of bounded algorithmic ε-scatter dimension, and (3+ε) FPT approximation in general metrics. score_reasons.novelty: Separates objective-oblivious center finding from structured mapping selection.
score_reasons.depth: Inactive-center wakeups, frozen buckets, charging and ordered-norm DP require a long technical analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Restrictions and bicriteria violations are stated explicitly, but the 104-page framework is demanding.

checked: Read the exact center-finding and mapping-selection theorem split; the latter has expected time 2^{poly(d/ε)}|I|^{O(1)} under its structure.

review.summary: For k≥3 and only two benchmark predictors, multiclass omniprediction has no uniform finite sample bound for all bounded proper losses, and exponential-in-k bounds for Lipschitz proper/GLM losses. score_reasons.depth: Requires packing geometry, proper-loss smoothing, information bounds and careful order-of-quantifier distinctions.
score_reasons.exposition: The table and definitions explicitly distinguish actual regret, pseudo-regret and simultaneous loss-adaptive performance.

checked: Traced bounded-proper pseudo-regret lower bound: unseen θ bits and independent benchmark choice force loss 1/2 while one benchmark has zero loss, yielding (1−n/|X|)/2.

Checked Lipschitz lower-bound reduction conditional on smoothing/packing lemmas: estimator errors force the sum of two benchmark regrets ≥24ε(errors/N)−ε/4; ≥N/4 errors yields 9/20 failure and expected regret ≥103ε/40.
Verified n≥cN/(kη²), η=8sqrt(kεlog(1/ε)) and packing size convert to exponent (k+2)/4; fixed loss/benchmark is chosen before the learner sample in this argument.
remaining: Audit smoothing lemma with its Lipschitz normalization, packing and information Lemma B.4, loss-adaptive and GLM constructions, online transfers and entropy-based upper bounds.

review.title: Parallelism and Adaptivity in Student-Teacher Witnessing
review.authors: Ondřej Ježil, Dimitrios Tsintsilidas
review.summary: Under Sigma_(i+1)^p not contained in Delta_(i+1)^p/poly, separates r+1 adaptive student-teacher rounds with one query from r rounds with polynomially many queries, for unbounded increasing polynomial-time sublinear r. Also separates appropriate total-query budgets (with an additional final round). A general witnessing theorem yields conditional separations of replacement and short-induction theories, plus unconditional extensions of circuit-bound unprovability to stronger theories.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier KPS90 single-query round hierarchy; first-level collection/short-induction separations relied on factoring or one-way-permutation assumptions. Claims solve Buss–Ressayre and Pollett questions conditionally at all levels; not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Fine-grained adaptivity versus parallelism yields substantive conditional answers about bounded arithmetic.
score_reasons.novelty: Common teacher response and good-pair advice covering turn parallel-query simulation into nonuniform decision algorithms.
score_reasons.depth: Witnessing, proof-theoretic conservativity and quantitative search separations require several layers.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear class definitions, though fine-grained input-length conventions and normalization steps need careful reading.

checked: For witness-all search, a normalized student can combine polynomially many candidate witnesses; teacher returns a shared least-index still-unwitnessed instance. Each p-tuple has a good omitted element since only p-1 previous responses are used. Counting good pairs gives a polynomial-size advice cover.
Appendix A fixed-point argument h(k)=g(nk)-k cannot jump from positive to negative without zero: monotonic g implies h(k+1)>=h(k)-1. Sublinear bound gives a polynomial search range for fixed epsilon.
remaining: Full normalization of parallel candidates and exact polynomial-time/padding conventions for every input length.
General witnessing theorem, all theory interpretations and unconditional unprovability extensions.
Parallelism theorem full reduction beyond its initial construction.

review.authors: Frederic Koehler, Pui Kuen Leung

score_reasons.significance: Settles a central conjecture underlying approximate BosonSampling complexity.
score_reasons.novelty: A Gaussian Fourier-compression comparison transfers determinant gamma-product control to permanents.
score_reasons.depth: A concise but substantial interpolation and distributional induction.
score_reasons.exposition: The benchmark, induction and exact density constant are unusually transparent.

checked: Traced the full central real/complex/quaternionic anticoncentration proof: Gaussian geometric interpolation in modulus, two-coordinate Fourier compression, Fourier-to-Laplace conversion and gamma-product induction.
Checked determinant cofactor rotational invariance, negative gamma moments, telescoping normalization and the monotone Gaussian-mixture limit giving n/pi in the complex case.
Rendered the interpolation and compression formulas to verify absolute-value bars omitted by text extraction; no missing phase assumption is needed.
Checked the real/complex additive-row replacement argument. The original Aaronson–Arkhipov source confirms that average-case hardness remains a distinct conjecture.
remaining: The supplementary quaternionic perturbation/independent-row extensions and appendix moment tables were not exhaustively checked.

sources.detail: Original Aaronson–Arkhipov statement separates anticoncentration from average-case hardness.

review.summary: Proves Gaussian permanent anticoncentration, including the Aaronson–Arkhipov conjecture: for a complex iid Gaussian n-by-n matrix, the normalized permanent has density at most n/pi, hence every epsilon-radius disk has probability at most n epsilon squared. score_reasons.novelty: Structural stacks reduce nonconvex geometry to directed-metric ATSP and convex mini-containers.

score_reasons.exposition: Detailed structural development and limitations, with minor repairable arithmetic in a local geometric bound.

checked: Read bowl enlargement inside a constant dilation and strict-stack reduction. Pairwise minimum vertical increments obey directed triangle inequality by removing the middle bowl; a metric ATSP tour produces an O(1)-approximate stack.
Checked the core-based reason size grouping costs O(log n) rather than O(log²n): separated aspect-ratio groups have disjoint cores, and a maximal disjoint core family bounds same-group containers.
Traced the final mini-container span condition to ℓ_max h_max=O(OPT) in the longest-radius coordinate frame.
remaining: Fine-type structural theorem, full rotational normalization, APX-hardness gadgets, robust computational geometry/degeneracy conventions, and external packing/ATSP algorithms require full audit.
issues: PDF p.19 Claim 13 second displayed estimate subtracts 7εr from X without a stated lower bound on Y. The available X≤10εr and Y≥0 instead give t≤2.5εw, still <h−Y; this appears a repairable constant calculation, not a failure of the lemma.

review.title: Two ReLU layers is all you need
review.authors: Florestan Brunck, Christoph Hertrich, Kilian Rueß, Jack Stade, Amir Yehudayoff
review.summary: Every continuous piecewise-linear function over any real subfield containing Q is exactly representable by a ReLU network with two hidden layers, of unrestricted finite width. In particular MAX_n has a rational two-layer representation. No polynomial-width or efficient-learning claim follows.
review.prior_frontier: Collapses the depth hierarchy, beyond earlier finite MAX_5/MAX_12 constructions and logarithmic-depth simulation. Integer/localized-ring lower bounds remain compatible because the construction uses rational division. Prior finite-case bounds not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the exact unrestricted-width depth hierarchy for ReLU networks, replacing logarithmic depth by the optimal constant two.
score_reasons.novelty: A signed family of pyramids over parallelepipeds gives a thermostat-walk cancellation identity for the simplex modulo lower-dimensional pieces.
score_reasons.depth: The direct proof combines support-function valuation, exact Minkowski slicing, signed permutation counting and dimensional induction; an independent homological proof is also provided.
score_reasons.exposition: The short direct proof gives explicit polytopes, cancellation factors and clear distinctions from width/precision lower bounds.

checked: Traced the complete direct central proof: each sign region P_A equals the sum of simplices Δ_(A∪{j})−e_j by fixing negative-coordinate slices; all but |A|=n−1 vanish modulo lower-dimensional support functions.
Verified the triangular coordinate change makes every K_(v,π,M) a pyramid over a parallelepiped, hence its support function has two hidden layers.

Traced thermostat cancellation: after summing marked sets, a nonzero walk rises below t and falls above t; minimal-coordinate condition gives a unique merge of positive/negative orderings, signed count (−1)^(s−1)s!(n−1−s)!.

Summing over v and sign regions leaves coefficient (−1)^n n! on h_Δ. Valuation modulo lower-dimensional cells and induction yield MAX_n, then the stated standard finite-max representation yields all CPWL functions. Valuation is justified by additive Euler integration of halfspace slices; finite subdivisions handle boundary corrections.

Independent exact integer/rational sanity check of Lemma 20 passed 50 generic points for every n=2,…,7 (300 total), enumerating all permutations; script audits/check980.py and results audits/check980-results.json.
remaining: The separate homological proof and polynomial bit-precision claim were not audited. No size bound or efficient conversion is certified; the central exact-representation result was traced through the direct proof.

review.authors: Tatiana Rocha Avila, Holger Dell, John Lapinskas
review.summary: For deterministic nonadaptive temporal undirected graphs with fixed positive vertex degrees, defines Phi=max_Delta min_{time windows, fixed cuts} max_{time in window} conductance(cut)/Delta and proves O(m/(d_min Phi)) consensus with probability at least 1/2, hence expected time by restarting. General interval-wise bounds and matching regular dynamic constructions are supplied; authors report a full Lean formalization.
