score_reasons.significance: Tight bounds handle connectivity invisible in every individual snapshot.
score_reasons.novelty: Stable/unstable volume intervals allow a fixed-cut temporal guarantee to control moving opinion cuts.
score_reasons.depth: Stopped drift and temporal lower-bound construction are technically substantive.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions and limitations are clear, but the infinite random-matching example overstates the uniform-in-time parameter.

checked: Stable-interval Lemma 3.7: expected accumulated cut mass either already >=phi Vol/8, or Markov bounds early stopping by 1/4 and cut deterioration by 1/6. The fixed-degree cut-variation lemma controls deterioration by accumulated current cut mass, giving success probability >1/2.
Corollary 3.6 stopped telescoping uses predictable survival indicators and volume within [1/2,3/2] of its initial value; constant 32(3/2)^(3/2)=24 sqrt(6) checked.
remaining: Unstable interval potential, arbitrary-opinion reduction, temporal lower-bound construction and formal Lean theorem correspondence/compilation.

Correct the illustrative infinite i.i.d. matching example on PDF6: for n>=4, every fixed finite window length almost surely has arbitrarily late runs of a single disconnected matching. Thus the all-time minimum window conductance and Phi are zero, even though finite-horizon high-probability examples may work. This does not refute the deterministic main theorem.

review.authors: Jonathan Conroy, Hung Le, Jack Spalding-Jamieson
review.summary: Every n-vertex K_h-minor-free graph has a 3/4-balanced vertex separator of size at most 16h√n, resolving the 1990 Alon–Seymour–Thomas conjecture. The new ingredient is a walk of length <13k/ψ hitting k possibly overlapping sets of size at least n/k in a vertex expander. The presented separator procedure is existential/exponential, not a polynomial-time construction.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the recent O(h√(n log h)) bound to O(h√n), removing the remaining √log h factor; earlier O(h√n+f(h)) structural bounds did not settle uniform dependence on h.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a long-standing central separator conjecture with optimal dependence on the excluded clique size.
score_reasons.novelty: The uniform-subset transport coupling handles overlapping large target sets and avoids the prior padding/flow barriers.
score_reasons.depth: Combines a concise probabilistic transport lemma with carefully maintained clique-minor and boundary invariants.
score_reasons.exposition: An accessible, essentially self-contained proof with precise constants and honest nonalgorithmic scope.

checked: Traced the full new argument in §§2–3. Conditional endpoint multiplicity p_J and the coupling to q_J preserve a uniform visited-index subset, including overlapping target sets.
Recomputed Eσ_i²=1/[t(k−t)] and negative off-diagonal covariance; hence E||p_J−q_J||₂²≤k/[r t(k−t)]. The transport bound and sum/integral ≤π give <13k/ψ.

Verified the essential external inequality against Bobkov–Houdré–Tetali original PDF pp.3–4: the normalized-counting λ∞ definition and Theorem 1 imply Var(f)≤2/(√(1+ψ)−1)² for graph-1-Lipschitz f. Together with finite-metric transport LP duality and ψ≤2 this gives the manuscript’s 4√n/ψ bound. Source: https://tetali.math.gatech.edu/PUBLIS/bht.pdf .

Checked the three separator cases, disjoint charging of sparse-cut sides, ball boundary replacing old branch-set boundary, radius ceil(√n/h) growth, and ≤15√n new branch set. |K|<h gives ≤16h√n boundary; removing ≤n/2 per iteration retains |H|≥n/4 and termination supplies 3/4 balance.
Checked small n/h trivial cases and extension from connected inputs by operating on a component larger than 3n/4. Viewed PDF p.14 to confirm the algorithm’s case-3 indentation.
remaining: No machine formalization was run or audited; the linked Lean repository is an author-provided artifact, not evidence of an independently verified build. The proof check is a mathematical reading, not a formal correctness guarantee.

Checked balanced constraints intersect each block at most once, so conditional per-variable maximization decomposes into independent local scores.

review.title: The Complexity of Correlated Equilibria Beyond Normal-Form Games
review.authors: Ioannis Anagnostides, Constantinos Daskalakis, Gabriele Farina, Noah Golowich, Tuomas Sandholm, Brian Hu Zhang
review.summary: For any prescribed polynomial support bound, inverse-polynomial approximate fixed sets are PPAD-hard; this gives unconditional CE hardness for two-player concave games quadratic in each player’s own strategy. Explicit multilinear polytope games are hard at exponential precision, and inverse-polynomial precision there is conditional on PCP-for-PPAD. Also gives swap-regret lower bounds and tractable restricted-deviation equilibria.
review.prior_frontier: Extends equilibrium hardness beyond fixed points and explains limits of general swap regret. Does not settle every extensive-form CE question; the support/precision tradeoff is essential because an O(1/ε)-support fixed set has an FPTAS. Prior complexity source results not independently re-proved.

score_reasons.significance: Characterizes a central obstruction to correlated-equilibrium computation beyond normal-form games and connects it to a new fixed-point relaxation.
score_reasons.novelty: Synchronizes one stationary transition matrix across many scaled copies of a map; an entropy plateau forces a supported approximate fixed point.
score_reasons.depth: Resolvent entropy, conditional variance, multiscale accuracy and imitation-game reductions give a delicate polynomial-support hardness theorem.
score_reasons.exposition: Formal theorems separate concave from multilinear-polytope models and acknowledge the PCP-for-PPAD assumption, though the abstract can suggest a broader unconditional claim.

checked: Traced complete central Theorem 1: geometric resolvent P(t)=t(I−(1−t)P)^−1, stationary interpolation K(t,s), entropy difference as expected KL, and a scale with entropy increment≤log k/r.
Verified conditional variance bound V(s)≤2(α+η)/s and V(t)−V(s)≤2(h(t)−h(s)); stationarity and Pinsker justify both.

Checked averaged displacement bound (8t+η)/α and Lipschitz conversion to residual; parameters r=Θ(log K), constant b and ε=δ/(16r b^r) give inverse-polynomial precision. The final numeric coefficient is below 1/2 and dimension D=O(d log d) preserves prescribed support.

Traced Proposition 3.6: CE conditional-mean deviations bound two squared residuals; composing x→y→x′ yields a stationary chain and 2√ε fixed-set error without enlarging support. This establishes Theorem 2 from the stated standard constant-precision Lipschitz fixed-point hardness.
Read fixed-set/convex-EFP duality and checked its finite-support convex dual construction.
remaining: Separate explicit-polytope/multilinear gadgets, swap-regret lower bound, restricted-deviation algorithms and external hardness source proofs were not audited. Main-proof-checked refers to central fixed-set hardness and its concave-game CE consequence, not all results.

review.title: Testing for a Large Induced Expander: Sublinear Algorithms and Query Lower Bounds
review.authors: Pan Peng, Ranran Shen
review.summary: In bounded-degree adjacency-list access, tests existence of an induced alpha n-vertex core of normalized inner conductance phi against absence of a kappa alpha n core with conductance Theta_{alpha,kappa}(phi²/log n), using O_{alpha,kappa}(sqrt(n) phi^-2 log n) queries for constant error. Boundary/exterior unrestricted. Adaptive lower bound Omega(n^(1/2+c_{kappa,phi} mu)) for rejection mu phi², uniform in mu, degree512 and phi<=9/20. Exact-size structural testing instead needs linear queries; distance relaxation retains size.
review.prior_frontier: Whole-graph expansion and near-spanning noisy-expander tests existed; new core can be any fixed fraction with arbitrary exterior. Lower bound adapts CKK18 noisy parity. Prior literature not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Nearly determines the square-root query frontier for a substantial expansion relaxation.
score_reasons.novelty: Trace visits compared to a common unknown endpoint distribution, with exceptional starts charged to size slack; vector parity labels support lower bounds for every constant core fraction.
score_reasons.depth: Excursion identities, collision tests and adaptive likelihood bounds form a lengthy argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Precisely distinguishes normalization by degree bound, size slack, distance soundness and uniform-in-mu lower-bound quantifiers.

checked: Stopping-time identity h(I-P)=e_x-nu and Cesaro telescoping give TV <=E[tau]/ell without stationarity of nu. Integrability/predictability justify expected visit sums.

Kac-type aggregate return identity sum_{x in U}(E tau_t-t)=t(|C_U|-|U|), and threshold 1+8(1-alpha)/beta leave at most beta n/8 bad starts. Combined trace mixing and averaging produce common distribution pi_U Q_ell; alpha=1 handled separately.
remaining: Full collision primitive with reused anchor samples, soundness partition estimate and final sample complexity.
Vector-parity adaptive lower bound and exact-size/distance constructions.

review.title: Marton's conjecture in polynomial time
review.authors: Srinivasan Arunachalam, Arkopal Dutt, Sabee Grewal, Aparna Gupte

score_reasons.significance: A major algorithmic counterpart to a central additive-combinatorial theorem, with broad learning consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Implicit density coins, entropy-slack regularization and terminal extraction turn entropic structure into algorithms.
score_reasons.depth: A substantial recursive algorithmization with rejection costs and success budgets.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear separation of oracle model, core traversal and applications, though the detailed bookkeeping is long.

checked: Checked the sum, fibre and endgame sampling/coin constructions, their envelopes and averaged entropy-slack/rejection-cost identities in Lemmas 4.4–4.6.
Traced the complete terminal heavy-self-sum extraction: entropy localization into a bounded quotient, coin estimates, rank growth and constant-index conclusion.
Checked candidate-subspace shrinking and the two-sided overlap/size verifier, including singleton handling and concentration margins.
Checked the final amplification and covering deduction conditional on the traversal guarantee.
remaining: Large-proof exception for the 64-page argument: the recursive bucketing and good-trajectory runtime proof in Section 4.3–4.4 remain unverified, as do the robust-sampling and learning applications.
The entropic PFR input is an external theorem; its full proof was not re-audited.

review.summary: Given uniform sampling and membership access to A in F_2^n with doubling at most K, outputs a basis for a subspace V of size at most |A| whose polynomially many translates cover A, in poly(n,K,log(1/delta)) resources. Applications include quadratic Goldreich–Levin and stabilizer-learning tasks.
review.prior_frontier: Algorithmizes the recent existential polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa theorem with polynomial rather than quasipolynomial parameter dependence. The access assumptions are both uniform sampling and membership, and the primary output is a subspace basis rather than an enumeration of A.

review.title: Optimal spectrum estimation
review.authors: Ainesh Bakshi, Apoorv Vikram Singh, Xinyu Tan
review.summary: Entangled measurements estimate an arbitrary d-dimensional spectrum in total variation epsilon using O(d^2 min{(epsilon log d)^(-4),(epsilon log d)^(-2)}) copies; an unentangled analogue has d^3 in place of d^2.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the previous polylogarithmic spectrum-estimation overhead and contradicts an earlier conjectured d^2/(epsilon^2 log^2 d) barrier. Entangled optimality relies on a cited recent lower bound; unentangled optimality remains conjectural.

score_reasons.significance: Determines the claimed entangled sample complexity across both error regimes.
score_reasons.novelty: Integer-valued CDF structure improves polynomial moment reconstruction beyond generic Lipschitz duality.
score_reasons.depth: Quantum Efron-Stein decomposition and higher-derivative observables yield sharp variance bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The proof exposes its two accuracy regimes and distinguishes measurement models, though technical dependencies are substantial.

checked: Read the reconstruction argument exploiting integral CDF differences to bound the squared derivative of a Wasserstein dual witness by the error itself.
Traced the centered tensor/quantum Efron-Stein decomposition and orthogonality over subsets; inspected the independent-measurement second-moment bound and Chebyshev derivative choices.
Checked the different full-interval and interior approximation regimes and that only the entangled upper bound is claimed optimal.
remaining: Audit the complete derivative-cycle variance calculation, Jackson approximation appendix, parameter constants, external bucketing/rank reduction, weak Schur implementation, and the cited matching lower bound.

papers.authors: Nikolai Chukhin, Karthik Gajulapalli, Alexander Golovnev, Ivan Mihajlin

review.title: A Little Derandomization Goes a Long Way: Unconditional Circuit Lower Bounds using Low-Degree PIT
review.authors: Nikolai Chukhin, Karthik Gajulapalli, Alexander Golovnev, Ivan Mihajlin
review.summary: Unconditionally, either NE has languages outside SIZE[2^n/(2n)] or constant-free VP_Z^0 differs from VNP_Z^0. Refines PIT-to-lower-bound tradeoffs; gives O_d(s t^(d−1)) fixed-finite-field constant-degree PIT and faster integer syntactically set-multilinear tests with an explicit intermediate coefficient-bound promise.
review.prior_frontier: Removes derandomization from a Boolean–arithmetic win–win while keeping a deterministic one-quantifier Boolean verifier, at the cost of a constant-free arithmetic alternative. Does not establish either disjunct individually or unrestricted VP≠VNP. Prior KI/source hierarchy results not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Obtains a substantial unconditional disjunction at major Boolean/arithmetic lower-bound frontiers.
score_reasons.novelty: Low-degree partition polynomials and bounded-coefficient integer tests allow the specific identity checks in a quantitative KI reduction to be derandomized.
score_reasons.depth: Interlocks set-multilinear tensor contractions, coefficient-bit bounds, nondeterministic SAT verification and circuit lower-bound transfer.
score_reasons.exposition: The constant-free/formal-degree distinctions and one-sided coefficient promise are explicit, but the 58-page reduction chain needs careful full audit.

checked: Traced finite-field PIT: sparse-support grid catches every monomial on ≤d−1 variables; otherwise the polynomial is homogeneous multilinear degree d and a first derivative is nonzero even in small characteristic; reverse differentiation gives constant-factor circuit overhead.

Traced integer central PIT Theorem 5: heavy-gate frontier splits each term into complementary types between d/3 and 2d/3; two contraction orders save max(min of opposing block sizes)≥d/6. Squared coefficient norm detects zero over Z.

Checked truncation rejects oversized intermediates without false acceptance; promised gate l1 bounds control all intermediates. Set-multilinear projection has 3^d circuit overhead and at most doubled coefficient exponent.

Verified selecting constant d≫c makes identity tests cost 2^(11n/12)poly(n); λ=1/(2d) yields the claimed nondeterministic branching-program speedup and the final formal-degree coefficient bound feeds the win–win.
remaining: Audit universal/partition polynomial completeness, nondeterministic proof soundness Lemma 6.3, conversion from branching programs to circuits and Theorem 7.1 lower-bound transfer; range-avoidance and MA applications remain unchecked.

papers.title: Verifiable Quantum Advantage and Computation via Quantum Circuit Obfuscation
papers.authors: Alexandru Gheorghiu, Aparna Gupte, Vojtěch Havlíček, Yunchao Liu

review.title: Verifiable Quantum Advantage and Computation via Quantum Circuit Obfuscation
review.authors: Alexandru Gheorghiu, Aparna Gupte, Vojtěch Havlíček, Yunchao Liu
review.summary: Assuming classical obfuscation of quantum circuits with approximate-channel iO security, gives private blind classical BQP verification with no additional hardness. Public verification adds postquantum OWFs. Two-message publicly verifiable proofs of quantumness use classically secure qiO and BQP not contained in infinitely-often P/poly (stronger than BQP≠BPP). An oracle separation and a conditional local-mixing route to qiO are further results, not unconditional standard-assumption constructions.
review.prior_frontier: Existing CVQC based on quantum-hard cryptographic primitives; proposes qiO-only private verification and a rigorous conditional peaked-circuit foundation. Prior literature claims not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Simple verification from qiO alone clarifies which hardness assumptions are actually needed.
score_reasons.novelty: Masks and hidden computation locations reduce cheating to guessing the planted set; same-channel obfuscation also yields indistinguishability of I and X under worst-case BQP hardness.
score_reasons.depth: Nonuniform security and worst-case circuit compilation are careful, with additional oracle and mixing-framework machinery.
score_reasons.exposition: Formal security and infinitely-often hypotheses qualify the more informal headline claims.

checked: Lemma 4.4 hardwire/amplify/copy/uncompute creates a one-logical-qubit channel negligibly close to I or X. Nonuniform qiO over all circuit families bounds max_x deviation, allowing a distinguisher to decide all inputs at infinitely many lengths.
Private proof-of-quantumness hybrids replace polynomially many obfuscations with I; final challenge independent of hidden bits has exact success 2^-t.

Theorem 5.2 replaces planted computations by canonical X^{s_ij}; uniform masks make s independent of planted locations. Wrong accepted response must flip exactly one hidden entry per row, probability <=cols^-rows. Same hybrids give blindness up to shape.
remaining: Public verification/one-way-function construction and security, oracle construction and precise local-mixing assumptions.
No independent assessment of feasibility of the approximate-channel qiO primitive.

papers.authors: Angus Lowe, Xinyu Tan

review.title: Random dimension reduction and learning symmetric properties of quantum states
review.authors: Angus Lowe, Xinyu Tan

score_reasons.significance: A broadly reusable rank-dependent method improves several quantum property-estimation bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: The learning interpretation and joint-purification separation are new, while the channel itself has prior precedent.
score_reasons.depth: Elegant linear algebra and representation-theoretic bookkeeping rather than a very long technical construction.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise common-isometry hypothesis, rank convention and prior-work qualifications.

checked: Traced the elementary channel identity through kernel support, Haar twirling, permutation moments and pseudoinverse normalization.
Checked the full no-joint-purification argument using two nonorthogonal pure inputs, Stinespring preservation and a swap observable.
Checked Schur-block implementation identities and the trace-distance/fidelity continuity transfer to the sample bounds.
remaining: The external sample-optimal tomography and efficient Schur-transform theorems were not re-proved; the separate random-purification construction and external operator-power estimate for Tsallis entropy were not fully audited.

review.summary: A common random dimension-reduction channel preserves simultaneous isometry-invariant properties of multiple quantum states. Combined with tomography it yields O(r^2/epsilon^2) copy upper bounds for pairwise trace distance, fidelity and squared Hellinger distance, where r is the maximum rank. It also rules out a corresponding joint purification channel.
review.prior_frontier: The channel's Schur-basis action was already present in universal-decoder work, explicitly acknowledged here. New contributions include its elementary formulation, multi-state learning use and purification impossibility; some purification results are simultaneous independent work.

papers.title: NP-Hardness of Bounded Distance Decoding for Reed-Solomon Codes and Variants, via Non-Archimedean Rings
papers.authors: Venkata Gandikota, Elena Grigorescu, S. Venkitesh

review.title: NP-Hardness of Bounded Distance Decoding for Reed-Solomon Codes and Variants, via Non-Archimedean Rings
review.authors: Venkata Gandikota, Elena Grigorescu, S. Venkitesh
review.summary: Deterministic NP-hardness for Reed-Solomon decoding with n^alpha agreement surplus beyond dimension, arbitrary fixed rate and subexponential field size; extends to folded codes with growing folding and shrinking capacity gap.
review.prior_frontier: Prior deterministic reductions allowed only logarithmic-scale surplus at particular rates or constant surplus. The result concerns constructed evaluation sets and vanishing gaps, not hardness for every RS code or fixed capacity gap.

score_reasons.significance: Substantially enlarges the hard decoding parameter range for a fundamental explicit code family.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses complete additive characteristic-p orbits, first two moments, and an Artin-Schreier coefficient to encode exact satisfiability without dividing by p.
score_reasons.depth: Careful field tower, polynomial independence, padding and folding transfer produce deterministic reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: All essential reductions and polynomial-time parameter choices are explicit and short enough to trace.

checked: Traced Theorem 1.6 throughout pp.18-27: explicit quadratic field tower; additive-orbit reciprocal product; distinct high-degree markers; first-two-moment forcing of whole orbits; coefficient-p recovery despite arbitrary padding; exact-one clause decoding.
Independently checked the Artin-Schreier descent: p does not divide extension degree, so L(x) in the base field implies x is in it (equivalently use the normalized trace).

Checked the RS leading-coefficient reduction in both directions and folded triangular scaling invertibility. The multiplier is found by avoiding roots of an explicit polynomial of degree at most n^4+1 in a field larger than that; it also has order greater than sn.

Checked n=h^A choices, prime p between d/2 and d, target cardinality margins, small-formula padding, subexponential field bound, and the final shrinking-epsilon folded regime. No randomized field-construction assumption is used.
remaining: Not a formal or machine-checked proof. The starting NP-completeness of exact-one 3-SAT and elementary prime-existence theorem are standard external inputs, not reproved here. Bibliographic priority and independent implementation are not certified.

review.title: Parallel Edge Ranking of Trees
review.authors: Jeff Giliberti, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Changki Yun
review.summary: Tree edge-ranking decision is P-complete even for diameter≤6, and constant-additive approximation is P-hard. Deterministic NC achieves additive log₂n/log₂log₂n in O(log⁴n) time; MPC computes optimal rankings in O(log D+n^(3/4)D^(1/4)/S) rounds with S=Θ(n^(3/4+δ)) and O(n) total memory.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves the cited longstanding parallel-complexity question and improves a previous additive log n NC approximation. MPC local memory is a particular strongly-sublinear regime, not fully scalable arbitrary n^δ memory. Prior sources not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a classical P-completeness question while showing meaningful approximation and MPC escape routes.
score_reasons.novelty: Encodes greedy binary allocation into shallow tree branches and compresses subtree merge information for MPC.
score_reasons.depth: Combines monotone-circuit reductions, visible-rank critical sets, product amplification and parallel merge analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Explains model distinctions and explicit diameter/memory tradeoffs clearly.

checked: Traced branch realizability: if binary weight of X dominates critical set C, raise the root edge to max(C△X) to shadow exactly the missing lower ranks.

Checked star branch gadget weight q−1 followed by one root edge implements binary increment to q; merging gadgets realizes allocation with diameter≤6 and polynomial O(sum log²qi) size, constructible via parallel prefix sums.
remaining: Audit monotone-circuit-to-allocation gadgets, constant-additive product amplification, NC approximation proof and MPC compression/cost bounds.

papers.title: Algorithmic Aspects of the Fermi--Hubbard Model
papers.authors: Ainesh Bakshi, Ankur Moitra, Xinyu Tan

review.title: Algorithmic Aspects of the Fermi--Hubbard Model
review.authors: Ainesh Bakshi, Ankur Moitra, Xinyu Tan
review.summary: Quantum Gibbs sampler for nearest-neighbor fixed-dimensional Fermi–Hubbard with beta<=c/(d³ t_max), mixing in O(log(n/epsilon)) from any physical even state, independently of on-site repulsion/chemical potential. General m-mode local fermionic systems need beta<=c4^-m(DL)^-3; qubits beta<=c(DL)^-3 independently of arbitrary fields. Exhibits efficiently preparable non-Gaussian-mixture fermionic Gibbs states and entangled qubit states; separability holds up to fields of order log(1/beta)/beta under suitable locality constants.
review.prior_frontier: Prior general high-temperature samplers controlled on-site terms too; weakly interacting results allowing hopping reference Hamiltonians address different regimes. No demonstrated universal quantum speedup is implied merely by leaving Gaussian/product mixtures.

score_reasons.significance: Uniform-in-on-site-energy preparation opens physically distinct regimes beyond existing high-temperature guarantees.
score_reasons.novelty: Field-resonant filters plus fermionic local disagreement/transport remove the field scale from contraction and propagation.
score_reasons.depth: Parity-aware partial traces, quasi-local Lindbladians and model-specific non-Gaussianity require substantial new analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit temperature normalization and comparisons carefully separate high-temperature relative to hopping from weak interactions around general quadratic references.

checked: On-site contraction Lemma 7.12: paired X/Y jumps cancel cross terms, and local tracelessness diagonalizes the update on three Pauli components. Gaussian convolution with Delta=max(h,1/beta), eta=sigma=sqrt(Delta/beta) bounds the resonant coefficient below e^-1/4/sqrt2 independently of h.

Lemma 7.13 expresses component-scaled locally traceless Hermitian operator through signed Pauli conjugates with total coefficient variation max(c_x,c_y,c_z); the stated coefficient choice verifies each component and trace-norm contraction.
Fermionic transport roadmap uses parity-preserving conditional expectations and telescoping disagreements rather than nonlocal Jordan–Wigner supports.
remaining: Full field-independent Lieb–Robinson/quasi-local filter estimates, Dobrushin matrix row sums and efficient simulation cost.
Fermionic on-site contraction and even-state norm analysis; non-Gaussian example, separability and classical-hardness claims.

score_reasons.exposition: Clear query invariants and explicit word-size hypotheses, though many dependencies require navigation.

checked: Traced the complete new two-layer special-rank composition: coarse rank identifies the local occurrence, concatenation offsets subtract preceding matching blocks, and padding cannot affect queried prefixes.

Inspected the bucket-code and small-universe baseline descriptions, including the boundary-rank lookup invariant.

papers.authors: Chengkai Zhang, Yuhao Li, Elaine Shi, Mengqian Zhang, Lirong Xia, Qishen Han

review.title: Sybil-Proofness of Generalized Adaptive Clinching and Implications for Blockchain Mechanism Design
review.authors: Chengkai Zhang, Yuhao Li, Elaine Shi, Mengqian Zhang, Lirong Xia, Qishen Han
review.summary: Generalized adaptive clinching is Sybil-proof under aggregate budget constraints; a two-sided AMM mechanism achieves exact settlement, individual rationality and weak Pareto optimality for eligible bids.
review.prior_frontier: Classical clinching provided truthful bidding and Pareto guarantees but its resilience to splitting budgets into arbitrary identities was unresolved; full Pareto/Sybil guarantees for AMMs face impossibility results.

score_reasons.significance: Adds a meaningful robustness guarantee to a foundational budget-constrained auction and a two-sided application.
score_reasons.novelty: Abstract target conditions support a merged-versus-Sybil comparison beyond fixed supply.
score_reasons.depth: Coupled gain inequalities, terminal budget accounting and cross-direction effects require delicate analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions make budget, censorship and weakened efficiency restrictions explicit.

checked: Read target admissibility and the new gain-gap argument: the minimum of group and outsider gain gaps satisfies a differential inequality preventing it from crossing below zero; inspected the merged-run termination extension using remaining budget.

The result prohibits aggregate overreporting in the true trading direction and assumes other bids cannot be censored. Efficiency concerns eligible bids and disallows counting reverse-direction pool trades as improvements.
remaining: Complete existence/regularity of the clinching dynamics, structural lemmas supplying gain inequalities, two-sided manipulations, and budget-overreporting impossibility remain unaudited.

review.summary: Polynomial-time obfuscation secure for equivalent circuit pairs possessing bounded-size Extended Frege proofs, with circuit/proof-size bounds public but proofs not supplied to the obfuscator. Assumes uniform logarithmic-input obfuscation, polynomial-security LWE at subexponential modulus/noise ratio, and a quantitative tunable discrete-log assumption.
review.prior_frontier: Addresses obfuscation without superpolynomial security reductions for this proof-bounded equivalence class; not unrestricted iO. Quantitative discrete-log advantage bounds are additional assumptions, not a consequence of ordinary polynomial hardness. Prior constructions not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A potentially important connection between feasible equivalence proofs and polynomial-security obfuscation, with substantial cryptographic qualifications.
score_reasons.novelty: Converts EF equivalence proofs to polynomial sequences of changes with three-wire support and combines this with short-proof HSS correctness.
score_reasons.depth: The 247-page construction interlocks proof normalization, circuit padding, multi-party HSS and security amplification.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed quantitative hypotheses and circuit interfaces are provided, although the complete dependency chain is exceptionally long.

checked: Checked the distinction between a fixed public proof-size bound and a proof input; checked the extra quantitative DSEDL assumption.

Traced width-three derivation to incremental changes: conjunction-factor swaps use three support wires; activating a line follows its at-most-four premises; output switching preserves the conjunction. Verified the O(K²) step count and constant changed-cell bound in Theorem 3.10.
Inspected fixed-topology selector construction and the zero-coefficient argument for externally inactive cells.
remaining: Full EF-to-width-three normalization and boundary details of Lemma 3.4 remain; the checked incremental-change argument is conditional on that normalization.
The HSS construction, its formal EF correctness proofs, and the cryptographic hybrids/quantitative security combiner spanning most of the 247-page paper remain unchecked.

papers.title: Kendall–tau Center Admits a PTAS
papers.authors: Diptarka Chakraborty, Debarati Das, Anish Mukherjee

review.title: Kendall–tau Center Admits a PTAS
review.authors: Diptarka Chakraborty, Debarati Das, Anish Mukherjee
review.summary: Deterministic PTAS for Kendall–tau 1-center of arbitrarily many complete rankings on arbitrarily many candidates, time (nd+1)^O_epsilon(1). A constant-size input subset determines movement intervals containing one near-optimal ranking; discretized sorting keys, influential-variable fixing and joint LP optimization handle all maximum-distance constraints.
review.prior_frontier: Previously trivial factor2 for unrestricted worst-case center, despite median PTAS and better average-case center algorithms; prior claims not independently checked. FPTAS excluded by integral objective and cited NP-hardness.

score_reasons.significance: A PTAS settles a long-standing factor2 barrier for a fundamental rank aggregation objective.
score_reasons.novelty: Inversion-union movement certificates localize one simultaneous near-optimum, followed by a nontrivial joint optimization framework.
score_reasons.depth: Discretization, multi-criterion pair-cost estimation and deterministic rounding occupy a long technical proof.
score_reasons.exposition: Roadmap explicitly avoids assuming pairwise comparison choices form a ranking or that the original optimum lies in the movement intervals.

checked: Theorem 4.3 greedy addition removes more than delta R* unrevealed optimal inversions each time, giving at most 1+ceil(1/delta) selected inputs (R*=0 handled).

Lemma 4.4 compares input-distance change to tournament-cost change pairwise; only unrevealed inversions agreeing with that input contribute an extra2. A minimum-cost tournament order is therefore simultaneously (1+2delta)-optimal.

Lemma 4.5: moving v before each wrong-side R candidate gives I>=b(b+1)/2-bh; moving all these R candidates after v gives I+b<=bh. Hence b+3<=4h for b>0, and symmetric bound yields movement <=5h. This relies on L-to-R comparisons inherited from an inversion union.
remaining: Entire sorting-key discretization, surrogate-cost decomposition and LP rounding Sections5–6.
Polynomial enumeration/runtime and derandomization for arbitrary number of inputs; movement lemma alone is not an algorithm.

review.summary: Claims a robust-solvability dichotomy for fixed signed symmetric Boolean promise templates, logarithm-free square-root robustness for mode/conservative-separable classes, and quantitative soft-equality transfer with a sharp universal exponent loss. review.summary: Specified LWE assumptions exclude quasipolynomial weak automatization of uniform growing-prime affine-query refutations; stronger quantitative assumptions yield near-quasipolynomial strong-search bounds for Boolean tree resolution and parity resolution.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier cryptographic nonautomatization results concerned stronger calculi; the direct affine system must locate an original false clause, not merely assert a global arithmetic contradiction.

score_reasons.significance: Extends proof-search hardness to a weak affine benchmark even when output uses any fixed sound efficient calculus.
score_reasons.novelty: Balanced residual and invalid-digit descents turn short integer relations into shallow original-clause refutations.
score_reasons.depth: Combines quantitative LWE tails and proof-size gaps with a separate Boolean lifting argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Especially careful about security rates, rounded Gaussian law, growing modulus and strong versus weak search.

checked: Traced the short-relation pigeonhole bound and two balanced descents, including unattainable weighted digit sums and verification of leaf clauses.
Checked the affine parameters m=3d, sigma=d, q=Theta(d^4), B=Theta(d log d), giving exceptional probability O(log(d)/d^(2/3)) and quasipolynomial refutation length.
The affine result is uniform over a growing input prime; the Boolean statements are strong automatization only and use a different reduction plus exponential security.
remaining: Audit the full Boolean circuit-gap and parity-lifting construction, quantitative search cutoffs, security/dual-attack compatibility, and external proof-system dependencies.

review.authors: Mohammad T. Hajiaghayi, Mahdi JafariRaviz, Alireza Kaviani, Soheil Mohammadkhani
review.summary: First polynomial-time algorithm claimed for Győri–Lovász connected partitions with arbitrary terminal count; extends to directed k-T-connected graphs and prescribed capacities. Maintains assignments to flow-essential terminals; a weighted implementation yields O(n k m^(2+o(1))) time.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves the claimed general polynomial-versus-exponential constructive gap, previously open even for fixed k>4; directed and weighted variants have additional model conditions. Historical and external flow-runtime claims not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A polynomial constructive form of a classical connectivity theorem would settle a central long-standing algorithmic question.
score_reasons.novelty: The flow-essential assignment invariant and cycle reassignment potential replace exponential partition search.
score_reasons.depth: The new criticality-transfer argument uses cut intersection/union and rerouting to force strict potential decrease, with weighted extensions requiring further machinery.
score_reasons.exposition: The core mechanism is exceptionally carefully illustrated, including cut-location tables and explicit invariants.

checked: Traced Lemmas 4.9, 4.13, 4.14 and 4.12: critical deletion reduces connectivity by one; rerouting through the matched terminal proves assignability; two deleted edges still admit κ−1 paths; cut intersection makes both endpoints cross while the union cannot be invalidated, giving contradiction.

Verified that cycle labels are distinct because their original terminals differ, capacities are preserved, and each moved vertex strictly reduces its set of critical secondary edges. The integer potential lies between zero and k times the number of nonterminals.
Inspected terminal deletion and outer contraction/deletion algorithm interfaces.
remaining: Complete verification of cut lattice lemmas, preterminal matching, all contraction invariants and outer algorithm recovery remains.
Weighted split-assignment construction, fast implementation and DAG refinement remain unchecked in this 67-page manuscript.

review.summary: Approximate-DP agnostic halfspace learning under standard Gaussian marginals with improper sample bound ~O(Dp/alpha²+Dp/(epsilon_DP alpha)), Dp=binom(d+p,p), p=O(alpha^-2), in high dimension d>=C alpha^-5. Proper learner adds alpha^-6 and epsilon_DP^-1 alpha^-5 terms and exp(O(alpha^-4 log1/alpha)) work; semi-agnostic proper error C OPT+alpha costs ~O(d/alpha²+d/(epsilon_DP alpha)). Known log-concave marginals and all-dimension improper variant incur an extra alpha^-1/2 in privacy cost.
review.prior_frontier: Claims first efficient private agnostic halfspace algorithms under these marginals with dimension exponents matching nonprivate counterparts. Privacy is free up to logs only in the specified epsilon_DP versus accuracy regime; prior claims not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Provides useful statistical/computational privacy guarantees across proper and improper structured-marginal learning.
score_reasons.novelty: Clipped Hermite features with a sharp second moment and low-dimensional proper conversion enable familiar private optimization primitives.
score_reasons.depth: Mehler generating functions, influence-subspace analysis and privatized iterative semi-agnostic learning are substantive.
score_reasons.exposition: Formal theorem exposes dimension restrictions and defines the privacy-for-free regime, though the abstract omits these qualifications.

checked: Clipping bias inequality |s q-y|<=s|q-y|+1-s pays only clipping probability, not the magnitude of an unbounded polynomial.
Lemma C.2 Mehler coefficient expansion yields E[(Kp/Dp)^2]<=exp(2p²/d); binomial ratio and (d/2+j)/(d+1+j)^2<=1/(2d) verified. Chebyshev gives rare clipping at 2sqrt(Dp) when d>=2p²/alpha.

Repeated independent private ERM training, nonnegative excess loss Markov amplification, uniform threshold grid and fresh validation exponential mechanism trace the improper learner accuracy calculation.
remaining: Privacy composition/dependency invocation, proper subspace lemma and semi-agnostic iterative noise analysis.
Full log-concave construction and numerical/arithmetic model.

score_reasons.significance: A meaningful fault-tolerant extension of foundational distributed graph sketches.
score_reasons.novelty: Subsampling removes failed-node interference while communicating only sampled-node sketches.
score_reasons.depth: Several public/private randomness constructions and failure/cheating distinctions.
score_reasons.exposition: Models and comparison table are clear; some probability statements use loose shorthand.

checked: Traced the public-coin subsampling warm-up and the two-phase failure-resilience mechanism: first isolate failed-node-containing blobs, then merge at most k remaining active blobs.
Checked the directed spanning-tree success events, inclusion-exclusion dependence types and harmonic geometric-waiting-time bound at the level of the stated sampler primitive.
Checked worst-case communication capping in the actual parameter regime with many subsamples.
remaining: Large-proof exception for the 46-page collection: malicious-message consistency checks, private-coin cover-free constructions and communication lower bounds remain unchecked.

Lemma 4.1's arbitrary-c wording needs the usual sufficiently-large-mean qualification for a high-probability constant-factor Chernoff bound; its actual applications have enough subsamples. Sampler success constants in pair-event upper bounds should be treated conservatively, without affecting the asymptotic margin.

checked: Read the exact exponential-size separation and SAT-to-short-versus-long-SA-proof reduction.

Read the conditioning-on-paths expansion underlying the polynomial moment formula.

review.authors: N. Efe Çekirge, Amit Chakrabarti, Purna Dutta, Andrew McGregor, Vinayak
review.summary: Puncturable graph sketches support post hoc deletion of fewer than k vertices with additive O(k) sketch dimension. Obtain public-coin O(k log³ n) and private-coin O(√(kn) log^(3/2)n) bits per node for vertex connectivity with polynomial-time sparse-certificate recovery; deterministic promise lower bound Ω(min{√n,n/k}).
review.prior_frontier: Public-coin connectivity improves O(k log⁴ n); private-coin bound generalizes the k=1 √n result; deterministic ordinary connectivity improves n^(1/3) to √n. These prior comparisons are manuscript claims, not independently rederived.

score_reasons.significance: Improves both communication upper bounds and a fundamental deterministic connectivity lower bound.
score_reasons.novelty: Retroactive vertex deletion uses vanishing-polynomial moments to turn adjacency sketches into scaled incidence sketches.
score_reasons.depth: The method couples algebraic sparse recovery, strong low-error fingerprints, adaptive certificate construction and communication lower bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The central transformation is explicit and cleanly separated from its applications.

checked: Traced Theorem 4: use distinct products of the first n primes in a sufficiently large Θ(n³) field; multiplying moments by P_F deletes forbidden neighbors, retains at least 2d moments and creates symmetric edge weights. Summing over a supernode cancels internal edges; Vandermonde recovery then identifies a boundary of size at most d.
Noted the harmless global sign-convention inconsistency between displayed sketch and later formulas; either uniform sign convention preserves cancellation and recovery.
Distinguished exponentially many theoretical deletion sets from the claimed O(n²)-query certificate implementation.
remaining: Fingerprint collision analysis, private-coin sampling, adaptive certificate recovery and deterministic lower bounds remain unaudited.

review.title: Exact Sum-of-Radii Clustering under Any Constant Stability
review.authors: Shyam Ravichandran, Lev Reyzin
review.summary: For every fixed gamma>1, deterministic exact recovery of unique minimum-sum-of-radii k-clustering in general finite metrics under arbitrary symmetric multiplicative [1,gamma] perturbations; perturbations need not be metrics, centers lie in their clusters and k is part of input. Runtime n^O((gamma-1)^-5) for gamma<2. Stability recognition and supplied-partition verification are coNP-complete under specified rational inputs.
review.prior_frontier: Extends prior gamma>=2 MSR recovery and separates MSR from MSD/k-center stability thresholds below2. Prior cited hardness not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Exact recovery under every constant stability factor is a substantial improvement for general-metric clustering.
score_reasons.novelty: Merge-and-split perturbations impose local density and linear growth, enabling bounded-treewidth local recovery.
score_reasons.depth: Combines global exchange structure, partitioning and cluster-count dynamic programming.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully specifies nonmetric perturbations, unique partitions versus centers, and feasibility on unstable inputs.

checked: Split-perturbation Lemma3.5: graph of distances>=radius has no isolated vertices; switch to a degree1 neighbor if present to choose center c and split point p. Scale all internal pairs except c-to-other remaining points, forcing every eccentricity to gamma r while remainder radius stays<=r.
Merge-and-split Lemma3.6 preserves exact k by merging s clusters and splitting s-1 disjoint nonsingletons; uniqueness forces strict exchange inequality.
Local density Lemma3.9 follows by splitting large clusters; small-cluster union radius <=2u+2b and optimality bounds total radii of large clusters inside a ball.
remaining: Random-partition success, bounded-treewidth dependency applicability and local DP coverage constraints.
Derandomization and coNP-completeness reductions, including metric-perturbation verification variant.

review.title: Solving Linear Systems in $\tilde{O}(m n \log \frac{\kappa}{\epsilon})$ Bit Operations
review.authors: Jonathan Kelner

score_reasons.significance: A major finite-precision sparse linear-algebra advance.
score_reasons.novelty: A simple perturbation makes the modular inverse identically I, removing Dixon lifting's dense bottleneck.
score_reasons.depth: Sharp bit bookkeeping, rational reconstruction and scale-independent certification.
score_reasons.exposition: A concise complete account with explicit encoded-exponent and residual conventions.

checked: Traced the complete new algorithm: modular lifting, residual magnitude invariant, Hadamard height bound, reconstruction precision, sparse per-step cost and perturbation residual.
Checked integer precision doubling and the exact rational residual certificate, including balanced-tree fraction arithmetic.
Checked floating-point normalization without expanding exponents, entrywise rounding, singular intermediate rounded matrices, acceptance certificate and short-output bounds.
Independently reproduced 120 exact-rational cases in dimensions 1–6, including singular core inputs: reconstructed solutions equal exact Gaussian elimination and satisfy A(Rz)-b=-z.
Verified the bounded rational-reconstruction criterion in Monagan's primary paper and the fast reconstruction dependency against the Pan–Wang publication.
remaining: The established fast integer multiplication and fast Euclidean reconstruction implementations were used as cited primitives, not reimplemented for performance benchmarking.

sources.detail: Theorem 1 and Algorithm RR: bounded rational reconstruction.

review.summary: Deterministically solves a nonsingular sparse linear system to relative residual epsilon in near O(mn log(kappa/epsilon)) bit operations for logarithmically encoded inputs. General floating-point input cost is accounted for separately, and the output uses short integer significands with one encoded exponent; no condition-number bound is required.
review.prior_frontier: Improves sparse polynomial-condition-number systems from roughly n^2.2707 to near-quadratic bit complexity in the stated regime. Dense matrix-multiplication algorithms may remain faster; this is a residual approximation, not an exact unperturbed solve.

review.title: Synergies between Proof Complexity and Cryptography

review.summary: Combining subexponentially secure iO with no infinitely-often subexponentially optimal proof system yields almost-everywhere circuit hardness in quasipolynomial unambiguous classes, conditional UP intersection coUP hardness, and non-Levin NP-hardness of implicit gap MCSP.
review.prior_frontier: iO alone previously implied a substantially weaker NEXP circuit lower bound; known learning hardness did not ensure a total single-valued implicit function on all reduction outputs.

score_reasons.significance: Connects strong cryptography and proof complexity to hardness in small semantic classes and a constrained MCSP representation.
score_reasons.novelty: A general fooling framework repairs semantic promises and enhances reductions using hard unsatisfiable formulas.
score_reasons.depth: Combines proof-system uniformity, NIWI, keyed one-way permutations and cryptographic hardness reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes nonconstructive existence, randomized versus nonuniform reductions and the extra derandomization premise.

checked: Read the exact joint assumptions and total-function sampler promise; this is implicit gap MCSP, not ordinary truth-table MCSP.
Inspected the central fooling lemmas: rejecting transcripts define sound proof systems; absence of optimal systems supplies a P-uniform hard family.
UP intersection coUP needs promise-BPP=promise-P; without it the claimed class has quasipolynomial unambiguous time. The reductions and hard languages are nonconstructive.
remaining: Verify the imported optimal-proof-system equivalence, NIWI and certifiable-permutation constructions, total-learning to implicit-MCSP transformation, and the non-Levin obstruction.

review.authors: Manuel Christalla, Sharat Ibrahimpur, Teng Liu
review.summary: Polynomial-time adaptive probing achieves expected O(log^(5/2)n) approximation to the clairvoyant optimum for stochastic asymmetric TSP with independent activations. A probe must immediately be followed by visiting an active vertex. Also obtains O(log(n+k)) expected final stochastic discrepancy against adaptive ordering when the whole candidate vector pool and activation probabilities are known.
review.prior_frontier: Contrasts with a polynomial obliviousness gap for fixed a-priori tours; this is a new intermediate information model, not a polylog approximation for fixed-order tours. Prior gap source not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Establishes a useful quantitative boundary between fixed-order and fully clairvoyant stochastic routing.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses activation-contingent bypasses as discrepancy signs and remaining-vector correction capacity to handle adaptive order.
score_reasons.depth: Bipartite circulation, iterative rounding and stochastic matrix-normalized martingales interact in the final routing bound.
score_reasons.exposition: Information assumptions, immediate-visit rule and final-versus-prefix discrepancy distinction are explicit.

checked: Traced the new signing martingale: Q_t=λI+sum of remaining p_i w_i w_iᵀ is known before activation; y_t=−Q_t⁻¹x_t has conditional mean y_(t−1), since expected signed increment is p_i w_i w_iᵀy_(t−1). General signs center by ηp_i and preserve this identity.
Checked that inclusion of coordinate vectors in the stopping condition gives final infinity norm at most λ(β−α)/2; this does not give bounded discrepancy at every prefix.
remaining: Concentration of the stopped martingale, failure-event contribution and polynomial numeric implementation remain.
Circulation comparison, iterative rounding and the final tour-cost accounting require a full audit.

papers.authors: Yuya Uezato, Yoshiki Nakamura

review.title: An Exponential Succinctness Gap between Three-Variable Logic and the Calculus of Relations
review.authors: Yuya Uezato, Yoshiki Nakamura
review.summary: An O(k)-size positive FO3 binary query requires at least 2^(k-1) relation-composition gates in any equivalent calculus-of-relations circuit, even with sharing, arbitrary Boolean operations/converse and agreement only on finite structures. No named vertices/order or vertex-dependent constants are free. Additional claims give tight 2^Theta(m/log m) fixed-single-relation circuit succinctness, FO2/tree and Boolean/tropical matrix-query bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Classical FO3-to-CoR translation is single-exponential; earlier existential-relation lower bounds did not tolerate unrestricted complement. The central lower bound is self-contained and audited; extension/upper-bound literature not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Settles necessity of an exponential compilation gap for a classical expressive equivalence.
score_reasons.novelty: Finite color folds and operation-local noticing bounds replace embedding arguments that fail under complement.
score_reasons.depth: A compact but strong circuit lower-bound method handles shared gates and all Boolean operations.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit models, color tables and distinction between noticing and propagated effects make the central proof unusually checkable.

checked: Lemma3.1 random N-color complete graph: each (u,v,w,mu,nu) failure <=exp(-(n-3)/N²); n³N² union bound <1 for n>=ceil(12N² ln(2N))+3. Two witnesses ensure one avoids the hub.
Lemma3.2 exact composition color table checked for distinct endpoints, endpoints-as-witnesses and loops; converse/Boolean operations commute with prediction, including complement.

Lemma3.5 folded hub loses color lambda. Away from hub all color pairs survive; hub row/column/diagonal change only if S_X={lambda}, S_Y={lambda} or S_X intersect S_Y={lambda}. If supports intersect these conditions coincide; if disjoint only first two remain. Thus at most2 folds per composition.

Topological induction Lemma3.4 works for DAG sharing: if no gate notices a fold, output remains its predicted value. Query G_k compares complementary colors and changes at unchanged (hub,v_{lambda^c}) for every lambda, forcing at least2^(k-1) distinct composition gates. k=1 has no self-complementary color and is covered.
DNF upper construction uses2^k compositions and O(2^k) shared intersection gates, confirming central exponential gap without an unverified structural dependency.
remaining: Fixed-vocabulary subexponential upper/lower bounds, FO2/tree refinements and Boolean/tropical matrix extensions have not been audited.
This is a compilation lower bound in the stated relational circuit model, not a general evaluation-time lower bound.

review.title: Improved Bounds for Online Matching with Random Edge Arrivals
review.authors: Yilong Feng, Haolong Li, Zonghan Yang
review.summary: For uniformly random edge arrivals of an unknown finite simple graph, a three-phase shadow-greedy algorithm is 0.5445-competitive in general graphs and 0.5535-competitive in triangle-free graphs. Upper bounds 0.6964 and 0.7043 hold for general and bipartite graphs even when the graph is known up to a random relabeling.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript compares with 1/2+epsilon in general graphs, 0.50009 in bipartite graphs and upper bounds 0.7833/0.8214; references not independently re-audited.

score_reasons.significance: A concrete substantial improvement over the half barrier in random-order matching, with improved impossibility bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: Shadow reservations coupled to a late restricted greedy phase exploit temporal conditioning; the upper bounds use exact posterior dynamic programs.
score_reasons.depth: The key three-variable coupling and positive mixture survival representation support a nontrivial factor optimization.
score_reasons.exposition: The model, phase parameters and independently computable small upper-bound instances are explicit.

checked: Traced the first-accepted-edge recurrence for survival probability and its inductive positive mixture of powers (1-t)^(n-1).

Checked conditional late XY arrival probability (1-b)/(1-s) and the stated p<=2/3 coefficient combination. Inspected the exact rational upper bounds and finite-state recurrence, without executing certificates.
remaining: Trace the full coupling inequality E[3N+2R+K]>=3k, triangle-free improvement, optimization across all mixture components and the exact finite-instance/certificate computations.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage in Local Certification of Graph Properties
papers.authors: Benjamin Jauregui, Masayuki Miyamoto

review.title: Quantum Advantage in Local Certification of Graph Properties
review.authors: Benjamin Jauregui, Masayuki Miyamoto

score_reasons.significance: First topology-only advantages, including a natural symmetry problem, significantly strengthen quantum local certification.
score_reasons.novelty: Joint rejection-weight accounting and a separate distance-independent quantum protocol overcome distinct prior losses.
score_reasons.depth: Substantial operator, spectral-gap and graph-encoding work, with adversarial entanglement explicitly handled.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear model and comparisons; a few harmless numerical slips occur in the path soundness proof.

checked: Traced Protocol 1's symmetric marginals, swap-test off-diagonal trace-norm bound, hypercube decomposition and joint rejection probability; disjoint-register accepting operators justify parallel repetition even with entangled proofs.

Checked that the one-round tree-property composition reconstructs strings only before endpoint measurements, with all earlier quantum operations independent of those strings; malformed routing/dimensions are explicitly rejected.

The constants still work after correcting two displayed intermediate values: the endpoint distance is at least 0.3857, sufficient for sum kappa >=0.19, and sqrt(u)+u/2>=0.19 yields u>=0.0305, sufficient for u>=1/35.
remaining: 64-page paper: the distance-independent protocol's spectral-gap/detectability analysis, full structural encoding and classical fooling-set lower bounds, and unrestricted symmetry construction have not been completely audited. Those headline claims remain a large-proof exception.

review.summary: Gives topology-only quantum advantages in local certification: logarithmic quantum certificates versus nearly linear classical certificates for a constructed tree property, and roughly n^(5/3) versus quadratic certificates for graph symmetry. Improves distributed equality on paths to min{r log N, N^(2/3) polylog N} qubits at every vertex.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier exponential advantages were measured in externally supplied string length. Previous path-equality cost was O(r^2 log N), and distance-independent variants still used linear certificates at relay vertices.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate with a checked central path-equality advance; broader graph-symmetry conclusions require the stated large-proof exception.

papers.title: A Counting Lemma for Somewhat Restricted 3-APs
papers.authors: Amey Bhangale, Subhash Khot, Yang P. Liu, Dor Minzer

review.title: A Counting Lemma for Somewhat Restricted 3-APs
review.authors: Amey Bhangale, Subhash Khot, Yang P. Liu, Dor Minzer
review.summary: Claims a positive-density counting lemma for 3-term progressions with differences in {0,1,2}^n, using a general arithmetic regularity theorem and Gaussian comparison. A stated Gaussian invariance step is false as written.
review.prior_frontier: Existence was known, but basis-dependent restricted patterns do not inherit the usual averaging-to-counting argument. The {0,1}^n counting problem remains open; quantitative density bounds here are at best inverse tower.

score_reasons.significance: A counting theorem for a genuinely constrained arithmetic pattern would be substantial, subject to resolving the comparison issue.
score_reasons.novelty: Develops arithmetic regularity for product-function structure and low-degree residuals.
score_reasons.depth: Rank regularization, decoupling, resilience and Gaussian reverse hypercontractivity form a substantial proof.
score_reasons.exposition: Scope and limitations are clear, but the complex invariance statement mismatches essential second moments.

checked: Read the exact counting and general no-integer-embedding statements, and inspected the resilience/regularity-to-Gaussian comparison chain.

Theorem 5.9 on PDF p30 is false as stated: take independent real Rademacher coordinates (the uniform product distribution on three binary alphabets), M=n^(-1/2) sum_i x_i, and Psi(z)=(Re z)^2. Degree is one, norm is one and maximum influence is 1/n, but E Psi(M(X))=1 whereas the prescribed proper CN(0,1) replacement has expectation 1/2, independently of n. Equivalently the holomorphic test z^2 has expectations 1 and 0.
Confirmed that Claim 5.24 and the truncation/mean comparisons on pp45-46 explicitly invoke this replacement.
remaining: A corrected Gaussian comparison matching the full real covariance (equivalently complex covariance and pseudocovariance), with the later reverse-hypercontractive argument revalidated, is required. Choosing a real orthonormal basis may provide a repair, but that repair has not been audited.
The counterexample concerns the stated invariance bridge, not the main counting theorem. The regularity and decoupling machinery has not received a complete correctness audit.
issues: PDF pp29-30 construct a proper complex Gaussian solely from E[XX*], although the discrete ensemble can have nonzero E[XX^T]. This invalidates Theorem 5.9 as stated and leaves the main proof bridge unresolved.

papers.title: The Complexity of Continuous Contract Design over Polymatroids
papers.authors: Max Klimm, Paul Lippke, Philipp Warode

review.title: The Complexity of Continuous Contract Design over Polymatroids
review.authors: Max Klimm, Paul Lippke, Philipp Warode
review.summary: Continuous effort over polymatroids: exact optimal linear contract is polynomial-time for linear costs but NP-hard for quadratic costs despite tractable unique best responses; response paths have 2^(n−O(log n)) breakpoints with polynomial-bit integer data. Homogeneous convex degree-p costs over compact convex action sets containing zero admit optimal share at most 1/p and O(1/ε) best-response approximation for fixed p.
review.prior_frontier: Extends finite-action contract complexity to continuous constrained effort; settles a stated polynomial-bit-size issue for two-parameter minimum cuts. Approximation uses best-response access; the explicit rational quadratic-polytope implementation is an FPTAS. Earlier claims not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Separates tractable agent optimization from hard principal optimization while retaining a broad positive approximation theorem.
score_reasons.novelty: Comb-shaped response paths encode Subset Sum; a homogeneous-cost scaling inequality gives a universal share bound.
score_reasons.depth: Hardness needs precise breakpoints and bit-length control; approximation relies on nonsmooth convex homogeneous comparisons.
score_reasons.exposition: Exact versus approximate and oracle versus explicit-input conclusions are carefully distinguished across the long appendix.

checked: Fully traced the homogeneous share-bound argument: convexity makes c^(1/p) convex; feasible-segment first-order comparisons bound reward growth between α and α′ by (α′/α)^(1/(p−1)); multiplying the nonincreasing normalized reward by (1−α)α^(1/(p−1)) proves the 1/p bound. Checked zero-cost edge cases and one-dimensional tight example.
Inspected exact NP membership bit-length accounting and the geometric-grid oracle approximation interface.
remaining: The two-comb hardness construction, exponential-breakpoint realization and polynomial-bit rank representation require extensive remaining verification (89 pages total).
Complete grid rounding and approximate-oracle error accounting are not audited.

review.title: Breaking the Quadratic Time Barrier for Flow Sparsifiers via Schur Complement Localization
review.authors: Gramoz Goranci, Monika Henzinger, Ali Momeni, Harald Räcke, A. R. Sricharan
review.summary: For undirected capacitated graphs with k prescribed terminals, constructs a flow sparsifier on exactly those terminals with quality O(log^(5/2) k) in randomized high-probability soft-O(m^(3/2) log U) time. Related Steiner oblivious-routing and multicut applications trade quality for faster construction.
review.prior_frontier: Prior quality O(log k/log log k) construction is cited with soft-O(k m^2) time; this improves construction time while losing quality, not simultaneous dominance.

score_reasons.significance: Breaks a central quadratic construction barrier for terminal-only flow sparsifiers and accelerates several downstream tasks.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses terminal-sensitive Schur-complement localization and entropy dissipation for forward/reverse electrical routing.
score_reasons.depth: The heat-kernel localization theorem, approximate Schur complements and width-bounded multiplicative weights interact in a technically demanding proof.
score_reasons.exposition: Quality/time tradeoffs and capacity precision are stated separately; the 77-page development is long but structured.

checked: Traced weighted congestion <=2 Lambda_reverse Lambda_forward using x_e=sqrt(p_e+1/m), p_e/x_e<=x_e and the normalized electrical projection.
Checked the width bound via row norm <=sqrt(xi), harmonic energy comparison and the multiplicative-weights logarithmic potential arithmetic.
Checked the integrated heat-kernel identity after annihilating the constant eigenspace; inspected initial pulse relative entropy log(1/mu_v).
remaining: Prove the central localization/entropy-dissipation inequalities across the long middle sections, approximate numerical embeddings and failure probabilities, and all application reductions.

review.title: Approximate Counting and the Provability of Combinatorial Principles
review.authors: Oliver Korten, Jiatu Li, Igor Oliveira, Hanlin Ren

score_reasons.significance: Clarifies the logical power of approximate counting and separates two important foundations for probabilistic complexity arguments.
score_reasons.novelty: The fresh partial-structure/priority-order game extends infinite-model obstructions to approximate counting.
score_reasons.depth: Deep interaction of bounded arithmetic, witnessing, adaptive decision trees and model-theoretic normalization.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise separation of relativized and unrelativized consequences; dense but organized proofs.

checked: Traced the fresh partial-injection adversary, adjacent priority-order swaps, collision probabilities, concentration and adaptive future-tree comparison giving mixture consistency.

Checked the Herbrand inspector's cached oracle responses, precision rounding, local-consistency mixture queries and final partial-structure witness extraction; exponential domain size dominates polynomial game parameters.
Checked the main distinction between infinite combinatorial models and arithmetic models, and the fact that no unrelativized rwPHP conclusion is claimed.
remaining: 53-page paper: full formal bounded-arithmetic encoding and Herbrand normal-form transfer, TFNP completeness/reduction details and the multiplicative counting hierarchy were not fully audited. Uses established witnessing/formalization results as primitives.

review.summary: Separates relativized additive approximate-counting theory APX1 from APC1 by unprovability of the retraction weak pigeonhole principle, and proves a Riis-style infinite-model obstruction for finite combinatorial principles. Also analyzes total-search characterizations and a multiplicative-error theory.
review.prior_frontier: APC1 has long formalized probabilistic reasoning; newer APX1 captured many arguments but whether it proves rwPHP was unresolved. The unconditional separation here is relativized, not an unrelativized independence theorem.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate; substantive core-game and inspector checks, with a large-proof exception for the remaining formalization and auxiliary hierarchy results.

papers.authors: Mohsen Ghaffari, Christoph Grunau

review.title: Faster Deterministic Distributed Matching: Breaking the Log-Squared Barrier
review.authors: Mohsen Ghaffari, Christoph Grunau
review.summary: Deterministic LOCAL matching rounding achieves roughly log^(3/2)(Delta) rounds, giving (1+epsilon) cardinality approximation, log^(6/5)(n) approximation and log^(8/5)(n) maximal matching bounds through existing frameworks.
review.prior_frontier: The local-rounding degree dependence had remained roughly log^2(Delta); previous n-dependent bounds were log^(4/3)(n) for approximation and log^(5/3)(n) for maximal matching.

score_reasons.significance: Improves a longstanding rounding bottleneck for central distributed symmetry-breaking problems.
score_reasons.novelty: Coordinates path cuts so the quadratic potential loss scales as inverse block length squared.
score_reasons.depth: Pairwise derandomization, reusable colorings, cleanup and recursive clustering turn the local gain into global bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The repeated-copy issue and unbounded-message LOCAL model are explicitly treated.

checked: Traced the actual cut-count second moment, including multiple virtual copies of one physical vertex inside a block; read the nonnegative pairwise objective used for derandomization.
Checked alternating rounding with pre-stage loads, the quadratic penalty, and the cleanup inequality deleting edges incident to load greater than one half.
Weighted matching is (2+epsilon), not (1+epsilon); bounds use LOCAL unbounded messages and polynomial dependence on inverse epsilon.
remaining: Check the external pairwise derandomization and approximation-boosting guarantees, the complete n-dependent clustering and maximal-matching recursion, and weighted extension.

papers.authors: Zhengyun Nie, Anant Shyam, Brian Bullins

review.title: Bias-Reduced and Parallel Heavy-Tailed Stochastic Convex Optimization in $\ell_p$ Geometries
review.authors: Zhengyun Nie, Anant Shyam, Brian Bullins
review.summary: For fixed 2≤p<∞ and unbiased gradients with bounded q-th moment, q=p/(p−1), gives parallel ℓp stochastic optimization depth soft-O(d^(p/(2p+2)) ε^(−p/(p+1))) and generalized-Gaussian bias-reduction tools. Dimension-dependent local-oracle lower bound soft-Ω(min{ε^(−p),d^(p/(3p−2))}) is for a subset of the unit ℓp ball.
review.prior_frontier: Extends Euclidean variance-bounded bias reduction and parallel smoothing to heavy-tailed dual moments and non-Euclidean geometry; improves sequential ε^(−p) depth only in the stated small-ε regime. Upper and lower bounds are not matching. Prior comparisons not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial extension of parallel stochastic optimization beyond bounded-variance Euclidean geometry.
score_reasons.novelty: Generalized-Gaussian reweighting and ℓp optimal-distance convergence couple with multilevel estimation and ball-oracle acceleration.
score_reasons.depth: Ninety-five pages of moment, proximal, acceleration and random-wall lower-bound arguments support the broad theorem package.
score_reasons.exposition: The separate query/computational depths are supplied, but notation and several long layered proofs demand careful tracking.

checked: Traced unbiased generalized-Gaussian reweighting by change of measure. Verified the q-moment bound: (p−1)-smoothness of half the squared ℓp norm yields a translated Gaussian integral times exp(p||v||²/(2(p−1)ρ²))≤e<3 for ||v||≤ρ.
Checked the announced small-ε improvement threshold and distinguished bounded q-th moment from bounded variance.
remaining: Full ODCp/multilevel bias analysis, accelerated solvers, all computational-depth counts and local-oracle lower bound remain unchecked.
Higher-moment lemma uses an additional score-function subgaussian fact whose proof/dependency remains to be checked.

review.title: Fine-Grained Complexity of Approximating Vector Knapsack: A Faster Algorithm and Equivalence with $k$-SUM in 2D
review.authors: Karl Bringmann, Ariel Kulik, Karol Węgrzycki
review.summary: In the real-RAM model, gives a (1-epsilon)-approximation for fixed d-dimensional vector knapsack in n^((d-1)/(2epsilon)+O(d)) time up to parameter/polylog factors, a near-linear (2/3-delta)-approximation in 2D, and fine-grained equivalences with exact real kSUM with k tied to 1/epsilon.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the cited n^(ceil(d/epsilon)-d) PTAS exponent. The conditional matching exponent depends on the appropriate kSUM hypothesis; recent special integer kSUM algorithms are not ignored.

score_reasons.significance: Nearly halves the leading PTAS exponent and identifies the exact fine-grained source of difficulty for 2D knapsack.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines profit-ordered meet-in-the-middle with capacity-independent low-profit representatives and bidirectional kSUM reductions.
score_reasons.depth: Preserving exact feasibility in every coordinate while rounding representative profits/weights and controlling disjointness requires several interlocking arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: Parameterized exponents, real-number assumptions and conditionality are unusually explicit.

checked: Verified the kSUM-to-2D construction with weights 1 +/- a/M: feasible k items exactly encode zero sum, and (1-epsilon)k>k-1 forces the decision.
Traced the d-1-constraint extreme-point slack lemma and its loss of at most d-1 maximum-profit items.
Checked representative-solution feasibility using (1+epsilon_prime)(1-epsilon_prime)<=1, maximal-coordinate guesses, exact preservation of the last coordinate, and the empty-set low-profit case.
Inspected the index-separated range-search meet-in-the-middle construction.
remaining: Audit the near-linear convolution approximation lemma, full exponent rounding, reverse reduction to kSUM, and the 2/3 approximation.
