papers.title: Beyond least-favorable distribution pairs: asymptotically instance-optimal robust hypothesis testing
papers.authors: Aytijhya Saha, Aaditya Ramdas

review.title: Beyond least-favorable distribution pairs: asymptotically instance-optimal robust hypothesis testing
review.authors: Aytijhya Saha, Aaditya Ramdas

score_reasons.significance: Useful instance-optimal refinement of a classical robust-testing problem, with both asymptotic regimes addressed.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines explicit clipping, FTRL regret and retained dyadic betting accounts; ingredients are recognizable but the synthesis is effective.
score_reasons.depth: Careful finite-alphabet concentration and boundary geometry rather than a new general testing framework.
score_reasons.exposition: Exceptionally clear qualifications on full support, fixed null geometry, regret, expected stopping time and asymptotic regimes.

checked: Checked threshold roots and reverse-projection optimality, null-valid clipped likelihood factors, including the boundary empirical-distribution extension.
Traced the two likelihood maximization telescopes and Laplace multinomial identity proving pathwise regret; checked expected regret and almost-sure growth separately.
Checked stopped likelihood-ratio information lower bound, localized bounded-increment concentration and summable tail control giving expected Wald optimality.
Checked TV-to-KL comparison including zero coordinates, independent pilot/betting-block concentration, retained-capital mixture, dyadic stopping-time tail sum and combination of the two regimes.
remaining: The O(log d) dynamic balanced-tree implementation and optional oracle-mixture appendix were not fully checked. Central statistical guarantees above use the explicit oracle and are independent of that implementation claim; Farrell lower-bound literature is used as the stated standard benchmark.

review.summary: Constructs an efficient sequential test for a total-variation ball around a fixed discrete distribution, achieving the exact instance-specific Wald stopping constant and optimal Farrell order via a mixture of clipped-Kelly and dyadic pilot-and-bet processes.
review.prior_frontier: Least-favorable-pair tests optimize worst-case alternatives. This learns the actual alternative, replacing the worst-case information number by its reverse-projection KL distance; Farrell optimality is order-wise uniformly, not a sharp constant or pointwise lower bound.
review.recommendation: Sound and well-exposed candidate; central statistical theorem audited, with a narrower impact than the leading broad breakthroughs.

papers.title: The Hyperclique Hypothesis is False
papers.authors: Nick Fischer

review.title: The Hyperclique Hypothesis is False
review.authors: Nick Fischer
review.summary: An explicit signed recursive algorithm counts k-cliques in h-uniform hypergraphs in n^((1-epsilon_h)k) time for fixed k>h, refuting the stated Hyperclique Hypothesis. The elementary 3-uniform 4-clique bound is n^3.99999.
review.prior_frontier: Exhaustive-search exponent k had not been beaten for h>=3; tensor-rank and fixed tensor-network-order lower bounds blocked standard algebraic approaches.

score_reasons.significance: Refutes a widely used fine-grained hardness hypothesis with a genuine fixed positive exponent saving.
score_reasons.novelty: Mixes evaluation orders across a signed decomposition instead of requiring one contraction order for all terms.
score_reasons.depth: A simple swap identity is combined with matrix-valued recursion, three-way inductive base algorithms and a contracting potential.
score_reasons.exposition: The core proof is compact, explicit and does not depend on the claimed recent matrix-multiplication breakthroughs.

checked: Traced the swap identity and block-matrix realization of both main and correction terms, including the additional three-index factors for general uniformity. Independently reconstructed the alternate x1/x4 reduction: move the shared digit into beta and duplicate the gamma index in corrections, so extra factors retain their required variable omissions.
Checked both 3-uniform base algorithms and their weighted-geometric-mean bound using only Strassen exponent <2.81. Checked the general h induction and all three lower-uniformity factor omissions.
Verified the potential multiplier rho=q^(-delta)+(1-1/q)2^(-delta), leaf dimensions, q choice and positive exponent saving; logarithmic internal-node overhead is absorbed in the advertised exponent.

Checked integer magnitudes: recursive entries are only copied/negated, and fixed-uniformity base computations use polynomially bounded integers. For k not divisible by h+1, brute-forcing the remainder still yields a uniform positive fractional saving after shrinking the constant.
remaining: Not formal verification or an implementation benchmark. Standard Strassen multiplication is the only nontrivial algorithmic input needed by the core proof. The optimized n^3.9583 remark and all listed downstream reductions (including k-AP and Max-CSP consequences) were not independently audited.

papers.title: Half-Optimal Induced Matchings in Random Graphs: Online and Low-Degree Algorithms
papers.authors: Abhishek Dhawan, Eren C. Kızıldağ, Neeladri Maitra, Cheng Mao, Timothy L. H. Wee

review.title: Half-Optimal Induced Matchings in Random Graphs: Online and Low-Degree Algorithms
review.authors: Abhishek Dhawan, Eren C. Kızıldağ, Neeladri Maitra, Cheng Mao, Timothy L. H. Wee
review.summary: In G(n,p), C/n≤p≤1−κ, greedy finds an induced matching of (1/2−ε)log_(1/(1−p))(np) edges; no irreversible vertex-exposure online algorithm, even with adaptive inspection and unlimited computation, exceeds (1/2+ε) times this scale except exponentially rarely. A parallel low-degree threshold is claimed in the sparse fixed-d regime.
review.prior_frontier: Makes the familiar half-optimum average-case barrier precise for induced matching, with a maximality principle and simpler online proof. The online model forbids revoking accepted edges and only accepts an edge incident to the just-exposed vertex; this is not unrestricted polynomial-time hardness.

score_reasons.significance: Establishes a sharp threshold across two important algorithmic models for an average-case combinatorial problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Maximality yields achievability and a one-instance stopping-time first moment replaces correlated-instance OGP for online hardness.
score_reasons.depth: The low-degree endpoint-overlap analysis is substantial; the online core is notably concise.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise exposure and acceptance rules make the barrier interpretable and the probability arithmetic is laid out.

checked: Traced the full online threshold proof. For a fixed k-edge matching, residual vertices avoiding its 2k endpoints are binomial with mean at least (np)^(2ε)/(2p); maximality forces their induced graph empty. Chernoff and counting dominate all matchings when C is sufficiently large.

At the first r=(1/2+ε/2)L accepted edges, each later accepted edge has a fresh endpoint. s=εL/2 such endpoints must be independent and avoid the existing 2r endpoints; conditional independence survives adaptive exposure. The union bound binom(n,s)(1−p)^(2rs+binom(s,2)) is at most exp(−ε²L log(np)/2), checking n/L≤np and the large-C arithmetic.
Checked irreversibility and one-new-edge-per-round are exactly the needed model restrictions.
remaining: The separate low-degree achievability and hardness results and the external information-theoretic optimum estimate remain unchecked; this status covers the central online theorem pair only.

sources.detail: Every maximal induced matching is large

papers.authors: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu

review.title: An FPRAS for Mixed Volumes
review.authors: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu

score_reasons.significance: A general mixed-volume FPRAS would settle a longstanding computational frontier and refute Gurvits's hardness conjecture.
score_reasons.novelty: The common-sum softening and balancing capacity bridge the gap between well-rounded and arbitrarily ill-conditioned bodies.
score_reasons.depth: Substantial convex geometry, elliptic spectral theory, randomized oracle implementation and finite-precision optimization.
score_reasons.exposition: Excellent motivated exposition and unusually explicit input/oracle and numerical-precision conventions.

checked: Traced the spherical Poincare derivation from the stated Alexandrov–Fenchel operator spectrum, including the vanishing self-adjoint second term and normalized PSD matrix bound.
Checked moving-tangent-basis differentiation and mixed-discriminant logarithmic gradient bound; checked the telescoping ratio estimator retaining three ball slots and bounded final test function.

Checked the 2-balancing factors conditional on the cited reverse mixed-volume inequality, differential inequality f'<=f^2 controlling softening, compact convex capacity comparison and covariance Hessian bound n^2 I.

checked: Traced restricted certification: a covering ball of radius>R already costs at least one third of any certified radius≤3R; otherwise the radius-R LP is a valid lower bound. This preserves the comparison despite a 3R-radius integral reference solution.

Traced the central bipoint rounding recursion: component-choice LP has at most one fractional component, so error is paid only on one recursive branch. If no cheap local replacement exists, weighted local sparsity bounds weight inside radius 2D while connectivity supplies weight inside D.

Verified D=εw/3, expected at most 6/ε cut balls, augmentation to ≤12/ε balls and covering cost ≤24R/ε; each remaining component has weight at most (1−ε/6)w. The 144R/ε² logarithmic potential drops enough to pay the boundary, and log+(uv)≤u+log+v yields additive O(R/ε³).
remaining: Full Lagrangian hierarchical DP, expected duplication control, bounded state count and high-probability amplification remain unchecked in this 43-page paper.

checked: Read the full new proof: detailed-balance integration by parts, the discrete derivative/conditional-generator commutator, and the nonnegative conditional Dirichlet-form term.
Verified that the remaining quadratic form is exactly the assumed local matrix, yielding ||Lf||^2>=delta <f,-Lf>. Symmetry follows from reversibility and the product of two insertion rates.

Checked the hard-core substitution and eigenvalue interlacing. Dead coordinates can be omitted; commutator expressions outside valid insertions occur only with zero rate. The mixing corollary uses the usual positive-denominator activity regime.
remaining: Not machine checked. The random-regular smallest-eigenvalue theorem and historical follow-up claims were not independently audited. This proves a spectral gap, not the stronger log-Sobolev statement from the earlier work.

review.title: Top-Down Lower Bounds for All Depths
review.authors: Oliver Korten
review.summary: Gives completely top-down communication-adversary proofs that depth-d De Morgan circuits for parity need exp(ε_d n^(1/(d−1))) wires for every fixed d≥2. Central new light-pattern estimate uses harmonic-mean coefficients of random projections of high-min-entropy distributions.
review.prior_frontier: Reproduces the classical essentially tight parity bound by a method previously established only through depth four; does not prove a new P-versus-NC¹ or PH communication lower bound. Exact historical frontier not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Completes a decades-long program connecting top-down communication reasoning to all-depth nonmonotone circuit lower bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: Harmonic-mean tensorization detects very light projection patterns without controlling heavy patterns, enabling linear rather than quadratic entropy loss in the sampling parameter.
score_reasons.depth: Combines a new analytic inequality with guided random walks, entropy conditioning and a round-by-round rectangle adversary.
score_reasons.exposition: The progression from weaker proofs to the tight exponent makes the key obstruction and its remedy unusually transparent.

checked: Traced the improved light-pattern lemma completely: variational harmonic mean gives concavity/coordinate monotonicity; the two-point inequality reduces to (c−d)²/(2c)≥0 and tensorizes. Bounded density gives E√H≥2^(−k/2); downward-closed transfer at r≤1/(512k) bounds bad probability by 5r(k/2+1)≤1/64.
Checked the transfer directly by taking floor(1/(4r)) independent r-random sets, whose union density is at most 1/4 and whose count is at least 1/(5r) for r≤1/20.

Traced guided mirror construction, entropy conditioning and the adversary. Substituting the stronger light-pattern lemma requires replacing the earlier 65k constant by a larger absolute multiple: conditional deficit≤64k and mass loss≤128k+2 give at most 194k, so 200k suffices. With k_i=O_d(m), p_i grows by O(k_i) per reflection and no first-round reflection is needed; p_d=O_d(m^(d−1)/n) gives the claimed exponent.
Verified final positive-density limit condition rules out a fixed output coordinate, and the KW correspondence turns communication cost into wire count.
remaining: The separate Fourier-based intermediate light-pattern proof in Section 3 was not fully audited; the tight theorem uses the independently checked Section 4 harmonic-mean route.
This is a mathematical proof trace, not formal verification; constants ε_d are depth-dependent as stated.

review.summary: Edge Clique Cover parameterized k below Lovász’s nonedge bound, and Edge Clique Partition parameterized k below floor(n²/4), admit O(k)-vertex, O(k log k)-bit kernels. review.prior_frontier: Adds above-guarantee-style constructive refinements to classical clique bounds using fine stability; these are not kernels parameterized by the absolute clique-cover optimum. Prior parameterized comparisons not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Strong compact kernels at natural classical extremal baselines, including compressed bit size for dense outputs.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses quantitative stability to obtain O(k) edit modulators to complete multipartite/bipartite graphs.
score_reasons.depth: Kernel rules interact with clique decompositions, cluster editing and sparse exceptional structures.
score_reasons.exposition: The randomized-equivalence guarantee and why linear vertices alone do not imply linear bit size are explicitly explained.

checked: Inspected exact kernel and stability statements; distinguished nonedge count in Lovász’s bound from edge count in runtime notation.

Traced first two safe cluster-editing reductions: isolating a vertex removes its distance-two pairs without creating new ones; when the common-neighbor fraction is below 1/9, neighborhood arithmetic gives deletion-to-eliminated-pair ratio below three in both degree cases.
remaining: Remaining reduction rules, 22k stability bound, kernel equivalence and linear-time randomized implementation remain unchecked across the 66-page manuscript.

sources.detail: Stability theorem and distance-two auxiliary lemma

papers.title: Robust Shattering Arguments
papers.authors: Peter Davies-Peck, Mohsen Ghaffari, Magnús M. Halldórsson, Yannic Maus, Alexandre Nolin

review.title: Robust Shattering Arguments
review.authors: Peter Davies-Peck, Mohsen Ghaffari, Magnús M. Halldórsson, Yannic Maus, Alexandre Nolin
review.summary: Identifies failures of independence and weak-adversarial-conditioning justifications in distributed graph shattering. Provides local supermartingale cost conditions implying product survival bounds and small components, with corrected analyses for distributed LLL, coloring, MIS and maximal matching algorithms.
review.prior_frontier: Repairs proof foundations rather than claiming a new asymptotic speedup for every application. Bounded-radius final events remain independent; superconstant-duration local procedures need the stronger history-conditioned stepwise condition.

score_reasons.significance: Repairs a foundational argument used in multiple leading distributed symmetry-breaking algorithms.
score_reasons.novelty: A product of local stepwise supermartingales handles globally correlated execution histories without assuming independent survival events.
score_reasons.depth: The generic probability argument is concise, while extracting suitable cost functions for adaptive LLL and symmetry-breaking processes is substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit counterexamples distinguish false lemmas from misapplied valid ones and make the replacement hypotheses testable.

checked: Verified the global modular-sum counterexample: every vertex survives with Delta^(-3c) even after fixing all others, but the entire connected graph survives with that probability.
Traced the product supermartingale conditioned on the full prior history, disjoint fresh neighborhoods, terminal Markov inequality and arbitrary-time joint bound.
Checked connected-set counting and the separate degree-2 path/cycle treatment; greedily extracted independent connected witnesses from large residual components.
Verified dependent-opportunity potentials, including p=1, and exp(p/2)[1-p+p/e]<=1; cumulative opportunity is needed only on surviving executions.
remaining: The 56-page manuscript applies the framework separately to adaptive-sampling LLL, coloring, MIS and matching. These application-specific opportunity/risk certificates and network-decomposition appendix have not yet been fully traced; no blanket correctness claim for those repaired algorithms.

review.title: Randomized query complexity can beat certificate complexity
review.authors: Shalev Ben-David, Robin Kothari

score_reasons.significance: Closes a fundamental query-complexity gap with nearly optimal simultaneous separations.
score_reasons.novelty: A succinct champion/proposal-card construction makes a difficult separation transparent.
score_reasons.depth: Proof is elementary once the function is found; efficient quantum tournament search is a cited primitive.
score_reasons.exposition: Outstanding six-page exposition with explicit malformed-input behavior and cumulative certificates.

checked: Read the complete new proof: unique champion, O(n log n) unambiguous certificate and constant-probability random candidate capture followed by deterministic elimination.
Checked the zero-input certificate lower bound at bit granularity: an untouched proposal card and fewer than n touched bits in its country's races permit a consistent champion completion.
Checked the virtual candidate tournament, duplicate-ID tie breaking and sink/king reduction; reversing tournament orientation reconciles the source's outward-king convention.

Checked all three quantum verification stages, especially binary search in cumulative proposal counts to access the fewer than n claimed non-athlete positions. Verified the published primary source provides a roughly sqrt(n) quantum king-finding algorithm.
remaining: Does not reprove the established Grover-search or quantum king-finding primitives. Ordinary bounded-error amplification and invalid-label rejection are implementation conventions, not new mathematical ingredients.

sources.detail: Primary published source verified for the roughly sqrt(n) quantum king-finding bound.

review.summary: Constructs a total Boolean function on roughly n^3 bits with certificate complexity Omega(n^2), randomized query complexity roughly n and quantum query complexity roughly sqrt(n), resolving whether randomization can substantially beat certificates.
review.prior_frontier: The R versus C separation was a longstanding open question; the achieved quadratic separation and simultaneous quartic Q versus C separation are optimal up to logarithms under general total-function inequalities. Independent concurrent work also obtained the quantum separation.
review.recommendation: Very strong candidate; the short central proof has been checked in full.

review.title: Fast mixing of the SYK model at high temperatures
review.authors: Yiyi Cai, Yongtao Zhan, Alexander Zlokapa
review.summary: For the quartic SYK model with Gaussian coupling scale J, proves a constant spectral gap for a specified Gaussian-filtered KMS Gibbs sampler when βJ≤1/1000, with probability at least 1−2 exp(−N); gives trace-norm mixing O(N+log(1/ε)) and polynomial-time Gibbs preparation through an existing implementation theorem. This concerns an engineered Lindbladian at high temperature, not arbitrary thermal dynamics or low-temperature SYK.
review.prior_frontier: Previous SYK thermal statements did not supply this global trace-norm rapid-mixing guarantee; bounds based on sums of absolute interaction strengths deteriorate for dense SYK.

score_reasons.significance: Global rapid mixing for a prominent dense random quantum model is consequential.
score_reasons.novelty: Exploits cancellation via Clifford-valued Jacobian estimates rather than absolute interaction bounds.
score_reasons.depth: Combines a noncommutative Bochner comparison, Gaussian filtering and high-moment coefficient estimates.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit temperature/disorder regime and a useful proof organization, with substantial technical dependencies.

checked: Read the filtered/unfiltered commutator comparison: a real-time Gronwall bound controls the Gaussian filter error by less than 1/14 and preserves the kernel.

Inspected the Jacobian-to-mixed-anticommutator reduction and the disorder word-coefficient moment comparison in Lemma 12, including the finite-degree moment restriction and the high-degree Hamiltonian norm tail.
remaining: Full Clifford Bochner identity, classical Jacobian Lemma 10 and Appendix A, and all constants in the simultaneous high-probability event remain to be checked.
The external Gibbs-sampler implementation and its complexity dependencies have not been independently checked.

papers.title: Robust Forecast Aggregation via Additional Queries
papers.authors: Mary Monroe, Bo Waggoner, Rafael Frongillo, Eric Neyman

review.title: Robust Forecast Aggregation via Additional Queries
review.authors: Rafael Frongillo, Mary Monroe, Eric Neyman, Bo Waggoner
review.summary: For independent mean-zero signals indexed by the subsets of experts observing them, DAG-elicitable higher-order queries exactly aggregate the signal sum with n queries. With at most d queries the minimax normalized error is 1−d/n; restrictions on order/agent complexity yield different polynomial-approximation tradeoffs, with vanishing upper bounds once d≫√n.
review.prior_frontier: Escapes impossibility for ordinary posterior-mean forecasts by changing the query interface. Exact aggregation and tradeoffs use the partial-information signal model, not arbitrary correlated information structures. Large-d exponential error is an upper bound, not a proved matching characterization.

score_reasons.significance: A substantive information-design improvement under a broad but specific independent overlapping-signal model.
score_reasons.novelty: Structured difference queries isolate each signal at its earliest observing expert, while intersection queries connect complexity to polynomial approximation.
score_reasons.depth: Requires strategic elicitation, minimax lower bounds and discrete approximation theory beyond the simple exact reconstruction.
score_reasons.exposition: Three complexity measures and the signal model are explicit, though the informal large-d characterization needs the later qualification.

checked: Traced difference-query induction: subtracting earlier conditional expectations removes each overlapping signal exactly once, indexed by its first observing expert; summing n queries reconstructs Y.
Checked intersection-query quadratic scoring recursively conditions on an observing expert and uses a DAG whose depth and relevant-agent count are at most d.
Inspected singleton-signal lower-bound instance for d-query error and the distinction between query-count and order-complexity guarantees.
remaining: Full DAG incentive compatibility, minimax quantifier handling, optimal d-query upper bound and polynomial approximation tradeoffs remain unchecked.

sources.detail: Large-d bounds explicitly only upper bounds

review.summary: Proves NP-hardness of distinguishing 2-colorable simple 3-uniform hypergraphs on N vertices from chromatic number greater than c sqrt(log log N / log log log N), for an absolute c>0, using polynomial-time reductions.
review.prior_frontier: The cited Dinur–Regev–Smyth result gives each constant under P!=NP; stronger polylogarithmic color hardness elsewhere uses a quasipolynomial-time complexity assumption. This is a different, unconditional NP-hardness quantitative frontier.

score_reasons.significance: Crosses from every fixed constant to a superconstant number of colors under ordinary polynomial-reduction NP-hardness.
score_reasons.novelty: Derandomizes the polymorphism selector domain using small Schrijver cores closed under the necessary inverse projections, alongside a growing-layer outer verifier.
score_reasons.depth: The local avoiding-set structure, domain-size accounting and low-error layered PCP parameters must simultaneously remain polynomial.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly separates NP-hardness from stronger-assumption bounds and explicitly tracks the reduction size.

checked: Traced local core enumeration and the Schrijver-based avoiding-set induction, conditional on the stated product chromatic lemma.
Checked pullback closure along bounded-depth projection paths and the repeated-variable conversion using clusters of 2C+1 vertices.
Verified C=gamma sqrt(log log n/log log log n) makes exp(O(C^2 log C)) at most log n for small gamma and gives polynomial output size.
remaining: Trace the low-error multilayer Label Cover construction, selector consistency and decoding, and verify quantitative hypotheses of the cited PCP and product-graph theorems.

review.title: On the Power of Determinism in Multi-Item Auctions
review.authors: Yiannis Giannakopoulos, Johannes Hahn

score_reasons.significance: More than halves a longstanding simple-auction factor and closes a separate exact two-item frontier.
score_reasons.novelty: Joint max of Myerson revenue and capped expectation, with subtraction of the largest excess, sharpens core-tail duality.
score_reasons.depth: Extensive dual-certificate construction, tail analysis and discretization/limit arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: Good overview and explicit benchmark distinctions, though the exact constants depend on lengthy technical appendices.

checked: Traced the master inequality's rectangular and circular dual flows, payment/allocation cancellation including boundaries, nonnegative multipliers and weak-dual objective.
Checked the price-above/below-cap comparison and largest-excess routing that yield the max{single revenue,capped mean} plus residual-excess bound.

papers.authors: David Naori, Haim Kaplan

review.title: Tight Bounds for k-Median++ and Improved Bounds for k-Means++
review.authors: Haim Kaplan, David Naori
review.summary: Analyzes standard D-sampling and oversampling against the optimal k-clustering cost. Obtains the exact metric k-median++ factor 2B(k,Δ), where B is a coupon-process recurrence, and improves Euclidean k-means++ to (1+φ)B(k,Δ). Euclidean k-median tightness is established for Δ=0; for positive oversampling its stated lower and upper constants differ. The Euclidean k-means constant is not claimed tight.
review.prior_frontier: The Euclidean k-means++ coefficient improves from 5 to 1+φ≈2.618; general-metric squared-distance coefficient improves from 16 to approximately 4.383. For Δ=0, B=1+H(k−1); oversampling has a more precise finite-parameter analysis.

score_reasons.significance: Sharper guarantees for widely used clustering seeding, including an exact metric result.
score_reasons.novelty: A balanced-cluster proxy and equal-mass coupon process unify constants and oversampling.
score_reasons.depth: The two-variable potential must account for past and future misses and permit adaptive cluster costs.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes metric/Euclidean and median/means cases and provides exact recurrences.

checked: Traced the balanced-process potential and its endpoint induction: choosing Γ=Δ cancels the sign-indefinite terms, leaving a nonpositive squared difference.
Read the coupling in Lemma 4.7 that maintains a difference of at most one removable item and establishes monotonicity of the past-miss payment probability.
remaining: The rest of Lemma 4.7, the cluster-balancing inequalities yielding the golden-ratio constant, and the matching lower-bound constructions need full checking.
The Lambert-W approximation and its error, and Euclidean oversampling lower bounds, have not been audited.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Strong Roberson Conjecture
papers.authors: Arnar Kristjánsson

review.title: Counterexamples to the Strong Roberson Conjecture
review.authors: Arnar Á. Kristjánsson
review.summary: Refutes the Strong Roberson Conjecture and its weak-immersion analogue: explicit connected graphs H have hom(H,·) determined by counts from graphs excluding H as a minor or immersion. A concrete minor witness is the 91-vertex circulant with jumps 1 and 5; its 182-vertex cubic bipartite split handles immersion. Failure occurs even for a minor-closed source class of pathwidth at most ten.
review.prior_frontier: Goes beyond earlier counterexamples to the CFI/oddomorphism proof route by refuting the actual homomorphism-distinguishing-closure conjecture. Does not refute the weak conjecture about distinguishing all nonisomorphic targets. Prior historical claims not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Explicitly settles two structural conjectures and changes the relationship between graph containment and homomorphism-count information.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses infinitely many modular orbit-quotient equivalences to obtain exact count dependence, plus rigid Hamilton-cycle minor models.
score_reasons.depth: Robust treewidth bounds force every minor branch set to be a cycle interval, allowing an arithmetic averaging obstruction.
score_reasons.exposition: The modular reduction, geometric obstruction and arithmetic contradiction are clearly separated and proved concretely.

checked: Traced the complete central proof: prime-order precomposition orbits give hom(F_p,X)=hom(H,X) mod p, and equality of all source counts forces a fixed integer difference divisible by infinitely many primes. CRT supplies infinitely many primes not ±1 modulo r.

Checked sliding-window pathwidth upper bounds and the robust lower bound tw(D_n−shortedge)=2r: two clean r-blocks have 2r internally disjoint long-edge routes; deleting fewer than 2r vertices leaves their component larger than n/2, contradicting a width-(2r−1) centroid separator with small external neighborhood. Cubic bounds follow explicit alternating bags and spoke contraction.

Traced model rigidity: block-deletion widths force every host vertex into a branch set; long Hamilton edges crossing labels must uniquely represent base Hamilton edges, yielding a closed nonrepeating walk around the base cycle and interval branch sets.

Verified arc-length averaging gives (d_r(N)+1)q≤(d_r(q)+1)N, and the analogous cubic inequality. For q=kr+1 and m not ±1 modulo r, the inverse coefficient lies between 2 and r−2, violating both inequalities. Cubic weak immersions are topological minors by degree counting.
Checked q=91,r=5 satisfies the strict q>4r²−2r condition and the pathwidth-ten refinement uses the same source witnesses.
remaining: Optional discussion of more general shift lifts was not audited. External historical attribution is not part of this correctness check; the central proof uses elementary facts reproduced in the manuscript.

review.title: Search and Verification for Strategyproof Facility Location on Metric Graphs
review.authors: Krzysztof Rogowski, Marcin Dziubiński
review.summary: For randomized facility location on continuous metric graphs, gives finite piecewise-linear attribution representations whose SP and approximation properties reduce to exact quadratic nonnegativity tests, and finite-domain LP-dual lower bounds for unrestricted SP mechanisms. Strong SP has finite linear constraints within fixed representation classes. Reports certified three-agent cycle ratio interval [1.0591,1.10747] and equal-path theta interval [1.0782,1.2028].
review.prior_frontier: Extends finite-domain automated mechanism design and previous circle bounds to continuous graphs with explicit verification. The finer 1.072288 cycle result is numerical, not presented here as a certified global bound.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a concrete verification/search framework and new certified gaps for a specialist mechanism-design problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Report-dependent affine mixtures and the stronger shortest-path incentive notion enable finite optimization and checking.
score_reasons.depth: The global quadratic reduction and unrestricted finite lower-bound reduction require care, though the quadratic oracle is standard exact finite optimization.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper distinguishes heuristic search, sampled objectives and exact certification, with explicit assumptions on arithmetic.

checked: Verified the finite benchmark proof: move toward a direction used by at least half the shortest report paths until a report/branch vertex, never increasing total distance.

Traced the exact quadratic simplex oracle including singular stationarity matrices: a null direction preserves objective and mass, reaches a smaller support, and yields a nonsingular minimal-support minimizer.
Checked barycentric homogenization of linear/constant terms and the exponential enumeration complexity, not a polynomial-time claim.
remaining: Audit the unrestricted continuous-to-finite cost-preserving reduction, SSP characterization and deterministic onto expressiveness; execute or inspect the actual certificates underlying numerical intervals.

checked: Checked the switching double count with the indispensable donor/inverse-multiplicity ratio, and the interior-inventory margin needed to bound log-weight changes.

review.title: Agnostic Product Mixed State Tomography via Robust Statistics
review.authors: Alvan Arulandu, Ilias Diakonikolas, Daniel Kane, Jerry Li
review.summary: Gives polynomial-time, polynomial-copy semi-agnostic tomography of an arbitrary n-qubit state by a product mixed state with trace error O(opt log(1/opt))+ε, using adaptive single-copy single-qubit measurements. The reduction also yields improved robust learning of binary product distributions. A pure-product corollary is nonadaptive but has the weaker O(sqrt(opt log(1/opt)))+ε error. Statistical-query lower bounds are model-specific.
review.prior_frontier: Improves robust binary-product estimation and approaches the stated SQ/QSQ lower bound up to a log-log factor; the information-theoretic O(opt) benchmark is distinct from the SQ computational guarantee.

score_reasons.significance: Connects a substantial quantum learning problem with a robust-statistical advance.
score_reasons.novelty: Learns local eigenbases from robust Pauli means and then a classical product density, with a tailored geometric filtering norm.
score_reasons.depth: Requires covariance control in a mean-dependent norm, robust filtering, and separate quantum lower bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The measurement and approximation regimes are explicit, though the technical development is long.

checked: Traced the tomography reduction: three Pauli settings give approximate local Bloch vectors; the qubit fidelity bound controls total off-diagonal error, and a second adaptive measurement learns the diagonal product distribution.
Read Lemma 4.14: good/bad weighted mean decomposition, Cauchy–Schwarz amplification of bad mass, diagonal subtraction, and absorption of linear terms give the off-diagonal covariance witness.
remaining: The goodness conditions and mean-dependent norm comparisons used in Lemma 4.14, the complete filtering algorithm and sample bounds need checking.
SQ/QSQ and nonadaptive-measurement lower bounds, and the pure-state rounding analysis, are not fully audited.

papers.authors: Anna Brandenberger, Ilan Doron-Arad, Elchanan Mossel

review.title: Genetic Algorithms with Optimization Guided Operators
review.authors: Anna Brandenberger, Ilan Doron-Arad, Elchanan Mossel
review.summary: Introduces a generation–mutation–recombination oracle model. For its parity-learning instance, exact target generation with live pool size w requires and suffices Θ(w+2^(n−w)) queries; broader compressed-memory hardness relies on streaming parity lower bounds. Separate examples establish operator necessity and Gaussian drift speedups.
review.prior_frontier: A formal model of guided operators, not a general guarantee for actual language-model optimization. The policy cannot submit arbitrary candidates, and all persistent information in the live-pool theorem must reside in retained queried candidates.

score_reasons.significance: A precise memory/diversity tradeoff for a useful abstract search model, with more limited practical implications than the motivation.
score_reasons.novelty: Separates cost of generating a target from knowing it, using nondegenerate stored subspaces and cheap screening before XOR synthesis.
score_reasons.depth: The central tradeoff has an elegant span-entry lower bound and a carefully memory-budgeted matching policy.
score_reasons.exposition: Feedback and retained-state restrictions are stated explicitly and the upper-bound phases are explained.

checked: Traced both directions of Theorem 3. Conditioning on x and prior generations fixes current span S; each fresh uniform generation enters x+S with probability ≤2^(min(w,j−1)−n). Summing gives both Ω(w) and Ω(2^(n−w)).

For achievability checked construction of a nondegenerate w−O(1) dimensional subspace, using an anisotropic vector or a hyperbolic pair; its equations determine q with x+q in S-perp. A fresh projected seed matches the unknown residual with probability at least 2^(−(n−w+5)).

Verified geometric screening accepts a wrong candidate with probability at most η/4 and costs fewer than two tests in expectation, while a correct candidate is eventually accepted after O(1/η) tests. Only O(1) candidates need O(w) XOR synthesis. Ordered zero markers fit within w retained candidates, and Markov truncation gives success ≥2/3.
remaining: General compressed-memory lower bound depends on Raz’s streaming theorem, not independently checked here; operator-necessity and Gaussian phase-transition results remain unaudited. Status covers the central live-pool tradeoff.

Traced the direct-product proof on pp. 5–7: overlap truncation, fixed-set conditioning probability, relative-entropy subadditivity, Pinsker and hardwiring. This yields the stated epsilon-cubed dependence conditional on the cited fixed-set lemma.
remaining: The separate DNF/forest separation, exact symmetric sampling and cell-probe applications were screened but their full proofs were not audited. The cited fixed-set and hypercontractive lemmas were used as external results, not independently reproved.

review.summary: Separates polynomial-size DNF samplers from polynomial-depth decision forests, proves a sampling direct-product theorem, and reduces AC0 sampler randomness to support entropy plus a constant.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier forest separations concerned logarithmic depth or distributions outside AC0; previous AC0 randomness reductions used quaslinear rather than near-minimum input length, with different explicitness guarantees.
review.recommendation: Competitive candidate based on the audited randomness-reduction and direct-product results; separate applications have narrower verification coverage.

papers.title: Mortality Is Undecidable for 2 × 2 Integer Matrices
papers.authors: Thanin Quartz, Ivan O. Shevchenko, Hans De Sterck, Jun Liu

review.title: Mortality Is Undecidable for 2 × 2 Integer Matrices
review.authors: Thanin Quartz, Ivan O. Shevchenko, Hans De Sterck, Jun Liu
review.summary: Claims undecidability of mortality for 2×2 integer matrices, even for exactly 5,799 distinct matrices with 5,798 fixed nonsingular generators of determinant ±p and one variable rank-one matrix with fixed image. The construction encodes a universal arithmetic program in rational projective points; a p-adic error set is intended to prevent invalid products from returning to valid configurations.
review.prior_frontier: Mortality was known decidable in dimension one and undecidable from dimension three; the unrestricted two-dimensional case is a long-standing boundary. Earlier decidable special cases such as determinants 0,±1 are deliberately avoided.

score_reasons.significance: Would resolve a fundamental dimension threshold in a classic undecidability problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses periodic p-adic unary codes, state residues and irreversible error detection in only two dimensions.
score_reasons.depth: The main burden is soundness of unrestricted matrix words, especially false division and contraction guesses.
score_reasons.exposition: A clear staged reduction and explicit generator tables, but delicate arithmetic cases remain central.

checked: Checked the rank-one outer-product reduction: any mortal word yields a nonsingular subword mapping the fixed image line into the variable kernel.
Read the invariant error set, disjoint state-residue blocks and bundled generator construction; a wrong digit or state cannot be repaired by the auxiliary maps.
Inspected the contraction false-split calculation in Lemma D.1: the remaining leading residues 3,4,−1 reject guesses that survive the first marker-count comparison.
remaining: The 36-page undecidability proof contains a long residue-validated counter-machine construction and a claimed formal companion. The checked rank-one reduction and false-split residue examples do not certify every module. Complete simulation and error-invariant coverage remain a large-proof exception.
The complete counter-machine simulation, every division/contraction module, the recovery validation Lemma D.3 and the residue invariant for all incorrect guesses require a full audit.
The exact generator count and padding argument, and the claimed companion Lean verification, have not been independently checked or executed.

papers.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo Beyond Hardy--Krause II: $(1 + \varepsilon) n$ Samples Suffice
papers.authors: Ekene Ezeunala, Agastya Vibhuti Jha, Haotian Jiang

review.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo Beyond Hardy--Krause II: $(1 + \varepsilon) n$ Samples Suffice
review.authors: Ekene Ezeunala, Agastya Vibhuti Jha, Haotian Jiang
review.summary: From (1+ε)n iid uniform points, online thinning retains n with high probability and gives mean-square integration error soft-O_(d,ε)(σ_SO(f)²/n²). A separate linear-feedback thinning achieves unnormalized star discrepancy O_(d,ε)(log^(d+1)n), with polylogarithmic per-sample work and no two consecutive rejections.
review.prior_frontier: Replaces the n² input samples of Bansal–Jiang’s beyond-Hardy–Krause construction by nearly n, and improves Haar-thinning discrepancy from log^(2d+1)n to log^(d+1)n. ε,d are fixed and hidden dependence is not dimension-free. Prior comparisons not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Removes a quadratic sampling overhead from a strong randomized integration guarantee and nearly reaches the standard low-discrepancy sequence scale.
score_reasons.novelty: A Haar symmetry makes distinct low-order discrepancy coefficients exactly uncorrelated; uniform shifts translate the bound to smoothed variation.
score_reasons.depth: Connects online thinning, martingale-type discrepancy control and function-space norm equivalences.
score_reasons.exposition: The covariance proof gives an explicit measure-preserving involution and cleanly tracks the algorithm under it.

checked: Fully traced the uncorrelated-Haar lemma: swapping halves of a dyadic interval flips one Haar function and fixes a distinct comparison function, while permuting all remaining functions up to sign without changing scales.

Checked equivariance of the target density: odd sign feedback cancels each function-sign factor, so transformed samples make identical acceptance decisions under shared rejection coins. Measure preservation makes the covariance equal its negative.
Verified uniform shifting is equivalent to shifting the integrand and does not change the iid input law.
remaining: Second-moment bounds for individual Haar coefficients, high-frequency remainder, shift-averaged variation equivalence and the separate linear-feedback discrepancy bound remain unchecked.

papers.title: The Geometry of Sapience: Polymeric Geometry and Gauge Dynamics on the Zeta Critical Line
papers.authors: Michael Sobolewski

review.title: The Geometry of Sapience: Polymeric Geometry and Gauge Dynamics on the Zeta Critical Line
review.authors: Michael Sobolewski
review.summary: Proposes a lattice/field metaphor for distributed services and claims a zeta-zero-based entropy stabilization and a derived metalogic equivalence identity. The claimed stabilization and derivation are mathematically invalid as stated.
review.prior_frontier: No validated computational complexity improvement is established by the inspected claims; the number-theoretic normalization incorrectly uses prime-counting asymptotics for zeros.

score_reasons.significance: The central claimed computational stability rests on a false number-theoretic limit.
score_reasons.novelty: Renaming geometric and logical quantities does not establish a demonstrated new algorithmic or mathematical result.
score_reasons.depth: The principal derivation fails elementary integration and the central asymptotic uses the wrong counting law.
score_reasons.exposition: Operational assumptions do not supply a formal bridge from the metaphysical assertions to proved guarantees.

checked: Visually verified PDF p6 equations (23)-(24): N(S) counts nontrivial zeta zeros up to height S, S_sys=N(S)/(S/log S), and the paper claims a limit of 1. The Riemann–von Mangoldt law instead gives S_sys ~ (log S)^2/(2pi), diverging. Verified the primary-source explicit estimate at arXiv:2107.06506.
Visually verified PDF p2 equations (7)-(8): dG=c_tau dS is claimed to integrate to G=S c_tau^2. For constant c_tau, integration gives G=c_tau S+C; e.g. c_tau=2, G=2S satisfies (7) and violates (8).
remaining: No further proof audit is needed for recommendation: these are concrete failures of the stated central mathematical support. If N counts a different selected subset, its selection/growth rule would need to be defined and proved; the asserted zeta-zero asymptotic does not supply it.
issues: Equation (24) is false for the stated zeta-zero counting function: the normalized ratio diverges rather than tending to 1.
Equation (8) does not follow by integration from (7) for a general fixed c_tau.

review.desk_reject_reason: Concrete failure of the central stabilization claim at p6 equations (23)-(24), independently reinforced by the invalid equivalence-principle derivation at p2 equations (7)-(8).

review.title: Adaptivity Gaps for Influence Maximization: Percolation and Depletion
review.authors: Gabriel de Azevedo, Ulysse Hennebelle

score_reasons.significance: Large general improvements in a standard adaptive diffusion problem, though constant gaps remain open.
score_reasons.novelty: A short depletion argument and a new combination of percolation inequalities drive the improvements.
score_reasons.depth: Careful conditioning and threshold aggregation make dependent cascades tractable.
score_reasons.exposition: Especially readable and economical proof architecture, with precise feedback and independence assumptions.

checked: Traced the directed depletion argument: swap optimality plus submodularity bounds each added marginal by OPT/k; Markov bounds each vertex's surviving high-influence probability by b^(-t); tail summation, residual-policy replay and b=sqrt(log n) give O(log n/log log n). Verified that cascade conditioning leaves internal inactive arcs independent.
Traced subtree packing/covering and the factor-2 bidirected-forest proof, including the residual influence bound after deleting a hitting set.

Traced all new undirected steps: augmenting the target set by a deterministic hub, three-point ratio inequality, weak/strong connection excess bounds, ordered-pair aggregation, and swap-rounding extension. Verified the invoked three-point inequality in Gladkov's primary PDF and the stronger Kozma–Nitzan theorem statement in Gouere's primary paper.
remaining: The external percolation theorems, adaptive-submodularity theorem and swap-rounding theorem were not independently reproved. This audit verifies the new deductions conditional on those published or publicly documented results.

sources.detail: Primary abstract and PDF inspected; Theorem 1 supplies the required Kozma–Nitzan inequality.

review.summary: Improves full-adoption influence-maximization adaptivity gaps to O(log n/log log n) for directed graphs, 5 sqrt(k) for undirected graphs, and 2 for bidirected forests.

papers.authors: Robin Kothari, Tony Metger, Ryan O'Donnell, Noah Shutty, Kewen Wu

review.title: Exponential quantum speedup for F_3^n-Subset-Sum? Or, rigorous classical algorithms for Binary-Error LWE
review.authors: Robin Kothari, Tony Metger, Ryan O’Donnell, Noah Shutty, Kewen Wu
review.summary: For random vectors in F₃ⁿ, gives a quantum algorithm finding a nonempty zero-sum subset in polynomial time from m=εn² vectors for every fixed ε>0, and a broader sample/time tradeoff. Its key classical component is a deterministic binary-error LWE decoder with a pointwise success guarantee over the random matrix, for secrets and errors independent of that matrix. No classical lower bound or proved exponential quantum separation is established.
review.prior_frontier: Prior polynomial classical algorithms required about n²/3 vectors; this paper also improves the classical constant to 0.1022. The quantum result covers every positive constant, reopening rather than settling the speedup question.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial average-case quantum-algorithm advance and rigorous cryptographic decoding analysis.
score_reasons.novelty: Turns heuristic algebraic sample/time behavior into a proven quotient-decoding guarantee.
score_reasons.depth: Uses symbolic rank, multiset shadows and a martingale bound, alongside a coherent quantum reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly separates proved algorithms from speculative speedup and cryptographic implications.

checked: Read the surjectivity progress argument with normalized increments and Azuma concentration.

Checked the symbolic-to-random rank step: determinant degree at most twice its rank, multiplicity Schwartz–Zippel, and rank deficiency bounded by root multiplicity give expected rank at least one third of symbolic rank.
remaining: The multiset-shadow lower bound, quotient-decoder recovery and coherent reduction with decoding errors remain to be fully audited.
The optimized classical 0.1022 constant and larger-field algorithms are not checked.

papers.title: Sublinear-Time Algorithms on Massive Data Streams
papers.authors: Omri Ben-Eliezer, Krzysztof Onak, Sandeep Silwal, Yinzhan Xu

review.title: Sublinear-Time Algorithms on Massive Data Streams
review.authors: Omri Ben-Eliezer, Krzysztof Onak, Sandeep Silwal, Yinzhan Xu
review.summary: Introduces forward-only stream testing measured by revealed entries rather than memory. Natural bounded-degree graph properties separate nonadaptive, worst-order streaming, random-order streaming and fully adaptive testers: triangle freeness O(d/ε) streaming, connectivity constant random-order versus Ω(√n) worst order, and bipartiteness n^(1−o(1)) random-order versus soft-O(√n) adaptive. Sequence common-element and 132-freeness tests use polylogarithmic queries.
review.prior_frontier: Connects testing and streaming via an intermediate access model; no sublinear wall-clock guarantee for physically receiving all entries and no memory bound. Prior testing separations not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A useful access-model hierarchy demonstrated by several natural graph and sequence problems.
score_reasons.novelty: Exploits the restricted forward adaptivity that ordinary nonadaptive testers lack, while distinguishing random arrival from arbitrary arrival.
score_reasons.depth: The separation package combines simple earliest-witness arguments with much harder nearly-linear lower bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The resource measured and differences from traditional streaming are explicitly motivated and tabulated.

checked: Traced triangle tester: sufficiently many disjoint triangle witnesses yield Ω(εn) earliest vertices; sampling each with probability min{1,6/(εn)} reveals its two later neighbors and hence the triangle. Expected O(d/ε) queries can be capped with small failure probability.
Checked sparse-graph distance normalization and that sequence order is fixed by the instance, unlike arbitrary graph arrival.
remaining: Random-order connectivity algorithm, worst-order connectivity lower bound, near-linear bipartiteness lower bound and sequence algorithms remain unaudited.

papers.title: NP-hardness for Bipartite Colorings up to the Maximum Degree
papers.authors: Andreas Galanis, Heng Guo, Yuchen He, Daniel Stefankovic, Eric Vigoda

review.title: NP-hardness for Bipartite Colorings up to the Maximum Degree
review.authors: Andreas Galanis, Heng Guo, Yuchen He, Daniel Štefankovič, Eric Vigoda
review.summary: For every fixed odd q>=5 and Delta>q, and for q=3 with Delta>=5, approximating the number of proper q-colorings of bipartite maximum-degree-Delta graphs within exp(cn) is NP-hard. Without a degree restriction, every fixed q>=3 has no FPRAS unless NP=RP. Even-q bounded-degree and (q,Delta)=(3,4) are deferred to a future full version.
review.prior_frontier: Strengthens prior #BIS-hardness, previously established in the bounded-degree range q<=Delta/(2 log Delta), to NP-hardness up to q<Delta for the proved odd-q range.

score_reasons.significance: Changes the expected approximation-complexity classification for bipartite colorings and approaches the degree threshold.
score_reasons.novelty: A bipartite connector realizes repulsive interactions between same-side phases; odd-q random-bipartite phase optimization supplies bounded-degree gadgets.
score_reasons.depth: Precise dominant-phase analysis, connector implementation and approximation-preserving gadget control are technically extensive.
score_reasons.exposition: The submitted parity restrictions and excluded remaining small case are explicit; the unbounded-degree warm-up exposes the mechanism clearly.

checked: Traced the unbounded-degree gadget reduction to a phase partition function with lambda>1, including cubic-graph field normalization and separation of consecutive maximum-cut values.
Checked phase suppression by strict concavity with N=n^3 versus h=n^2 and global biclique suppression with L=n^9.
Independently recomputed the connector transfer matrix using exact rational arithmetic for q=4,...,10; every determinant equals -(q-2)^2(q-1)/9 as claimed.
remaining: Large-proof exception (57 pages). The unbounded-degree phase construction and its scale separation were traced, and the connector determinant was independently recomputed exactly for q=4 through10. The maximum-degree bounded construction, odd-q phase Hessian and quantitative reduction are still unverified.
Audit the bounded-degree connector and random-gadget construction, the odd-q dominant-phase optimization and its Hessian, quantitative hardness gap, and q=3 appendix.

review.title: Lower Bounds for Adaptive Relaxed Locally Decodable Codes via the Capped Horvitz--Thompson Estimator
review.authors: Guy Goldberg, Tom Gur, Sidhant Saraogi
review.summary: Extends the nearly tight relaxed-LDC blocklength lower bound to arbitrary nonlinear binary encodings and adaptive decoders with two-sided error. For constant decoding radius and every fixed ε>0 it proves n≥Ωε(q⁻²(k/log k)^(1+1/((2+ε)q))); for constant q this is k^(1+Ω(1/q)), and constant rate forces q=Ω(log k/log log k).
review.prior_frontier: The matching exponent was previously proved for nonadaptive perfect-completeness codes and hence linear codes; the general bound had a roughly quadratic query dependence in its exponent.

score_reasons.significance: Closes a meaningful adaptivity/nonlinearity gap in relaxed local decoding.
score_reasons.novelty: Introduces a capped Horvitz–Thompson estimator combining unconditional concentration with spreadness-controlled bias.
score_reasons.depth: Couples adaptive decision-tree sampling, spread extraction and self-bounding concentration.
score_reasons.exposition: The estimator and the source of each loss are clearly explained.

checked: Inspected the coordinate-cap linear program and the soundness union-bound strategy over guessed heavy coordinates.
Checked the elementary overload inequality and the trimming construction bounding the lost estimator mass by summed overloads; read the variance expansion indexed by intersections.
remaining: The full spreadness variance bound, self-bounding inequalities and adaptive sample-decoder reduction require checking through their precise parameter choices.
The external spread-extraction theorem has not been independently verified.

review.title: A Faster FPTAS for Weighted Completion Time Scheduling
review.authors: Karl Bringmann, Anita Dürr, Karol Węgrzycki
review.summary: For fixed m≥2 identical machines, weighted completion-time scheduling admits an FPTAS in O(n(n/ε)^((m−1)/2+α)) time for any constant α>0, and O(n√(n/ε)) for m=2. Claims matching 1/ε exponent under CNF-SETH, allowing arbitrary polynomial dependence on n in the lower-bound formulation.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the classical/folklore ε exponent m−1 by nearly a factor two; the exact pseudopolynomial exponent remains m−1 under the stated hypothesis. This concerns fixed m and does not give an FPTAS for variable m.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial speedup for one of the earliest FPTAS problems and a sharp separation between approximation and pseudopolynomial complexity.
score_reasons.novelty: Future schedule costs become directional linear functionals of load/cost states, so geometric ε-kernels replace uniform DP rounding.
score_reasons.depth: Careful extension-preserving representative sets give a short and robust approximation proof; conditional optimality needs a separate fine-grained reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: The geometry-to-DP link, accumulated error and runtime are presented explicitly.

checked: Traced the entire new FPTAS argument. Smith ordering gives the load/cost DP; future completion cost equals a state-independent term plus ⟨prefix loads, differences of suffix weights⟩+prefix cost.
Verified U≤mOPT by serializing an optimum in completion order and Ti W_(>i)+Ui≤U. Therefore a relaxed δ/m additive directional approximation suffices for δOPT error for every suffix.
Checked ε-kernel reduction: subset width preservation bounds loss in minimum inner product by ε times the original width≤2m(AX+B); no normalization ambiguity remains because the direction is (x,1).

Representative-set errors add through transitions; δ=ε/n gives final (1+ε)OPT. Cited standard fixed-dimensional ε-kernel size O(δ^(−(m−1)/2)) and construction time yield the claimed bounds, with Chan’s planar construction removing α for m=2.
remaining: The CNF-SETH reduction and broad scheduling classification appendices remain unchecked. The main-proof check covers the algorithm and accepts the explicitly stated standard ε-kernel construction theorems as dependencies; those geometric source proofs were not rederived.

review.title: On the pseudorandomness of simple quantum processes

review.title: Improved Exact and Approximate Quantum Fourier Transforms from Multiplication
review.authors: Chandrima Kayal, Rajat Mittal, Manaswi Paraashar, Nitin Saurabh
review.summary: Assuming Boolean integer multiplication size M(n)=O(n(log n)^α), constructs exact q-qubit QFT of size O(q(log q)^α), and ε-approximate QFT of size O(q(log log(q/ε))^α). Exact circuits use one extra q-dependent single-qubit rotation; approximate circuits replace it by dyadic phase gates. Both circuit families are nonuniform as presented, and the unit-cost arbitrary dyadic phase-gate model does not include fault-tolerant gate synthesis costs.
review.prior_frontier: Removes one logarithmic factor from the multiplication-based exact and approximate circuit bounds. With α=1 this yields exact O(q log q); a claimed sub-n-log-n multiplication improvement is only an optional conditional specialization.

score_reasons.significance: Improves a central quantum primitive, with an important nonuniform gate-model qualification.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines Fourier-label averaging, exact amplitude amplification and multiplication-based answer testing.
score_reasons.depth: A concise construction whose resource accounting and coherent cleanup can be checked directly.
score_reasons.exposition: Gives explicit clean-ancilla guarantees and discusses the extra gate and uniformity limitation.

checked: Checked Fourier-state copying by modular subtraction and the exact label test using a product phase, Hadamards and a zero-state reflection.

Checked the full exactification: average success over a coherent uniform label shift, rotate success to 1/4, use one Grover iterate, copy the certain answer, uncompute and erase the Fourier input. Each step preserves the fixed-label subspace and overall phases cancel in the cleanup.
Checked product-phase truncation error <4π2⁻ᵏ per recursion node, unequal splits, O(q/k) leaves, reusable workspace and deferred wire permutations.
Checked dyadic replacement of the extra rotation, six-call error accounting on the full input/workspace unitary, balanced scalar phases and the final 16πq2⁻ᵏ bound.

The required constant-error approximate QFT baseline can be reconstructed from the stated product-phase recursion using the standard exact recurrence T(n)=2T(ceil(n/2))+O(M(n)), giving O(n log^(α+1)n) base circuits; this avoids assuming a stronger unproved baseline.
remaining: This is a main-argument check in the manuscript’s nonuniform unit-cost gate model, not formal verification or a circuit implementation.
No independent verification of the optional claimed faster multiplication algorithm, nor any uniform angle-generation algorithm or physical gate-synthesis cost.

papers.title: Efficiently Learning SYK Hamiltonians

review.title: Efficiently Learning SYK Hamiltonians
review.authors: Anurag Anshu, Srinivasan Arunachalam, Sitan Chen, Yeongwoo Hwang
review.summary: Learns quartic Gaussian SYK couplings from Gibbs states at every fixed known inverse temperature β>0 to arbitrary normalized squared error ε in poly(min{β,1}^(−1),2^(β²),n,ε^(−1),log(1/δ)) resources, for all but O_β(1/n) Hamiltonians. A separate fixed-time evolution algorithm learns coupling direction up to sign, with polynomial resources and total evolution time proportional to the supplied t*.
review.prior_frontier: Improves fixed-temperature SYK learning from limited accuracy to arbitrary accuracy and rigorously validates the thermal commutator nullspace heuristic. It is typical-case Gaussian quartic SYK, not worst-case all-to-all Hamiltonian learning; constants and n threshold depend on β.

score_reasons.significance: Removes a major accuracy limitation for learning a canonical dense interacting quantum model at constant temperature.
score_reasons.novelty: Proves robust identifiability of the commutator linear system through low-degree Gaussian Hermite structure and noncancellation of a connected cubic contribution.
score_reasons.depth: Seventy-four pages combine exterior-algebra contractions, random tensor bounds, thermal coefficients and scale reconstruction.
score_reasons.exposition: The theorem distinguishes average-over-Hamiltonians failure, measurement error, temperature dependence and direction-only dynamical access.

checked: Checked measurement interface: six- versus four-Majorana commutators only require degree-four/eight correlators, and thermal stationarity makes the true coupling vector a null vector.

Traced quartic contraction Lemma 3.4: three annihilations split 0+3,3+0,1+2,2+1; mixed-input norm counts 12 appearances per quartic coefficient and the degree-(3,2,1) wedge map has norm≤√60, giving 12√5 times the stated operator products.

Checked the concluding spectral-gap accounting conditional on its tensor and coefficient lemmas: positive leading c_(1,4), connected cubic correction, O_β(n^(−1/2)) L2 error and Markov give an O_β(1/n) exceptional fraction; Cauchy–Schwarz transfers overlap gap to a singular-value gap on g-perp.
remaining: The central noncancellation coefficient inequality c_(1,4)−2c_conn≥c min{β,1}exp(−Cβ²), full random tensor/Hermite tail bounds and associated appendix dependencies remain unchecked.
Scale learning and the fixed-time evolution phase-gap argument remain unchecked; no full theorem certification is assigned.

checked: Verified unitarity of the local rotation on its three invariant sectors and the Cayley block identity by solving the two block equations.

score_reasons.significance: Closes the main computational question left by the optimal-error existence theorem.
score_reasons.novelty: Transforms a controllable but non-gradient certificate into an affine online optimization game.

score_reasons.exposition: Exceptionally explicit algorithms, model assumptions and proof modules.

checked: Traced the complete central ERM-oracle theorem: corruption-certificate algebra and linearization, weighted ERM reduction by resampling, normalized gradient/diameter bounds, small self-loss via majority approximation, uniform certificate stability under eta-fraction replacements, and generalization over convex combinations of k-majorities.

Checked the approximate online Frank–Wolfe recurrence and regret constants in Appendix F, including strong concavity, tracking the regularized maximizers and the O(T^(3/4)) regret bound. The claimed T=O(epsilon^-4) oracle count follows.
remaining: The separate end-to-end polynomial learner, adaptive weighted filtering, L1 approximation/SQ implications and deterministic-hypothesis extension were not fully audited. This main-proof status applies to the central ERM-oracle result, not to all 52 pages.

Reduces arbitrary disk chains to local potential inequalities, then a four-parameter differential/interval verification. The chain reduction can introduce slack, so this does not identify the exact optimum.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the previous 1.998 upper bound to within 0.0017 of the known lower bound, with consequences for constructions using Delaunay stretch as a black box.

score_reasons.significance: A dramatic tightening of a classical geometric constant.
score_reasons.novelty: A local progress potential and a pencil deformation reduce an unbounded chain problem to finite-dimensional verification.
score_reasons.depth: Combines geometric reductions, degenerate corner analysis and a substantial exact/interval certificate.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly describes the certificate and reproducibility, but full assessment requires both analytic and computational checks.

checked: Checked the forward-path argument in the width-two ladder: a simple path crosses a two-edge cut exactly once.
Traced the exact clipped difference/mean update and the telescoping cost-minus-progress identity.
Inspected the four-coordinate reduction and certificate structure: 3,150 rational coefficients and over one million boxes, with outward-rounded arithmetic.
remaining: The 67-page Delaunay result combines a checked ladder recurrence with a large computational certificate. The triangulation reduction and more than one million interval boxes are not verified; this is a large-proof/certificate exception, not a certified numerical stretch bound.
The triangulation-to-chain reduction, pencil and corner lemmas, and the explicit potential’s feasibility still require a complete audit.
The archived programs/data and more than one million interval boxes have not been independently inspected or rerun; the claimed numerical bound is not certified by this review.

review.summary: For N users with n iid d-dimensional observations each and covariance at most identity, withstands ε fully corrupt users and αNn arbitrary sample replacements among the rest, achieving O(√α+√(ε/n)+√((d+log(1/δ))/(Nn))) error in soft-O(Nnd) time. Requires sufficiently small corruption fractions and N≥log(1/δ).
review.prior_frontier: Strengthens previous per-user-limited double corruption while replacing high-degree polynomial SoS runtime and multiplicative confidence dependence by near-linear filtering and additive log(1/δ). Prior minimax and algorithmic comparisons not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Simultaneously strengthens the adversarial model, confidence guarantee and computational efficiency in batched robust estimation.
score_reasons.novelty: Two reference populations, at sample and batch-mean level, support coupled filtering instead of treating all corruptions as a single flat contamination fraction.
score_reasons.depth: Must preserve useful user structure through sample reweighting and control empirical covariance and mean at both levels.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise corruption budget and theorem prerequisites are clear, though the 66-page filtering analysis is intricate.

checked: Traced sample-score dominance conditional on reference stability: weighted covariance splits into good, bad and between-means terms; good mean displacement contributes at most (bad mass/total mass) times the total score, so bounded good covariance controls its score share.
Checked reweighting error bound from weighted Cauchy–Schwarz and the decomposition showing average within-user covariance is bounded by overall weighted covariance.
Distinguished a global αNn sample budget over good users from the weaker αn per-good-user assumption.
remaining: Construction of the stable reference sets with sub-Gaussian confidence, filtering loss invariants, batch-level analysis and near-linear matrix routines remain unchecked.

review.title: Semi-Streaming Matching in a Single Pass II: Greedy is Optimal
review.authors: Sepehr Assadi, Max Jiang, Mars Xiang
review.summary: Proves that a single adversarial-order pass with O(n polylog n) space cannot approximate maximum matching by any fixed factor greater than 1/2 with constant success probability, even for bipartite graphs with a perfect matching. Also states the optimal 1/2 competitive ratio for preemptive online matching. The theorem does not cover random-order or multipass streams.
review.prior_frontier: The previous lower-bound threshold was approximately 0.558; the result meets the elementary greedy half-approximation and settles the single-pass question.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a foundational question in graph streaming with a tight answer.
score_reasons.novelty: Completes the blueprint framework using random walks with symmetrized maxima.
score_reasons.depth: The limiting blueprint must obey combinatorial constraints while approaching value 2/3.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states the streaming restrictions and explains the connection to the previous framework.

checked: Inspected the blueprint-to-approximation transformation α=(2−2v)/(2−v) and the limit v→2/3 yielding 1/2.
Checked the telescoping normalization and partial-sum calculation for the initial random-walk distribution that makes terminating maxima symmetric and yields termination probability 2m/(3m+1).
remaining: The 44-page matching lower bound has checked final approximation algebra and initial walk normalization. The full delayed-walk blueprint and its prior lower-bound theorem remain unchecked; this is a large-proof exception.
The entire delayed-walk blueprint construction, rounding/truncation losses and properness constraints remain to be checked.
The prior blueprint lower-bound theorem and the preemptive-online reduction are essential dependencies not independently audited here.

papers.title: Characterizing Quantum Advantage for Generalizations of the Boolean Hidden Matching Problem
papers.authors: Mark Bun, Joao F. Doriguello, John Kallaugher, Nadezhda Voronova

review.title: Characterizing Quantum Advantage for Generalizations of the Boolean Hidden Matching Problem
review.authors: Mark Bun, Joao F. Doriguello, John Kallaugher, Nadezhda Voronova
review.summary: For every fixed predicate f of sign degree d≥2 and fixed block density α∈(0,1), f-Boolean Hidden Partition has randomized one-way communication Θ(n^(1−1/d)); quantum complexity is between Ω(n^(1−2/d)) and O(n^(1−1/ceil(d/2)) log n). Exactly sign degree two gives exponential quantum advantage; every d≥2 gives polynomial advantage. The quantum exponent gap for odd d remains.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves the Doriguello–Montanaro sign-degree conjecture, replacing pure-high-degree lower bounds and removing their small-density restriction. Prior claims read in this manuscript, not independently reverified.

score_reasons.significance: Classifies the predicates producing quantum advantage in a central family of communication separations.
score_reasons.novelty: The hard distribution may correlate Alice’s bits strongly with Bob’s unknown partition, handled by sequential conditioning rather than independence.
score_reasons.depth: Combines LP-dual sign degree, scalar and matrix hypercontractivity, and sign-polynomial sampling.
score_reasons.exposition: The distinction between sign degree and pure high degree, and the remaining odd-degree gap, are clearly explained.

checked: Traced the quantum lower-bound core: after fixing every block placement except block i, average the other input bits conditioned on prior f-values. The resulting ν_i remains a density matrix, and the remaining block is uniformly injected into (1−α)n+k positions.

Fourier coefficients of qf vanish below d by the sign-degree dual witness. Triangle/Cauchy–Schwarz and matrix hypercontractivity bound the expected trace norm by O((c/n)^(d/2)). The telescoping conditional-message hybrid over Θ(n) blocks gives advantage O(c^(d/2)/n^(d/2−1)), hence the claimed quantum lower exponent.
Checked normalization: the 2^(i−1) conditional factor makes ν_i a convex combination, while Q contributes 2^((α−1)n); converting to normalized Fourier coefficients leaves precisely 2^k.
remaining: Full classical lower-bound normalization with a possibly non-full-support witness q remains to check.
Formal upper protocols and their second-moment/communication accounting remain to audit, beyond the overview sampling argument.
Matrix hypercontractivity is an explicitly cited external dependency, not reproved here.

review.title: Linear-length cycles in the supercritical percolated hypercube
review.authors: Michael Anastos
review.summary: For every sufficiently small fixed epsilon>0, bond percolation of Q_d at p=(1+epsilon)/d has, with high probability as d grows, a cycle of length Theta(epsilon^2 2^d), constructible in O(d^2 2^(2d)) time. Also estimates giant-component 2-core size as (2epsilon^2+O(epsilon^3))2^d. Epsilon is fixed, not an arbitrary shrinking critical-window parameter.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the prior Omega(2^d/(d log d)) supercritical cycle guarantee to linear length, with optimal epsilon dependence supplied by the 2-core upper bound.

score_reasons.significance: Settles the linear-circumference question immediately above the percolation threshold and obtains the correct small-epsilon scale.
score_reasons.novelty: Packs medium cycles using local expansion and edge sparsity, then joins them across independently percolated subcubes.
score_reasons.depth: Robust merging, 2-core size/concentration and expansion control must coexist at different scales.
score_reasons.exposition: The roadmap explains why direct global expansion loses a factor d and why the 2-core improves epsilon^3 to epsilon^2.

checked: Traced the repeated DFS dichotomy yielding a long cycle or a medium almost-connected set with a small residual neighborhood.

Checked the cycle-packing double count: assign poorly expanding components to their latest removed neighbor, bound their union by 2C/c, then compare incoming/outgoing edges to get total coverage c/(7C).
Read the successful-terminal construction and thinning condition that makes projected terminal sets disjoint; checked its role in invoking the merging proposition.
remaining: Audit the full multi-round path-joining proposition, 2-core asymptotic and expansion theorem, and all conditional independence/concentration estimates in the subcube construction.

review.title: Optimal stabilizer testing and learning with limited quantum memory
review.authors: Srinivasan Arunachalam, Louis Schatzki

score_reasons.significance: Sharp memory/sample tradeoffs settle natural testing and learning questions.
score_reasons.novelty: Connects partial Bell sampling to a hidden-shift affine-consistency test and develops average likelihood-ratio methods.
score_reasons.depth: Substantial symplectic combinatorics and quantum memory lower-bound machinery.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear modular overview; several notation slips and endpoint statements need correction.

checked: Checked partial-Bell marginalization and the Fourier/subspace formula for prefix mass; traced the hidden-shift bias calculation and affine-graph union bound.

Checked the global soundness argument: large Pauli coefficients commute, extend to a Lagrangian, the stabilizer of that Lagrangian makes conditional intersections uniform, and the resulting averaged prefix-mass estimate gives Omega(epsilon) bad-prefix probability, including the k=0 conditioning argument.

The headline O((n-k)/epsilon) cannot literally hold at k=n (or for unrestricted k>n). Use O((1+n-min(k,n))/epsilon), and N proportional to m+1 at m=0. This is a local endpoint correction; the n-k growing regime is unaffected.
remaining: The 67-page manuscript's central matching lower bound, orthogonal-group likelihood estimates, nonadaptive learning tradeoff and coherent-memory purity lower bound remain unaudited.

A complete implementation audit of hidden-shift phases and the optional ancilla-free circuit was not performed. The endpoint correction should be incorporated before treating the stated theorem as literal for every k.

checked: Read the distinction between fixed terminals with every matching and full tree universality.

review.summary: For every vertex fixed before random ranks are sampled, memoized rank-ordered pruned greedy MIS makes at most CΔ^90(1+h) fresh calls except with probability e^(−h). Expected fresh calls are O(Δ^90); total calls incur an additional Δ factor. This is not a simultaneous all-vertices bound or an arbitrary neighbor-scan order guarantee.
review.prior_frontier: Improves exp(O(Δ)) worst-starting-vertex analysis of this specific greedy recursion to polynomial dependence; other polynomial-query MIS LCAs already existed. Prior bounds taken from the manuscript.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a longstanding complexity question about a canonical greedy process, with uses across local and sublinear graph algorithms.
