checked: Traced Lemma 5.2 conditional on the root rank: exponential memorylessness makes the instantaneous expected loss of active attached k-sets equal the sum of their active-neighborhood sizes. Lemma 5.1 gives f′≤−(k/e)f^(1+1/k), and integration yields E Y_k(t)≤(e/t)^k independently of the initial graph size.

Verified the one-arrival expansion: multi-arrival probability O_G(δ²) is harmless because the finite graph is fixed before δ tends to zero. Conditioning the root above t removes its arrival from the hazard sum without weakening the bound.
Integrated the stated exponential tail to get E Q≤2CΔ^90, and checked the total-call conversion 1+ΔQ.
remaining: The deterministic attached-set inequality itself, its prescribed-starting-ranks extension, and Section 6 adaptive union bounds remain unchecked.
The multiscale deterministic tree-size recurrence and low-rank remainder leading to exponent 90 need a full audit.

Traced the complete new white-box hardness reduction: reversible plateau clock, nondegenerate spectrum, efficiently prepared 3/4-overlap eigenvectors, commutator mass transfer to the completed-computation plateau, V-dagger=VW-dagger substitution, and bounded-error postselection/repetition. Uniformity is enforced by a single family encoding all instances.
Verified Eppstein's iterated reversible-computation completeness dependency in its primary publication description. The new reduction uses it as an external theorem.
Rendered PDF p. 24 to verify the repetition count is 10^100 (not 10100); its displayed probability bounds suffice for the stated success guarantee.
remaining: The independent upper-bound simulation of random square roots in Sections 4–5 was not audited. This status covers the traced new hardness and oracle separation arguments, not the entire simulation theorem.

sources.detail: Primary Eppstein publication confirming FP^PSPACE completeness of iterated reversible computation.

review.summary: Shows that efficient square roots for every efficiently implementable unitary would imply BQP=PSPACE, and gives an Omega(N) versus O(log N) black-box separation between ordinary and arbitrary square-root queries.
review.prior_frontier: Aaronson's square-root question had been regarded as answered positively, but the earlier result applied only to a restricted unitary class. Iterated reversible computation supplied classical PSPACE hardness, not robustness to every quantum square root.
review.recommendation: Leading candidate with the central new hardness and separation proofs checked; additional simulation result has narrower audit coverage.

papers.title: Removing Spanning Trees Better Than Nash-Williams
papers.authors: Nathan Klein, Neil Olver, Zi Song Yeoh

review.title: Removing Spanning Trees Better Than Nash-Williams
review.authors: Nathan Klein, Neil Olver, Zi Song Yeoh
review.summary: Constructively finds a spanning tree in every k-edge-connected multigraph whose removal loses O(k/sqrt(log k)) edge connectivity, proving Pritchard’s conjecture by a combinatorial method. Also derives an asymmetric splitting statement. The paper explicitly acknowledges a recent stronger thin-tree result implying O(1) connectivity loss.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the published Nash–Williams-based loss near k/2; its contribution relative to the acknowledged stronger recent result is an independent, simpler combinatorial route and structural near-cut lemmas.

score_reasons.significance: A useful constructive conjecture resolution, tempered by an acknowledged stronger contemporary theorem.
score_reasons.novelty: Shows that sufficiently small cuts in a nearly twice-tree-packed graph split into few laminar families.
score_reasons.depth: A compact iteration using laminar thin-tree rounding and an elementary crossing-cut count.
score_reasons.exposition: The proof is short and transparent; a few informal splitting-ratio statements contain reciprocal notation slips.

checked: Checked the warm-up: cuts below 3k/4−66C are laminar because two crossing cuts require at least three edges in each packed tree.

Checked the full structural argument with the elementary alternative: each crossing cut is fundamental in at least 3εt/4 trees; at most two disjoint crossing shores and at most 8/ε nested shores bound the crossing graph degree by O(ε⁻²).
Checked layer-edge counting, including pure layers and the lower bound against the sum of cut sizes; greedy coloring supplies the laminar families without the polygon representation.

Checked repeated 44-to-1 tree thinning, preservation of previously repaired cuts, geometric η reduction and product-size estimate exp(O(η⁻²)); choosing η=Θ(1/sqrt(log k)) leaves one tree and a sublinear loss.

Verified the required laminar fractional-tree rounding statement against the original Klein–Olver paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07674 (saved as 1092-KO23.pdf), including its polynomial-time, less-than-22 multiplicative guarantee.
remaining: This checks the main connectivity theorem using the manuscript’s elementary alternative, whose larger constant changes only hidden constants in the iteration.
The stronger recent thin-tree preprint and its separately claimed 3k+o(k) splitting consequence were not audited; they are not needed for the checked result.
No implementation or formal proof was run.

papers.title: The Complexity of KKT Points of Quadratic Programs with Polynomially-Bounded Coefficients
papers.authors: Argyrios Deligkas, Michail Fasoulakis, Stavros Ioannidis

review.title: The Complexity of KKT Points of Quadratic Programs with Polynomially-Bounded Coefficients
review.authors: Argyrios Deligkas, Michail Fasoulakis, Stavros D. Ioannidis
review.summary: Computing an exact box-constrained KKT point of a quadratic polynomial remains CLS-complete with unary-encoded, polynomially bounded integer coefficients. In contrast, square-free quadratic polynomials with unary integer coefficients admit Boolean local search in polynomial time. This theorem does not claim hardness for inverse-polynomial approximation or constant coefficients.
review.prior_frontier: Answers the unary-coefficient question left by binary-coefficient quadratic KKT completeness. The reduction invokes the prior exact Quadratic-KKT CLS-completeness theorem.

score_reasons.significance: Separates coefficient magnitude from intrinsic hardness in a fundamental continuous local-search problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Encodes exponentially fine coefficients in interior auxiliary stationary values using a constant-coefficient quadratic chain.
score_reasons.depth: An exact Schur-complement-style identity plus interiority eliminates spurious boundary stationary points.
score_reasons.exposition: The short proof gives explicit coefficients, closed-form stationary values, and complete encoding-size accounting.

checked: Checked the entire new reduction. Clear denominators and divide by 2^L with L=O(input bits); signs and zeros of all original partial derivatives are preserved, and coefficients expand into polynomially many signed dyadic monomials.

For m=k+2, the gadget 3Σ(2u_i−u_(i+1))²+9u_m²−6xu_1+6syu_m+x²+y² has positive-definite auxiliary quadratic part. Its unique auxiliary KKT point is u_i=(2^(1−i)x−s2^(i−m)y)/3, solving both boundary equations and the interior recurrence, and |u_i|≤2/3.
Substitution cancels both pure-square contributions and leaves s2^(2−m)xy=s2^(−k)xy. This remains valid when x=y or a factor is the constant one.

Disjoint auxiliary blocks force every joint KKT point to the interior minimizer of each block. The chain rule has no auxiliary contribution, so original derivatives exactly match the normalized polynomial. Affine u=2v−1 preserves KKT boundary signs.

LCM bit length is bounded by the sum of denominator bit lengths; O(n²L²) auxiliaries and constant coefficients per gadget yield polynomial unary size after collecting terms. The square-free tractability contrast follows from integer objective decrease by at least one per improving Boolean flip.
remaining: The cited starting theorem that binary-coefficient exact Quadratic-KKT is CLS-complete is used as a standard external dependency; its proof was not re-audited.
No quantitative approximation-preservation or constant-coefficient hardness follows from this exact reduction.

papers.title: Price of Ignorance in Pairwise-Independent Prophet Inequalities
papers.authors: Shaza Abdallah, David Wajc

review.title: Price of Ignorance in Pairwise-Independent Prophet Inequalities
review.authors: Shaza Abdallah, David Wajc
review.summary: For pairwise-independent nonnegative values with known marginals, shows that the best correlation-blind competitive ratio equals the correlation-aware ratio and also equals the worst-case blind-to-aware online price of ignorance. Bounds this common adversarial-order constant between .439 and 525/1109, and gives .529 under random order. Meta-theorems require finite-support bounded witnesses and suitable null-signal padding.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the prior [sqrt(2)-1,1/2] range, strictly separates pairwise from full independence, and formalizes ignorance of the joint distribution rather than ignorance of marginals.

score_reasons.significance: Identifies the exact conceptual cost of correlation ignorance and improves both ends of a fundamental stopping-problem interval.
score_reasons.novelty: Reciprocal-prophet reweighting makes minimax work for ratios; secret-sharing padding turns online hard distributions into blind-versus-aware gaps.
score_reasons.depth: Quantifier order, infinite-support approximation and the empirical distribution hidden among many encoded worlds are central technical points.
score_reasons.exposition: Benchmark definitions and different arrival models are distinguished clearly.

checked: Verified the finite minimax reweighting mu_j proportional to y_j/P_j, which converts a mixture of ratios into a ratio under a feasible k-wise-independent joint law with fixed marginals.
Traced the pairwise-independent encoding using two uniform pads and a third modular share, retaining arbitrary encoded witness distributions.

Checked the empirical-world reduction: the aware algorithm knows the selected world, while blind reward is bounded by original-witness optimum plus a total-variation error vanishing as the number of worlds grows.
remaining: Audit finite-support truncation, random-order padding, the 525/1109 instance and the randomized-threshold .439/.529 optimization and tie-breaking proofs.

papers.title: Achieving the Optimal Abstention Rate for Learning with Distribution Shift
papers.authors: Gautam Chandrasekaran, Georgios Gkrinias, Adam R. Klivans, Konstantinos Stavropoulos, Arsen Vasilyan

review.title: Achieving the Optimal Abstention Rate for Learning with Distribution Shift
review.authors: Gautam Chandrasekaran, Georgios Gkrinias, Adam R. Klivans, Konstantinos Stavropoulos, Arsen Vasilyan

score_reasons.significance: Removes a severe computational dependence in robust selective learning with broad polynomial-approximation applications.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines capped moment-transfer weights with a linear-program selector and a uniform capped-support-function argument.
score_reasons.depth: Substantial uniform empirical-process, optimization and adversarial contamination analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear separation of distributional assumptions, computational parameters and adversary model; detailed appendices support the main guarantee.

checked: Traced the central selective-learning theorem: sandwiching-polynomial nonnegative disagreement majorants, Chow/moment transfer, capped training weights, LP acceptance objective and cancellation of the cap in the error guarantee.

Checked the uniform capped-weight transfer proof via support functions, the hinge-threshold representation, VC-subgraph bounds and moment envelopes; this supports data-dependent choices of the cap and weights.
Checked the common-occurrence feasible solution under replacement corruption, the excess-abstention grid and randomized selector rounding, including the near-total-corruption fallback.

Checked confidence amplification by fresh random block partition after the adversary's choice: clean-event independence, uniformity over corruptions, conditional independent rounding and the blockwise replacement-mass bound. The independent reference sample and finite-moment requirements are essential.
remaining: Known agnostic regression and sandwiching-polynomial approximation theorems are used as external inputs. The independent PQ-learning reduction and TLA/PQ separation were not fully audited.
Polynomial dependence on excess abstention does not mean polynomial dependence on all accuracy parameters: the sandwiching degree may itself depend strongly on the error tolerance.

review.summary: Achieves nearly optimal abstention under adversarial distribution shift with polynomial rather than exponential dependence on the excess-abstention parameter, under bounded-coefficient sandwiching-polynomial assumptions. The selective error is controlled by training error and the joint optimum.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier efficient testable-learning-with-abstention guarantees paid exponential dependence on the excess-abstention parameter. This work makes that dependence polynomial while retaining a degree-dependent dimension cost, and applies to Gaussian halfspaces via known sandwiching approximators.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate; central abstention theorem traced, with independent reductions and applications outside this audit.

papers.title: Tight Release Schedules under Distribution Shift
papers.authors: Jing Wang

review.title: Tight Release Schedules under Distribution Shift
review.authors: Jing Wang
review.summary: Characterizes minimax cumulative excess risk for passive Gaussian linear regression with a known nearby pretrained predictor and at most B released predictors. In the stationary case the rate is dΛB(TΔ²/d); a drifting-target result adds a release-design objective and tracking floor. Matching lower bounds have explicit dimension restrictions in few-release/high-horizon regimes. This is not a guarantee for neural-network retraining or arbitrary covariate shifts.
review.prior_frontier: Separates passive information collection from a pathwise predictor-release quota, refining related limited-switching and tracking models with initial-shift dependence.

score_reasons.significance: A precise statistical tradeoff in a restricted but useful deployment model.
score_reasons.novelty: The common-event lower bound handles adaptively chosen release times.
score_reasons.depth: Uses a bounded multiscale prior, likelihood comparison and phasewise minimax charging.
score_reasons.exposition: Careful qualifications distinguish stationary, gradual drift and abrupt-change families.

checked: Read the stopped-predictor extension to a deterministic scale horizon and the union bound over release/scale pairs.
Traced the few-release lower-bound phase charges and AM–GM optimization yielding geometric schedules; the dimension condition pays for a single event covering all releases.
remaining: The likelihood-ratio second-moment estimate and full multiscale prior construction need checking.
The drifting-path lower bound, structured-block reduction and separate sliding-window results are not audited.

papers.title: Maximum Cardinality Matching in $n^{2+o(1)}$ Time
papers.authors: George Z. Li, Jason Li, Junkai Zhang

review.title: Maximum Cardinality Matching in $n^{2+o(1)}$ Time
review.authors: George Z. Li, Jason Li, Junkai Zhang
review.summary: Randomized maximum-cardinality matching in general graphs in n^(2+o(1)) time with high probability, via simple unit-capacity integral skew-symmetric flows. The manuscript explicitly acknowledges a concurrent m^(1+o(1)) algorithm; its contribution is an alternative combinatorial route, not the best overall runtime after that result.
review.prior_frontier: Previously dense general matching relied on matrix multiplication, with O(m√n) classical combinatorial time. The concurrent almost-linear claim is acknowledged in the submission but not independently verified in this screen.

score_reasons.significance: Near-quadratic combinatorial general matching is a major algorithmic result, tempered by the acknowledged stronger concurrent runtime.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses stochastic single-edge barrier toggles instead of globally reweighting an entire obstructing cut.
score_reasons.depth: Extends flow sampling to skew-symmetric barriers and proves bounded weight growth with two supermartingales.
score_reasons.exposition: The core is concise but has minor notation errors in the second martingale and an overly broad flow-theorem statement relative to the unit-capacity setup.

checked: Traced the negative total-charge lemma: vertex potentials contribute −2|f|, a regular path cannot use both symmetric entrance edges of a small fragment, and fewer than K/2 large fragments contribute less than K in total.

Traced the first supermartingale: sampling proportional to |d_e|/x_e makes expected un-clipped change proportional to d_e; energy pays for clipping via 1−x≤−log x, and explicit augmentation/count budgets absorb resets. Optional stopping bounds support weights exceeding B by O(n²log U/B).

Traced the second-stage bound after support weights are bounded: total sample weight is ≥1/B, so each variable’s expected increase is ≤B before clipping; summing and budgeting n² variables gives O(Bn⁴log U/U). Choosing B=√U/n balances the two bounds at O(n³log U/√U).
Checked the height/cut reduction for nonzero charges and the small-fragment accounting Σs²≤(2n/K)Σs=O(n²/K) per regular-path search.

The second martingale display must sum over all active graph edges, not only edges in the search subgraph H; subsequent statements Q≥U/“Q is nonnegative” should refer to R. This is a direct notation repair consistent with the argument, not a discovered counterexample.
remaining: The resumable regular-reachability algorithm and dynamic-expander decomposition, particularly adaptive-update guarantees and recourse implementation, remain external dependencies to verify.
The broad flow theorem should explicitly retain unit capacities; the proof assumes them throughout.
High-probability runtime conversion for rejection sampling and all dependency failure probabilities still need a complete audit.

papers.title: A Spectral Local-to-Global Principle for Spin Systems on Graphs with Girth At Least Five
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu

review.title: A Spectral Local-to-Global Principle for Spin Systems on Graphs with Girth At Least Five
review.authors: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu
review.summary: For fixed positive delta and sufficiently large maximum degree Delta, proves an Omega_delta(1/n) heat-bath Glauber spectral gap for proper q-colorings of girth-at-least-five graphs when q>=(1+delta)Delta, and for antiferromagnetic Potts when q>=(1+delta)(1-beta)Delta. Gives a general girth-five criterion from pinned star spectral contraction.
review.prior_frontier: Lowers the prior near-Delta coloring girth assumption from seven to five. General-graph coloring thresholds elsewhere in this catalogue remain above Delta; the paper does not establish the pinned/list extension required for optimal n log n mixing.

score_reasons.significance: Reaches the natural near-degree sampling threshold under substantially weaker local sparsity and supplies a broader spin-system principle.
score_reasons.novelty: A weighted-star Bochner inequality uses unique common neighbors at distance two, followed by a low/high Fourier-degree Schur complement.
score_reasons.depth: Converting interaction-matrix contraction to star block estimates and retaining uniformity as degree grows is substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: The theorem separates irreducibility, pinning, local contraction and the missing list-coloring extension.

checked: Verified the local-to-global Bochner double count: nonadjacent update projections commute; girth five uniquely assigns distance-two pairs to stars.
Checked the weighted-star square expansion and cancellation yielding T_v >= (L_v-eta_v L_N(v))/2, hence the global gap from neighbor sums of eta.
Read the orthogonal Hoeffding decomposition and precise star Schur-complement criterion r<1/5, eta=||(P_v)_10||^2/((1-r)(1-4r)).
remaining: Audit the Schur complement proof, all interaction-matrix/star marginal contraction bounds, and their proper-coloring and Potts parameter substitutions.

papers.title: Rank-1-perturbed trickledown theorems: Mixing time of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model up to $\beta \le \tfrac{1}{2} + \eps$
papers.authors: Mathews Boban, Anqi Li, Shayan Oveis Gharan

review.title: Rank-1-perturbed trickledown theorems: Mixing time of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model up to $\beta \le \tfrac{1}{2} + \eps$
review.authors: Mathews Boban, Anqi Li, Shayan Oveis Gharan

score_reasons.significance: Crosses a significant mixing threshold for a central disordered spin model, beyond the concurrent beta<1/2 result.
score_reasons.novelty: Rank-one perturbed local inequalities retain signed interactions and exploit averaged rather than worst-case local losses.
score_reasons.depth: Combines a uniform two-spin perturbation calculation with Gaussian comparison, delocalization and local-field concentration.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear model distinctions and concurrent-work comparison; lengthy algebra is explicit and supported by uniform-error explanations.

checked: Traced the rank-one perturbed Bochner argument, averaged two-spin inequalities and the conditional identity converting weighted gradients into a positive local-field correction.

Checked the entire local 3-by-3 quadratic-form argument: normalized product basis, uniform Taylor moment bounds despite possibly extreme external fields, explicit mixed-moment identities, sum-of-squares decomposition and uniform positive definiteness.

Checked the Gaussian comparison/delocalization lemma, lower-tail mass estimate and concentration, plus the conditional-common-Gaussian representation establishing large local fields simultaneously over all spin configurations.

Traced the final two-case coefficient argument and mixing conversion. Recomputed the displayed threshold constants at 80-digit precision: both coefficient bounds exceed 0.000109 and the Bernoulli relative entropy exceeds log 2. This numerical replay is not a formal certificate.
remaining: Classical Gaussian comparison, concentration and random-matrix spectral-edge theorems are external inputs rather than re-proved results.
The improvement beyond 1/2 is stated for zero external field; it should not be advertised as a stronger version of every guarantee in the concurrent arbitrary-field work.

review.summary: Proves an inverse-linear spectral gap and quadratic-time Glauber mixing for the zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model up to inverse temperature 1/2+0.00005, with high probability over the random interaction matrix.
review.prior_frontier: The previous all-start polynomial-mixing threshold was approximately 0.295. Concurrent independent work reaches every fixed beta<1/2 with a stronger modified log-Sobolev guarantee uniformly over external fields; this paper crosses 1/2 for zero field with a spectral-gap guarantee.
review.recommendation: Leading candidate; central mixing proof traced, including the local inequality and threshold constants.

papers.title: Bellman-Ford in Almost-Linear Time
papers.authors: Isaac M Hair, George Z. Li, Jason Li, Junkai Zhang

review.title: Bellman-Ford in Almost-Linear Time
review.authors: Isaac M. Hair, George Z. Li, Jason Li, Junkai Zhang
review.summary: Gives a Las Vegas randomized m^(1+o(1))-time algorithm for single-source shortest paths in directed graphs with arbitrary real edge weights, with high-probability running time. Improves betweenness reduction and adds a shortcut-unfolding invariant to prevent recursive graph densification. The result is in the real-weight arithmetic model, not a bit-complexity bound independent of weight representation.
review.prior_frontier: Previously real negative weights required substantially superlinear bounds, including recent n^(2+o(1)) shortcutting algorithms; near-linear integer-weight results did not resolve this model.

score_reasons.significance: Would bring a classical shortest-path problem to almost-linear time in its general real-weight form.
score_reasons.novelty: The combined uniform betweenness analysis and original-edge charging overcome two distinct shortcutting bottlenecks.
score_reasons.depth: Maintains recursive Steiner-edge invariants under potentials and multiple graph generations.
score_reasons.exposition: Full subroutines are presented, but the invariants and charging proof demand a detailed audit.

checked: Read the uniform-over-potentials betweenness statement and the multiscale slice pruning used to derive total search bounds.
Inspected the clamping and real/auxiliary shortcut-edge definitions.

Traced the stated unfolding/charging mechanism: alternately decrease endpoint generation indices until an original edge is reached, with polylogarithmic hop overhead and charges controlled by historical search counters.
remaining: The 39-page shortest-path algorithm has an inspected unfolding/charging mechanism, but the probabilistic slicing and cross-generation reweighting invariants remain essential unchecked components. The near-linear runtime and Las Vegas certification are a large-proof exception.
The central probabilistic slicing lemma, all Steiner invariants and cross-generation reweighting Lemma 4.21 need full verification.
The complete recursive runtime, negative-cycle handling and Las Vegas certification remain unaudited.

papers.title: Gibbs Sampling in the Shattered Phase by Decoded Quantum Interferometry
papers.authors: Leo Zhou, Noah Shutty, Mark Sellke, Stephen Jordan

review.title: Gibbs Sampling in the Shattered Phase by Decoded Quantum Interferometry
review.authors: Leo Zhou, Noah Shutty, Mark Sellke, Stephen P. Jordan
review.area: Average-case sampling; quantum algorithms; spin glasses
review.summary: For random signed k-uniform XORSAT with fixed large k and average degree D≥k, proves shattering and failure of stable samplers for (1+ε)√(2 log k/D)≤β≤√(k/(2D)), yet gives polynomial-time DQI+USD and classical Prange samplers whenever D tanh β<K*(k), with K*(k)/k→1. At D=3k, β=1/4 both samplers achieve vanishing expected total-variation error while Glauber mixing is exponential. This is not a quantum advantage over all classical algorithms.
review.prior_frontier: Extends shattering-based sampling obstructions to the sparse frustrated model near the predicted dynamical threshold, while showing that algebraic classical and quantum methods escape that obstruction. Prior literature not independently re-audited.

score_reasons.significance: Demonstrates efficient sampling inside a rigorously hard regime for stable methods, clarifying the scope of widely used average-case barriers.
score_reasons.novelty: Connects coherent decoding and a classical random-constraint mixture to exactly the same achievable temperature threshold.
score_reasons.depth: The full result combines Fourier/decoding reductions, sparse random-matrix rank thresholds, planted free-energy analysis, soft overlap gaps and disorder chaos.
score_reasons.exposition: Quantifiers, TV versus Wasserstein error and absence of unrestricted quantum advantage are made explicit.

checked: Fully traced the new Prange sampler argument: expand each Gibbs factor as 1+(e^(2β)−1)1[satisfied]. The exact retained-clause distribution is the Bernoulli(tanh β) proposal tilted by normalized solution count Z̃_S.

Below the full-row-rank threshold, a Chernoff/coupling argument gives Z̃_S=1 with high probability jointly over instance and retained subset. Although exceptional solution counts can be large, E Z̃_S=1 and nonnegativity imply E|Z̃_S−1|=2E(1−Z̃_S)_+=o(1). Jensen controls the normalizing partition function, and bounded convergence controls TV of the tilted law.

Checked USD erasure probability 2√(γ(1−γ)) and the substitution γ=(1−sech β)/2, giving erasure rate tanh β. Gaussian elimination recovers erased coordinates exactly when the retained rows are independent.

Checked the decoding-to-Gibbs postprocessing: sampling a uniformly random preimage of Bx=y preserves Gibbs weights on fibers, and TV contracts. Markov applied to the cited average decoding-error theorem gives the stated √δ/ε exceptional-sign probability.
remaining: The 53-page manuscript’s soft-OGP, shattering, disorder-chaos and stable-algorithm lower-bound proofs remain unaudited.
External random-XORSAT rank threshold and quantum coherent-decoder error theorem are essential cited dependencies, not independently re-proved.
The optimal threshold asymptotics and detailed quantum circuit/resource construction remain to check.

papers.title: Multivariate Resultants: Complexity and Applications to Real Feasibility
papers.authors: Gorav Jindal, Bhargav C S, Himanshu Shukla, Radu Curticapean

review.title: Multivariate Resultants: Complexity and Applications to Real Feasibility
review.authors: C. S. Bhargav, Radu Curticapean, Gorav Jindal, Himanshu Shukla
review.summary: Proves existential real feasibility belongs to the counting hierarchy, using compact coefficient access to resultants, finite critical-point witnesses and short partial Thom encodings. Separately proves polynomial-size quadratic resultant circuits imply VP=VNP, modular evaluation is #P-hard, addressed absolute-value bits are PP-hard, and signs are parity-P-hard even for nonzero sparse symmetric cubic tensor determinants.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the recent complex-feasibility/resultant counting-hierarchy upper bound to real feasibility and substantially strengthens NP-hardness for resultant computation. Tensor determinant is not the general geometric hyperdeterminant, and the paper explicitly does not settle the latter conjecture.

score_reasons.significance: Places a large class of geometric decision problems in a substantially narrower complexity framework and clarifies algebraic hardness of a fundamental invariant.
score_reasons.novelty: Short isolating derivative-sign fingerprints and resultant-sign parity tests avoid writing exponentially long Thom encodings.
score_reasons.depth: Critical-point perturbation, compact coefficient arithmetic at fixed CH levels and independent tensor-coefficient hardness reductions are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Careful distinctions among tensor determinants, geometric hyperdeterminants, unary bit addresses and reduction types.

checked: Verified the isolating-fingerprint halving argument: distinct Thom strings give an isolating list of at most ceil(log2 D) coordinates for some root.
Checked the sign-conjunction polynomial: rational sign error 1/(4s), squared discrepancies separate <=1/16 from >=9/16, positive denominator preserves the sign of 2E-1.
Traced the parity acceptance and universal projection quantifiers, including zero/constant/squarefree cases and why all indices remain polynomial length.
remaining: Large-proof exception (49 pages). The isolating fingerprint, sign-conjunction rational transformation and projection/parity quantifiers were checked. Fixed-level CH arithmetic and the particular resultant/critical-point dependencies used here need verification; the parent review of a different AGS application does not establish them.

Audit the fixed-level CH arithmetic closure and Andrews-Garg-Schost dependency, critical-point finite witness construction, derivative separation and rational approximants, and all algebraic/modular/sign hardness reductions.

review.title: Nearly Optimal Polynomial Time Transformation from Non-private to Private Correlation Clustering
review.authors: Alma Ghafari, Mina Dalirooyfard, Slobodan Mitrović

score_reasons.significance: Closes a substantial tradeoff between multiplicative quality and additive privacy error for a standard clustering problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Privately releases sparse disagreements from a coarse clustering, then projects in a semidefinite residual norm before rounding.
score_reasons.depth: Effective synthesis of sparse cut release, Grothendieck relaxation, variance-aware rounding and adaptive privacy composition.
score_reasons.exposition: The full proof is accessible and explicit; minor notation and editing blemishes do not obstruct its central argument.

checked: Checked residual truncation sensitivity: changing one input edge changes at most two retained pairs for fixed public cap and reference clustering; group privacy and adaptive composition fit the allocated budget.
Checked the clustering-cost bound by the SDP norm, feasibility of the truncated input for projection, explicit dual SDP and additive optimization tolerance.
Checked variance at most the residual cap, Bernstein/Jensen control uniformly over all partitions, the expected cap estimate, and absorption of the square-root OPT term into eta OPT.

Verified the sparse weighted cut-release dependency in the original Elias–Kapralov–Kulkarni–Lee theorem, including a public total-mass bound, expected error and unordered-edge l1 adjacency. Its guarantee suffices for the slightly weaker epsilon dependence used here.
remaining: The coarse private clustering and sparse cut-release algorithms are external results, not re-proved here. The stated transformation is for unweighted graphs and edge privacy, with expected utility.
Polynomial-time SDP claims use the manuscript's usual finite-precision and boundedness assumptions. The headline instantiated factor inherits the chosen nonprivate algorithm's guarantee.

sources.detail: Original sparse private graph-release theorem 1.1 and weighted adjacency definition 3.2 verified.

review.summary: Transforms any constant-factor rho approximation for unweighted correlation clustering into an edge-private polynomial-time algorithm with expected cost at most (rho+eta)OPT plus a nearly linear additive term O-tilde(n/(eta epsilon^2)).
review.prior_frontier: Near-linear additive-error private algorithms had a very large constant approximation factor, while black-box transfers preserving a good multiplicative factor paid roughly n^(3/2) additive error. This combines near-linear additive error with essentially any available nonprivate constant factor.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate; the full new transformation and privacy argument have been traced.

papers.title: New Lower and Upper Bounds for the Grothendieck Constant
papers.authors: Rahul Saha, Alan Li, Anton Xue, Swarat Chaudhuri, Adam Klivans, Pravesh K. Kothari, Raghu Meka

review.title: New Lower and Upper Bounds for the Grothendieck Constant
review.authors: Rahul Saha, Alan Li, Anton Xue, Swarat Chaudhuri, Adam Klivans, Pravesh K. Kothari, Raghu Meka
review.summary: Claims new bounds 6π/11≤KG≤π/(2 log(1+√2))−3.47×10⁻⁴ for the real Grothendieck constant. The lower bound follows from a universal affine constraint on Krivine correlation coefficients plus asymptotic optimality of mixed Krivine schemes; the upper bound uses a high-dimensional cubic–quintic limiting scheme and rigorous numerical certification.
review.prior_frontier: Raises the lower bound from about 1.6769 (with tiny recent improvements) to about 1.7136, and improves recent explicit upper-bound savings of order 10⁻⁵. These concern the real bilinear SDP integrality gap, not the complex constant.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial advance on a classical constant spanning analysis and approximation algorithms.
score_reasons.novelty: Lower bounds through limitations of all Krivine schemes and an asymptotic-dimensional upper construction are distinctive.
score_reasons.depth: Combines Hermite variational inequalities, analytic inverse majorants and interval certificates.
score_reasons.exposition: The conceptual structure is clear, but both branches have significant analytic and computational dependencies.

checked: Read the agreement/disagreement substitution and rotation reducing the linear agreement direction to one Gaussian coordinate.
Inspected the constrained one-dimensional cubic rearrangement and the final high-range scalar inequality used for b₃≥2b₁−11/6.
Read the inverse-majorant certification criterion and how finite-dimensional schemes are recovered from a strict limiting certificate.
remaining: The 66-page Grothendieck result has inspected Gaussian rearrangement and scalar lower-bound steps. Its disagreement/fiber argument and numerical inverse-majorant certificates remain unchecked; this is a large-proof/certificate exception, not numerical verification.
The disagreement/fiber inequality, the full affine constraint and its translation using Naor–Regev optimality need a complete audit.
The upper correlation computation, tail enclosure and both sets of interval-arithmetic certificates have not been independently rerun.

review.title: Efficient Agnostic Learning of Tensor Network States
review.authors: Matthias C. Caro, Natalie McHugh, Sergii Strelchuk
review.summary: Improper agnostic tomography of arbitrary mixed inputs relative to tensor networks on a known bounded-degree tree, jointly polynomial in n,d,χ,1/ε,log(1/δ), with output bond dimension O(dn²χ/ε²). General known contraction-width-C graphs have costs polynomial in χ^C; the output may be a dependency-tree network rather than the original graph. Guarantees overlap OPT−ε, not estimation of OPT or proper learning.
review.prior_frontier: Extends efficient agnostic MPS reconstruction to bounded-degree trees and graph contraction hierarchies; contrasts with prior proper TTN learners whose exponents depend on parameters. Prior comparisons not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Substantially enlarges the structured quantum states that admit efficient robust learning with both copy and computational guarantees.
score_reasons.novelty: Laminar compression controls the reference state’s Schmidt ranks without imposing low rank on the unknown mixed input.
score_reasons.depth: A sharper projection estimate and postselection-overlap invariant feed into graph-width and tomography complexity bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states improper output, supplied graph structure, overlap objective and collective-copy access.

checked: Traced Lemma 3.1: discarded Schmidt-rank-r vector has quadratic mass at most rη using PSD entrywise Cauchy–Schwarz; a second PSD Cauchy–Schwarz converts this to overlap loss ≤2√(rη).
Checked top-eigenspace truncation from a noisy state: Weyl and λ_(Λ+1)≤tr σ/(Λ+1) give discarded operator norm ≤1/(Λ+1)+2γ.

Traced the laminar rank invariant: each earlier operation lies wholly inside or outside the current graph cut, so cannot increase Schmidt rank, and already projected coordinates are removable product factors.

Traced Proposition 3.5: per-step overlap loss is below α with Λ≥64r/α² and γ=α²/(128r); choosing α=min(ε,ϑ)/(4L) maintains postselection success ≥ϑ/2. Collected commuting projections make K†K a projector, and the final top eigenvector loses at most 2γ_fin.
Checked removal of the overlap promise by running the bounded-budget algorithm at ϑ=ε: if OPT<ε every normalized output already meets the target.
remaining: Remaining 77-page proof package: subnormalized tomography budgets and gate complexity, precise tree/contraction-width construction, explicit output tensors and all stated dimension/copy exponents.
Realisable tomography and cutwidth/tree-cutwidth representation theorems remain unaudited.

review.title: On Zeros and Algorithms for Disordered Systems II: The Antiferromagnetic Ising Model up to Kesten–Stigum
review.authors: Ferenc Bencs, Brice Huang, Daniel Z. Lee, Kuikui Liu, Guus Regts
review.area: Approximate counting / random graphs and spin systems
review.summary: For fixed d>=3 and fixed delta>0, deterministically estimates the zero-field antiferromagnetic Ising partition function on a uniformly random d-regular graph in (n/epsilon)^C(d,delta) time, with high probability over the graph, for beta<=(1-delta) beta_KS(d), beta_KS=2 arctanh(1/sqrt(d-1)). Proves high-probability zero-freeness in a constant-width complex strip. Does not supply a sampling algorithm or efficiently testable success certificate.
review.prior_frontier: Reaches the entire fixed-slack replica-symmetric regime beyond prior constant-fraction-of-Kesten-Stigum algorithms; excludes the exact threshold and growing-degree/slack uniformity.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the predicted counting regime for a central average-case statistical physics model.
score_reasons.novelty: Cycle-count reweighting and truncated overlap moments repair both constant fluctuations and exponentially large rare-event second moments.
score_reasons.depth: Complex saddle-point estimates, planted-model overlap control and analytic zero counting span a long proof with delicate uniform parameters.
score_reasons.exposition: Precisely distinguishes deterministic computation from random-input success and explicitly warns counting does not self-reduce to sampling here.

checked: Traced the Jensen zero-count reduction for the analytic normalized/reweighted partition function with f(0)=1.
Checked transfer of real rare-overlap bounds to complex beta via absolute-value domination and a lower bound on the complex first moment.
Traced the Holder truncation bound: constant higher moments of the reweighting factor and sufficiently small exponent absorb exponential deterministic partition-function bounds.
remaining: Large-proof exception (98 pages). The analytic zero-count reduction, complex absolute-value transfer and Holder truncation were traced. The complex moments, planted-overlap rare-event estimates and uniform zero-free strip are substantial independent arguments that remain unaudited.
Audit complex first and reweighted second moment asymptotics, quantitative planted overlap/truncation proof, short-cycle factor moments, uniformity of the strip, and interpolation implementation.

review.title: A Complete Characterization of Eventually Evasive Binary Patterns
review.authors: Simone Faro, Francesco Pio Marino, Arianna Pavone

score_reasons.significance: Completes a longstanding qualitative classification in a foundational string-query problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Connects special homometric rigidity to cyclotomic factor inversion and a primitive Wronskian, extending the established algebraic recurrence approach.
score_reasons.depth: Substantial geometric case analysis and algebraic-number-theoretic control of recurrence cancellation.
score_reasons.exposition: The main line is clear and limitations are unusually explicit; appendix bookkeeping is detailed, while novelty qualification remains conservative.

checked: Checked the signed occurrence enumerator by inclusion-exclusion, full autocorrelation norm, and the reduction from recurrence nonvanishing to decision-tree depth.
Traced the full geometric rigidity proof: large initial gap, completion of an existing grid, residue-class restrictions, the uniform long-pair obstruction and separate k=2 and k=3 counting cases.
Checked norm saturation over Galois fields, uniqueness and descent of the non-reciprocal factor, the primitive Wronskian argument and isolation from root-of-unity rotations.
Checked the Skolem–Mahler–Lech reduction using an isolated simple root, monotonicity in text length and application of the HHS upper bound. Verified that upper bound directly in HHS Lemma 8.
remaining: The proof gives no effective general bound for the eventual threshold. It does not determine exact complexity at all finite lengths or the full c=p case.
The independent stronger torsion-profile appendix was not fully audited. Fine–Wilf and Skolem–Mahler–Lech are external standard inputs.

The manuscript itself asks for further historical comparison of its geometric and factorization ingredients. The limited primary-source check supports the stated 2018 comparison but is not an exhaustive priority search.

sources.detail: HHS 2018 primary paper, Lemma 8 and preceding almost-all-pattern frontier.

review.summary: Characterizes eventual evasiveness of every binary pattern. If the gcd c of all periods is smaller than the shortest period p, its deterministic query complexity on sufficiently long texts is exactly n−(n mod c); nonunary patterns are eventually evasive exactly when c=1.
review.prior_frontier: He, Huang and Sun settled the query complexity for all but a negligible fraction of patterns in 2018 and supplied the matching universal upper bound. This addresses the remaining eventual classification, not exact complexity at every finite text length.
review.recommendation: Leading candidate; central classification proof traced, with an ineffective eventual threshold and historical-priority qualification.

review.title: Multiplicative and Additive Extractors for Low Entropy Samplable Sources Under Reduced Assumptions
review.authors: Marshall Ball, Eshan Chattopadhyay, Mohit Gurumukhani, Ronen Shaltiel, Yunya Zhao
review.summary: Under exponential nondeterministic-circuit hardness for E, constructs seedless extractors for polynomial-size samplable sources: one bit at constant error from O(log n) entropy, and almost all entropy with polynomially small error from n^α entropy for any fixed α>0, including a multiplicative guarantee. Under Σ₂-circuit hardness, obtains almost-all extraction at polylogarithmic entropy. The constructions extend to samplers with nondeterministic postselection.
review.prior_frontier: Reduces high polynomial-hierarchy hardness assumptions and near-full entropy thresholds for many-bit extraction; the one-bit logarithmic-entropy result matches a recent result under an incomparable assumption.

score_reasons.significance: Substantially improves conditional extraction parameters in a general source model.
score_reasons.novelty: Introduces robust errorless block condensation and correlation breaking against small circuits.
score_reasons.depth: A long composition of reconstruction, low-degree/list-recovery, counting and condenser machinery.
score_reasons.exposition: Precisely separates assumptions and output/error regimes, though the 106-page proof is extensive.

checked: Traced polynomial pinning and nondeterministic local correction: agreement on sufficiently many line points yields a unique answer, and hardwired repetitions cover all target points.
Read the robust-condenser correction that tests validity using the original samplable joint distribution rather than an inaccessible good mixture component.
Checked how the mixture mass and a Goldwasser–Sipser mass threshold give a recognizable superset of good y-values while preserving conditional entropy requirements.
remaining: The robust condenser completeness/soundness parameter chain and all output amplification remain unaudited.
The correlation breaker and many-bit low-entropy construction, and external counting/list-recovery dependencies, require substantial further checking.

review.title: Should We Combine Our Data? Algorithms and Limits for Privately Assessing Data Sharing
review.authors: Mahdi Haghifam, Kumar Kshitij Patel, Avrim Blum, Giulia Fanti, Juba Ziani
review.summary: Tests whether two sensitive datasets are jointly realizable versus have at least t unavoidable errors under information-theoretic pure two-party DP. For finite-domain thresholds, near-optimal t is soft-Θ(log log m/ε); for homogeneous halfspaces the domain dependence rises to log m, with upper O(d² log m(d+log log m)/ε) and lower Ω(d log(m/d)/ε) in the sufficiently-large-data regime.
review.prior_frontier: A trusted curator needs only O(1/ε) resolution; private threshold learning needs Ω(log m/ε) samples. This is a testing/compatibility guarantee, not a certificate that sharing improves prediction. Prior results read through cited comparisons.

score_reasons.significance: Establishes a sharp testing-versus-learning and interactive-versus-one-way separation for a natural private data-compatibility task.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses private prefix comparison for thresholds and geometric cutting planes/containers for halfspaces.
score_reasons.depth: Combines information-complexity reductions, robust coding and interactive privacy accounting.
score_reasons.exposition: The empirical-loss objective and worst-case full-domain privacy are clear, although the motivating notion of benefit is broader than the theorem.

checked: Traced the threshold lower-bound encoding: pad Alice with negative minima and Bob with positive maxima, each with t copies of an encoded point. The joint optimum is zero for i<j and exactly t for i≥j.
Group privacy bounds internal information by O(εt), while the cited greater-than distribution requires Ω(log log m), yielding the resolution lower bound at arbitrary dataset size n≥t.
Checked why arbitrary interaction is allowed in this lower bound and why the separate one-way information argument strengthens log log m to log m.
remaining: Interactive prefix-search correctness and privacy composition remain unaudited.
Halfspace coding lower bounds, dual cutting-plane algorithm and computational dependence on dimension remain to check.
Essential greater-than information-complexity lower bound is cited, not independently reproved.

review.title: Optimal Sub-Gaussian Mean Estimation in Low Dimensions
review.authors: Jasper C. H. Lee, Suraj Mathashery, Paul Valiant, Kun Wang
review.summary: Claims a polynomial-time scale/shift/rotation-equivariant estimator for arbitrary finite unknown covariance achieving (1+o(1))*sqrt(2||Sigma||op log(1/delta)/n) Euclidean error in constant or slowly growing dimension, with o(1) uniform over the distribution when log(1/delta)/n and d^2 loglog(1/delta)/log(1/delta) tend to zero. Uses an SDP trimming rule and a computer-assisted quantified inequality.
review.prior_frontier: Closes the sharp-constant low-dimensional gap left after one-dimensional optimal mean estimation; does not claim the same sharp formula uniformly in arbitrary high dimension.

score_reasons.significance: Sharp Gaussian-optimal constants under only finite covariance would resolve a fundamental multivariate statistical problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Data-dependent quadratic trimming with a KKT maximal-variance condition avoids the loss from intersecting one-dimensional confidence strips.
score_reasons.depth: The custom Chernoff certificate, two levels of nets and multi-regime quantified inequality are deep and extensive.
score_reasons.exposition: The obstacle examples motivate the optimization, but the stated exact binary-search algorithm has an unhandled degenerate-input case.

checked: Traced the moment-generating-function upper bound from a pointwise quadratic majorant and E[XX^T] bounded by a multiple of identity.
Read the KKT derivation of the trimming form min(1,x^T A x) and maximal empirical variance along positive eigendirections.
Checked the claimed algorithm on an all-zero input: alpha_max=0, every optimization gives w=0, so the required positive total trimming (1/3)log(1/delta) cannot be attained.
remaining: Resolve the explicit degenerate-input/output branch and finite-precision termination requirements; then audit SDP dual attainment, the quantified inequality certificates, tail/net arguments and all constant/dimension dependence.
issues: Algorithm 2 p9 is undefined on all-zero centered data: alpha_max=0 and the unique minimizer w=0 cannot attain positive target trimming. Lemma 3 claims every sample set. A special output branch may repair the estimator, but it is not specified in the inspected algorithm or proof; this is not a refutation of the broader sharp-constant statistical possibility.

review.title: A Constant-Factor Approximation for Capacitated Facility Location with Outliers
review.authors: Rajni Dabas

score_reasons.significance: Extends constant approximation to the substantially more general arbitrary-cost outlier setting while preserving both feasibility constraints.
score_reasons.novelty: The signed rejection-count comparison and warm-start penalty relation yield a sharper quota-recovery bound than ordinary penalty approximation.
score_reasons.depth: Careful extension of exchange-forest accounting, capacity-preserving matching merges and polynomial local-search certificates.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly isolates the genuinely additional signed guarantee and supplies implementable searches and parameter choices.

checked: Checked the assignment-path decomposition, nonnegative rejection remainder, feasible fractional savings and single-improvement close averaging. The sign of the negative savings is retained correctly when padding target uses to five.

Compared the up/down exchange-forest construction with Bansal–Garg–Gupta Sections 4–5. Traced the disposal-leaf extension, nonpositive remainders, five-use/two-quantity bounds and twice-per-edge charging without treating rejection as a metric point.
Checked the integral matching-path merge, grouped opening-charge bound, maximum-opening-cost guess and warm-start envelope yielding 12/11 times the factor-five signed comparison.

Checked the objective-scale and penalty grids, zero-cost case, telescoping bound on accepted changes, and flow/knapsack dynamic programs implementing all certificate searches in polynomial time for explicit unit-demand clients.
remaining: The result is metric and uses explicitly represented unit-demand clients; it is not a strongly polynomial or succinct-demand guarantee.

The earlier exchange-forest technique and minimum-cost-flow integrality are external foundations; the review checked the construction's use and modifications rather than re-proving all prior facility-location results.

sources.detail: Bansal–Garg–Gupta exchange-forest construction, Sections 4–5 checked against the claimed adaptation.

review.summary: Gives a deterministic (60/11+epsilon)-approximation for metric capacitated facility location with outliers, arbitrary opening costs and nonuniform hard capacities, respecting both capacities and the outlier budget.
review.prior_frontier: Exact-feasible outlier guarantees relied on uniform opening costs, with a recent (3+epsilon) result in that restricted setting. Ordinary capacitated facility location without outliers has factor 5+epsilon; this handles arbitrary opening costs and outliers at about 5.455.

review.title: Bipartite Matching is in NC
review.authors: Abhranil Chatterjee, Sumanta Ghosh, Rohit Gurjar, Roshan Raj, Thomas Thierauf
review.summary: Claims deterministic NC algorithms for bipartite matching, weighted linear matroid intersection and noncommutative rank. The weighted matching theorem explicitly assumes polynomially bounded edge weights; search is obtained through weighted-decision reductions. The construction replaces graph entries by folded Vandermonde blocks and encodes weight through polynomial degrees.
review.prior_frontier: Improves deterministic bipartite matching from quasi-NC to NC, a classic parallel derandomization boundary; it does not claim the same for arbitrary nonbipartite matching.

score_reasons.significance: A major claimed resolution with broad algebraic and parallel consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses strong subspace-design root bounds to create an explicit rank certificate for Hall obstructions.
score_reasons.depth: The weighted-degree argument, search reduction and matroid/rank extensions add considerable depth beyond decision.
score_reasons.exposition: Gives explicit block matrices and parameter inequalities; the extension proofs are substantial.

checked: Traced the unweighted block-rank argument: Hall deficiency yields too few supported columns; conversely private folded roots force the nonzero dependency polynomials to be independent, and additional graph-column roots give a Hall-deficient support.
Checked the parameter inequalities δ≥n and r>n²δ in this reduction.
Read the weighted matrix setup and its larger r>4n³δW requirement, which explains the polynomially bounded weight restriction.
remaining: The 61-page NC matching result has a traced unweighted block-rank reduction conditional on the folded-Wronskian root theorem. The root theorem, deterministic field implementation and weighted/search extensions remain substantial unchecked parts; this is a large-proof exception.
The folded-Wronskian root theorem and field/bit-complexity implementation need independent verification.
The weighted determinant-degree approximation, NC search reduction, linear matroid intersection and noncommutative rank proofs are not fully audited.

review.title: A Near-Logarithmic Approximation for All-or-Nothing Multicommodity Flow
review.authors: Zijian Zeng, Jiayin Cao, Weinan Dai, Rui Wang, Yuhao Liao
review.summary: Claims polynomial-time log^(1+o(1)) k approximation and LP integrality-gap upper bound for unit-capacity undirected all-or-nothing multicommodity flow, with congestion exactly one and splittable commodity flows. Weighted profits retain a log^(2+o(1)) k bound; the result is not edge-disjoint paths.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the cited O(log²k) bound and resolves a Bansal–Jambulapati–Saranurak conjecture, using their integral-node-weight flow-expander decomposition. The full dependency and congestion-one rounding still need checking.

score_reasons.significance: Near-logarithmic approximation for a longstanding multicommodity routing problem is a substantial advance, with a guarantee against the natural LP.
score_reasons.novelty: A fixed discretized weighting allows one flow-expander decomposition, bypassing weight changes during recursive well-linked decomposition.
score_reasons.depth: The novel decomposition is short; exact-congestion rounding and handling nonuniform paired weights contain the main remaining technical burden.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully distinguishes splittable flow, profit weights, dependence on k rather than n, and prior rounding provenance.

checked: Fully traced the new decomposition conditional on the stated expander theorem: take ε=F/(2k), d_i=floor(x_i/ε), K≤2k and εK≥F/4; total endpoint weight is 2K≤4k.
The calibrated call obtains |C|≤εK/4 and ϕ≥ε/(16Γ(2K)). Separated pairs consume at least εΣd_i cut capacity, so at least 3K/4 of integral pair weight survives.
Restricting a flow-expanding node weighting to surviving endpoints gives product-demand flow-linkedness by scaling; paired weights satisfy π_i≤1/8, and total surviving weight is ≥3F/(128Γ(4k)).

Checked composition across vertex-disjoint pieces and the final 3LP/(2^26 Γ(4k)) bound, conditional on the stated paired-weight rounding. Shared/coincident endpoints can be normalized by distinct degree-one leaves without changing LP or routable subsets.
remaining: The exact-congestion-one clustering/rounding proof and its nonuniform copying reduction remain unaudited.
The precise integral-weight expander-decomposition theorem, its permitted zero weights and overhead parameters are essential external dependencies still to verify.
No independent audit of the competing/current prior frontier beyond manuscript sources.

Checked conversion of the left sub-eigenvector inequality into a uniform hitting-time tail, including minimum weight and accumulated coupling error.
Traced one-step and multistep logarithmic tracking, shrinking per-step tolerances, exponentially growing sample concentration and the bound excluding accidental folding.

review.title: Optimal Approximation Algorithms For Satisfiable Ordering CSPs
review.authors: Yury Makarychev
review.summary: For every fixed finite ordering constraint language, characterizes the polynomial-time approximation threshold on completely satisfiable instances via transformations of solutions to both canonical left and right relaxations. The algorithm is unconditional; matching perfect-completeness hardness assumes the Rich 2-to-1 Games Conjecture. In particular it matches the 1/2 algorithm for satisfiable Betweenness.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the author’s one-order framework to two orders and supplies hardness previously unavailable even for satisfiable Betweenness. The required richness condition is stronger than the ordinary 2-to-1 conjecture.

score_reasons.significance: A general approximation classification on satisfiable ordering problems.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses two-order transformations and a sequence of relaxation-gap transfers preserving perfect completeness.
score_reasons.depth: Requires permuton classification, LP-to-SDP completion and multi-slice/Gaussian soundness.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes the unconditional framework from its stronger conjectural hardness assumption.

checked: Read the IDU-plus transformation family and exact threshold statement.
Checked the local covariance completion lemma: linear scopes prevent overlapping off-diagonal corrections and degree D bounds total private covariance loss by ηD.
Traced how this preserves local distributions, hence perfect-completeness structure, rather than merely producing an approximate covariance matrix.
remaining: The increasing-embedding construction supplying the private covariance, two-order classification and gap constructions need full checking.
The Rich 2-to-1 reduction, multi-slice invariance and Gaussian collision bounds remain unaudited.

papers.title: Smoothed Analysis for Distributed MIS
papers.authors: Dipan Dey, Fabien Dufoulon, William K. Moses Jr., Gopal Pandurangan

review.title: Smoothed Analysis for Distributed MIS
review.authors: Dipan Dey, Fabien Dufoulon, William K. Moses Jr., Gopal Pandurangan
review.summary: For every base graph, edge-flip smoothing p=β log n/n with sufficiently large constant β permits randomized LOCAL MIS in O(√log n) rounds with high probability. For p≤(1/2−δ)log n/n, some base graph still requires Ω(log n/log log n) rounds. Upper algorithm sees only the smoothed graph; the lower bound even permits identifying the noise edges.
review.prior_frontier: Contrasts with worst-case almost-logarithmic LOCAL lower bounds and O(log n) classical algorithms; identifies the smoothing scale up to constants. Prior lower-bound dependencies not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Quantifies when a basic distributed symmetry-breaking problem escapes worst-case hardness under small random perturbations.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines low-degree MIS, isolated low-degree helpers and gathering through the whole smoothed graph.
score_reasons.depth: Main work is controlling dependence between helper selection and random shortcut structure, plus a smoothing-robust lower-bound reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Model distinctions and success-probability dependence of β are explicit; introductory discussion is considerably longer than necessary.

checked: Checked algorithm assembly: isolated candidates form an independent helper set; complete-component gathering yields consistent component MIS choices; the remaining low-degree graph has degree exp(O(√log n)), so the cited degree-sensitive MIS algorithm finishes in O(√log n) rounds.

Traced Case (2a): either a base-high vertex already lies within distance two of the large low-degree neighborhood Z_Q, or B_0|Z_Q| distinct absent base edges independently offer such a connection. Failure ≤exp(−λB_0|Z_Q|/n)≤exp(−λ√B_0); union bounds do not condition on the degree event and preserve independence.
Checked threshold t=min(B_0,floor(n/(16Mk))) meets exp(.49√log n)≤t≤B_0 when M<n/√B_0, enabling the stated diameter lemma.
remaining: Full large-neighborhood diameter lemma, sparse-helper Case (2b) and their dependency handling remain unaudited.
Symmetric-difference extension and all smoothing lower-bound simulation arguments remain to check; this is not a complete proof audit.

papers.title: Asymptotically Good Quantum Locally Testable Codes
papers.authors: William Gay, Fernando Jeronimo

review.title: Asymptotically Good Quantum Locally Testable Codes
review.authors: William Gay, Fernando Granha Jeronimo
review.summary: Constructs polynomial-time explicit binary CSS quantum LDPC families with constant rate, constant relative distance, bounded check/qubit degrees and constant all-state local-test soundness H >= (sigma/N)D_Q. Instantiates a cubical cosheaf framework using arithmetic tree-product quotients, Frobenius-twisted equivariant Reed-Solomon codes and uniform product expansion on distinct norm-one grids.
review.prior_frontier: Claims unconditional good qLTCs, alongside a separately acknowledged subsequent unconditional construction and two conditional approaches. The key Reed-Solomon expansion constant is independent of local lengths; equal evaluation grids are explicitly excluded.

score_reasons.significance: Would resolve a foundational quantum coding existence problem with explicit qubit codes and full soundness.
score_reasons.novelty: Twisted endpoint representations enable positive rate while distinct norm-one grids and Frobenius rigidity provide length-uniform product expansion.
score_reasons.depth: Combines arithmetic lattices, polynomial interpolation/rank arguments, two-sided homological expansion and binary/all-state conversion.
score_reasons.exposition: Makes constant-selection order and compatibility assumptions explicit, and separates the transpose-sector transfer from the local expansion theorem.

checked: Verified the bounded chain-homotopy transfer: nontrivial cohomology distance loses M, and soundness loses M^2/alpha+M via y=psi(z)+d h x.
Traced the finite perturbation contraction identity with S=(I+delta h)^-1 and nilpotence of delta h, in characteristic two.
Checked horizontal cube contraction and vertical exact-star contraction give bounded finite sums when t and local degrees are fixed.
Read why small-syndrome cocycles can be greedily repaired after local-minimality distance, with one bounded-star correction per syndrome-weight decrease.

Traced the complete new unequal-grid interpolation argument (PDF pp.43–51): degree-preserving linear Noether normalization, isolated-zero divided-difference separators, Frobenius restriction-rank upper bound, generic-fiber remainder lower bound, and the two-component intersection estimate. Checked the key invariant-variety claim by the two tower-degree calculations: distinct q_i contradict a minimal dependence among nonconstant coordinates. In the interpolation contradiction, minimal dependent rows exclude isolated points and coordinate flats, representatives by grid trace keep Y+ and Y- without common components, and the degree recurrence gives the claimed strict N<N contradiction.

Traced the product-expansion conversion (pp.52–55): descending lexicographic monomial profile in the internal-line extension lemma, duality giving inner generation on closed support, tensor-Vandermonde closure size, and counting nonzero parallel lines. The same closed support works for all coefficient coordinates, so collective expansion has no coefficient-dimension loss. Checked independent primal/dual choices via the norm-one RS dual formula and monomial transformations. The constant depends on t,tau,epsilon rather than q_i; the unequal-grid hypothesis is essential.

Checked the binary and all-state conversion (pp.34–36): trace-dual bases make transpose commute with binary expansion; block-weight comparisons preserve both syndrome inequalities; orthogonal Pauli syndrome spaces diagonalize both testing Hamiltonian and quantum distance. Also checked the order of constant selection and positive-rate arithmetic on p.61: rho and lambda_0 are fixed before q_1 grows, and Gamma_k>=1/2 follows with beta=2^(-2t-2).
remaining: Large-proof exception: the 66-page construction combines several substantial independent arguments. The local filling/face-walk recursion and small-support expansion in Sections6–8, arithmetic quotient connectivity and Ramanujan spectrum in Section11 including their cited deep theorems, equivariant Frobenius endpoint compatibility and efficient enumeration in Section14, and the comparison-complex rate lemma were not completely audited. These are essential remaining obligations for the unconditional good-qLTC conclusion; the checked interpolation and conversion do not by themselves verify the whole construction.

papers.title: Non-manipulability and Approachability Beyond Two-Player Games
papers.authors: Natalie Collina, Elijah Fullerton, Jingyi Liu, S. Matthew Weinberg

review.title: Non-manipulability and Approachability Beyond Two-Player Games
review.authors: Natalie Collina, Elijah Fullerton, Jingyi Liu, S. Matthew Weinberg

score_reasons.significance: Extends a basic strategic-robustness guarantee and approachability theory beyond the two-player setting.
score_reasons.novelty: Auxiliary-game equilibria generate product halfspace responses; nearby static distributions encode desired Nash responses for menu completion.
score_reasons.depth: Combines geometric approachability, compactness-based menu construction, a reduction from approximate Nash and bandit monitoring of defection.
score_reasons.exposition: The final appendix carefully distinguishes fixed-game asymptotics, horizon awareness, information requirements and algorithmic hardness, though the full construction is long.

checked: Checked auxiliary Nash equilibria supply a product learner action and target point with nonpositive discrepancy inner product; the quadratic potential gives the stated fresh-run approachability rate.

Traced static menu completion: approximate Nash-response codebook, distinct frequency labels, empirical commitment test, pathwise containment, uniform static attainability and the one-action degenerate case.

Checked the exploitability payoff reduction, zero coarse-correlated benchmark, random-round extraction and amplification; hardness requires polynomial convergence as well as polynomial work per round.

Checked necessity and sufficiency of the product halfspace condition and both examples separating response satisfiability. Traced the importance-weighted defection monitor, stopping-time concentration and its composition with the stated bandit swap-regret fallback.
remaining: The construction is horizon-aware and information-theoretic for each fixed finite game. Compactness gives no game-uniform convergence modulus; the completed/monitored protocol does not retain the fresh-run O(T^-1/2) rate.

The optimizer observes current mixed strategies but not fresh action samples. Learners know learner utilities and share deterministic conventions and public optimizer history; they do not share random samples.
The fallback uses the external Blum–Mansour Exp3 inequality. The audit checked its stated use, martingale conversion and switching argument, rather than re-proving that prior bandit theorem.

review.area: Algorithmic game theory and online learning
review.summary: Constructs independent multi-learner algorithms with individual no-swap regret and joint non-manipulability, characterizes jointly approachable convex sets by a product-strategy halfspace condition, and proves a Nash-computation barrier to efficient uniform guarantees.
review.prior_frontier: For one learner, no-swap regret captures non-manipulable no-regret behavior. Multiple independent learners cannot implement arbitrary correlated one-round responses, so the classical two-player response condition and individual swap-regret guarantees alone are insufficient.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate; central construction, characterization and hardness reduction traced with important model and rate qualifications.

papers.title: Existence of the Core in Approval-Based Committee Elections
papers.authors: Patrick Becker, Matthias Greger, Dominik Peters

review.title: Existence of the Core in Approval-Based Committee Elections
review.authors: Patrick Becker, Matthias Greger, Dominik Peters
review.summary: Proves that every approval-based committee election has a core-stable committee, in fact one robust to the paper’s fractional core+ deviations, and gives a polynomial-time algorithm for finding one at the Hare quota. Uses a harmonic-entropy payment objective and approximate single-candidate local optimality. Computing its global optimum is a distinct, harder problem.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves general exact core existence and computation beyond earlier constant-factor approximations and restricted election classes.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a central exact existence question with an efficient construction.
score_reasons.novelty: The harmonic entropy has exactly the marginal identity needed for addition and deletion under payment caps.
score_reasons.depth: A substantive but self-contained combination of majorization, exchange arguments and truncated LP optimization.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions, strict inequalities and algorithmic precision are handled explicitly.

checked: Checked the water-level identities, repeated Robin Hood operator, eventual uniformity, series representation and uniform tail bound (d−1)/L. Convex water levels imply continuous concave harmonic entropy.
Checked candidate addition: Robin Hood transfers supply reserve-sized gain, and mixing with the old system enforces the new candidate’s quota while preserving that gain.

Checked the minimum-reserve optimal payment choice and continuous de-reserving construction in Lemma 6.4. An unsaturated candidate remains a maximal payment for each supporter; reversing one Robin Hood step gives the exact entropy deletion cost.
Checked the add/delete exchange: a P3 violation forces a swap gain at least δ=q−n/(k+1)>0, so a sufficiently local optimum has all four payment properties.
Checked directly that those payments exclude fractional core+ deviations by summing voter lower bounds and candidate quota upper bounds; at least one outside candidate gives the strict contradiction.
Checked the polynomial LP for truncated entropy, 0≤V−V_L≤nk/L, swap threshold δ/2 and termination count. For Hare q=n/k, inverse δ is polynomially bounded.
remaining: The main existence and polynomial-time Hare-quota construction are checked; this is not formal verification or a numerical implementation.
Separate Droop-boundary refinements, Pareto/priceability comparisons, exact objective computation and NP-completeness claims were not fully audited.

papers.authors: Yury Makarychev

review.title: Approximation Algorithms for Satisfiable Phylogenetic CSPs
review.authors: Yury Makarychev
review.area: Approximation algorithms; infinite-domain CSPs; model theory
review.summary: Gives nontrivial approximation guarantees for 13 NP-hard arity-four phylogenetic predicates on completely satisfiable instances. A canonical tractable relaxation followed by finite mixtures of basic tree transformations approximates the best guarantee within this framework to arbitrary accuracy. Does not claim optimal approximation over all algorithms or extend to nearly satisfiable instances.
review.prior_frontier: Prior UGC resistance applies even to nearly satisfiable phylogenetic CSPs; the new exact-satisfiability regime permits beating the predicate-dependent trivial guarantee. Prior classifications used as external dependencies.

score_reasons.significance: Opens a distinct approximation regime for phylogenetic constraints despite strong near-satisfiability resistance.
score_reasons.novelty: Classifies invariant random tree/order structures to prove completeness of a concrete finite-mixture rounding family.
score_reasons.depth: Combines amenability, Fraïssé-limit structure, coupled branchpoint orders and convex-geometric mixture reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Concrete four-leaf examples clarify an otherwise substantial model-theoretic proof package.

checked: Checked the first explicit rounding example: independently partition leaves into two groups; x3,x4 together and x1 opposite has probability 1/4 and guarantees one of the original two patterns regardless of x2, exceeding the stated trivial 4/21 benchmark conditional on that benchmark.

Checked the canonical relaxation construction as the conjunction of all implied even-parity split predicates; a common tractable language, rather than tractability of each predicate separately, is explicitly required.

Traced the sampled-location coupling in Theorem 12.1 conditional on the invariant-structure classification: N iid colors induce a finite template; s≤k fresh leaves choose iid sample indices, and on no index collision the colors are iid with the right law and output trees coincide. Collision probability is at most binom(k,2)/N; repeated atomic locations cause no additional error.
remaining: Invariant-order and template-location classification, amenability reduction and full Carathéodory finite-mixture conclusion remain unaudited.
Exact numerical guarantees for all 13 predicates and their hardness/trivial-baseline certificates remain to check.

papers.authors: Guglielmo Beretta, Tom Cesari, Roberto Colomboni, Andrea Paudice

review.title: A Minimax Analysis of the Last Iterate of the SubGradient Method in Finite Dimension
review.authors: Guglielmo Beretta, Tommaso Cesari, Roberto Colomboni, Andrea Paudice
review.summary: For deterministic projected subgradient descent with one constant step size on convex L-Lipschitz objectives in R^d and initial distance at most R from a minimizer, proves optimal minimax last-iterate error Theta(L R sqrt(min{d,log n}/n)). Feasible sets may be unbounded; the step size can depend on d,L,R,n but is fixed throughout the run.
review.prior_frontier: Settles the fixed-dimension last-iterate question and identifies sharp square-root dimension dependence after optimizing the constant step size. Does not extend the result to stochastic gradients or arbitrary variable-step schedules.

score_reasons.significance: Gives a sharp dimension/horizon characterization for a basic optimization method, including the previously open fixed-dimension regime.
score_reasons.novelty: Last visits to objective-value bins generate pairwise obtuse vectors in a common half-space, converting ambient dimension into a last-versus-best gap.
score_reasons.depth: Geometric upper-bound refinement and reusable-direction lower-bound constructions address long horizons without increasing dimension.
score_reasons.exposition: Precisely distinguishes minimax optimization over constant steps, standard fixed steps, stochastic variants and time-varying policies.

checked: Checked the projected one- and two-step distance inequalities and their use for last-bin midpoint contraction.
Verified the resulting pairwise-negative inner products and common positive subgradient direction imply at most d independent vectors.
Traced the need for an extra infinitesimal projected step to improve the coarse d+1 bound to d.
remaining: Finish the extra-step boundary case and linear-independence dependency, then audit the geometric lower-bound construction, arbitrary-step quantifiers and matching min{d,log n} regime arithmetic.
