review.title: Approximate Polynomial Satisfiability is in the Counting Hierarchy
review.authors: Nikhil Balaji, Mahsa Shirmohammadi, Sébastien Tavenas, James Worrell

score_reasons.significance: A substantial complexity-class improvement for border and image-closure problems, with hitting-set certification consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: The prescribed infinitesimal-coordinate reduction and valuation test distinguish this route from the acknowledged independent work.
score_reasons.depth: Combines minimal dependence, localization, trailing resultants and uniform coefficient access; handles finite characteristic explicitly.
score_reasons.exposition: The overview, running example, encoding conventions and separated error analysis make the proof unusually accessible.

checked: Traced the complete new APS-to-MRV reduction: adjoining Y,YX gives full transcendence degree and an invertible Jacobian minor in every characteristic; generic projection preserves APS with a separately budgeted error.

Checked the principal annihilator argument, positive-valuation root construction, denominator localization and integral-extension lifting; the sampled bad-polynomial degree bounds ensure finite nonempty fibers for every required coordinate choice.

Checked that the T-trailing resultant includes every isolated affine solution, that distinct W powers remove infinity factors without cancellation, and that the base-(D+1) exponent substitution preserves the strict valuation comparison.

Recomputed the Gauss-valuation criterion as a sum of positive root valuations. Traced sparse input access, singly exponential coefficient indices and fixed CH oracle alternation, including uniformly described extension fields.
Checked the circuit-to-cubic-APS amplification gadget: residual valuations exceed multiplication depth times the largest input pole, so approximate gates imply approximate original outputs.
Verified the essential AGS26 Lemmas 4.6–4.7, resultant circuit size/uniformity statement and Theorem 6.7 in the primary arXiv text, including finite-extension coefficient reduction.
remaining: Established algebraic dependencies, including the GSS random-projection theorem and AGS resultant-circuit construction, were used as external theorems rather than reproved in full.
The auxiliary HN-to-APS and ETR reductions were read, but the external effective Nullstellensatz and quantitative real-separation bounds were not separately rederived.

sources.label: AGS26 primary dependency, Lemmas 4.6–4.7 and Theorem 6.7

review.summary: Places approximate polynomial satisfiability over rational and finite-field coefficients in the counting hierarchy, improving PSPACE. The problem is origin membership in a polynomial image closure over the algebraic closure, not fixed-tolerance numerical feasibility.
review.prior_frontier: Guo–Saxena–Sinhababu gave PSPACE; Andrews–Garg–Schost recently placed exact Hilbert Nullstellensatz in CH. The manuscript acknowledges independent APS-in-CH proofs and a characteristic-zero alternative through ETR.

review.title: Small classes have linear neighbourhood complexity
review.authors: John Sylvester, Viktor Zamaraev, Maksim Zhukovskii
review.summary: Proves that every hereditary graph class of labelled speed at most n!cⁿ has linear neighbourhood complexity. Consequences include O(log²n)-bit adjacency labels, improving O(log³n), and known algorithmic consequences for this class. Linear distance-r neighbourhood complexity for every fixed r remains open.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the previous O(n log n) neighbourhood-complexity bound to O(n), resolving the stated small-class conjecture; the O(log n) small implicit graph conjecture is not resolved.

score_reasons.significance: A general structural consequence of counting-small hereditary classes with several downstream applications.
score_reasons.novelty: Controls multiplicity in labelled extension counting through small cores with few automorphisms.
score_reasons.depth: Combines minimal diverse bipartite witnesses, Haussler packing and group stabilizer bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The distinction between small, factorial and bounded-parameter classes is careful.

checked: Traced the extension-counting argument from Theorem 16, including restoration of internal edges because the bipartition is label-determined.
Inspected the bound on repeated labelled constructions using the core automorphism group and diversity outside the core.
Read the minimality setup and canonical-neighbourhood defect construction used to obtain a small rigid core.
remaining: The complete two-case proof of the rigid-core theorem, including stabilizer injections and auxiliary graph lemmas, remains to be audited.
External packing and algorithmic/labeling corollaries, and the faster-speed complementary results, are not independently checked.

papers.title: The Computational Complexity of Avoiding Strict Saddle Points in Constrained Optimization
papers.authors: Andreas Kontogiannis, Ioannis Panageas, Vasilis Pollatos

review.title: The Computational Complexity of Avoiding Strict Saddle Points in Constrained Optimization
review.authors: Andreas Kontogiannis, Ioannis Panageas, Vasilis Pollatos
review.area: Continuous local search; constrained nonconvex optimization
review.summary: Proves PLS-hardness of approximate second-order stationary points already on [0,1]² with every approximate KKT point in [1/12,11/12]². SOSP1 is PLS-complete in arbitrary dimension; the stronger feasible-direction SOSP2 is PLS-complete in every fixed dimension ≥2. Functions are white-box polynomial-time evaluable with binary precision; this does not rule out polynomial dependence on 1/ε.
review.prior_frontier: Addresses constrained SOSP complexity beyond the CLS-complete first-order problem. Continuous-update obstruction assumes every approximate fixed point decodes to an SOSP; it is not a blanket prohibition on convergent continuous dynamics.

score_reasons.significance: Separates first- and second-order stationary search on a compact convex domain and eliminates boundary pathology as the cause.
score_reasons.novelty: The hardness construction allows unwanted interior first-order points while certifying negative curvature there.
score_reasons.depth: Lengthy geometric interpolation combines with discretized negative-curvature descent and face-dimension potentials for PLS membership.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions and computational-model qualifications are careful, but the 89-page case analysis is demanding to audit.

checked: Traced the box-domain PLS membership potential p=f+η dim Null(A′), with η=ε⁴/(100d Lmax²). A true gradient/curvature descent pays more than the worst dimension-penalty increase and rounding error; a boundary-hitting step reduces face dimension and the penalty pays for rounding.
Checked rounding to a grid dividing each side length preserves all active box constraints and moves by at most γ√d, with γ≤ε⁵/(1000 d^(3/2)Lmax³).

Checked exact rational negative-curvature implementation: a witness w to non-PSD(PHP+ε_H I) projects to u=Pw with u^T H u<−ε_H||u||². Rational rescaling gives norm squared in [999/1000,1] while retaining curvature −(999/1000)ε_H.

Verified the bounded backtracking logic: after polynomially many halvings α≤κ/L2 and the cubic Taylor upper bound ensures sufficient decrease; failed Taylor checks return an allowed violation witness.
remaining: The central two-dimensional Iter hardness construction, biquintic cell classification, boundary margin and rescaling occupy most of the manuscript and remain unaudited.
General-polytope face-preserving rounding, fixed-dimensional SOSP2 membership and local-Nash applications remain to check.
Exact source descent lemmas and the full finite-bit integer-potential encoding require dependency review.

score_reasons.significance: A large exponent improvement for a basic algebraic primitive, with a clearly separated computational model.
score_reasons.novelty: Sharing relation matrices and remainder tables across a batch, plus simultaneous good-position arguments, is a substantive algorithmic advance.
score_reasons.depth: The presentation-module, rectangular-product and large-value-fiber machinery is technically substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Costs and failure conditions are explicit; extensive appendices and several external relation-basis routines make independent verification demanding.

checked: Traced presentation normal forms and remainder doubling, including why multiplying reduced vectors preserves the quotient class and why the table can be constructed within the precomputation budget.
Checked the linear batched reduction and both stages of the two-relation-matrix evaluation; independently matched matrix dimensions, polynomial degrees and the n^(2/3) MM(n^(1/3),n^(1/3),k) cost.

Traced the simultaneous good-position Vandermonde specializations and union of failure polynomials, plus the separate degree certificate; a generator is essential and nongenerators can obstruct the rank condition.
Checked that every giant-step argument is a Frobenius image and hence remains a generator, including after scalar extension; verified doubling batches, field-descent correctness and expected retries.
Recomputed the distinct-degree factorization exponent balance, obtaining (ω+7)/6 with square products and the stated two-point rectangular formula.

review.summary: Claims Las Vegas finite-field polynomial factorization in n^1.5532+o(1) log q field operations, uniformly in characteristic, via batched modular composition. Also extends the n^((ω+3)/4) single-composition exponent to arbitrary arguments modulo separable polynomials.

review.summary: Maintains LZ77 under character insertion, deletion and substitution in Õ(min(n^(2/3),z)) worst-case update time and Õ(z) space, supporting LZ77 queries in polylogarithmic time and initialization directly from an LZ-like compressed representation. Establishes O(z log³n) irreducible LPF positions and new dynamic compressed substring tools.

score_reasons.novelty: Compresses the LPF tree and maintains leftmost grammar occurrences through local edits.
score_reasons.depth: A long interaction of signature encodings, periodicity, synchronized sets and dynamic range queries.
score_reasons.exposition: States the interface and compressed initialization precisely, with extensive technical implementation detail.

checked: Read the exact worst-case update and compressed-space guarantees and the irreducible LPF bound.
Inspected the unique LZ phrase-boundary association of each irreducible equality interval and the two-sided maximality claim used in charging.
Read the dyadic scale decomposition and use of a phrase-local synchronizing set to charge aperiodic irreducible positions.

review.title: High-Magnetization Sampling at Low Temperatures: Ising Models and Bayesian Sparse Linear Regression
review.authors: Syamantak Kumar, Purnamrita Sarkar, Kevin Tian, Yusong Zhu
review.summary: For each fixed inverse temperature β, samples high-magnetization SK slices k≤c_β d in polynomial time under arbitrary external fields. High-field SK sampling reaches within a constant factor of the asymptotic Almeida–Thouless line; reaching the asymptotically exact line additionally assumes the signs of the mean vector. Bayesian Gaussian spike-and-slab posterior sampling improves measurements from roughly k³ log³d to k^(3/2)log²d+k log³d, uniformly over signal-to-noise ratios.
review.prior_frontier: Improves sparsity dependence in low-temperature sampling and the prior polynomial-time sparse-regression posterior bound; does not attain the information-theoretic k log d measurement scale. Prior numerical frontier read from manuscript sources.

score_reasons.significance: Connects low-temperature spin sampling and Bayesian sparse regression through a sharper sparsity-sensitive mixing framework.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses mixed ℓ1/ℓ2 quadratic-form control and link-spectrum trickle-down instead of entrywise Dobrushin bounds alone.
score_reasons.depth: Requires uniform sparse operator-norm bounds, spectral mixing, annealing and a nontrivial support-posterior comparison.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates unconditional high-field conclusions from the stronger result requiring mean-sign information.

checked: Traced the sparse-Dobrushin coupling: common deletion coalesces with probability 1/k; otherwise couple exceptional added coordinates first and couple remaining up-step laws with disagreement ≤α, giving expected Hamming distance ≤1−1/k+α.

Checked the mixed-norm spectral estimate: test e_i±e_j to bound |K_ij|, expand exp(K)=1+K+R with entrywise R=O(τ²), and apply Young to get u^TXu≤.5||u||²+5τ²||u||_1². Since τ≤1/4, subtracting ||u||² gives the claimed ρ≤5τ² bound.
Traced shelling: blocks of size ceil(||u||_1²/||u||²) have summed ℓ2 norms ≤2||u||; a sparse-operator bound on unions of two blocks converts to the required mixed norm bound.
Visually checked PDF page 17 because text extraction dropped absolute-value bars: Lemma 4 correctly assumes sup |log(P/Q)|≤Δ. There is no one-sided-density flaw.
remaining: Full linear-magnetization GOE estimate, trickle-down spectral dependencies, annealing normalization and posterior-support argument remain unaudited.
High-field/Almeida–Thouless constants and exact measurement/runtime accounting remain to verify.

papers.authors: Davi Castro-Silva, Ryan Dancy, Sergii Strelchuk

review.title: Entanglement Lower Bounds for Symmetric Quantum Circuits
review.authors: Davi Castro-Silva, Ryan Dancy, Sergii Strelchuk
review.area: Quantum circuit complexity / finite model theory
review.summary: Exhibits a classical polynomial-time graph property requiring entanglement width Omega(n/log n) in polynomial-size symmetric quantum circuits with arbitrary one/two-qubit gates and unrestricted depth; symmetry under even vertex permutations suffices. Width measures largest tensor factor on basis inputs after each commuting layer. Also gives unrestricted-entanglement symmetric BQP simulation and width-one computation of FPC graph properties.
review.prior_frontier: Extends classical symmetric-circuit pebble lower bounds to a quantum entanglement resource tradeoff; this is not an unrestricted quantum circuit lower bound, and width is block size rather than entropy or Schmidt rank.

score_reasons.significance: Provides an unconditional quantum lower-bound framework tied to a meaningful resource and shows entanglement is necessary even for a P graph property under symmetry.
score_reasons.novelty: A partial-trace pebble game and reconstruction of bounded-width pure states from multisets of local marginals connect logic to quantum circuits.
score_reasons.depth: Support/orbit group bounds, partition symmetry and CFI indistinguishability interact nontrivially.
score_reasons.exposition: Access to symmetry, commuting layers, basis-input width and the polynomial-time hard property are precisely delineated.

checked: Traced the orbit-index support bound and logarithmic support size under the alternating-group small-index lemma.
Read the reconstruction argument matching indecomposable pure tensor factors using tuple counts, and checked why partially overlapping pure marginals would contradict indecomposability.
Verified the layer argument: gates avoiding the output tuple can be commuted last and disappear under partial trace, while equivalent-wire permutations preserve the incident gates.
remaining: Audit the quantum pebble indistinguishability induction, CFI parameter transfer and uniform BQP/FPC constructions. Check the tuple-count proof with projective state automorphisms: density-matrix equality permits a global phase, whereas the displayed Aut(|xi>) uses exact vector equality.

review.title: Even Coarse Matching Estimates Require Nearly Linear Streaming Space
review.authors: Gillat Kol

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a natural longstanding space question for a central streaming problem, in a substantially stronger multipass range.
score_reasons.novelty: The hidden-core construction and removal of a common distribution component turn XOR disjointness into a large matching-versus-cover gap.
score_reasons.depth: A technically economical reduction uses a quantitative unrestricted-round marginal-information consequence.
score_reasons.exposition: The overview and formal reduction agree closely; distributions, simulation and parameter losses are carefully explained.

checked: Traced the entire new graph and communication reduction: the core-plus-exceptional-vertices cover, independent outside-neighbor matching, and the two-sided approximation gap with a=24c².
Checked the hybrid simulation over repeated passes, reuse of Alice's sampled lists, exact conditional input law after public random labeling, and the 2p+1-message count.

Verified the replicated unique-disjointness construction has fixed set sizes and uniform random intersection multiplicities; common-component subtraction yields Q_b=(1−ρ)F+ρP_b with ρ≥2^(1−t), preserving acceptance-gap hardness without a sampling reduction in the wrong direction.
Recomputed the final exponent inequalities with γ=ε/4, m≈n^(1−ε/2), and c,p≤n^(ε/16); rounding a upward and m down to the required multiple preserves all asymptotic inequalities.

Checked the crucial quantitative Lemma 3.1 against the primary Iyer–Rao paper: Theorems 5–6, Section 7's communication expression and equations (59)–(62) support the chosen exponentially small error and g^(O(1)/t) advantage. Then traced the amplified disjointness gap contradiction.
remaining: The established Razborov disjointness lower bound and full Iyer–Rao marginal-information theorems were used as external results; their internal proofs were not rederived.
The theorem is an asymptotic adversarial-order lower bound with constants depending on ε, not a random-order or bounded-arboricity lower bound.

review.summary: Proves nearly linear streaming space for even coarse maximum-matching size estimates, allowing both polynomial approximation factors and polynomially many passes. The hard graphs are simple bipartite graphs in vertex arrival with known bipartition.
review.prior_frontier: Prior lower bounds focused on near-exact estimates or stronger output/adversary requirements. Random-order streams permit inverse-polylogarithmic approximation in polylogarithmic space; this result rules that out for adversarial order.

review.summary: Conditional explicit binary CSS qLTCs with constant rate, relative distance, soundness and check weight, assuming Conjecture 5.6 on product expansion of structured Reed–Solomon tuples over binary extension fields. This is not an unconditional construction of good qLTCs.

score_reasons.significance: Good qLTC parameters address a central coding frontier, with the conjectural premise stated explicitly.
score_reasons.novelty: Non-Abelian RSV cubes are made compatible with projective RS codes by weights and Frobenius permutations.
score_reasons.depth: The construction combines arithmetic cube symmetries, sheaf-like local constraints, product expansion and quantum homology.
score_reasons.exposition: The two-dimensional worked construction explains the obstruction before the four-dimensional framework.

checked: Inspected Lemma 4.5 setup: coordinate weights and Frobenius twists repair endpoint relabeling; divisibility (s_i-1)|(2^h+1)d_i removes the unwanted scalar dependence.
Checked the stated conjecture and parameter choice: m_i=L+8,16,32,64, h=4 and degrees (s_i-1)/17 or 16(s_i-1)/17; distinct 2-adic valuations force pairwise coprime s_i+1.

papers.authors: Philip Whittington

review.title: Quasipolynomial 3-Coloring of Diameter-2 Graphs via Domain Reduction from Nogoods
review.authors: Philip Whittington
review.summary: Deterministically solves decision, search and exact counting for 3-Coloring and fixed-palette List-3-Coloring on diameter-at-most-two graphs in 2^(O(log³n)) time. Does not give a polynomial algorithm; NP-hardness would imply NP⊆QP.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the cited 2^(O(n^(1/3)log²n)) subexponential algorithm to quasipolynomial time, addressing an explicitly posed QP question. The covering potential is adapted from Gao–Ma–Rong–Tran, now implemented with explicit nogoods.

score_reasons.significance: A major advance on the longstanding unresolved complexity of diameter-two 3-coloring, extending to exact counting.
score_reasons.novelty: Turns bounded shattering into an effective disjoint domain-reduction algorithm without extension queries or solution enumeration.
score_reasons.depth: Combines a nontrivial overlapping-chain color-forcing construction with a certificate-table potential and a separate counting recursion.
score_reasons.exposition: The algorithms, certificate invariants and counting issue beyond 2-SAT are laid out explicitly.

checked: Traced the full main argument. Certificate-table projection preserves soundness; slicing descends a matching nogood. Pairing scopes T and T∪{v} proves Σ_b Φ(W_v^b)≤(|D_v|−1)Φ(W), including the size-ℓ boundary.

A target solution never certifies the empty scope, hence its path has at most K=O(σℓlog n) minimum-label slices. Deterministic replay of exception positions covers all solutions, and the first differing position makes boxes disjoint. Construction cost exp(O(σℓlog²n)) includes initial nogood enumeration.

Traced the diameter-two nogood construction: independent terminals create 4^a>n connector chains on 5a−2 vertices; premature adjacency immediately gives a nogood, otherwise two final roots coincide. The one-zero and all-nonzero fold patterns force incompatible final colors. Their shared binary equality/inequality constraints are forests; splitting further variable positions cannot create cycles.

Independently enumerated all 45,056 overlap/differing-position patterns through chain length 22; every signed constraint system was consistent and yielded zero versus nonzero final folds. Script audits/check1137.py. This supplements, rather than replaces, the general forest argument.

Traced exact counting: different two-color lists have a forbidden pair via adjacency or a common neighbor. Branching on a vertex outside the largest list class fixes at least n₂/6 vertices on one branch, giving T(n₂)≤T(n₂−1)+T(floor(5n₂/6)) and exp(O(log²n)) leaves. Uniform-list components contribute 2^h after a bipartiteness check. Combining disjoint boxes gives the claimed 2^(O(log³n)) total.
remaining: Supplementary lower bound on necessary box-cover size, ordinary/list reduction refinements and general ternary CSP application were not fully audited.
Published prior-runtime comparisons were not independently checked beyond the cited manuscript discussion.

Also transfers any instance I to such a three-item instance J with LP(J)=M=O((LP(I)+1)^4) and OPT(I)-LP(I)<=3+96(OPT(J)-LP(J)).

score_reasons.significance: Shows near-one-third instances capture the additive configuration-LP difficulty of general bin packing, a structural advance beyond the slow-growing explicit lower bound.
score_reasons.novelty: Finite-state path encoding transfers fractional and integral packings while exact primary-score conservation limits all noncanonical bins.
score_reasons.depth: A nontrivial combinatorial reduction with controlled rational precision and tower-growth bookkeeping, but considerably shorter than the source hardness construction.

checked: Traced Lemma 2.1: canonical zero-primary-score triples encode transitions and endpoints; at most 96t bad items arise from t surplus bins; remaining paths decode to at most b+96t source bins. Checked all three possible zero-primary-score triple types.

Traced the universal reduction: large-item threshold 1/(B+1), support reduction to at most m configurations, copied partial loads with integer capacities, and reinsertion of small items give gap(I)<=3+96 gap(J).
Checked the explicit competing-tree recurrence, shared-quota unhit-path argument, tower bound and c(n)=floor((log* n-4)/(4A0))-1 polynomial-size choice.
Verified the SAT-to-vertex-cover gap arithmetic and both compositions giving hardness and unconditional LP gaps.

papers.authors: Sunghyeon Jo, Taekyun Lee

review.title: The Exact Online Threshold for the Asymmetric Binary Perceptron
review.authors: Sunghyeon Jo, Taekyun Lee
review.summary: Exact online feasibility threshold alpha_on(kappa)=2/(pi E_*(kappa)) for the Gaussian asymmetric binary perceptron, with signs irrevocably chosen as columns arrive. E_* is a Brownian control problem with an essential-supremum-in-time L2 drift budget. Below threshold a deterministic O(MN)-arithmetic online algorithm succeeds with high probability; at zero margin certified bounds give 0.327479... <= alpha_on(0) < 0.366634....
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript compares a prior proved polynomial-time offline density 0.1 and online small-constant guarantees. Its threshold is not the offline storage capacity or a universal computational hardness threshold; concurrent Lipschitz offline work is distinct.

score_reasons.significance: An exact algorithmic threshold and a factor-over-three increase in a proved zero-margin algorithmic density are substantial.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses one-sided monotonicity and a final correction block to turn a typical-coordinate Brownian limit into simultaneous feasibility.
score_reasons.depth: Requires stochastic-control compactness, high-dimensional Gaussian signing couplings and certified numerical control bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully distinguishes online information restrictions, storage capacity and other algorithmic models.

checked: Read the precise Brownian norm and finite positive control-value bounds.
Inspected Proposition 4.7: empirical L2 concentration keeps the signing projection inactive; p>4 moments give the final-stage union bound, and coupling error O(N^(-1/4+1/(2p))) tends to zero.
Read the final-block split into deterministic shortfall compensation and independent Föllmer drift, with strict margin slack absorbing errors.
remaining: The lower-bound compactness argument, full conditional Gaussian coupling and control approximation lemmas are not audited.

papers.title: One Trap Is Enough: The Structure and Complexity of Robust Contracts for Sequential Search
papers.authors: Michal Feldman, Hu Fu, Bo Peng, Zhihao Gavin Tang

review.title: One Trap Is Enough: The Structure and Complexity of Robust Contracts for Sequential Search
review.authors: Michal Feldman, Hu Fu, Bo Peng, Zhihao Gavin Tang
review.summary: For robust sequential search with independent actions and principal-favored ties, one additional deterministic trap action approximates Nature’s worst response after a lossless contract restriction. On finite known support, a costless trap at a known output attains the worst case, giving polynomial evaluation. Design is polynomial for fixed output count but NP-complete already with three known actions; monotone/debt contracts have tight 1/m gaps, while linear contracts have no constant guarantee.
review.prior_frontier: Extends one-known-action debt optimality to evaluation, structure and computational complexity for finite multiaction technologies. Does not assume infinitely many independent copies of each known type.

score_reasons.significance: Reduces an infinite adversarial technology-design problem to a tractable finite worst-response characterization.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses lexicographic covered pairs to account exactly for principal-favored tie-breaking, then freezes one unknown-outcome realization.
score_reasons.depth: Structural averaging and residual floors support a substantial optimization and hardness classification.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly distinguishes infimum from attainment and finite-support results from general unknown technologies.

checked: Traced the finite-support covered-pair proof: perturb wages by ε times principal residual, then compare the linear coefficient of the finite policy maximum with the lexicographic covered-call representation.
Checked residual-floor bound: a capped pair’s secondary index is an average residual over outcomes with wage at least its primary index, hence at least D_w(t).

Traced finite-support one-trap reduction: independence separates the maxima of known and unknown covered pairs; some unknown realization has no larger expected payoff than their mixture. If its primary value is zero the null option suffices; otherwise choose a deterministic output within η of the residual floor at that value. For each known realization, decreasing this residual raises payoff by at most η even at ties.
remaining: General unbounded-support/infinite-index extension, free-trap sharpening and lossless contract restriction remain to verify.
All design algorithms, hardness reductions, approximation examples and Markovian extension remain unaudited.

score_reasons.significance: Settles the optimal erasure threshold while simultaneously achieving constant rate and linear processing.
score_reasons.novelty: A recursive monochromatic-block protocol turns erased feedback into paid Hamming-distance loss, yielding a simple potential certificate.
score_reasons.depth: The central argument is concise rather than technically sprawling, with an exact cost-based GMD reduction.

Independently enumerated every valid single-block case for q=2,...,8: equal/unequal starting bits, receipt/no receipt, and feedback delivered/erased independently in the two executions; all meet the 2L potential increment.
Verified pairwise costs sum to B=(2R-q)M, including capping/inconsistent transcripts, and the exact B-threshold GMD averaging bound over errors/erasures.
Checked delta=epsilon/10, R=ceil(10q/epsilon), M=(2q)^R and total T=3MNR/2 make the actual erasure budget strictly smaller than (1-delta)BN/2.

Verified the external Guruswami-Indyk Theorem 3 provides constant alphabet/rate and linear-time decoding for the required mixed-error/erasure inequality; fixed epsilon makes inner enumeration and B outer trials constant.
remaining: No unresolved gap in the central construction found. The established outer-code theorem and previous 2/3 converse are used as dependencies rather than reproved; no full implementation was built.

score_reasons.depth: Combines decoding energy barriers, Lindblad perturbation estimates and encoded adiabatic simulation.

papers.title: Multi-Party Error Resilience beyond $\frac{1}{n}$
papers.authors: Klim Efremenko, Gillat Kol, Raghuvansh Saxena, Zhijun Zhang

review.title: Multi-Party Error Resilience beyond $\frac{1}{n}$
review.authors: Klim Efremenko, Gillat Kol, Raghuvansh R. Saxena, Zhijun Zhang
review.summary: Characterizes adaptive information dissemination resilience as Θ(1/√n) in collision-as-silence radio broadcast, allowing receiver-specific corruptions. Crucial correctness condition: every receiver with at most 10δ local corruption must learn all n inputs; at least 90% qualify. It does not guarantee every receiver under a global δ budget. The protocol uses soft-O_η(n^(3/2+η)) rounds for one-bit inputs, not constant rate.
review.prior_frontier: Breaks the 1/n limit of fixed speaking-order protocols under the stated robust-receiver correctness criterion; a matching erasure impossibility holds even for adaptive protocols. Prior bounds not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Identifies the optimal adaptive noise scale in a basic multiparty communication model.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses disagreement-driven transmission schedules, vote cushions and silence as evidence to protect poorly disseminated inputs.
score_reasons.depth: The adaptive impossibility must control speaking schedules that themselves depend on adversarial feedback, while the upper bound handles corruptions and varying dissemination quality.
score_reasons.exposition: The all-input versus all-receiver distinction is explicitly explained and essential to interpreting the headline.

checked: Checked the selector-family probabilistic lemma: independently include each party with probability 1/(2√n); every target inside a set of size ≤√n is isolated with probability ≥1/(6√n). m=Ω(nlog n) samples make the Chernoff exponent dominate exp(O(√nlog n)) choices.

Traced the multibit extension: constant-rate distance-.49 encoding, coordinatewise simulation at global budget .1δ, and per-receiver budget δ leave at least .8 of columns both globally and locally good. Error .2 is below half the code distance, so every input decodes.

Traced the initial adaptive lower-bound selector: under all-erasure histories each input-dependent schedule is fixed. A doubled multiset of T rounds loses >T/k occurrences per selected party, so fewer than 2k parties suffice; fully removed rounds contain two forced speakers and hence free collisions, while the remaining target schedule has ≤T/k occurrences.
remaining: Full corruption-resilient upper protocol and vote/silence invariants remain unaudited.
The final indistinguishability/adversary construction and optimization at k≈√n remain to check beyond the initial selection lemma.

papers.title: Pretty good shadow tomography

review.title: Pretty good shadow tomography
review.authors: Sabee Grewal, Angelos Pelecanos, Jack Spilecki, Ewin Tang, John Wright
review.summary: For any known collection of m>=2 bounded observables and arbitrary unknown d-dimensional mixed state, collective measurements achieve simultaneous epsilon-accurate estimates with failure delta using O(log(m) log(m/delta)/epsilon^2) copies, independent of d. This is an information-theoretic offline result; it does not give efficient implementation or an observable-independent classical shadow.
review.prior_frontier: Removes the dimension dependence and attains the classical epsilon^-2 dependence, leaving one log(m) above the general classical lower bound. A concurrent Jeronimo-Huang-Liu result reaches the same bound; the introduction explicitly distinguishes the analyses.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves dimension-independent polylogarithmic shadow tomography for unrestricted mixed states with essentially optimal precision dependence.
score_reasons.novelty: Shows exponentially small prior mass of states with poor conditional integral-PGM performance, avoiding the false assertion that raw PGM errors universally decay exponentially.
score_reasons.depth: Combines a matrix-log derivative inequality, a relative-entropy increment bound, Bernoulli prediction, and prior-reweighting amplification.
score_reasons.exposition: The proof exposes the failed approaches, exact good/bad distinction, and the sharper delta amplification separately.

checked: Traced integral-PGM normalization and the operator-concavity proof of Lemma 3.2, including singular-X support limits.

Checked the Bernoulli auxiliary-state Pinsker reduction and integral-PGM relative-entropy inequality; tensor entropy cancellation, data processing and telescoping give the prior-relative-entropy bound in Lemma 4.9.

Independently derived the Laplace-estimator bound used in Lemma 4.13: Jensen on log(1/(K+1)), with E[1/(K+1)]=(1-(1-theta)^(m+1))/((m+1)theta), yields log((m+2)/(m+1)), including endpoints by continuity.
Verified the bad-prior bound 2 exp(-T/128), Appendix A weight recursion Z_R<=(3/2)^R and conditional independence giving failure m(sqrt(3)/2)^R.

Checked finite-family minimax: finite output discretization makes the POVM set compact and success bilinear. A sufficiently fine trace-distance net (radius at most delta/O(n) and epsilon/O(1)) extends it to all states without sample overhead.
remaining: No unresolved substantive gap in the central sample-complexity proof found. No efficient circuit realization is claimed or verified. Background counterexamples in Section 2 are not prerequisites for the main bound.
resolved_notes: Minor notation slips (p/q and s/n in Lemmas 4.8/4.10) are resolved by the displayed derivation; they do not alter the argument. Standard logarithm convention is max(1,log m), or m>=2.

review.authors: Mu-Xia Sun

score_reasons.significance: Would settle a prominent algorithmic frontier with a sharp structural theorem of independent interest.
score_reasons.novelty: Separating a likely failed cut inside each recursive call and the cut-character hypercontractive argument provide distinctive mechanisms.
score_reasons.depth: A long implementation and variance analysis connects contraction trajectories, tree packings, importance resampling and general edge probabilities.
score_reasons.exposition: The main architecture is clear, but the final log²n bound depends on extensive technical appendices and a companion manuscript.

checked: Traced the disjoint-event recursive estimator and unrolled second-moment inequality; selected-cut randomness is conditioned on before independent continuations are averaged.

Checked the complete cut-character/tree-packing argument: tree edge signs identify the parity space, commuting noise operators compose Lp improvements, and the cubic moment counts ordered distinct cut pairs.

Traced the exponent-shift interpolation from the stated Karger phase-transition inputs, including real-capacity approximation and deterministic-probability limits. Checked the fixed-cut refinement and the r-component moment argument and cycle sharpness.

Verified the unusual unbiased confidence amplification in Appendix J: median/mean truncation is corrected by an independent rare nonnegative term, preserving expectation while keeping failure probability small. It is not an unsupported claim that a median is unbiased.
remaining: The full 65-page near-linear algorithm was not verified: adaptive search failures, timing/charging, sparse tree packing and reverse importance-resampling implementation remain unaudited.

papers.title: The Power of Recruiting the Smaller Side: Two Additional Traders Suffice in Two-Sided Markets
papers.authors: Yang Cai, Vineet Gupta, Yanchen Jiang, Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Grigoris Velegkas, Di Wang, Mingfei Zhao

review.title: The Power of Recruiting the Smaller Side: Two Additional Traders Suffice in Two-Sided Markets
review.authors: Yang Cai, Vineet Gupta, Yanchen Jiang, Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Grigoris Velegkas, Di Wang, Mingfei Zhao
review.summary: For m >= n iid unit-demand buyers and unit-supply sellers with buyer distribution first-order stochastically dominating seller costs and finite original expected GFT, Seller Trade Reduction with exactly two additional sellers attains the original first-best expected GFT. Two is uniformly necessary even for randomized prior-independent DSIC, IR, weakly budget-balanced mechanisms. Further r-dominance extensions are claimed.
review.prior_frontier: Prior results needed a large constant on both sides or four traders in bilateral trade; the paper resolves recruitment solely on the smaller side with the tight constant two. Prior comparison is manuscript-reported.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the exact competition complexity of a well-defined two-sided-market question.
score_reasons.novelty: A pointwise rank-integral comparison and randomized-mechanism lower bound sharpen the previous augmentation framework.
score_reasons.depth: The sharp constant follows from a compact but nontrivial beta-distribution truncation inequality and payment-identity argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear decomposition separates arbitrary distributions, symmetric warm-up, stochastic dominance, atoms and tightness.

checked: Traced Theorem 1.1: STR pair i trades precisely when buyer i exceeds seller i+1; integrating its surplus yields the binomial recruitment gain minus the exact-i-sellers loss. Verified the two-additional-sellers binomial expression A_n,i.

Checked Lemma 3.7: the truncated integrand is decreasing, so prefix nonnegativity follows from its total integral; min(z,W)^d <= z^d and <= W z^(d-1), averaged with i/(n+2) and d/(n+2), give the beta mean inequality.

Checked arbitrary CDFs via inverse quantiles and F_B(x-), including atoms; FSD gives 1-F_S(F_B^-1(u)) <= min(1-p,1-u). For m>=n, beta-density ratio proportional to (1-w)^(m-n) and the symmetrized double-integral covariance prove the required prefix inequality.

Traced Theorem 1.2: symmetrization preserves iid expected GFT; payment identities and IR/WBB force inf_tau x_1(1-rho(1-tau),tau,1)=0. Independently checked the two-point expectation bounds and p=3/4, rho<1/8 contradiction.

The STR incentive/feasibility properties are the standard threshold-payment trade-reduction mechanism; no novel external mathematical dependency is needed for the checked rank comparison or impossibility argument.
remaining: The separate r-dominance generalization and its quantitative lower bounds are not covered by this main-result audit.
This is a mathematical reading check of Theorems 1.1–1.2, not formal verification.

papers.title: Functional inequalities from the fundamental limits of Bayesian estimation
papers.authors: Shuchen Li, ILIAS ZADIK

review.title: Functional inequalities from the fundamental limits of Bayesian estimation
review.authors: Shuchen Li, Ilias Zadik
review.area: High-dimensional probability; functional inequalities; Bayesian estimation
review.summary: For smooth Φ with Φ″>0 and concave 1/Φ″, equates a log-concave prior’s Φ-Sobolev constant C with Bregman Bayes risk ≥Ent_Φ(f)/(1+Ct) under Gaussian observations √tX+G. Applications include a new O(K²n^(1/4)) log-Sobolev bound for smooth K-subgaussian log-concave measures and a Bayesian reinterpretation of recent KLS proofs.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the cited O(K²√n) log-Sobolev bound, but explicitly acknowledges a concurrent independently claimed dimension-free result. Its O(√n) Poincaré proof is a new proof of an older bound, not a new best KLS estimate.

score_reasons.significance: A unified estimation interpretation may make functional-inequality tools accessible to techniques from information theory and average-case complexity.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses Bregman Bayes risk and Gaussian-channel divergence contraction as a common bridge across Poincaré and log-Sobolev inequalities.
score_reasons.depth: The applications need sophisticated testing-to-estimation, posterior concentration and information-contraction estimates.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear distinction between new equivalence, recovered older bounds, new quantitative result and concurrent stronger claim.

checked: Traced the equivalence conditional on stated standard functional-inequality facts. Posterior means minimize Bregman loss and entropy decomposes as risk plus entropy of the posterior mean. Gaussian observation makes the posterior t-strongly log-concave, giving risk≤Dirichlet_Φ/(2t).
From the assumed Bayes-risk lower bound, combine that upper bound and let t→∞ to recover constant C; a single-SNR lower fraction b gives constant 1/(bT).

For the reverse direction, shift f to positive values, normalize a tilted prior dν/dμ=f/Ef and rescale Φ to Ψ. The output likelihood ratio is E[f|Y]/Ef, so Gaussian-channel Ψ-divergence contraction by Ct/(1+Ct) gives the desired residual-risk fraction.
Checked the indicator/MMSE-to-isoperimetry step using posterior Cheeger bounds and Fatou on nonnegative neighborhood increments.
remaining: The key n^(1/4) log-Sobolev improvement, null-posterior concentration and low-degree-MMSE recasting of KLS proofs remain unaudited.
Bakry–Émery for this Φ class and Gaussian-channel Φ-divergence contraction are essential cited facts whose precise generality remains to check.
Concurrent dimension-free claims have not been independently assessed here.

papers.title: Resolution Lower Bounds versus the Weak Pigeonhole Principle
papers.authors: Noel Arteche

review.title: Resolution Lower Bounds versus the Weak Pigeonhole Principle
review.authors: Noel Arteche
review.summary: Shows that polynomial-size constant-depth Frege proofs of naturally tight Resolution lower bounds are equivalent, in the specified formalizations, to short proofs of the quadratic-stretch weak pigeonhole principle. More quantitatively, a depth-d Frege size-T refutation of Ref_s(phi), where phi has a Resolution refutation of length L and depth D, yields a depth-(d+2) proof of PHP^L_(s/D) of polynomial size. Under the WPHP hypothesis obtains barriers to such lower-bound proofs and conditional non-automatability consequences for AC0-Frege on CNFs.
review.prior_frontier: Prior conditional barriers used stronger or less tightly characterized assumptions; this gives necessity/sufficiency tied to WPHP and parallel proof compression. The ETH-style consequence remains conditional on the explicitly stated WPHP hypothesis.

score_reasons.significance: Connects two central bounded-depth proof-complexity problems with a quantitative depth-preserving reduction.
score_reasons.novelty: Parallel compression uses a fixed refutation and hypothetical injective clause-to-hole map rather than an expensive sequential pointer chase.
score_reasons.depth: Requires detailed bounded-depth derivations of refutation axioms, lower-bound formalizations and extensions to Res(k).
score_reasons.exposition: Quantifiers and the meaning of naturally tight are stated explicitly, though the 62-page formalization has substantial bookkeeping.

checked: Checked the local substituted Ref-1 axiom derivation: injectivity at the current or parent hole handles unequal clauses; when clauses agree, nonpivot literal inheritance gives the desired conclusion.
Checked the aggregation into constant-depth cedents and Ref-3/4/5 derivations using disjunctions over known clauses.
remaining: The other substituted axioms, full depth/size accounting, WPHP sufficiency formalization and automatability reduction have not been traced completely.

score_reasons.significance: An exact universality result, rather than a constant-factor discrepancy estimate, answers a concrete question in online random optimization.
score_reasons.novelty: The auxiliary fair-sign/product-vector coupling addresses the dependence introduced by a sign chosen from the entire column, including nonsymmetric laws.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines causal martingale estimates, strong approximation, drift delocalization and terminal confinement.
score_reasons.exposition: The moment and uniformity qualifications and the precomputed-control evaluation model are explicit; the stochastic-control details are extensive.

checked: Traced the novel one-column drift approximation, conditional density and sequential maximal-coupling construction, including measurability and independence of the product vector from the auxiliary signs.
Checked iteration in the causal filtration and recomputed the predictable-bias and Burkholder–Rosenthal exponents after summing over M=Θ(N) coordinates.

Checked why conditioning on auxiliary signs permits rowwise strong approximation, why the Gaussian enlargement must follow the martingale estimates, and why the deterministic split preserves the needed final-block independence.

Recomputed the fourth-moment tail bound for discarded entries and its conversion into failure probability and expected excess at a fixed margin. Uniform convergence requires uniformly integrable fourth moments, not just a common fourth-moment bound.
Read the first-failed-test argument and parameter exponent budgeting in Appendix D; these correctly distinguish the globally valid auxiliary process from the intended control before failure.

review.summary: Claims the exact proportional-regime online vector-balancing optimum is universal for centered variance-one entry laws with finite fourth moment, identifying the Rademacher optimum and the positive-margin online symmetric-perceptron threshold with the Gaussian control value.

papers.title: Linear Hashing Is Poissonesque
papers.authors: Vinayak Kumar

review.title: Linear Hashing Is Poissonesque
review.authors: Vinayak M. Kumar
review.summary: For every fixed subset of an F2-vector space, uniformly random linear hashing satisfies a Poisson log-potential inequality. This bounds expected top-r and bottom-r average loads by Poisson Chernoff thresholds; for n balls/n bins the expected maximum is at most fully random hashing plus 3/2+o(1). For m>n log n, all loads deviate by at most 5 sqrt(m log n/(epsilon n)) with probability 1-epsilon.
review.prior_frontier: Improves constant-factor and second-order expected maximum-load bounds and dense-regime expectation 16m/n to (1+o(1))m/n. A concurrent concentration result is explicitly acknowledged; linear hashing does not acquire fully independent Poisson tails.

score_reasons.significance: Sharp bounds for a basic universal-hashing family resolve a dense-regime question and give nearly exact expected maximum loads.
score_reasons.novelty: Taking the logarithm before averaging, plus a dimension-extension limit removing surjectivity, gives a versatile new analytic principle.
score_reasons.depth: The proof is concise and elementary once the correct potential is identified.
score_reasons.exposition: Precisely explains why full Poisson tail equivalence is false and states concurrent results.

checked: Traced the complete main potential proof: grow a random kernel by independent vectors; including excluded kernel shifts raises the correlation average, so E Phi_(i+1)<=Phi_i^2; Jensen gives E log Phi_(i+1)<=2 log Phi_i. The initial Bernoulli potential yields the centered Poisson cumulant bound for every real lambda.

Checked the surjectivity-removal lemma: embed S in arbitrarily large domains, restrict a uniform map, bound nonsurjectivity by 2^(-U+ell), and use boundedness of the finite load-vector statistic. Nonnegativity of the log-potential follows from centered-load Jensen.
Traced top/bottom-r Jensen extraction, Markov on the common nonnegative potential, and optimization lambda=log(t/mu), including r=n and zero lower-threshold edge cases.

Checked dense-regime estimates from integrals of log(1+u), the two-sided union bound and constant (2+sqrt(2))*sqrt(2)<5. The density-subset guarantee is uniform over subsets of one fixed density, not a fully independent tail statement.

Traced the additive maximum-load comparison using standard Poissonization for decreasing occupancy events and Stirling: threshold s=floor(t-1/2-eta) is attained with probability 1-o(1/t), eta=1/sqrt(log t), and vanishing threshold increments give the stated fractional-part subsequence.
remaining: No formal verification or empirical implementation is claimed. Standard Poissonization and Stirling estimates are used; no new unverified technical lemma is needed in the audited core.

review.title: Beyond the Bochner Method: Optimal Spectral Gaps for Block Dynamics of Spin Systems like the O(N) Model
review.authors: Jonathan Leake, Anqi Li
review.summary: Sharp matrix-valued local-to-global spectral bounds for block Glauber dynamics after arbitrary marginalization; applications give O(N) gap (1-||J_abs||/N)/n with arbitrary fields and weighted forest pair correlation at most 4/3 times the product.
review.prior_frontier: Ordinary Bochner bounds handle single-site global gaps; manuscript compares O(N) row-sum threshold 0.5874N and forest correlation factor 2. These prior comparisons were not independently re-proved.

score_reasons.significance: The block theorem unifies marginalization and grouping and the O(N) threshold and 4/3 forest result are major applications.
score_reasons.novelty: A Schur-complement comparison for the Bochner operator retains the full matrix of local interactions.
score_reasons.depth: Infinite-dimensional projection geometry, tilted-sphere covariance and a stable auxiliary forest polynomial address different obstacles.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed derivations and explicit assumptions make the broad framework accessible, although Gaussian sharpness details are omitted.

checked: Traced Lemma 20: d1d0=0 gives Bd0=d0Q and d0*B^-1d0 equal to the projection off ker d0; coercivity excludes spectrum in (0,alpha).

Traced the full abstract Theorem 21 comparison: inverse off-diagonal blocks are bounded entrywise using the nonnegative Neumann series of I-S; Schur complements satisfy Btilde_ii>=c_ii I and ||Btilde_ij||<=-c_ij. Since alpha<=1, blockwise quadratic inequalities imply Btilde>=alpha Dtilde. The compression minimization inequality then yields the block projection Poincare bound.

Checked the spin-system specialization: functions of retained sites lie in HT, global connectedness makes the common kernel constants, and conditional expectations on complementary retained blocks lie in each block kernel.

Traced the forest polynomial identity: the differential matching operator joins at most two rooted components; the coefficient for a chosen edge subset in each final tree is 1+|S|, matching principal minors of I+11*. Its Hessian at zero is 4Cov(X)-3diag(p)-S, giving the 4/3 bound conditional on stability preservation.
remaining: The tilted-sphere covariance lemma underpinning the sharp O(N) application and its mixing-time refinement remain unaudited.
Check the cited stability-preserving differential-operator fact and local spectral/projection equivalence in full; the 42-page paper has several independent applications.
Gaussian simultaneous equality is asserted without details and has not been separately reconstructed.

review.summary: With a classically known reference of rank at most r and an unknown state of supplied rank bound s, root-fidelity estimation under unrestricted collective measurements has worst-case copy complexity between c q^2/(epsilon^2 log^4(q+1)) and C q^2/epsilon^2, q=min(r,s). checked: Verified the beta-overlap moments and orthogonal covariance computation giving MSE <=4s min(s,(tr sqrt(sigma))^2)/(n+1).

checked: Read exact input representations and the restricted image-closure theorem.

Inspected the parallel pruning step: remove factors corresponding to every higher-dimensional auxiliary variety, combine quotients by GCD, then lift a specialized squarefree factor to its Chow factor after a generic coordinate change.
Read the final threshold-circuit size, random-coordinate failure bound and CH simulation/circuit-input transition.

review.authors: Ilan Doron-Arad, Joseph (Seffi) Naor
review.summary: Unweighted known-instance online set cover has randomized oblivious-adversary competitive ratio Omega(sqrt(m)), with unrestricted computation; additional random-order Omega(m^(1/3)) and polynomial-memory Omega(m/log m) bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Previously Omega(log m) unrestricted randomized lower bound versus soft-O(sqrt(m)) upper, as cited; the main theorem closes the polynomial gap up to logs.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the long-standing information-theoretic gap for a canonical online problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Forcing batches translate hidden candidate covers into an oblivious random filtration and force many purchased witnesses.
score_reasons.depth: The core combines a tailored union-expanding family with a clean conditional-independence argument; extensions require further machinery.
score_reasons.exposition: Parameters, the known-instance distinction and unrestricted-computation scope are unusually explicit.

checked: Main Theorem 1.2 fully traced: a forcing batch contains complement-of-X precisely to exclude small purchased X containing no candidate cover; conversely every candidate cover covers its batch.
Verified first-moment family construction with k=floor sqrt(m),q=ceil sqrt(m),r=floor m/32,M=2^(4q). The logarithmic bad-event bound is (4 ln2+H(1/32)-ln32+o(1))m<0 and M<binomial(m,k).

For every chosen witness, independent uniform halving discards it with conditional probability 1/2 regardless of history. Thus the discard indicators are iid; at least q occur except with exp(-q/4) probability. Discarded witnesses cannot recur and q distinct witnesses have union larger than r.

The full filtration is sampled before play, so the adversary is oblivious on one fixed incidence universe. Its final surviving k-set covers all batches, while expected purchases are Omega(m), giving the claimed ratio. Proactive purchases and repeated requests do not break the argument.
remaining: The separate tree-amplified parameter ranges, random-order construction, polynomial-memory lower bound and exact streaming tradeoff have not received a full audit.
The previously known upper bound is a cited comparison, not independently verified here.

papers.title: A dimension-free bound for the isoperimetric constant of unconditional log-concave measures
papers.authors: Pierre Bizeul, Dan Mikulincer, Ilias Zadik

review.title: A dimension-free bound for the isoperimetric constant of unconditional log-concave measures
review.authors: Pierre Bizeul, Dan Mikulincer, Ilias Zadik
review.summary: Proves a universal dimension-free Poincare bound for every isotropic unconditional log-concave measure. Gives two proofs; the shorter second proof yields CP(mu)<=max_j E X_j^2 +(1/3)max_j E(1+|X_j|)^4 through an averaged inverse-Hessian Brascamp-Lieb inequality and an orthant contraction.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the unconditional-class logarithmic bounds to a constant. The manuscript acknowledges that concurrent work subsequently proved general KLS, so this is independently significant for its distinct methods and quantitative moment formulation rather than a strictly stronger final class.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a prominent symmetry-restricted case and provides a useful averaged-curvature inequality despite concurrent general KLS resolution.
score_reasons.novelty: A coordinate contraction convexifies the orthant measure while keeping the inverse Hessian controlled by individual fourth moments.
score_reasons.depth: The second proof is concise, combining spectral Bochner cancellation, weighted Cauchy-Schwarz and sign decomposition.
score_reasons.exposition: The two routes and their assumptions are explained well, although the standalone Proposition 1.2 omits an essential positivity hypothesis that is established in its use.

checked: Traced the complete second proof of the main theorem: integrated Bochner and Poincare applied to gradient coordinates give E<H grad f,grad f><=lambda|E grad f|^2; weighted Cauchy-Schwarz gives CP<=||E H^-1||op when H is positive definite.
Verified the one-dimensional even-unimodal mixture-of-uniforms inequality and its conditional use in the sign-cube variance decomposition.
Differentiated h(t)=sqrt(1+t^2)-1: h prime<=1, h double-prime>=0 and -(log h prime) double-prime=(1+3t^2)/(t^2(1+t^2)^2)>=3/(1+t^2)^2.
Verified coordinatewise monotonicity of the unconditional convex potential, the full transformed Hessian, contraction transfer, and the resulting fourth-moment bound.

Checked the approximation route: convex-domain exhaustion for the inverse-Hessian inequality and smooth unconditional log-concave convolution for the final inequality preserve the needed integrable moment controls.
remaining: The alternative Dunkl-operator proof and its operator-domain appendix have not been fully checked; they are not required for the independently traced second proof. General KLS papers cited for context were not audited here.
issues: Proposition 1.2 as printed omits positive-definiteness of the Hessian (or an appropriate strictly convex regularization). Its proof explicitly uses it. Proposition 4.2 proves that hypothesis in the only application needed for the main result; the standalone statement needs correction.

papers.title: Better Upper Bounds for Square-Root-Sum and Straight-Line Program Positivity
papers.authors: Alex Meiburg, Eric Allender, Markus Bläser

review.title: Better Upper Bounds for Square-Root-Sum and Straight-Line Program Positivity
review.authors: Alex Meiburg, Eric Allender, Markus Bläser

score_reasons.significance: A major improvement for two canonical numerical complexity problems.
score_reasons.novelty: Averaging finite-field presentations and pseudorandom phase-magnitude tests bypass separate obstructions in extracting the sign.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines coefficient extraction over prime powers, counting functions and a recursively accessible product-test generator.
score_reasons.exposition: The randomized argument is well motivated, but the earlier deterministic procedure has several inconsistent thresholds and a search-range typo that require correction.

checked: Traced the complete coefficient-extraction lemma: trace-zero irreducible presentations, prime-power Teichmuller lifts, root-of-unity orthogonality, invertible presentation count and canonical CRT summation give a uniform #P residue representative.
Checked the finite-difference sign encoding and the GapP approximate-phase construction modulo one, including exponentially many terms with polynomial-length indices.
Recomputed the small/large cosine-mean gap, the recursive expander product-test error, seed length and random-access evaluation, and the sampling and phase-approximation error budgets.

Traced the fresh-randomness adaptive bisection without assuming monotonicity in its ambiguous range. Its terminal invariant gives a readable multiplier; the separate largest-scale test distinguishes zero.

Checked a corrected deterministic argument using the procedure described on pp10–11: search all j up to s for the first distance at least 1/8. Before that event the true doubled phase has modulus below 3/8, and its approximation below 7/16, so its sign is readable.
remaining: The literal p5 deterministic pseudocode must be aligned with pp10–11: its j<N range and truncated four-bit event do not express the later first-threshold algorithm. The stated 3/16 and 5/16 upper bounds should be 3/8 and 7/16 in that argument. These corrections do not enter the separately traced randomized algorithm.
The manuscript should consistently distinguish balanced phase representatives from ordinary fractional parts; no machine-checked proof was performed.

review.area: Counting complexity and numerical decision problems
review.summary: Places PosSLP, and hence Square-Root-Sum, in BPP with a PP oracle and also P with an NP-to-PP oracle. The randomized bound lowers the established counting-hierarchy placement; the deterministic bound has a different oracle structure.
review.prior_frontier: The previous uniform upper bound lay in PH with a PP oracle. Merely evaluating modular residues did not reveal the sign of an exponentially long integer.
review.recommendation: Strong shortlist candidate; proof check principally supports the randomized theorem, with explicit deterministic exposition corrections

papers.title: Improved Approximations for Two-Edge-Connected and Two-Vertex-Connected Spanning Subgraphs
papers.authors: Afrouz (new email) Jabal Ameli

review.title: Improved Approximations for Two-Edge-Connected and Two-Vertex-Connected Spanning Subgraphs
review.authors: Afrouz Jabal Ameli
review.summary: Polynomial-time (1040/833+epsilon)-approximation for unweighted simple-undirected 2-edge-connected spanning subgraph and (13/10+epsilon) for 2-vertex-connected spanning subgraph. Conditional stronger ratios require a mu-approximation for minimum {3,4}-cycle-free 2-edge-cover; the displayed 11/9 and 9/7 are accounting thresholds, not hardness results.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript compares 2ECSS with 5/4-eta (eta>=10^-6), and 2VCSS with 21/16+epsilon. Weighted network design is not covered.

score_reasons.significance: Improves established approximation constants for two central connectivity problems.
score_reasons.novelty: Debt-free bridge covering, small-credit cut-vertex exchanges and exact bounded-treewidth completion combine complementary cycle distributions.
score_reasons.depth: The 154-page argument contains extensive interacting canonical-form and credit-preservation cases.
score_reasons.exposition: A useful short version identifies the new accounting ideas and separates conditional improvements.

checked: Read precise unconditional/conditional ratios and the simple unweighted input model.
Inspected type-2 chain exchanges: replacing t+1 cycles by paths and adding at most t+2 connecting edges costs at most one edge; the derived credit change is -7/10+2r+delta-h/5.
Checked numerical cases of Claim 8.38, including h>=17 for disjoint terminal cycles and the 14>13 contradiction when both chains have one 4-cycle.
remaining: Most structural exchange cases, preprocessing, invariant preservation and the final two-algorithm optimization remain unaudited.
This is initial screening, not a large-proof eligibility exception; a substantial central audit is still required.

papers.title: Linear-Time Encodable Quantum Codes near the CSS GV Bound
papers.authors: Rachel Yun Zhang

review.title: Linear-Time Encodable Quantum Codes near the CSS GV Bound
review.authors: Rachel Yun Zhang (catalogue; anonymous PDF)
review.summary: For each fixed even s>=4 and epsilon>0, constructs CSS codes of rate 1-2/s and both distances at least (h^-1(1/s)-epsilon)n, with O(n) CNOT gates and O(log n) encoding depth; no efficient decoder is established.
review.prior_frontier: Previous linear-size quantum encoders gave asymptotically good codes far from the CSS GV tradeoff; classical interleaved accumulate/derivative constructions are a key predecessor.

score_reasons.significance: Near-GV distance together with linear gate count is a meaningful improvement in quantum encoding.
score_reasons.novelty: A constant-size CSS outer encoder is combined with interleaved accumulators and derivatives, reducing both distances to parity-outer classical ensembles.
score_reasons.depth: Controlling subexponentially many low-weight words requires separate boundary enumerator bounds beyond spectral shapes.
score_reasons.exposition: The model and absent decoding guarantee are explicit; no quantitative convergence rate in epsilon is proved.

checked: Checked outer CSS construction: even s makes block repetition self-orthogonal, encoding s-2 qubits per block; the displayed coset superposition is stabilized by X^s and Z^s.

Traced conjugation X(a)->X(La), Z(b)->Z(L^-T b), so distances are bounded by classical parity-code images under L and L^-T. Reversal conjugates A^T,D^T to A,D, giving the two claimed ensembles without assuming their independence.

Checked reversible prefix recurrence and its inverse: two parallel CNOT layers per recursion, O(log n) depth and O(n) gates; qubit permutations are treated as wiring rather than geometrically local operations.

Traced spectral-zero threshold convergence conditional on Propositions 3.5-3.7: maximizing paths stay bounded away from 0 by delta^(2), and away from 1/2 by the outer entropy deficit; each transition then loses a fixed positive amount, contradicting positive spectral shape for arbitrarily many rounds.
remaining: The lengthy boundary/middle expected-enumerator estimates proving absence rather than merely subexponential abundance of low-weight words remain unaudited.
Appendix proofs of the outer enumerator bounds and spectral monotonicity, plus the repaired predecessor arguments, need independent checking.
Author is supplied by the catalogue because the PDF title page is anonymous. No decoding or geometric locality claim should be inferred.

papers.title: Dimension-Free $\ell_2^2$-Sampling Algorithms for Eigenvalue Estimation
papers.authors: Nicolas Menand, Erik Waingarten

review.title: Dimension-Free $\ell_2^2$-Sampling Algorithms for Eigenvalue Estimation
review.authors: Nicolas Menand, Erik Waingarten
review.summary: For symmetric real A with entry queries and squared-row-norm sampling/access, estimates every ordered eigenvalue to additive epsilon||A||F using O(log(1/epsilon)/epsilon^2) distinct rows/columns and O(log^(3/2)(1/epsilon)/epsilon^4) entries, independent of n. Adaptive lower bounds are Omega(log(1/epsilon)/epsilon^2) rows and Omega(log(1/epsilon)/epsilon^4) entries.
review.prior_frontier: Previous bounds in this row-norm model retained polylog(n/epsilon); this settles the dimension-free question and pins down row complexity. A sqrt(log(1/epsilon)) gap remains in entry-query complexity. The cost of providing row norms is outside the stated query model.

score_reasons.significance: Gives essentially sharp dimension-independent access bounds for an important spectral primitive.
score_reasons.novelty: Avoids an n-way union bound by conditioning on sampled columns and uses sparse resampling of the principal submatrix.
score_reasons.depth: Combines spectral splitting, refined operator-norm estimates and adaptive coupon-collector lower bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The entry and row complexities and differences from bounded-entry access are stated clearly.

checked: Checked the row/column-copy isometric embedding and the padded-spectrum truncation argument with the factor-15 accuracy rescaling.
Checked the zeroing error Cauchy-Schwarz argument removing the old dyadic log(n) loss.
Traced the adaptive row lower bound: lazy random permutation gives unseen-block probability <=2/k, and harmonic potential H_k-H_unseen yields k log(k) required rows.
remaining: The refined upper-eigenvalue estimate, full sampled-column norm calculation, sparse-resampling bound and stronger entry-query lower bound remain incompletely audited.

papers.title: On the VC Dimension of Autoregressive Linear Threshold Functions
papers.authors: Ilan Doron-Arad, Idan Mehalel, Elchanan Mossel

review.title: On the VC Dimension of Autoregressive Linear Threshold Functions
review.authors: Ilan Doron-Arad, Idan Mehalel, Elchanan Mossel

score_reasons.significance: Closes the quantitative deterministic VC-dimension gap for a canonical recurrent model.
score_reasons.novelty: A fixed threshold gate simulates row selection, digit extraction and persistence using carefully separated lag positions; the stochastic counter uses an oscillatory modular-count probability.
score_reasons.depth: The construction requires noninterfering coefficient assignments, prompt synchronization and explicit error control over an enormous stochastic horizon.
score_reasons.exposition: The model, fixed-weight restriction, rational bit complexity and small-margin limitation are clear.

checked: Traced the full deterministic row-decoding recursion, modular difference construction, duplicate-bit cancellation and suppression of all unintended positions.

Verified the fixed prompts are label independent and that their shifts synchronize the chosen output coordinate at every sufficiently large common horizon; checked the small-d case and weight bit lengths.

Independently executed 12,020,400 exact integer position checks of the block compiler, exhausting all m=2 label matrices and using fixed-seed samples for m=3,5,9. These tests supplement the symbolic check, not replace it.

Traced the complete stochastic construction: base-4 digit margins, fourth-root-of-unity Bernoulli-count identity, phase and amplitude bounds, affine logistic sampling, counter circuit, coefficient separation and first-disagreement coupling.
Checked that the chosen gain makes all simulation error smaller than the explicitly tiny output margin and that the horizon depends only on dimension.
remaining: No formal verification; the stochastic theorem allows real parameters, doubly exponential generation time and vanishingly small majority margins. It does not establish a practical sampling or constant-margin separation.

review.summary: Proves VC dimension Θ(d²) for a single deterministic autoregressive threshold gate at every horizon T≥d², and exponentially large VC dimension for the majority-of-output-probability class of a logistic generator at a doubly exponential horizon.
review.prior_frontier: For deterministic autoregressive threshold functions only the linear lower bound and quadratic counting upper bound were known. The stochastic statement concerns exact majority predictions with extremely small margins, not constant-accuracy distribution learning.

papers.title: Language Generation Beyond Adversarial Examples
papers.authors: Debmalya Panigrahi, Fan Wei, Ian Zhang

review.title: Language Generation Beyond Adversarial Examples
review.authors: Debmalya Panigrahi, Fan Wei, Ian Zhang
review.summary: Introduces helpful-order active and fixed-global-order neutral generation of infinite languages, proves strict inclusions Adv_NR=Adv_R subsetneq Neu_NR subsetneq Neu_R subsetneq Act_NR subsetneq Act_R=All, and strict finite-example hierarchies. Repetition permits earlier outputs to repeat but never permits outputting an already observed example.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the Kleinberg–Mullainathan adversarial generation-in-the-limit model; the statements concern abstract language collections and presentation orders, not runtime or practical language-model accuracy.

score_reasons.significance: Clarifies how presentation order and output novelty change the expressive power of generation.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses Ramsey obstructions and delayed error detection from canonical enumerations to separate models.
score_reasons.depth: Several infinite combinatorial constructions and hierarchy separations are needed.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions carefully distinguish repeated outputs from previously observed inputs.

checked: Read model quantifiers and the active timing-channel construction using gaps between descents.
Inspected the neutral repetition separation: three consecutive forced outputs have only two possible values.

Read the countable-union proof ranking component generators by index plus detected errors; eventual refutation in canonical order excludes every infinite-error generator among finitely many contenders.
remaining: Ramsey-based active hierarchies, all strict containment constructions and their effectiveness conventions are not completely audited.

papers.title: Estimating a Transition Point from Gibbs and Ground States
papers.authors: Yuhao Cai, Zhenzhang Li

review.title: Estimating a Transition Point from Gibbs and Ground States
review.authors: Yuhao Cai, Zhenzhang Li
review.summary: Under an explicit uniform first-order-transition promise for bounded translation-invariant three-state cubic interactions with a fixed common boundary, at beta=512/epsilon changing the side-length cap from floor(1/(16epsilon)) to C/epsilon changes copy complexity from exp(Omega(1/epsilon)) to O(log^2(1/epsilon)); total spins are Theta(epsilon^-3) for beta>=512/epsilon.
review.prior_frontier: Builds on finite-size boundary effects and Gibbs Hamiltonian learning, but isolates system size as a query resource; the fixed-temperature Theta_beta(epsilon^-2) result permits exponential classical computation.

score_reasons.significance: A sharp size-access separation and matching spin cost clarify an important limitation of equilibrium-state learning.
score_reasons.novelty: One boundary-hidden ferromagnetic pair is uniformly indistinguishable across every adaptive field and permitted size.
score_reasons.depth: Combines an excited-sector combinatorial count with adaptive trace-distance hybrids and free-energy concavity.
score_reasons.exposition: The phase promise, supplied state-preparation oracle and classical-processing qualifications are clearly stated.

checked: Traced the central low-temperature and ground-state results. Cubic line counting gives |boundary S|>=6|S|/L; the C-favoring bulk term is beaten by the common boundary for rL<6kappa, leaving exactly the same A/B ground projectors for both instances.

Checked excited-sector counting: a complement spanning forest encodes A/B labels with at most 2^|boundary S| roots and a (1+exp(-beta kappa)) factor per forest edge. Injective boundary encoding and at least six boundary edges give (12R^3)^6/6! times exp(-2kappa beta) and the stated residual exponential factor.

Checked adaptive hybrid with actual query probabilities under either reference instance; classical query blocks tensor the new state, contraction propagates errors, and almost-sure termination plus monotone convergence handles unbounded stopping. This gives both total-spin and restricted-copy lower bounds.

Checked upper comparison: block tiling bounds energy density by C/L; Gibbs free-energy error adds log3/beta; secants at gamma/2 bound order-parameter error by 4eta/gamma. L=ceil(32C/(d gamma)), beta>=256/(d epsilon), and geometric failure allocations give correct interval updates, O(log^2(1/epsilon)) copies and O(epsilon^-3) spins. Constants yield exp(52/epsilon) at beta=512/epsilon.
remaining: The separate fixed-positive-temperature reconstruction/minimax Theta_beta(epsilon^-2) theorem and exponential classical spectral computation remain unaudited.
Audit is of the supplied-equilibrium-state query model; it says nothing about efficient preparation of those Gibbs or ground states.

papers.title: Merkle Trees Minimize Verifier Complexity in the ROM
papers.authors: Miranda Christ, Oliver Korten, Tal Malkin, Noam Mazor, Shyamal Patel

review.title: Merkle Trees Minimize Verifier Complexity in the ROM
review.authors: Miranda Christ, Oliver Korten, Tal Malkin, Noam Mazor, Shyamal Patel
review.summary: Any vector commitment with deterministic verification and binding against computationally unbounded polynomial-query adversaries to a random oracle {0,1}^theta->{0,1}^lambda satisfies 2+(3k theta)^k(|c|+lambda)>=n asymptotically. For sublinear commitments and sufficiently large n relative to lambda this yields k=Omega(log_theta n), matched by high-arity Merkle trees. Also proves a computational disjoint-product lemma with loss exp(tk).
review.prior_frontier: Earlier optimality results restricted hash usage to DAG constructions. This covers general deterministic verifiers in the ROM, but neither randomized verifiers nor arbitrary computationally secure algebraic commitments. The logarithm has base theta, not a uniform Omega(log n) with growing hash input length.

score_reasons.significance: Closes a natural efficiency question for generic hash-based commitments under a clearly stated oracle-security model.
score_reasons.novelty: A disjoint-product lemma controls adaptively found disjoint witnesses even when their existence is common but finding one is hard.
score_reasons.depth: The new coupling and likelihood-ratio argument combines cleanly with transcript compression and iterative hardening.
score_reasons.exposition: The manuscript gives exact commitment/query tradeoffs and spells out the nonuniform-in-vector-degree nature of the corollary.

checked: Traced the complete central disjoint-product proof: ideal oracle is conditioned on success; maximal coupling is implementable with one true query per tree node; conditional agreement factors multiply on distinct queries.
Verified product of likelihood ratios equals delta, the AM-GM/exponential correction with |I|<=tk, and expectation sum(r_i-1)<=0, giving success at least exp(-k)delta^(1/t).
Checked transcript-only witness normalization, p-hardening failure bound, and fixed-transcript union bounds without conditioning the oracle on the actual sent message.

Checked p=Q+2kn+n^3 suffices for rerunning the honest committer in the residual oracle, the maximal disjoint-family invariant certifies all n bits after k rounds, and the message recurrence gives (3k theta)^k(|c|+lambda).
Verified the shared-random-oracle prefix coding contradiction and the accumulator adaptation under the stated query-unbounded-computation security.
remaining: No unresolved substantive gap found in the main verifier lower bound. Section 7 near-tightness of the exp(tk) disjoint-product loss was not fully checked; it is a secondary result.
