review.title: Better Approximation for Sparsest Cut Oracles with Balance Guarantees
review.authors: Robin Münk, Monika Henzinger, Harald Räcke

score_reasons.significance: Improves a widely used graph decomposition primitive with explicit balance guarantees.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines semidefinite cut information with a balance-preserving fast oracle.
score_reasons.depth: The implementation and its application guarantees require substantial multilevel analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: The parameter range and weighted model are stated; several layers separate the main guarantee from its proof.

checked: Read the weighted cut-oracle statement, parameter restrictions and semidefinite reformulation; checked the stated balance alternative and application scope.
remaining: The central oracle, its expected running time and the recursive balance analysis have not been audited. The small SDP reformulation alone does not verify the headline result.

review.summary: Claims a balanced sparsest-cut oracle with O(sqrt(log n/kappa)) approximation in roughly (m+n^(1+kappa)) log W time, and improved hierarchical clustering and expander decompositions.

papers.title: Algorithmic List Decoding at Capacity and Optimal Proximity Gaps for Reed--Solomon Codes
papers.authors: Fernando Granha Jeronimo

review.title: Algorithmic List Decoding at Capacity and Optimal Proximity Gaps for Reed--Solomon Codes
review.authors: Fernando Granha Jeronimo
review.summary: For every fixed slack gamma>0 and bounded input-list size, every evaluation set of an ordinary Reed–Solomon code over a prime field q>=n has deterministic capacity-slack list recovery in q^{O_gamma(1)} field operations and n^{O_gamma(1)} output list size independent of q. Also claims polynomial-exception-budget mutual correlated agreement along fixed-degree received-word curves at the same radius.
review.prior_frontier: Goes beyond the general Johnson-radius algorithmic guarantee for ordinary RS, building on recent hidden-derivative interpolation. Runtime is polynomial in q, not poly(n,log q) for arbitrary huge fields; MCA is nonvacuous only when q exceeds its polynomial exception budget.

score_reasons.significance: Capacity-slack decoding for every prime-field evaluation set and field-independent polynomial lists would settle a major coding frontier.
score_reasons.novelty: Adds bounded-degree low-dimensional geometric covers and agreement pruning to the differential-interpolation framework.
score_reasons.depth: Combines local rank counting, uniform-rate padding, differential root solving, algebraic families and exact-support isolation.
score_reasons.exposition: The manuscript sharply separates runtime, list size, characteristic requirements and the range where MCA is useful.

checked: Read precise prime-field, fixed-slack and bounded-list hypotheses and rate-uniform padding K=ceil((1-gamma/2)A).
Inspected local-rank counting: a weighted tail-monomial simplex controls substituted coefficient counts, yielding rank O(|T|m^3 r^{1/c-1}).

Traced the new jet-cover argument: nonsingular Hasse–Taylor lifting has denominator H^(2t-1) and numerator degree at most (2t-1)(D+B); singular branches differentiate the highest Y variable, decreasing total Y degree. The d

Read support-pruning proof: any k independent evaluation equations isolate a candidate; a positive-dimensional component lies in at most k-1 incidence hyperplanes, so the agreement surplus gives a Bezout double-counting bound.
remaining: The 42-page Reed–Solomon result has traced its local-rank mechanism, jet-cover recursion and incidence pruning. Complete interpolation parameters and rational-image/MCA geometry remain unchecked; this is a large-proof exception, retaining prime-field and fixed-slack hypotheses.
The complete hidden-derivative multiplicity construction and all global rank/dimension estimates have not been checked.
External differential root enumeration, rational-image degree prerequisites and the full MCA isolation proof remain unaudited.
High significance here records the stated theorem; correctness eligibility is not yet established.

papers.title: Online Shadow Tomography Matching the Classical Bounds
papers.authors: Sitan Chen, Ryan O'Donnell, Angelos Pelecanos, John Wright

review.title: Online Shadow Tomography Matching the Classical Bounds
review.authors: Sitan Chen, Ryan O’Donnell, Angelos Pelecanos, John Wright
review.summary: Online shadow tomography of arbitrary d-dimensional states attains O(sqrt(m)/epsilon^2) copies and a complementary O(sqrt(K) log(m+K)/epsilon^2) bound with K=Theta(log(d)/epsilon^2), at constant simultaneous success probability.
review.prior_frontier: Improves earlier online log^2(m)log(d)/epsilon^4 and essentially linear-m dimension-independent rates; subsequent stronger dimension-independent OFFLINE results are explicitly acknowledged.

score_reasons.significance: Closes the quantum-versus-classical online sample-rate gap on a central learning task.
score_reasons.novelty: Tracks expected excitation energy instead of accumulated trace-distance disturbance.
score_reasons.depth: A compact-noise Fourier channel and operator inequalities control many adaptive measurements without a union-bound loss.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise protocols, failure trees and subsequent-work distinctions are exceptionally clear.

checked: Fully traced Theorem 1.3, the dimension-independent online bound. The excitation decomposition and Cauchy–Schwarz count give (Abar-mu)^2 <= 9(N+1)/n; a state supported on deviation >=xi therefore has trace <=18E/xi^2 when n xi^2>=18.

Verified compact cosine kernel normalization and derivative energy pi^2/(4omega^2). Plancherel expresses the average measurement channel as symmetric random conjugation by exp(it Abar), with that finite second moment.

Checked Lemma 4.8 for F=I using D=U-I, D+D*=-D*D and the symmetrized expansion. Since each Q_j sees only exp(it A_j/n), per-mode damage is at most 2t^2/n^2 and normalized total energy increment is at most pi^2/(2n^2 omega^2).

Compact support makes every bad outcome supported on deviation >3epsilon/4. Stop each adaptive branch at its first bad outcome; integrals of unnormalized states have total trace <=1 per level. Telescoping expected energy then bounds any failure by O(m/(n^2 epsilon^4)), establishing n=O(sqrt(m)/epsilon^2) without assuming nonadaptive queries.
remaining: The separate logarithmic-in-m protocol, matrix-multiplicative-weights wrapper and logistic outcome-weighted damage bound have not been fully traced.

Optimality comparisons have hypotheses: the cited classical dimension-independent lower bound additionally assumes empirical-sample accuracy. This audit does not certify an unconditional matching lower bound for every learner.
Gate-efficient implementation is not asserted; this is sample complexity with general measurements.

papers.title: Improved Quantum Query Bounds for Boolean Matrix Product Verification
papers.authors: Amin Shiraz Gilani, François Le Gall, Xingyu Zhou

review.title: Improved Quantum Query Bounds for Boolean Matrix Product Verification
review.authors: Amin Shiraz Gilani, François Le Gall, Xingyu Zhou
review.summary: For n-by-n Boolean-semiring matrix-product verification, gives quantum entry-query upper bound soft-O(n^(17/12)) and lower bound Omega(n^(5/4)). Establishes equivalence with n-dimensional Orthogonal Vectors up to constant dimension changes, and a polynomial query separation: diameter<=2 has those bounds, whereas radius<=2 has soft-Theta(n^(3/2)).
review.prior_frontier: Improves the standard O(n^(3/2)) Grover upper bound and soft-Omega(n^(19/18)) lower bound for Boolean verification. This is query complexity, not a faster classical matrix multiplication algorithm or a quantum running-time bound.

score_reasons.significance: Makes the first polynomial improvement on both sides of a longstanding quantum-query benchmark and separates two familiar graph quantifiers.
score_reasons.novelty: Reusable left/right coordinate lists and a pivot coverage potential support a Johnson-graph walk with variable-time checking.
score_reasons.depth: The general-input first-common-one treatment and matching lower-bound reductions require substantial oracle bookkeeping.
score_reasons.exposition: The promise version, its removal and the graph reductions are organized around explicit parameters.

checked: Checked the pivot coverage drift: each selected heavy one covers more than t new neighbors, giving expected total left-list size at most n^3/(st).
Checked coordinate coverage and right-list/remaining-coordinate bounds, and the Chernoff size-class construction.
Verified the advertised parameter balance s=n^(1/3), t=n^(5/6) makes n^2/sqrt(st), n sqrt(t) and n^(5/4)sqrt(s) all n^(17/12).
remaining: The general-input first-common-one data structure, coherent walk implementation, full variable-time composition and surjectivity reductions have not yet been audited.

papers.title: An FPRAS for Counting Common Bases of Two Matroids
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu

review.title: An FPRAS for Counting Common Bases of Two Matroids
review.authors: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a fundamental approximate-counting problem subsuming important earlier special cases.
score_reasons.novelty: The soft overlap penalty and external-field optimization turn a uniform spectral gap into frequent exact intersections without altering their relative weights.
score_reasons.depth: The proof connects a local curvature identity, induced chains, a limiting exchange process, stochastic optimization and self-reducibility.
score_reasons.exposition: The main route is clearly organized and arithmetic assumptions are explicit; the numerous broader corollaries require separate scrutiny.

checked: Traced the full new argument for common bases, via the homogeneous subset-convolution theorem. Checked the matroid/complement specialization and the zero-count case.
Recomputed the integrated Bochner identity by grouping each two-coordinate square, including why curvature forces missing intermediate support points to be present.

Checked the translated-measure curvature via derivative limits, the overlap-penalty curvature blocks, and the induced-chain harmonic-extension proof. Passing to infinite external scale yields the displayed reversible exchange rates and gap one.
Traced the crucial defect-probability lemma: balancing zero/two occurrences by a single external-field change, applying the gap to the missing-coordinate indicator, and bounding its boundary rate.

Checked coordinate descent's bounded iterates and deterministic budget, approximate-sampling error accumulation, self-reduction under pinning, product-estimator error, and rational-field/coin-simulation bit complexity.
Verified the required matroid basis-polynomial log-concavity statement against its primary Anari–Oveis Gharan–Vinzant source.
remaining: The broader nonhomogeneous/curvature generalizations and Appendix C applications, including quantum ground-state estimates and all network-reliability reductions, were not fully audited. The main-proof status applies to the two-matroid common-bases result.
Established matroid log-concavity and the standard counting-to-sampling theorem are checked interfaces rather than re-proved external results.

sources.detail: Primary source verifies matroid basis-polynomial log-concavity used in the common-bases specialization.

review.summary: Gives an FPRAS for counting common bases of two arbitrary independence-oracle matroids. More generally, develops a soft-intersection and convex-programming framework for counting coefficients of products of log-concave measures.
review.prior_frontier: FPRAS results covered bipartite perfect matchings and bases of a single matroid; arbitrary two-matroid intersections were a longstanding obstacle. Concurrent work uses a different transport-flow and annealing approach and is acknowledged.

papers.title: Combinatorial Bernoulli Factories with Polynomially Many Coins
papers.authors: Rad Niazadeh, Renato Paes Leme

review.title: Combinatorial Bernoulli Factories with Polynomially Many Coins
review.authors: Renato Paes Leme, Rad Niazadeh
review.summary: Exact rounding of unknown coin-bias vectors to vertices: for rational affine slices of the cube, an interior input is handled without supplied distance-to-boundary advice in expected O(d^{7/2} delta_*^{-3} log(d/delta_*)) flips, with exact rational membership/decomposition operations. Bipartite perfect matching specialization uses O(n^8 delta_*^{-2} log(n/delta_*)) flips. General polytopes require supplied interior radii and a known interior reference point.
review.prior_frontier: Prior combinatorial factories can require n^{2n-1} flips even at the uniform doubly stochastic matrix; this gives polynomial interior complexity. It does not provide boundary termination, negative dependence, or a prescribed distribution beyond exact marginals.

score_reasons.significance: Turns an exact but exponentially inefficient sampling framework into polynomial expected complexity on its full interior domain.
score_reasons.novelty: An unknown-mean random reserve pays both estimation mistakes and signed residual corrections without bias.
score_reasons.depth: Requires exact debiasing, adaptive pilot moment bounds, ratio factories and careful expected-cost cancellation.
score_reasons.exposition: Proof separates exactness from concentration and explicitly discusses why racing with a boundary-valid factory is unsafe.

checked: Traced interior construction: project an unbiased empirical mean onto aff(P), expand from u to reserve correction probability, preserve the pointwise signed residual identity, and realize its expectation by a lottery over projected anchors u +/- r e_i.

Verified universal pilot overshoot and tail estimates, including E lambda>=delta_*/32 and finite inverse-square/log moments; these pay for inaccurate radius estimates in proportion to the mean reserve a. Constant coordinates are explicitly deleted by LP.

Checked the unknown-ratio coin: race yields q=cp/(a+cp), geometric mixing of exact 2q coins yields q/(1-q)=cp/a; the promise cp/a<=1/32 is stronger than required. Fresh independent correction uses a=E reserve rather than the observed reserve.
Verified exactness E[(1-reserve)Ytilde]+a(u+ER/a)=x and cancellation of the 1/a expected correction cost against its probability a, despite reserve/batch correlation.

Read the self-contained scalar factory: bounded martingale (c_l p)^i, positive exponent drift, geometric phase survival, <140c expected input flips and polynomial expected bit cost. Checked p=0 and initial/final boundary cases.
Verified Birkhoff parameters d=n^2, r=1/n and delta_*=min X_ij; all computation assumes exact standard rational polytope decomposition, as stated.
remaining: This checks the central construction mathematically, not through formal verification. The standard constructive polytope-decomposition algorithm is used as a specified oracle/known polynomial-time routine.
Unknown boundary inputs deliberately do not terminate; this is a stated limitation, not an audited guarantee.

papers.title: Large Growth Happens: Gaussian Elimination with Partial Pivoting on Random Matrices
papers.authors: Daniel Spielman, Xifan Yu

review.title: Large Growth Happens: Gaussian Elimination with Partial Pivoting on Random Matrices
review.authors: Daniel A. Spielman, Xifan Yu
review.summary: For iid Gaussian n-by-n matrices, exact-arithmetic partial-pivoting elimination has growth >=rho with probability at least exp(-710 log^2(rho/sqrt(n)) log n), over the explicit range from 100 sqrt(n) log n up to exponential growth.
review.prior_frontier: Disproves stronger exponential-tail conjectures while remaining consistent with Urschel’s proved superpolynomial decay above n^(1/2+epsilon); it is not a claim of practical instability.

score_reasons.significance: Refutes influential conjectures about the most widely used dense linear-system algorithm.
score_reasons.novelty: Constructs a repeatedly amplifying covariance process rather than a rare fixed bad input matrix.
score_reasons.depth: Combines adaptive Gaussian covariance, determinant moments and conic-event probability comparison.
score_reasons.exposition: The distinction between growth-tail conjectures and the surviving Trefethen conjecture is carefully explained; constants obscure some arithmetic.

checked: Traced the covariance recurrence by conditioning only on the current pivot column; remaining columns stay independent Gaussian under the common linear elimination transform.

Checked Proposition 4.15 determinant lower bound: QR separates the Haar subspace from R; inverse determinant-ratio moments reduce to Wishart chi-square products, telescope to product_{j,i}(i+2j)/(n-d+i+2j), and a union bound handles the adaptively selected pivot row subset.
Checked determinant update det(Sigma_next)=det(Sigma) r*Sigma^-1 r by a Schur complement and rank-one determinant lemma; Sigma>=I and ||r||_infinity<=1 imply growth by at most d.

Checked the isotropic conic event probability >=0.16^d/(2d): maximal-coordinate index is independent of the symmetric ratio norm, and a sign reflection gives the final 1/2. Conditional growth events can then be multiplied using the deterministic determinant cap, not an independence assumption.
remaining: The conic comparison lemma and covariance-eigenvalue amplification inequality have not been reconstructed in full.
Final conversion from covariance norm to the exact stated growth-factor range and constant 710, plus all initialization tail constants, remain to audit.
Only exact-arithmetic U growth is established; no numerical-error lower bound in floating-point arithmetic follows automatically.

papers.title: Finding Stationary Points under Higher-Order Smoothness: Trapping Algorithms and First-Order Lower Bounds
papers.authors: Huanjian Zhou, Masashi Sugiyama, Taiji Suzuki

review.title: Finding Stationary Points under Higher-Order Smoothness: Trapping Algorithms and First-Order Lower Bounds
review.authors: Huanjian Zhou, Masashi Sugiyama, Taiji Suzuki
review.summary: Develops value-only and strict-gradient-only trapping for C^(p,beta) nonconvex objectives with known smoothness and initial-gap bounds. In dimension two, randomized gradient-only stationarity for C^(1,1) takes soft-O(epsilon^(-4/3)), versus the deterministic epsilon^-2 barrier. Gives arbitrary-dimensional lazy trapping with explicit polynomial dimension factors and higher-order accuracy exponent nu/(nu-1), nu=p+beta, plus high-dimensional randomized first-order lower bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Extends fixed-dimensional trapping beyond Lipschitz gradients and refutes the proposed randomized two-dimensional gradient-only epsilon^-2 lower bound. Some high-dimensional lower bounds are subsequently strengthened by other work acknowledged here. All rates count exact oracle evaluations; potentially expensive model minimization is excluded.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a concrete randomization question and unifies several otherwise distinct smoothness/oracle/constraint regimes.
score_reasons.novelty: Gradient line integration and reusable boundary reconstruction provide a different implementation of trapping without higher-derivative queries.
score_reasons.depth: The 114-page development combines geometric certificates, high-order interpolation, lazy updates and delayed-information lower bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: Oracle models and known-parameter requirements are explicit, but many interdependent rate tables and long deferred proofs make verification demanding.

checked: Traced Lemmas 3.5/3.6: minimizing f(y)-f(x)+eta||y-x|| excludes artificial boundaries and gives stationarity or projected-gradient control; approximate boundary minimization inflates eta by error/distance.
Checked Lemma 3.9: a gradient-accurate scalar model with 3epsilon/4 distance penalty preserves a strict barrier; normal-cone equality in relative cube interiors yields the claimed KKT bound.
Checked that arbitrary computation/model minimization is explicitly excluded and that fixed-dimensional and dimension-dependent claims use different parameter regimes.
remaining: The reconstruction and line-integration algorithms, full lazy-update amortization and the 20-page delayed-information randomized lower-bound proof remain to be audited. No proof clearance follows from the checked geometric certificate alone.

papers.title: Finding full immersions is fixed-parameter tractable in labeled tour graphs
papers.authors: Hadas Barabash, Jim Geelen, Rose McCarty, Caleb McFarland, Paul Wollan

review.title: Finding full immersions is fixed-parameter tractable in labeled tour graphs
review.authors: Hadas Barabash, Jim Geelen, Rose McCarty, Caleb McFarland, Paul Wollan

score_reasons.significance: A substantial structural algorithm with implications for vertex-minor testing and future decomposition theory.
score_reasons.novelty: Free edges and flooding dictionaries preserve information needed to use every host edge, beyond ordinary immersion testing.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines constructive parity min–max arguments, folios and an irrelevant-vertex construction.
score_reasons.exposition: The technical overview explains why ordinary immersion algorithms cannot simply absorb unused edges; the full proof spans 86 pages.

checked: Traced the certificate upper bound, including the parity loss for an odd component and the treatment of free edges.

Checked the full reduction from signed flooding improvement to free-edge optimization: toggling an unforced free edge increases the optimum by exactly one, and parity forces one improvement call to reach it.
Traced the transition-majority lemma's same-circuit reversal and two-circuit reconnection cases, including the dangerous-loose-circuit qualification needed to preserve a candidate.
Checked the simultaneous-transition intersection and contraction argument that combines opposite representatives into a loose circuit, and the related two-even-circuit combination lemma.
remaining: The remainder of the signed dictionary algorithm, label/color-rich grid construction, 2-edge-cut folios and full irrelevant-vertex proof were not fully audited.
These are substantive checked components of an 86-page structural proof, not verification of the complete O_H(n^5) algorithm or every vertex-minor corollary.

review.summary: Claims fixed-parameter O_H(n^5) full-immersion testing for binary-vector-labelled 4-regular tour graphs, with vertex-minor consequences for apex circle graphs and an algorithmic rooted circuit-decomposition min–max theorem.
review.prior_frontier: Even one-bit labels lacked a polynomial-time algorithm for arbitrary fixed full-immersion targets; the prior signed flooding min–max theorem was nonconstructive.

papers.title: Geometrically Constrained Learning I: Agnostically Learning Adversarially Robust Classifiers
papers.authors: Jane Lange, Cassandra Marcussen, Arsen Vasilyan

review.title: Geometrically Constrained Learning I: Agnostically Learning Adversarially Robust Classifiers
review.authors: Jane Lange, Cassandra Marcussen, Arsen Vasilyan
review.summary: Under standard Gaussian features with arbitrary labels, learns h with classification error opt_K+epsilon and radius-r boundary volume O(Kr), competing with all Boolean functions whose boundary profile is at most K at every radius. Runtime d^{O-tilde(K^2/epsilon^2+K^4 r^2/epsilon^4)}, matching nonrobust SQ exponents up to logs when Kr=O(epsilon).
review.prior_frontier: Extends robustness-preserving agnostic learning beyond halfspaces to the full bounded-boundary-profile class. Prior low-degree regression can learn a robust target inaccurately in geometry: its output need not itself be robust. Log-concave extension is conditional.

score_reasons.significance: Addresses the gap between learning a robust target and producing a robust hypothesis with nearly optimal error.
score_reasons.novelty: Functional lifting adds a boundary-distance coordinate and convex gradient-defect certificates instead of hard polynomial extrema.
score_reasons.depth: Uses Gaussian smoothing, polynomial approximation, convex learning and rounding/partition arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes boundary volume, classification error and robust risk.

checked: Read exact Gaussian and boundary-profile assumptions, including robustness guaranteed at the requested radius rather than all radii simultaneously.
Inspected the defect-certificate proof: convexity and OU smoothing contract the gradient defect; Gaussian change of mean controls it throughout a ball from one noisy squared-defect value.
Checked the Gaussian density-ratio step at auxiliary coordinate zero, giving the 1/sigma smoothing penalty in average certificate failure.
remaining: Full polynomial approximation/existence, empirical convex optimization, sample/runtime bounds and randomized rounding/partition geometry remain unaudited.

papers.title: Polytope Sampling at the Speed of Isoperimetry
papers.authors: Anming Gu, Bobby Shi, Kevin Tian, Hubert Yang

review.title: Polytope Sampling at the Speed of Isoperimetry
review.authors: Anming Gu, Bobby Shi, Kevin Tian, Hubert Yang
review.summary: Samples the uniform law on an m-facet n-dimensional polytope to TV error delta in O(m^2 n^(omega-1) log^3(m/delta)) time plus an explicit analytic-center term; no warm start is assumed, but a feasible point and inner/outer radius bounds are supplied.
review.prior_frontier: For m=O(n), manuscript claims an n^(2/3) improvement over prior runtimes. It distinguishes warm-start comparisons and the cost of finding an analytic center.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial polynomial acceleration for polytope sampling, including warm-start generation.
score_reasons.novelty: Dual-conditioned functional stochastic localization tolerates an average defect instead of requiring every backward conditional to be well behaved.
score_reasons.depth: Combines geometry-aware localization, weak Poincare contraction and a cooling scheme across several technical modules.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise runtime and initialization assumptions are supplied; 59 pages make the dependency chain substantial.

checked: Checked Lemma 30: conditioned on x, each gamma_i slack_i is Gamma(tau,1); the exponential mgf gives two tails exp(-tau/64), hence an average unstable mass <=2m exp(-tau/64).

Traced the new local backward-walk argument: dual whitening makes the potential Hessian between I/4 and 4I on the wider stable region. A Gaussian proposal of variance 1/(64n) has probability >=1/4 of both bounded norm and nonpositive gradient dot product, stays in that region, and is accepted with probability >=1/8.

Near starting points therefore have lazy-kernel TV overlap >=1/32. Applying the stated conditional isoperimetry gives conductance >=c/sqrt(n) after subtracting the unstable mass; the weak-Poincare inequality yields exp(-N/(Cn)) variance decay plus an explicit oscillation defect.

Verified the final algebra of Lemma 31 from its cited weak-Poincare inequality: laziness gives Var(f)-Var(Kf)>=Dirichlet(f), and geometric iteration keeps the additive defect at 2delta osc(f)^2. Checked batching n Gaussian proposals permits amortized matrix-multiplication work without conditioning proposal increments on acceptance.
remaining: The 59-page proof’s functional cooling, ideal FSL spectral bound, averaged backward-oracle comparison and final runtime/error accumulation remain unaudited.
Essential cited conductance/isoperimetry and weak-Poincare lemmas need their hypotheses checked against the full source statements.
No strongly polynomial algorithm to find an initial feasible point is proved; supplied radius information and the separate analytic-center term matter.

papers.title: The sum-of-squares complexity of linear-algebraic principles
papers.authors: Dmitriy Kunisky, Xifan Yu

review.title: The sum-of-squares complexity of linear-algebraic principles
review.authors: Dmitriy Kunisky, Xifan Yu
review.summary: Determines exact degree 2r+2 for real SoS refutations of XY^T=A when X,Y have r columns and rank(A)>r, contrasting with degree 4 for XX^T=I. Gives exact inverse/orthogonality implication degrees in its specified squared-conclusion encoding, and norm-budget upper bounds that can fall to O(sqrt(n) log n).
review.prior_frontier: Prior low-degree/Boolean rank-principle results did not characterize unrestricted real bilinear factorization; claimed comparisons and applications to sign rank, rigidity, tensors and ABPs are not independently literature-audited.

score_reasons.significance: Exact separation between bilinear factorization and symmetric Gram constraints clarifies a basic SoS limitation.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses real vanishing geometry of rank-constrained zero products to remove the highest square terms of any supposed low-degree proof.
score_reasons.depth: Degree-sensitive ideal membership and norm-budget Chebyshev constructions extend beyond a simple determinant certificate.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions explain the nonstandard implication encoding; exact algebraic statements and degree accounting are explicit.

checked: Traced the minimal-SOS-degree contradiction: parity averaging reduces multiplier degree to 2r-2; vanishing of the top sum of squares forces each top summand into the bilinear ideal; subtracting its ideal representation reduces square degree while preserving the total degree bound.
Checked the square-difference factorization and multiplier degree max(D-2,2d-2) on pp18–19.
remaining: The geometric vanishing proposition and its primary primality dependency, matching upper bounds, and norm-budget extension still require full audits.

papers.title: Free-Probabilistic State Evolution and Random Matrix Discrepancy
papers.authors: August Chen, Ahmed El Alaoui

review.title: Free-Probabilistic State Evolution and Random Matrix Discrepancy
review.authors: August Chen, Ahmed El Alaoui

score_reasons.significance: Answers a concrete algorithmic question while furnishing a potentially reusable spectral AMP theorem.
score_reasons.novelty: Strong operator convergence and a controlled terminal rounding query go beyond empirical-coordinate state evolution.
score_reasons.depth: Adaptive Gaussian conditioning, noncommutative limits and stochastic controls must be reconciled.
score_reasons.exposition: The assumptions and asymptotic order of limits are explicit; a few conditioning and projection subscripts need correction.

checked: Traced the adaptive Gaussian conditioning lemma through both half-steps; checked the normalized Hilbert-space covariance and the known/unknown orthogonal block decomposition.
Recomputed finite-rank projection errors and checked the positive-diagonal argument giving a nondegenerate projected innovation and Gram-matrix invertibility.

Traced the terminal-query stability proof: bounded discontinuity-almost-everywhere test functions, tight conditional operator bounds, smooth L2 approximation and the Gaussian integration-by-parts estimate giving 2(1+sqrt(alpha)).

The displayed Lemma 5.1 has a dimensionally wrong left projection and an incorrect conditioning subscript; the required statement follows from Lemma 4.1 with the range projection and the appropriate current history.
remaining: The full Onsager-cancellation induction, the imported joint strong-convergence theorem and the control-to-signing construction with its optimized large-alpha asymptotics were not fully audited.
The component checks do not certify the complete state-evolution theorem or final discrepancy constants. The finite iteration count may depend badly on accuracy and aspect ratio.

review.summary: Develops matrix-valued AMP with strong free-probabilistic state evolution and applies it to signing independent GOE matrices below their typical spectral radius for every fixed positive aspect ratio, with O(1/sqrt(alpha log alpha)) norm at large alpha.
review.prior_frontier: Existence was known through moment methods; the algorithmic question remained open. Concurrent work obtains matching large-alpha guarantees by a different method. This concerns random GOE inputs, not arbitrary matrix discrepancy.

papers.title: Gross Substitutes Welfare in Random Order
papers.authors: Renato Paes Leme, Martin Pal, Neel Patel

review.title: Gross Substitutes Welfare in Random Order
review.authors: Renato Paes Leme, Martin Pál, Neel Patel
review.summary: For signed, possibly nonmonotone GS valuations in random order with value queries restricted to arrived items, achieves optimal 1/e secretary value and per-optimal-item inclusion. For several GS bidders, obtains (3-2sqrt(2))/e welfare; 1/e is obtained for weighted binary/ternary matroid bidders or finite-field representations revealed on arrival. The general GS survival implementation is exponential, with polynomial time left open.
review.prior_frontier: Extends recently claimed 1/e matroid secretary algorithms to GS and introduces signed GS welfare. The manuscript explicitly leaves a 1/e guarantee for arbitrary multi-bidder GS unresolved.

score_reasons.significance: Sharp secretary performance extends to a richer signed discrete-concave valuation model, with a new welfare guarantee.
score_reasons.novelty: Induction on a displaced item replaces weight-order arguments; frozen routing converts single-bidder guarantees to welfare.
score_reasons.depth: Requires canonical-demand persistence, survival-law comparison and value control despite negative marginal contributions.
score_reasons.exposition: Important oracle, sign, running-time and multi-bidder limitations are explicitly stated.

checked: Read survival acceptance ratio and its dependence on a law over exponentially many subsets; did not infer polynomial-time implementation from the prior matroid algorithm.
Inspected the reduction from inclusion to value via containment in a canonical demand, explaining why arbitrary random subsets fail for signed GS.
Read frozen-routing proof: recipients depend only on the sample and fixed label order, so later pools have valid random arrival order; training marginals give the welfare comparison.
remaining: The full new survival-law comparison induction and distribution matching remain unaudited.
Binary/ternary representability and conditional-admission construction, and essential recent secretary dependencies, require checking.

papers.title: Constant-Factor Approximation for Capacitated Clustering\\in Low Dimensions with $(1+\varepsilon)k$ Centers
papers.authors: Kangke Cheng, Guanlin Mo, Hu Ding

review.title: Constant-Factor Approximation for Capacitated Clustering\\in Low Dimensions with $(1+\varepsilon)k$ Centers
review.authors: Kangke Cheng, Guanlin Mo, Hu Ding
review.summary: For fixed epsilon>0 in bounded doubling dimension, deterministic polynomial algorithms with k+floor(epsilon k) centers and exact uniform soft capacities obtain ratios 3-2epsilon for median and 9-8epsilon for means (5-4epsilon in Euclidean space), each plus arbitrary fixed additive accuracy; extensions cover hard/nonuniform capacities.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier polynomial bicriteria ratios grew polynomially in 1/epsilon except planar median; this result stays constant as epsilon approaches zero, but runtime degree depends on epsilon.

score_reasons.significance: Removes the blowup in approximation quality for almost-k-center capacitated clustering in low dimension.
score_reasons.novelty: A rescue lemma exploits acyclic optimal transport so one extra center can effectively rescue two blocks after closing redundant optimal centers.
score_reasons.depth: The combinatorial budget argument must integrate with hierarchical routing, exact capacities and one-sided dimension reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: The soft/hard and one-sided/joint dimension distinctions are explicit; the full 60-page scope is demanding.

checked: Checked splitting an uncapacitated k-clustering into capacity-U blocks gives strictly fewer than 2k blocks because n<=kU. Cycle cancellation preserves integral transportation margins and does not increase cost.

Traced the rescue lemma in full: a bottom-up forest separator removes <3k/(L+1) vertices; rescue separator blocks and all nonpositive-excess components, then choose positive-excess components by saving/excess ratio within the remaining budget. Each excess <=L bounds rounding loss.

Verified the crucial ratio: d_plus < b_plus+k-b+|Z_J| and b_plus>=b-|Z_I| give rescued savings fraction at least (b-|Z|-L)/k. Cross multiplication reduces to nonnegative (b-|Z_I|-L)|Z_I|+|Z_J|(k-b+L+|Z_J|).

Checked approximation accounting: block movability plus transport gives beta=3^z; rescuing an epsilon fraction of savings leaves A+(1-epsilon)sum W, hence beta-(beta-1)epsilon up to the explicitly reserved small losses.
remaining: The network/dynamic-program implementation that finds the existential transport/rescue solution, decomposition derandomization, and all exact-capacity feasibility details remain unaudited.
Euclidean beta=5, one-sided dimension compression, nonuniform/hard extensions and bit-complexity implementation require separate checks.
This is a bicriteria result for every fixed positive epsilon, not a constant-factor exact-k algorithm; all advertised ratios omit a fixed additive delta.

papers.title: Geometrically Constrained Learning II: Agnostic Proper Learning of Lipschitz Functions
papers.authors: Jane Lange, Cassandra Marcussen, Arsen Vasilyan

review.title: Geometrically Constrained Learning II: Agnostic Proper Learning of Lipschitz Functions
review.authors: Jane Lange, Cassandra Marcussen, Arsen Vasilyan
review.summary: Properly learns globally lambda-Lipschitz functions under known Gaussian covariates in (d+1)^poly(lambda/epsilon) time, samples and evaluation complexity, including agnostic regression with a known label-variance bound. All randomness is fixed during training, and the returned entire function is globally Lipschitz.
review.prior_frontier: Improves improper-only polynomial guarantees and exponential-dimensional proper correction; the variance/scale control in the agnostic statement is essential. Prior comparisons are manuscript-sourced.

score_reasons.significance: An efficient proper learner for the full Lipschitz class under Gaussian inputs resolves a substantive constraint absent in polynomial regression.
score_reasons.novelty: Gaussian probability-based extension and a second finite-probe smoothing stage turn an approximate corrector into an exactly Lipschitz evaluable function.
score_reasons.depth: Combines gradient-defect convex optimization, Gaussian isoperimetry and uniform value/gradient complexity of piecewise-polynomial correctors.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes fresh-query randomness from a single stored hypothesis and spells out preprocessing/evaluation resources.

checked: Checked the final correction: OU smoothing of a sup-norm-beta residual costs at most sqrt(beta) in Lipschitz constant; finite fixed probes approximate both values and gradients on a Gaussian-mass ball; projection and division by 1+2sqrt(beta) enforce the global bound.
Verified that clipping, sorting and minimum selection preserve local Lipschitzness and piecewise-polynomial gradients almost everywhere; discarded probes are normalized by the original sample count.
remaining: The Gaussian mass extension, polynomial optimization and the uniform derivative pseudo-dimension bound in Appendix B remain unaudited; these are essential to the polynomial implementation.

papers.title: Approximation and Hardness in Optimization Games
papers.authors: Erik Jahn, Aaron Koolyk, Rafail Ostrovsky, Yuval Rabani, Leonard Schulman

review.title: Approximation and Hardness in Optimization Games
review.authors: Erik Jahn, Aaron Koolyk, Rafail Ostrovsky, Yuval Rabani, Leonard Schulman

score_reasons.significance: A clean quantitative extension of a classical tractable family of perfect-information games.
score_reasons.novelty: Minimum-weight disjoint bases control both players' guarantees, with hidden transversal matroids showing their information-theoretic limits.
score_reasons.depth: The arguments combine weighted exchange, union-rank minimizers and adaptive oracle indistinguishability.
score_reasons.exposition: The payoff normalization is explicit and the proofs are largely self-contained; deletion/contraction notation and a few informal sentences deserve cleanup.

checked: Traced the three weighted-exchange cases establishing MIN's excess-cost upper bound and the greedy weighted-deletion argument establishing MAX's lower bound.
Checked the uniform-rank-two example attaining the range of the factor-two interval.

Traced both oracle lower bounds, including the sparse-paving-style transversal matroids, the fixed all-true-query transcript, the hidden partner exception and the hidden-transversal query union bound.
Checked the union-closed family of sets spanned by disjoint independent sets, its maximum-minimizer characterization and the contraction rank decrement used by the rank-game strategy.

Verified the rank-game upper and lower bounds and the change of first player using a new coloop. The rank identity under contraction is what the proof uses; its informal assertion that contraction prevents spanning should not be read literally.
remaining: Standard matroid intersection/union and weighted exchange results are used as established dependencies. The short final appendix on arbitrary move sequences was not independently audited.

review.summary: Gives polynomial-time factor-two strategies for the excess cost in a weighted matroid base-selection game, matching independence-oracle lower bounds, and an exact formula and optimal strategies for the matroid rank game.
review.prior_frontier: Classical Lehman–Edmonds theory handled win/lose spanning games; it did not give these quantitative weighted excess-payoff guarantees. The lower bounds are oracle-information bounds, not PSPACE approximation hardness for explicit graph inputs.

papers.title: A Few Experts Suffice: Near-Optimal (Private) Online Learning with Limited Subscriptions
papers.authors: Hilal Asi, Vitaly Feldman, Satyen Kale, Tomer Koren, Mihir Singhal, Kunal Talwar

review.title: A Few Experts Suffice: Near-Optimal (Private) Online Learning with Limited Subscriptions
review.authors: Hilal Asi, Vitaly Feldman, Satyen Kale, Tomer Koren, Mihir Singhal, Kunal Talwar
review.summary: Against oblivious full-information expert losses, obtains near-optimal sqrt(T) regret up to polylogarithms using only polylog(N,T) distinct subscribed experts, while switches remain unrestricted. Gives pure-epsilon-DP regret O-tilde(sqrt(T)+1/epsilon), and the analogous optimal-up-to-logs rate for fixed-dimensional private online convex optimization.
review.prior_frontier: Prior low-switching private algorithms incurred polynomial-T privacy overhead. The result distinguishes subscriptions from switches, memory limits, and limited feedback; adaptive adversaries may require linear subscriptions.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the oblivious-versus-stochastic private regret gap and identifies a substantially cheaper online resource than switches.
score_reasons.novelty: Recursive threshold harvesting and sampled Hedge baselines boost a soft minimum of advantages.
score_reasons.depth: Uses stopping-time-safe regret control, progress probabilities and private sparse-vector/binary-tree mechanisms.
score_reasons.exposition: The model and privacy adjacency are clear, with a detailed staged overview.

checked: Read the exact full-information/oblivious-adversary model and single-round privacy adjacency.

Inspected the boosting proof: sampling from the fixed current Hedge distribution misses at most q mass of better experts uniformly over future times; the oblivious sequence makes this conditional sampling argument valid.
Read the softmin identity and split into well-covered experts and exceptional mass, plus the harvesting recursion failure-budget accumulation.
Inspected privacy changes: compare gains against the largest sampled-expert gain to bound sensitivity, rather than a potentially sensitive adaptive baseline.
remaining: The 39-page limited-subscription learning result has checked its fixed-distribution sampling mechanism and inspected privacy sensitivity. The full harvesting induction, progress guarantees and composition/lower bounds remain substantial unchecked components; this is a large-proof exception.
Complete harvesting subroutine induction, progress/high-probability analysis, privacy composition constants, lower bounds and convex extension remain unaudited.

papers.title: Homomorphism Indistinguishability Beyond Graphs: Relational Weisfeiler--Leman and Hypertree Width
papers.authors: Panagiotis Aivasiliotis, Hubie Chen, Andreas Göbel, Matthias Lanzinger, Marc Roth, Markus Schneider

review.title: Homomorphism Indistinguishability Beyond Graphs: Relational Weisfeiler--Leman and Hypertree Width
review.authors: Panagiotis Aivasiliotis, Hubie Chen, Andreas Göbel, Matthias Lanzinger, Marc Roth, Markus Schneider
review.summary: Defines relational k-RCR whose distinguishing power is exactly homomorphism counts from connected structures of generalized hypertreewidth <=k, with O(||A||^k log ||A||) stable-color computation for fixed signature and k.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the previous relational color-refinement characterization at k=1 to all k; ordinary Gaifman treewidth does not capture higher-arity edge-cover structure.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the proposed higher-arity WL/hypertreewidth correspondence.
score_reasons.novelty: Profiled exploded tuple encodings and carefully controlled extension multiplicities handle partial bag covers.
score_reasons.depth: The proof must compare unprofiled/profiled refinement and transfer counts despite unequal numbers of bag extensions.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed definitions make the model clear, although copied cross-references in the central bijection proof need editorial cleanup.

checked: Checked the full-GHD extension partition: every homomorphism extends by assigning the original covering tuples; conversely adjacent-bag equalities and running intersection determine one global map, and fullness forces all source relations to be preserved.

Traced the central reason that extension counts cannot simply be equated with original homomorphism counts. They factor over independent choices of non-bag entries; stable colors determine all grouped extension multiplicities.

Checked the proposed BFS transfer fixes each bag grounding and filters complete groups according to parent-overlap constraints. Equal stable-color neighbor counts permit corresponding ordered choices, preserving the binary tree relations.
Recorded the no-isolated-domain convention used to recover the global map. The result is about homomorphism COUNTS and isomorphism refinement, not a CSP existence lower bound.
remaining: The cross-color consistency/extension-class bijection (Claims 3.18-3.19), converse reconstruction from tree witnesses, and equivalence of k-RCR with k-proRCR require a complete audit.
The 54-page fractional-hypertreewidth extension and near-linear-in-tuple-power implementation are unverified.
Any claimed graph-WL lower bound cited in the introduction is explicitly treated by the manuscript as unverified external work, and is not needed for its upper result.

review.title: List Coloring Uncrowded Hypergraphs at the Shattering Threshold
review.authors: Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku, Minh-Quan Vo
review.summary: For each fixed k and epsilon, sufficiently large-degree uncrowded (Berge-girth at least 5) k-graphs satisfy chi_list <= (1+epsilon)((k-1)Delta/log Delta)^(1/(k-1)), also under color-degree bounds. Linear hypergraphs have ordinary coloring constant [((4k-5)(k-1))/(k-2)]^(1/(k-1)), tending to 1 with k.
review.prior_frontier: Improves Iliopoulos constant k-1 to (k-1)^(1/(k-1)); establishes Molloy’s k=3 conjecture only for the stronger uncrowded hypothesis, not all girth-at-least-4 hypergraphs. Matching shattering scale does not mean the known extremal constant gap is closed.

score_reasons.significance: Sharpens a longstanding hypergraph coloring constant and obtains a color-degree form with palette-sparsification consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Tracks a normalized sum of all residual edge-size color degrees, rather than their separate maxima; refined partitioning transfers to linear hypergraphs.
score_reasons.depth: The nibble requires simultaneous concentration of mixed residual constraints and long quantitative recursion control.
score_reasons.exposition: Frontier, girth restrictions and the remaining factor k^(1/(k-1)) are carefully separated.

checked: Checked the deterministic nibble recursion bounds through (S1)–(S5): list/degree ratio inflation is controlled by s delta=o(1), beta remains at least log^-2 d, and convexity of gamma^(k-1) bounds keep between 1-eta and 1-Omega(log^-k d).
Verified the exact linear-hypergraph constant and that its corollary is ordinary coloring, not the same list-coloring claim.
remaining: The single-step concentration, dependent-event estimates, final local-lemma completion, and two-stage linear-hypergraph partition proof remain to be audited.

score_reasons.significance: A useful generalization with meaningful high-dimensional estimation applications.
score_reasons.novelty: The unifying interface and element–block construction are the main advances over established filtering paradigms.
score_reasons.depth: Joint privacy, friendliness after filtering and application-specific Gaussian comparisons require distinct arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper carefully states privacy on arbitrary inputs and separates abort/utility guarantees.

checked: Checked the PFR composition argument by conditioning on the retained records outside the changed slot, using a mixture of friendly neighboring releases, and charging the bad-friendliness probability in both privacy directions.
Read the concavity aggregation and the explicit block/sample and privacy parameter requirements.
remaining: The element–block filter's joint privacy proof, its quantitative retention analysis and the principal-subspace and other application guarantees were not fully audited.

papers.authors: Jonas Conneryd, Yassine Ghannane, Jakob Nordström, Shuo Pang, Kilian Risse, Dmitry Sokolov

review.title: On the Power of Polynomial Calculus over Non-Boolean Domains
review.authors: Jonas Conneryd, Yassine Ghannane, Jakob Nordström, Shuo Pang, Kilian Risse, Dmitry Sokolov
review.summary: Exponential polynomial-calculus size lower bounds for functional pigeonhole over the Fourier basis and graph coloring in roots-of-unity encodings; NP-hardness of automation with simultaneous Boolean/Fourier extension variables. Conversely, characteristic-zero nonzero encodings whose ratio is not a root of unity simulate bounded-coefficient cutting planes and prime-field Gaussian elimination using specified range encodings.
review.prior_frontier: Closes roots-of-unity size questions left open by degree lower bounds and exposes a representation-dependent barrier. The conference theorem focuses on Boolean/Fourier extension variables; broader extension-variable generalizations are discussed but not all proved.

score_reasons.significance: Shows both robust lower bounds and surprising strong simulations across truth-value representations.
score_reasons.novelty: A unified splitting framework controls pairs of monomials rather than relying on the usual Boolean size-degree relation.
score_reasons.depth: Long arguments must preserve hardness under structured restrictions and simulate arithmetic rules with sparse range polynomials.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully separates the proved extension-variable case, generalized prospects and previously retracted stronger claims.

checked: Read precise field/domain restrictions and random graph coloring parameter range.

Inspected elementary splitting: invertible transformations of restriction vectors eliminate monomial pairs while preserving deduction; hardness preservation is a separate problem-specific requirement.
Read the range-polynomial encoding m_l=product y_i^{a_i}, roots c^a, and scalar-multiplication simulation; the non-root-of-unity hypothesis makes encoded ranges distinct.
remaining: Full size-degree reduction, graph/PHP hardness restoration, automation reduction and all simulation rules remain unaudited.
The SoS consequence uses the specified range-polynomial encoding and an additional simulation; it is not an unrestricted basis-invariant claim.

papers.title: Burnside Problems for Matrix Semigroup Quotients with Applications to Border Complexity
papers.authors: Roland Guttenberg, Nathan Lhote, Mahsa Shirmohammadi, James Worrell

review.title: Burnside Problems for Matrix Semigroup Quotients with Applications to Border Complexity
review.authors: Roland Guttenberg, Nathan Lhote, Mahsa Shirmohammadi, James Worrell
review.summary: Gives quantitative finiteness criteria for quotients of finitely generated rational matrix semigroups under congruences, using uniform bounds on stable/rank-stable subsemigroup images or groups in the Zariski closure; applies them to nonclosed fixed-width homogeneous ABP classes and restricted determinant/permanent orbits.
review.prior_frontier: Classical matrix Burnside theorems do not apply to arbitrary semigroup quotients, which need not have finite-dimensional faithful representations. Border separations use specifically constructed congruences/reduction monoids.

score_reasons.significance: Provides structural finiteness tools with applications spanning automata and border complexity.
score_reasons.novelty: Adapts factorization forests to congruence classes whose equivalent matrices may have different ranks.
score_reasons.depth: Exterior algebra and algebraic-group closure arguments underpin increasingly strong diameter bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The hypotheses are carefully separated; determinant/permanent applications require attention to their restricted reductions.

checked: Traced Theorem 1 conditional on the cited rank-stable factorization-forest theorem. Truncating the height-(d+2) forest at its first multi-child nodes leaves <=2^(d+2) factors. Rank-preserving products have one of |T|^2 kernel/image pairs; each stable pair has <=N quotient classes.

Checked induction on the MINIMUM rank of a congruence class, rather than rank of an arbitrary representative. Decomposing at shortest rank-dropping prefixes gives at most m(n+1) rank-r representative types; replacing them cannot lower their combined rank without contradicting the minimum rank of the full class.
Verified recurrence M_r<=n+(n+1)(1+t+Nt^2)^h and rescaling K_r=M_r+1 gives the stated F_d bound; a shortest quotient word has distinct prefix classes and hence diameter no greater than cardinality.

Checked the restricted permanent-orbit witness calculation: singular matrices sum u_jR_j map permanent to n! product_i(sum_j u_j(x_ij-x_i1)); later allowed actions only scale this polynomial. Distinct projective u give inequivalent classes whereas determinant maps only to scalar determinant.
remaining: The essential cited factorization-forest theorem itself, stronger rank-stable/group criteria, closed-congruence corollary and explicit ABP border witness remain to audit.
The permanent/determinant separation is under a specially chosen commuting monoid of reductions, not general determinant complexity or VP versus VNP.
The manuscript is 51 pages with several independent algebraic applications; only the first finiteness chain and the restricted-orbit calculation were traced here.

papers.title: Global Sinkhorn Convergence and Spectral Stability of Matrix Scaling
papers.authors: Kun He

review.title: Global Sinkhorn Convergence and Spectral Stability of Matrix Scaling
review.authors: Kun He
review.summary: For nonnegative row-stochastic A admitting a finite doubly stochastic scaling B with g=1-s_2(B)^2>0, ordinary Sinkhorn needs O((D+log n+log(1/epsilon))/g) cycles for total marginal l1 error epsilon, where D is the minimum logarithmic scaling radius. Additional spectral/expansion criteria certify small D, and examples show radius dependence is necessary.
review.prior_frontier: Improves a manuscript-compared global term O(n D^2/g^4) to O(D/g), while retaining the known endpoint spectral scale. Spectral certification requires the stated imbalance-gap inequality; input spectral gap alone does not guarantee small radius.

score_reasons.significance: Makes the endpoint spectral gap govern the complete Sinkhorn trajectory with only linear logarithmic-radius cost.
score_reasons.novelty: A reciprocal second-moment potential contracts globally, avoiding a separate costly entrance into a local regime.
score_reasons.depth: Elementary but nonobvious spectral/reciprocal inequalities yield the main theorem; structural certificates require further expansion arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: Quantities, support assumptions and cycle versus iteration conventions are explicit; proofs are detailed, sometimes overexpanded.

checked: Fully traced Theorem 1.1 via Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 3.1 on pp15–21. For P=B^T B, both F(w)<=Pw and F(w)^(-1)<=P(w^(-1)); the spectral second-moment contraction and (Ew E1/w)^2 <= (Ew^2 E1/w^2+1)/2 contract Phi by (1+s_2(B)^4)/2.
Checked the cross-term algebra using Var(w)Var(1/w)>=0, the exact Sinkhorn coordinate update M(w)->M(F(w)), initial Phi<T^4, and conversion Phi<=epsilon^2/(16n^3) to column errors epsilon/n.
Checked T=e^(2D), 1-s_2^4>=g, support zeros and positive denominators; no additional full-support assumption is used.
remaining: The other major results—input spectral certification, buffered expansion, and sharp lower-bound constructions on pp22–70—have not been proof-audited. Main-proof-checked applies to the global convergence theorem just described.
issues: Page 17 has a displayed equality before Jensen that should be an inequality; the immediately following Jensen derivation uses the correct inequality and the contraction is unaffected.

review.title: A (4m - 5)-Competitive Deterministic Algorithm for Online Transportation
review.authors: Aditya Anand, Jonathan Conroy, Ian DeHaan, Gary Hoppenworth, Chaitanya Nalam, Milind Prabhu

score_reasons.significance: A substantial constant improvement for a longstanding online problem and a tight auxiliary theorem.
score_reasons.novelty: A direct deadline-walk reduction avoids the rounding losses of earlier algorithms.
score_reasons.depth: The key existence argument uses an integral deficit and a fractional-to-integral time shift, followed by a careful exchange interpretation.
score_reasons.exposition: A short, clear proof distinguishes the two size parameters and explains the root-patch obstacle.

checked: Traced the full weighted-tree deadline proof: DFS patches, recursive root-patch deadline truncation, the 1-Lipschitz budget function and strict positive integral when deadlines differ.
Recomputed the weighted variance identity and verified that moving backward to eliminate a partially red edge preserves the strict inequality and terminates after at most the number of edges.
Checked polynomial breakpoint enumeration, the smaller-root-component induction, and the conversion from downward cost to the exact 2n−3 traversal bound.
Traced the MST bottleneck transportation algorithm, monotone garage priorities, threshold-by-threshold excess-demand charging and integration.
Checked that label swapping implements irrevocable assignments without increasing total travel and that nearest-garage relocation yields 2f(m)+1=4m−5.
remaining: This is a manual proof check, not formal verification. The result does not attain the 2m−1 lower bound for the garage parameter.

review.summary: Improves deterministic online transportation to (4m−5)-competitive for m garages, using an optimal (2n−3) guarantee in terms of metric points and a tight weighted-tree walk theorem.

papers.authors: Jiachen Shen, Hui Zhong

review.title: Pseudorandom Unitaries from a Random Permutation and One Layer of Single-Qubit Gates
review.authors: Jiachen Shen, Hui Zhong
review.summary: A uniform computational-basis permutation preceded by independent single-qubit Clifford gates is pseudorandom against adaptive forward queries: optimal distinguishing advantage is (1+o(1))*binom(t,2)*(2/3)^n for polynomial t, and Theta(min(1,t^2*(2/3)^n)) more generally. Claims a criterion for other local gate distributions and a constant-query mixed forward/inverse attack.
review.prior_frontier: Removes the random phase from the earlier local-Clifford construction and extends security to adaptivity. Efficient instantiation uses a permutation secure against quantum forward and inverse queries; the resulting unitary guarantee itself is forward-only.

score_reasons.significance: Simplifies the quantum randomizer and sharply characterizes query security and the access-model separation.
score_reasons.novelty: Isolates an arbitrary-randomizer compilation lemma in an exact path-recording framework, then analyzes tensor-product local moments.
score_reasons.depth: Representation-theoretic reweighting, noncommuting projectors and sharp collision asymptotics interact.
score_reasons.exposition: Access models, arbitrary-reference adaptivity and the classical-permutation instantiation are stated explicitly.

checked: Read the exact recording compilation statement and which imported facts are claimed distribution-independent.
Inspected the move of C^tensor(t) onto the Haar record, the common-projector reweighting comparison, and removal of a discarded-record projection at its failure probability rather than a square root.
Checked arithmetic giving the additive 28t^2/N error conditional on the imported recording identities.
Read pair-collision and uniform-superposition tensorization bounds for arbitrary entangled inputs; the distinct/non-plussed projectors need a separate angle inequality because they do not commute.
remaining: Essential FLMNW recording/projector/eigenvalue identities have not been traced to their original proofs.
Sharp leading constant, all-query lower bound, gate-distribution criterion and mixed-access attack remain unaudited.

papers.title: Algorithmic Principles For Multiclass Learning Are Hard To Come By: Limits of Regularization and Proper Learning
papers.authors: Julian Asilis, Shaddin Dughmi, Vatsal Sharan, Alec Sun, Shanghua Teng, Chang Wang

review.title: Algorithmic Principles For Multiclass Learning Are Hard To Come By: Limits of Regularization and Proper Learning
review.authors: Julian Asilis, Shaddin Dughmi, Vatsal Sharan, Alec Sun, Shang-Hua Teng, Chang Wang
review.summary: Constructs a realizable multiclass PAC-learnable class contained in no properly learnable envelope; additional separations show proper learning can require sublinear training error and regularization templates do not capture all learnable classes.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves three questions about proper envelopes, SRM and local regularization; concurrent independent work on the local-regularization question is acknowledged.

score_reasons.significance: Rules out a fundamental strategy for simplifying general multiclass learning, even by enlarging the hypothesis class.
score_reasons.novelty: A tree of missing output patterns forces every successful learner’s image to have infinite DS dimension.
score_reasons.depth: The central diagonal construction is elegant; the wider classification requires independent incidence and regularization arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: The main no-envelope proof is explicit and self-contained apart from the standard dimension necessity.

checked: Fully traced Theorem 3.1. Every finite-path target exposes one public bit per node and uses a target-identifying private label elsewhere. On an all-public sample, the deepest example reconstructs every preceding block; a fixed maximal prefix of mass below 1-epsilon bounds failure by exp(-m epsilon).

For any successful learner and fixed d, either its image realizes every binary pattern on some d-point block, or one follows a missing pattern at every node to an infinite path. This includes all randomized output hypotheses.

The latter case is impossible: use 2m depths and independent uniformly chosen public coordinates. At every unseen depth the output disagrees on at least one of d coordinates, while that coordinate remains uniform conditional on all observed data and learner randomness. Expected loss is >=1/(2d).

Taking m at the PAC guarantee epsilon=1/(4d),delta=1/(8d) bounds expected loss by <3/(8d), contradiction. Thus image(A) has arbitrarily large binary cubes and any proper envelope would have infinite DS dimension, violating necessary PAC learnability.
remaining: Proper-learning noninterpolation, the exact sublinear training-error scale, global/local regularizer lower bounds, and positive SRM characterizations have not been fully checked.
The DS-dimension necessity is a standard cited dependency not re-proved here; the result concerns unrestricted statistical learnability, not computational efficiency.

papers.title: Replicable Parity Learning: Cubic Sample Complexity and a Geometric Characterization
papers.authors: Jiachen Shen, Hui Zhong

review.title: Replicable Parity Learning: Cubic Sample Complexity and a Geometric Characterization
review.authors: Jiachen Shen, Hui Zhong
review.summary: Polynomial-time parity learning on d bits uses O(d^3/(epsilon rho^2)+log(1/delta)/epsilon) samples, with replicability on every labeled distribution and accuracy on parity-realizable distributions. Near-quadratic efficient learning on the standard basis is equivalent, up to polylogs, to efficiently described robust near-isoperimetric approximate tilings.
review.prior_frontier: General efficient sample dependence improves d^6/(epsilon^2 rho^2) to d^3/(epsilon rho^2); a quadratic information-theoretic lower bound remains. The tiling equivalence is for standard-basis distributions, with only a one-way implication from general parity learning.

score_reasons.significance: Substantially narrows the efficient statistical gap for a canonical non-SQ learning problem and characterizes a geometric obstruction.
score_reasons.novelty: Token min-hash and staged budgets replace thresholding the stable partition; robust tilings give a reverse computational reduction.
score_reasons.depth: Finite precision, shared randomness and every-distribution replicability require careful reductions beyond sample concentration.
score_reasons.exposition: The statistical, polynomial-time, basis-supported and general-parity statements are clearly separated.

checked: Checked Lemma 3.1 via conditional Efron–Stein and the at-most-2d support of multiplicity differences.

Traced token truncation symmetric-difference bound, sufficiently independent polynomial hashes and collision probability; the top-quarter chain argument forces empirical coverage, and a union bound over subspaces gives true coverage.
remaining: Stage amplification and additive confidence implementation, robust finite-bit tiling equivalence, and exponential-time benchmark are not fully audited.

review.title: Robust Analysis of First-Price Auctions with Large Supply
review.authors: Jason Hartline, Anant Shah, Matthew vonAllmen
review.area: Algorithmic game theory / auction price of anarchy
review.summary: For large-supply first-price auctions with independent unit-demand values, uniformly bounded support and a uniform positive density lower bound, studies approximate Bayes–Nash equilibria with no overbidding. As approximation error tends to zero, welfare tends to optimal; fixed small epsilon gives a 1-O(epsilon log(H/epsilon)) lower bound. Also develops atomless perturbations and critical-bid structure.
review.prior_frontier: The paper explicitly acknowledges that Swinkels (1999) recovers the exact-equilibrium limit and an extension yields the stronger 1-O(epsilon) approximate-equilibrium welfare bound. Its novelty is the smoothness-compatible structural analysis, not a best welfare ratio.

score_reasons.significance: Useful structural progress in robust auction analysis, with the main welfare frontier already stronger elsewhere.
score_reasons.novelty: Characterizes the critical-bid distribution and eliminates atoms while preserving welfare under small equilibrium perturbations.
score_reasons.depth: Requires asymptotic order-statistic concentration and approximate best-response arguments for asymmetric agents.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states the density/no-overbidding assumptions and acknowledges the stronger earlier-method consequence.

checked: Read uniform support/density parameters and pointwise-in-value additive approximate-equilibrium definition.
Inspected the smoothness welfare reduction: critical-bid CDF area controls the efficiency loss after bounding optimum by a constant times supply.
Read Chernoff control of threshold bids and the contradiction strategy forcing a deterministic limiting critical bid under asymptotically exact best responses.
remaining: Full atomless perturbation construction, approximate-equilibrium CDF estimates and monotonicity/continuity arguments remain unaudited.

papers.title: Dynamic Edge Orientation on Low-Arboricity Graphs: Breaking the log n Barrier

review.title: Dynamic Edge Orientation on Low-Arboricity Graphs: Breaking the log n Barrier
review.authors: Sam Hiken, Nicole Wein
review.summary: The Brodal–Fagerberg algorithm maintains an 11alpha-outdegree orientation of a fully dynamic loopless arboricity-alpha multigraph in O(alpha log log n) amortized time; an offline (5alpha-2)-orientation sequence with that many flips supplies the proof.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the longstanding O(alpha+log n) analysis, including the forest case; this is amortized with fixed known arboricity, not a worst-case bound.

score_reasons.significance: Breaks a 27-year update-time barrier for a widely used dynamic sparsity primitive.
score_reasons.novelty: A nearly isolated time/subgraph hierarchy and batch outdegree reduction reveal a better bound for the existing algorithm.
score_reasons.depth: A two-endpoint density potential amortizes hierarchy additions; entropy-style summation converts a logarithmic height into log log n.
score_reasons.exposition: The offline-to-online distinction is clear; intermediate logarithms need conventional constant buffering at degenerate ratios.

checked: Traced the central offline flip bound. Shortest directed paths from excess vertices to vertices below target exist by doubling balls: all unfilled balls have >=2alpha outgoing edges per vertex but induced arboricity <=alpha. Summing path lengths yields the batch cost.

Checked hierarchy construction and potential psi(I)=2alpha|S|-|E_start(S)|-|E_end(S)|. Parent/child edge counting gives drop >=2alpha|X|+2|E(A,B)|; nonnegativity and O(alpha|U|) leaf potential bound total additions and crossings. Vertex-set telescoping then bounds overlap sum and total |S| by O(|U|log |U|).

Checked recursive isolation: near isolation bounds outside incident edges by 2alpha-1, so targets 5alpha-2-|E(S_child,v)| are at least 2alpha. Excess is charged only to edges currently directed out of the child. Boundary flips and batch reduction maintain the promised orientation at each update.

With Gamma=alpha(|X|+|Y|)+crossings, the log-sum bound and totals sum Gamma=O(alpha|U|),sum alpha|S|=O(alpha|U|log |U|) give O(alpha|U|log log |U|). Blocks of Theta(n) updates cost O(alpha n) to reorient their exterior, replacing log log |U| by log log n. Substitution delta=5alpha-2,Delta=11alpha in the stated BF comparison has a constant ratio.
remaining: The original Brodal–Fagerberg competitiveness/runtime lemma and downstream maximal-matching reduction are cited dependencies not re-proved here.

Intermediate expressions Gamma log(alpha|S|/Gamma) should be interpreted with a constant buffered argument (e.g. C alpha|S|/Gamma), or 1+log, to cover equal/near-equal ratios; adding the O(sum Gamma) term preserves the claimed final bound.
No worst-case update guarantee, adaptation to unknown changing alpha, or bound on temporary outdegrees during the online flip process is established.

papers.authors: Tenghui Lin

review.title: Sharp Second-Order Thresholds for Random Algebraic Coverage
review.authors: Tenghui Lin
review.summary: For every odd-order finite group of order N, uniform increasing-order random subset products cover at median log_2 N+log_2 ln N+O(1), uniformly in the group. Gives analogous fixed-alphabet finite-field results, sharp limsup subset-sum coefficient 1/ln 2, and mixed-characteristic contrast F_2^d x F_3.
review.prior_frontier: Matches the classical Erdos–Renyi upper location and strengthens the recent prime-cyclic lower coefficient 1/(2 ln 2) to 1/ln 2. Binary vector spaces alone have d+O(1), so no universal all-group claim is made; the mixed-characteristic sharp bound uses Yu’s four-bases theorem.

score_reasons.significance: Locates the second-order all-target threshold uniformly across a broad noncommutative algebraic class.
score_reasons.novelty: A logarithmic-depth circuit sieve estimates polynomially rare avoidance probabilities relatively rather than additively.
score_reasons.depth: General-group passage involves chief-series layers, dimension-uniform dependency counts and careful original-stream block estimates.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper explicitly distinguishes target orbits, indexed events and actual full-rank defect extensions, avoiding several tempting independence shortcuts.

checked: Checked the alphabet-stabilizer quotient: simultaneous saturation of targets preserves intensity m_H(B)(b^k-1)/N; proportional pairs outside the stabilizer remain separately counted.
Traced the stopped-kernel argument: three fresh coordinates yield zero-map probability at most (b^2-1)/b^3 because a nonzero translation cannot preserve a b-element set for p>b.
Checked the finite broken-circuit pairing and why an actual unmatched extension has full row rank before extracting its target probability.
remaining: The finite sieve remainder bounds at logarithmic depth, general odd-group matrix coefficient estimates and two-block arguments, and Yu dependency remain unaudited.

review.authors: Dhanush Giriyan, Dana Randall, Andréa W. Richa
review.summary: For fixed λ>1, fixed-mass nearest-neighbour Kawasaki dynamics of nonnegative heights on a k-cycle mixes exponentially in mass n for k=2,3,4, but polynomially for all 5≤k≤n: O(λ⁴k⁶n¹⁰[n(1+log λ)+log(1/ε)]). Also gives fixed-k polynomial and growing-k quasipolynomial bounds for λ<1.
review.prior_frontier: A sharp cycle-size threshold for this fixed-mass SOS model; no general polynomial theorem for fixed λ<1 and growing k. Source comparisons to zero-range mixing not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Identifies an exact transition between macroscopic energy bottlenecks and polynomial mixing in a natural conservative chain.
score_reasons.novelty: Two moving empty windows and a complementary configuration encode a mass-preserving low-congestion path.
score_reasons.depth: The proof must simultaneously maintain nonnegative reservoir masses, avoid adjacent incompatible piles, and invert the encoding.
score_reasons.exposition: The opening, slides, energy charging and reconstruction are separated into explicit lemmas with honest remaining λ<1 limitations.

checked: Traced the full λ>1 main proof: k=2,3,4 bottleneck sets and boundary energy ≥floor(n/2); k=5 gathering/hopping path.
Checked mountain-climber admissibility from zero partial-sum differences; all mode-I/U/T slide changes and nonadjacent reservoir relocation.

Checked slide energy against the complementary w, opening with at most six modified sites, and injectivity: undo the walking unit, recover T/U coordinates, store eight window coordinates plus entering value, and recover the last two by total mass.
Multiplied O(nk³) length by O(λ⁴k³(n+1)^9) congestion and logarithmic stationary-mass term; no substantive gap found in the sharp λ>1 threshold.
remaining: Growing-k λ<1 quasipolynomial flow and discrete-log-concave heat-bath reduction not audited. Classical mountain-climber and canonical-path inequalities used as cited standard dependencies.

review.authors: Marcelo Arenas, María Alejandra Schild, Bernardo Subercaseaux
review.summary: Proves #P-completeness under polynomial-time Turing reductions for perfect elimination orderings even on split graphs, N-free height-3 linear extensions, bipartite successive vertex orderings and shellings, st-numberings and planar peeling sequences. Recovers source counts by rational interpolation and limiting gadget amplification.
review.prior_frontier: Settles the stated N-free height-3 conjecture and peeling question; also supplies an independent proof of the already-known height-2 linear-extension hardness. The reductions are Turing, not parsimonious.

score_reasons.significance: Several natural ordering-counting problems receive hardness classifications while retaining restrictive graph/poset structure.
score_reasons.novelty: Amplification at infinity or finite negative poles filters unwanted gadget orderings through exactly reconstructible rational functions.
score_reasons.depth: The common framework is elementary, while preserving structure and equal surviving weights requires tailored gadgets.
score_reasons.exposition: The split-graph PEO example is fully worked through with precise interpolation degree and normalization.

checked: Fully checked Theorem 1.1’s reduction from height-2 linear extensions. With an anchor remaining, an upper vertex is simplicial exactly after all lower predecessors disappear.
For fixed original order and m vertices before the final anchor, counted q! binom(m+q-1,q-1) interleavings, yielding q/[m! product_{j=m}^n(q+j)].
Verified the polynomial common denominator degree n+1, n+2 positive polynomial-sized oracle instances, polynomial-bit interpolation, and surviving limit #LE(P)/n! only from m=n.
remaining: The remaining six classifications, especially finite-negative-pole extraction and geometric realizability, are not proof-audited. Main-proof-checked refers to the complete split-graph PEO result and central interpolation mechanism. The established height-2 #LE hardness is used as a published dependency.
