review.authors: Gautam Chandrasekaran, Jesse Goodman, David Zuckerman

score_reasons.significance: A major reduction in the entropy needed for a basic algebraic source class.
score_reasons.novelty: The derivative-entropy decomposition and rank-combiner construction provide new routes beyond the previous black-box framework.
score_reasons.depth: Combines structural source decompositions, correlation breaking and algebraic rank arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: The conceptual components are explained well, although several local notation and rounding slips need correction.

checked: Traced the smooth min-entropy chain rule and near-injective partition-preservation lemma, including the coupling and Markov losses. Lemma 4.18's probability wording should read 'at least 1−δ'.

Checked the iterative derivative-conditioning structure theorem: constant derivative fibers are affine and invariant under the selected direction, splitting off a fresh affine bit while preserving the untouched seed variables.
Checked Lemma 6.1's squared Fourier-bias argument for a quadratic-correlated seed, including the zero derivative, bad-seed probability, fourth-root loss and XOR-lemma conversion.
Checked the rank-combiner-to-extractor reduction for both quadratic and affine sources; quadratic bias is bounded by the kernel probability of the polar matrix.

Traced the Sidon-weight construction, polynomial witness interpolation, sparse-dependency dimension bound and determinant root-multiplicity argument, as well as field reduction through the low-rank coefficient subspace and a linear extractor. Integer rank/degree roundings and harmless constant slack need to be made explicit.
remaining: This 46-page paper has not received a complete end-to-end audit: the full correlation breaker, final entropy/error parameter composition and local-source applications remain unchecked.

review.summary: Explicit extractors for quadratic sources over F₂ with polylogarithmic min-entropy, using a derivative-entropy structure theorem, quadratic correlation breaking and explicit rank combiners.

checked: Verified Lemma 5.1 algebra: Hermitian dilation contributes factor 2, real/imaginary products give 4^(-m)(1+(-1)^m product σ), character orthogonality yields joint zero tests, and 2mG<Ω removes modular aliasing.

review.title: Error accumulation in reverse diffusion with an imperfect score: beyond path-space analyses
review.authors: George Giapitzakis, Ankur Moitra, Andrej Risteski, Dhruv Rohatgi
review.summary: Under uniform-in-time L² score error ε² and stated smooth positive-density/Lipschitz regularity, learned continuous reverse OU diffusion has bounded-statistic error ηT+2ε sqrt(1+log(max(1,CP(p;f))))+ε²T; gives TV under Poincaré and balanced-mixture statistics. Information-theoretic identification removes ηT and ε²T; multiscale Gaussian examples match sqrt(log K) dependence up to dimension. No discretized algorithm or efficient optimal identification is supplied.
review.prior_frontier: Standard path-space bound ε sqrt T; previous improvements assumed stronger exponential score-error control. These literature comparisons were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Sharply identifies when diffusion error accumulation is geometric rather than horizon driven.
score_reasons.novelty: Statistic-conditioned negative-Sobolev energy plus variance depletion yields logarithmic, rather than linear, geometric dependence.
score_reasons.depth: Combines adjoint stochastic calculus, Hilbert-space duality, critical-time mixture arguments and a matching Gaussian construction.
score_reasons.exposition: Self-contained core proofs and explicit regularity, continuous-time and computational limitations.

checked: Traced LemmaA.1 from bounded-statistic log-density inequality, localized Girsanov and Itô isometry; drifts differ by 2ε, giving ε²T remainder. Checked Girsanov localization pp40–41: finite path energy from uniform Lipschitzness, stopped-law coupling, TV convergence and Fatou identify the density.

Checked posterior variance identity, weak realizability/Riesz duality, OU propagation Vt=e^{-t}E[V|Zt], Riccati variance bound and interval decomposition; constants imply the stated 2ε sqrt(1+log C) term. Initialization contributes by data processing.
Checked Poincaré and balanced-mixture corollaries. Weak-field interpretation resolves the expressly noted differentiability caveat in F.2.
Checked identification: mixture-score minimization, overlap Poincaré ≤3max, χ² bound from density ratio≤2 and continuity at first TV=8ε contradiction; K=1 and large ε cases valid.
Checked lower example with dyadic covariance eigenvalues and means ε sqrtλ/2: split at λ=e^{2t} bounds score error by ε² uniformly, and whitened mean norm ε sqrt m/2 gives TV Ω(min(1,ε sqrt m)).
remaining: No numerical discretization analysis is claimed or audited.

The optional bounded-support time-to-isoperimetry corollary uses a cited smoothing estimate not independently traced; this is outside the checked central Poincaré/statistic and identification results.
Standard Itô/Poincaré facts are used with the stated regularity; no formal proof verification.
issues: Minor domain typo in LemmaD.7 writes score time domain (0,1), whereas its hypothesis and proof require all t≥0; surrounding D.1–D.2 state the intended domain.

review.title: Dynamic Approximate Text Indexing
review.authors: Panagiotis Charalampopoulos, Jonas Ellert, Jakub Radoszewski

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a basic missing dynamic analogue of approximate text indexing, with applications to dynamic wildcard matching.
score_reasons.novelty: Balanced pattern partitions and locally consistent parsing provide a new anchoring framework.
score_reasons.depth: Periodic fragments, edit distance and dynamic nesting-query infrastructure require a substantial construction.
score_reasons.exposition: The square-free Hamming case clearly motivates the more technical general construction.

checked: Checked balanced monotone range decomposition: prefix splitting, strict descent of all second-phase pieces, termination, the O(kλ) interval count and evaluation complexity.
Traced the square-free parse-tree representation and local update accounting, including why only O(β log² N) anchor neighborhoods change and recomputation costs O(β² log³ N).

Checked the square-free anchoring lemma: a clean block among k+1 equal-level blocks gives a shared context-insensitive node, and splitting at mismatches bounds its required left/right neighborhoods by β.
remaining: The full 60-page construction includes essential periodic-fragment and edit-distance extensions, dynamic k-errata nesting queries and global rebuilding; these were not audited end to end.
The imported locally consistent parsing guarantees were used as stated, not independently re-proved.

review.summary: A dynamic approximate text index with polylogarithmic update overhead for constant mismatch/edit budget, matching static k-errata-tree tradeoffs up to logarithmic factors and supporting character insertions and deletions.
review.prior_frontier: Dynamic exact indexing was near-optimal, while approximate indexing lacked efficient updates with static-quality query bounds. The claimed update bound is soft-O(c^k log^k n/k!), and correctness is unconditional while runtime bounds hold with high probability.
review.recommendation: Strong shortlist candidate with a substantial but limited proof audit.

papers.title: Real-to-Integer Reduction for All-Pairs Shortest Paths
papers.authors: Nick Fischer, Adam Polak, Jonas Schmidt

review.title: Real-to-Integer Reduction for All-Pairs Shortest Paths
review.authors: Nick Fischer, Adam Polak, Jonas Schmidt
review.summary: Randomized combinatorial reductions turn an O(n^{3−ε}polylog u) integer APSP algorithm into real APSP in n^{3−Ω(ε³)}, and integer Exact Triangle into real Exact Triangle in n^{3−Ω(ε²)}. Reductions use a realistic comparison-addition model; the standalone subcubic corollary via Yuval needs multiplication in real RAM.
review.prior_frontier: Prior real-to-integer reduction was for 3SUM; independent Alman–Vassilevska Williams already gives subcubic APSP in a weaker real model. Thus the reduction/model-equivalence technique, not first subcubic APSP priority, is the contribution.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a major real-versus-integer equivalence, retaining combinatorial relevance despite independent APSP breakthrough.
score_reasons.novelty: Extends additive-combinatorial compression from equality/3SUM to graph matrices and inequalities.
score_reasons.depth: Approximate rank, popularity pruning, low-doubling compression and Fredman dominance reductions interact quantitatively.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit ε losses and careful computational-model/concurrent-work qualifications.

checked: Read the popular-edge n³/K triangle count to Ω(n²/K^{2/3}) edges and O(K^{2/3}) iterations; L=K^{O(1/ε)}, K=n^{Θ(ε)} gives the Exact Triangle ε² loss.
Read Lemma6.1 start: approximate rank reduction isolates very negative triangles so remaining negative triangles are approximate zero triangles; full dominance reduction not yet traced.
remaining: Audit approximate rank decompositions, real-to-integer compression and probabilistic reductions.
Complete Lemma6.1 and accounting for APSP ε³ loss.
Essential previous 3SUM framework and multiplication-model integer APSP dependency not independently checked.

papers.title: Quantum algorithms for stochastic nonlinear differential equations
papers.authors: Sergey Bravyi, Adam Byrne, Mykhaylo Zayats, Sergiy Zhuk, Alexander Zlokapa

review.title: Quantum algorithms for stochastic nonlinear differential equations
review.authors: Sergey Bravyi, Adam Byrne, Mykhaylo Zayats, Sergiy Zhuk, Alexander Zlokapa
review.area: Quantum algorithms; nonlinear stochastic differential equations
review.summary: For succinct sparse norm- and volume-preserving homogeneous quadratic drifts, estimates linear/quadratic observables of a Gaussian-initialized and Brownian-perturbed SDE in poly(T,log N,1/ε,1/p,1/q)exp(2||Y||²/p) quantum time. Identifies bounded-initial-norm parameters where noisy estimation is BQP-complete while the noiseless problem is PP-hard.
review.prior_frontier: Prior Carleman methods require dissipativity/weak nonlinearity; supplies a rigorously controlled strong-nonlinearity class. Noise is in the mathematical problem, not quantum hardware; no advantage claimed for all physical SDEs or arbitrary initialization access.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a concrete noise-induced change from PP-hard deterministic dynamics to efficiently quantum-solvable stochastic dynamics.
score_reasons.novelty: An expanding coordinate frame converts noise into Hermite-degree damping that controls a nonlinear degree-raising generator dimension-independently.
score_reasons.depth: Requires infinite-dimensional generator regularity, uniform projection error, sparse bosonic simulation and two complexity reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: The input circuits, initial-state cost, two noise sources and conjectural rather than proved PP upper bound are carefully separated.

checked: Checked Gaussian invariance from norm/volume preservation, expanding-frame damping q/[2(p+qt)], and the L² density-ratio bound using change of initial law and Cauchy–Schwarz.

Traced the projection-error argument conditional on coupling and weighted-energy lemmas: boundary forcing at degree k costs J²rρk(k+1)/λ*, integrated degree-(k+1) energy cancels k+1, yielding dimension-free exp(-Θ(√k)) decay.

Checked uniform weighted-tail convergence, continuous generator action, uniqueness by dissipativity, and the dual backward finite-degree test identifying the limiting coefficients with the actual SDE density.
Checked that bounded ||Y|| and p≥Ω(1/log log N) make exp(2||Y||²/p) polynomial in log N; unrestricted initial norms would not give that runtime.
remaining: Full 51-page proof not completed: bosonic coupling lemma and initial weighted-energy estimate, block-encoding simulation and precision costs, BQP-hardness construction and PP-hard angle-amplification reduction remain to audit.
Smooth-cutoff SDE splitting and cited quantum simulation results used conditionally, not independently rederived.

papers.title: The Complexity of Unpredictability
papers.authors: Aryan Agarwala, Dani Dorfman

review.title: The Complexity of Unpredictability
review.authors: Aryan Agarwala, Dani Dorfman
review.summary: Introduces middle-bit UNPRED: construct a small multiset defeating given predictors. Shows UNPRED in FP implies SearchCL in FP, which implies TC^1-restricted UNPRED in FP; proves exponential deterministic black-box lower bounds and parallel/next-bit connections.
review.prior_frontier: Provides a near-characterization of catalytic-logspace derandomization rather than proving CL=P or resolving its containment. The unrestricted-circuit versus TC^1 gap is retained explicitly.

score_reasons.significance: Organizes several catalytic-computation problems around a concrete prediction search task with unconditional oracle barriers.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses middle-bit prediction, lossy coding and hypercube degree imbalance as a bridge to catalytic restoration.
score_reasons.depth: Seventy-three pages develop reductions, reversible compression and oracle adversaries in carefully differing computational models.
score_reasons.exposition: Main implications and their circuit-class gap are clear; the broader future-directions discussion sometimes goes beyond what is established.

checked: Checked WeakExcess-to-UNPRED: two deterministic predictors per label emulate tie-breaking; their average success at a vertex is exactly 1/2+(indegree-outdegree)/2^(ell+1).
A multiset with all predictor advantages below 2^(-ell-1) must contain a nonnegative-outdegree-excess vertex by averaging and integrality.
Verified self-loops cancel in the imbalance and that label determinism makes the paired edge predicates computable.
remaining: The catalytic compression restoration, loss-coding reduction, circuit evaluation simulation and black-box lower bounds remain unaudited.

papers.title: Data-Dependent Probability Estimation via Sample Amplification
papers.authors: Vitaly Feldman, Satyen Kale, Mahbod Majid, Kunal Talwar

review.title: Data-Dependent Probability Estimation via Sample Amplification
review.authors: Vitaly Feldman, Satyen Kale, Mahbod Majid, Kunal Talwar

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the stated sample-complexity question for unrestricted data-dependent queries with an efficient estimator.
score_reasons.novelty: Reverse-order sample amplification and penalized multiplicative weights control dependence without requiring query stability.
score_reasons.depth: A precise distributional recursion and empirical penalty replace invalid independent-feedback intuition.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear separation of the simple algorithm, sharper bound, computational implementation and limitations.

checked: Checked the one-sample amplifier likelihood ratio and its exact chi-squared variance: pair terms are uncorrelated even when they share an index, giving (support size−1)/binomial(n+1,2).
Traced the complete-run recursion and fresh-sample comparison. Reversing amplification order is essential; the argument does not falsely condition each repeatedly reused sample as independent.
Checked projected MW progress, penalized KL optimality, absorption of the second-moment error and the empirical fourth-moment and concave-log estimates for the penalty.
Verified the sample/update/error parameter choices and the convention that a query evaluation returns the complete d-dimensional vector.

Checked the projection implementation: reduction to a monotone scalar root, Pinsker-based sensitivity, nested coordinate/multiplier bisections, exact mass restoration and duality-gap tolerance. Runtime counts arithmetic operations and logarithm/exponential evaluations.
remaining: The separate Gaussian theorem, smoothed-sample-size theorem and complete new lower-bound construction were not checked end to end. This audit establishes the main discrete upper-bound route, not every result in the 46-page manuscript.

review.summary: An efficient estimator answers an arbitrary event or bounded query chosen after seeing its entire sample, reaching constant mean squared error with soft-O(√d) samples on a d-point domain, without stability or symmetry assumptions.
review.prior_frontier: Learning the whole distribution requires Θ(d) samples for constant error; the known lower bound for this data-dependent task was Ω(√d). The new upper bound matches that sample threshold up to logarithms, but the full mean-squared-error dependence is not tight in every regime.
review.recommendation: Strong shortlist candidate; main discrete upper bound and its implementation checked.

papers.title: Finding Hypercliques Faster Than Brute Force
papers.authors: Josh Alman, Baitian Li, Neha Pant, Kevin Pratt, Ryan Williams

review.title: Finding Hypercliques Faster Than Brute Force
review.authors: Josh Alman, Baitian Li, Neha Pant, Kevin Pratt, Ryan Williams
review.summary: For every fixed k≥3, uniformly constructs Z[1/2] arithmetic circuits of size O(n^{k−εk}) for the k-hyperclique polynomial, with εk=2^{-Θ(2^k)}. Gives exact counting, faster Max-Degree-kCSP and subquadratic fixed-length AP detection.
review.prior_frontier: Refutes the standard fixed-k hyperclique and unrestricted-clause Max-kSAT hypotheses; tensor rank alone remains Θ(n^k). Independent alternative hyperclique work also exists in this catalogue, so no exclusive priority claim.

score_reasons.significance: Breaks multiple extensively used fine-grained conjectures, including counting rather than detection only.
score_reasons.novelty: Mixed partition decompositions plus a low/high-degree tensor-power dichotomy bypass the flattening barrier.
score_reasons.depth: Uniform recursive circuits require combining entropy bounds, transpose-eigenspace decompositions and lower-order hyperclique multiplication.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed explanation of why ordinary tensor-rank amplification fails and precise uniformity/constant ring; substantial technical construction.

checked: Read mixed-partition tensor-power analysis: low-degree row-space dimension sum uses q³(q−1)/2 and q³(q+1)/2; high-degree rank uses (q⁴+r)^{d−b}r^b.
Read exact inductive statement Theorem6: lower-order saving ε and B with 2^{εB}≥(eB)² imply ε/(4B) saving; checked blocking and Strassen base case.

Completed the new circuit proof on PDF pages17–25. The partial-transpose operators commute and (tau+(I−tau)) products decompose the identity exactly. Orthogonal diagonal/symmetric/skew basis matrices have squared norm2^u and the stated integer low-degree eigenvalues, so all scalar denominators are powers of two.

Checked the high-degree inductive reduction: fixing j and the unswapped digits of i combines U and V into one mode, leaving a rectangular(k−1)-hyperclique tensor. Blocking at q^|A| includes the cost of forming the combined inputs. Expanding high-degree operator coefficients and summing binomial tails with2^(epsilon B)≥(eB)² gives exponent saving epsilon/(2B).

Checked the low-degree circuit, not just its rank. The type-dependent biclique partition covers each support edge exactly once; its sides have sizes(q−1)^rho and2^(u−rho), both at least ell=2^((B−1)floor((d−t)/B)). All Q-coordinates are batched matrix products. All P-coordinates are derivatives of a genuinely(k−1)-mode hyperclique polynomial: Y omits j, V omits sigma and each X_s omits z_s, including its sign factor. Baur–Strassen computes every required derivative with constant circuit overhead.

Checked input assembly, output summation and support-edge accounting. There are at most n^(2+epsilon/(2B)) support edges; each left basis vertex has at least2^(d−t) neighbors, so final summation costs do not exceed the main bound. Since ell≥constant·n^(3/(4B)), the total low-degree size is O(n^(k−epsilon/(4B))). Padding to the next q power costs only a k-dependent constant.

Checked uniformity and exponent recurrence: B_j=ceil(8log2(1/epsilon_j)/epsilon_j) satisfies the tail hypothesis, and L_(j+1)≤2L_j+log2 L_j+6 gives L_j=O(2^j). Enumerating the explicit basis/biclique wiring takes circuit size times polylogarithmic overhead; integer coefficients have O(log n) bits for fixed k. Evaluating modulo any odd M>n^k exactly recovers the hyperclique count, avoiding uncontrolled rational bit growth. Division by k! occurs only after recovering the ordinary integer tuple count.

Checked the k-wise product as the gradient in the omitted-coordinate input group. The stated Max-Degree-kCSP and arithmetic-progression reductions have the right parameter substitution, giving exponent saving epsilon_(k+1)/(k+1) and2epsilon_k/k respectively, conditional on the cited reduction interfaces.
remaining: The central arithmetic-circuit theorem, exact hyperclique counting and gradient application are traced. The external LVW18 CSP and DFG+26 arithmetic-progression reductions were used as stated, not fully re-proved. Sparse-join, weighted and listing extensions mentioned without details were not independently audited. This is not a verification of the unrelated external claims about ETH.

papers.title: A mixing time method for estimating the sample complexity of quantum state discrimination
papers.authors: Juntai Zhou, Felix Leditzky

review.title: A mixing time method for estimating the sample complexity of quantum state discrimination
review.authors: Juntai Zhou, Felix Leditzky
review.summary: Characterizes fixed-error sample complexity of geometrically uniform pure-state discrimination by a generalized quantum Dobrushin coefficient on the Hecke algebra. Gelfand pairs reduce to classical hypergroup mixing; triangular phase features give O_q,d,ε(n^(d−1)) copies for fixed prime q and d≥2, resolving the stated phase-learning upper-bound conjecture.
review.prior_frontier: Unifies prior problem-specific Gram-matrix/PGM analyses; prior Boolean phase bound was Θ(n^(d−1)). No efficient implementation of the optimal collective measurement is asserted.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a reusable sample-complexity characterization and closes an identified finite-field phase-learning question.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses the all-ones state as worst initial state within the invariant algebra and conditional Fourier estimates for triangular features.
score_reasons.depth: Combines quantum contraction, invariant algebras and finite-field polynomial anti-concentration.
score_reasons.exposition: The distinction between fixed-error complexity, asymptotic Chernoff exponents and unrestricted average-error instability is particularly clear.

checked: Traced the GU characterization: PGM fidelity formula, covariant measurement equalizing conditional errors, majority amplification, and trace-distance contraction under the Schur channel nρ proving the all-ones state worst.
Checked generalized Dobrushin lower/upper time bounds, including attainment of the positive supremum since (1−κ(T^s))/s→0, and primitivity equivalence through off-diagonal Gram moduli.
Checked triangular Fourier proof by conditioning on all earlier sampled coordinates, factoring conditional characters across independent copies, Parseval/Jensen, and summing conditional TV errors.

Checked degree-d application: canonical reduced monomials remove global phase, coefficient polynomial nonzero probability ≥q^(-(d-l)), phase separation ≥4sin²(π/q), hence λ≤1−4sin²(π/q)/q^(d+1), and each block has O_d(n^(d−1)) coordinates.
remaining: General noncommutative mixed-state/minimax extensions, even-composite-q Boolean phases, hypergraph formula and full Gelfand-pair hypergroup construction not audited. Published GU-PGM optimality used as a standard dependency.

papers.title: Kadison--Singer in Deterministic Polynomial Time
papers.authors: Ekene Ezeunala, Haotian Jiang

review.title: Kadison--Singer in Deterministic Polynomial Time
review.authors: Ekene Ezeunala, Haotian Jiang
review.summary: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time signing of rational Hermitian rank-at-most-one matrices with norm at most 13||sum H_i^2||^(1/2), implying Weaver KS2 with constant 13/2.
review.prior_frontier: Turns the existential rank-one discrepancy guarantee into polynomial time with a worse constant than the known existential 4; acknowledges concurrent independent polynomial algorithms by Kathuria and Song–Yue, with the latter sharing the potential.

score_reasons.significance: Algorithmic resolution of a central discrepancy formulation of Kadison–Singer, with a general rank-one variance-sensitive guarantee.
score_reasons.novelty: Coupled matrix inverse barriers and concave coordinate reservoirs allow endpoint moves or a certified negative-curvature descent.
score_reasons.depth: The proof balances noncommutative KKT sensitivities, a low-codimension covariance choice and crossed-weight drift cancellation.
score_reasons.exposition: The analytic core is detailed; the quantitative derivative and finite-precision implementation justification is compressed and requires supplementation.

checked: Traced the full analytic argument on pp4–24: normalization, compact attainment, positive dual matrices, tight constraints, strict convexity/uniqueness and invertibility of the KKT linearization.
Checked the feasible fixed-t path and second-variation bound (11/4)E_h-c sum chi_i h_i²(b_i p_i+a_i q_i), including the 4/3 Young inequality and chi positivity.

Recomputed the scalar bounds, chi/(alpha beta)>=5/9 polynomial certificate, weighted Frobenius feedback estimates and covariance constants: beta*=3/8, kappa=25/8, c=40 leave trace n/225 and energy factor 8.
Verified drift cancellation gives 11-5c/18=-1/9 and leaves coordinate decrease 1/2-11/40>0. The regularization bounds feedback inverse polynomially and supplies state-independent movement.

Verified the primary covariance dependency: Bansal, Theory of Computing 20(6), Theorem 2.5 p10, gives precisely range in the chosen subspace, diagonal <=1, covariance <=kappa diagonal and trace >=dimension-ambient/kappa.

Supplied the missing quantitative sensitivity argument: L inverse, H, and their inverses have polynomial bounds; the scalar KKT Schur denominator e^T L^(-1) H L^(-1)e is at least lambda_min(H)||e||²/||L||², hence inverse polynomial. Differentiating this bounded system gives polynomial second/third derivative bounds away from endpoints. Choosing s<=sigma/2 and bounding on the sigma/2 interior keeps the Taylor segment in that region.

Checked deterministic gradient/negative-Hessian choice from the drift certificate and finite precision: inverse-polynomial descent permits polynomial-bit value/gradient/Hessian approximations and rational steps; the strict initial constant slack below 13 permits accumulated approximation error.
remaining: The cited covariance theorem is used as a verified published theorem, not reproved. No executable implementation or exhaustive formal proof was constructed.
resolved_notes: Page 6 attributes polynomial derivative bounds to compactness alone, which only proves finiteness; the quantitative KKT bounds on pp10–11 supply the needed polynomial bound as explained in this audit. Use sigma/2 interior bounds for the entire Taylor segment.

Page 18 last expression for c² b-tilde² swaps u and v: it should be r^(2/3)v²(1-x+2xu/3)/(1+x-2xv/3). The preceding expression is correct, and the maximum-at-u=v=1 bound remains valid. Visually checked PDF p18.

Page 19 one intermediate expression prints 5(1-x²) rather than 5(1-x)²; the subsequent polynomial and completed-square identity are correct for the latter. Other minor endpoint-direction typographical slips do not change the argument.

papers.title: Optimal tomography of bosonic and fermionic Gaussian states
papers.authors: Senrui Chen, Marco Fanizza, Filippo Girardi, Ludovico Lami, Francesco Anna Mele, Michael Walter, Freek Witteveen

review.title: Optimal tomography of bosonic and fermionic Gaussian states
review.authors: Senrui Chen, Marco Fanizza, Filippo Girardi, Ludovico Lami, Francesco Anna Mele, Michael Walter, Freek Witteveen

score_reasons.significance: A clean optimal characterization for important structured quantum-state families.
score_reasons.novelty: Generalized random purification and symmetry representation theory unify the models.
score_reasons.depth: Noncompact bosonic symmetries and mixed-state reduction require substantial representation-theoretic analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear high-level decomposition and explicit information-theoretic versus implementation distinction.

checked: Checked the stated reduction from a purified-distance upper bound to trace distance and from pure-state lower bounds to both metrics, and inspected the pure/mixed tomography interfaces.
remaining: The representation-theoretic random/quasi-purification construction, concentration estimates and matching lower bounds have not been audited.

review.summary: Determines information-theoretic tomography sample complexity for bosonic and fermionic Gaussian states: Θ((m²+log(1/δ))/ε²), independently of energy bounds and for both pure and mixed states.
review.prior_frontier: Gaussian-state tomography lacked this complete optimal sample-complexity characterization. This manuscript explicitly merges and extends two prior works; the proposed collective measurements are not claimed to be efficiently implementable experimental schemes.
review.recommendation: Strong result; retain for comparison, requiring a substantial proof audit before selection.

papers.title: Complexity of Autobidding Equilibria in GSP Sponsored Shopping
papers.authors: Kristoffer Arnsfelt Hansen, Yuhao Li, Xinhao Nie

review.title: Complexity of Autobidding Equilibria in GSP Sponsored Shopping
review.authors: Kristoffer Arnsfelt Hansen, Yuhao Li, Xinhao Nie
review.summary: In single-auction GSP sponsored shopping without self-pricing, exact budget- and ROI-constrained autobidding equilibria are in FIXP; positive inverse-exponential-accuracy approximations are in PPAD, and every fixed γ<1 is PPAD-hard even when all items display with unit click-through rates. Some exact equilibria are necessarily irrational.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier work established existence and welfare; prior pacing hardness used multiple auctions. Manuscript claims first bounded-forward-span Pure-Circuit hardness; references not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Nearly complete complexity classification for a meaningful multi-item position-auction model.
score_reasons.novelty: Quantile coupling compresses rankings; one-sided payment rounding preserves exact feasibility; bounded-forward-span gates isolate hardness in a shared ranking.
score_reasons.depth: Upper-bound circuit and constant-approximation hardness need distinct nontrivial constructions.
score_reasons.exposition: States γ=0 versus positive-γ membership distinctions and the no-self-pricing model explicitly.

checked: Traced ROI payment rounding bound 0≤Pi−Pihat≤γVi and fixed-point clamp proof: any infeasibility forces αi=1, where bid consistency proves Pi≤Vi; strict underpayment forces αi=A. Vi=0 is treated.
Read structural requirement: forward span ≤5, backward span unrestricted; this is not a bounded-bandwidth circuit claim.
remaining: Quantile allocation circuit, linear-OPT external framework and exact FIXP construction.
Complete bounded-span Pure-Circuit reduction and both auction hardness gadget analyses.

papers.title: Scheduling Jobs to Maximize Minimum Fractional Completion
papers.authors: Kunal Agrawal, Sanjoy Baruah, Gregory Kehne, Jubayer Nirjhor, Kei Rockwell, Nicole Wein

review.title: Scheduling Jobs to Maximize Minimum Fractional Completion
review.authors: Kunal Agrawal, Sanjoy Baruah, Gregory Kehne, Jubayer Nirjhor, Kei Rockwell, Nicole Wein
review.summary: Preemptive single-machine online max-min fractional completion with release times/deadlines admits tight 1/2 competitive ratio, even against randomized oblivious algorithms, and O(log³ n) per arrival implementation. Weighted variant, lexicographic no-constant lower bound and O(n log² n) exact offline densest-interval algorithm are also claimed.
review.prior_frontier: Introduces this particular job-wise max-min objective; differs from throughput and total fractional value. Strongly polynomial offline density computation improves the stated quadratic benchmark, not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A complete optimal ratio for a natural fairness objective with an unusually efficient online implementation.
score_reasons.novelty: Scaled EDF adjusts all completion targets to the decreasing prefix optimum; extremal-instance transformations isolate wasted processing.
score_reasons.depth: The competitive argument and online densest-interval structure are distinct substantial components.
score_reasons.exposition: The overview is helpful, but infinitesimal-job arguments need careful reading, and the abstract reverses the weight convention used in Section 5.

checked: Checked the extremal family calculation: with interval lengths w_i/W and prefix benchmark 1/(sum_{j≤i}w_j), wasted work is sum_{i<j}w_iw_j/W²≤1/2.
Checked weighted benchmark min{min λ_i,1/ρ*} for the Section-5 objective min_i λ_i c_i/w_i, and why naive uncapped rescaling fails; the pilot-run rescaling eliminates the unit cap.
Inspected transformation lemmas and lower-bound interval-density calculation, without treating them as a completed audit.
remaining: The 59-page manuscript requires verification of finite-job approximation/limits behind Lemma 4.8 and preservation of failure by all transformations; small positive jobs may straddle boundaries despite the displayed exact accounting.
Randomized oblivious lower bound, lexicographic impossibility and polylogarithmic dynamic density data structure remain unaudited.
issues: Presentation: the abstract says min f_i/λ_i, whereas Section 5 and the algorithm use min λ_i f_i. Reciprocal reparameterization gives an equivalent problem family, but the algorithm and prose must use one convention. Lemma 4.9 statement reverses the harder-instance direction proved immediately below it.

papers.title: Quantum Copy Complexity of Testing Monotonicity and Other Properties
papers.authors: Preksha Naik

review.title: Quantum Copy Complexity of Testing Monotonicity and Other Properties
review.authors: Preksha Naik
review.summary: For uniform Boolean quantum function-state copies and arbitrary collective measurements, monotonicity testing has copy complexity Theta(min(n/epsilon^3,n^(3/2)/epsilon^2)) over 2^(-sqrt(n)/200)<=epsilon<=1/128. Also gives Omega(n²) lower bounds for union-closedness and 2-monotonicity.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the prior soft-O(n²/epsilon²) upper bound and trivial Omega(1/epsilon) lower bound. These are copy bounds, not coherent-query complexity or computational runtime guarantees.

score_reasons.significance: Closes a large quantum-sample complexity gap for a canonical Boolean property across a broad accuracy range.
score_reasons.novelty: A path-test observable supplies an upper bound; coherent Poissonization converts independent local-function constructions into tensor-factorizable Gram matrices.
score_reasons.depth: Requires delicate local fidelity estimates and tuning between block weights, band widths and distance from monotonicity.
score_reasons.exposition: Access models and the lower-bound accuracy window are explicit and separated from the classical and quantum-query settings.

checked: Checked the coherent Poisson-state normalization and overlap identity exp(-lambda dist(f,g)); additive disjoint-block distances then factor exactly over blocks.
Checked the independent reversed-dictator distance mean/variance and the Chebyshev bound 4p_max/(rho beta); this is distinct from the subsequent quantum distinguishability bound.
remaining: The block Gram-isometry, local fidelity estimates, de-Poissonization, parameter optimization and path-observable variance bounds remain unaudited.

review.title: Testable Sanitization via Boundary Geometry
review.authors: Yang Cai, Katerina Mamali, Katerina Sotiraki, Zihan Yu, Manolis Zampetakis

score_reasons.significance: A meaningful framework connecting backdoor sanitization and adversarial robustness.
score_reasons.novelty: Geometric certification and repair allow guarantees unavailable to direct testing.
score_reasons.depth: Combines smoothing, geometric lower bounds and curvature-sensitive guarantees.
score_reasons.exposition: Model assumptions and completeness/soundness roles are explicit, though the full 86-page development is lengthy.

checked: Inspected the exact radius/query-complexity tradeoff and the regularity/curvature assumptions; applications to polynomial thresholds and networks require additional randomness assumptions.
remaining: Smoothing soundness, adversarial lower bounds and smooth-boundary extensions have not received a proof audit.

review.summary: Introduces testable sanitization: reject a classifier or return a nearby robust classifier, with matched dimension-dependent approximation barriers and improved accuracy under boundary curvature assumptions.
review.prior_frontier: General black-box robustness testing faces impossibility results. Sanitization relaxes acceptance to permit repair; efficient general guarantees lose Θ(√(d/log d)) in robustness radius, and curvature assumptions enter completeness for stronger accuracy.
review.recommendation: Solid candidate, below the highest-priority breakthroughs pending comparison.

papers.title: RARE: Response-Aware Rational Equilibrium in Budget-Constrained Pricing Games
papers.authors: Bhaskar Ray Chaudhury, Jugal Garg, Xin Huang, Eklavya Sharma

review.title: RARE: Response-Aware Rational Equilibrium in Budget-Constrained Pricing Games
review.authors: Bhaskar Ray Chaudhury, Jugal Garg, Xin Huang, Eklavya Sharma
review.summary: Defines response-aware equilibrium requiring each responder to weakly gain relative to the post-deviation profile. Under continuous allocation and continuous strictly monotone utilities, exact RARE exists for rivalrous goods, and bavg/bmin-approximate RARE for non-rivalrous goods (exact for equal budgets). A guarantee-revenue oracle dynamic reaches additive δ stability in floor(B/δ) rounds in the exact settings.
review.prior_frontier: Pure Nash may fail in these budgeted pricing games; a new weaker response-aware notion supplies existence, not a Nash-equilibrium existence theorem. Lean verification is claimed but artifacts were not run.

score_reasons.significance: A substantive new stability notion with general existence, though its economic/algorithmic utility depends on coordinated counterresponses.
score_reasons.novelty: Nested KKM and compact response caps address both simultaneous individual rationality and nonclosed unbounded response sets.
score_reasons.depth: Proves continuity/limit variants, compactness and oracle convergence with unequal-budget limitations.
score_reasons.exposition: Careful counterexamples and distinctions between continuous allocation and selectable limiting allocations.

checked: Read inner KKM box-boundary lemma and market-share restoration: gains sum to zero and lower-coordinate faces cannot gain, providing the covering property.
Read compactness fix for outer deviation/response sets and sequential-limit proof of closedness; unrestricted Cj need not be closed, explicitly acknowledged.
remaining: Unbounded-deviation deterrence, full outer covering argument and convergence proof.
Complexity of computing guarantee revenue remains open; round bound is not polynomial-time implementation.
Lean source and its precise theorem correspondence not checked.

papers.title: Multiplying matrices via polynomials: operational asymptotic spectrum barrier
papers.authors: Alimzhan Amanov, Maxim van den Berg, Jeroen Zuiddam

review.title: Multiplying matrices via polynomials: operational asymptotic spectrum barrier
review.authors: Alimzhan Amanov, Maxim van den Berg, Jeroen Zuiddam
review.summary: Defines a formal operational preorder generated by specified polynomial-multiplication degenerations, direct/partial sums and tensor products. Proves these ingredients cannot yield square exponent below 9/4 or improve the stated piecewise rectangular bound, even after asymptotic closure. Also recovers existing any-field upper bounds.
review.prior_frontier: A limitation of a curated proof system, not a lower bound ω≥9/4 for unrestricted matrix multiplication. The paper explicitly attributes the 9/4 algorithm and rectangular bounds to prior/concurrent work.

score_reasons.significance: Precisely identifies what additional ingredients are necessary to advance a major new matrix-multiplication method.
score_reasons.novelty: Constructs explicit operational spectral functionals on formal expressions, with ℓ_p aggregation for partial sums.
score_reasons.depth: The central piecewise functional must satisfy concavity, tripling and catalyst-separation inequalities simultaneously for every rectangular shape.
score_reasons.exposition: The distinction between formal combinations and actual tensors prevents the barrier from being overstated.

checked: Traced the full operational-barrier proof in Section 5: p_i=θ_i/((1−θ_j)(1−θ_k)) lies in (0,1), the two formula branches match C¹, and the second-derivative bracket is increasing up to zero at the boundary, giving concavity.

Verified tripling from the asymptotic affine slope, and both multiplicative bounds of Proposition 5.8(iv). Hölder with m^(1−p) proves catalyst separation; all listed restriction and isomorphism rules preserve the functional.
Checked optimizing θ for c(a+b)>ab gives (ab+bc+ca)²/(4abc), while θ_1→0 yields a+b in the other regime; symmetric θ gives 3/4 per leg and n^(9/4).
Checked tensor-power multiplicativity and normalization remove 2^o(n) overhead, extending the barrier to asymptotic closure. No substantive gap found in Theorem 5.4.
remaining: Sections 3–4 recovering the actual degeneration upper bounds and the full operational-spectrum maximum characterization were not independently audited. Remark 5.12 explicitly omits its proof and is not needed for the checked barrier.

sources.detail: Exact generating rules and barrier theorem
Functional on formal expressions, not arbitrary tensors

papers.title: Correlated Group Actions: Founding Cryptography on S4 and Sn
papers.authors: Donald Beaver

review.title: Correlated Group Interactions: Founding Cryptography on S4 and Sn
review.authors: Donald Beaver
review.summary: A deterministic table protocol extracts one perfect semi-honest random oblivious transfer from an asymmetrically observed uniform S4 permutation, with one ternary public message. Also claims a reverse simulation proving optimality and linear OT extraction from Sn. The forward 24-case protocol checks, but the claimed secure reverse simulation leaks information about Alice’s output hand.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript compares one OT per S4 sample against generic distillation rate 1/2, and linear Sn extraction against rate 1/27. Those historical comparisons were not independently established.

score_reasons.significance: A concrete small correlated source supports perfect one-shot OT, but advertised resource equivalence is not proved by the supplied reverse protocol.
score_reasons.novelty: Custom group/table structure avoids asymptotic distillation.
score_reasons.depth: Finite conditional distributions are transparent; larger-deck extensions require further work.
score_reasons.exposition: Tables permit exact checking, but ordered versus unordered hands and reverse privacy are insufficiently distinguished.

checked: Enumerated all 24 permutations: outputs agree, all eight random-OT triples occur three times, Alice sees both selection bits equally, and each Bob view leaves the unchosen bit balanced.
Examined reverse protocol, Theorem 5.1, and its claimed conditional-independence proof.
remaining: Sn extraction and MPC composition not audited; manuscript explicitly does not formally prove composability.
issues: Theorem 5.1 reverse privacy is false for the displayed protocol: conditional on Bob’s output card 0, Alice’s unordered hand is each of {1,2},{1,3},{2,3} with probability 1/3. Conditional additionally on public message X, only {1,2} and {1,3} remain possible, so the transcript leaks Alice’s output. The proof confuses a joint probability with conditioning on the public transcript. This invalidates the presented optimality reduction, not the verified forward extraction.

papers.authors: Benny Applebaum

review.title: Quadratic Statistical Randomized Encoding for All Functions
review.authors: Benny Applebaum

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a longstanding central randomized-encoding question with multiple cryptographic consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: A constant-leakage quadratic gadget is amplified through iterated Reed–Muller sharing.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines exact leakage structure, coding-theoretic likelihood moments and cubic contraction.
score_reasons.exposition: The proof architecture and the distinction between general contraction and the special initial leakage calculation are clearly exposed.

checked: Exhaustively checked the basic quadratic decoding identity on all 1,024 input/random-tape combinations; traced the exact equality-leakage simulator and its bijective change of random variables.
Checked RM(1,4) two-privacy, three-multiplicativity, parity-constrained child-output simulation and preservation of affine symmetry and degree under recursion.

Traced the likelihood-Gram product-reference calculation, posterior comparison lemma and cubic-contraction argument; these correctly avoid treating correlated child transcripts as independent under their actual distribution.

Independently enumerated all 4,096 binary 3×4 matrices, reproduced the rank counts and exact P(1/16), and verified both scalar entry steps and constant 113 using rational arithmetic. Reproducible script and audit artifact are included.
Checked the recursion depth, leaf count and correctness/privacy parameter composition conditional on the special two-level entry lemma.
remaining: The decisive specialized two-level leakage estimate in Appendices B–D has not been independently replayed; the checked scalar steps start from its stated bound.
The 65-page manuscript also contains the ZPP gadget, entropy-preserving regularity and multiple cryptographic application reductions; these and the imported locality reduction were not fully audited.

review.summary: Claims statistical randomized encodings of degree 2 and locality 3 for every finite function, with efficient encodings for NC¹ and specified log-space classes, resolving the degree-two universality question with negligible error.
review.prior_frontier: Degree 3/locality 4 was universal with perfect privacy; degree 2 is not universal with perfect privacy, and negligible statistical error had remained open. Efficient encodings for all polynomial-time functions additionally assume one-way functions in NC¹ and provide computational privacy.
review.recommendation: Very strong shortlist candidate with an explicit large-proof qualification.

review.title: Packing Bins in the Euclidean Plane: An Almost-Optimal Approximation for Unsplittable Capacitated Vehicle Routing
review.authors: Jannis Blauth, Fabrizio Grandoni, Bence Mátravölgyi, Ramin Mousavi, Kinter Ren, Mohammad R. Salavatipour
review.summary: For unsplittable Euclidean planar CVRP with arbitrary binary integer capacity/demands, obtains a polynomial-time (3/2+ε)-approximation, meeting the bin-packing lower frontier; polynomially bounded capacity permits a PTAS.
review.prior_frontier: Previous ratio 2+ε; unit-demand Euclidean CVRP recently has a PTAS. The contribution is general unsplittable demands, not the unit-demand result.

score_reasons.significance: Closes a large approximation gap for a central geometric routing problem up to ε.
score_reasons.novelty: Preassign singly served cells, then split tour-cycle structures into two depot walks jointly costing OPT, so the cheaper reconnects residual demand at half cost.
score_reasons.depth: Combines this new geometric lemma with capacity rounding, Arora-style DP and an unsplittable q-path PTAS for many tours.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates few/many-tour cases and explicitly explains why a dominating-set shortcut stops at 5/3.

checked: Traced Lemma7 and Claim8 completely: indegree-one auxiliary components are trees or one directed cycle; split each cycle tour between its two marked cells, assign depot-containing paths to ensure both assembled walks visit depot, and add O(mτ) connectors. BFS assigns each attached tour to a walk missing its dense cell.
Traced demand transfer/parity repair Lemma9, cost bound τ/δ=O(ε), and residual-capacity rounding DP with polynomially many states per tour for constant tour count.
remaining: Tour partitioning dependency and all preliminary rounding/slack constants.
Complete many-tour reduction and unsplittable q-path PTAS (Sections3–4), plus bounded-instance reduction from prior work.
The main theorem is not yet fully audited despite the checked new few-tour lemma.

papers.authors: Rajat De, Dominik Kempa

review.title: Near-Optimal Compressed Algorithms and Data Structures by Eliminating Recursive Substructures
review.authors: Rajat De, Dominik Kempa
review.summary: LZ78 size-z text admits a nonrecursive dictionary of total size O(z log z) and O(z log²z) phrase sequence. Gives soft-O(z^(2ω/(ω+1))) rank preprocessing and soft-O(z^((ω−1)/(ω+1))) query time; near-linear semicompressed subsequence recognition and faster fully compressed Hamming distance, with conditional lower bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Separates LZ78 from general grammar-compressed complexity. Rank optimality is conditional on all-edges sparse triangle hardness; fully compressed subsequence hardness uses OV itself, not an assertion that SETH remains true.

score_reasons.significance: Improves multiple basic compressed-string operations and supplies a reusable representation theorem.
score_reasons.novelty: Heavy paths followed by Fenwick-prefix decomposition remove recursive substructures; heavy alphabet/dictionary reductions expose matrix multiplication.
score_reasons.depth: Algorithmic exponents require balancing explicit small-word expansion against dense frequency multiplication and separate fine-grained reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: Core representation is simple, but several indexing and multiplicity errors in printed pseudocode obstruct literal implementation.

checked: Checked the representation theorem: z trie edges partition into heavy-path words of total length z; each phrase uses O(log z) prefixes, each prefix O(log z) Fenwick intervals, total dictionary length O(z log z).
Checked the conceptual rank tradeoff after heavy-symbol and long-word reduction: O(z² log³z/τ+τ^ω) preprocessing and O((z/τ)log²z) queries, optimized at τ=z^(2/(ω+1))log^(3/(ω+1))z.
Read literal block, dictionary and alphabet reductions and identified corrections needed; the stated high-level frequency-count method is compatible with these local repairs.
remaining: Full Hamming/subsequence algorithms and conditional lower-bound reductions remain unaudited in this 42-page paper.
Before an implementation-level correctness claim, correct and recheck the indexing throughout Lemmas 4.1–4.4.
issues: Local pseudocode errors: p.17 blocksα must count phrase multiplicities rather than set an entry to 1 (D=(a), X=(1,1) otherwise counts one a instead of two). Query prefixes on pp.18–20 must stop at the preceding phrase/block boundary and use dictionary index x_p; g/h on p.19 must store retained occurrence positions, not dictionary labels. These have straightforward conceptual repairs but were not silently certified as printed.

review.title: Fractional colorings of $K_r$-free graphs with local demands
review.authors: Ewan Davies, Abhishek Dhawan, Abhishek Methuku, Huy Nguyen, Jaehyeon Seo
review.summary: For every r≥4 and Kr-free graph, proves a distribution over independent sets with each vertex included with probability at least (κ/r) log(d(v)+2)/(d(v)+1), with a universal κ>0. Extends this to arbitrary objective and auxiliary vertex weights; deterministic weighted and distribution algorithms lose specified constant factors and run in 2^{O(r²)} times polynomial input size.
review.prior_frontier: Claims to remove the loglog² loss in Kelly–Postle local demands, strengthening recent average independence bounds to simultaneous weighted local guarantees. Historical theorem comparisons are manuscript-based.

score_reasons.significance: Solves the stated local-demand problem rather than only average independence.
score_reasons.novelty: Two independently weighted potentials allow local degree demands and arbitrary weighted optimization.
score_reasons.depth: Convex-dual potential, weighted triangle control and algorithmic near-stationarity are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Main statements cleanly distinguish existential demands and constant-factor algorithmic losses.

checked: Traced deletion Lemma 4.3: weighted sum of deletion gains equals (1−c)S−6cT minus the stated gradient residual; checked edge multiplicity two, triangle multiplicity three and the scalar potential identity.
At criticality the residual vanishes, so the triangle bound yields a profitable deletion for the asserted c.
remaining: The central weighted triangle bound, its Kr-free neighborhood application, global potential optimization and full algorithmic complexity remain unaudited.

review.title: The Communication Complexity of Verifying Distribution Properties
review.authors: Tal Herman

score_reasons.significance: Extends communication lower bounds to a previously poorly understood verification model.
score_reasons.novelty: Transfers gap-disjointness hardness through sampled distribution statistics and private verifier behavior.
score_reasons.depth: Requires detailed distributional indistinguishability and protocol simulation.
score_reasons.exposition: The stronger model is well motivated; informal worst-case parameter statements need reading together with the precise family qualifications.

checked: Checked the exact-gap-disjointness reduction by block replication and padding, including its universe-size and sparsity conditions; also checked the Poisson singleton/doubleton product approximation.
remaining: The central distribution-to-communication simulation, computational soundness transfer and matching upper protocols remain unchecked.

review.summary: Communication lower bounds for verifying entropy, support size and distance from uniform in private-coin and computationally sound distribution proof systems, with matching bounds on designated hard families.
review.prior_frontier: Distribution verification had focused on sample complexity, with communication bounds largely limited to public coins. The new lower bounds cover stronger models but have explicit sample-budget and family restrictions.
review.recommendation: Solid candidate; main reduction still requires checking before selection.

papers.title: Subgaussian Vector Balancing by an Ising Model
papers.authors: Heng Guo, Daniel Spielman, Xinyuan Zhang

review.title: Subgaussian Vector Balancing by an Ising Model
review.authors: Heng Guo, Daniel A. Spielman, Xinyuan Zhang
review.summary: For norm≤1 vectors with no three parallel unit vectors, the explicit symmetric law proportional to product_{i<j}(1−σiσj〈vi,vj〉) makes the signed sum 1-subgaussian, also under external fields after centering. Glauber gap is at least (1−max||vi||²)/n. A general Ising criterion uses λmax(tanh J)<1. Unit-vector degeneracies can be removed, and scaling/rejection supports approximate sampling.
review.prior_frontier: Matches the optimal constant of the Gram–Schmidt Walk rather than improving it; provides a first claimed closed-form sampler and a new spectral condition. Faster earlier balancing algorithms remain available.

score_reasons.significance: A simple explicit law for an important optimal discrepancy guarantee, with a broad new mixing criterion.
score_reasons.novelty: Lorentzian Alexandrov–Fenchel controls covariance and, via interpolation, full variance tensorization.
score_reasons.depth: The function-representation/interpolation step turns an inequality for product observables into a spectral-gap theorem.
score_reasons.exposition: Core proof is transparent and exposes norm-slack, degeneracy and sampling-time limitations.

checked: Verified external Lee–Oh–Seo arXiv:2506.13659v2 Theorem3.1 and Proposition4.1, including allowance of a signed first polarization vector; this is essential for signed coefficients in Lemma12.
Traced Lorentz matrix 11ᵀ−VᵀV, the two auxiliary vectors 0 and εθ, and second-order limit yielding tilted covariance≤I; integrated log-partition Hessian for centered 1-subgaussian MGF.

Traced Lemmas11–15: add sqrtα0 orthogonal coordinates; represent f and each −σi(I−Pi)f jointly on {0,±1}^n; coordinate-degree-two Lagrange interpolation moves evaluations into a sufficiently small cube. This yields Var f≤α0^{-1}ΣE[(I−Pi)f]² and gap α0/n.
Checked general Ising Gram realization ρI−tanh J≽0, and SK perturbation Frobenius norm O(n^{-1}) in expectation. Checked parallel-vector cancellation and norm-reduction threshold sqrt3−1.
remaining: Section8 general spin-system/Potts extensions were not fully audited; main vector-balancing and Ising results are the checked scope.
The optional cooling-schedule improvement is cited/sketched rather than reconstructed.

Finite-time Glauber sampling approximates the ideal law in TV; the exact 1-subgaussian statement concerns the specified distribution, not an automatic exact MGF guarantee for every approximate implementation.

review.title: An Explicit 4n−O(log(n)) Size Lower Bound against General Boolean Circuits
review.authors: Om Swostik Mishra, Rahul Santhanam
review.summary: An explicit polynomial-time Boolean function requires general fan-in-two Boolean circuits of size at least 4n−O(log n). More generally a dimension-d affine disperser has circuit complexity at least 4n−10d, with a deterministic poly(n,2^d) refuter.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the stated published 3.1n−o(n) frontier (and the authors’ earlier 3.5n bound). Uses Li’s 2023 explicit O(log n)-dimension affine disperser as a cited dependency; that extractor construction was not re-proved.

score_reasons.significance: Raises a longstanding explicit general-circuit size frontier to coefficient four, without restricting the fan-in-two gate basis.
score_reasons.novelty: Paired constraints and a semi-circuit affine-coordinate representation amortize otherwise expensive gate eliminations.
score_reasons.depth: The weight s+4q+6u and five-case reduction maintain affine dimension through coordinate swaps, Gaussian elimination, and nonlinear-gate simplification.
score_reasons.exposition: Cases and their potential changes are explicit, though the unusual semi-circuit representation requires careful bookkeeping.

checked: Traced the complete central reduction on pp.12–26: injective affine embedding, paired constraint zero locus, coordinate replacement using a nonzero inverse-matrix coefficient, and preservation of syntactic degrees.

Checked elementary simplifications D1–D4 and all paired-parameter cases. Verified the two-unpaired-input step changes a=m−q by −1 and weight by at most −10, and the one/two-paired-input cases give at least the same saving.

Verified potential induction W<10(a−d) from s<4n−10d, strict descent of m+s, and the terminal affine/AND output’s constant subspace of dimension at least a−1≥d. Enumerating that subspace supplies the refuter.
remaining: The cited Li affine-disperser construction and its extractor proof were treated as an external theorem rather than re-proved. This is a human main-argument check, not a formal verification.

sources.detail: Minimal nonlinear gate and paired cases

review.title: Parallel Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering in Low Dimensions
review.authors: MohammadHossein Bateni, Laxman Dhulipala, Willem Fletcher, Kishen N. Gowda, D Ellis Hershkowitz, Rajesh Jayaram, Jakub Łącki

Read serialization/anchor progress roadmap and exact CC-hardness promise.
remaining: Full phase-count/packing proof, parallel data structures and CC reduction are not audited.

review.title: Optimal Dynamic Strings in Compressed Space
review.authors: Anouk Duyster, Tomasz Kociumaka, Hanna Komlós

score_reasons.significance: Reconciles optimal dynamic-string time with compressed live-space bounds and deletion, an important infrastructure result.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses relative grammar complexity, sharp concentration and reclaim-and-resample random orders.
score_reasons.depth: Requires a delicate combination of parsing, dependent-level concentration, memory reclamation and exact dictionaries.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully distinguishes expected versus high-probability bounds and oblivious versus timing-adaptive operation sequences.

checked: Traced the relative grammar-size proof: novel-substring witness coverage, deterministic exclusive-symbol count and the injection from large blocks into monotone pieces.

Checked the conditional factorial-tail estimate and the moment-generating-function expansion, which uses deterministic bounds and successive conditioning rather than unjustified independence between blocks or levels.
Checked the Chernoff optimization yielding the Poisson-shaped grammar tail, subject to the stated parsing locality invariants.

Traced reference-count reclamation and the random-order resampling proof: a fixed final family has probability equal to the product of old/new list-size factorial ratios despite adaptively interleaved insertion discovery.
remaining: This 81-page manuscript's full parsing locality, extraction/completion implementation, PILLAR queries, exact dictionary costs and final collection reduction were not audited end to end.
The resampling check relies on the later completion lemma's claim that no unneeded entries are created or removed during an update.

review.summary: Persistent dynamic strings with optimal logarithmic update time and compressed space measured by the current live collection, including reclamation after deletion and PILLAR queries.
review.prior_frontier: Optimal-time persistent dynamic strings could accumulate space with operation history; compressed editable-string structures had slower updates and expected-space guarantees. papers.title: A Complete Hierarchy of Local Lemmas

review.title: A Complete Hierarchy of Local Lemmas
review.authors: Dimitris Achlioptas, Konstantinos Kritharidis, Kostas Zampetakis
review.summary: A finite-memory deletion-recursion hierarchy starts at asymmetric LLL and converges for every locally finite graph to the uniform Shearer threshold, with gap≤min(1/q,π²/(q+1)²), worst-case order tight. Effective finite presentations give certified threshold approximation; fixed periodic lattices require exp(O(ε^{-1/2})) time. Extends to positive deletion representations and zero-free polydiscs.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier local lemmas improved specific lattice thresholds but did not provide this complete uniform finite-memory hierarchy. Uniform activity thresholds are distinct from full multivariate region membership.

score_reasons.significance: A general complete and quantitatively convergent hierarchy for a central probabilistic criterion.
score_reasons.novelty: Retained deletion histories and weighted geometric suffix averages bound the cumulative cost of forgetting.
score_reasons.depth: Combines exact branch recursion, zero-freeness, infinite-state comparisons and rational certificate algorithms.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit finite-presentation/order assumptions and exact-versus-numerical certification distinctions.

checked: Checked Lemma3.5 algebra: Hölder followed by AM–GM for messages and residuals cancels interior suffix values, leaving endpoint error≤1/q. Read suffix legality comparison, where legality is tested before forgetting.
Read quadratic refinement setup and weighted-geometric-means bound with midpoint weights; full sine-weight implementation not yet audited.
remaining: The 48-page local-lemma hierarchy has a traced message-error cancellation identity. The exact deletion criterion, sharp quadratic convergence and matching obstruction remain unchecked; this is a large-proof exception.
Canonical branch uniform bound, exact deletion criterion, complete O(q^{-2}) derivation and matching cycle example.
Finite-presentation algorithms and rational rounding/bit-complexity proof.
Extensions beyond independence polynomials and computational certificates.

papers.title: XOR Functions and Beyond in the Random Query Model
papers.authors: Sumegha Garg, Janani Sundaresan, Santhoshini Velusamy

review.title: XOR Functions and Beyond in the Random Query Model
review.authors: Sumegha Garg, Janani Sundaresan, Santhoshini Velusamy
review.summary: Randomized bounded-error query algorithms for XOR functions g(x,y)=f(x⊕y) satisfy T(S+log T)=Ω(n sens(g)); a general degeneracy bound gives TS=soft-Ω(n dgn(f)). Gives nearly quadratic tradeoffs for low-influence examples and matching symmetric-function algorithms up to logarithms.
review.prior_frontier: Extends random-query time-space lower bounds beyond previously studied high-influence functions; separates sensitivity-based XOR results from the more general degeneracy theorem. Prior historical comparisons were not independently re-established.

score_reasons.significance: Obtains strong time-space tradeoffs even for natural low-influence functions where ordinary query complexity alone is insufficient.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses a new XOR information/direct-sum route and a stationary-edge hard distribution for degeneracy.
score_reasons.depth: The information lower bound and missing-element communication simulation are substantial distinct mechanisms.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise random-query and branching-program models are stated, but the 62-page proof has several long dependency chains.

checked: Traced the degeneracy hard distribution: degree-biased endpoints make the hidden-coordinate posterior error sum at least dgn(f)/(2n).

Checked the missing-element simulation with a public random permutation and fresh/old sampled indices, its asymmetric errors, truncation of unusually small sets, amplification, and the conversion k≈T log(1/δ)/n into the soft-Ω(n dgn) bound.
Checked the symmetric-function adjacent-layer degeneracy characterization and CountOnes partition algorithm, including why overflow is only required to be unlikely on the low-weight side.
remaining: The central new XOR information and direct-sum proofs on pp.17–42 have not been traced.
Dinur’s missing-element lower bound is used as cited; independently checking its asymmetric-error hypotheses remains. The complete 62-page manuscript warrants this substantive large-proof exception.

papers.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Multiclass and List Learning
papers.authors: Chirag Pabbaraju

review.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Multiclass and List Learning
review.authors: Chirag Pabbaraju
review.area: Learning theory / multiclass and list PAC learning
review.summary: Proves maximal shifted ℓ-density of every one-inclusion hypergraph is at most its ℓ-DS dimension. Consequently obtains realizable ℓ-list PAC sample complexity O((d_DS^ℓ+log(1/δ))/ε), including arbitrary label sets. Matching list lower bounds require the stated label-richness condition; multiclass is ℓ=1. Also gives agnostic, compression and universal-learning consequences with separate qualifications.
review.prior_frontier: Closes the gap between the prior approximately d_DS^{3/2}/ε realizable upper bound and the linear lower bound. Builds crucially on Hanneke–Meng–Moran–Shaeiri’s polynomial spanning result, and the established leave-one-out to high-probability conversion.

score_reasons.significance: Settles the main realizable multiclass sample-complexity dependence and its list analogue.
score_reasons.novelty: A short basis-counting argument converts a sharp polynomial spanning lemma into the long-missing density bound.
score_reasons.depth: Combines dimension counting, hypergraph orientations, compactness and confidence amplification; additional lower bounds have independent content.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes label-richness lower-bound assumptions and remaining logarithms in agnostic results.

checked: Traced Theorem 1: choose a basis of monomials having at most d high-exponent coordinates; low-degree-on-fiber subspaces have dimension sum_e min(ℓ,|e|), forcing enough high-coordinate basis elements to account for sum_e(|e|−ℓ)+. Summing over coordinates gives density≤d.

Verified the critical spanning lemma in primary arXiv:2604.12952 pp7–8, including interpolation and iterative low-degree-fiber peeling. Verified its finite orientation construction via integer max-flow on pp22–24.
Checked Appendix A compactness extension to infinite label sets: closed per-vertex/per-edge conditions, finite-subgraph orientations and zero extension give the finite-intersection property.

Checked leave-one-out applicability, deterministic Top-ℓ voting loss and randomized prefix selection with independent validation on pp17–20. Verified symmetry and bounded-loss hypotheses and 4.82 bound against primary arXiv:2304.09167 pp4–5. A constant fraction of prefixes has error≤ε/4; O(log(1/δ)) draws and O(log(R/δ)/ε) validation samples retain the optimal rate.
remaining: Agnostic bounds, new list lower-bound details, compression and universal-rate extensions have not received a full proof audit. Established conversion theorem checked for applicability, not completely reproved.

papers.title: TFNP in the Random Oracle Model

review.title: TFNP in the Random Oracle Model
review.authors: Noah Fleming, Mika Göös, Ziyi Guan, Oliver Korten, Daniel Mitropolsky, Toniann Pitassi, Artur Riazanov, Dmitry Sokolov, Tianqi Yang, Weiqiang Yuan

score_reasons.significance: Settles a central random-oracle TFNP hardness question and separates PPAD/EoPL behavior from UEoPL.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines a singleton-free hypergraph search problem, balanced code constructions and explicit End-of-Line cancellation.
score_reasons.depth: The hardness, totality and query-efficient upper-bound sides require distinct substantial techniques.
score_reasons.exposition: The model and query-versus-computation distinction are clear; the full landscape spans several independent proofs.

checked: Checked the adaptive exposure argument: the j-th first-exposure events are disjoint across paths, avoiding a union bound over all decision-tree leaves.
Checked singleton concentration after fixing at most 3τ/2 queried labels and at most τ planted void labels; Ω(τ) expected singleton labels and bounded differences give exponentially small success.
Traced the balanced signed polynomial identity and explicit two-matching End-of-Line construction, including the unique planted source and recovery of a non-special solution.
Checked the folded-RS hypergraph parameter interface, polynomial interpolation involution for balancedness, codeword intersection bound and final exponential query/success parameter composition.
remaining: The imported folded-RS list-recovery theorem has not been independently source-audited, although its stated parameter substitution was checked.
The separate UEoPL upper bound and public-coin PLS separations occupy substantial further sections of this 42-page manuscript and remain unchecked; no claim of full landscape verification is made.

review.summary: Average-case PPAD hardness in the random-oracle model, contrasted with polynomial-query UEoPL solvability by computationally unbounded solvers, plus separations from PLS under public-coin reductions.
review.prior_frontier: Random-oracle hardness was known for PLS and other TFNP classes, while PPAD remained unresolved. The UEoPL upper bound concerns oracle queries, not polynomial running time or an unconditional standard-model algorithm.
review.recommendation: Very strong shortlist candidate; PPAD core traced with additional theorem qualifications.

review.title: A General Technique for Metrical Task Systems with Action Predictions
review.authors: Júlia Baligács, Christian Coester, Alexa Tudose
review.summary: A block synchronization reduction incorporates action predictions into MTS formulations. Obtains optimal logarithmic normalized-error dependence for weighted paging, polylogarithmic dependence for k-server and online matching, and optimal square-root dependence for Euclidean convex-body chasing, with robust fallback bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Prior weighted-paging logarithmic dependence was conjectured; prior k-server/matching/chasing dependence was linear. Claimed comparisons not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Improves prediction-error dependence across several foundational online problems.
score_reasons.novelty: Random-offset synchronization reduces prediction use to competitive algorithms on short sequences; adds server activation/deactivation and an algorithm-combination theorem.
score_reasons.depth: Short-horizon embeddings and combining guarantees are substantial despite the simple core reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Clean explanation of service before synchronization and independence assumptions for randomized predictions.

checked: Traced Theorem6 block argument for fixed request/prediction/reference sequences: running cost≤ρ(OFF+boundary errors), synchronization≤running cost+OFF+2boundary errors, and offset averaging yields (2ρ+1)OFF+(2ρ+2)η/H.
Random predictions extension explicitly assumes independence from algorithm randomization.
remaining: Full short-sequence weighted paging/k-server guarantees, online metric matching reduction and HST dependencies.
Infinite algorithm-combination theorem, chasing lower bound and exact quantifiers for hindsight/random-reference choices.

papers.title: Settling the Approximability of Submodular Facility Location
papers.authors: Adam N. Elmachtoub, Bento Natura, Meike Neuwohner

review.title: Settling the Approximability of Submodular Facility Location
review.authors: Adam N. Elmachtoub, Bento Natura, Meike Neuwohner
review.summary: Proves the Θ(log log |C|) approximation threshold for homogeneous metric submodular facility location in the value-oracle model, even for matroid-rank facility costs, together with a matching-order configuration-LP gap. Separate computational hardness is also claimed under NP≠RP.
review.prior_frontier: Matches the previously known O(log log |C|) upper bound. The value-oracle lower bound is information-theoretic, even with unlimited computation between queries; the computational-hardness appendix is a different assertion.

score_reasons.significance: Settles the oracle approximability order for a recognized facility-location generalization and identifies a matching natural LP obstruction.
score_reasons.novelty: An extended symmetry-gap construction preserves public orbit information and integer matroid-rank costs; cyclic lifts turn local expansion into a global covering obstruction.
score_reasons.depth: Combines hidden balanced replication, adaptive-query indistinguishability, sparse capped rank functions, and quantitative random regular graphs.
score_reasons.exposition: The proof separates the query-model theorem from the combinatorial gap, with explicit constants and model qualifications.

checked: Traced minimization and symmetry lemmas, the reference/hidden cost constructions, whole-orbit rounding, and balanced-query equality. Verified the adaptive transcript union bound includes the final assignment queries.
Checked random base-graph existence: the covering-event coupling yields probability ≤exp(−mq); the small-set expansion union bound has base 2e^(d−1)(d−2)^2/K=o(1).
Traced cyclic-lift layer counting, capped-rank submodularity via minimizing witnesses smaller than K and their union below 2K, and the matroid-rank characterization.
Checked cheap split assignment cost ≤4m and whole-orbit cost ≥m log d/2, using truncated shortest-path distances and K exceeding all near-client neighborhoods.
Verified R=d^4, λ=d^3, N=d^(2d+11), the exponential oracle lower bound, and Proposition 18’s symmetric fractional assignment lift giving the configuration-LP gap.
remaining: The separate NP≠RP computational-hardness appendix was not audited. The earlier matching upper-bound algorithm is cited rather than re-proved.

sources.detail: Metric gap and quantitative oracle theorem

papers.title: Optimal Quantum Junta Testing
papers.authors: Jinge Bao, Minbo Gao, Penghui Yao

review.title: Optimal Quantum Junta Testing
review.authors: Jinge Bao, Minbo Gao, Penghui Yao
review.summary: Determines junta-testing query complexity in four models: Boolean functions Θ(sqrt(k/ε)); unitaries with forward and inverse queries Θ(sqrt(k)/ε); forward-only unitaries and channels Θ(k/(ε² log k)). The common stated window is sufficiently large k, n≥2k and 2^{−k/16}≤ε≤1/16. Distances are uniform Boolean distance, phase-invariant normalized Hilbert–Schmidt unitary distance and normalized Choi Hilbert–Schmidt channel distance, not diamond distance. Forward upper testers use product inputs and single-qubit measurements without ancillas.
review.prior_frontier: Removes logarithmic factors in earlier Boolean/standard-unitary upper bounds; raises forward/channel lower bounds from approximately sqrt(k) to k/log k at constant distance. Establishes optimal union-size testing from independent samples and reversible samplers.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a coherent family of central query-testing bounds with a sharp inverse-access separation.
score_reasons.novelty: Union-size testing and pointwise normalization of phase-averaged path sectors provide reusable new tools.
score_reasons.depth: Moment matching, dependent-coordinate polynomial estimation, reversible group testing and oracle ensemble analysis are extensive.
score_reasons.exposition: Oracle models and distance measures are explicitly separated; 80 pages contain several independent proof chains.

checked: Fully traced Theorem 5.11 exact classicalization: independent Haar phases remove unequal address histograms; each sector depends on at most q labels. Symmetrizing q IID samples and using homogeneous-polynomial coefficient uniqueness makes total sector weight pointwise one, yielding a [0,1] classical acceptance rule. Handles arbitrary ancillas, adaptive known operations, padding and q=0.

Checked phase-masked diagonal unitary construction and YES support count. For NO instances, empirical top-s mass error is ≤sqrt(s||p_f−p||²), while a missing address bit has influence≥1/4 with high probability via independent phase pairs.

Checked normalized partial-trace singular-value formula for unitary junta distance, and its influence implications. Checked r=ceil(log(Ck/δ²)), s=k−r, δ=(4/3)(2ε²−ε⁴) ensure r≤k/2, alphabet≥2s and failure<1/20 in the claimed parameter window.
Checked conversion of ensemble success to a classical support-size testing acceptance gap.
remaining: 80-page multi-result proof: independent-sample union tester and its Poisson polynomial variance analysis, reversible tester, matching moment-matching sample lower bound and Boolean tiny-distance refinement remain unchecked. Channel-distance completion proof and influence-sampling dependency not fully audited. Thus the final matching bounds rely on substantial unverified components.
