review.title: Catalan Hashing: Efficient Linear Probing for Variable-Length Items
review.authors: Alex Conway, Hanna Komlós, William Kuszmaul

score_reasons.significance: A useful extension of a fundamental data structure with cache-oblivious consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Nested placement, erasure-code write optimization and high-load placement analysis form an inventive combination.
score_reasons.depth: The dynamic/high-load analysis is substantial but more specialized than the strongest frontier resolutions.
score_reasons.exposition: The staged static, low-load and high-load development makes the construction approachable.

checked: Checked the negative-query reduction from expected positive scan lengths, including independence of the absent key's hash from placement.
remaining: Erasure-code reinflation, dynamic update accounting and the high-load placement guarantee remain unaudited.

review.summary: Catalan hashing extends locality-friendly linear probing to variable-length items, with expected amortized O(|x|/ε) positive scans, O(1/ε) negative scans and nearly comparable update scans.
review.prior_frontier: Unit-size linear probing's spatial-locality guarantees do not directly survive variable item lengths; naive shifts can cause severe write amplification. The result adds a polylogarithmic-in-item-length factor for updates.

papers.title: A $(3+\epsilon)$-Approximation for Fair $k$-Means and a Matching Lower Bound
papers.authors: Kangke Cheng, Guanlin Mo, Shihong Song, Hu Ding

review.title: A $(3+\epsilon)$-Approximation for Fair $k$-Means and a Matching Lower Bound
review.authors: Kangke Cheng, Guanlin Mo, Shihong Song, Hu Ding
review.summary: A drift-regularized convex relaxation plus a ρ-approximation for weighted k-means gives exactly fair fractional assignments within 2ρ+1+ε; fixed dimension yields 3+ε. Claims NP-hardness below 3 even on a line with overlapping groups. Integral rounding permits additive fairness violations, not exact integral fairness. Also improves k-sparse Wasserstein barycenters.
review.prior_frontier: Prior fractional ratio 1+4ρ, giving 5+ε in fixed dimension; no prior fairness-specific lower bound is claimed. External comparisons not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: A matching fixed-dimensional approximation threshold for fractional fair k-means and a substantial barycenter improvement.
score_reasons.novelty: Drift stationarity controls the cross-alignment loss that previously doubled the black-box k-means factor.
score_reasons.depth: Convex optimization with finite candidates and a fractional Label-Cover hardness construction both require deep checks.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear distinctions between fractional exact fairness, additive integral violations, dimension and support-size constraints.

checked: Checked Lemmas22–23 algebra: λ=ρ/(1+ρ), stationarity bounds the alignment cross term and gives CT+ρOPTπ≤(2ρ+1)comparison−2ρCν+(1+ρ)τ.
Read the four-part convergence roadmap; neither finite-candidate approximation nor hardness has been audited.
remaining: Complete Frank–Wolfe LP implementation, stationarity tolerance and polynomial bit complexity.
Label-Cover soundness including fractional assignments and group encoding; this is critical to the claimed sharp threshold.
Barycenter equivalence and external integral-rounding guarantees.

papers.title: Dual Coppersmith:Finding Small Roots Without Multivariate Polynomial Systems
papers.authors: Taehun Kang, Jebin Kim, Changmin Lee, JeongHwan Lee

review.title: Dual Coppersmith:Finding Small Roots Without Multivariate Polynomial Systems
review.authors: Taehun Kang, Jebin Kim, Changmin Lee, Jeong Hwan Lee
review.summary: DualCoppersmith reconstructs modular polynomial small roots from a short vector in a scaled congruence-kernel lattice, avoiding a multivariate polynomial-system solve. Recovery is rigorous under a second-successive-minimum gap; the stated product bound relies on Gaussian and second-minimum heuristics.
review.prior_frontier: Changes the root-recovery mechanism rather than giving an unconditional improvement of the multivariate Coppersmith exponent. Claimed heuristic product bound is ∏X_i<p^(1/d−ε); shift parameters are fixed for the polynomial bit-complexity claim.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a potentially useful alternative to the expensive algebraic reconstruction stage, with applicability limited by an explicit geometric heuristic.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses the dual congruence lattice and a primitive root-vector line rather than extracting algebraic equations.
score_reasons.depth: Requires Smith-normal-form covolumes and first-jet geometry, but the central conditional recovery argument is short.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly separates the rigorous gap theorem from heuristic root-size predictions, although those distinctions matter to the headline interpretation.

checked: Checked the exact congruence lattice, scaled root vector and determinant calculation via Smith normal form.
Traced the gap theorem: both the root vector and the LLL vector fall below λ2, hence are collinear; the constant monomial makes the scalar integral, and coordinate ratios recover the root.
Checked fixed-shift-parameter polynomial bit complexity and that final substitution verifies any returned root.
remaining: The first-jet second-minimum prediction and Gaussian heuristic are assumptions rather than proved guarantees. Experiments and cryptanalytic parameter regimes were not reproduced.

papers.title: Deterministic Approximate Nearest Neighbors in High Dimensions
papers.authors: Ying Feng, Piotr Piotr Indyk

review.title: Deterministic Approximate Nearest Neighbors in High Dimensions
review.authors: Ying Feng, Piotr Indyk
review.summary: Fully deterministic Euclidean (1+ε)-ANN for n≥d uses n^{poly(1/ε)} preprocessing and space and O(d²+d poly(1/ε,log n)) query time. All queries are answered correctly. Bounds count arithmetic operations; the manuscript does not claim full bit complexity.
review.prior_frontier: Closes the stated long-standing gap from deterministic approximation 3+ε to 1+ε with polynomial space for fixed ε and polylogarithmic n dependence in query time.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a fundamental randomness question for high-dimensional nearest-neighbor search.
score_reasons.novelty: Conditional variance plus expander superblocks overcomes the single-block factor-three argument.
score_reasons.depth: Second-moment comparison, deterministic moment-based sign selection and expander conditioning are substantial but economical.
score_reasons.exposition: Full proof fits 21 pages with explicit constants and deterministic implementation qualifications.

checked: Traced all new proofs pp9–19. Conditional means satisfy E||a_I−a||²≤Var(X)/s; balanced pairwise database differences yield projected conditional variance and polarization controls differences of averages with error 12τE||X−x*||². The bias/variance cancellation gives the stated factor.

Verified deterministic signed-Hadamard blocks: Parseval is exact for all signs, centered squared Rademacher sums have (CpL)^p moments, degree-O(log n) truncated exponential generating functions compute conditional expectations in polynomial arithmetic time. Greedy sign fixing yields every required database-pair balance.

Checked expander replacement: uniform endpoint marginals and symmetric W^ell give conditional-mean variance≤ρ²/(1−ρ²) times residual variance. Repeated walk endpoints are retained; only d local structures needed. Parameter δ=ε/100,τ=ε²/10^6,ρ≤ε/200 makes the final factor≤1+ε.

Checked appendix deterministic low-dimensional primitive against primary HPIM12 pp10,15,21–23: exact median-connectivity computation can replace randomized selection, grid volume gives (C/δ)^{O(m)} cells and balanced dictionaries give the claimed conservative query time.
Checked power-of-two expander padding with duplicated Margulis graph or tensor with two-point averaging. d=1 and n=1 are handled; zero database differences impose no condition.
remaining: Not a bit-complexity or practical-memory guarantee. Classical Margulis–Gabber–Galil spectral bound used as an established dependency, not reproved.
resolved_notes: Minor typographical slips include α=q+δ on p8 (must be 1+δ) and k versus d in an overview sum; subsequent statements and proof use the correct quantities.

checked: Checked the message-before-random-coordinate information bound and the truncated-trace privacy transfer, including why no expected-cost bound on the altered input is required.

papers.title: Learning Random Quantum Circuits and the Emergence of Pseudorandomness
papers.authors: Makrand Sinha, Qizhao Huang, Srinivasan Arunachalam

review.title: Learning Random Quantum Circuits and the Emergence of Pseudorandomness
review.authors: Srinivasan Arunachalam, Qizhao Huang, Makrand Sinha
review.summary: For a public polynomial-size gate set sampled Haar-randomly, learns random fixed-dimensional brickwork circuits exactly from output-state copies in poly_k(n,d,1/δ)2^{O_k(dℓ)} time/samples, for d≤.01n^{1/k}. Gives Haar-unitary polynomial small-ball bound 64m² ε^{1/(24πdegree)}. Exact recovery is for the discrete public ensemble, not arbitrary unknown continuous Haar gates.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier random-circuit learners used unitary access and fixed locality; prior state learners could increase depth or incur larger light-cone costs. PRS existence above the threshold is not proved.

score_reasons.significance: State-only learning reaches a natural logarithmic depth-locality boundary in every fixed lattice dimension.
score_reasons.novelty: Local two-site correlation tests and dimension-independent small-ball exponent bypass full backward-light-cone learning.
score_reasons.depth: Haar Remez analysis, Bell-pair witness routing and circuit peeling require nontrivial probability and geometry.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise theorem exposes the finite public gate set, which is less explicit in the abstract headline.

checked: Read Bell-pair/SWAP witness producing Frobenius correlation≥3/4 for a wrong last-layer inverse.

Traced multigate anticoncentration Lemma4.4: sequential ratios relative to fixed maximizing gates, conditional negative moments at half exponent, tower property and Markov yield (1+64m²)^r ε^{1/(48πd)}.
Read the one-dimensional analytic Remez reduction tail; full unitary reduction not yet audited.
remaining: Full Haar inequality and its normalization, witness routing for all lattice dimensions, peeling and union bounds.
Finite-gate-set collision/precision transfer and exact recovery probability.
Pseudorandomness discussion is a boundary interpretation, not a PRS construction.

papers.title: Node Differential Privacy via Node-Stable Graph Projections

review.title: Node Differential Privacy via Node-Stable Graph Projections
review.authors: Ishaq Aden-Ali, Adam Sealfon, Adam Smith, Thomas Steinke, Jonathan Ullman
review.summary: Near-linear randomized degree projection preserves D-bounded graphs and has distributional node stability, with output degree (1+o(1))D+polylog(n)/ε². Also gives an O(m log m) exact-stretch Lipschitz extension of bounded weighted edge sums and applications to vector sums/optimization.
review.prior_frontier: Prior efficient projections required safe-domain tests or incurred larger changes after a node insertion; prior combinatorial extensions principally handled unweighted counts. The projection itself is not a privately releasable graph.

score_reasons.significance: Gives a general preprocessing primitive that tolerates high-degree outliers while preserving node privacy downstream.
score_reasons.novelty: Randomized threshold counters localize the privacy cost to retained neighbors; sorted greedy edges yield a sharp weighted extension.
score_reasons.depth: Adaptive counter composition and sensitive-size handling supplement a clean alternating-path argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly distinguishes distributional stability from private output and clipping from abstention.

checked: Fully checked the weighted-extension proof: sequential insertion of a new node’s edges in decreasing order yields a nonincreasing alternating path; saturated vertices cannot recur and the new node has no later inserted edge. Weighted-degree ℓ1 changes telescope to twice the first weight, and at most D inserted edges affect the final prefix.
Read the projection coupling and black-box composition requirements, including why ordinary composition cannot be invoked directly on the sensitive projected graph.
remaining: Projection’s adaptive strong-composition proof, counter fast-forwarding, private-size wrapper, and vector/SCO applications remain unaudited; the 41-page combined result is only partially checked.

papers.title: Optimal Quantum Query Bounds for Identifying Classes of $3$-Tensors
papers.authors: Elena Grigorescu, Brendan Juba, Karl Wimmer, Ning Xie

review.title: Optimal Quantum Query Bounds for Identifying Classes of $3$-Tensors
review.authors: Elena Grigorescu, Brendan Juba, Karl Wimmer, Ning Xie
review.summary: For an arbitrary explicit list of L trilinear forms over a fixed finite field, identifies an unknown member with O_q((log L)^{2/3} log(1/δ)) quantum value-oracle queries, independent of ambient dimension, and proves a matching worst-case class-size lower bound. Corollaries include orbit identification in O_q(n^{4/3}) queries and low-slice-rank learning in O_q(n SR(f)) queries. These are query bounds with unrestricted classical computation, not efficient tensor-isomorphism algorithms.
review.prior_frontier: Extends dimension-based tensor interpolation bounds to arbitrary finite classes and beats the classical information-theoretic log_q L lower bound for growing classes. Historical comparisons follow the manuscript.

score_reasons.significance: Uniform class-size bounds apply beyond specially structured tensor families.
score_reasons.novelty: Constructing large vanishing product subspaces and weighted candidate elimination are new algorithmic ingredients.
score_reasons.depth: Analytic-rank projection, kernel pivots and sequential weighted dictionary learning require several substantial lemmas.
score_reasons.exposition: Formal model is clear but the overview overstates tensor agreement and Proposition 2 has reversed min/max definitions.

checked: Checked central rank inequality 2 rank(B restricted to coker A×ker A)+rank(A)≤rank(B)+rank(A+B): isolate a rank-t block on a kernel complement, then use rank subadditivity.

For a linear matrix space, a rank≥Rmax/2 pivot contracts all restricted ranks by at least 1/4, and pivot codimensions telescope to at most 2Rmax. The needed probability≥1/2 follows by translation by a maximum-rank matrix.
remaining: Good-fiber finding, weighted-list identification, full query accounting and matching lower bound not audited.

Proposition 2 defines its medians incorrectly: the displayed minimum with tail probability≥1/2 can be zero; intended threshold is the maximum. The required rank-half probability has the short translation proof noted above. The introductory claim of arbitrarily overwhelming agreement is inaccurate for nonzero fixed-field trilinear differences, whose nonzero fraction is bounded below by (1−1/q)^3; it is not needed by the inspected rank argument.

Read reduced auxiliary ratio and exact rejection-sampling construction; acceptance coins are Bernoulli factories rather than estimated probabilities.

Full optimizer convergence, promised-domain Bernoulli factories and recursive work bound.
Worst-case truncation with always-feasible shared-tape consistency and bipartite rounding, including adaptive query order.

score_reasons.novelty: Connects orientation-sensitive packing lower bounds to Kakeya tube-union volume after shearing and thickening.
score_reasons.depth: Combines metric MST packing, grouped auxiliary bodies, angular separation, and reduction to rounded parallelepipeds.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully separates the established subpolynomial claim from two stronger external estimates and states width slack for bin/strip packing.

checked: Checked the geometric lower-bound core: retained slope intervals are separated by 9τ/100, so intersecting shortened/thickened bodies would force original interiors to intersect.
Verified the shear determinant bτ/c, inscribed-tube containment, angular separation via a triangle in z=1, and summing disjoint group volumes.
Checked MST scale integration and the exponent accounting 66→67→69; the alternative exponent 4→5→7 is conditional.
remaining: Full enclosure/rounding and assembly algorithm, bin/strip reduction, and applicability of the external Kakeya statements remain to be checked. The cited Lean project was not built.

review.summary: A single parameter-to-sample SDPI with contraction tending to one yields excess-memorization lower bounds: Boolean means Ω(d/(nα²)), Gaussian means Ω(d²/(nα²)), top-k selection Ω(k log²(m/k)/(nα²)), and rank-one spiked Gaussian PCA Ω(d²/(nγα)). score_reasons.significance: A common lower-bound framework links three estimation tasks, privacy and replicability with stronger quantitative dependence.
score_reasons.novelty: Weak SDPI contraction remains useful when accuracy forces high parameter information; agreement testing converts replicability to bounded information.
score_reasons.depth: PCA needs a restricted SDPI and score/log-Sobolev estimates, beyond the simpler Gaussian mean reduction.

remaining: Restricted PCA SDPI, hard-prior accuracy-information lower bounds and exact approximate-DP dependencies not fully audited.

Read start of support-count contradiction and explicit constants.
remaining: Complete measure bound Lemma5.2, final support contradiction and all elementary numerical enclosures.
External HJN critical equations and values of the two critical configurations.

score_reasons.novelty: Replaces precomputed expansion structures by energy-charged partitions and soft-max centrality by clipped inverse-square updates.
score_reasons.depth: A 89-page interdependent sampler, potential, data-structure and higher-moment analysis controls the logarithmic exponent.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed invariants and constants are provided, but cross-section dependencies and some loose displayed arithmetic hinder checking.

checked: Checked the reduction to a two-cost assignment LP and the clipped direction’s box/ball optimality, gradient gain, and clipped-coordinate count.
Checked how the five sampling intensities sum to O(√m) conditional on the curvature estimate.
Read the sixth-moment rank-one expansion through two-block patterns and adjacent three-block patterns; centeredness removes singleton indices.
remaining: The full centrality drift/acceptance proof, residual feasibility, nonadjacent sixth-moment patterns, query-driven data structure, resistance estimator, and amortization remain unchecked. The size and interdependence of the 89-page proof justify only a partial audit.

The p.30 displayed derivation retains a 200m term before asserting a 100(η√m/θ+m) upper bound; the quoted inequalities alone do not imply that constant. Sharpening the scalar bound or increasing the constant appears possible, but has not been checked through later constants.
issues: Local displayed constant arithmetic at p.30 needs repair or a sharper scalar estimate; no counterexample to the overall theorem established.

review.authors: Leon Schiller
review.summary: For every fixed 0<ε≤1/2, sufficiently large fixed d, and q≥d+d^{1/2+ε}, Glauber dynamics on G(n,d/n) mixes with high probability in O_{d,ε}(n^{2+ζ}(1+log(1/δ))), ζ=C_ε log(q)/d^ε. review.prior_frontier: Earlier Glauber range was q>(1.7632+o(1))d; concurrently Li–Yang obtain q≥(1+ε)d with an unspecified polynomial exponent. Other non-MCMC samplers already worked near d. This improves a specific chain, not the existence of any sampler.

score_reasons.significance: Brings standard single-site dynamics to sublinear surplus above average degree despite unbounded maximum degree.
score_reasons.novelty: Port-gradient elimination retains useful random-graph spectral information after isolating hubs.

remaining: Full covariance decay on tree/unicyclic blocks, construction of breakpoint blocks, trimmed random-graph spectral bound and separator-based Glauber comparison remain unaudited.

review.authors: Mu-Xia Sun

score_reasons.significance: Turns difficult rare-event evaluation into global relative optimization without polynomial dependence on 1/OPT.
score_reasons.novelty: Connectivity log-concavity and pivotal-cut investment bounds supply useful directions although unreliability itself is nonconvex.
score_reasons.depth: Combines matroid polynomial limits, weighted stochastic mirror descent, recovery queries, and near-minimum-cut freezing.
score_reasons.exposition: States estimator assumptions, numerical operation model, and the separate preprocessing dependence explicitly.

checked: Checked pivotal derivative identities, including self-loops and parallel edges; the mark is zero unless exactly two components remain.
Traced connectivity log-concavity from spanning-set polynomials via r parallel copies and the exponential limit, and derived the relative-gap gradient inequality.
Checked minimum-cut/component domination using exponential merger clocks and the stochastic-gradient normalization/second-moment calculation conditional on the pivotal-investment lemma.
remaining: The cited matroid-morphism polynomial theorem’s exact applicability, pivotal-investment entropy/induction proof, marked estimator extension, mirror-descent recovery and frozen-cut regime remain to audit. These form a substantial 60-page dependency chain.

review.title: Approximate Syzygies of Smoothed Polynomials and Applications
review.authors: Aditya Bhaskara, Anxin Guo, Tanmay Sinha, Vaidehi Srinivas, Aravindan Vijayaraghavan
review.summary: For fixed degrees and fixed output degree t, powers of independently Gaussian-smoothed polynomial generators have every approximate syzygy polynomially close to the Koszul syzygy space when Σ_i n^{−d_iD_i}≤n^{−ε}. Gives polynomial conditioning of the restricted Macaulay matrix. Applications include smoothed power-sum recovery for m=O(n^{2dD/(3d−2)}) and robust global uniqueness of smoothed symmetric cubic decompositions of rank O(n^{3/2}); uniqueness is not an efficient recovery algorithm.
review.prior_frontier: Extends exact/generic algebraic statements to quantitative smoothed conditioning, resolves the stated power-sum smoothed-analysis question, and improves robust uniqueness from linear to superlinear rank. Explicitly repairs an earlier incorrect degree-four syzygy claim with an n^{−ε} loss.

score_reasons.significance: A general robust syzygy theorem supports several substantive algebraic and statistical consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Handles a random kernel of exact cancellations through variable gradation and successive shrinking rather than naive independent-column arguments.

checked: Traced Lemma 4.2 reconstruction: decompose h modulo ideals, differentiate Σb_i h_i to degree t−1, use the lower-degree pseudoinverse, then Euler’s identity. The remainder coefficients d_jD_j Γ_ji−d_iD_i Γ_ij are skew-symmetric and therefore Koszul; multiplication by y preserves that space.
Checked the resulting h=k0+(I−L2 M)g+L2 f and its stated operator-norm reduction under Bombieri multiplication/differentiation identities.
remaining: Large-proof exception (106 pages). The derivative/pseudoinverse reconstruction and Koszul skew-symmetry lemma were traced, with the displayed operator norm reduction. The successive-shrinkage probability argument and application-specific robust uniqueness proofs remain necessary and unverified.

Main successive-shrinkage anti-concentration, all induction uniformity/probability accounting, and robust power-sum/global uniqueness applications remain unaudited. The inspected reconstruction lemma alone does not establish the main theorem.

review.summary: Randomized fully dynamic connectivity on initially empty simple undirected graphs uses O(log³ n) worst-case insertion/deletion time, optimal O(log n/loglog n) query time, and O(n log² n) words. Correct throughout any fixed polynomial update horizon with high probability, including an adversary observing query answers only. An extra current-edge dictionary makes positive answers always correct and adds O(m) space.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the decade-old O(log⁴ n) worst-case cutset-based deletion bound by removing nested-forest propagation. Does not provide full internal-state-adaptive or Las Vegas correctness.

score_reasons.significance: Improves a long-standing worst-case bound for a basic dynamic graph problem while retaining space and query guarantees.
score_reasons.novelty: Nonnested forests with representative mass and one merge per level replace containment-based progress.
score_reasons.depth: Limited-independence read-two concentration and final-forest cut counting complement a concise deterministic invariant.
score_reasons.exposition: Interfaces, adversary model and always-valid time versus probabilistic correctness are carefully stated.

checked: Checked light-upper-tree promotion: mass zero supplies a lower-tree crossing path; mass one uses its successful cutset pair or a path from the relevant representative. Euler-tour bisection only needs endpoint membership disagreement, not monotonicity.

Verified counting lemma: heavy upper trees imply 2cc(F_i)≤2cc(F_{i−1})−S_i and hence deficit contraction by 127/128 when S_i≥D(F_{i−1})/64. One merge offsets the at-most-one deficit increase of a single update.
Read k-wise concentration roadmap: products of quadratic failure majorants use at most k labels and can transfer to fully independent read-two bounds.
remaining: Large-proof exception (36 pages). The light-tree promotion and forest-deficit contraction were checked, including the nonmonotone Euler-tour bisection argument. The limited-independence concentration and reuse-of-randomness implementation are the remaining central probabilistic/data-structural obligations.
The full limited-independence tail calculation, soundness under reused randomness, final-forest repair and RAM implementation still need audit.

review.title: Near-Optimal One-Way Functions, Direct Product Hardness and Hash Functions from iO and NP versus coNP
review.authors: Rahul Ilango, Alex Lombardi, Yaxin Tu

score_reasons.significance: Near-optimal low-success hardness is a substantial conceptual strengthening of standard one-wayness.
score_reasons.novelty: Planting many satisfying preimages and symmetrizing an arbitrary inverter turns rare inversion into a set-size certificate for UNSAT.
score_reasons.depth: The puncturing, point-probability-to-statistical-distance conversion, and quantitative regularity estimates must hold at exponentially small scales.
score_reasons.exposition: The warm-up isolates the key argument, although the distinction between success-probability and running-time hardness needs care.

checked: Traced the central OWF theorem through the perfect-sampler warm-up and full Claims 4.6–4.9: planted SAT witnesses, averaged preimage counts, and the Goldwasser–Sipser probability gap.
Checked Lemma 4.10's collision test and maximum-load bound, including the random-output versus random-image loss and exclusion of noninjective inner PRFs.

Checked the four-hybrid puncturing argument for equality of individual preimage probabilities, summation over possible inverter outputs, and conversion to total variation at sufficiently large polynomial security parameter.
Traced the zero-circuit inversion argument deriving subexponential OWFs from iO and nondeterministic hardness.
remaining: The direct-product, collision-resistant/output-intractable hashing, and output-permutable trapdoor-permutation extensions were not fully audited.

The precise CCR16 obfuscated-puncturable-PRF lemma and standard cryptographic compiler dependencies are used as cited; direct retrieval of the primary PDF returned HTTP 403, so these external proofs were not independently replayed.

review.summary: Assuming subexponentially secure iO and NP not contained infinitely often in coNP/poly, constructs one-way functions with inversion probability at most 2^(−n+n^ε) against polynomial-time adversaries, with near-optimal direct-product hardness and related hash constructions. The claim concerns very small success probabilities for polynomial-time adversaries, rather than near-exponential running-time hardness.
review.prior_frontier: Prior quantitative hardness and direct-product results did not obtain this near-optimal exponent from the stated qualitative nondeterministic hardness and iO assumptions; ordinary hardness amplification loses constants in the exponent.

review.title: Tight Low-Diameter Decompositions and Tree Embeddings in Partially Dynamic Graphs
review.authors: Ioannis Dorkofikis, Maximilian Probst Gutenberg
review.summary: Maintains O(log n)-quality low-diameter decompositions and tree embeddings in either incremental or decremental graphs with m^{1+o(1)} expected total update time and near-linear expected recourse, against an oblivious adversary.
review.prior_frontier: Prior near-linear partially dynamic methods did not match the logarithmic static quality; the stated comparison rules out a previous log^{3−Ω(1)}-quality subquadratic result.

score_reasons.significance: Recovers the static quality in a major dynamic metric primitive.
score_reasons.novelty: Independent exponential radii and monotone candidate/blur machinery improve the dynamic tradeoff.
score_reasons.depth: White-box approximate shortest-path maintenance and correlated cut-distance estimates.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit partial-dynamic, adversary, and expectation qualifications.

checked: Checked the annulus proof of the center-distance second moment: conditioning on the permutation, independent radii give e^(2−k)/(N+1), and controlled ball growth makes the squared-distance tail summable. Read the weighted edge-cut setup.
remaining: Full weighted-cut bound, dynamic candidate graph invariant, and amortized update/recourse proofs remain unchecked.
The embedding is not necessarily a spanning subgraph tree; these are not fully dynamic or adaptive-adversary guarantees.

papers.title: A Note on a Result of Chen Li: the Thinning Problem via the Kernel Method
papers.authors: Xuan Fang, Tianyu Wang

review.title: A Note on a Result of Chen Li: the Thinning Problem via the Kernel Method
review.authors: Xuan Fang, Tianyu Wang
review.summary: For a q-spread random set J, independent t-thinning is stochastically dominated by product measure of density tq/(1−t+tq). In particular αp-spread J thinned at α≤(√5−1)/2 is dominated by product density p, settling the stated Talagrand thinning conjecture.
review.prior_frontier: Adapts Chen Li’s recent vanishing-kernel argument for fractional discrete convexity. The further implications for Talagrand Conjectures 7.3 and 7.11 are attributed to Talagrand rather than proved here.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a named dimension-independent stochastic-domination question with explicit parameters.
score_reasons.novelty: Changes the kernel’s zero pattern to encode containment of a thinned parent and extracts a nonnegative Fourier certificate.
score_reasons.depth: The central proof is short but conceptually effective; it relies only on biased Fourier orthogonality after constructing the kernel.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly explains why the kernel may be signed and distinguishes independence of the thinning mask from the final containing coupling.

checked: Checked every step of the main proof: one-coordinate kernel entries and normalization, zero on (1,0), and the pointwise indicator ≤ square of the lifted function.
Verified biased Walsh expansion and Parseval, then q-spreadness bounds nonnegative coefficients by (β²q)^|I|≤1.

Solved the parameter inequality for p and checked the golden-ratio α choice. Checked that the final coupling can preserve the original independent (J,mask) pair by sampling its target conditional on the intersection.
remaining: The historical identification and the two further Talagrand implications are cited, not independently reconstructed. The main quantitative domination theorem is self-contained.

papers.title: Comparison is All You Need: Settling the $t$-wise independence of AES
papers.authors: Angelos Pelecanos, Stefano Tessaro, Vinod Vaikuntanathan

review.title: Comparison is All You Need: Settling the $t$-wise independence of AES
review.authors: Angelos Pelecanos, Stefano Tessaro, Vinod Vaikuntanathan
review.summary: Generalized AES on n=d²b bits, b≥4,d≥2, with independent uniform round keys is ε-approximately t-wise independent after O(n²b²(nt+log(1/ε))) rounds for 2≤t≤2^n−2. Uses the actual inversion S-box/full linear round layers. This is not a security proof for the practical AES key schedule or practical round counts.
review.prior_frontier: Prior higher-order bounds concerned idealized S-boxes or censored mixing layers, whereas recent practical-round improvements were only pairwise. Achieves the full parity-allowed t range with polynomial round dependence.

score_reasons.significance: Establishes higher-order statistical security for an important exact algebraic round architecture under a clearly idealized key model.
score_reasons.novelty: Balanced simulations compare a symmetrized AES walk directly to a constant-gap alternating-group expander.
score_reasons.depth: Reversible gate compilation into byte gadgets and congestion-free comparison are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Strong headline is appropriately qualified by independent keys and potentially enormous round count.

checked: Checked balanced-gadget cancellation Lemma 4.2 for depths0–3: mirrored seven-key words produce conjugated translations with 2+4j steps; repeated words retain each label’s uniform marginal despite correlations.

Verified why marginally balanced permutation paths suffice for L² Dirichlet comparison: for each fixed label sequence, change variables by its prefix permutation before averaging; no conditional independence of successive labels is required.
Checked spectral transfer from (P³)^T P³ and parity/transitivity restriction t≤2^n−2.
remaining: Core AES byte arithmetic/Toffoli compilation and its exceptional-input corrections, plus ancilla-free short Kassabov-generator dependency, not audited.

review.title: Zero-Knowledge PCPs of Quasilinear Size via Locally Simulatable Sheaf Codes
review.authors: Hadas Zeilberger, Jack O'Connor, Tom Gur, Nicholas Spooner

score_reasons.significance: The proof-length improvement concerns a central PCP and zero-knowledge tradeoff.
score_reasons.novelty: Extendable covers of sheaf codes provide a reusable route to perfect local simulation.
score_reasons.depth: The construction combines affine extension, recursive code gluing, Reed–Solomon proximity testing, and locality-preserving query reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: The layered definitions are substantial but the simulator and parameter dependencies are stated explicitly; some local runtime notation is imprecise.

checked: Traced the extendability-to-local-simulation core: affine solution sampling, equal-size fibers of linear restrictions, conditioning on prior answers, and adaptive point-query simulation.
Checked the extension lemmas based on dimension, disjoint supports, transitivity, and the MDS dual-distance condition.
Checked the final parameter interface: simulator locality and query budget, t=max(b²,T)polylog(T), and the role of locally computable gap amplification.
remaining: Large-proof exception: the full 50-page recursive gluing and explicit Reed–Solomon extendability/testability construction were not completely checked.
The imported RLACSP reduction and the complete locality analysis of Dinur query reduction remain unchecked.
Lemma 6.11's displayed per-step runtime omits the accumulated query-set size; its proof establishes poly(|P_A*|), consistent with the q-dependent polynomial bound in Theorem 6.7.

review.summary: Constructs constant-query perfect zero-knowledge PCPs for NTIME(T) of length soft-O(T+b²), secure against verifiers making b proof queries. Thus b up to roughly √T is compatible with quasilinear length. Locally simulatable sheaf codes replace the interactive proximity component of earlier constructions.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier zero-knowledge PCP constructions and succinct-constraint-detection approaches did not simultaneously provide the stated quasilinear length and constant query complexity with this bounded-query perfect-zero-knowledge guarantee.

papers.authors: Petra Berenbrink, Dhanush Ramadas Giriyan, Thorsten Götte, Andrea Richa

review.title: Fast Minority Dynamics with $\Theta(\log^2 n)$-Size Samples
review.authors: Petra Berenbrink, Dhanush Giriyan, Thorsten Götte, Andréa W. Richa
review.summary: Binary minority dynamics with unanimous-sample retention and odd sample size Θ(log² n) reaches consensus from every initial configuration in expected O(log² n/log k) rounds and O(log² n) rounds with high probability.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier fast-consensus analysis required samples of order at least √n log² n; constant-size samples can be slow.

score_reasons.significance: Substantially reduces the sample size needed for polylogarithmic consensus.
score_reasons.novelty: Weighted core-return contraction handles the nonmonotone folded-binomial chain.
score_reasons.depth: Detailed excursion kernels and local concentration estimates.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear transition model, but the multiple retained regions and kernels make verification substantial.

checked: Checked the lower-region growth estimate by summing shrinking relative errors rather than multiplying a worst error by the path length; j=(1+o(1))k^h z limits the possible return lengths to three or two. Read how weighted return bounds yield the final hitting-time estimates.
remaining: The complete 3/4 weighted-core contraction and local auxiliary-chain coupling require audit.
Applies to the specified complete-population sampling-with-replacement process and k=Θ(log² n), not arbitrary networks or every larger k.

papers.authors: Xuan Fang, Tianyu Wang

review.title: A Two-regime Khintchine Inequality and an Improved Bound on the Degree-1 Fourier Weight for Linear Threshold Functions
review.authors: Xuan Fang, Tianyu Wang
review.summary: Proves an exact four-coordinate Khintchine stability profile, an initial six-coordinate regime, global robust slope 1/20, and W≤1(f)≥0.55100929 for every Boolean linear threshold function. The conjectured 2/π Fourier bound remains open.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the explicitly stated robust slope 8×10^−5 and earlier qualitative 1/2+ε Fourier-weight progress. The Fourier corollary uses separate coefficient/conditioned-Chow estimates rather than depending on the robust theorem.

score_reasons.significance: Gives sizable explicit progress on a classical Fourier-weight conjecture and near-optimal robust Khintchine slope.
score_reasons.novelty: Separates sharp finite-coordinate regimes and exploits sixth-moment tail minorants plus conditioned Chow information.
score_reasons.depth: Exact numerical endpoints and global regime coverage are needed in addition to analytic inequalities.
score_reasons.exposition: Distinguishes proved six-coordinate interval from conjectural continuation and states exact rational numerical constants.

checked: Fully checked the four-coordinate profile proof by conditioning on the first two signs, applying sharp Khintchine to the tail, and tracing equality cases.

Read and checked the structure of the robust-slope case split and Fourier-weight reduction: q≥4/3 uses Chebyshev and conditioned Chow; 1≤q≤4/3 uses the concave Khintchine lower bound; q≤1 invokes a separate analytic estimate.
Checked the Wallis-ratio recurrence calculation and its limiting comparison.
remaining: The six-coordinate global-minimizer certificate, supporting curvature/rational endpoint inequalities, sixth-moment minorant, and conditioned Chow lemma remain unverified. They are substantial parts of the 29-page multi-theorem proof, so the final constants are not certified by this partial reading.

papers.title: Nash Equilibria, Variational Inequalities, and Fixed Points: Beating Brute Force via Smoothed Analysis
papers.authors: Idan Attias, Yuval Dagan, Constantinos Daskalakis, Rui Yao, Manolis Zampetakis

review.title: Nash Equilibria, Variational Inequalities, and Fixed Points: Beating Brute Force via Smoothed Analysis
review.authors: Idan Attias, Yuval Dagan, Constantinos Daskalakis, Rui Yao, Manolis Zampetakis
review.summary: Under pointwise bounded-density and Lipschitz assumptions, a deterministic cover-refinement algorithm finds approximate fixed points with expected C^n P_v Vol(B_n) log(1/epsilon) evaluations; VI uses projection with separate boundary density. For m-player n-action games with deviation-payoff vector density at most M^(mn), expected (CmM)^(mn) log(m/epsilon) evaluations. A separate first-order homotopy theorem gives another smoothed bound under stronger joint derivative densities.
review.prior_frontier: Beats epsilon^(-Theta(n)) black-box brute force in accuracy dependence, not the exponential dimension barrier; independent random payoff entries give M growing as n^((m-1)/2), whereas constant action-cost perturbations yield the cleaner exponential bound. Prior comparison taken from manuscript.

score_reasons.significance: Accuracy dependence drops from dimension-dependent power to logarithm under a concrete smoothed model.
score_reasons.novelty: Multiscale bounded-density covering and a distinct normalized homotopy analysis.
score_reasons.depth: Joint Jacobian/path conditioning and projected boundary density need substantial geometric control.
score_reasons.exposition: Density assumptions are explicit; not every random game gives constant M.

checked: Checked cover refinement: Brouwer fixed point always has a retained nearby center, expected survivor count cancels radius^n against grid size, local children count <18^n, and enumeration via bounded integer prefixes is C^n.
Checked projected approximate fixed point implies VI error at most (L0+2) times residual, including boundary multiplier lambda.
remaining: Nash-specific covering proof and all homotopy conditioning/path-length arguments have not been fully audited; boundary-density corollary only locally checked.

papers.authors: Andrew Krapivin, Jiatu Li, Elaine Shi

review.title: Fine-Grained Proof Complexity for Elementary Arithmetic in Extended Frege
review.authors: Andrew Krapivin, Jiatu Li, Elaine Shi

score_reasons.significance: Near-circuit-size proofs of basic arithmetic are a meaningful advance in fine-grained proof complexity.
score_reasons.novelty: The dynamically computed counterexample index offers a particularly reusable proof-compression device.
score_reasons.depth: The full result requires detailed bit-level FFT, rounding, carry, and proof-cost bookkeeping.
score_reasons.exposition: The context/extension conventions and worked witness circuit make the main mechanism inspectable despite the 148-page length.

checked: Traced Lemma 3.4 completely: balanced failure-witness circuit, local selectors, conditional equality propagation, application at the computed witness, and OR-tree unfolding.
Checked cost sums O(m) for witness construction, O(m log m) for selector comparisons, and S+O(m(|P|+w+log m)) overall without copying the premise derivation.
Checked the required arbitrary-extended-context hypothesis and Appendix B's gatewise equality propagation and selection-through-circuit proofs.
Checked the linear-size commutativity-of-addition warm-up.
remaining: Large-proof exception: the full 148-page FFT implementation, finite-precision error bounds, nested index-generalization applications, and arithmetic identity derivations were not audited end to end.
No formal proof checker was run; the checked object is the mathematical proof-generation argument.

review.summary: Gives quasilinear-size Extended Frege proofs of elementary arithmetic identities for FFT-based multiplication and linear-size proofs for ripple-carry addition. An index-generalization rule converts a proof at a variable array index into proofs at every index without copying the entire derivation for each entry.
review.prior_frontier: Direct coordinate-by-coordinate formalization of FFT arithmetic incurs a quadratic proof-size loss even when the underlying circuit is quasilinear. These are proof-size constructions, not a claim of a supplied machine-checked formalization.

papers.title: A Complete Characterization of Central String Queries in Compact Space
papers.authors: Dominik Kempa, Tomasz Kociumaka

review.title: A Complete Characterization of Central String Queries in Compact Space
review.authors: Dominik Kempa, Tomasz Kociumaka
review.summary: Gives constant-factor-preserving equivalences between central compact string queries and simpler prefix operations, preserving alphabet and all four space/time measures. Constructs the PLCP bitvector deterministically in O(n min{1,log σ/√log n}) time, with O(n log σ) working bits and O(n)-bit/O(1)-query final indexing.
review.prior_frontier: Compact BWT/LF/Phi/LCP/SA queries had disparate bounds and reductions losing alphabet or preprocessing parameters; optimal-size PLCP indexing lacked this sublinear packed-input construction.

score_reasons.significance: A broad unification plus a concrete faster construction for a central succinct index.
score_reasons.novelty: Alphabet-preserving encoding and LCP-profile reduction are substantial new machinery.
score_reasons.depth: 191-page collection of independent reductions, packed-string primitives, synchronization, and periodic/nonperiodic cases.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed definitions and parameter accounting, but exceptional length limits a complete initial audit.

checked: Checked Lemma 6.11 completely: the encoded block-start suffixes form a contiguous interval, retain original suffix order, and their BWT predecessors reveal each base-alphabet digit including the cyclic predecessor case.

Checked Lemmas 9.12–9.13 completely: synchronization gives an order-preserving occurrence/label bijection; capped LCE profiles recover nonperiodic PLCP marks; disjoint owned intervals bound total unary-profile length, with distinct-label charging for the exceptional cases.
Checked the algebra combining Theorems 8.18 and 9.23 into Theorem 10.1 and the select-based O(1) PLCP query conversion in Theorem 10.2.
remaining: Large-proof exception: 191 pages contain multiple independent equivalence families. The full packed-string implementation primitives, LF/Phi/LCP/SA equivalences, periodic PLCP treatment, and LCP-profile construction algorithm remain unchecked.
The Dictionary Matching conditional lower-bound reduction and the final alphabet/length-preserving wrappers require independent audit.
The paper characterizes several unresolved tradeoffs by equivalence; it does not give optimal numeric bounds for every query.

papers.title: Lossless Hardness Condensation in Deterministic Communication Complexity
papers.authors: Simon Mackenzie

review.title: Lossless Hardness Condensation in Deterministic Communication Complexity
review.authors: Simon Mackenzie
review.summary: Every finite total Boolean matrix of deterministic fixed-leaf-output communication complexity c≥4 contains an original 2^k-square with k≥(εc−4)/3 and complexity ≥(1−ε)(k+1). Gives a fixed-size c/3−O(log c) guarantee and doubly-exponential-parameter constructive extraction.
review.prior_frontier: Answers a lossless-condensation question recorded by Göös–Newman–Riazanov–Sokolov, improving Hrubeš’s stated √c input-length scale. The result uses arbitrary original row/column restrictions and deterministic protocols, not randomized or coordinate-query restrictions.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a general structural question about where deterministic communication hardness resides and contradicts a recorded negative conjecture.
score_reasons.novelty: Counts domains of whole executable protocols, avoiding the loss from rectangle partitions, then combines rank-sensitive covering with hard nonsingular minors.
score_reasons.depth: Careful finite counting, two-sided restriction budgets and fixed-output rank refinements achieve near-maximal hardness.
score_reasons.exposition: Defines compatibility correctly with one Bob choice working for every retained row and illustrates each combinatorial operation.

checked: Traced the entire existential main proof. Verified compatibility domains are intersection/union trees with common Bob assignments, not row-dependent choices.
Checked minimal leaf constraints yield I_q or J_q−I_q witness matrices and at most 2(r+1)^(r+1) conditions via row sums on basis columns.
Verified the domain count, finite hitting set, strict-halving cover using at most r domains, and legal protocol concatenation.

Checked both restriction steps, size padding with distinct original inputs, the rank-refined lower bound for nonsingular squares, and high/low-rank parameter cases yielding both stated existential guarantees.
remaining: The constructive extraction running-time analysis and multiplayer appendix have not been fully audited. The checked principal existential theorem is self-contained; this is not a formal verification.

papers.title: Learning CNF Formulas with Uniform Random Solutions and Membership Queries

review.title: Learning CNF Formulas with Uniform Random Solutions and Membership Queries
review.authors: Weiming Feng, Yixiao Yu, Yiyao Zhang
review.summary: With uniform satisfying samples and membership queries, learns constant-(k,d) CNFs in the LLL regime k roughly (1+1/t)log d in n^{O_t(1)}/epsilon time; t=1 gives soft-O(n^3+n^2/epsilon). For fixed k>=10^5 and alpha<=2^{k-soft-O(k^{4/5})}, exactly learns random k-CNF as a solution set in soft-O_{k,alpha}(n^{2+o_k(1)}). Sample-only hardness is conditional on specified junta-learning hypotheses.
review.prior_frontier: Sample-only Valiant enumeration retains n^k despite small sample complexity; improvement requires membership queries and very large fixed width for the random-formula theorem. Prior bounds stated in paper.

score_reasons.significance: Removes the width-dependent exponent in structured CNF learning with active access.
score_reasons.novelty: LearnCore uses membership queries to find minimal violating flip sets.
score_reasons.depth: LLL/random-formula structural analysis and junta hardness are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Different distributional, query and exact-learning guarantees are carefully separated.

checked: Checked minimal-core antichain and unique clause witnesses; each core intersects at most dk others.
Checked shrinking by k+1 parts retains a violated width-k clause, and pruning preserves an undiscovered witness with probability at least 1/[2(16dk)^k] conditional on any history.
remaining: Need full recovery/approximation assembly from cores, random formula witness probabilities and junta reduction; no whole-paper correctness clearance.

score_reasons.significance: Clarifies when privacy removes the benefit of private verifier randomness and connects this to concrete testing tasks.
score_reasons.novelty: The smooth consistency gate lets a prover propose the original transcript while retaining privacy control.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines DP-to-replicability transfer, pairwise-independent steering, and acceptance-probability analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: The formal theorem usefully exposes runtime and communication qualifications absent from the informal equal-cost statement.

checked: Inspected the formal conversion parameters and the gate κ²p_Sq_S/(U²+κ²p_S²).

remaining: The complete soundness and differential-privacy proof, transfer-theorem dependencies, and independence-verification bounds have not been audited.

review.summary: Studies differentially private verification of distribution properties, including a private-coin to public-coin conversion in a strong-privacy regime and sample/communication bounds for independence verification. The conversion uses replicability and a smooth acceptance gate, and is not computationally efficient.

papers.title: Proof of Quantum Work with Classical Verification
papers.authors: Mohammed Barhoush

review.title: Proof of Quantum Work with Classical Verification
review.authors: Mohammed Barhoush
review.summary: Constructs publicly classically verifiable proof of quantum work in the QROM. The metered variant at difficulty d=O(log λ) requires and achieves Θ(λ+2^d) quantum queries for inverse-polynomial success, even with polynomially many classical queries.
review.prior_frontier: YZ gives classically verifiable quantum advantage but does not by itself meter the quantum-query work. Previous PoQW proposals lacked this hybrid quantitative guarantee.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a precise resource lower bound for a cryptographic primitive.
score_reasons.novelty: Transcript-indexed low-degree amplitude bound handles adaptive interleaved classical/quantum queries.
score_reasons.depth: A concise Fourier dimension argument coupled with list recovery.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully distinguishes quantum gating, metering, and one-block oracle security.

checked: Checked Theorem 4 in full: append verification queries, list a candidate at its Kth distinct classically queried coordinate, and bound the number of candidate/context pairs by (C+1)L using list recovery.

For each fixed transcript, its remaining m inputs are fixed and never classically queried on that transcript. Unnormalized amplitudes have degree ≤Q in those bits, despite adaptive quantum measurements. Fourier/Cauchy–Schwarz gives the binomial factor, and summing transcript probabilities uses the candidate count rather than an invalid conditioned-uniformity assumption.
Checked the oracle simulation and binomial/Hoeffding consequences in Theorem 5 and Corollary 3. Verified the exact YZ list-recovery parameters against original Lemma 4.2 (arXiv:2204.02063, PDF p22).

Verified the linear-query honest solver: original YZ preparation and correctness (PDF p29) have independent fresh trials with conditional success at least 1/3; a total 6N-trial cutoff fails exponentially rarely and preserves the intended states.
remaining: The separate quantum-gated construction was not fully audited; the main check covers the metered construction and its principal new lower bound.
Security is in the random-oracle, oracle-independent-initial-state, charged-preprocessing, one-block experiment. Concrete hash instantiation, consensus security, and energy efficiency are not proved.

papers.title: The Price of Agreement in Secure Multiparty Computation

review.title: The Price of Agreement in Secure Multiparty Computation
review.authors: Ran Cohen, Pouyan Forghani, Juan Garay, Vassilis Zikas
review.summary: Unanimous-abort broadcast against t≤n−2 static rushing omission corruptions requires expected rounds at least t/[2(n−t)], for any input-independent setup. Gives exact fixed-round lower bounds and transfers the expected-round obstruction to unanimous-abort MPC.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the asymptotic GKKO broadcast barrier to agreement with abort, where the usual honest-sender forcing argument fails. Constant-round sufficiency uses prior cryptographic assumptions and a constant honest fraction.

score_reasons.significance: Closes the possibility of expected constant-round unanimous-abort MPC with a vanishing honest fraction.
score_reasons.novelty: A chain of omission executions identifies a slow witness, then two rushing adversaries implement the coin-dependent cut without knowing honest randomness.
score_reasons.depth: The critical issue is realizability of the selected attack from local messages, not just an existential slow execution.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear distinction between rushing, oblivious omission, fixed versus expected rounds, and input-independent setup.

checked: Traced the yes/no/slow status chain and first-yes argument, including why validity plus input blindness makes the first yes negligible.

Checked Claim 3.3’s local simulation: deleting future honest messages changes a witness only after graph-distance propagation; one attack uses current-round honest messages, precisely accounting for rushing.
Checked the two-event probability union and the L=floor(n/(n−t)) arithmetic giving the expected-round coefficient asymptotically in the security parameter.
remaining: The complete line construction and all fixed-pattern simulated-security claims on pp.11–16 need checking; fixed-round and oblivious-adversary variants were not audited. This 32-page combined lower-bound analysis is only partially traced.

papers.title: Non-Interactive Network Sum-Secure Computation
papers.authors: Yang Bai, Xuan Guang, Lizhi Wang

review.title: Non-Interactive Network Sum-Secure Computation
review.authors: Yang Bai, Xuan Guang, Lizhi Wang
review.summary: For scalar linear computation of a sum over sufficiently large finite fields on DAG networks, characterizes solvability by mincut(S,rho)>=r+1. Feasible independent source-key counts z_i correspond to r+1 edge-disjoint paths with at most 1+z_i starting at i; optimal total keys equal r+1 minus maximum number of distinct starting sources. Security is the explicitly defined equality of probabilities of existential-input compatible key sets, not ordinary secrecy for arbitrary input distributions or user-input privacy.
review.prior_frontier: Introduces and solves a topology-dependent sum-security model; no blanket improvement for standard MPC. Manuscript explicitly distinguishes its security condition from information-theoretic secrecy under arbitrary input laws.

score_reasons.significance: Exact graph and randomness characterizations for a specialized security definition.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines source-local transformations with mincut-constrained key placement.
score_reasons.depth: Union-of-subspaces avoidance and path/rank constraints underlie construction.
score_reasons.exposition: The compatibility-of-key-set definition is precise but the informal indistinguishability language needs its restriction retained.

checked: Checked randomness formula follows from path multiplicities a_i and z_i=(a_i-1)^+.
Checked block-diagonal basis change sends a vector with each source block nonzero to the sum vector; wiretap spans have dimension at most r while receiver span has at least r+1.
remaining: Full finite-field subspace avoidance construction and necessity for every key assignment remain unverified.

review.summary: Settles the optimal deterministic competitive ratio for online joint replenishment with arbitrary weighted linear delays at ρ≈2.7549, where x=ρ−1 satisfies x(x−1)^2=1.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the longstanding upper bound 3 to the existing approximately 2.7549 single-phase lower bound, establishing equality of single- and multi-phase ratios.

score_reasons.significance: Closes a longstanding exact competitive-ratio gap in a standard aggregation problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Online budget revision and future slack forecasts improve on the prior primal-dual accounting.
score_reasons.depth: Ghost usage of served requests and purchase/checkpoint invariants.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise event ordering and a self-contained lower-bound budget argument.

checked: Checked Lemma 3: continuous monotone budget excess attains the joint cost, final budgets satisfy every purchase constraint, and summing over an offline solution bounds their sum by OPT. Read the actual slack-update identities around a purchase.
remaining: The complete purchase invariant and its case analysis remain unchecked.
The guarantee is deterministic and for linear delays; it does not resolve arbitrary-delay or deeper multi-level aggregation ratios.

review.title: Polynomial-time Tensor Decomposition under the Kruskal Condition and the Lovitz--Petrov Generalization
review.authors: Shiri Sivan
review.summary: Randomized polynomial-arithmetic-time tensor decomposition under the Lovitz–Petrov uniqueness condition, hence under Kruskal’s condition, with probability one over continuous real randomness. Allows exact univariate root finding; also gives polynomial verification of the LP condition and uniqueness certification.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves the stated algorithmic question at the Kruskal uniqueness threshold in an algebraic real model. This is not a numerical stability guarantee or a polynomial bit-time algorithm over rational inputs.

score_reasons.significance: Turns a classical identifiability threshold into an efficient decomposition criterion, including a strictly broader rank condition.
score_reasons.novelty: Alternating contractions produce two-dimensional component spaces, followed by a relative second contraction and spectral separation.
score_reasons.depth: Generic Dilworth truncation and determinant separation enable a Jennrich-like spectral algorithm without high individual factor rank.
score_reasons.exposition: The exact-root and continuous-randomness model is explicit; the algebraic geometry is compact and mostly self-contained.

checked: Traced the alternating contraction formula, component block recovery and generic-section argument. The LP inequality makes singleton blocks minimal in the Dilworth partition formula and gives direct 2-dimensional component spaces.

Checked the merged-pair generic-section argument supplies a vector outside R_i+L; annihilating that vector makes one determinant vanish but not the other, establishing generic distinct eigenvalue ratios.
Verified the inverse skew-form spectral operator acts by those ratios on component spaces, projectors recover contractions, and nonzero off-diagonal rank-one blocks recover all factors.

Checked polynomial input-size accounting after removing scalar modes, submodular minimization with a forced pair for LP verification, and the separate uniqueness proof for alternative decompositions not promised LP.
Independently fetched Antolini–Dewar–Tanigawa, arXiv:2508.04798, and checked Theorem 2.10 states the exact generic codimension-d Dilworth formula used here.
remaining: Did not execute the reference implementation or assess numerical conditioning; neither is claimed by the algebraic theorem. The external Dilworth theorem itself was checked for statement/hypotheses, not re-proved. Trivial rank-one/scalar-mode preprocessing must be handled separately when fewer than three nontrivial modes remain.

sources.detail: Uniqueness without LP promise on alternative
Verified external Theorem 2.10, generic codimension-k Dilworth truncation; downloaded primary-source PDF

review.title: Counterexamples to EFX for Submodular and Subadditive Valuations
review.authors: Hannaneh Akrami, Simon Mackenzie, Alexander Mayorov, Kurt Mehlhorn, Shreyas Srinivas, Mashbat Suzuki, Christoph Weidenbach
review.summary: Constructs three-agent eight-good monotone valuations with no complete EFX allocation and transfers the counterexample, with the same agents/goods, to weighted coverage. Extends to n>=3,m>=n+5. Separately claims existence for three agents <=7 goods, subadditive approximation obstruction alpha>2^{-1/6}, and a weighted-coverage obstruction near .957455; these further results were not audited. EFX quantifies every removed good, including zero marginal ones; the result does not settle additive valuations.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves general monotone, submodular and subadditive EFX nonexistence using a small explicit counterexample; additive EFX remains open. Exact prior landscape taken from manuscript.

score_reasons.significance: Explicit counterexample closes central existence questions for broad valuation classes.
score_reasons.novelty: Forces pair-based EFX shape then destroys it using exceptional triples; ordinal coverage transfer preserves all comparisons.
score_reasons.depth: Symmetry-based exclusion and coverage Möbius inversion give unusually transparent structural proof.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear complete central proof; several additional 67-page claims require separate checks.

checked: Traced Lemma3.1 and Proposition3.2 forced allocation Ay|BCCx|AB under pair values; Lemma3.3 exceptional triples cannot create another EFX allocation, and Theorem3.4 eliminates the forced shape.
Traced Lemma3.7: strictification preserves violations, rank-based F(S)=B^{q-k(S)}, B=2^m, has positive Möbius feature weights; resulting coverage equals B^q-B^{q-k(S)} and preserves the order.
Verified extension using k additional large goods and k extra copies forces each large-good bundle to be singleton and recovers the base contradiction.

Independent exact enumeration of all 3^8=6561 allocations found 24 EFX allocations for pair profile, zero for final monotone and zero for weighted coverage. Used strictification 100v+|S|, 31 ranks, 255 positive features per agent (minimum weight255); direct feature sums equal closed formula for all256 subsets. Script audits/audit1295.py and output1295-audit.json.
remaining: Three-agent seven-good positive theorem and the quantitative approximate-EFX barriers/positive approximation theorem were not audited. No additive-valuation consequence is claimed.

review.title: Linear-time erasure recovery for quantum expander codes
review.authors: Anirudh Krishna, Christopher Pattison

score_reasons.significance: Reaches the full guaranteed erasure radius with linear decoding time on an important code family.
score_reasons.novelty: Local degeneracy permits envelope replacement when ordinary peeling stalls.
score_reasons.depth: Two expansion projections force a large valid pair, followed by an equivalence-preserving progress invariant.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit algorithms, local-view diagrams and a queue-based amortized analysis make the central proof particularly accessible.

checked: Traced the complete new decoder proof: unique-neighbor alternatives, the two projection/expansion steps, and the forced rectangular pair of erased qubits.
Checked Fill's syndrome-parity assignments, the unknown stabilizer-complement bit, shrinking envelope, and telescoping equivalence invariant.
Checked the linear-time queue accounting and exhaustive constant-size generator-subset search for fixed degrees; input is a sparse erasure/syndrome list.
remaining: The Pauli-error corollary imports Small-Set-Find; that external decoder was not independently audited.
No implementation or formal proof checker was run.

review.summary: Small-Set-Peeling corrects every erasure set smaller than the design distance of a quantum expander code in O(|L|) time for fixed graph degrees and expansion error below 1/4. It uses stabilizer equivalence to replace part of the erasure envelope rather than insisting the correction stay inside it.
review.prior_frontier: Generic quantum erasure decoding is polynomial but not linear; previous quantum expander decoders did not provide this full design-distance erasure guarantee in linear time. The design distance is a lower bound on actual code distance.

papers.title: No size-preserving amplification with quantum advice
papers.authors: Shih-Han Hung, Han-Hsuan Lin

review.title: No size-preserving amplification with quantum advice
review.authors: Shih-Han Hung, Han-Hsuan Lin
review.summary: Shows that fixed-length quantum advice does not admit generic size-preserving error amplification: for every growing polynomial advice budget m, some languages separate errors ε and ε+δ, with δ=O(√(log m/m)) for fixed ε<1/2. The higher-error algorithm can use only randomized classical advice.
review.prior_frontier: QMA witnesses have Marriott–Watrous size-preserving amplification; ordinary BQP/qpoly error reduction can enlarge advice, leaving the exact-budget question open.

score_reasons.significance: Clarifies a fundamental difference between witnesses and advice with quantitative vanishing gaps.
score_reasons.novelty: Efficient Toeplitz random-access codes with a shared mask/shift header make an entropy diagonalization computationally meaningful.
score_reasons.depth: Elementary but carefully combined coding, entropy perturbation, and nonuniform information theory.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed parameter rounding and uniform decoding model make the proof unusually checkable.

checked: Checked the full new Toeplitz-code construction: nonzero-word syndrome collision bound via a triangular full-rank submatrix, second-moment covering, shift/mask symmetrization, and reuse of one header across blocks. Marginal bit recovery needs no block independence.
Checked the decoder time and header space, Theorem 3.8 floor/ceiling and entropy bounds, and the O(log k) parameter header in Theorem 4.2.
Checked the QRAC diagonalization against Nayak’s standard mixed-state bound m≥(1−H(ε))k, including the strict inequality from k=floor(m/(1−H(ε)))+1 and countability of all uniform circuit generators.
Checked the polynomial-time specialization and δ bounds in Corollary 4.6. Noncomputable parameter choices are stored in advice; quantum circuit generators explicitly receive the advice length.
remaining: The external standard Nayak entropy bound is used as a known theorem, not reproved here.

This is an existential language separation with arbitrary advice preparation; it does not provide an efficient natural hard language or contradict amplification that increases advice length. Near-1/2 errors can make the displayed larger-error class trivial at some lengths.

review.title: Multi-Selection Pandora's Box with Nonobligatory Inspection: A PTAS and a Structural Separation
review.authors: Hedyeh Beyhaghi, Tianyang Han, Ahmed Luqman
review.summary: A PTAS for selecting up to constant k prizes in Pandora’s box with nonobligatory inspection. Shows single-selection policy structure fails already for two closed claims, while a state-dependent two-phase description survives if at most one prize may be claimed unopened.
review.prior_frontier: Prior multiselection guarantees were constant factors; existing single-selection PTASs relied on structural properties that do not extend. Polynomial running time fixes both k and ε.

score_reasons.significance: Extends an approximation scheme to genuine multiselection while explaining why the old policy representation cannot simply be reused.
score_reasons.novelty: Mixed-state discretization and a high-floor continuation proxy separate small-value losses from a one-time tail loss.
score_reasons.depth: Requires adaptive-policy rounding, action exclusion and a two-source proxy-error estimate.
score_reasons.exposition: The fixed-k restriction and the distinction between unopened-claim budget and total selections are clear.

checked: Checked the stochastic-DP formulation and reward telescoping, including replacement by expected value for unopened boxes independently of their unseen value.
Traced the opposite-order top-k matching identity and decomposition into overflow and chain losses.
Checked that a high floor makes E[min(k,N)]≤ε, and independence of each box from the other competitors bounds the chain loss by εΦ and overflow by εΦ/k.
remaining: Full mixed-state rounding, verification of all Fu–Li–Xu framework assumptions, policy reconstruction and structural counterexamples/one-closed-claim induction remain unaudited.

review.title: Encoding orders and trees in real-valued functions
review.authors: G. Conant, C. Terry
review.summary: For f:X×Y→[0,1], a tree of height binomial(2k,k)-1 and gap2delta yields a length-k nonuniform delta ladder. Uniform extraction costs height ceil(1/epsilon)*4^k with gap2delta+epsilon, giving double-exponential dual sequential fat-shattering bounds. A further tight-threshold theorem gives height (1/epsilon)^{O(k/epsilon²)}.
review.prior_frontier: Improves earlier tree-to-threshold quantitative bounds, resolves Daskalakis–Golowich dual-dimension question and claims to recover the stronger previously flawed tight-threshold bound of Jung–Kim–Tewari. Prior-source comparison not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Settles two quantitative structure questions connecting stable functions and online learning.
score_reasons.novelty: Nonuniform ladders and parallel node/leaf colorings avoid an expensive Ramsey step.
score_reasons.depth: Asymmetric real-valued tree embeddings require paired induction and careful scale control.
score_reasons.exposition: Self-contained combinatorial framework clearly separates uniform and tight conclusions.

checked: Traced node-coloring Lemma2.6 by induction, proper extension of embeddings, and uniformization Proposition2.9.

Traced full Theorem1.11 two-outcome induction: T(k,l)<=T(k-1,l)+T(k,l-1)+1, B=2*binomial(k+l-2,k-1)-1; B(k,k+1)=binomial(2k,k)-1. Opposite branches prepend the chosen leaf with the correct strict versus weak thresholds.

Checked uniform corollary, dual reversal of uniform ladders, and complete binary-search ladder-to-tree TheoremA.4; plugging k=2^t gives the claimed double exponential. Checked scale2delta necessity via intersecting nonnested prefix cylinders.
remaining: The separate tight-threshold Theorem1.14 (Section4), agnostic-tree extensions and bibliographic optimality comparisons were not fully audited.

score_reasons.novelty: Height itself encodes frequency and reseeding limits the persistence of exceptional heights.
score_reasons.depth: The joint trajectory filtration is needed because repeated searches share dependent heights.
score_reasons.exposition: The paper carefully distinguishes confidence regimes and restricted dynamic benchmarks, but is long for the central mechanism.

checked: Checked Lemma 3.6's conditioning argument: truncated nondecreasing trajectories reveal only the first level crossing, and independent item trajectories remain independent.
Inspected the epoch schedule and the explicit stationary-source additive terms.
remaining: Full height-tail, horizontal scanning, reseeding and dynamic-comparison analyses have not been checked.

review.summary: Analyzes a counter-free self-adjusting skip list with height-dependent promotions. Gives entropy-sensitive concentration bounds, a matching need for an F log(1/δ) term without height resets, and an epochal-reseeding guarantee with additive n log(1/δ). Dynamic comparisons are restricted to weakly bounded skip lists and stationary or piecewise-stationary sources.
review.prior_frontier: Expected static optimality and frequency-adaptive randomized dictionaries were known; the advertised advance is stronger concentration and reduced explicit frequency state, not general dynamic optimality.

papers.title: Low-Temperature Sampling via Equilibrium Disagreements
papers.authors: Andreas Galanis, Daniel Stefankovic

review.title: Low-Temperature Sampling via Equilibrium Disagreements
review.authors: Andreas Galanis, Daniel Štefankovič
review.summary: Develops equilibrium-disagreement canonical paths yielding phase Glauber convergence in n^{3/2+o(1)} steps on random regular graphs throughout fixed-parameter low-temperature regimes for hard-core, Ising, and real-q>2 random-cluster models. An n^{2+o(1)} sampler combines phases without high-accuracy partition-function estimation.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier low-temperature algorithms required stronger interactions or large degree, leaving portions of the non-uniqueness regimes open.

score_reasons.significance: Broadly closes parameter gaps for three canonical models at every fixed degree.
score_reasons.novelty: Geometry of two equilibrium samples replaces typical-pinning spectral analysis; upper-tail phase estimators are a second useful idea.
score_reasons.depth: Canonical-path congestion, double-planted random graph analysis, annealing, and phase recombination.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear separation of phase mixing, full sampling, and threshold-dependent constants.

checked: Read the one-component variance reduction: skeleton orientations carry equal pair weights, small components concentrate phase magnetization, and hypercube tensorization charges exceptional orientations to an additive weak-Poincaré error.
Checked the telescoping moment formula for the annealed product estimator in Lemma 15 and the rejection filter’s clipped-estimator phase probabilities.
remaining: The 68-page low-temperature sampling result has checked a phase-component variance mechanism and estimator moment identity. Complete path congestion, model-specific planted transfer and annealing coupling remain unchecked; this is a large-proof exception for typical random-graph phase starts, not worst-case mixing.
The full component-path congestion bound, planted-model transfer and subcritical disagreement analysis for all three models, and annealing coupling require audit.

These are natural extremal/phase initializations on typical random regular graphs, not worst-case rapid mixing. Hard-core/Ising parameters are fixed strictly beyond threshold; constants need not remain uniform as the distance shrinks.

review.title: Efficient Algorithms for Approximately Counting Bipartite Independent Sets in Low Threshold Rank Graphs
review.authors: Charlie Anne Carlson, Alexandra Kolla
review.summary: Counting and sampling independent sets in d-regular bipartite graphs in exp(O(n/d)) polynomial-accuracy time. At d≥C log(n+1), time is 2^O(k)poly(n,B,1/ε) for fixed-cutoff positive threshold rank k; extends to hard-core fugacity λ≥fixed λ0>0.
review.prior_frontier: Removes the stated log³d factor from the prior regular-bipartite exponent and extends dense-graph FPRASs to logarithmic-degree low-threshold-rank graphs. Does not solve unrestricted #BIS.

score_reasons.significance: Substantially sharpens the degree-dependent exponent and yields an FPRAS in a meaningful spectral class beyond dense graphs.
score_reasons.novelty: Samples near the solid cube in a spectral subspace instead of enumerating an n^k grid; combines arbitrary-radius recovery with weighted container witnesses.
score_reasons.depth: The 18-page proof connects geometric covering, localization, weighted reconstruction and overlap-corrected sampling.
score_reasons.exposition: Parameters and degree/fugacity restrictions are explicit, with the core combinatorial estimates proved in the text.

checked: Traced spectral cut approximation: an eighth-scale contraction toward a target occupies 8^−k volume and rounding incurs O(distance²+1) errors, with a union bound over all Boolean targets.

Checked localization/recovery by removing neighborhoods of target vertices, bounding candidate additions through internal edges, and a vertex-cover branch recovering every nearby maximal independent set.
Verified weighted union rejection sampling and its geometric total membership-query count, including truncation and counting estimates.
Traced container refinement, degree accounting for |S|−|F|≤θt, and reconstruction via W=(W*\E)∪N(D). Checked weighted closure counts and the three-witness subset generating-function estimate.
Checked cutoff, error budgets and exp(O(k+ne^−ad)) accounting, then spectral trace bound and d≥C log n specializations.
remaining: Standard hit-and-run mixing/finite-precision sampling theorems are used as cited; their proofs and an implementation were not rechecked. The numerical-subspace perturbation is stated briefly with slack, rather than fully quantified in the manuscript.

review.summary: For fixed-round KACs with independent public ideal round permutations, a public random iterative key schedule from one independent ideal permutation reduces the master key to one block while retaining q=o(|G|^{t/(t+1)}) security with high probability over the schedule.
