score_reasons.depth: Dependent public-permutation schedules and algebraic coverability require distinct tools.
score_reasons.exposition: The two idealizations and restricted lower bound are clearly stated.

checked: Checked transcript-uniform concentration transfer: union bound over all transcripts permits adversary dependence on the fixed public schedule, and appending the master key preserves the likelihood-ratio argument.
remaining: Permutation-schedule coupling, Fourier transcript bounds, explicit algebraic constructions and attacks remain unaudited.

review.title: Santa Claus and Weighted Nash Social Welfare with Subadditive Valuations
review.authors: Yuhang Chen, Yuda Feng, Weijiang Hu, Shi Li, Ruilong Zhang
review.summary: Gives O(√n)-approximation for Santa Claus with subadditive demand-oracle valuations, and weighted Nash welfare approximation O(exp((ln n−H(w))/2)), with matching configuration-LP gaps for every weight vector even for XOS valuations.

score_reasons.significance: Tight LP-scale guarantees for two major allocation objectives, including weight-sensitive welfare.
score_reasons.novelty: Charges large-item matching damage to at most n selected items and combines conditional rounding with colored repetitions.

review.title: The CNF Encoding Complexity of Boolean Functions
review.authors: Andrew Krapivin, Benjamin Przybocki, Bernardo Subercaseaux
review.summary: Measures clauses in existential CNF encodings with unrestricted width. An advice RAM taking time t, with m advice bits and at most b accessed advice bits, has an encoding with soft-O(t+sqrt(mb)) clauses. Gives stronger encodings for k-CNF functions and sharp worst-case sparse-function bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the linear-in-advice term in the standard Robson conversion. Clause count permits very wide clauses and is not bounded-fan-in circuit size or literal count.

score_reasons.significance: A general encoding theorem compresses repeated access to nonuniform information and supplies nontrivial CNF encoding separations.
score_reasons.novelty: Hall expanders share sparse advice checks among all accesses, rather than checking each bit independently.
score_reasons.depth: Combines sparse truth-table encodings, mass production and log-cost nondeterministic RAM simulation.
score_reasons.exposition: The size measure, advice model and construction-time dependence are stated explicitly.

checked: Traced the main advice theorem and mass-production lemma: guess accessed addresses, check their values together, then use Robson for the advice-free computation.
Checked the sparse truth-table construction using one-hot rows, binary columns and wide clauses, with O(n+sqrt(nM)) clause accounting.
Checked the expander/Hall assignment of distinct positive inputs to active slots, the converse via equality checks, and Cauchy–Schwarz giving total soft-O(sqrt(2^n b)) clauses.
Checked repeated inputs do not require distinct slots and polynomial construction time permits enumeration of the advice truth table.
remaining: The main encoding theorem was checked using the stated standard Robson simulation and Teutsch expander theorems; those external constructions were not re-proved. Later derandomized data structures, sharper k-CNF constructions and matching sparse-function asymptotics were not fully audited.

remaining: 45-page solver chain not fully verified: spectral approximation and sampling-score implementation, recursive error/runtime recurrence, restart-to-high-probability conversion, and finite-precision appendices all remain. Binary entropy bounded by2min(sqrt(sigma),1/sqrt(sigma)); diagonal averaging and aligned relative-time integrals reduce packing to geometrically growing z_i=2q^i s_t(ceil x ell_i), whose K-sum is bounded. Feasible scales use m_i ell_i<=n_i; infeasible scales contribute O(n_i^{-eta/2}) and sum.
Checked leader-election success probability at a good monotone-code slot >=1/(2sqrt(e)); conditional repeated-block failure contracts.
Checked capped-arrival coupling for window progress: if cap exceeded, delta A_i>delta³N_i>=H_i>=D_cap; otherwise runs coincide.
remaining: Code constructions and their full monotonicity/smoothness proofs not audited; central lower-bound theorem is checked, but matching upper bound still depends on those constructions. Full unbounded-contention testing, potential and almost-sure stability proof remain unchecked.
scope_notes: Retain the complete Theorem 4.1 entropy/cohort lower-bound check and the inspected good-slot/capped-arrival lemmas. review.title: On the Composition Theorem for Approximate Degree, Randomized and Exact Quantum Query Complexity
review.authors: Samruddhi Pednekar, Supartha Podder

score_reasons.significance: Three major composition results: closes total approximate-degree multiplicativity, gives logarithmic-loss partial randomized composition, and refutes exact quantum multiplicativity.
score_reasons.novelty: A degree-filtered spectral operator and a trigonometric interpolation family provide the approximate-degree mechanism.
score_reasons.depth: The claimed operator bandwidth, squarefree extraction bounds and randomized forecasting reductions are demanding and decisive.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed proofs of the spectral interpolation and forecasting curvature machinery permit checking all three central arguments; a minor constant-display typo is harmless.

checked: Approximate-degree lower bound, complete central argument (pp16,22–24,41–49): checked the dual-witness degree filtration, banded multiplication operators, capped generator A, commutator norm at least d/3 and singular-vector probability interpolation. Verified derivative scale κ=2λ and total Fourier bandwidth of the lifted approximant.

Checked both analytic extraction lemmas: squarefree projection has norm at most 4^r via complexification and independent circle variables with only moments 0 and 1; homogeneous Taylor coefficients satisfy (eD/r)^r by Cauchy and rational-direction restriction. The truncated extracted polynomial has error at most 1/10+1/7<1/3 at the asserted product-degree threshold. Totalness is used to bound the inner lifted approximant everywhere.

Randomized result, complete new forecasting proof (pp25–34,54–59): checked the entropy-regularized Bellman identity including determined-query self loops; the softmax curvature identity, harmonic endpoint-deficit inequality, variance bound 36αG+384p, exceptional-stop error, support-size induction, recentering and noisy-query potential telescoping.

Checked initial/terminal potentials and α=2c/R(f), including the small-R case and finite-tree definition. Verified Lemma12 directly against Ben-David–Blais Theorem4.5 and Lemma3.6: balanced hard distributions give posterior squared bias≤480 E[Q]/R(f). Verified the cited noisyR composition theorem applies to partial functions and to the expected γ² cost model.

Exact quantum counterexample (pp34–37): checked telescoping correction of the bounded-error block algorithm, coefficient mass η≤2^(-4n)n3^n<1, coherent selector implementation costing O(md+n²√m), and exact amplitude-amplification polynomial 3a−4a³ at a=±1/2. Controlled calls are legitimate in the standard bit-query oracle model with a dummy address.

Verified Ambainis’s source uses precisely the stated four-bit h and has Q(h^k)=Ω((5/2)^k). Substitution n=4^k,m=64^k yields composed cost O(128^k), product lower bound Ω(160^k), hence ratio O((4/5)^k). The exact OR lower bound also follows from the degree-m all-zero amplitude polynomial.
remaining: This is an independent mathematical audit of the three main new proof routes, not formal verification. The introductory OR/promise-threshold warm-up proofs were not separately audited because the general approximate-degree result subsumes them.

Established external theorems were checked for statement and applicability, not reproved in full: approximate-degree robust-composition upper bound, minimax hard distribution, noisyR composition, and Ambainis’s iterated-function quantum lower bound.
PDF p29 has an apparent 3/8 versus 8/3 transposition in a recentering display; the following chosen constant uses the correct 8/3 upper bound, so this does not affect the result.

sources.detail: Independent central-proof audit, PDF pp22–37 and appendices pp41–49,54–59.

score_reasons.novelty: Median dimension splitting plus an extremal-label boosting game is a new and broadly interpretable mechanism.
score_reasons.depth: Careful conditional-potential recursion and two-parameter recurrence analysis.

checked: Checked ThinLabel completely: restricted contractions on at most half the dimensions, clipping relative to the median half-side, and transfer of an extremal coordinate error to opposite faces establish the thin labeling.

Checked Amplify’s one-sided conditional contract: recursive band inclusion under bounded shifts, light iterations preserving gap order, last heavy iteration supplying >3B/4 correctly classified mass, irreversible correct direct labels, and the product-budget decoding rule.

Checked the recurrence A(P,τ)≤1+A(P,τ/2)+129A(3P/4,τ), its binomial bound, and the dimension-halving product yielding O(log² d) exponent. Checked the contraction reduction for nonexpansive residual approximation.

Checked that the robust model permits a third response and does not assert distribution-free acceptance on every near-halfspace.

review.title: d-DNNF is Not Polynomially Closed Under Negation
review.authors: Marcelo Arenas, Oliver Broadrick, Vincent Liew, Guy Van Den Broeck
review.summary: There are n-variable functions with O(n)-size deterministic decomposable negation normal forms whose complements require 2^Ω(n)-size even nondeterministic DNNFs. Also gives a structured-case quasipolynomial separation and automata/grammar consequences.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves polynomial closure under negation for unrestricted d-DNNFs negatively with an exponential separation; the output lower bound holds for the larger DNNF class.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a fundamental closure question for a central knowledge-compilation representation with an exponential gap.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses three disjoint two-colour edge predicates for the small representation and independent-set mass to defeat every balanced rectangle of its complement.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines expander matchings, conditional independent-set probabilities and rectangle covers without relying only on worst-case counting.
score_reasons.exposition: The main separation is concise and the crucial conditional-probability argument is explicit.

checked: Fully traced the main exponential separation. The three cyclic colour-present/colour-absent predicates are disjoint and each has a linear OBDD on the union of two matchings.
Checked that an expander supplies linearly many separated crossing edges of one colour for every balanced partition.
Conditioning outside endpoints, each free edge has the three equally likely independent-set states. Rectangle closure forces one endpoint to be absent, giving a factor 2/3 per free edge.

Checked conditional probability at least 1/16 of a free edge despite prior exposed blocks: the exterior neighbour set has at most four vertices and the all-zero assignment is always feasible. Stochastic domination and Chernoff then give exponentially small rectangle mass.
Checked the conversion from exponentially many balanced rectangles to exponential DNNF size using the stated standard rectangle-cover theorem and the expander/edge-colouring construction.
remaining: The standard balanced-rectangle cover theorem and expander existence are used as cited rather than re-proved. The separate structured lower bound, automata/grammar corollaries and complexity-conditional appetizer were not fully audited.

review.title: The Computational Cost of Agreement in Correlated Sampling
review.authors: Rupkatha Hira, Moshe Noivirt, Jessica Sorrell, Eliad Tsfadia
review.summary: Efficient implicit correlated sampling of circuit distributions with marginal and additive agreement errors <=1/1000 would invert every polynomial-time regular function with constant probability; hence regular OWFs suffice for hardness. For Bernoulli circuits, near-linear expected Otilde(1/alpha) sampling is possible, while exponentially small agreement error and inverse-polynomial marginal error yield RP algorithms for SAT if runtime is polynomial in log1/alpha.
review.prior_frontier: Weakens rerandomizable public-key hardness to regular OWFs, not arbitrary OWFs; exponentially accurate hardness needs only NP!=RP. Claimed ETH implications remain explicitly conditional.

score_reasons.significance: Separates precision regimes and substantially weakens assumptions for computational correlated-sampling hardness.
score_reasons.novelty: Predicts preimage inner products via a shifted sampler agreement event and two-hash almost-injection.
score_reasons.depth: Combines distributional errors, output/domain ratio and Goldreich–Levin recovery.
score_reasons.exposition: The marginal and agreement errors are separately quantified.

checked: Checked shift averaging and singleton-target rescaling M/N in Lemma3.3, obtaining success >=3/4-2eta_F-(M/N)(alpha+2nu).
Checked two-hash collision bound: same fiber contributes1/64, other outputs1/32, so expected nonuniqueness<=3/64; m=n+5 keeps sampler error amplification constant.
remaining: Full inversion algorithm/regularity guessing, Goldreich–Levin applicability, Bernoulli expected-time construction and SAT reduction remain unverified.

score_reasons.significance: Unifies several hardness certificates and supplies multiclass and simultaneous-loss extensions.
score_reasons.novelty: Input-dependent stochastic channels replace reweighting, with the correct fidelity determined by convex conjugacy.
score_reasons.depth: The central duality is clean Fenchel theory; multiclass losses and simultaneous calibration require additional structure.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates a universal predictor from a genuinely universal channel and states finite-domain and regularity assumptions.

checked: Checked the distribution-weighted quotient space and conjugacy underlying Theorem 3.3, including zero-probability coordinates and attainment conditions.
Traced the simplex shift and ℓ1 penalty dual to indistinguishability constraints in the hardness-fidelity theorem.
Checked the constant-predictor specialization for best-response duality and the two calibration conditions that transfer simulated-label equality to real-label bounds.

score_reasons.significance: Removes the logarithmic discrepancy loss almost down to the necessary sparsity threshold and settles a central online special case.
score_reasons.novelty: A double-exponential compact density gives the curvature tail needed by a three-walk Metropolis coupling.
score_reasons.depth: The proof controls local Taylor remainders near the support boundary and sums nearly exponential coordinate costs.
score_reasons.exposition: The short proof cleanly separates the coupling, potential choice, tail estimate and adversary restriction.

checked: Traced the complete 10-page main argument: stationarity under time-varying fixed vectors, curvature criterion, coupled signing and prefix telescoping.
Checked the bump-potential derivatives, boundary-safe Taylor bound, curvature-tail inversion, truncated exponential-moment estimate and final sparsity substitution.
Independently verified the finite coupling lemma on all 27 vertices of its marginal parameter polytope using exact rational certificates; convex mixtures cover the full domain (audit1324.json).
remaining: The expected-operation statement uses continuous sampling and evaluation of the potential; finite-bit implementation is not established by this audit.

review.summary: For obliviously fixed d-sparse vectors in [−1,1]^n, achieves Oη(√d) discrepancy simultaneously over all prefixes, with failure at most CηT exp(−cηd/log^(2+η)(ed)). Thus the optimal scale holds down to d≈log T·(log log T)^(2+η), and resolves the online Spencer regime.
review.prior_frontier: The general online bound was O(√(d log T)). This result is independent of recent offline Komlós progress and does not cover an adversary adapting vectors to the output signs.

review.title: Efficient classical simulation of Fermi-Hubbard models with Kramers symmetry
review.authors: Chaithanya Rayudu, Jun Takahashi, Ojas Parekh, Andrew Zhao
review.summary: Gives a classical randomized relative approximation to Tr exp(−βH) in poly(N,r,β,Λ,1/ε) time for the attractive Kramers Hamiltonian class H=a†ha−ΣU_i n(v_i)n(Θv_i), with Θ²=−I, ΘhΘ⁻¹=h and U_i≥0.
review.prior_frontier: Sign-free determinant QMC for Kramers-symmetric models was known, but sign positivity alone did not prove polynomial convergence. The result covers attractive Hubbard models and a half-filled bipartite repulsive transformation.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial rigorous simulation guarantee for an important interacting-fermion family.
score_reasons.novelty: Quaternionic determinant weights admit a positive worm expansion and a log-concave generating polynomial.
score_reasons.depth: Trotterization, quaternionic Pfaffian identity, Hadamard-product sampling, and valid-sector control.
score_reasons.exposition: Formal theorem exposes interaction-norm dependence omitted from the informal abstract shorthand.

checked: Checked Lemma 7’s coefficient-isolation argument: the determinant expansion retains exactly the designated block rows by rank, giving det G[A,B]² times the squared monomial; positivity fixes the Pfaffian square-root sign and log-det concavity gives the generating-polynomial result.
Checked the free-energy-to-ground-energy error β≈N/ε.
remaining: Explicit large-proof exception: only the listed mathematical passages were checked. The complete central theorem and its remaining dependencies have not been verified; this record must not be presented as a correctness certification.
Full fermionic expansion, worm-transition spectral gap, probability of valid configurations, and cited Hadamard-product mixing theorem require audit.

Runtime is polynomial in the numerical norm Λ and inverse temperature, not merely their bit lengths. Applies to the specified attractive Kramers decomposition, not every sign-problem-free fermionic Hamiltonian.

review.recommendation: Candidate under the large-proof exception, with only the stated partial verification; evaluate merit separately from full correctness.

review.prior_frontier: Adds a constructive additive-d integrality guarantee to fractional sample-removal methods. Equality targets are distinct and weakly NP-hard even for a binary regressor with an intercept.

score_reasons.significance: Provides useful integral guarantees and exact algorithms for a concrete robustness diagnostic.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines fixed-estimate LP sparsification with monotonicity in each observation weight.
score_reasons.depth: The primary proof is a compact rank-one-update argument; geometric variants and exact-data certificates add specialist detail.
score_reasons.exposition: States the mass, general-position, nondegeneracy and inequality-versus-equality qualifications explicitly.

checked: Fully checked the main rounding theorem: maximize retained mass under fixed normal equations to obtain at most d fractional weights, retain a spanning integral core, then choose feasible endpoints using Sherman–Morrison monotonicity.
Checked compactness/attainment above mass d−1 and the strict additive-d bound.
Checked the Subset Sum equality-target reduction and the min-plus fixed-effects algorithm, including its positive-denominator qualification and doubling runtime.
remaining: The separate saddle-lifting geometry, finite non-range examples and empirical exact-arithmetic certificates were not fully reproduced. The main rounding theorem does not cover arbitrary singular designs or insufficient retained mass.

review.title: Nearly Optimal Submodular Sparsification, with and without Cardinality Constraints
review.authors: Zhengting Bao, Dongrun Cai, Xue Chen, Yuchen He, Chihao Zhang
review.summary: For sums of arbitrary nonnegative submodular functions, constructs component reweightings of size O(n² log n/epsilon²) preserving every subset query, without monotonicity or symmetry. Also claims O(nk log n/epsilon²) for |S|<=k, with matching Omega(nk) scale. Weights computed by nested submodular minimization then independent component sampling.
review.prior_frontier: Improves prior O(n³/epsilon²) general sparsifiers to near the Omega(n²) directed-cut lower bound. Cardinality-sensitive theorem is distinct and not covered by this audit.

score_reasons.significance: Near-optimal general submodular sparsification settles the stated conjecture up to logarithms.
score_reasons.novelty: Minimum-ratio ground-state prices and nonnegative multiscale chaining avoid the cubic sensitivity bottleneck.
score_reasons.depth: Combines submodular parametric decomposition, cross-marginal dominance and uniform concentration.
score_reasons.exposition: Self-contained deterministic-weight proof is accessible; many additional Gibbs/cardinality variants substantially extend length.

checked: Traced entire unrestricted Theorem4.1 chain. Endpoint normalization on n+2 elements preserves submodularity and embeds every query; block min-cut submodularity and residual inequality follow from feasible unions/intersections.

Checked greedy minimum-ratio blocks have strictly increasing slopes; resulting b lies in base polytope, largest minimizers are price prefixes, sum component shares<=n-1 and h_i(C)<=s_i max_C b. Recover recursion and largest-minimizer oracle implementation traced.

Checked marginal-dominance price monotonicity using union of two parametric minimizers. Cross-terminal submodularity gives total query influence<=2F(S), while subadditivity and low-price shares give residual_i<=theta p_i and sum p_i<=2n(n-1).

Checked positive chaining and complete query-independent dictionary: each increment nonnegative and telescoping, sum ell_j theta_{j-1}<=8F(S), dictionary size<=(4n)^ell. Self-contained mixed Bernstein lemma checked from exponential moment; Lambda=56epsilon^-2 log(32n/delta) yields <=11epsilon F/14 and union failure<delta/2. Zero components and zero queries handled; Chernoff gives sparse support.
remaining: Cardinality-restricted O(nk) construction and its auxiliary capped/low-collision lemmas, lower bounds and Gibbs alternative are not audited. Polynomial-time claim uses standard submodular minimization as a primitive; detailed best runtime of cited minimizer is not independently re-proved.

score_reasons.depth: The 96-page proof coordinates rewinding, recovery, returned quantum registers and computational binding.

checked: Checked the recovery-isometry identity and basis/logical-decoding compatibility.

score_reasons.novelty: Identity-prefix transcript information and completion-threshold coupling handle adaptivity without replacing an interaction by one advice string.

checked: Checked deterministic-prover reduction and measurable maximizing choice; conditional product states require the explicitly stated absence of shared initial setup.

Checked the length-respecting diagonal separation and unique-witness Hadamard-test verifier.

Checked the gap construction: sampler puncturing in operator norm, independent per-query completion thresholds, meta-verifier absorbing adaptively chosen descriptions, exchangeability at the middle hybrid, and second-moment/Borel–Cantelli fixing of one oracle/completion.
remaining: The oracle separation is explicitly length-respecting and uses a quantum oracle; it is not an unrelativized separation or the concurrent classical-oracle result.

score_reasons.significance: Links randomized and deterministic fine-grained circuit frontiers and gives unusually efficient problem-specific amplification.
score_reasons.novelty: Repeated compaction of failed subinstances plus downward self-reduction.
score_reasons.depth: Reversible routing, geometric failure queues, and iterative sorting amplification.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates zero error from bounded error and circuit nonuniformity from uniform algorithms.

checked: Checked the central OV amplification: n²/t² subinstances, halving queues for log t rounds, brute-force final n²/t³ residuals, fresh conditional randomness, and failure exp(−Ω(n^{2−3κ})). κ=1/4 makes a union bound over 2^{2nd} inputs valid for d=n^{o(1)}.
Checked dimension preservation d=ω(log n), n^{o(1)} under t=n^κ and that the routing overhead is absorbed for α<1.
remaining: The sorting bootstrap and bounded-error multiset checker, plus the precise reversible compaction dependency, require audit.

Provides a nonuniform circuit implication, not an explicit uniform deterministic OV algorithm. Does not apply the OV result to arbitrary two-sided-error circuits; the low-dimension hypothesis is essential.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a central constrained fair-division existence problem for goods, chores and mixed signs.
score_reasons.novelty: Price-prefix perturbation makes all welfare-maximizing witnesses interlace, allowing KKM witnesses to be consolidated.
score_reasons.depth: Combines weighted assignment duality, alternating recolouring, topological selection and complexity reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states the constrained efficiency notion and why mixed manna needs removal of both a good and a chore.

checked: Fully traced the interlacing lemma: item edges and paired price-sorted agent edges form alternating paths/even cycles; two-colouring preserves balance and total welfare while maximizing every prefix sum.
Checked that score maximality forces every prefix inequality to equality, hence the one-position interlacing inequalities for both signs.
Traced conversion to common interval prices, complementary-slackness residual-envy bounds, acyclic positive flows and consolidation at a source witness.
Checked the finite-allocation limit preserves exact fairness and fPO without relying on positivity of limiting weights.
remaining: This 66-page existence-and-complexity paper remains partially audited: dual regularization, KKM boundary coverage, PPAD membership/hardness and the fixed-agent exact algorithm require complete checking.

score_reasons.novelty: Uses truthful competitive top-set marginals plus jointly constrained reservations and compensation.
score_reasons.depth: Two laminar constraint families coordinate popularity-prefix caps and deficient-agent load rounding.
score_reasons.exposition: Distinguishes cardinal implementation from ordinal expected allocation and ex-post/ex-ante guarantees.

checked: Checked fractional-rule truthfulness: only own top-set bonus depends on own report; ex-ante envy difference equals [v_i(T_i)−v_i(T_j)]/(n−1).
Checked rounded-prefix summation by parts and reservation supports form two laminar families; dummy-prefix rounding bounds load by max1/k_i+sum p_i/k_i<=1.

papers.title: Draw, Then Draw: The Metric Distortion of Random-Size Stable Lotteries
papers.authors: Nisarg Shah

review.title: Draw, Then Draw: The Metric Distortion of Random-Size Stable Lotteries
review.authors: Nisarg Shah
review.summary: Introduces random-size stable lotteries, proves distortion at most 2.13609 by an exact interval/algebraic certificate and greater than 2.136 for every rule using a fixed draw distribution; gives a real-arithmetic polynomial-time 2.13609+epsilon approximation. The manuscript acknowledges a stronger concurrent 2.1248 upper bound for general randomized voting rules.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the earlier 2.5 benchmark with a new stable-lottery family and nearly pins down that family. It is not the best general bound among the work acknowledged in the submission: Cai–Hastings–Ramakrishnan–Wang–Ye achieve 2.1248. The approximately 2.1126 universal lower bound remains distinct from this paper’s 2.136 restricted-family bound.

score_reasons.significance: A substantial new mechanism family with a near-tight characterization; the acknowledged concurrent 2.1248 general upper bound limits its status as a best-possible general distortion advance.
score_reasons.novelty: Joint stability for a random number of draws and a rank-cut charging criterion.
score_reasons.depth: Analytic metric reduction plus exact continuous-domain certificate verification.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed certificate map and boundary conventions; main numeric claim depends on external executable evidence.

checked: Checked the rank-cut criterion: threshold tail integration and diameter≤2d(v,o), monotone rearrangement, and selecting a common minimum K_j after voter-dependent certificate choices give the distortion bound.
Read the exact draw probabilities, rational target constant, and certificate-to-lemma map including atoms and endpoint conventions.

Traced random-size stability existence: labeled-copy self-play gives F(P,P)=E[1/(D+1)]; convexity/continuity in P and linearity in the challenger allow minimax, including countably supported D by dominated convergence. Support candidates have equal comparison score by the self-play average.

Independently checked Lemmas 2–5: metric tails charge the lower cutoff, each fixed capped rank cut is active over thresholds of diameter at most 2d(v,o), rearrangement places remaining marked mass at the right end, and the common minimum K_j makes voter-dependent certificate choices legitimate. For approximate stability the complementary-candidate sum gives error delta*(1-p), and K_min<=K_0 yields the stated robustness term.

Audited the primary certificate implementation at github.com/nisarg89/metric-distortion commit 6a2507c66a62b8fa06371135058a9aba788c3753. Read the interval engine, polynomial/derivative primitives, full finite-family domain parameterizations, witness generation, rank-cut composition, endpoint checks, and robustness checker. Verified normalization H=(mu*x-Phi)/(1-mu), psi=(mu-phi)/(1-mu), exported lambda/tau division by 1-mu, and positive-denominator clearing on 0<p<1. Re-derived the small-p internal factor cancellation and large-p divided-difference identities used to evaluate stable polynomial residuals.

Checked coverage of the certificate domains: mass knots contain b and every root-interval endpoint; bottom/top parameterizations together cover a<=min(p,r), and internal caps cover p<=A<=r. Rank measures use F(z)=nu([0,z)), with an atom at b included exactly when a<=b<A; the nine composition branches cover r<A and r>=A, including saturation above h_j. Positive mixed-difference coefficients establish q-f<=0; shifted tail coefficients establish a+eta_j*(mu-phi(a))<=0 beyond h_j. p=0 and p=1 use separately specified endpoint values, not limits of singular expressions.

The review audit ran verify_v3.py --full successfully under the Python verification environment: 729671 finite-family boxes, 421652 additional rank-cut boxes, all exact algebraic compositions and 152 Bernstein robustness intervals passed (log audits/metric-certificate.log). I inspected that log and independently ran the lower-bound checker and all 12 repository tests successfully with the same environment. Acceptance uses rigorous Arb enclosures, exact rational inputs and symbolic identities; floating point is confined to subdivision heuristics/statistics.

Traced the new all-integer-draw lower bound: permutation averaging preserves convex stability, a strict challenger-score inequality at P_p forces every stable Q to have Q(H)>=p, and reducing rational z makes distortion strictly >267/125. Checked both (r,p,N) choices, d=1,2 exact gaps, and decreasing normalized d>=3 tail. Infinite-support D is covered by bounded termwise averaging. The lower construction can also be realized directly: candidate o-to-H and distinct H-to-H distances 1; first-type voters have costs 1/2 to o and H above o, 3/2 to H below o; second-type voters sit at o. This verifies the used 0/1-offset instance without relying on the full external offset characterization.

Checked the efficient approximation: remove unanimously dominated candidates so T<=2n*SC(o); use delta=epsilon/(32n), N=ceil(log(m)/(2delta^2)), learning rate 4delta. Hoeffding exponential-weights regret gives log(m)/(4delta*N)+delta/2<=delta, and convex averaging preserves score error. The fixed degree-33 primitive permits O(nm) per iteration, hence O(nm^2+n^3m log(m)/epsilon^2) in the explicitly stated real-arithmetic/exponential-evaluation model.
remaining: No mechanized proof of the full metric-to-cut reduction was constructed. Arb/python-flint and SymPy arithmetic implementations are trusted dependencies; the entire external general offset characterization and prior/concurrent papers were not independently re-proved. The computational guarantee is real-arithmetic, not an established bit-complexity bound.

review.title: New Results in Adaptively-Secure Broadcast Encryption and Succinct Computational Secret Sharing from Standard Lattices
review.authors: Rishab Goyal, Saikumar Yadugiri
review.summary: Constructs fully compact programmable pseudorandom set samplers from LWE, with poly(λ,log N) parameters; obtains succinct graph secret sharing and a standard-model adaptive-security compiler for flexible broadcast encryption. The final flexible-encryption instantiation assumes decomposed LWE.
review.prior_frontier: Removes the representation-size loss in these PPS applications and random-oracle dependence for the stated flexible-encryption instantiation. Key-generation/decryption still read the set description; public-parameter and robustness tradeoffs differ across applications.

score_reasons.significance: Improves compactness and adaptivity for useful cryptographic primitives under falsifiable lattice assumptions.
score_reasons.novelty: Garbles a small matrix digest rather than a large membership circuit and uses an equivocal PRF to explain an earlier ciphertext after the set is chosen.
score_reasons.depth: Combines homomorphic evaluation, reusable blind garbling, noise smudging and adaptive compilers.
score_reasons.exposition: Assumptions and size bounds are spelled out, although the abstract should be read with the stronger decomposed-LWE application qualification.

checked: Traced the PPS construction and decoding identity; checked noise cancellation and exclusion of rounding boundaries.
Checked set membership has O(log N) depth despite O(|S|log N) size, and that the garbled circuit depends on a compact digest, giving polylogarithmic parameter sizes.
Traced the first equivocal-PRF hybrids and the selective challenge-index versus adaptive challenge-set distinction.
Checked the final flexible-broadcast corollary uses decomposed LWE, while the PPS theorem uses the stated standard-LWE parameters.
remaining: The 72-page security development is only partly audited. Full garbling/equivocation hybrids, smudging parameter feasibility, payload hiding, adaptive compiler and robust/evolving secret-sharing reductions remain to be checked.

papers.title: Anchored Extra-Proximal Methods: Optimal Higher-Order Methods for Monotone Inclusion Problems
papers.authors: Ruichen Jiang, TaeHo Yoon

review.title: Anchored Extra-Proximal Methods: Optimal Higher-Order Methods for Monotone Inclusion Problems
review.authors: Ruichen Jiang, Tae Ho Yoon
review.summary: For monotone F with Lp-Lipschitz (p−1)st derivative and maximal monotone H, anchored extra-proximal methods attain tangent residual ε in soft-O((Lp R^p/ε)^(2/(3p−1))) pth-order oracle calls. Matching deterministic lower bounds allow dimension at least 2N+1; nonexpansive fixed-point complexity is the minimum of this rate and R/ε. Taylor-model inclusion solves are additional work, not bounded general arithmetic operations.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript contrasts prior ε^(−1/p) proximal-residual rates and restricted tensor lower bounds. It explicitly acknowledges concurrent optimal and logarithm-free methods; its particular contribution is a direct anchored framework, adaptive search and unrestricted deterministic lower bound. Prior primary papers not checked.

score_reasons.significance: An optimal oracle-complexity frontier for a broad monotone-inclusion class.
score_reasons.novelty: Direct anchored inexact proximal construction and resisting-oracle model, with concurrent optimal results acknowledged.
score_reasons.depth: Potential stability, large-step search and higher-derivative hiding are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear model and residual distinctions; many proofs are deferred.

checked: Read tangent-residual definition, potential and relative-error framework, Taylor remainder and maximal-monotone affine Newton subproblem.
Checked second-order rate algebra: weighted displacement stability and step lower bound give sum A_i²/a_i⁴ bounded, Hölder leads A_k=Ω(k^(5/2)) and residual O(k^(−5/2)).
Inspected lower-bound oracle quantifiers, n≥2N+1 and a smoothed shift whose derivatives vanish in unrevealed directions.
remaining: Full potential-decrease identity, bisection merit Lipschitz proof, general-p model solvability and resisting-oracle construction not yet audited.
Oracle complexity excludes arbitrary cost of solving each Taylor-model inclusion.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Rank Estimation in Turnstile Streams
papers.authors: Yang S. Hu, Cheng Jiang, Yinchen Liu, Huacheng Yu

review.title: Tight Bounds for Rank Estimation in Turnstile Streams
review.authors: Yang S. Hu, Cheng Jiang, Yinchen Liu, Huacheng Yu

score_reasons.significance: A complete bit-space characterization closes a longstanding gap for a standard sketching task.
score_reasons.novelty: A digitwise hard distribution and conditional-variance partition extract more information than earlier reductions.
score_reasons.depth: The linear-sketch argument must be transferred to general turnstile algorithms and optimized across parameter regimes.
score_reasons.exposition: The theorem clearly exposes the three competing space terms and query-success convention.

checked: Inspected history-independent cancellation, suffix independence and the conditional-variance-to-diagonal-information setup.
remaining: The full information lower bound, general-streaming transfer, and all-regime upper bounds remain unaudited.

review.summary: Claims tight, constant-factor bit-space complexity for rank estimation in turnstile streams across all accuracy/universe/frequency regimes. In the common polynomial-size regime the bound is Θ(min{ε^(−1)log^(5/2)U, ε^(−2)log²U}), with matching rank/select upper bounds and polylogarithmic operation times.
review.prior_frontier: The strongest preceding rank lower bound left a √log U gap from Dyadic CountSketch. The result also distinguishes sampling and exact-recovery regimes; success is for each fixed query, not simultaneously every query.

papers.title: Combinatorial Boolean matrix Multiplation in n^3/2^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})} Time
papers.authors: Piaoyang Cui, Yiming Liu, David P. Woodruff

review.title: Combinatorial Boolean matrix Multiplation in n^3/2^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})} Time
review.authors: Piaoyang Cui, Yiming Liu, David P. Woodruff
review.summary: Claims deterministic combinatorial BMM and triangle detection in n³/2^{Ω(√log n)} time via a 2^{O(d²)}-piece grid-regularity decomposition with a bounded fractional density-weighted volume.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the prior n³/2^{Ω((log n)^{1/7})} combinatorial bound, answering the explicit square-root-log saving question. It remains n^{3−o(1)}.

score_reasons.significance: A major quantitative advance for a fundamental combinatorial primitive.
score_reasons.novelty: Density-jump telescoping, L_d witness estimation, and a weighted budget prevent overlap from erasing savings.
score_reasons.depth: Nested regularity sifting with density-dependent depth and exact 2-path decomposition.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit machine model and potential accounting; the linked Lean claim needs separate verification.

checked: Traced the complete new argument: L_d norm estimation by exact outer averaging and extractor sampling, dyadic witness sifting, capped rectangle searches and support-preserving peeling, column-degree buckets, aligned cube search, unique routing of every integer 2-path, fractional-potential induction, jump-adaptive recursion count, and the triangle/BMM parameter choice.

Verified each of the four normal-branch potential charges against the residual concavity credit, the boosted density-versus-depth inequality, and the ceiling sparse batching factor. The recursion charges large density jumps by skipped depth rather than multiplying their full cost at every level.

Verified the extractor-to-sampler construction against GUV2009 Theorem1.5 and Vadhan2012 Corollary6.24/Definition3.29, including two-sided failure factor, domain-padding bias, truncation of output bits, exact rational bit lengths, and absorption of (log n)^{O(d)} into n^{1/8}(d/alpha)^{O(d)}.

Verified the regular-product and triangle-to-BMM interfaces in AFKLM arXiv:2311.09095v2 Theorem2.1 (PDFp7) and Lemma6.1 (PDFp29). The three-case query uses the integer-product identity and the quarter-power potential; it never computes the dense products explicitly.

Inspected the linked Lean repository trust boundary. The manuscript itself explicitly says cited samplers are hypotheses, matrices use noncomputable reals, costs use CostM rather than a formal Word-RAM, and ancillary applications are outside the formalization. The manual acceptance check does not rely on an unqualified formal-proof claim.
remaining: The linked Lean build was not independently compiled. External extractor/regular-product theorems were checked at their exact interfaces, not reproved from scratch.

Ancillary black-box applications listed in RemarkC.1 were not individually audited; the audited headline is combinatorial BMM/triangle detection in n^3/2^{Omega(sqrt(log n))}, not a constant-exponent subcubic algorithm.

sources.detail: Exact primary regular-product and BMM-reduction interfaces checked.
Theorem1.5, PDFp4, unrestricted error parameter extractor.
Read formalization trust boundary; not independently compiled.

papers.title: The Quartic Gap Between Quantum and Dequantized Algorithms for Linear Algebra Is Tight
papers.authors: Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Dylan Herman, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Guneykan Ozgul

review.title: The Quartic Gap Between Quantum and Dequantized Algorithms for Linear Algebra Is Tight
review.authors: Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Dylan Herman, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Guneykan Ozgul
review.summary: Dense linear systems with any prescribed constant condition bound κ0>1 require Ω(ρ⁴/log ρ) classical sampling/query accesses but Θ(ρ) coherent accesses to sample their solutions within sufficiently small constant TV error, where ρ=||A||F/||A||. Extends to several positive-definite and matrix-function tasks.
review.prior_frontier: Matches the quartic dequantized upper dependence for linear systems up to logarithms. Input-access data structures are given free; this is a query-model separation, not an end-to-end practical runtime claim.

score_reasons.significance: Closes the main worst-case exponent gap between quantum and dequantized linear-system sampling.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses a fixed subset of global Fourier coefficients and a bounded sine/cosine witness to defeat adaptive classical sampling.
score_reasons.depth: Connects transcript martingales, normalization concentration, well-conditioned block matrices and a matching quantum search reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Input/output access, fixed right-hand side, accuracy thresholds and condition-number dependence are unusually explicit.

checked: Fully traced the main linear-system separation. Fixed entry magnitudes make norm/sampling queries input-independent; each classical entry query reveals one sign, with coherent access likewise simulated in constant queries.
Verified characteristic-function moments, adaptive-transcript conditional independence, Azuma union bound over K coefficients, transfer inequality and expected-query truncation.

Checked the triangular system inverse, Frobenius norm, condition-number bound and solution norm concentration. The sine witness has constant bias while its normalization error is O(n^−1/2), giving Ω(n²/log n)=Ω(ρ⁴/log ρ).

Traced the coherent state-preparation combination and success probability Ω(1/n), then amplitude amplification. Checked the duplicated-Hadamard-row family and its marked-coordinate probability yielding the matching Ω(sqrt n) search bound.
Checked κ0 arbitrarily close to one is achieved by taking a small fixed coupling, with correspondingly small but constant permitted error.
remaining: The positive-definite, regression, matrix-function and principal-component extensions and streaming-memory appendix were not fully audited. Standard amplitude-amplification/search lower-bound results are used as cited; QRAM construction cost is excluded by the model.

papers.title: A Fast and Accurate Algorithm for the $p \to q$ Norm of Sparse Non-Negative Matrices
papers.authors: Marco Pirazzini, Daniel Spielman

review.title: A Fast and Accurate Algorithm for the $p \to q$ Norm of Sparse Non-Negative Matrices
review.authors: Marco Pirazzini, Daniel A. Spielman
review.area: Numerical linear algebra and convex optimization
review.summary: For a nonnegative matrix with s nonzeros and 1≤q≤p, a high-accuracy algorithm approximates the p→q norm within 1−ε in expected soft-O(s^(3/2) log(1/ε)) time using a power-cone IPM and Laplacian solvers. The nonnegative, nonhypercontractive regime is essential.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript cites soft-O(s/ε) low-accuracy algorithms and general dense cutting-plane high-accuracy methods; advantage in sparse high-accuracy regime, roughly ε<1/sqrt(s). References not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Substantial sparse high-accuracy norm computation improvement.
score_reasons.novelty: Unexpected scaled M-matrix structure in a power-cone Hessian.
score_reasons.depth: Nontrivial barrier geometry and approximate Woodbury/Newton stability.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit matrix formulas and initialization expose the main mechanism.

checked: Checked positive-coordinate dual-norm reformulation and affine generalized-power-cone slice.

Traced Theorem 10 local Schur complement algebra with r=γ²/(z^(2/q*) y^(2/p)): off-diagonal −4r/[pq*(1−r²)], diagonal remainder positive because 1/q−1/p≥0. Scaling by diag(z,y) therefore gives strict SDD; simplex constraints contribute rank two.
Checked zero rows/columns are removed, ensuring no isolated zero diagonal in the assembled M-matrix.
remaining: Complete approximate-solver error analysis, IPM complexity and cited power-cone self-concordance not audited.
Runtime is arithmetic-model/solver based; do not infer signed-matrix or p<q result.

papers.title: Finding Integer Roots of Polynomials in Nearly Optimal Time
papers.authors: Yansong Feng, Itamar Nir

review.title: Finding Integer Roots of Polynomials in Nearly Optimal Time
review.authors: Yansong Feng, Itamar Nir

score_reasons.significance: Improves a natural exact algebraic task and removes square-freeness, with a meaningful unconditional parameter range.
score_reasons.novelty: Top-coefficient truncation and a Mahler-measure bound keep the total candidate bit length small.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines root-exclusion tests, Graeffe squaring and size-sensitive exact multipoint evaluation.
score_reasons.exposition: The dependence on the disputed external runtime is unusually explicit, and the elementary fallback is fully specified.

checked: Traced the unconditional algorithm: truncation places every nontrivial integer root within distance2 of a truncated root; Pellet/Graeffe tests safely prune dyadic intervals.
Checked O(d) surviving centers per scale, O(db) tests, soft-O(d²b) test cost, and the O(b) total candidate-bit bound from Mahler measure.
Checked Lemma3.5's bit-length buckets, coefficient blocks, modular multipoint evaluation and recombination, yielding soft-O(nb+nS).
remaining: The soft-O(nb) theorem for unrestricted b remains conditional on the cited Pan runtime; this audit does not resolve the authors' concern about that external analysis.
The full perturbation argument for the conditional approximate-root route was not independently audited.

review.summary: Finds all distinct integer roots of an integer polynomial of degree n and b-bit coefficients in soft-O(nb), conditional on Pan's approximate-factorization runtime. A self-contained alternative takes soft-O(nb+min(n,b)^3b²), giving unconditional quasilinear time when b≤n^(1/4), without square-freeness.
review.prior_frontier: The preceding deterministic bound was soft-O(n^(3/2)b) for square-free polynomials. The authors explicitly flag that they could not verify parts of Pan's runtime analysis; the unconditional alternative is therefore a separate guarantee.

review.title: Generalized Sorting via Four-Cycles
review.authors: Soheil Behnezhad, Shane Ferrante
review.summary: Randomized polynomial-time generalized sorting uses O(n^(4/3) log^(4/3)n) allowed-edge comparisons, with failure at most 1/n, when the unknown acyclic orientation contains a Hamiltonian path.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the cited Õ(sqrt(mn)) and worst-case Õ(n^(3/2)) query bounds; prior literature not independently re-audited.

score_reasons.significance: Polynomial improvement for the general restricted-comparison sorting problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Four-cycle witnesses certify many opposite edges after one inverted edge is exposed.
score_reasons.depth: Combines local prediction, nonuniform degree buckets and witness-core peeling.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise promise and query accounting are presented with a useful regular-graph overview.

checked: Read the witness mechanism, peeling count Ω(p^4/n^4)<Tp, and outer balance n^3/M versus sqrt(Mn), giving M=n^(5/3)log^(2/3)n.
remaining: Audit local prediction consistency, bucketed Reduce proof and polynomial-time implementation of majority predictions.

papers.title: Algorithms for Min-Color Path with Bounded Color-Degree
papers.authors: Ajaykrishnan E S, Daniel Lokshtanov, Jie Xue, Saket Saurabh

review.title: Algorithms for Min-Color Path with Bounded Color-Degree
review.authors: Ajaykrishnan E S, Daniel Lokshtanov, Saket Saurabh, Jie Xue
review.summary: Min-Color Path with connected colour classes is polynomial on K3,h-minor-free graphs for fixed h and colour-degree; general graphs admit an n^O((Δ+1)^5/ε) PTAS. Bounded ply plus colour size gives exact polynomial time, with parameterized lower bounds separating stronger goals.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves the bounded-colour-degree planar obstacle-removal question; does not assert FPT in colour-degree or drop colour connectivity.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a recognized planar path problem with applications to obstacle removal and extends it beyond planar graphs.
score_reasons.novelty: Chromatic width and crossing number replace a false bounded-treewidth intuition for optimal path diagrams.
score_reasons.depth: Structural separators, LP dual sampling and representative partial-solution filtering drive several algorithms.
score_reasons.exposition: Parameters and hardness limitations are explicit, with a simple common algorithm separated from its lengthy structure proof.

checked: Checked Combine&Filter’s polynomial-size interface and why ordinary path-diagram treewidth can be unbounded at colour-degree one.
Traced Lemma5.1: path-cost intervals overlap on edges, every threshold gives a separator, and assigning each vertex to a heavy incident star bounds expected star-cover number by (2Δ+3) times the LP.
Checked the prefix/suffix colour count setup for the well-linked-diagram shortcut contradiction.
remaining: The 65-page structural proof is partially checked. The full shortcut construction, bounded-crossing decompositions, representative filtering induction and hardness gadgets remain unaudited.

papers.title: Simulated annealing and Weak Poincar\'e inequalities with inverse-polynomial accuracy for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model
papers.authors: Zhe Hou, Jingcheng Liu, Yixiao Yu

review.title: Simulated annealing and Weak Poincar\'e inequalities with inverse-polynomial accuracy for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model
review.authors: Zhe Hou, Jingcheng Liu, Yixiao Yu
review.summary: For zero-field Gaussian SK and every fixed β<1, obtains a weak Poincaré inequality with polynomial inverse-defect dependence and simulated annealing using Glauber dynamics from uniform spins with arbitrary inverse-polynomial TV error and disorder failure probability. Running-time exponent depends on β and requested error powers. This is not a worst-initial-state Glauber mixing theorem.
review.prior_frontier: Extends earlier β<1/2 TV/WPI and β<1 Wasserstein methods; manuscript acknowledges several concurrent β<1 results, including faster annealing and claimed stronger fixed-temperature mixing/counting. Its distinct contribution is cost-tolerant posterior-mean path control avoiding strong covariance estimates.

score_reasons.significance: Important high-temperature sampling guarantee, qualified by stronger concurrent results.
score_reasons.novelty: Gaussian path isoperimetry with integrated and terminal Lipschitz-failure costs.
score_reasons.depth: TAP residual, cavity/deletion stability and rare-path bounds are extensive.
score_reasons.exposition: Careful concurrency and metric distinctions; 89-page argument requires staged verification.

checked: Fully traced Lemmas 6.1–6.3 conditional on their cost and averaged-posterior-variance hypotheses. Grönwall/Cauchy–Schwarz controls endpoint shift from Cameron–Martin and integrated costs.

Checked Hellinger-affinity comparison: centered sums yield 2(a^(−2)−1)(VarP+VarQ), Jensen yields a^(−2)≤exp((KL(P,Q)+KL(Q,P))/2), and tilted symmetric KL equals inner product of field and mean differences.

Checked quantile argument removes at most v/8+v/4 mass from each tail, Gaussian isoperimetry supplies nearby paths, squared endpoint bound yields n^B v^(−Γ), and integrating quantile gaps gives polynomial defect dependence.
remaining: The substantial SK-specific derivation of the cost function, high-probability integrated/terminal cost bounds and posterior strong-field variance bound remains unchecked.
Annealing schedule/counting reduction and cited TAP/cavity/strong-field dependencies not fully audited.

papers.authors: Kevin Ren, Charles Fefferman, Jonathan Marty

review.title: Recovering Geodesic Distances from Noisy Observations
review.authors: Kevin Ren, Charles Fefferman, Jonathan Marty

score_reasons.significance: Learning the link while reconstructing geometry broadens the recovery model substantially.
score_reasons.novelty: Ruler construction and held-out cluster averaging separate unknown response calibration from distance recovery.
score_reasons.depth: The proof coordinates geometric visibility, concentration, clustering and shortest paths.
score_reasons.exposition: The formal theorem exposes independence, normalization and geometric constants that the broad abstract could otherwise obscure.

checked: Inspected the normalized identifiability assumptions and the Hilbert-space separation argument.
Checked the role of held-out anchors in preserving independence for noisy cluster averages.
remaining: The full ruler calibration, missing-data concentration and partial-observability guarantees are not audited.

review.summary: Recovers sampled geodesic distances under independent heterogeneous subgaussian noise with an unknown increasing bilipschitz link function. With diameter normalization and volume/visibility hypotheses, full-data error is O(ε log(1/ε)); extensions handle distance-dependent missingness and separate observer/observed sets.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier noisy-distance recovery assumed a known link or more restrictive noise distributions. The new quantitative observer-set guarantee complements stability results for boundary data.

papers.title: Iterative Rounding for Determinant Maximization and Real Stable Polynomials
papers.authors: Nikhil Bansal, Wenzheng Li, Mohit Singh, Yuze Xu

review.title: Iterative Rounding for Determinant Maximization and Real Stable Polynomials
review.authors: Nikhil Bansal, Wenzheng Li, Mohit Singh, Yuze Xu
review.summary: Deterministic polynomial-time e^(14d+ε)-approximation producing a matroid base for determinant maximization in dimension d and rank r≥d. Extends to degree-d homogeneous multiaffine real stable polynomials with a value oracle; coefficient-oracle access additionally requires a support-matroid oracle and yields a randomized guarantee.
review.prior_frontier: Closes the stated e^O(d) estimation versus d^O(d) constructive approximation gap for general matroids; cited prior bounds not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a major approximation gap for a broad matrix-design optimization problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Self-reducible relaxation and bounded entropy regularizer permit constructive rounding.
score_reasons.depth: Must control singular Hessians, proportional faces and finite precision while maintaining matroid feasibility.
score_reasons.exposition: The distinction between selected-base variables and auxiliary marginals is clearly emphasized.

checked: Inspected exact theorem and general-rank regularized objective; marginal a is deliberately not fixed when selected-base x reaches one.

Traced the central curvature and rounding argument on pp.11–19: the positive-eigenvalue trace bound, maximum-cut Laplacian subspace lemma, entropy reformulation, proportional exchange derivative, and contraction of fixed-x coordinates into a supervertex. Checked the dimension counts and strict positive curvature in both regularizer branches.
remaining: Large-proof exception for the 43-page argument: the continuous core was checked, but the finite polynomial-time implementation and its entropy/covariance oracles in Section4 and AppendixC remain unverified. Standard stable-polynomial and matroid-face interfaces are used as stated.

review.recommendation: Candidate under the explicit large-proof exception; retain the checked scope and remaining dependencies in any selection.

review.title: Sharp detection thresholds for random geometric graphs with polynomial average degrees
review.authors: Hang Du, Cheng Mao, Nike Sun, Yihong Wu, Jiaming Xu
review.summary: For hard-threshold spherical random geometric graphs with p→0 and np≥n^δ for fixed δ>0, KL divergence from G(n,p) vanishes when d≫(np log(1/p))³.
review.prior_frontier: Matches the conjectured signed-triangle threshold throughout polynomial average degree, removing the earlier extra d≥(1+ε)n condition. Does not cover bounded/subpolynomial average degree.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the sharp indistinguishability threshold across a substantial previously open sparse regime.
score_reasons.novelty: Couples posterior harmonic moments with truncated neighborhood divergence to close a self-bounding recurrence.
score_reasons.depth: Requires Fourier degree truncation, spherical harmonic contraction and a carefully weighted finite-degree cavity recursion.
score_reasons.exposition: The sharp parameter regime and dependence of fixed truncation orders on δ are clear.

checked: Traced the final KL closure: the degree-two contribution is ε_n/n, higher degrees gain powers of np, and Δ≤o(1/n)(1+Δ/p) closes because np grows polynomially.
Checked finiteness of the normalized posterior supremum before absorbing its recursion.
Verified exponent arithmetic in the bounded-degree recurrence, including the (np)^(t−M)+ weight, 3q−k≥s+2h and the resulting O(log^M n/(np)²) contraction.
Checked the high-degree escape estimate uses the selected fixed cutoff M and the polynomial-degree hypothesis.
remaining: The 44-page proof remains partially audited: the full cavity derivation, bad-denominator control, Fourier-tail identities and spherical-harmonic contraction/remainder estimates have not all been traced.

review.title: Improved Algorithms in the Random-Order Model: Knapsack, GAP, and Beyond
review.authors: Saksham Agrawal, Arindam Khan, Akash Pareek
review.summary: For known n and uniformly random order of an adversarially fixed instance, claims 0.2564-competitive integral knapsack/GAP against integral optimum. A deterministic remaining-capacity-scaled prefix-LP algorithm is 1/e-competitive for fractional GAP against fractional optimum, extended to resource-deletion/scaling packing assignment. No small-item assumption; integral and fractional benchmarks differ.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript reports earlier integral GAP (1−ln2)/2≈0.1534 and knapsack 0.1789, and optimal fractional 1/e threshold. Those prior bounds/hardness were not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Large ratio improvement for arbitrary-size random-order allocation and a clean fractional guarantee.
score_reasons.novelty: Integral multirule certificates and deterministic binwise remaining-capacity scaling.
score_reasons.depth: Integral numerical/analytic certification and action-compatible multi-resource extension are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Fractional proof is transparent; integral constant spans long appendices.

checked: Fully traced fractional GAP Theorem 4.1: fixed set-based LP tie-breaking, exact capacity update, setwise induction E[r_b|S]≥t/|S| and conditional current-item averaging. Restricting a global optimum to a random prefix gives E[OPT(prefix)]≥k OPT/n; summing yields t/n sum_(h=t)^(n−1)1/h.
Verified feasibility also for sizes exceeding capacity because recommended normalized consumption is ≤1. No independence between bins or residual capacity and recommendation is assumed.
Checked deletion-to-fractional-scaling Lemma D.1 via nested threshold resource sets and telescoping convex weights; it does not imply integral scaling.
Independently justified finite-n sample bound: harmonic trapezoid lower bound and −log y≥1−y imply ≥1/e for n≥9, with n=2..8 directly checked.
remaining: Integral 0.2564 guarantee, multirule finite/continuous certificates and integral GPAP lift not audited.
Full fractional generalization appendix and matching 1/e impossibility dependency not fully traced.

review.title: Private Online Release of Adaptive Linear Queries
review.authors: Haohua Tang, Aleksandar Nikolov

score_reasons.significance: Closes a meaningful adaptivity gap in private linear-query release.
score_reasons.novelty: Layered Euclidean database construction lets factorization handle adaptively changing query directions.
score_reasons.depth: Orthogonal direction transfers combine geometric progress with weighted target-charging privacy analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: The formal theorem records the privacy, confidence and factorization-competitiveness dependencies.

checked: Checked the orthogonality of directions kicked out of each layer and the resulting pairwise squared-privacy-cost bound.
Traced the potential contraction by a factor9 between layers and why the final untested layer stays empty.
remaining: The weighted target-charging theorem, growing-point factorization interface, and complete lower-bound argument remain unaudited.

review.summary: Gives private online release of adaptively selected linear queries with error polylogarithmically competitive with offline γ₂-factorization bounds, and proves that a polylogarithmic loss is sometimes necessary. The comparison with arbitrary offline private mechanisms requires sufficiently large datasets.
review.prior_frontier: The preceding online factorization mechanism handled obliviously chosen queries and could fail under adaptive selection. This addresses the adaptive-versus-oblivious separation question up to polylogarithmic factors in the stated large-data regime.

papers.title: An $\Omega(\sqrt{N})$ Lower Bound for Path Following Interior Point Methods on Single-Source Shortest Paths
papers.authors: Deeksha Adil, Daniel Dadush, Rasmus Kyng, Adrian Vladu

review.title: An $\Omega(\sqrt{N})$ Lower Bound for Path Following Interior Point Methods on Single-Source Shortest Paths
review.authors: Deeksha Adil, Daniel Dadush, Rasmus Kyng, Adrian Vladu
review.summary: Sparse unit-demand single-source shortest-path flow LPs require Ω(sqrt(n)) jumps for every path-following sequence with max_e s_e f_e≤gap/(αn), fixed α>0, where each jump changes either all slacks or all primal coordinates by at most factor two. Applies to this explicit iterate model, not all LP algorithms or unrestricted IPMs.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier redundant Klee–Minty lower bounds did not simultaneously give sparse full-rank graph instances and this barrier-switching primal-or-dual jump model. Prior historical comparisons not re-audited.

score_reasons.significance: Explains a square-root iteration barrier on natural sparse shortest-path instances.
score_reasons.novelty: A rank of flow-reversal gadgets bounds progress even with nonmonotone gaps and changing barriers.
score_reasons.depth: The new proof is elementary but carefully handles two alternative jump restrictions and all unit demands.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions separate centrality, step-size restrictions and iteration counts from linear-system solves.

checked: Checked complete Theorems 3.1 and 4.1: conservation gives gadget net flow 2k−i−FS, and unit-demand variant 2k²−ki−FS,out; gap decomposition and centrality bound Dmax<4kFS/η or γFS,in.

Checked a rank drop >2h forces middle-gadget forward slack from >1 to <1/2 and backward flow from ≥h to <h/3 (scaled by k for unit demands), contradicting both allowed jump types. Telescoping does not require monotonicity.
Checked counts n=bk²+1, m=(2b−2)k²+k, η=αn≥6k²≥2(2k²+k); h=ceil(12bk²/η) gives L≥η/(48bk)≥αk/48. Endpoint gap bounds yield FS,out>2k² and <k².
Weighted centrality implies their η condition by summing products and bounding the largest weight; standard rank/leverage identities support the stated Lewis-weight specialization.
remaining: This is not a formal verification. Claims about a particular implementation require verifying that its consecutive iterates obey the stated jump restriction; the paper itself does not lower-bound linear-system solves.

review.title: Metric TSP in Sublinear Time: Breaking Two Approximation
review.authors: Amir Azarmehr, Soheil Behnezhad
review.summary: For some absolute ε,δ,γ>0, estimates metric TSP value within factor 2−δ using O(n^(2−ε)) distance queries and O(n^(2−γ)) time, with probability at least 2/3. No MST is supplied.
review.prior_frontier: Breaks the longstanding factor-two barrier for general metric TSP value estimation; prior strict improvements required special metrics or a supplied MST. It does not output a tour in subquadratic queries.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a longstanding sublinear approximation question for unrestricted metrics.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses the cut-LP dual and dominated Steiner trees, recovering enough of an unknown MST’s shortening structure through a sampled core.
score_reasons.depth: Requires local/global dual solutions, fragment access and nontrivial subquadratic implementations.
score_reasons.exposition: The distinction between estimating value and constructing a tour, and between supplied and unknown MSTs, is clear.

checked: Checked the cut-LP relationship and dominated-tree dual representation via uncrossing.
Fully traced the MST-shortening lemma: overlap edges in the dual tree weigh at most M−K; zeroing them gives a dominated shortening of weight at least M−2(M−K).
Checked the subset version of the shortening bound and read the constructive dual-load-to-core conversion used for subquadratic time.
remaining: The 48-page algorithm is only partially audited. Core selection/refinement, cell construction, global feasible dual and approximation accounting, estimator variance and all subquadratic query/time exponents remain to be checked.

review.title: Dynamic Steiner Tree under Edge Updates
review.authors: Jeff Giliberti, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Mohammad Mahdavi, Xinchen Yang
review.summary: Deterministic fully dynamic Oζ(1)-approximate Steiner tree for a fixed terminal set in connected undirected graphs with positive polynomial-range weights, soft-O(n^(1/2+ζ)) amortized updates, O(1) cost estimates and soft-O(n^(1+ζ)) explicit reporting, for fixed 0<ζ<1/2. Also a simpler randomized incremental tradeoff.
review.prior_frontier: Manuscript identifies absence of prior constant-approximation sublinear-in-n edge-update algorithms; terminal-update algorithms on a fixed metric do not solve this model. Core dynamic spanner/sparsifier primitives are cited, not independently checked here.

score_reasons.significance: Breaks sublinear edge-update barrier independent of terminal count.
score_reasons.novelty: Frozen owner-tree expansion, zero-cost hub repairs and constant-boundary top-tree selection localize metric disruption.
score_reasons.depth: Nontrivial approximation decomposition and integration of dynamic distance primitives.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise separation of cost estimation and explicit tree reporting.

checked: Traced Lemmas4.5–4.10 approximation chain. Open tour of an old-edge optimal component costs 2w(K)−dK(x,r); frozen owner distance≤σdK(x,r) pays for attachment and yields 2σw(K).

Checked replacing metric MST edges through coherent owner-tree routes and deleted-edge hub bypasses, conditional on MST augmentation/expansion lemmas; selected forest cost≤2σOPT. Each selected component has a terminal, giving OPT(Q)≤w(F)+OPT, and spanner/sparsifier MST reconnection yields factor 2σ+2σρη(1+2σ).
Checked rounding for weights≥1 and phase cost n^(1+ν)/B+B n^η; balancing B=n^((1+ν−η)/2) gives stated exponent for ν=η=ζ.
remaining: Top-tree22-state recurrence, coherent expansion/MST augmentation lemmas and HLS/CP primary dynamic primitives remain unchecked.
Full adaptive-update implementation and incremental theorem not audited.

review.title: Homomorphism in Expectation
review.authors: Zeyu Liu, Xianhui Lu, Ruida Wang, Xinxuan Zhang

score_reasons.significance: The assumption reduction is interesting for approximate arithmetic, but the range-relative error is a substantial restriction.
score_reasons.novelty: Aggregating binomial routing and probability-digit counts compresses the exponentially unfolded sampling process.
score_reasons.depth: The implementation must preserve occurrence independence and control finite-precision weights and sampling errors.
score_reasons.exposition: The ideal and finite models are separated, although the headline needs the range qualification.

checked: Traced the ideal signed-stream induction, including independent repeated occurrences when both children are the same node.
Checked request aggregation, endpoint probability encoding, depth-dependent input-rounding error and Hoeffding averaging.
remaining: The finite-precision binomial sampler, full rounded-weight analysis and complete bit-complexity/compactness guarantees are not audited.

review.summary: From additive encryption over Z₂, evaluates polynomial-depth real arithmetic circuits with additive error ε times a public circuit-range bound. Signed Bernoulli encodings turn multiplication into XOR, and aggregated request counts avoid exponential circuit unfolding. The guarantee is range-relative, not general exact Boolean FHE.
review.prior_frontier: Direct stochastic bitstream evaluation incurs exponential depth overhead. The work claims compact approximate outputs and polynomial evaluation by counting repeated sampling requests, with precision depending on the public range rather than the actual possibly small output.

review.title: Entanglement in random graph states
review.authors: Xiaonan Chen, Asaf Ferber, Kenneth Goodenough, Marcelo Sales
review.summary: For fixed p∈(0,1), random graph local minimum degree is (min{p,2p(1−p),θ0}+o(1))n, with θ0≈0.1893; maximum independent set over the local-complementation orbit is Θ(sqrt(n)). Also improves the universal local-degree upper bound to 0.3413n+o(n).
review.prior_frontier: Extends uniform-p random-graph results to all fixed p and improves the quoted 3n/8 universal bound. Historical dependencies not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Determines two entanglement-related random-graph parameters across the full fixed-density range.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines parity-neighborhood second moments, binary coding bounds and local-complementation nullity methods.
score_reasons.depth: Dependence across overlapping parity sets and diagonal perturbations requires substantial probabilistic work.
score_reasons.exposition: States dense and sparse regimes separately and gives exact graph-state interpretations.

checked: Read parameter definitions, θ(p) branches and conclusion of the second-moment argument. Verified the two-vertex upper bound from Bin(n−2,2p(1−p)).
remaining: Full overlap covariance estimates, coding-theoretic constant and random matrix nullity/LC independence arguments remain unchecked.

papers.title: One-Shot any Code
papers.authors: Andrew C Yuan

review.title: One-Shot any Code
review.authors: Andrew C. Yuan
review.summary: Claims a bounded-degree CSS code transformation preserving k with stretched-exponential single-shot suppression in an overhead parameter, and a single-shot-to-self-correction implication. Formal noise-transfer theorem assumes a locally trivial seed; formal parallel time is O(log m)+τ_seed.
review.prior_frontier: Extends recursive self-correcting-code methods toward active correction with noisy measurements, but the unrestricted headline and seed-independent efficient decoder require clarification.

score_reasons.significance: A general single-shot transformation would be substantial, but the formal scope is narrower than the abstract.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines recursive cleaning, local measurement repair and joint physical/measurement-noise transfer.
score_reasons.depth: The central challenge is maintaining stochastic sparsity across levels and time while controlling repair-induced errors.
score_reasons.exposition: Definitions are detailed, but headline claims omit seed conditions and the proof sometimes delegates multi-time extensions to similarity.

checked: Checked the positive-Fourier-coefficient coset-weight inequality and its implication that Gibbs-distributed valid syndromes are local stochastic.
Traced the constructed one-round correlated-noise experiment equating logical failure with p times the Gibbs mass of unstable syndromes; the dynamical self-correction implication is cited externally.
Read the active-history cover/noise-transfer proof, identifying where local triviality removes zero-syndrome local increments.
Checked the parallel local-repair contraction and the formal O(ℓ)+τ_seed runtime statement.
remaining: Full level-map/cleaning appendix and cluster witness estimates remain unaudited. Multi-time stochastic domination is only partly spelled out, and the cited instability-to-lifetime theorem was not independently checked.
Before selection, the authors must explain how arbitrary input seeds satisfy or are reduced to local triviality, and how the advertised O(log m) runtime removes or bounds τ_seed.
issues: The abstract says any CSS QLDPC input, but Remark39 requires local triviality and Theorem80 uses it essentially; Lemma95 only preserves this assumption. No general preprocessing reduction was found.

The abstract advertises O(log m) efficient local decoding, whereas Theorem101 proves O(log m)+τ_seed for a supplied seed decoder. This is an unresolved scope/efficiency gap, not a counterexample to the conditional theorem.

papers.authors: Joseph Carolan, Andrew Childs, Matthew Coudron, Amin Shiraz Gilani, David Miloschewsky, Supartha Podder

review.title: Algorithmic Wave-Particle Duality: Pathfinding in Welded Trees is Hard
review.authors: Joseph Carolan, Andrew M. Childs, Matthew Coudron, Amin Shiraz Gilani, David Miloschewsky, Supartha Podder
review.summary: For a distribution over single-cycle welded trees of height n, any unrestricted quantum adjacency/colored-neighbor query algorithm finding any entrance–exit path has success O(q/2^(n/3)+nq³/2^n); consequently soft-Theta(2^(n/3)) queries are needed and sufficient. Exit finding alone remains polynomial-query.
review.prior_frontier: Strengthens earlier genuine/rooted algorithm restrictions and combines preliminary works into a near-tight general lower bound. The output-path task is strictly stronger than outputting the exit label.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a longstanding limitation question for an exponential quantum walk speedup.
score_reasons.novelty: Compressed-permutation good spaces handle retaining and erasing structural records for unrestricted algorithms.
score_reasons.depth: Coefficient-space conditioning, operator leakage and single-cycle reduction are deep.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed49-page proof; abstract graph records and norm identifications require care.

checked: Traced coefficient decomposition Lemma4.4: recursively subtract conditional means across weld edges; independence conditioned on endpoints yields pairwise orthogonality preserved under fixed-root weights.

Traced Lemma4.5 injectivity projection: remove kernel components, bound within-component coincidences with Cauchy–Schwarz and cross-component coincidences with orthogonality, obtaining O((n+1)m³/N) loss and norm≤sqrt2 lift.

Inspected full central edge-query leakage Lemma4.6 conditional on reference-assignment and polar perturbation primitives: insertion/deletion J, normalized partial isometry, fixed-data split, separately bounded retained-vertex deletion and leaf deletion.
Checked final telescoping arithmetic: q sqrt(εl)+q sqrt(nq/N) norm leakage gives q²εl+nq³/N; choosing l=floor(2n/3) and verification loss q/Nl yields claimed threshold.
remaining: Exact-versus-ordinary compressed oracle bridge, reference-weight construction in Section3, polar perturbation lemma, label-query proof completion and single-cycle distribution reduction not fully audited.
Thus this is a substantive partial audit, not full clearance of the49-page theorem.
