review.title: Four Ways to Stream: Exponential Separations from Random Order and Quantum Memory
review.authors: Nadezhda Voronova

score_reasons.significance: A substantial comparison of four streaming models and a consumability conjecture.
score_reasons.novelty: Rebuilding consumable quantum phase states from randomly interleaved repeated data gives the new separation.
score_reasons.depth: Forest-information and conditioned streaming lower bounds supplement the constructive phase-state argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully distinguishes arbitrary order, data-first order, request semantics, and gaps measured against stream length.

checked: Traced the complete random-order quantum upper bound, pp20–22: phase errors average at most pi²/mu using negative correlation in sampling without replacement; requests depend only on the independent schedule, so correlated registers require only a union bound.
Checked the weak-composition factorial-moment bound, initial-bank failure, exhaustion union bound over 100m banks, and total error below 1/3 with O(logN logm) live memory.
Checked data-first upper bounds, including sampling a vertex set and the matching-pair avoidance product; reviewed admissible communication-cut requirements.
remaining: Large 51-page manuscript: the new forest-information lower bounds and Noisy Gap Cycle quantum lower-bound machinery have not received a complete independent proof audit. Selection, if made, uses the explicitly permitted large-proof exception.

review.summary: Separates random-order quantum streaming exponentially from both random-order classical and data-first quantum streaming, via repeated Hidden Matching. Establishes linear multiple-request quantum communication bounds and quantum random-order Noisy Gap Cycle lower bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Each resource separately gave exponential space savings; their joint advantage and the linear consumability bound were not known. Requests must be answered on arrival; the adversarial entry is data-first, not arbitrary order.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate; large-proof exception for the unaudited lower-bound branches.

papers.title: Enumerating Posterior-Supported Priors: First-Order Error of Finite-Integral Cross-Categorical Measurement Morphisms
papers.authors: Ning Ni, Yongxin Zhu

review.title: Enumerating Posterior-Supported Priors: First-Order Error of Finite-Integral Cross-Categorical Measurement Morphisms
review.authors: Anonymous Author(s)
review.summary: Proposes a quotient-partition error-accounting framework. The stated core Theorem 7 includes normalized counting of predicate-mismatch blocks; its three-channel closure explicitly excludes intra-block errors and several learning mechanisms. A foundational refinement implication is false as stated.
review.prior_frontier: The manuscript expressly reuses standard measure and categorical facts; its claimed increment is an error-reading construction rather than a new distributional distance or convergence theorem.

score_reasons.significance: The checked core identity is additivity on a finite partition, and a foundational general claim fails.
score_reasons.novelty: The accounting vocabulary is elaborate, but an independently useful algorithmic guarantee was not established in the inspected claims.
score_reasons.depth: Many interdependent definitions obscure which hypotheses carry the asserted conclusions.
score_reasons.exposition: Assumption 1 alternates between atomlessness and a strictly stronger refinement property; the error closure excludes a central error source by convention.

checked: Read the sole-assumption statement, exact core theorem and proof, and Appendix C.13 clarification. The finite counting identity in Eq(33) is valid but does not justify the refinement implication.
remaining: A corrected refinement hypothesis and re-established downstream conclusions are needed. The complete 159-page construction and experiments were not audited.
issues: PDF136 Eq(93) asserts atomlessness plus non-null binary children implies every infinite refinement branch has measure tending to zero. Counterexample: Lebesgue measure on [0,1], distinguished nested cells C_n=[0,1/2+2^(-n-1)] (C_0=[0,1]); split C_n into C_(n+1) and its positive-measure remainder, splitting every other cell in half. All finite partitions are genuine and the measure is atomless, but μ(C_n)→1/2. This refutes the displayed implication, not the entire experimental pipeline.
PDF41 Theorem7(c)/Proposition23c excludes intra-block micro-level error by convention; it must not be interpreted as proving such error absent.

review.authors: Vladimir Braverman, Kuan Cheng, Jiaqing Zhu

Real-arithmetic and finite-precision versions are separate.
review.prior_frontier: Previously optimal terminal dimension constructions were randomized; the paper derandomizes with fixed-ε polynomial preprocessing. Historical comparison not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Obtains optimal target dimension deterministically for terminal distance preservation.
score_reasons.novelty: Finite empirical averages and a Gaussian-to-sign pessimistic estimator replace a continuous convex-hull test.
score_reasons.depth: The quadratic-to-norm conversion, signing, query extension and finite precision require distinct arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: The tradeoff and computational models are explicit.

checked: Traced Lemma 3.2: E||Z_s||²=ν/s+(1−1/s)t² and the analogous quadratic identity; choosing s around t^−2 or S gives uniform additive norm error.
Checked zero-diagonal block quadratic signing, operator/Frobenius bounds 1/m, log-determinant mgf estimate, and cosh(a)≤exp(a²/2) under one-coordinate replacement.
Checked union-bound test count and target-dimension arithmetic; inspected the extra-coordinate query extension and final squared-distance error.
remaining: Efficient evaluation of conditional pessimistic estimators, full query convex-program implementation and the finite-precision/bit-complexity analysis remain unverified. This 34-page construction has multiple distinct algorithmic layers.

review.title: Inevitable Knowledge in Communication Complexity and the LOCAL Model
review.authors: Ofer Grossman, Tomer Grossman, Moni Naor, Jonathan Shulman
review.summary: Defines inevitability as extracting a search witness from any decision transcript with little extra communication/rounds. Proves entire set intersection is O(s log²(1+n/s))-inevitable for deciding |a∩b|≤s and a witness is O(sqrt(n) log n)-expected zero-error inevitable from an exact dot-product transcript. Also claims k-coloring is not o(n)-inevitable from k-colorability for every fixed k≥2, plus positive LOCAL examples.
review.prior_frontier: Introduces a unifying transcript-sensitive notion rather than ordinary search-to-decision reductions; contrasts witness hiding and relates to bounded-witness nondeterministic complexity. No claimed universal decision/search equivalence.

score_reasons.significance: Foundational distinction with substantive communication and LOCAL examples.
score_reasons.novelty: Rectangle characterization isolates what any transcript must reveal.
score_reasons.depth: Adaptive incompatibility sets and LOCAL indistinguishability constructions.
score_reasons.exposition: Quantifiers, determinism and zero-error randomness clearly distinguished.

checked: Fully checked rectangle characterization Lemma1.4 in both directions, including constructing a decision protocol with any chosen accepting rectangle as transcript11.

Fully checked central positive communication Theorems1.5/1.6. Candidate set contains all intersections; announced r-subset removes incompatible indices, while two failed-good-set bits force intersection upper bound r to decrease. Successful rounds halve |H|−s; failed rounds cost only2bits, yielding O(s log²(1+n/s)), not s times that.

Inspected Brooks-based LOCAL example; stronger linear-round coloring construction not audited.
remaining: MAIN-PROOF-CHECKED refers to the central positive communication theorems only. LOCAL linear lower bounds, positive LOCAL inevitability, privacy characterization and proof-system sections remain unchecked.

review.title: A Quantum Lower Bound for Triangle Finding
review.authors: Arjan Cornelissen, Amin Shiraz Gilani, Xingyu Zhou

score_reasons.significance: Breaks a longstanding linear lower-bound barrier on a central quantum graph problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines transfer comparisons with a new conditional-resampling error estimate.
score_reasons.depth: The distribution-preserving comparison and query-error norm are technically decisive.
score_reasons.exposition: A clear overview identifies the dependence obstacle and the source of the exponent.

checked: Checked the full central proof pp14–34. The comparison theorem correctly separates Hilbert-norm error (maximum over query indices) from infinity-norm exceptional error (sum over indices); no norm bound on the transfer map is assumed, and exact verification annihilates all negative-input states.

Checked conditional-resampling resolvent F=(I+H/R)^−1, norm and order bounds, commutator identity, and weighted energy bound R/4. Verified every allowed two-bit conditional support and the rank-one projection overlap p, giving the commutator/anticommutator estimates in Lemma4.3.

Checked common-block Lemmas4.4–4.5: spectral gap 1−pd, summed commutator square bound 2(1+p)(pd)², and separate handling of bad OUTSIDE assignments. Checked Lemma4.6 for moving a difference past F, including exceptional infinity norms and the pd≤2/5 absorption.

Checked stochastic domination of any downward-conditioned Bernoulli law, triangle-filling probability≥1−3Δp², exact normalization ratio r_T, and four-negative-input transfer f_singletons−2f_empty. Verified the local variance comparison incurs 1/p rather than 1/p².

Checked star averaging and triangle-sum multiplicities. The proof correctly uses an outside-star maximum-degree event for Lemma4.5 and a full-input degree event only for Lemma4.6. Their different measurability requirements are respected.

Checked one-query error in all cases: containing the queried edge, sharing exactly one endpoint, and disjoint. Verified the Jacobi commutator estimate, residual Δ²p/R² term, choice R=(Δp)^(2/3), and that m exceptional errors are absorbed under Δp≥C log(2m).

Checked complete-tripartite substitution M=n³, Δ=2n, p=1/(10√(2n)), giving query error O(n^−13/12), including padding arbitrary N with isolated vertices. Primary sources confirm the constant-factor unrestricted search-to-detection reduction and connected chromatic-number reduction used for the corollary.
remaining: No formal verification was performed. This audit checks the main lower-bound proof and the hypotheses/statements of the cited detection reductions, not the full proofs of those earlier reductions.

The ancillary sparse-graph matching-upper-bound discussion and the new upper-bound entry attributed to Kintali in the introduction were not audited; neither is used in the N^(13/12) lower-bound proof.

sources.detail: Independent full conditional-resampling and triangle-query audit, pp14–34.
Primary dependency checked: Corollary5.3, connected graph/chromatic-number reduction.
Primary dependency checked: Lemma23, constant-size connected unrestricted search-to-detection.

review.summary: Claims the first superlinear quantum adjacency-matrix query lower bound for triangle finding, Omega(N^(13/12)), with detection consequences for fixed connected nonbipartite graphs.
review.prior_frontier: The elementary Omega(N) search lower bound remained below the O(N^(5/4)) upper bound. Conditional resampling must handle dependence in the triangle-free input distribution.

papers.title: Optimal Robust Community Detection

review.title: Optimal Robust Community Detection
review.authors: Samuel B. Hopkins, Yiding Hua, Sidhanth Mohanty, Amit Rajaraman, David Steurer
review.summary: For fixed sparse two-community SBM parameters and ε>0, a nearly-linear-time estimator attains uncorrupted information-theoretic optimal correlation minus ε while tolerating ηn arbitrary edge changes, for a sufficiently small parameter-dependent η>0. Also proves spectral nonbacktracking initialization of belief propagation is asymptotically optimal.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier robust methods gave weak recovery or optimality only at high SNR; uncorrupted optimal estimators existed. These historical claims were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Achieves robustness and optimal accuracy throughout the detectable sparse SBM regime.
score_reasons.novelty: Constant-depth walk-score characterization links nonbacktracking eigenvectors to analyzable BP initialization.
score_reasons.depth: Requires spectral perturbation, adversarial preprocessing, SDP recovery and local broadcast-tree comparison.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly allows added and deleted edges and records parameter-dependent constants.

checked: Inspected exact expectation-over-SBM/worst-corruption guarantee; checked the walk-score telescoping reduction conditional on cited SM22 norm and increment bounds. Read BP stability/initialization roadmap.
remaining: Explicit large-proof exception: only the listed mathematical passages were checked. The complete central theorem and its remaining dependencies have not been verified; this record must not be presented as a correctness certification.
Audit SM22 dependencies, BP local-law analysis, Bethe-Hessian controls, robust SDP and nearly-linear implementation.

review.recommendation: Candidate under the large-proof exception, with only the stated partial verification; evaluate merit separately from full correctness.

papers.title: Sublinear Approximations for Spanning Tree Congestion

review.title: Sublinear Approximations for Spanning Tree Congestion
review.authors: Sunny Atalig, Marek Chrobak, Petr Kolman, Hans Raj Tiwary
review.summary: Randomized polynomial-time soft-O(n^(2/3)) approximation for spanning-tree congestion of simple unweighted connected graphs, via O(k² log^5 n) congestion when optimum is k; also claims (2−ε)-hardness.
review.prior_frontier: The first sublinear-in-n approximation is claimed; the comparison tree has congestion O(√mn), and prior hardness was 6/5. Historical priority and hardness dependency were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Crosses the sublinear approximation barrier for spanning-tree congestion.
score_reasons.novelty: A laminar isolating-cut hierarchy and potential-improving partition control every small cut before confluent routing.
score_reasons.depth: Combines cut uncrossing, quota bisection, branch loads, and expansion accounting across logarithmic depth.
score_reasons.exposition: The construction is modular and quantitatively explicit, though the contraction cut comparison merits explanation.

checked: Traced the main upper-bound proof. Minimum isolating sets can round any cut toward their retained hub name without increasing boundary by submodularity; this resolves the apparent branch-cut issue in (3.17).

Checked half-hub contraction and logarithmic depth, expansion edge/vertex loads, and the partition potential: a violated small cut yields a quota set with x_P(Z)>1.5 b(Z) and a strictly improving integer swap.

review.title: Near-Optimal Quantum Lower Bounds for Convex Optimization via Fourier Rank
review.authors: Brandon Augustino, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Enrico Fontana, Dylan Herman, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Guneykan Ozgul, Nadezhda Voronova

score_reasons.significance: Resolves multiple central quantum optimization lower-bound questions in their stated oracle models.
score_reasons.novelty: Fourier rank replaces polynomial degree on the orthogonal group.
score_reasons.depth: Continuous-register closure and geometric reductions carry the main technical burden.
score_reasons.exposition: The oracle and accuracy regimes are stated precisely, with a reusable abstract method.

checked: Checked complete strongest proof routes, Sections3–6 and AppendixA. Fourier-rank bookkeeping handles completed L² amplitude spaces, arbitrary separable workspace, measurable query-label fibers, controlled/inverse queries and L¹ convergence of outcome probabilities. A reflection fixing each rank-deficient frequency reverses determinant, so fewer than n/2 phase queries have exactly zero Haar-average advantage.

Checked exact membership rank growth via uniformly bounded Fejér approximants of qᵀQq threshold phases. The threshold/boundary exceptional sets are Haar-null for every nonzero q in dimension≥2. AppendixA correctly makes the approximants jointly measurable and uses Tonelli plus dominated convergence for continuous query registers; it does not pretend the analytic approximants are actual queries.

Verified the orthogonal-component eigenangle density formulas against Meckes–Meckes, arXiv:1210.2681 Proposition1, including normalization by π and the forced ±1 eigenvalues. Checked the endpoint Markov bound and two-phase-query simulation yielding the minimum-eigenvalue lower bound at Θ(n^−2) accuracy.

Checked random-objective determinant predictor: Rademacher fourth moment and Paley–Zygmund lower tail4/27; Haar-positive trace integral gives E[Z²]≤√2π/100<9/200. Recomputed the 223/400 threshold, 125-run median failure<1/1000 and strictly positive average advantage>1/2000.

Checked ellipsoid normalization, exact/approximate feasibility geometry, scale-dependent objective error, finite union of objective-dependent query grids, odd-dimensional padding, and T≥d/250≥n/500. Main membership model is exact binary membership; it is not a simulation by matrix-vector queries.

Checked complete strongly convex reduction: even hidden block d=2 floor(min(√κ,n)/200), Hessian eigenvalues in[1,κ], constant objective gap gives Euclidean inverse-application accuracy, two rank-one phases per gradient query, scalar clipping/square-root estimate, and small-q zero-query obstruction. Obtained explicit bound T≥min(√κ,n)/10^5.
remaining: No formal verification was performed. Section7’s older, weaker inverse-iteration proof is not audited; the independently checked Sections4–6 prove the stronger main claims without it.

The matrix and gradient lower bounds concern the stated ideal continuous phase/translation oracle (or finite labels with those exact phases). They do not automatically apply to every finite-precision matrix-vector-output encoding.

The known upper bounds and historical priority comparison are not independently reproved. Strong convexity uses a family with polynomially large initial objective gap; this is not a joint √κ log(1/ε) lower bound.

sources.detail: Independent strongest main-proof audit, pp14–36 and48–50.
Primary spectral dependency checked: Proposition1 exact even orthogonal-component determinantal kernels.

review.summary: Claims linear quantum membership-query lower bounds for high-accuracy convex optimization over ellipsoids, an n/2 continuous matrix phase-query determinant lower bound, and optimal-up-to-log strongly convex gradient-query bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Extends finite-field determinant lower bounds to real matrices and closes the high-accuracy membership optimization question. Accuracy and feasibility scales are essential: objective Theta(n^(-1/2)), approximate feasibility Theta(n^(-3/2)).

review.title: Deterministic Parameterized Inapproximability of the Shortest Vector and Minimum Distance Problems
review.authors: Shuichi Hirahara, Bingkai Lin, Yuwei Liu, Kazuki Ogitsuka

score_reasons.significance: Removes randomness from a longstanding parameterized lattice hardness question.
score_reasons.novelty: A finite-field nonsingular-solution lemma replaces randomized dense-object construction.
score_reasons.depth: Geometric point counting and explicit Reed–Solomon local density must work within FPT size.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear separation of classical NP-hardness and parameterized hardness; details the norm and threshold regimes.

checked: Traced Lemma 2.19: the rank-(n−1) Jacobian gives a unique smooth curve through the rational point; Frobenius preserves that component, so it descends; full-rank Jacobian prevents the last polynomial vanishing identically. Bezout bounds forbidden zeros by Δ deg f_n. Verified Q>9Δ^5 makes Δ²√Q<Q/3 and 5Δ^5<5Q/9, leaving >Q/9>Δ deg f_n rational points.

Checked Cafure–Matera Theorem 7.1 in the original PDF: the manuscript uses exactly its r=1 specialization and valid Q>4δ² hypothesis. Standard Jacobian/Frobenius descent/Bezout facts are accepted dependencies, not re-proved from foundations.

Traced every lattice gadget step, Theorems 3.2–3.5: selected coordinates equal the short CVP residual over the integers, third block certifies nonzero completeness, β and q eliminate all short soundness vectors. For u≠0, the collision-avoiding polynomial has a single vanishing Y factor at the seed; Vandermonde gives the remaining Jacobian block. Degree product (k−1)! depends only on the parameter, while deg g is linear in m. No witness search is required to construct the output gadget.

Independently reconstructed the Reed–Solomon lattice minimum-norm dependency: if ||v||_p^p<2k<q then ||v||_1<2k, sum v=0 over integers, positive/negative multisets each have size <k, and the moment equalities plus Newton identities in characteristic q force identical multisets, hence v=0.

Verified computable-real parameter rounding with positive rational error <1/2, k≥2, D^p<2k, and d^p+W+1<(γ^p/2+8)d^p≤(cd)^p, with γ′c<γ. Fixed γ,c exist for every γ′<2^(1/p), and all work has FPT size/time.

Traced code construction and reduction, Theorems 4.2–4.4: omitted characteristic-p moments follow by Frobenius; a Vandermonde kernel argument excludes weight ≤D; independent derivative columns exist by the root bound. The collision polynomial only needs to avoid selected coordinates for codes, since collisions elsewhere cannot increase support. The u=0 case separately supplies a nonzero vector. Repetition factor D+1 replaces integer scaling and gives soundness.

Verified all-field extension preserves minimum distance by expanding coefficients in a prime-field basis; tensor product distance multiplicativity and fixed-power amplification yield every constant factor.

Checked the original BCGR paper, Definitions 2.6/2.10 and Theorems 2.7/2.11: its CVP hardness premise includes every nonzero integer multiple of the target, exactly as this reduction needs; NCP is the stated fixed-field approximation problem.
remaining: Did not reconstruct the established W[1]-hardness reductions inside BBE+21/BCGR24 from Clique. Their exact quoted hypotheses were checked in the primary BCGR paper.

Did not re-prove standard algebraic-geometric Jacobian criterion, Frobenius descent, Bezout or the underlying Weil theorem; verified the crucial quantitative point-count statement in its primary source.
No claim of formal verification or independent novelty certification against all concurrent papers.

sources.detail: Primary CVP/NCP hypotheses and hardness statements, Sections 2.3–2.4; cached ext_bcgr.pdf.
Original Theorem 7.1 quantitative Lang–Weil bound, r=1 specialization; cached ext_cm.pdf.

review.summary: Deterministic FPT reductions establish W[1]-hardness of gamma-approximate SVP in every computable finite lp norm for gamma<2^(1/p), and of constant-factor MDP over every finite field.
review.prior_frontier: Finite-norm parameterized SVP hardness was randomized or conditional. Concurrent MDP hardness uses an exponentially growing threshold; this construction preserves a linear threshold before amplification.
review.recommendation: Strong shortlist candidate after central-proof audit; final selection pending global calibration.

review.title: Approximating \#BIS in $\exp(\widetilde O(n^{1/3}))$ Time
review.authors: Jingcheng Liu, Yitong Yin
review.summary: Randomized approximate counting and TV sampling for independent sets in arbitrary bipartite graphs in exp(O(n^(1/3)log^(4/3)n)) times polynomial accuracy overhead. Generalizes to efficiently evaluable positive log-supermodular Boolean weights with dependence on log-weight range.
review.prior_frontier: Prior general #BIS approximation cited O(2^(.2372n)); recent announced exact-CNF bounds are explicitly treated as unconfirmed background, not a dependency.

score_reasons.significance: A fixed-power subexponential bound for general #BIS would substantially change a central approximate-counting frontier.
score_reasons.novelty: Adaptive threshold smoothing loses only quadratic objective value while giving linear-rate aggregate Fourier-tail decay.
score_reasons.depth: Combines a variational relaxation, low-degree optimization and weighted self-reduction-tree sampling.
score_reasons.exposition: The full new route is explicit and independently checkable, including the exact energy identity, finite convex search, capped weighted-tree sampler, and finite-bit error budget.

checked: Complete central variational construction, PDF pp. 13–20: checked Gibbs entropy chain rule, one-bit rearrangement inequality, causal Boolean-guide telescoping deficit into rearrangement losses and Bernoulli KL, layer-cake extension to fractional guides, and exactness/concavity via the Lovasz extension of a normalized supermodular potential. Causality is preserved by every layer; the guide optimum is exactly log Z, not a perturb-and-MAP upper bound.

Complete finite optimization algorithm, pp. 20–25: verified marginal bound Lambda=2B, bin-score integrability and discretization loss, clipped-guide soundness of the concave penalized extension on all real coefficients, interaction-degree truncation and [-1,1] Walsh coefficient witness. Checked dimension P≤d(1+dm)^D, bounded sample gradients, projected stochastic ascent potential, independent validation, amplification, lower-estimate margin, and 1/8 aggregate additive-error budget. The algorithm computes its objectives from the weight evaluator and fresh product samples, without evaluating the existential exact guide or conditional probabilities.

Complete threshold-smoothing proof, pp. 27–30: checked shared sequential perturbations preserve the target leaf law, KL/chi-square upper bound gives w²c(1−c) entropy loss, and conditional Jensen supplies the potential bound. Independently traced the exact weighted Hoeffding-norm induction with rho=1−w/2: ||g_T||_rho²=p||g_1||_rho²+(1−p)||g_0||_rho²=E T². This aggregate identity yields degree-D tail ≤(1/2)rho^((D+1)/2); it does not claim false componentwise contraction. D=ceil(4kappa/w) ensures the estimator tail tolerance. Also checked the simpler ordinary-resampling baseline and the ancillary one-threshold smoothing-cost lower bound.

Complete counting/sampling conversion, pp. 40–42: checked weighted stationary leaf law, root stationary-mass bound and root-start L2/TV mixing calculation, capped repeated-chain leaf extraction, conditional endpoint law, fresh cached estimator seeds and exponentially small per-node failure probabilities. Verified weighted conductance applicability against Sinclair–Jerrum 1989 Lemmas 4.1–4.2 (original pp. 113–115): every use of leaf counts is a disjoint-subtree mass sum and therefore extends to positive weights. Checked residual self-reduction frequency estimation, adaptive majority branch choice, chain-rule product and relative-error conversion.

Complete bit implementation, pp. 39,43–45: checked dyadic bin scores rounded down preserve soundness; approximate potential increments need not be supermodular, but the explicit gradient error 2xi sqrt(P) contributes at most 4Pxi=gamma/16 to the ascent bound. Verified exact rational iterates and fixed grids, corrected validation margin, remaining loss below 1/8, bounded transition simulation from fair bits, polynomial-bit mass weights via rounded base-two exponents, and cumulative TV error. All iteration and random-bit budgets are predetermined, including failed estimates.

Checked final parameter balance dw²+log(d)log(d+B)/w, dyadic choice of w, and exact-enumeration fallback giving min{d,d^(1/3)log^(2/3)d log^(2/3)(d+B)}. Verified positive log-supermodular residual closure and #BIS marginal weight W(S)=2^{|R\N(S)|}, value-length B=n+1, exact counting identity, and TV-contracting completion of the sampled left side.
remaining: This is a mathematical audit, not a formal verification or execution of the full exponential-time implementation. Standard Lovasz-extension and elementary concentration facts were checked in the forms used; the whole literature and announced SAT algorithms were not audited. The latter are background comparisons, not dependencies.

The general theorem assumes positive rational log-supermodular weights with an exact evaluator and a supplied value-bit-length bound B. It is an approximation/sampling algorithm, not exact #BIS counting or an FPRAS; polynomial accuracy factors and weight-evaluation costs remain.

review.recommendation: Exceptional candidate: complete central new proof and finite-bit implementation checked; genuinely general fixed-power subexponential #BIS approximation.

sources.detail: Checked original Sinclair–Jerrum weighted-tree conductance dependency, printed pp. 113–115.

papers.title: Tight Bounds on the Menu-Size Complexity of Approximately Optimal Auctions with Two Items
papers.authors: Hau Chan, Mingyu Guo, Nguyen Thach

review.title: Tight Bounds on the Menu-Size Complexity of Approximately Optimal Auctions with Two Items
review.authors: Hau Chan, Mingyu Guo, Nguyen Thach

score_reasons.significance: Closes a large exponent gap on a basic auction representation question.
score_reasons.novelty: Atomic optimal-menu certificates combined with rigidity of nearly optimal allocation fields provide the proposed lower bound.
score_reasons.depth: The certificate, weak Calderon–Zygmund estimate and planar subdivision argument are decisive.
score_reasons.exposition: Good geometric explanation; exact distribution quantifiers are clearly separated from fixed-distribution bounds.

checked: Traced the upper bound, Lemmas3.1/3.2 and Theorem1.1: Minty grouping by v+g(v) yields at most ceil((R+1)/t)^2 supporting planes and utility error t²/2. Discounting needs the enlarged square [0,1/(1−δ)]²; subgradient comparisons give the stated pointwise revenue bound, including ties. Substitution δ=1/k, t=(1+k/(k−1))/k, and a 1/k² near-optimality allowance yields total loss <4/k≤ε.

Traced the finite positive-certificate identity (D.1) by collecting utility and allocation coefficients. Verified nonnegative mass normalization and complementary slackness for the proposed menu. Recomputed both four-edge outgoing moment identities and both incoming stencil identities (sum of coefficients, divergence=2, rotated moment) symbolically with SymPy; all match Equations17–18.

Traced D.2: positive first-coordinate displacements make the recurrence inverse nonnegative; r^-4 gives negative full-stencil value, so taking positive boundary inlets and inverse comparison produces grid weights between constants times h², inlets totaling Θ(1), and multipliers Θ(h). Checked the omitted-boundary comparison, O(h^-1) boundary count, and total-inlet lower bound.

Traced radial completion: I maps to Ir/r′, leaving weight I(r′−r)/r′; ratios telescope. Source and terminal locations, highest-price selection, and coincident-point merging preserve tightness and both balance equations. Three unit-source anchor chains supply uniform source/terminal penalties, while full-cell edges have normalized coefficients Ω(h).

Checked triangular-lattice geometry and positivity on the 5–15 degree sector, ownership of left vertices, exact Q−Q_h=h²/2 at vertices, existence of full cells away from O(h) boundary strips, and source/bundle crossings approaching the desired curves.

Traced D.3: the missing left-to-left slack is bounded by three retained constraints using B0=T+D0−R+. Neighboring planes almost agree at shared-side endpoints; their tangential gradient differences give three independent constraints whose kernel is scalar matrices. Integrating over triangles cancels h^-2 and yields the total-defect estimate.

Traced the weak rigidity argument D.4: recovered ∂1Φ1 from T11(∂1Φ1−∂2Φ2)+T12(∂2Φ1+∂1Φ2), checked Fourier multipliers and the full dyadic good/bad decomposition, kernel cancellation outside enlarged squares, L² convergence/Fatou for countable bad pieces, and the weak-(1,1) bound.

Traced the compactness/anchor argument: uniform convex utility convergence gives subgradient convergence at differentiability points and L¹ interpolation convergence; T(Hessian)=0 forces a constant scalar Hessian. Three noncollinear zero-utility sources fix the affine term; two distinct terminal coordinate sums and bundle allocations fix scalar=1. A compact cutoff plus weak rigidity yields derivative convergence in measure, avoiding an invalid mere-L¹-gradient inference.

Traced the menu-vertex lemma and counting: without a vertex within 100 triangle lengths, nearby chords are nearly parallel; their convex gradient jumps occupy one narrow cone, contradicting the determinant bound of a map within 0.1 of identity. Removing lower-dimensional-only entries preserves utility and allows revenue-increasing full-cell selections. Euler counts O(N) vertices, whose O(h) neighborhoods cannot cover fixed positive area if N<c h^-2. The compactness contradiction supplies uniform loss Ω(h), and h=2ε/c_loss yields Ω(ε^-2).

Checked the smoothing transfer via coupled values and discounted menus: constrained and unconstrained optimum revenues change by ≤2δ+d/δ, giving the same exponent for an ε-dependent family of smooth densities.
remaining: Did not audit AppendixE examples or its n-item constant (3n/ε)^n; the two-item upper/lower theorems and smooth-density corollary were the audited main claims.
Standard convex subgradient, separation, Fourier/Plancherel, Lebesgue differentiation, and Arzelà–Ascoli facts were used as established prerequisites, rather than re-proved from foundations.

Did not independently verify all historical priority comparisons. The lower-bound family varies with ε, is correlated, and its smooth densities need not have uniformly bounded height or derivatives; no stronger fixed-distribution/independent-value conclusion is warranted.

review.summary: Claims a tight Theta(epsilon^(-2)) worst-distribution menu size for additive-epsilon optimal revenue with one additive buyer and two bounded-value items, plus an n-item upper bound.
review.prior_frontier: General upper bound O(epsilon^(-4)) and a fixed independent-distribution lower bound Omega(epsilon^(-1/4)); the new matching lower bound permits epsilon-dependent correlated distributions.
review.recommendation: Strong shortlist candidate after central-proof audit; final selection pending global calibration.

Inspected evidence normalization and the exact election/signature/message assumptions.

papers.authors: Alex Conway, Laxman Dhulipala, Martin Farach-Colton, Yarin Shechter, Torsten Suel, Richard Wen

review.title: Sparse $\alpha$-Navigable Graphs in Euclidean Space via Steiner Points
review.authors: Alex Conway, Laxman Dhulipala, Martín Farach-Colton, Yarin Shechter, Torsten Suel, Richard Wen
review.summary: For α=1+1/d, n points in R^d of aspect ratio Δ admit a Steiner α-navigable graph with O(min(n²,n^(3/2)sqrt((1+logΔ)log n))) edges and no Steiner-to-Steiner edges. For any constant α>1, some Θ(log n)-dimensional constant-aspect sets still force Ω(n²) edges with arbitrary Steiner locations; finer lower bound Ω(n²log n/(d log d)) when α−1≥c log n/d. Routing to an input uses floor(logαΔ)+2 moves. General queries have local-minimum factor Cα=(α+1)/(α−1); bounded-budget search guarantees Cα+ζ, not exact local-minimum convergence.
review.prior_frontier: Existing no-Steiner navigable graphs can require quadratic density; fixed-α Steiner augmentation still cannot fix worst case, while dimension-dependent α enables sparse construction. This does not improve LSH nearest-neighbor query bounds.

score_reasons.significance: Meaningful geometric feasibility boundary for navigable graphs.
score_reasons.novelty: Annular random Steiner covers reused via landmarks; spherical-cap bound handles arbitrary adversarial Steiner locations.
score_reasons.depth: Clean but substantial probabilistic geometry and search analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit caveats on degree, fixed augmentation, near-neighbor approximation and exact greedy termination.

checked: Fully traced upper construction: constant-probability spherical cap annular cover, m=floor(sqrt(n/a)) landmarks for a=O((1+logΔ)log n), all-to-candidate edges plus patch edges. Expected patch count≤n²/m by nearest-landmark ranks, verified resampling yields n^(3/2)sqrt(a) and no Steiner-to-Steiner edges.

Fully traced warm-up and general lower bounds: two shells radii γ/2 and1, all covered targets lie in a cap with threshold sqrt(γ)/2; sqrt(γ)/4-net plus K=ceil(512log(2/γ)/γ) target union bound gives ≤K per edge. Constants128,4096, aspect≤4/γ and odd-n origin augmentation checked. Standard spherical tail follows independently from even moments, and net size from disjoint small balls.

Fully checked routing and general-query lemmas: no consecutive Steiner moves restores original separation; recurrence d_(i+1)−Cαr≤(d_i−Cαr)/α, budget and small-r split give Cα+ζ. Returning a Steiner local minimum’s best input neighbor must terminate immediately.
Read fixed-augmentation set-cover optimization and degree transfer; its cited fast set-cover and DiskANN primitives were not independently audited.
remaining: MAIN-PROOF-CHECKED covers sparsity upper/lower and routing/query guarantees. Optional fast fixed-augmentation degree optimization relies on cited set-cover/DiskANN algorithms not audited.
Abstract O(ceil(logαΔ)) routing shorthand needs additive constant when Δ=1; precise Lemma6.7 correctly gives +2.

score_reasons.significance: Gives an exact class equivalence for a natural intermediate randomness-access model.
score_reasons.novelty: Checkpoint histories yield a product conditioning event and recursive rejection sampling with rare-event cost cancellation.
score_reasons.depth: Must preserve visit counts and inherited constraints through nested replay, then bound average rather than worst conditional rejection time.
score_reasons.exposition: Formal execution, candidate and replay definitions make the delicate conditioning claim inspectable.

checked: Traced the main simulation proof. Checkpoint boundary histories allow splicing inside and outside random assignments, proving A_{j,D}=E_D×F_D and Pr(reach D)≤q_D.

Checked candidate canonical encoding, replay from the original entrance rather than resetting at D, inherited crossing checks, prescribed-bit test before completing the r-th visit, and rejection of auxiliary-check failures as parent failures.
Verified accepted candidate distribution: trial mass a_{D,Y}/Q_r, success q_D/Q_r, hence the desired next-outcome kernel; intervals strictly shrink.
Checked expected-cost cancellation Pr(reach D)/q_D≤1, recurrence A_r≤(T+1)N_rQ_r(A_{r−1}+H), O(k²b) stack space and time exponent; global Markov cutoff gives TV≤ε with O(log1/ε) extra bits.
remaining: No formal implementation or machine-checked verification; historical derandomization announcements are not used for the read-k=BPL theorem.

score_reasons.exposition: The bipartite mechanism is clearly isolated before the more technical generalization.

checked: Traced the uniform violating-mass lemma: at most (2n)^n block decompositions, each forbidden set of mass >3n ln n avoids the sample with probability <n^−3n.

Checked high/low split δ=ε√log n, reciprocal-potential recurrence and pass bound 96δ/ε²+2log n/δ.

score_reasons.novelty: Norm-based trace extraction and multiplicative lookup simulate arbitrary packed configurations without secret addition.

Checked the two cases of the packed bit-append formula and public-clock constant-width simulation.

Traced inverse refresh and multiplication algebra: fixed endpoints reconstruct offset correlations; the front/back tensor compression yields c-s0*s1, and the only target-dependent public coordinate is the cached first left coordinate. This is an algebraic check, not a full conditional-distribution certification.

Read/traced the bounded-exposure and adaptive hybrid structure: carry every idle register, retain physical identifiers across invocations, stop before exceeding H, charge H lambda + ceil(log Q), introduce challenge before producer observations and keep transparent output pairs outside storage hybrids.
remaining: Full exact conditional laws and random-tape reconstruction in Lemmas 4-9, the underlying LRS extractor bound, and all fixed-clock sampler/deletion details are not fully verified.
Lemma 12 physical lifetime implementation and complete simulator termination/online distribution proof need further audit.
PKE/LPN parameter corollaries and iO/LWE sampler-removal construction remain unchecked; neither hardware removal nor constant-noise-LPN PKE under mere polynomial hardness is inferred.

papers.title: Optimal Learning under Tsybakov Noise
papers.authors: Steve Hanneke, Hongao Wang, Mingyue Xu

review.title: Optimal Learning under Tsybakov Noise
review.authors: Steve Hanneke, Hongao Wang, Mingyue Xu

score_reasons.significance: The log-free ERM theorem would settle a central statistical learning-rate question.
score_reasons.novelty: Noise-region concentration removes a global logarithmic cost.
score_reasons.depth: The upper proof is compact; its localized empirical-process ingredient needs a corrected justification.
score_reasons.exposition: Several formal defects need correction, including an impossible unrestricted-parameter lower bound.

checked: Traced the noise stratification, excess-risk identity, geometric sums and excess-risk peeling in the upper-bound route.

Visually verified Theorem3 on PDF p10: its sample-size requirement is independent of a while the lower-bound threshold grows as a^(1/(2−alpha)). For fixed allowed n,d,alpha and sufficiently large a it exceeds one, which an excess risk cannot do.
Checked that the proposed distribution's nonzero mass a'(s/2)^(alpha/(1−alpha)) scales as a^(2/(2−alpha)); it exceeds one without an additional a-dependent sample-size condition.
remaining: The main ERM upper theorem may remain correct after repairing the localized concentration justification. No fatal desk-reject judgment on the whole result is inferred from these local issues.
issues: Theorem3 is false over the stated unrestricted parameter range; a cap or an a-dependent n condition is missing. This is a range error, not a refutation of the asymptotic fixed-parameter learning rate.

AppendixA p15 assigns envelope 1_Delta to centered functions (f−Ef)/2; these functions can be nonzero outside Delta. An uncentered-process argument may repair the concentration derivation, but the displayed justification is invalid.

Theorem 3 is false as written for arbitrary a≥1 at fixed n satisfying its a-independent threshold: its demanded excess risk can exceed 1. The construction q=a′(s/2)^(alpha/(1−alpha)) has q=C(alpha,k,d,n)*a^(2/(2−alpha)), so q≤1 requires an omitted a-dependent sample-size condition. A restricted regime or truncated lower bound could repair it; this does not refute the main ERM upper rate.

Definition 1 demands the noise inequality for all t>0. At t=1/2 its left side is 1, forcing a≥[alpha^alpha(1−alpha)^(1−alpha)]^(−1)>1. Thus TN_H(1,alpha) is empty under the literal definition, while the lower theorem claims a distribution exists. The construction only verifies 0<t<1/2; either that range or a larger a threshold must be stated.

The centered class (f−Ef)/2 is generally nonzero outside Delta, so 1_Delta is not its envelope. Applying the quoted empirical-process inequality to the uncentered localized class, which is supported in Delta, is a plausible local repair, but the proof and constants should be rewritten. No claim that this invalidates the main statistical upper rate.

review.summary: Claims that every ERM learner achieves the log-free optimal excess-risk rate under Tsybakov noise, with a sharp dependence on the noise exponent, and a matching lower bound.
review.prior_frontier: A logarithmic upper/lower gap persisted for general VC classes. The main upper-bound idea stratifies the instance space by noise before peeling hypotheses by excess risk.
review.recommendation: Hold: substantial result, but correct the lower-bound range and concentration-envelope argument before selection.

review.title: Almost Tight Hardness of Approximation for 0-Extension

score_reasons.novelty: Pruned expander towers preserve enough local forest structure to support earthmover fractional solutions.
score_reasons.depth: Combines uniform partitions after random construction with recursive representative charging.
score_reasons.exposition: The relaxation distinction is clear; the unconditional hardness headline depends on an external claimed UGC resolution not verified here.

checked: Read precise gap theorem and conditional MNRS08 transfer. Checked the representative separation estimate: surviving matching has >half good endpoints in the nontrivial case, enabling averaged distance and expansion charging.
remaining: Explicit large-proof exception: only the listed mathematical passages were checked. The complete central theorem and its remaining dependencies have not been verified; this record must not be presented as a correctness certification.

review.title: 3SUM Made Simpler (Without Matrix Multiplication), $k$-SUM Hypothesis Refuted for Odd $k$, and Real 3SUM/APSP Derandomized
review.authors: Timothy M. Chan, Reina Itakura, Zhiyuan Ma, Yuancheng Yu

score_reasons.significance: Extends and simplifies major fine-grained algorithmic breakthroughs and removes randomness for real inputs.
score_reasons.novelty: Selective subset/vector convolution supplies a different mechanism for odd-k SUM.
score_reasons.depth: The combinatorial transforms and deterministic halving reductions require careful exponent accounting.
score_reasons.exposition: A concise paper clearly distinguishes the independent integer route from the imported real-input route.

checked: Complete new integer 3SUM proof, PDF pp. 5–9: verified covering-product inclusion–exclusion and the precomputed size≤s / query-downset size≥s dynamic programs; checked that all intermediate integers have O(log N) bits for polynomially bounded inputs. Verified random-prime collision removal, conditional affine-hash independence after removing both bad buckets, no-carry disjointness, second-moment sum-of-squares certificate, good-prime probability, trial count, and one-sided false-negative amplification/capped expected-time conversion. Independently recomputed entropy exponents: preprocessing 1.964011076, N multiplier .898044999, and query multiplier .964370965, all strictly below the displayed rounded 1.965/.899/.965 bounds.

Complete odd-k extension, pp. 11–14: checked multiplicity-quotient transform state counting for coordinate multiplicities ≤r−1 (the case actually used), factorial rescaling of subset convolution, balanced-vector count, (r!)^(d/r) decompositions, rho=r²/(r!)^(1/r), collision bound, and exponent accounting. For s=(1−delta)(r−1)d/2, checked Hoeffding saving in preprocessing and injection of dominated high-weight vectors into subsets of t tokens. Choices delta=epsilon^.49 and r=epsilon^(−.48) give preprocessing saving greater than epsilon and query exponent O(1/log(1/epsilon)); grouping (2k+1)-SUM into n^k,n,n^k lists yields a positive 2^(−Theta(k)) saving for every fixed k. This result is randomized and restricted to polynomially bounded integers.

Complete deterministic real APSP reduction, pp. 14–17: checked reduction by repeated squaring/rectangular blocking, low-global-average-rank interval descent, two Fredman comparisons, unique dyadic left/right witnesses for inequalities, exact triangle counts, high-degree middle-vertex bound O~(d^(4+2delta)), low-degree enumeration, and total O(d^(1+delta)) rather than product-of-batches count. Checked tie handling can use equal-value compressed ranks and lexicographic perturbation; minimum-rank queries must be kept unchanged. The off-by-one details needing correction are recorded below.

Complete deterministic real 3SUM reduction, pp. 17–21: checked sorted-block monotone staircase gives O(n/d) relevant cells per query, with exterior predecessor/successor endpoints handled directly. Verified rank-squared potential sum lambda(lambda−1)(lambda−2)/12, average ≤lambda²/12, 1/2+1/sqrt(12)<.8 contraction, and small-interval binary searches. Checked expansion into powers 0,1,2, three Fredman inequalities, unique dyadic witnesses, middle-degree O~(d^(12+2delta)), O(d^delta) total batches, and the final n²/d^(1+delta) selected-entry budget.

Verified external Alman–Vassilevska Williams dependency directly in official arXiv:2610.06783v1, Corollary 31 and Table 2. Its deterministic integer-entry matrix primitive applies to the 0/1 adjacency matrices here despite original real inputs. For c=21,theta=.0145, independently calculated gamma=.008352022427..., q=.077646868298..., and maximum thinness .056853889885.... Checked final APSP savings exceed .00031359 and real 3SUM savings exceed .0002374 after the rounding correction below, so the claimed O(n^2.9997) and O(n^1.9998) bounds survive logarithmic factors.
remaining: The external 76-page selected-entry matrix multiplication proof is an imported theorem; verified its precise statement, numerical parameters, deterministic model, and applicability rather than re-auditing its entire proof. The independent integer algorithms do not use it.

No Lean certificate or implementation was executed. Informal potential Las Vegas improvement and unexpanded Exact Triangle extension are not included in this audit. Arithmetic/model claims are word-RAM for polynomial integers and exact real-comparison RAM for real inputs, not finite-bit real approximation.

Checked local correction, not a headline-theorem failure: Repairable exposition/range omissions: Lemma 3.2 counts [r]^d multiplicity vectors although arbitrary sets in [dr] could have multiplicity r. Restrict its collections and queries to multiplicities at most r−1, as in its sole application Theorem 3.3; the checked proof and headline theorem then apply.

Checked local correction, not a headline-theorem failure: PDF p. 16 Lemma 4.6 mixes rank conventions. With the one-based ranks actually counted by ≤, size([d])=r−1 and sum-rank=r(r−1)/2, giving average r/2 for r>1; rank-1 entries have empty improvement sets and should be retained. The displayed size=r and the assertion for r≥1 need correction. Stop interval descent before asking the counting routine about a child shorter than d^(1−delta), then brute-force its parent of length <2d^(1−delta); this constant-factor boundary repair also applies to Lemma 5.5.

Checked local correction, not a headline-theorem failure: PDF p. 20 Lemma 5.8 statement omits the square in the selected-entry budget n²/d^(1+delta); the proof on p. 21 and final Theorem 5.9 both use the correct squared budget. Other obvious transcription slips (A in place of B in Problem 4.2, q-prime-plus in place of q-prime-minus in the lower bracket of Problem 5.2, and a repeated minus-child symbol in Lemma 5.5) should be corrected.

Checked local correction, not a headline-theorem failure: PDF p. 21 numerical rounding: d=n^.0046983 makes inner exponent (12+2*.050534)*.0046983=.0568544477844, which slightly exceeds both the stated .056853 and exact Corollary 31 limit .056853889885.... Taking d=n^.0046981 repairs this and still yields a saving >.0002374, comfortably proving the displayed n^1.9998 bound. This is not a failure of the headline theorem.

sources.detail: Complete central new proof audit, PDF pp. 5–21; title/assumptions pp. 1–4; references pp. 21–24.
Verified precise deterministic selected-entry matrix theorem and Corollary 31 parameters; Table 2 checked.

review.summary: Gives a matrix-multiplication-free randomized truly subquadratic integer 3SUM algorithm, refutes the integer k-SUM hypothesis for every odd constant k, and derandomizes real 3SUM/APSP reductions to selected-entry matrix multiplication.
review.prior_frontier: Recent truly subquadratic 3SUM and subcubic APSP algorithms depended on selected-entry rectangular multiplication. The new integer route uses subset convolution; deterministic real results still depend on the imported multiplication theorem.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate: all central new proof routes checked, with explicit repairable local corrections and imported multiplication dependency.

Read linked Lean source for the appendix analytic step: q<1/sqrt(2) truncated radial kernels converge to adjacent correlation 2sqrt(2)/3; incident edge vectors have average correlation at least (1+3lambda)/4; concavity of acos bounds open vertices; bounded dependence, finite threshold grids and window/tail counts give an all-cuts layout.

Checked worst-case and average-case extractor reductions, the unambiguous peeling partition and residual acceptance error. Primary Li23 Theorem 7.13 and CL22 Theorem 1 have the needed entropy/error and explicitness.
An exact Fraction/Taylor computation in audits/1432-constant-check.json proves the coefficient exceeds 4.5624 using a rational sqrt(2) lower bound and pi>3.14159.

Reproduced linked formal source build at b7c27d13c0545dedd78ec2614ca6792df160e8ed: lake build --wfail succeeded (3317 jobs). Main.lean guards all six theorem axiom sets as exactly propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. remaining: No unresolved substantive gap found in the traced main bound. Linked Lean kernel build was reproduced, but separate external paranoid checker was not run. review.title: A Near-Optimal Generalized Sorting Algorithm
review.authors: Sanjeev Khanna, Aaron Putterman, Junkai Song

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a longstanding polynomial-versus-near-linear comparison gap.
score_reasons.novelty: Error isolation uses sampled bad edges and validation over all sample orderings.
score_reasons.depth: The symmetry bound and bounded-degree charging give a compact but nontrivial argument.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear proof and candid statement that computation, unlike comparisons, can be exponential.

checked: Traced the complete new proof pp7–14: coarse-predictor union bound, vertex splitting, flagging thresholds, and edge-removal accounting.

Checked the core exchangeability step: for each left vertex, the distinguished bad-edge endpoint must be the unique earliest neighboring sample among s+1 iid draws; its probability is at most1/(s+1), including repeated draws.

Verified training/validation separation, s! union bound, four contributions summing to1/4 expected residual error, log n iterations, f/2 fallback, rare-event contribution and total O(n log^4 n) queries.

review.prior_frontier: Extends experts memory tradeoffs to structured hypothesis classes and arbitrarily late horizon guarantees, including parities and other SQ-hard classes.

score_reasons.significance: Shows low Littlestone complexity alone does not ensure memory-efficient low regret, even for natural classes.
score_reasons.novelty: Block-noise distinguishing and a small-memory approximate mistake counter avoid the usual bounded-horizon limitation.
score_reasons.depth: Combines arbitrary-distribution SQ-to-extractor conversion, branching-program lower bounds and online-to-distinguishing reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Finite-horizon and uniform late-horizon statements are carefully separated.

checked: Checked SQ-to-extractor second-moment calculation for a near-orthogonal family and the d^−1/8 threshold.

Checked converting expected Bayes gain to a high-probability bound for any predictor using nonnegative conditional Bayes gain plus Azuma.
Checked block-rounded mistake counter uses O(log T_block) memory, error εT/40, and rare exceptional blocks, rather than an O(log T) full counter.
remaining: The central extractor-based branching-program likelihood-ratio lower bound, all parameter matching and late-horizon conclusion remain unchecked in the 39-page proof.

score_reasons.novelty: Bootstrap recoloring with smoothly capped hierarchical metrics avoids repeated constant-factor losses.
score_reasons.depth: Random lifts, rare exceptional-edge marking, local l1 embeddings and simultaneous concentration require careful interdependent parameters.
score_reasons.exposition: Long but explicit parameter and resampling arguments; distinction between relaxation gaps and hardness matters.

checked: Traced the Part II parameter regime L=2^{r+1}, n=Lambda^{10000L}, level lengths, LP cost <=3r, r<=log_2 log k and conversion L/(90r log r) into the stated gap.

Read the sampling concentration proof after projection to the fixed older target: permutation bounded differences, union over at most k^{N_i} maps and theta^2 Delta >=64 log k. Checked exceptional connected-subgraph counting, conditioned-resampling factor, small/large m split and inherited expected added LP cost.

Traced recoloring decoupling by averaged triangle inequalities, adjacent-level D/lambda factor, distant-level additive errors, special level-2 vertex charge, final bootstrap and base constant-map bound. Checked (D/lambda)^r=1+O(r^-2), accumulated O(r^-2)b error and zero-weight-terminal padding.

remaining: 35-page proof has not been fully verified: Part I and primary CGJ18 expander spectral, CMM10 local l1 embedding and ABTL06 path-decomposition dependencies remain unchecked. The audit establishes the Part II arithmetic and recoloring chain conditional on these inputs.

checked: Traced the deterministic multilinear/Hausdorff reduction and support-function identity, Maurer vector contraction for max-coordinate functions, Bernoulli symmetrization and exact-size balanced-pair symmetrization. Verified the gamma_i weight choice and all scaling powers.

Checked arbitrary-p sparse Max-Cut chaining, edge-count variance, denominator comparison including empty samples, pn<1 fallback, and the two-clique CLT sharpness calculation.

score_reasons.novelty: A positive hyperbolic Laurent-polynomial family and compact log-rate mixtures admit near-π progress per query.
score_reasons.depth: The exact proof combines a moment/sign comparison at quartic endpoints, periodized determinant bounds and parity-respecting endpoint completion.
score_reasons.exposition: Provides two complementary analytic constructions with explicit separation of expected and exact guarantees.

checked: Traced the exact main proof: normalized geometric-polynomial square proves positivity, reversal components give alternating feasible updates, and periodized kernels reduce hybrid positivity to a 2×2 determinant.

papers.title: When quantum thermal states look classical
papers.authors: Jordan Cotler, Harald Putterman, Alexander Zlokapa

review.title: When quantum thermal states look classical
review.authors: Jordan Cotler, Harald Putterman, Alexander Zlokapa

score_reasons.significance: Broad, quantitatively sharp connection between thermal entanglement, magic and classical algorithms.
score_reasons.novelty: Pauli defect repair and birth/closing accounting exploit cancellation unavailable to generic norm bounds.
score_reasons.depth: Combines polymer expansions, weighted transcript sampling and structural obstructions.
score_reasons.exposition: Long but organized; several distinct thresholds and norms require careful reading.

checked: Traced ordered-Pauli polymer construction, connected-factor trace factorization and multinomial cancellation.
Checked canonical birth/repair transcript estimator, multiplicity correction and unbiasedness, including complex weights.
Reconstructed the key bound: births b<=m/2 and at least b closing repairs give weight at most B(4 beta max{s,sqrt(Jsk)})^m; derived absolute activity and finite-cutoff Kotecky–Preiss bound.
Read formal normalizations and algorithmic guarantees; separable product-mixture sampler's polynomial running time is not near-linear.
remaining: 102-page large-proof exception: infinite-volume/cutoff passage, full random cluster estimator, pinning machinery, separability lower constructions and near-commuting magic proof have not been fully audited.
No numerical or formal certification of the entire algorithmic package.

review.summary: Proves high-temperature classicality thresholds for Pauli Hamiltonians: separability at scale 1/(sk), and zero-free/phase-transition bounds at scale 1/max{s,sqrt(Jsk)}, with nearly commuting improvements, sampling and thermodynamic algorithms. Here s is local strength, k locality and J the largest Pauli coefficient; the distinctions between these normalizations matter.
review.prior_frontier: Improves locality/degree dependence in high-temperature separability and zero-free bounds; introduces a weighted notion of approximate commutativity rather than assuming small operator-norm commutators. Polynomial algorithms can have large exponents.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate under explicit large-proof exception; verified polymer core, not the entire theorem package.

review.title: A Scheme-Comparable Formulation of Uniqueness Entropy for k-mer Sketches on Repetitive Genomes
review.authors: Akmuhammet Ashyralyyev, Can Alkan
review.summary: Defines position-weighted log seed multiplicity and an approximate prediction under a planted Zipf-repeat genome model, combining chance collisions, mutation-dependent sibling matches and context co-selection. Several scheme-specific parameters are measured or simulated.
review.prior_frontier: Extends practical density/conservation comparisons with repeat-sensitive summaries; not a new general sketching complexity bound.

score_reasons.significance: Useful specialized analytical comparison, with empirical rather than worst-case algorithmic scope.
score_reasons.novelty: Unifies repeat multiplicity, co-selection and boundary effects in one predictive statistic.
score_reasons.depth: Main derivation uses size-biased Zipf moments, binomial siblings and Poisson collision modeling.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly notes tandem repeats outside the model and approximation for multiplicity-aware schemes with divergence.

checked: Checked the log-multiplicity definition and nonnegative sketch-versus-genome distortion. Read Theorem1 decomposition and its stated approximation qualifications. Zipf size-bias changes exponent α to α−1 and gives −ζ′/ζ log-moment.
remaining: No full audit of conditional sibling independence, ratio-of-random-count effects or empirical estimates; no correctness certification.

review.title: Breaching the 2-Approximation Barrier for Prize-Collecting Steiner Forest
review.authors: Miguel Bosch-Calvo, Fabrizio Grandoni, Bence Mátravölgyi
review.summary: Polynomial-time (2−10^−25)-approximation for prize-collecting Steiner forest with nonnegative edge costs and demand penalties. A below-two edge-cost bifactor bound with a large penalty factor is combined with two pair-removal candidates.
review.prior_frontier: Extends recent below-two ordinary Steiner-forest techniques past the unknown-optimum-demand obstacle; the natural LP has gap at least 9/4, so this is not a claim to round that LP below its gap.

score_reasons.significance: Breaks the factor-two barrier for a standard prize-collecting network-design problem.
score_reasons.novelty: LP pruning removes both pairs and moats to restore identical-or-disjoint separation neighborhoods, enabling autarkic contractions.
score_reasons.depth: The proof must preserve useful dual mass while paying for removed penalties and combine extremely small constant improvements.
score_reasons.exposition: The bifactor and final ratio are distinguished, and the tiny numerical saving is explicit.

checked: Traced pruning LP constraints for exactly-three incidences and rounding thresholds 2τ+2σ=1; surviving neighborhoods must be identical or disjoint.
Checked color-mass sampling probabilities normalize and the removed-pair penalty bound via a comparison-forest feasible LP solution.
Checked feasibility cases: a bad pair pays one, uncovered valuable moat pays one, or two unvalued good moats contribute halves; covered valuable moats cannot form a three-incidence pattern.
Inspected the three-candidate and bifactor interfaces and their parameter roles.
remaining: Remaining central work includes the useful-dual-loss refinement, expected contraction savings, parametric primal-dual balancing and final 10^−25 arithmetic across the 54-page proof.

papers.title: Compressed Permutation Oracles Revisited
papers.authors: Joseph Carolan, Christian Majenz

review.title: Compressed Permutation Oracles Revisited
review.authors: Joseph Carolan, Christian Majenz
review.summary: Improves soundness of the existing compressed permutation oracle from N^{1/12} to the tight square-root query scale, allowing coherent forward/inverse queries and ideal-cipher key superpositions. Explicit advantage is <=120q/sqrt(N−q+1)+q(q+1)/(N−2q+1) when 3q−1<=N. Applications give concrete sponge and Davies–Meyer search bounds.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier compressed-oracle soundness reached only the twelfth-root scale; other exact representation-theoretic recording oracles are distinct constructions. Historical references were not independently exhaustively checked.

score_reasons.significance: Makes a reusable permutation-security framework sound throughout the natural birthday range.
score_reasons.novelty: Builds compression as the normalized completion-state POVM; contraction first, isometry second avoids larger accumulated errors.
score_reasons.depth: Symmetric-group frame spectrum, harmonic incidence gap and both row/column operator estimates are central.
score_reasons.exposition: Distinguishes contraction from isometry, swap from XOR oracle cost, and additive state error from success probability.

checked: Traced completion frame, orthogonal levels, Gram eigenvalue product and resulting contraction/isometry gap; checked exact synthesis using harmonic zero sums and level bandedness.

Read the incidence-gap representation calculation and explicit leakage rows. Checked how column/row bounds 64/m,32/m,24/m combine with answer-register decomposition and three-level overlap to the one-query constant60/sqrt(N−t).

Traced adjacent-frame ratio bounds, isometry conversion, q-query hybrid and ideal-cipher tensor/direct-sum extension without key-count factor. Checked square-root-scale reflection attack and its angle/count.
remaining: 36-page proof only partially audited: full representation-theoretic branching/Pieri inputs and every incidence multiplicity count have not been independently reconstructed. Applications/fundamental database lemma and hash-specific constants remain unverified.

papers.title: Seed Recycling: Explicit Codes for Mixed Synchronization Errors Matching the Leading Term of the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound
papers.authors: Quan D. Bui, Manabu Hagiwara, Shuche Wang, Van Khu Vu

review.title: Seed Recycling: Explicit Codes for Mixed Synchronization Errors Matching the Leading Term of the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound
review.authors: Quan D. Bui, Manabu Hagiwara, Shuche Wang, Van Khu Vu

score_reasons.significance: Closes a central explicit-coding leading-term gap for several synchronization channels at once.
score_reasons.novelty: Recycling ranks of two good seeds is a clean general tag construction.
score_reasons.depth: The coding application requires boundary projection, deterministic root finding and recursive tag protection.
score_reasons.exposition: The recovery order and implementation are unusually explicit and inspectable.

checked: Traced both root-counting bounds, seed ranks, collision separation and injective recovery. Seeds are present before ranks are decoded, so there is no circular decoder dependency.
Traced equal-length prefix/suffix projection for full Damerau–Levenshtein distance using a moving boundary, including a transposition crossing the boundary. The equal-length hypothesis is essential.
Checked greedy protected-tag size, radius-2t competitor enumeration, decoder uniqueness and the one-level bootstrap giving polylogarithmic precomputation and stated redundancy.
Traced deterministic root enumeration by gcd with Z^Q−Z and trace-coordinate splitting; checked rank/select cost and encoding/decoding exponents.

Independent finite checks passed 16,384 rank-recycling cases over GF(16), 512 confusable-pair tests and 2,810 equal-length boundary projections; scripts/audit1449.py and review-data/audit1449.json record scope.
remaining: Uses standard finite-field arithmetic and Shoup's deterministic irreducible-polynomial construction in fixed characteristic; checked the primary published abstract rather than re-proving that algorithm.
Finite checks supplement the general proof; they are not exhaustive over block lengths or error budgets.

review.summary: For each fixed t, constructs explicit binary codes correcting t mixed insertions, deletions, substitutions and adjacent transpositions, with redundancy 2t log n + 2t log log n + O_t(log log log n) and polynomial-time encoding/decoding. Seeds are used to carry payload bits, so choosing collision-free hashes does not pay their full description length.
review.prior_frontier: Improves leading redundancy from (4t−1) log n for t deletions and 4t log n for edits (8t via the elementary transposition reduction) to the Gilbert–Varshamov leading term 2t log n. The claim is fixed t, not uniformly efficient growing-error codes.
review.recommendation: Strong shortlist candidate; central construction, correctness and complexity traced.

papers.title: Improved quantum volume estimation with transducers and amortized quantum walks

review.title: Improved quantum volume estimation with transducers and amortized quantum walks
review.authors: Arjan Cornelissen, Simon Apers, Sander Gribling
review.summary: Quantum convex-body volume estimation uses Õ(d^3.5+d^1.75/ε) membership queries via transducer-based amortized quantum walks; develops a general way to amortize star-state preparation. Query complexity only: full time efficiency remains open.
review.prior_frontier: Improves prior Õ(d^3.5+d^2.25/ε); acknowledges concurrent Zhang bound Õ(d^2.5+d^1.5/ε) with different walk/product-estimation methods, so not the overall best concurrent query bound.

score_reasons.significance: A reusable quantum amortization framework beyond its improved volume-query application.
score_reasons.novelty: Amortizes preparation of varying-cost neighbor/star states using electrical-flow transducer witnesses.
score_reasons.depth: Requires adversary composition, annealing and detailed continuous-to-discrete walk control.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicitly distinguishes query from time complexity and discusses stronger concurrent results.

checked: Read precise radius-dependent volume-query bound and rounding overhead. Inspected Lemma4.5 parallel star-reflection composition and the witness cost separation for stationary and orthogonal components.
remaining: Audit adversary conversion and witness removal, discrete speedy-walk bounds, annealing and complete volume estimator.

papers.title: Unique Optimality with Polynomially Bounded Scores
papers.authors: Hirotaka Ono, Kazuhisa Seto

review.title: Unique Optimality with Polynomially Bounded Scores
review.authors: Hirotaka Ono, Kazuhisa Seto
review.summary: Defines polynomial-score unique-optimum class UOP, proves unique maximum clique complete for it, separates it from DP under PH≠S_2^NP, and builds a strict score hierarchy and UOP⊊P_dtt(US)⊊Θ_2^P relative to one recursive oracle and a comeager set.
review.prior_frontier: Refines the classification of unique maximum clique; does not settle its unrelativized Θ_2^P completeness question.

score_reasons.significance: Clarifies the computational resource represented by bounded-score unique optimality and gives conditional/oracle distinctions.
score_reasons.novelty: Uniform per-candidate oracle obstruction permits score-range hierarchy separation independent of candidate count.
score_reasons.depth: Combines isolation-based collapse, polynomial-method oracle queries and simultaneous forcing constructions.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes conditional, relativized and comeager assertions.

checked: Checked the coDP score gadget: unique default, doubled G witnesses, and higher weighted F witnesses; random maximum-weight isolation has zero false positives and ≥3/4 success.
Traced the fixed-list disjunction degree bound: product_j(c_j−1) vanishes exactly off the zero oracle, so multilinear degree N≤mq; preprocessing fixes ≤q_0 bits.
Inspected simultaneous recursive-oracle and dense-open construction, including freezing every candidate query and replacing occupancy promises by total predicates.
remaining: No full audit of the central uniform score-evaluator obstruction, clique completeness gadget or external noncollapse implication; these remain required for all headline separations.

papers.title: Tight Lower Bounds for Differentially Private Continual Counting
papers.authors: Charlie Harrison‎, Ethan Leeman

review.title: Tight Lower Bounds for Differentially Private Continual Counting
review.authors: Charlie Harrison, Ethan Leeman
review.summary: For eta=max(epsilon,delta), L=log(n eta), U=1+min{L,log(eta/delta)}, proves unrestricted binary prefix-sum error Omega(L^{3/2}sqrt(U)/eta) in expected l_infinity and Omega(L^2 U/eta^2) in mean/max-coordinate expected square loss, for n eta sufficiently large, epsilon<=1,delta<=1/4. Blocked Laplace/Gaussian tree mechanisms match; high-privacy errors saturate at n and n^2.
review.prior_frontier: Prior constant-delta cases were known; concurrent Bairaktari–Dahl–Larsen covers pure-DP l_infinity. This paper adds all parameter regimes and unrestricted squared-error bounds. Concurrent historical comparisons are manuscript-reported.

score_reasons.significance: Completes asymptotic error tradeoffs for a standard privacy primitive, even against offline mechanisms.
score_reasons.novelty: Cross-parity tree probes and clipped evidence yield a unified lower bound directly for arbitrary mechanisms.
score_reasons.depth: Martingale score, telescoping range/variance potentials and group-privacy parameter optimization fit tightly.
score_reasons.exposition: All parameter regimes, padding, blocking and differing error notions are explicit.

checked: Traced the four-ary tree score: target block is excluded from active probes; signed shifted score gains 1/2 per level before clipping. Verified zero-sum martingale, range and variance potential telescoping, and error-to-clipping-loss bounds.

Checked group-privacy comparison after flipping a uniform expanded bit: new residual is independent of target index, so two Azuma tails bound tagging. Verified k=floor(beta U/eta) with k>=1, H=floor(log_4(n/k)), a=(1/16)sqrt(H/(1+k epsilon)), delta_k bound, q/n>1/4 and C0=exp(5500) sufficient for a>=2.

Checked high-privacy two-input lower bound, Laplace/Gaussian sensitivities, analytic Gaussian calibration in both delta<=epsilon and delta>epsilon regimes, blocked rounding bias and exponential-moment maximum error bounds. Verified Balle–Wang18 primary Theorem8 formula.
Traced parameter-regime matching and the simultaneous high-probability error corollary. No finite-n all-regime claim beyond the explicitly stated asymptotic thresholds is inferred.
remaining: No unresolved substantive gap found in the central lower/upper bounds. No formal certificate or exhaustive independent literature survey is claimed.

review.title: Four-Message Arguments for NP \circ batchQMA and Six-Message Arguments for QMA from LWE
review.authors: Rishab Goyal, Venkata Koppula

score_reasons.significance: Substantial reduction in interaction under a standard post-quantum assumption.
score_reasons.novelty: A carefully ordered extraction and encrypted key-chain hybrid extends the batch compiler.
score_reasons.depth: Quantum residual-state preservation and succinct NP policy enforcement complicate the reduction.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear theorem separation, but the 68-page security chain has many interdependent primitives.

checked: Traced the four-message basic batch compiler: pre-challenge extraction, post-extraction consistency and uniform FHE correctness along the encrypted path.
Verified that the proof drops extra acceptance tests before CPA hybrids, erases the key chain root-to-leaf without needing the challenged secret key and preserves the residual quantum state.
Checked the endpoint reduction has a first response fixed before the base challenge, and read the exact selective/semia­daptive and amplified soundness qualifications.
remaining: 68-page large-proof exception: NP policy extractor/state preservation, six-message prefix rewinding, amplification and the full imported LWE primitive package remain unaudited.
The unamplified six-message soundness bound is weak inverse-polynomial; negligible soundness uses amplification and loses the stated public-coin property.

review.summary: Obtains four-message all-short arguments for NP composed with batchQMA and six-message arguments for general QMA from post-quantum LWE. The structured batch statement is not a coQMA verifier, and fixed preprocessing is excluded from the online succinctness bound.
review.prior_frontier: Replaces additional functional-encryption assumptions for all-short batch protocols and reduces general-QMA interaction from eight to six messages. Selective/semia­daptive soundness and the amplification's private-coin qualification are material.
