review.title: An Efficient 1/4-Competitive Prophet Inequality for Subadditive Combinatorial Allocations
review.authors: Twan Kroll, Calum MacRury, Rebecca Reiffenhäuser, Siddharth M. Sundaram
review.summary: For independent finite-support monotone subadditive buyer valuations with demand oracles, gives expected-polynomial-time (1/4−ε)-competitive allocation against the ex-ante configuration LP. Also claims a <0.46 upper bound against that benchmark.
review.prior_frontier: Improves existential and efficient 1/6 guarantees; upper bound distinguishes subadditive from XOS LP performance and is not necessarily a prophet-optimum impossibility.

score_reasons.significance: Material constant improvement in a central subadditive online allocation problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Sharpened mirror thresholds retain historical structure instead of completing both reference maxima.
score_reasons.depth: Constructs recursive score distributions with exponential tails and a polynomial truncation.
score_reasons.exposition: Specifies demand-oracle, finite-support and ex-ante benchmark assumptions.

checked: Read sharpened threshold/retention mechanism and exact theorem. Checked final LP scaling θ=1−2ε and accuracy ε/2 gives (1/4−ε/2)(1−2ε)≥1/4−ε.
remaining: Full sharpened mirror lemma, recursive-score existence/tails, implementation and ex-ante lower-bound construction require audit.

papers.title: Calibeating Bandit Advice
papers.authors: Jason Hartline, Chang Wang, Yifan Wu

review.title: Calibeating Bandit Advice
review.authors: Jason D. Hartline, Chang Wang, Yifan Wu
review.summary: Bandit calibeating simultaneously obtains soft-O(K√T) swap regret and loss against the best post-processing of mixed recommendations. A deterministic oblivious lower bound Ω(K√T/log^6 K) is proved at T=K^4; robust recommendation tradeoffs and continuous-pricing bounds follow.
review.prior_frontier: Claims to close Ito’s dependence-on-K question. The formal lower theorem fixes T=K^4; it is not a uniform matching lower bound for every K,T. Pricing with common K-point support has soft Θ(T^(3/4)+K^(1/3)T^(2/3)). Prior claims not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Settles the action dependence of a basic bandit regret problem and simultaneously handles recommendation post-processing.
score_reasons.novelty: Auxiliary hidden best arms attached to a binary-tree swap-regret construction force exploration while preserving distinct swap witnesses.
score_reasons.depth: The lower bound combines transcript change of measure, martingale transfer and per-action comparison charges.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly explains why deleting the internal tree nodes destroys the lower bound; formal horizon restriction is narrower than the informal statement.

checked: Checked action-count feasibility, period construction and the root-mixture lower charge G_i≥Q_i/(4H) for unnamed actions.
Distinguished regret against a recommendation’s post-processings from ordinary swap regret and checked the T=K^4 specialization.
remaining: Trace internal-node and auxiliary-arm information bounds, martingale transfer to realized swap regret, calibeating fixed-point upper bound and pricing discretization.

review.title: Unlocking Fractional Moments in Delphic Set Streams
review.authors: Aranya Kumar Bal, Sourav Chakraborty, Arijit Ghosh, Rudrayan Kundu
review.summary: One-pass (1±epsilon) estimation of fractional frequency moments 0<k<1 for Delphic set streams using soft-O(log^2(m)log^2(|Omega|)/epsilon^4) space/update time, uniformly in k, with size/membership/uniform-sampling access. Extends to the soft-capping span given cutoff/evaluation/scale-sampling access to the function.
review.prior_frontier: Fractional moments were efficiently estimable for element streams; Delphic set streams previously had efficient union estimation but no stated counterpart for these moments. Prior union-estimator performance is cited, not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Substantive extension of streaming estimation to exponentially large implicit set updates.
score_reasons.novelty: Whole-set thinning plus selectively subtracting/add-back large-set cardinalities controls correlated inclusion.
score_reasons.depth: Control-variate variance, Efron–Stein and integral importance sampling handle the main dependence obstacle.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates the function representation assumptions, although real-scale/finite-precision implementation deserves explicit accounting.

checked: Traced the central selective variance bound: threshold h<=16Q and large-set expected mass<=4Q/3; small-union Efron–Stein bound hQ; repeated large-element excess variance<=D^2; independent small/large retention bounds intersection variance. Together Var(X_t)<=70Q(t)^2.

remaining: Initial screening, not a full proof audit. Primary Delphic union estimator, finite-precision costs for real scales/probabilities and full soft-capping implementation assumptions remain unchecked.

Also claims multiple separations among sabotage, conflict, linearized and noisy complexity and composition limits.
review.prior_frontier: Refutes the total-function composition conjecture explicitly stated in Ben-David–Blais–Goos–Maystre22. That primary paper and its inner LR composition theorem were checked. The further measure-separation historical claims were not fully surveyed.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a central total-function randomized query composition question negatively.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines an exact one-sided pointer detector with private certificate cells to totalize weak approximate indexing.
score_reasons.depth: Self-contained central-layer lower bound, adaptive private-cell simulation, list direct-product and robust small-error AND–OR evaluation.
score_reasons.exposition: Careful about totality, varying detector rates, malformed witnesses and the exponential outer/inner size disparity.

checked: Main composition claim only: traced exact detector on all pointer arrays, including fake candidates and reciprocal checks; affine correction gives correctly signed bias on every input.

Checked private linear-cell encoding by row-weight union bound, adaptive transcript indistinguishability before12b bits, and list direct-product product-potential proof. Traced seed erased-table bound, expected local-cost summation, and total certificate function ordinary-query lower bound.

Traced self-contained inner lower bound: exact negative-transcript likelihood ratio, hidden-row search, product posterior, Bernoulli adjacent-mass Fourier bound, central-layer exceptional probabilities and private-encoding transfer. Verified pivotal-cell argument gives LR=Theta(bq q^2).

Checked robust AND–OR small-error walk with fixed9m^2 budget and epsilon/(1−4epsilon) error, composed weak-address algorithm, exact certificate verification and all q,s,u,b query counts. Verified size conversion and matching ratio via primary2208.12896 Theorem1.
remaining: Main total–total composition proof traced with no unresolved substantive gap found. Additional Sections6–10 separation and composition-limit theorems have not been fully audited. Claimed Lean repository Timeroot/no_randomized_composition returned repository-not-found, so no formal build is asserted; the PDF itself says its certificate proves only little-o on a subsequence, not the sharp Theta(1/log) rate.

review.title: Exponential memory/query-complexity tradeoffs in high-accuracy feasibility problems

score_reasons.significance: Substantially changes the understood role of memory for accurate continuous optimization.
score_reasons.novelty: Anisotropic stretching and nested noisy Grassmannian phases reach a previously inaccessible regime.
score_reasons.depth: Conditional resampling, information compression and geometric blocking interact nontrivially.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed proof structure; several local algebraic transcription errors need cleanup.

checked: Checked bounded stretched regions and geometric validity of the constructed separation oracle, conditional on the stated transformation condition-number lemma.

Traced conditional resampling to produce robustly independent nearly perpendicular vectors, the blocking-to-acceptance argument, geometric waiting-time bound and thresholding of conditional success probability.
Checked that adaptive-oracle and bit-memory assumptions are retained in the statement.
remaining: 46-page large-proof exception: compression-game information lower bound, full Grassmannian volume estimates, transformation condition-number lemma and final parameter optimization remain unchecked.

Local slips: Lemma9's first bound writes 1−q where Definition2 supplies q; the subsequent union-bound calculation uses the correct q. The feasibility proof also drops d in an exponential tail display. These do not refute the inspected steps when corrected.

review.summary: Proves exponential memory/query tradeoffs for high-accuracy separation-oracle feasibility. Memory d^(1+delta) log(1/epsilon) entails at least (d log(1/epsilon)) raised to a soft-Omega(d^((1−delta)/8)) query lower bound. review.recommendation: Strong candidate under large-proof exception; geometric and resampling components checked.

checked: Checked pair averaging, the merge identity and logarithmic coefficient-mass accounting.

Checked arbitrary-marginal update normalization, endpoint existence, nonnegative zero-objective case and sequential fixing of high-incidence coordinates.
remaining: Audit initial gradual-rounding error, retained-piece coloring implementation, low-incidence progress product and complete application/bit-model details.

review.title: The k-server conjecture is true
review.authors: Christian Coester, Elias Koutsoupias, Marek Zbysiński
review.summary: Proves deterministic work-function algorithm k-competitive on every metric: WFA <= k OPT + clique(C0), with stronger terminal subtraction clique(XT). Handles pseudometrics and duplicate server locations through labeled points. No polynomial-time implementation of WFA is asserted.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves the deterministic k-server conjecture, improving the long-standing general-metric (2k−1) bound for WFA. Randomized claims in the related-work section are separate and not reviewed.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a foundational competitive-analysis conjecture for all k and general metrics.
score_reasons.novelty: Represents reachable work functions by valuations of determinant columns and uses weighted symmetric-square minors as a potential.
score_reasons.depth: Fresh-symbol noncancellation and a compact non-Archimedean potential argument replace case-specific work-function inequalities.
score_reasons.exposition: Self-contained algebraic argument with explicit endpoint potential, extended-cost accounting and direct duality proof.

checked: Traced fraction-field valuation, initial matching determinant with independent gamma monomials, determinant-preserving normalization qr=e1 (k>=2) and fresh first-row replacement reproducing the exact work-function recurrence. Repeated-point determinants and zero-distance labels are handled.
Checked det(Sym^2 A)=(det A)^{k+1} by scaling/swap/shear generators and minor-valuation monotonicity under nonnegative-valuation column combinations.

Traced old potential <=mu(Qhat)+mu(H), new potential =mu(Qhat)+mu(Hhat): triangle inequality makes all three-block comparison coefficients nonnegative; selected request-pair columns attain the reverse bound without duplicate columns.

Checked Appendix algebraic extended-cost identity via Cramer coefficients, minimum H basis and recurrence; avoids relying on an unverified external duality lemma. Initial row valuations give −clique(C0), terminal selected symmetric-square basis gives (k+1)w(X)−clique(X), and WFA accounting telescopes to the theorem.

Independent exact-integer DP checked 240 random shortest-path metric instances, n=3..7,k=2..4, 40 requests each, random lazy tie-breaking: all9600 prefix checks satisfy both stronger extended-cost and WFA inequalities. Script/results: audits/audit1467.py and1467-audit.json. These finite checks are supplementary, not a proof.
remaining: No unresolved substantive gap found in the full central proof. No formal certificate, exhaustive literature survey or audit of unrelated randomized-algorithm commentary is claimed.

papers.title: Optimal XOR Lemmas for Information Complexity
papers.authors: Alexander A. Sherstov

review.title: Optimal XOR Lemmas for Information Complexity
review.authors: Alexander A. Sherstov
review.summary: Establishes optimal XOR and direct-sum laws for information complexity. For total Boolean communication problems, IC_1/3(F XOR n)=Θ(n IC_1/(3n)(F)), apart from separable XOR functions; partial problems require the paper’s split-output information complexity term.
review.prior_frontier: Independently verified Sawettamalya–Yu arXiv:2411.13015v2 Theorems2/4 (PDF p.4): prior XOR bounds subtract both a constant and an input-length/n^lambda term; the distributional single-copy error is n^-lambda. The new paper removes those losses, gives an exact total/partial distinction and achieves distributional error Theta(1/n), with different absolute error constants in its lower/upper bounds.

score_reasons.significance: Sharp information-complexity composition laws have broad implications for communication lower bounds.
score_reasons.novelty: Fallback protocols replace costly conditioning and distinguish the genuinely different partial-function law.
score_reasons.depth: Combines recursive decomposition, minimax information bounds, and split-output rounding.
score_reasons.exposition: The exceptions, error parameters, and recursive proof structure are unusually explicit.

checked: PDF pp.14–25: checked the precise announced-output versus private split-output information conventions and promise domains. Verified private-coin conditional independence, concavity/continuity of information cost, both minimax constructions including the exact-protocol mixture removing slack, conditional fallback composition, independent execution bounds even for correlated coordinates, and the exact standard-embedding information chain-rule identity. Posterior distributions remain on the legal domain, and no crossed illegal input value is used.

PDF pp.26–30: checked the complete total-function extraction proof. Rectangle factorization makes the two block biases conditionally independent given (X_0,Y_1,R,M). Threshold product bias 1/4 gives summed child error≤4epsilon/3, bad-event probability≤8epsilon/3 and summed information≤I+4+16epsilon K/3. Fallbacks supplied by minimax have cost I/2^i+4+eta at depth i. Summing the recursion gives coefficient13/5 from sum(2/3)^i and average error N^-log(3/2)/10. After minimax, three repetitions reduce the worst-case error to<1/(3n); computed constants32I/n+64 and480I/n+64 after 15-fold amplification.

PDF pp.20–21,31–34,55–57: checked complete removal of additive losses for direct sums and non-XOR-reducible total XORs. A varying row/column gives n(1-h_2(epsilon)); a nonfactorable total sign matrix contains AND or its negation, hence an inner-product restriction. Independently checked AppendixB product posterior, KL control of heavy-coordinate masses, truncated spectral estimate, theta=(|X||Y|/||A||²)^(1/4), and small-n entropy bound yielding the explicit n(1-h_2(1/3))/48. Checked the XOR-reducible exceptions and partial-cycle counterexample with shared random cut and union-bound error n/m.

PDF pp.34–40: checked grouping extraction for partial functions, including error control outside the embedding distribution support and protocol-class minimax without error loss. Five repetitions yield error<1/(2m³) before split-output extraction divides cost by k. Checked the complete one-message Haar-basis rounding proof: selected-direction density cos²(phi)/pi, exact error(theta-sin(theta)cos(theta))/pi, exact expected KL_nat=2sin²(theta), integrability and the integration-by-parts identity. Reference-law conditioning yields information≤2s/ln2 and error≤s^(3/2). The small-margin-deficit versus grouping cases with m=ceil((3n/2)^(1/3)) cover all n and eliminate the additive constant.

PDF pp.22–24,54–55: checked the partial-matrix margin extension: gamma_2 unit-ball factorization and padding, separating-hyperplane dual formula min_mu gamma_2*(mu circ A), product witness for the lower bound and tensor dual distribution for the upper bound, and discrepancy≤margin. Combined the external discrepancy bound with the entropy baseline to obtain a purely multiplicative n log(1/margin) bound. No total-matrix theorem was applied directly to unspecified entries.

PDF pp.41–44: checked priced distributional information and cost profiles using conditional KL reference identities, including absolute continuity on supported inputs. In the two-block split, cost-profile conditional independence yields E[C0 C1]=(E g0)(E g1)/lambda², and choosing the cheaper of output and fallback gives W(H0 xor H1)≥W0+W1-W0W1/lambda-4. Checked product-slack iteration with lambda=100(I+4k), product>97/100>30/31, sum W_j<lambda/30, and existence of a block with priced cost<lambda m/(30n).

PDF pp.45–49: checked the complete distributional vector-output machinery. Weighted rounding gives error≤deficit and additional information≤(4/ln2)deficit<6deficit. Hellinger-weighted transcript gluing produces fixed vectors of deficit≤2Delta_pi+2IC. For the new XOR-to-vector lemma, verified conditional beta_j measurability, tower/martingale relation, telescoping sum E(F_i beta_i-beta_(i-1))²≤4epsilon, and the independent-coordinate projection bound Var(qbar)≤epsilon/m. Independently expanded the rational unit-sphere map Phi_a and used two independent embeddings to square the conditional error coefficient, yielding Delta_pi≤32epsilon²Delta+80epsilon/m and information≤2I/m.

PDF pp.49–51: checked final distributional constants and the low-information case rather than absorbing an unjustified additive loss. For I≤1/2, conditional output entropy gives Gamma^n>1/4 and a zero-information split protocol with error<ln2/n. Otherwise k=min(n,ceil I)≤2I, the priced block has epsilon<m/(60n), Delta<9k/n, and the vector protocol has deficit<3/(2n). Its rounded cost≤lambda/(15n)≤60I/n because lambda≥400 and k≤2I. Thus the n/60 SIC_(2/n) lower bound and the independent-copy upper bound with error1/(100n) follow with the stated distinct distributional error parameters.

Verified primary external dependencies: Braverman–Weinstein arXiv:1112.2000 Theorem1 (PDF p.3) gives the stated distributional discrepancy lower bound at error1/10, with worst-case amplification remark. Lee–Shraibman–Spalek author PDF dpt.pdf Theorem17 (pp.11–12) states and proves gamma_2* tensor multiplicativity for arbitrary real matrices, exactly the scope used for zero-filled partial-matrix dual witnesses. The new manuscript reproves its minimax extension and standard embedding instead of requiring an unstated partial-domain extension.
remaining: No formal proof assistant or executable checker was run. This is a complete mathematical check of the new main arguments with exact external theorem-scope verification, not a formal certificate.

Standard general information identities, separating-hyperplane/minimax facts and the full Braverman–Weinstein discrepancy theorem were not reproved from first principles. The author-hosted tensor product theorem and its short proof were inspected.

The precise historical numerical exponent .41 was not independently derived from the older paper; its positive-lambda input-length penalty and distributional error loss were verified directly and suffice for the novelty comparison.

review.summary: Fixed-rate Optimistic Hedge from uniform initialization has O(n log n) horizon-independent regret in all two-player general-sum games at η=c/n, but some three-player n-action games force exponential-in-n regret for every sufficiently small fixed rate, and linear-in-T regret when η≥Cn2^(-n/8).
review.prior_frontier: Makes explicit the previously nonconstructive horizon-independent bound and separates two from three players. Also simplifies the recent O(√m log n log T) upper bound; it does not rule out better regret from other learning dynamics.

score_reasons.novelty: Temporal approximation by frozen exponential sums yields polynomial constants; cascaded oscillators create the three-player obstruction.
score_reasons.depth: The upper proof controls changing variance norms and freezing error, while the lower proof requires stable coupled oscillators and a shared normalizer.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully states fixed common rate, uniform initialization and loss feedback, separating rate-independent from horizon-tuned statements.

checked: Traced frozen variance seminorm embedding Π_p, which preserves the number of exponential terms only because p is time-independent.
Checked Lemma 5.4 tuning W=Kn, η≤c/n, absorption constants and the negative variance coefficient in the final RVU regret bound.
Checked discrete-to-continuous Jensen comparisons and the endpoint additive term.
remaining: Complete local energy/freezing estimate, external exponential-sum Bernstein inequality and 20-page oscillator cascade lower bound remain unchecked.

review.title: A passive self-correcting quantum memory in three dimensions
review.authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, Ting-Chun Lin
review.summary: Claims a non-translation-invariant three-dimensional bounded-density geometrically local CSS stabilizer memory for one qubit with lifetime exp(n^eta) at sufficiently low fixed temperature. Technical analysis uses thermal-syndrome encoding and Gibbs-stationary local Lindblad noise, with a rate-normalization factor. Perturbative Hamiltonian stability is not established.
review.prior_frontier: Would resolve existence of a3D passive self-correcting quantum memory in the specified thermal model; prior3D power-law energy barriers alone did not prove such a lifetime. Primary Chesi–Loss–Bravyi–Terhal0907.2807 verified bibliographically, theorem not fully rederived.

score_reasons.significance: Foundational three-dimensional memory claim, with thermal encoding and dynamical assumptions essential.
score_reasons.novelty: Alternating local homological replacements amplify both error sectors, combined with an RG decoder and connected witness Peierls argument.
score_reasons.depth: Large geometric embedding, sheaf/homological construction, local decoder and thermal entropy-energy analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Detailed102-page development, but several displayed formulas and witness-direction statements need correction.

checked: Traced the decoder assembly equation delta f=sigma from commuting coarse-graining maps and alternating nonincrease/half-contraction conditions. Inspected RZ parity definition and RX cleaning/induced cohomology route, plus the local-update stability proof structure.

Checked witness Peierls summation conditional on componentwise decoder and homology lemmas: witness coboundary allows an injective syndrome deletion preserving the partition function; root-connected graph count is exponential in size; geometric contraction yields size>=2^(k−1) and sum of syndrome weights<=4 top weight. Bounded local support leads a convergent exponential series at sufficiently large beta.

Checked distinction between thermal-syndrome encoding and ground-state initialization, and that perturbative stability/TQO2 is explicitly left open. Single-qubit Pauli stability is the detailed argument; broader bounded-local noise is claimed by extension.
remaining: Large-proof exception: have not fully verified the initial complex homology, RX local cleaning lemmas, all embedding/LLL constants, or explicit scale8 construction. In particular componentwise independence (Claim5.5/Lemma5.6), including cancellation in local corrections, still requires checking against the actual decoder maps. The external dynamical theorem and all non-Pauli extensions remain unaudited.

Constant-level repairs are needed in the final Peierls display: Lemma5.9 factor |V2| disappears in Eq233, and the stated log(1+x)<=x log2 inequality is reversed on(0,1). A larger fixed beta and restoring the fixed prefactor preserve the asymptotic argument, but the displayed threshold is not verified.
resolved_notes: Introductory lifetime definition Eq5 uses <= threshold, which includes t=0; intended first-loss condition must use the opposite inequality. Main technical trace-norm bound has the meaningful direction.
Text preceding Definition5.7 says witness implies unstable; the established direction used for the probability upper bound is unstable implies witness.

checked: Traced the shadow coupling: maximal-coupling mismatches plus Bernoulli mixing yield Hamming change counts, and group privacy bounds the output likelihood ratio.
Checked the Bayes-risk conclusion can use whichever intermediate decision event has probability at least 1/2, retaining the vanishing exceptional probability before taking limits.
Checked γ=√(1−1/n) in the Laplace MGF gives the (n−1)Cε−log n achievable bound.

score_reasons.exposition: Model distinctions between rational approximate samplers and real-uniform exact samplers are explicit.

checked: Traced the finite best-response representation: threshold sums may equal the budget only if all choices are closed; strict slack permits uniform positive offsets for every open choice.
Checked candidate quantile rounding preserves allocation feasibility by downward movement and controls opponent payoff via marginal CDFs.
Recomputed final regret budget 9/16+2/40+2/64+2/128=179/320<1 and verified complete-row sampling preserves cross-battlefield correlations.

review.prior_frontier: Upgrades Hatami pseudo-junta structure to narrow monotone DNF approximation. Primary Hatami Annals2012 construction pp517–521 verified, including exact activation definition, arity, multiplicity load and approximation error.

Checked independent random forcing changes bias to2p−p^2 and each arity-d activation likelihood ratio<=2^d; weighted averaging gives one realization with both low error and bounded active-union expectation.

Verified positive-certificate extraction by zeroing inactive coordinates, Markov truncation, all epsilon constants and exponential width. Checked p near1 constant approximation via Poincare; remaining compact-bias case uses standard biased junta theorem and monotone conditional-majority readout.

remaining: Main proof traced with no unresolved substantive gap found. Claimed Lean formalization was not supplied as an accessible artifact in the manuscript and was not built. Standard compact-bias junta theorem is used; its full original proof was not rederived.

review.summary: For log n≪d≤(1/2−ε)n, binary linear codes exist with size Ωε(n) times the Gilbert–Varshamov bound. The proof is existential and does not give an efficient construction.

score_reasons.significance: A uniform linear-factor improvement over a foundational coding bound is a major result.
score_reasons.novelty: Counts short odd dependencies in a random kernel, then removes all bad vectors with one extra parity check.
score_reasons.depth: The new argument is concise but uses sharp existing Fourier moment and tail inequalities.
score_reasons.exposition: A seven-page proof exposes the complete probabilistic reduction and all analytic estimates.

checked: Traced every step of the central proof: a circuit of length ℓ has rank ℓ−1; ordered return walks bound circuit counts; the odd Poissonized return sum bounds expected odd circuits; absence of odd circuits makes the all-ones row annihilate the dependency kernel and hence lie in the row span, so one extra parity check eliminates every low-weight vector.
Verified τ∈[(1−ζ)R/2,(1−ζ)R), R=ln(2^n/V)=Θε(n), the small-Fourier contribution O(e^(−τ)/V), and the large-tail ratio ≤exp(−ζR/2)/(2τ). The resulting dimension gives |C|≥(1−ζ)R 2^n/(4V).

Fetched arXiv:1909.11929 (dependency1909.11929.pdf); checked Corollary1.4 and Theorem1.5 on PDF10–11 and definitions/properties on PDF15–17. They do apply to nonhomogeneous degree≤w polynomials. Algebraically substituted p=3 and (1−2u)²=ρ/(2−3ρ) into ψ to recover H(ρ)/2−γ(ρ). Checked the positive γ asymptotics, Parseval normalization, entropy/binomial bounds and tail threshold rounding.
Checked the optional all-circuit argument: exp(z)−1−z−z²/2≤0 for z≤0 and the same bounds show expected total circuits o(1).
remaining: No unresolved substantive gap found in the new proof. The published Fourier-inequality proofs are relied on as dependencies rather than re-proved; this is a mathematical audit, not a machine-checked certification.

review.title: Tight Information-Theoretic Threshold for Decoded Quantum Interferometry with Local Quantum Decoders
review.authors: Brandon Augustino, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Enrico Fontana, Dylan Herman, Guneykan Ozgul, Ruslan Shaydulin, Shreehari Sureshbabu, Jacob Watkins

score_reasons.significance: An exact local decoding threshold materially clarifies a prominent quantum optimization proposal.
score_reasons.novelty: The message-spectrum/Nishimori correspondence gives a sharp structural explanation.
score_reasons.depth: Lossless channel reductions, sparse-code geometry, and statistical-mechanics thresholds are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: The main local theorem is clearly separated from longer global results and conditional simulation.

checked: Traced the local tree core on pp.23–27: symbol-node Gram/isometry reduction, check-node block decomposition, posterior-orbit Nishimori law including stabilizers, and the recursion correspondence. Checked zero Fourier coefficients are handled by clause convolution, and the D versus D−1 root degree does not alter non-reconstruction.

review.title: Tight Query Lower Bounds for Quantum Sampling, with an Application to Certified Randomness
review.authors: Keshav Bhateja, Mehdi Esmaili, Atul Mantri
review.summary: Claims Θ(N^(1/3)) queries to beat the honest expected XEB score by a constant for random Boolean Fourier sampling and Haar state access. For Fourier and canonical Haar oracles, near-ideal scores by poly(log N)-query devices imply almost log N bits of smooth private min-entropy, even with prior entanglement and later oracle disclosure. These are ideal oracle results, not guarantees for arbitrary circuits.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the cited Haar lower exponent 1/4 to 1/3 and answers the expected-score Fourier question; the single-output entropy statement is stronger than earlier entropy accumulation guarantees.

score_reasons.significance: Optimal quantum sampling-score bounds and near-maximal private entropy address prominent oracle questions.
score_reasons.novelty: Pair-removal coherence and orthogonal Dirichlet degree replace looser query-to-copy reasoning.
score_reasons.depth: The Haar and entropy extensions require substantial independent operator and concentration arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: Oracle access, initial independence, no communication to Eve, and expected-score scope are clearly defined.

checked: Fully traced the Fourier lower-bound argument in §4.1–4.4, PDF24–30. Fourier characters give degree≤q; ax lowering operators yield Σb†b=D and [b,b†]=I−2D/N. Directly checked the pair-removal commutator norm identity 4⟨D−nx⟩/N.

Verified the exact identity I+b†²b²−b†b=(b†b−I)²+(2/N)b†Db and the score expansion; projection branches give B≤3−2/N+2λ+2(1−1/N)λ². Orthogonal query branches give growth ≤2√(t/N), hence λ≤4q^(3/2)/(3√N) and the stated Ω(N^(1/3)) constant-score lower bound.

Checked that arbitrary finite adaptive value/controlled query paths can be grouped into fixed controlled-query rounds with local purification and record-dependent swaps. The Fourier result allows Eve as a passive tensor factor and counts controlled queries explicitly.
remaining: The 99-page paper has additional central theorems: Haar Dirichlet projection and query-growth lemmas, Haar-unitary reduction, matching squaring-algorithm score analysis, and smooth-min-entropy comparison all remain unverified. The checked scope is the complete Fourier lower-bound branch, not a full certification of the paper. This substantial independent scope is the reason for the large-proof exception.

review.prior_frontier: Extends the degree-zero CSP dichotomy to all fixed degrees and identifies the exact hardness threshold; every positive threshold occurs even for trivially satisfiable languages. Domain labels, language and degree remain fixed.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves the complete degree-sensitive classification of a natural algebraic CSP problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Taylor operations induce multilinear indicator-space operations whose absorbing subspaces reconstruct global spans from pairs of local blocks.
score_reasons.depth: Combines cyclic operations, saturated integer lattices, subspace distributivity, rational reconstruction and hardness witnesses.
score_reasons.exposition: The finite span criterion is explicit and the distinction between solving a CSP and learning all bounded-degree identities is well motivated.

checked: Traced the saturated-lattice argument: Φ(v_i)≡v_i mod p in H∩Z^N gives coefficient matrix I+pK and nonzero determinant, so diagonal products span.
Checked absorbing-subspace distributivity by multilinear expansion with separate absorbing inputs.
Checked pair-projection component-balance equations, homogeneous empty-block coordinate and conversion of ideal membership to a rational row-space test.
remaining: Complete pair-block reconstruction, covered-endomorphism transfer, many-one hardness construction and degree-threshold examples remain unchecked.

review.authors: Rafael Frongillo, Haipeng Luo, Nishant Mehta, Jon Schneider

score_reasons.significance: A nearly universal minimax forecaster is a major strengthening of calibration guarantees.
score_reasons.novelty: Dirichlet perturbations are familiar, but the Bernstein-gap comparison supports a broader loss-adaptive statement.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines Stein identities, strong converse approximation, and a coalescent scale comparison.
score_reasons.exposition: Several important intermediate equalities are inaccurate as written, though the central scale comparison has a direct convexity repair; proof presentation needs revision.

checked: Traced Dirichlet Stein/telescoping and nonnegative stability, reduction to the scalar Beta–Bernstein window, the integration-by-parts signed-measure bound including a=1 or m=1, the entropy chord-gap argument, and the O(K log T) startup/shift bounds. Checked the iid minimax lower-bound mechanism.

The ancestor equality on p.29 is false: descendants give nonuniform weights to ancestors. The required inequality survives: conditional on ancestor weights and labels, average over exchangeable permutations of the weights and apply Jensen, obtaining E[F(Q_j)|A_j=a] >= B_a F(q). The occupancy recurrence should be stated for the backward lineage-count process, which has the needed marginal law, rather than the forward process. These repairs preserve the required inequality direction.
Checked the scale constants algebraically: the last p.30 display has an extraneous n after 78; (36n/(n−1/2)+6n/m) <=78 for 1<=n<=m. The headline constant bound follows.
remaining: 49-page large-proof exception: the external Sangüesa strong-converse theorem and all Appendix D technical lemmas have not been independently re-proved; the special-family upper bounds and complete integrability/selection details remain unaudited.

The p.35 Gamma calculation should use independence of P and U to write E[G_i^(rho−1)1_min]=E[U^(rho−1)]E[P_i^(rho−1)1_min]; its displayed product with E[U^(1−rho)] is not an equality. The intended ratio lower bound follows directly from the correct identity. This does not certify the rest of that special-case theorem.

review.summary: A single loss-independent Dirichlet predictor achieves expected regret within O(K log T) of the minimax value for each proper loss with finite continuous convex Bayes potential, including unbounded losses.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier U-calibration guarantees were generally uniform worst-case guarantees or specialized to bounded/smooth losses; the paper seeks near-minimax adaptation separately for every loss.
review.recommendation: Promising major result, with checked local repairs and explicit remaining analytic dependencies; exposition below the strongest contenders.

review.prior_frontier: Extends a cited constant-answer NEXP result to polynomial answers and resolves the maximal-correlation-one case for unital qubit noise.

score_reasons.significance: A full complexity dichotomy describes exactly when this noisy resource retains unbounded entangled-proof power.
score_reasons.novelty: Positive low-degree square-root approximation and Pauli folding improve dimension dependence.
score_reasons.depth: The proof couples noncommutative approximation, collision-pattern bounds, certificates and noninteractive entanglement manipulation.
score_reasons.exposition: The resource-state computability and qubit/marginal restrictions are stated explicitly.

checked: Read the polynomial-answer obstruction and the Pauli-folding route. Checked the four-term multiplication-error decomposition and normalization bookkeeping on PDF57 conditional on Lemma4.25: its three errors sum to O(k^64/D)||A||4²||B||4², and summing t outcome errors incurs the explicit Cauchy–Schwarz factor t.
remaining: Explicit large-proof exception: only the listed mathematical passages were checked. The complete central theorem and its remaining dependencies have not been verified; this record must not be presented as a correctness certification.
The central collision-rank lemma, positive approximation, succinct-certificate bit complexity, and correlation-one RE reduction require complete audit.

review.recommendation: Candidate under the large-proof exception, with only the stated partial verification; evaluate merit separately from full correctness.

review.title: Leakage-Resilient Computation via Matrix Refreshing
review.authors: Stefan Dziembowski, Sebastian Faust
review.summary: Uniform invertible-matrix refresh of two inner-product shares tolerates continual local leakage with statistical error O(T2^(6λ−n/9)); a stateful Boolean compiler has O(S2^(18λ−n/27)) error and efficient simulation. Uses only-computation-leaks, private communication and erasures.
review.prior_frontier: Replaces complex or leak-free-component-based refreshes with a simple shared-matrix protocol; trusted private-input initialization and output decoding remain. Claimed Lean formalization was not run.

score_reasons.significance: Addresses a central continual-leakage primitive and supports arbitrary stateful circuit computation without leak-free internal refresh hardware.
score_reasons.novelty: A spectral approximation of conditional answer tables controls leakage correlated through the shared matrix.
score_reasons.depth: Security requires pointwise factor energies, hybrid transitions through inconsistent encodings, nonlinear shortening and bounded-use wire compilation.
score_reasons.exposition: The model and remaining trusted interfaces are explicit, with quantitative leakage fractions and operational costs.

checked: Checked refresh and NAND tensor/shortening algebra; each wire copy participates in at most three operations, including repeated-input gates.
Traced the factor-two consistency correction in the conditional answer table and rowwise Pythagoras energy bound ≤1/β.
Checked leakage fractions λ/n<1/54 for refresh and <1/486 for compiler and expected O(n^6) gate cost from dimension n²+1 matrices.
remaining: Central nuclear-norm/residual estimate, whole transcript hybrid, shortening simulator and stateful composition remain unchecked in the 99-page proof. Lean code and claimed prior-proof gaps were not independently audited.

review.prior_frontier: Resolves a central total-function class separation by bypassing all large monochromatic rectangles, not merely equality-oracle protocols. NP query cost is charged by nondeterministic communication.

score_reasons.novelty: Combines algebraic-geometry proximity certificates with XOR of strong-extractor outputs to destroy large rectangles.

Checked large rectangle fiber pruning, strong-extractor image size>half for a common seed, Hamming concentration to a close pair and XOR certificate intersection; zero exists by small total acceptance density.
Traced Appendix B randomized Omega(log r) lower bound, including unavailable-preimage probability, rectangle threshold2^{r/2}, and leaf union bound.

remaining: 63-page large-proof exception: the boundary/Macbeath reduction, constructive additive-combinatorial lifting, properization and bit-complexity appendices, witness recovery, and the full proximity-based integer-program extension have not been independently audited. review.area: Exact algorithms; subset sum and integer programming
review.summary: Claims deterministic O_{d,epsilon}(n+N^(d+epsilon)) time for fixed-dimensional subset sum with coordinates bounded by N, including a near-linear-in-maximum-item one-dimensional algorithm, and improved fixed-row integer-program feasibility.
review.prior_frontier: One-dimensional near-linear algorithms depended on target t or the mixed scale sqrt(Nt); fixed-row integer programming had N^{O(d²)} coefficient dependence. The new bound is almost linear in the input-coordinate box volume.
review.recommendation: Highest-priority exact-algorithm candidate, with explicit large-proof exception for geometric and additive-combinatorial dependencies.

review.title: Finite-Memory Search: Rational Compilation and Arithmetic Lower Bounds
review.authors: Qian Qi
review.summary: For rational two-location imperfect-detection search, compiles an ε-optimal autonomous finite-state controller with exact rational risk certificate and logarithmically many labels for fixed failure rates. Under explicit non-tie separation, randomized M-state excess risk is governed by the optimal word’s repetition horizon; an explicit 28-to-29-state jump is claimed.
review.prior_frontier: Separates its counted autonomous-memory contribution from classical unrestricted approximation, greedy search, and finite-state factorization results.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a precise memory/resource tradeoff for a specialized search game.
score_reasons.novelty: Relates physical risk to a predictive-rank obstruction and supplies rational certificates at fixed budget.
score_reasons.depth: Needs controlled infinite tails, arithmetic separation and same-budget perturbation.
score_reasons.exposition: Initial and transient labels, randomness, free-clock exclusions and irrational-cost limitations are explicit.

checked: Checked Lemma6.1’s rank contradiction: excess<d_F/2 forces a common prefix with probability>1/2, producing an (M+1)×(M+1) strictly diagonally dominant future-test matrix; autonomous M-state transitions factor it through dimension M. Conditioning is only on observed prefixes, not the future success event.
Checked lasso upper-bound handling of monochromatic cycles: replace the last two labels by AB and lose only a bounded prefix length, so no free clock or uncounted initialization is used.
remaining: Uniform rational envelope and compiler, same-budget density theorem, and the claimed exact 28/29-state finite certificate have not been fully checked or executed.

review.authors: Kristóf Bérczi, Siyue Liu, Victor Reis, Jakub Tarnawski
review.summary: Any matroid ground set partitionable into k bases admits a partition whose base weights differ by at most the maximum nonnegative element weight, with a strongly polynomial rational-weight algorithm. Also gives weighted degree-bounded-base rounding, O(log n) prefix discrepancy, and counterexamples to weighted carpooling/two-sided unsplittable-flow conjectures.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the recently proved unweighted subset-count equitability theorem; acknowledges an independent weighted representable-matroid result.

score_reasons.significance: A sharp balancing theorem for arbitrary matroids and related conjecture counterexamples are substantial.
score_reasons.novelty: Localized exchange plus LP duality handles arbitrary weights; truncation makes balancing strongly polynomial.
score_reasons.depth: The constructive potential and weighted rounding go beyond simple pairwise exchanges.
score_reasons.exposition: The distinct equitability, rounding, and prefix questions are well organized.

checked: Read the block-weight gap argument. Conditional on the localized exchange theorem, checked complementary slackness y(S)=γ and the exchange contradiction: a heavy block containing more than half of S changes weight by u_e−1∈[−1,0), violating the assumed >1 gap; the symmetric light bound forces γ≤0.
remaining: Localized exchange dependency, global rebalancing termination, strongly polynomial truncation potential, weighted-base theorem and explicit flow/carpooling counterexamples need full audit.

review.title: Spectral Structure and Exact Arithmetic of Finite-Feedback Measurement Discrimination
review.authors: Qian Qi

Proves the binary concave spectral identity max(A+B=R)[F(λ_s(A))+F(λ_s(B))]=2F(c/2), c_i=λ_i(R)+λ_(2s+1−i)(R), and gives exact/approximate rational arithmetic results. score_reasons.depth: The 116-page work combines operational reduction, spectral inequalities, arithmetic compilation and exact-decision reductions.
score_reasons.exposition: The model qualifications are explicit, but the many distinct exact and approximate tasks require careful separation.

checked: Traced the active-rank Gram lifting: enlarging the joint Gram spectrum to the active spectrum of R increases each diagonal block, and the unused spectral tail is pooled rather than renormalized.
Traced the central binary algebra: average the two Horn-feasible spectra; apply Lidskii to K+JKJ to obtain c≺2x; Schur concavity gives the upper bound, and reverse-paired ± eigenvectors attain it.
Checked that c need not be ordered because F is symmetric, and zero padding handles d<2s.
remaining: The operational trace-budget reduction, general feedback-budget results, rational compiler and square-root-sum reduction throughout the remaining manuscript were not fully checked.

score_reasons.novelty: The fixed-table interface provides a concrete system design but the mathematical information-flow statement is elementary.
score_reasons.depth: The two formal propositions follow from deterministic equality and a Markov chain; most work is empirical evaluation.
score_reasons.exposition: The threat model and limitations are visible, although the large empirical presentation can obscure the conditional nature of privacy.

checked: Verified Proposition 1 by coupling adaptive server interactions under identical metadata and fixed proxy tables.
Verified Proposition 2 from S→M→O: I(S;O|M)=0 and I(S;O)≤I(S;M).
Inspected utility losses and attack-protocol qualifications; the theorem does not protect secrets recoverable from the retained metadata.

review.title: Single-Exponential Algorithms for Directed Feedback Vertex Set on Planar Digraphs
review.authors: Daniel Lokshtanov, Saket Saurabh, Jie Xue

score_reasons.significance: Closes a major parameter-dependence gap on a central planar deletion problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Alternation excess gives a surprisingly direct substitute for degree in FVS branching.
score_reasons.depth: The central structural identity and probability/measure recurrences are elegant rather than excessively complex.
score_reasons.exposition: The short proof is accessible, but several deterministic pseudocode and inequality slips need correction.

checked: Checked Euler corner counting, charging every directed facial walk to a solution corner, positive-weight sampling, and the planar vertex-splitting reduction for bimodal-only completion. Protected arcs can use weight n+1 instead of infinity, with infeasibility detected by the optimum weight.

Traced the randomized success recurrence and its product/binomial bound. Odd parity can be handled by padding the budget by one, affecting only a constant factor in O((2+sqrt(5))^k). Positive alternation cannot increase after deletion.

Traced the deterministic face-incidence counting, first-deleted-positive branching, bimodal completion leaf bound, and measure k−alpha|M|. Independently checked that c=8.03 permits alpha=−log(1−4/c)/log(c)≈0.33094435 and satisfies the leaf inequality, equivalently (c+1)^6<=c^5(c−4)^2.

Verified the cited primary MSW paper's Lucchesi–Younger weighted dijoin theorem and planar splitting/min-max framework. Polynomial weighted planar feedback-arc optimization follows from the integral cycle-cover LP with polynomial minimum-weight-cycle separation.
remaining: Local repairs required in the deterministic presentation: use the proof's invariant that no deletable positive solution vertex touches a marked face; Lemma5.1's stronger hypothesis that all incident vertices are protected is unnecessary for its own counting proof. Prune branches whose marked facial cycles are destroyed; the good branch never destroys them. Sum face counts separately over cyclic SCCs.

The proof's |P|>3|M| at a leaf should be <; the measure recurrence uses c^(−alpha), not c^alpha; branch height is O(k), not necessarily <=k. These repairs preserve the exponent. The abstract's 8.04 bound is a looser rounding than the main theorem's 8.03.
Manual audit with explicit local repairs; no implementation or formal certificate executed.

sources.detail: Checked weighted Lucchesi–Younger statement and planar splitting framework.

review.summary: First single-exponential polynomial-space algorithms for planar Directed Feedback Vertex Set: randomized (2+sqrt(5))^k and deterministic approximately 8.03^k, based on an Euler alternation identity and a polynomial bimodal-completion routine.
review.prior_frontier: General directed FVS retains 2^{O(k log k)} dependence. Planarity had not previously yielded single-exponential dependence; the result is confined to planar digraphs.
review.recommendation: Select: all central new arguments traced, with explicit repairable deterministic presentation issues.

review.title: Hitting time for loose Hamilton cycles in the random hypergraph process
review.authors: Jared León, Xizhi Liu
review.summary: For even n, the random 3-uniform hypergraph process acquires a loose Hamilton cycle exactly when its last isolated vertex disappears, with high probability. Higher-uniformity and counting extensions are stated separately, with graph Hamiltonicity corresponding to minimum degree two.
review.prior_frontier: Sharpens the cited asymptotic edge-density threshold to an exact hitting-time theorem that accommodates degree-one vertices.

score_reasons.significance: An exact hitting-time theorem settles a prominent random-hypergraph Hamiltonicity question.
score_reasons.novelty: Mixed cycles retain prescribed pairs to absorb low-degree vertices while adapting matching entropy methods.
score_reasons.depth: Requires conditioned random-core laws, entropy stability, resampling, local cycle surgery and stopped martingales.
score_reasons.exposition: The modifications beyond perfect-matchings arguments and the dependencies are clearly mapped.

checked: Verified Claim4.4’s conditional core law: the hitting-time weight of an m-edge graph is proportional to the number of edges containing a degree-one vertex; exposing the low-degree set and incident edges fixes that weight, leaving the core uniform subject to degree lower bounds.

Checked the inspected transfer from conditional auxiliary-matching edge marginals to oriented cycle triples by total probability and triangle inequality; this remains conditional on the preceding entropy estimates.
remaining: Explicit large-proof exception: only the listed mathematical passages were checked. The complete central theorem and its remaining dependencies have not been verified; this record must not be presented as a correctness certification.

Full entropy stability, resampling under degree constraints, cycle-switch comparison and martingale accumulation need audit. The advertised Lean repository and generalized extensions have not been checked or compiled.

review.recommendation: Candidate under the large-proof exception, with only the stated partial verification; evaluate merit separately from full correctness.

review.summary: Characterizes the limiting maximal product-state energy of mixed random Pauli p-spin Hamiltonians by a scalar Parisi variational formula, with universality extensions. For the pure p=2 model, obtains C(ε)n² optimization under an explicit no-overlap-gap condition.
review.prior_frontier: Previously even-p limit existence and large-p asymptotics were known without this fixed-p characterization. This optimizes product states, not unrestricted entangled ground states; efficient optimization is conditional. Prior results and the vector-spin Parisi input were not independently checked.

score_reasons.significance: Gives a precise asymptotic variational description for a natural quantum variational class.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses Bloch vectors and rotationally scalar covariance to simplify a matrix-valued Parisi problem and derive an IAMP algorithm.
score_reasons.depth: Combines covariance comparison, zero-temperature limits, strict convexity, universality and state evolution.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes product-state energy and the conditional algorithm, though several substantial imported results require close hypothesis checks.

checked: Checked the Bloch-sphere reduction and the Gaussian Lipschitz/concentration normalization.
Traced sampling with versus without replacement to obtain the covariance discrepancy Σp(p−1)c_p² plus the tail, and its vanishing normalized free-energy error.
Checked the spherical-cap volume (δ²/4)^n and Gaussian modulus bound give a temperature-to-ground-state error uniform in n.
Inspected how ξβ(A)=β²ξ(Tr A) makes the gradient scalar in the vector-spin variational formula.
remaining: The exact hypotheses of the imported vector-spin Parisi formula for all allowed mixtures, scalar-path minimization/strict convexity, zero-temperature optimizer existence and IAMP state evolution remain unaudited.

score_reasons.significance: Near-exact length feasibility closes a consequential obstacle in planar network design.
score_reasons.novelty: Builds on existing separator and junction-tree frameworks but introduces persistent clocks and a shared-edge charging argument.
score_reasons.depth: The proof coordinates cost rounding, immutable paid prefixes, endpoint-specific deadlines, layered LP flows, and density search.
score_reasons.exposition: The compact proof is detailed and explicitly separates integral-reference and fractional-reference guarantees.

checked: Traced all central new arguments on pp.3–16: bounded-cost path DP, forward record clocks and the last-old-boundary invariant, the two-branch integral recursion with immutable paid edge sets, and polynomial recursion size.
Checked layered-flow preparation, per-depth deletion/renormalization, and preservation of endpoint deadlines without using contracted arcs as length witnesses.

Checked the paired-junction shared-edge exchange: adjusted prefix/suffix values are δ-separated on a bounded interval, bounding repeated charges. Verified cumulative alternating layer balls, three-layer witness containment, and separator recursion.
Checked the two-phase search LP, demand bucketing, median-contact complementary deadlines, additive rooted repair, and harmonic covering analysis.
Verified the external three-root-path planar separator in Friggstad–Mousavi, arXiv:2302.04747v2, Theorem 3/Corollary 4 (PDF pp.3–4).
remaining: This is a manual central-proof check, not a formal proof or an implementation benchmark. Standard planar embedding, LP, and separator primitives are used as stated.

review.summary: Polynomial-time bicriteria algorithms for length-constrained planar directed Steiner tree and forest preserve path lengths within 1+ε, with polylogarithmic cost approximation. The rooted integral-reference bound is O(ε⁻¹ log² k); the forest bound is O(ε⁻² log⁷ q).
review.prior_frontier: Chekuri–Jain obtained polylogarithmic cost with O(log k) length violation. The new result makes the length violation arbitrarily small, at higher cost factors; it is not an exact-length approximation.
review.recommendation: Strong shortlist candidate; distinguish the near-exact length guarantee from the larger polylogarithmic cost factors.

review.title: Lattice Reduction at Average Precision
review.authors: Yang Zhou, Zhedong Wang, Mingsheng Wang
review.summary: For a nonsingular integer basis with summed row bitlength L, computes a 2^O(n)-approximate shortest vector in expected Õ(n^ω(L/n+1)) bit time and a complete indexed-successive-minimum approximate basis in Õ(n^ω(L/n+n)); also claims rational polynomial factorization in Õ(N^ω(N+τ)). Outputs are exact lattice vectors, not necessarily LLL-reduced bases.
review.prior_frontier: Improves worst-row-precision dependence to average precision and gives a matrix-multiplication reduction in the high-average-precision regime; the underlying reduction-oracle dependency is not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Precision-sensitive lattice reduction and faster classical factorization have broad algorithmic implications.
score_reasons.novelty: Digit/carry membership embeddings and quotient recursion avoid spreading large-coordinate precision.
score_reasons.depth: Requires exact lifting, inverse-norm bounds and amortized bit accounting.
score_reasons.exposition: Models are explicit, but many formulas appear as raw LaTeX in this PDF, making the technical presentation harder to read.

checked: Checked Theorem3.3’s gap mechanism conditional on the balanced membership lemma: choose residual scale T above the oracle approximation times σ√r·2^(D/r); then any returned short vector has zero residual block and projects exactly into the original lattice. Reviewed the block inverse bound and exact scaling.
remaining: Balanced Smith/HNF conversion, early low-precision branch, complete-basis quotient recursion, matrix-multiplication reduction, factorization analysis, and the cited reduction oracle need full verification.

review.title: Counting Exact-One Hitting Sets in Subexponential Time
review.authors: Shiteng Chen, Tao Jiang, Yijie Zhu
review.summary: Reduces exact-one hitting-set counting on r variables to the difference of two ordinary 3-CNF counts on at most 2r−2 variables. Also represents every nonempty explicit VC-dimension≤1 Boolean relation by 2-CNF plus signed exact-one equations. The advertised subexponential algorithm imports an external fixed-width #SAT theorem.
review.prior_frontier: The earlier marker–parity reduction plus row selection already gives the same claimed asymptotic time; the path saves marker variables and extends to bounded-length DNF terms. OpenAI [Ope26], The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False, is the essential external algorithmic dependency and has not been independently verified here.

score_reasons.significance: Useful compact counting reductions and a structural representation theorem, but the dramatic running-time claim comes from an imported general counting result.
score_reasons.novelty: Eliminates marker variables through a two-boundary equality path and extracts signed exact-one separators from VC-one tables.
score_reasons.depth: The new core arguments are short algebraic/combinatorial reductions rather than a new subexponential counting algorithm.
score_reasons.exposition: Carefully separates declared variables, exact cancellation, row rank and the external theorem.

checked: Traced the path identity pointwise: all satisfied predicates force the zero path; any failed edge permits a suffix-flip bijection between endpoint choices, including h=1 and empty terms.
Verified rational row selection preserves all Boolean solutions and full column rank is handled by testing the unique rational candidate.
Traced VC-one closure enumeration and exact-one separation: minimal disagreement support has size≥3, singleton witnesses supply 10/01/00, and any double disagreement would shatter a pair.
remaining: The external fixed-width exact-counting theorem supplying every subexponential headline was not verified; no unconditional certification of that running time is claimed.
Additional graph applications and weighted/cardinality encodings were not fully audited.

review.title: Quantum Separability in Polynomial Time
review.authors: Giulio Malavolta

Does not give inverse-polynomial precision or trace-distance membership.
review.prior_frontier: Improves fixed Frobenius-gap algorithms; separate trace-distance hardness conditional consequence is not part of this proof audit.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a fundamental metric-specific quantum separability algorithmic frontier.
score_reasons.novelty: Local Haar flattening plus bounded-coordinate near-optimizers reduces the quartic problem to dense CSP.
score_reasons.depth: Two-stage hypercontractive tail control, truncation/refill, penalties and Frank-Wolfe implement the separation oracle.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear quantitative lemmas and explicit distinction of norms and accuracy regimes.

checked: Traced Haar entry moments via Gaussian normalization and inverse-Gamma moments, two hypercontractive applications, thresholded tail Frobenius control and partial-trace projection.
Checked truncation l1 loss, random-phase refill using vanishing partial traces, norm concentration/conditioning and normalization: all bounded-coordinate constants depend on accuracy, not dimension.

Checked quartic grid Lipschitz estimates and norm penalties by completing squares, including zero-norm fallback; primary Yoshida-Zhou Theorem5 admits bounded real payoffs, tuples with repeated indices and additive dense-CSP accuracy in polynomial time for fixed alphabet/accuracy.

Traced all parameter budgets in additive optimization and Frank-Wolfe recurrence with approximate linear oracle; compression-and-trace-refill proves unequal dimensions. Finite precision appendix perturbation/tail arithmetic checked.
remaining: Main real-arithmetic algorithmic proof traced with no substantive gap found. Standard hypercontractivity accepted in stated form. Finite-bit Haar sampler dependency BGVKS23 PropositionC9 not independently rederived; appendix sketches transfer. Separate trace-distance/3SAT hardness result not audited.

papers.title: List Decoding, Linear Hashing, and Furstenberg over $\mathbb{F}_q$
papers.authors: Vinayak M. Kumar, Geoffrey Mon

review.title: List Decoding, Linear Hashing, and Furstenberg over $\mathbb{F}_q$
review.authors: Vinayak M. Kumar, Geoffrey Mon

score_reasons.significance: Connects three central problems and resolves the fixed-field hashing order while controlling the difficult high-error coding regime.
score_reasons.novelty: The two-level multiplicity allocation and dimension reduction provide a new unifying mechanism.
score_reasons.depth: The proof combines Hasse derivatives over a function field, random projection, rotational amplification, and probabilistic applications.
score_reasons.exposition: The conceptual development is strong, but several literal equalities and small-field formula conventions need correction.

checked: Traced the central Furstenberg argument on pp.12–21: interpolation constraints with two multiplicities; derivative restriction and homogeneous substitution over F_q(t); multiplicity counting on the product grid; limiting dimension count; and the optimized density bound.

Checked the random projection collision estimate, rotational amplification, and compression to codimension plus logarithmic richness. Verified that passing from surjective to unrestricted random hashes can be handled by extra independent columns.
Checked the exact theorem distinctions on pp.7–8, including the uniform list-size bound max{O(q/log q)H_q(p)/ε,O(q)} and the stated concurrent-work comparison.
remaining: Large-proof exception: the 37-page paper's complete hashing tail integration, coding application, and matching lower-bound constructions were not fully audited. Selection relies on a checked core theorem plus these explicitly unverified applications.

Local repairs: derivative degree and restriction multiplicity should be inequalities, not equalities; asymptotic limits yield non-strict inequalities. Integer multiplicities require rounding or a rational-parameter limit. These weaker statements suffice for the inspected core argument.
The dimension-reduction construction should separate the case n<k+2t; the numerical bound in that case follows directly from the preceding ambient-dimension bound.

The displayed q log log q/log q hashing expression needs a positive small-field convention at q=2. The proof explicitly notes this and supplies an O(log n/log log n) binary bound; do not interpret the negative literal coefficient as a valid numerical inequality.

review.summary: A multiplicity-gap polynomial method gives dimension-independent finite-field Furstenberg bounds, optimal-order maximum load for linear hashing over each fixed field, and random-linear-code list sizes uniformly controlled even near the maximal error rate.
review.prior_frontier: For fixed fields beyond the binary case, linear hashing had weaker polylogarithmic load bounds. Prior and concurrent list-decoding results have sharper leading constants in other regimes but additive terms that can grow sharply as the error rate approaches 1−1/q. This paper supplies a different uniform tradeoff, not a dominance claim over every concurrent bound.
review.recommendation: Strong candidate under the explicit large-proof exception; the new core is substantial, with the application audits still outstanding.

score_reasons.novelty: Additional SPQR/ST-tree summaries remove the search logarithm.

Read the lazy-tail modification and its purpose in constant-time split/merge.
remaining: The complete pre-split invariants, lazy-tree implementation and critical-path searches still need a central-proof audit.
The general-graph reduction and exact initialization costs have not been independently checked.

Checked the dependency qualification: after fixing lower layers the replaced block is independent of all other inputs used by the bounded-depth circuit; the target and sampling functions depend only on A.
Inspected the salted-majority parallel-repetition route needed for nonuniform average-case security.

papers.authors: Duri Andrea Janett, Robert Robere, Anastasia Sofronova, Dmitry Sokolov

review.title: Lower Bounds Between Random CNFs and PRG Tautologies For Dag-like Communication
review.authors: Duri Andrea Janett; Robert Robere; Anastasia Sofronova; Dmitry Sokolov
review.area: Proof complexity and communication lower bounds
review.summary: Claims a stretched-exponential triangle-DAG lower bound for random conjunctions of clause-or-parity constraints: width Δ=d log n and m=αn2^Δ, with sufficiently large constants. This is an intermediate problem toward inner-product NW generator tautologies, not that open lower bound itself.
review.prior_frontier: Existing random-CNF lower bounds exploit sparse rows; parity has density 1/2 and defeats that argument. The new approximation scheme aims to handle this obstacle.

score_reasons.significance: Would remove a concrete obstacle in a recognized proof-complexity program.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines robust sunflower pruning with limited independence of random parity outcomes.
score_reasons.depth: The construction tracks asymmetric indicators through triangle DAGs.
score_reasons.exposition: The model distinction is clear, but the error-set invariant and some theorem constants are not consistently specified.

checked: Verified the unsatisfiability union bound on page 6: a constraint fails a fixed assignment with probability 2^(-Δ-1), requiring α>2 ln 2 for the displayed bound.
Checked that boundary expansion gives linearly independent parity constraints on small subsets, hence the stated local uniformity.
remaining: The approximation/error propagation invariant must be repaired or justified before the claimed lower bound can be endorsed.
External robust-sunflower and AC0 limited-independence parameters have not been fully traced.
issues: Page 12 Claim 5.3 removes AccErrX×AccErrY and subsequently uses that the remaining set is a triangle. Removing an arbitrary rectangle does not preserve triangular/Ferrers structure: rows {a,b} and {a}, after deleting {first row}×{a}, become {b} and {a}. A special invariant ruling this out is needed.

Page 15 equates the product of accumulated row/column error sets with a union of same-node new-error products. In general (union A_i)×(union B_i) contains cross-node products absent from union (A_i×B_i). The manuscript does not establish the additional common-origin property needed for the displayed equality. checked: Traced all new arguments on pp9–24: adaptive hidden-Gaussian conditioning, Schur-complement reduction, shifted smallest-singular-value tail, inverse-Frobenius trace reduction, deterministic rotation reduction, odd-polynomial approximation and quadrature lower bound, symmetric Fejer-polynomial upper bound, and backward-to-residual conversion. The probability calculation on p13 needs m=ceil(16/rho) and success p>=1-rho/(2m), not an arbitrary larger m with the displayed fixed p. This preserves existence of a sufficiently high universal success probability. Normalize the quadrature measure before claiming weights<=1; actual continuous support satisfies the quadrature hypothesis. The residual-polynomial sign typo is harmless in the absolute-value bounds.

review.title: An LP Algorithm for Counting Eulerian Orientations Through the Lens of Promise Polymorphisms
review.authors: Jincheng Guan, Shuai Shao, Ke Shi
review.summary: Polynomial-time algorithm for weighted Eulerian-orientation signatures in the former FP^NP tractable class, removing the NP oracle and obtaining an FP/#P dichotomy; associated complex Holant consequence with a nonzero odd-arity signature.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier Meng–Wang–Xia dichotomy had an FP^NP class; prior hardness classification is used as a dependency, not reproved here.

score_reasons.significance: Eliminates the oracle gap in a counting dichotomy.
score_reasons.novelty: LP attainable local supports are affine via ternary-XOR promise closure.
score_reasons.depth: Subtle support restriction preserves complex weighted sums and product-type tractability.
score_reasons.exposition: Short, transparent proof with explicit LP and signature interfaces.

checked: Traced complete new algorithm on pp11–12: local-distribution LP, edge marginal conservation, positivity tests, L supports containing all globally extendible local configurations.

Verified ternary convolution cubes each edge bias, preserving opposite-bias conservation. All forbidden-side outputs have one-sided positive imbalance, while total expected imbalance is zero, so they have zero probability. Averaging three witness solutions before convolution proves ternary closure.

Independently checked affine constant-weight support lies within complementary coordinate pairs: character expansion of total signed weight forces equal positive/negative coefficients for each F2 character, allowing coordinate pairing. Restriction to the larger pairing support, rather than arbitrary affine L, preserves EOP product structure; EOA uses affine quadratic-phase counting.
Checked termwise preservation of every nonzero global orientation, empty-LP zero case, and self-loop reduction. Classical affine/product weighted counting is used at its standard interface.
remaining: Earlier #P-hardness classification, odd-arity Holant reduction and the full classical affine/product counting dichotomies were not re-proved; the new LP removal of the NP oracle was checked.

review.authors: Yunqi Huang, Lvzhou Li, Zekun Ye, Shenggen Zheng
review.summary: For position-permutation-invariant partial functions over any finite alphabet, proves R_ε=O(Q_ε²), uniformly for 1/6≤ε<1/2. Graph properties satisfy R=O(Q⁴), fixed-k hypergraph properties O_k(Q^(2k)), with explicit promise families nearly attaining exponent 2k.

Checked degree-bounded telescoping state residuals and that a dilation of the input-independent contraction preserves the total T input queries without postselection.

checked: Traced the full path-product span lower bound and the gated-product upper construction, plus dyadic approximation error and threshold-gate simulation.

papers.title: A Tight FPT Approximation for Capacitated k-Median
papers.authors: Aditya Anand, Yichen Huang, Ragesh Jaiswal, Amit Kumar, Euiwoong Lee, Jatin Yadav

review.title: A Tight FPT Approximation for Capacitated k-Median
review.authors: Aditya Anand, Yichen Huang, Ragesh Jaiswal, Amit Kumar, Euiwoong Lee, Jatin Yadav
review.summary: Deterministic (1+2/e+ε)-approximation for hard-capacitated metric k-median in f(k,ε)|I|^{O(1)} time, opening exactly k distinct facilities and respecting every capacity.
review.prior_frontier: Improves capacitated (3+ε) FPT ratio to the uncapacitated threshold; matching lower bound assumes PIH.

score_reasons.significance: Closes the capacitated-versus-uncapacitated FPT approximation gap.
score_reasons.novelty: Capacity-preserving branching version of continuous greedy and quota matching savings.
score_reasons.depth: Leader selection, finite types and capacity-dominating submodular maximization.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit hard-capacity and feasibility guarantees.

checked: Checked the complete new approximation proof (PDF pp6–19,22–23), including the deterministic leader construction. The nearest-client fallback either supplies a good leader or forces enough D-sampling mass in the near-optimal cluster ball; an LP-relative greedy hitting set then yields the required weighted leader-distance bound. Enumerating geometric radius VALUES, as Algorithm1 does, gives FPT list size.

Checked the relative-distance client types, with common nearest-leader offset and rounded differences in [0,d(leader,leader)]. Their count is k·O(1/ε)^k. Proxy distances dominate actual distances, every count-matching assignment has the same proxy cost Z, and Z≤(3+O(ε))OPT.

Checked quota-savings submodularity through disjoint type-specific facility slots and weighted matching valuation. Discarding the lowest savings to return from rounded-up quotas to true counts retains at least1/(1+ε) of each type/facility savings; leftover type counts can then be assigned feasibly because every selected capacity dominates its optimal counterpart. This gives Z−(1−1/e−O(ε))(Z−OPT).

Checked the capacity-preserving submodular theorem in full. Enumerating singleton-value guesses and marginal buckets gives a path containing only capacity-dominating representatives. Independent Bernoulli occurrences produce a monotone gain of at leastη(1−ε) times the remaining optimum gap. Exact enumeration of O(k²/ε) occurrences makes all expectations deterministic FPT. The final one-per-group fixing lemma follows by submodularity and E|Ri|≤1, preserving the value without breaking capacities.

Checked the truncated/scaled metric preprocessing for strictly positive client–facility distances, FPT accounting via (log n)^t≤n t!, zero-singleton-value branching and empty-optimal-cluster handling. Verified the PIH-to-tight-MaxCoverage dependency in Karthik–Lee–Manurangsi, IPEC2024, PDF p3; the k-median transfer is the stated standard coverage metric construction.
remaining: No implementation was run. The positive-distance normalization must explicitly address overlapping client/facility locations as described below; the central theorem is checked with that elementary preprocessing repair.
resolved_notes: Input-normalization corner: if C and F overlap, C=F={a,b}, k=2, Ua=0, Ub=2 and d(a,b)=1 has capacitated OPT=1 but uncapacitated cost Q=0, so Algorithm1 divides by zero. The displayed preprocessing preserves zero client–facility distances. Repair: first handle an exact zero-cost solution, otherwise for each guessed positive D make disjoint point copies and replace distances between distinct copies by d+εD/n before scaling. This is a metric, adds at most εD≤εOPT to every assignment, and makes Q positive. The result and factor survive, but the literal pseudocode needs this case.

Exposition slips on pp7 and11 confuse the rounded radius/count value with the number of possible values; Algorithm1 explicitly enumerates the geometric-value set, which has the intended logarithmic size.

sources.detail: PIH implication for tight MaxCoverage hardness; inspected dependency statement.
