review.title: Hardness of Unique Shortest Vectors and Bounded Distance Decoding
review.authors: Sergei Kudria; Jason Luo
review.summary: Randomized NP-hardness of constant-factor unique-SVP and BDD at every fixed radius fraction below 1/2 for each fixed computable ℓp norm, 1≤p<∞, including search. Finite-field code BDD below half distance is deterministically equivalent to UniqueCircuitSAT. Polynomial uniqueness/radius gaps are obtained for rational p>2 and p=∞.
review.prior_frontier: Extends earlier Euclidean search hardness from uniqueness tending to one and radii above λ1/sqrt(2); deterministic promise-preserving NP-hardness would require NP=UP in specified cases.

score_reasons.significance: Moves several standard lattice and unique-decoding hardness frontiers substantially.
score_reasons.novelty: Symmetric tensor encodings amplify distance while retaining recoverable unique satisfying selections.
score_reasons.depth: Isolation, tensor-rank distance estimates and lattice embeddings require careful promise preservation.
score_reasons.exposition: Decision/search versions, randomness and fixed-parameter computability are separated.

checked: Verified the code-BDD reduction’s final distance arithmetic conditional on Theorem 6.2: θ=1−1/(2(q+1)), αθ=1+1/(2q), and fixed t gives d(C0)>w/ρ, while the satisfying tensor has weight≤w.
Checked uniqueness/recovery and the reverse unambiguous verifier: two candidate errors differ by a codeword of weight≤2w<d(C0).

Checked the central tensor amplification argument in full (PDF pp19–22,34–37): the rank-one characterization works in every characteristic in the diagonal-block case and uses P>N exactly in the lattice case; fixing a slice reduces the column-span dimension, forcing flattening rank at least the tensor order when no rank-one matrix exists.

Checked the deletion-of-long-columns induction. A functional killing surviving columns would produce a nonzero product-code word supported on fewer than δ^(r−1) positions, contradicting product distance. The short independent columns occupy enough rows to propagate the amplification. For codewords, the q+1 projective combinations give union support at least(1+1/q)δ.

Checked the integer-column agreement count and constants in LemmaB.2, then the b_r=max(1,r/(256 ceil(p))) recurrence. In the unique-selection kernel case, subtracting the selected word yields at leastδ/2 outside-support slices, each with no rank-one obstruction; summing their pth-power norms gives the stated linear-in-order separation. The final ε=1/(10m) choice preserves a constant distance factor.
remaining: Scoped large-proof review of a 55-page manuscript: the core tensor amplifier and the code reduction arithmetic are checked, but random isolation/label replication in AppendixA, full-rank lattice completion in AppendixF, and the separate polynomial-gap moment-encoding construction in AppendixD have not been independently audited. These are necessary for the full lattice hardness claims; this is not a certification of every advertised theorem.

review.title: Coupling Independence Implies Zero-Freeness
review.authors: Shuai Shao; Ke Shi

checked: Checked the normalized-pinning convention and why the only removed zero factor is z^(number of monochromatic pinned edges).
Traced the complex-average stability setup: center h, interpolate under an optimal coupling, retain |M−1|≤exp(1/4)−1, and bound |M′/M| by less than 2(A E d+2γ).

Checked the complete new coupling-independence-to-zero-freeness transfer (PDF pp11–18). A single coupling bounds the sum of shell Wasserstein costs, allowing a shell with cost C/L. Pinning the shell makes the exterior independent of the root color, and the smaller-instance response bound controls differences of its analytic logarithms along Hamming paths. The complex-average estimate then contracts the response budget and an open-half-plane argument gives parent nonvanishing.

Checked the hard endpoint separately, including one-vertex comparison ≤q^Δ by greedy list-coloring of the first shell. The non-hard-feasible terms carry a factor z; exterior ratios are bounded by iterated one-vertex comparisons, so their total error is O(|z|) relative to a fixed feasible shell contribution, uniformly in graph size. The hard-feasible parent terms have positive real part and dominate that error. Joining this disc to the compact positive-activity interval is valid.
remaining: Scoped review of the 42-page paper: the general transfer theorem and its zero endpoint are checked in full, but the separate soft-flip coupling and its 11Δ/6 numerical case analysis on pp19–27 are not fully audited, nor is the imported equality-case coupling bound independently checked. score_reasons.exposition: Gadget indices, boundary conventions and the remaining 8-bead gap are unusually explicit.

checked: Traced the complete central PureCircuit reduction: a majority home block forces exactly one cut; its position is b−s+S or b−S according to orientation.

Checked the designated segment yields garbage only at S=κ and otherwise the threshold [S<κ]. NOR uses four sensor beads and b≥5; non-purification uses three beads and thresholds 1,2, so at most one output is garbage; duplicate-bead NOT completes PURIFY.
Verified the unique output-host condition, polynomial construction, all 10-bead budgets and robustness for pure inputs.
Checked K disjoint copies with K>(Kn₀)^(1−δ) force an exact-cut copy under the allowed extra cuts.

papers.title: PIT and Reconstruction for Sums of High Powers
papers.authors: Amir Shpilka, Nimrod Kaplan, Yann Tal

review.title: PIT and Reconstruction for Sums of High Powers
review.authors: Nimrod Kaplan, Amir Shpilka, Yann Tal
review.summary: For sums of r powers of inner degree-Δ polynomials, lifts an inner interpolating set of size s to a hitting set of size (s−1)Δd+1 when d+1≥(r−1)², in characteristic zero or sufficiently large characteristic. Proper reconstruction at d>(r+1)^4Δ and an individual-degree variant yield deterministic reconstruction and PIT for several sparse, roABP and shallow-circuit families.
review.prior_frontier: Extends an earlier sparse-polynomial manuscript; differs from a companion border-power paper by proper high-power reconstruction and different model and characteristic coverage.

score_reasons.significance: A reusable deterministic lifting framework with applications across several restricted circuit models.
score_reasons.novelty: Polynomial ABC supplies independence of high powers; canonical differential operators and robust anchors enable reconstruction.
score_reasons.depth: Wronskian uniqueness, factor-search pruning and coordinate hybrids are substantial new machinery.
score_reasons.exposition: Thresholds, proper versus nonproper outputs, and overlap with companion work are explicit.

checked: Checked the PIT curve restriction: an interpolating set preserves nonassociation, ABC guarantees the restricted sum is nonzero, and univariate degree bounds give the stated set size. Read the Wronskian reconstruction and robust-hybrid roadmap.

Checked the univariate reconstruction core, PDF pp15–28, conditional on the stated function-field ABC theorem. The ordinary-derivative Wronskian/ODE kernel argument correctly requires characteristic above the degree bound. A primitive minimal-leading-degree annihilator is unique: bounded-degree coefficient relations among the high powers force each summand to vanish, and subtracting two order-r operators gives an impossible lower-order annihilator.

Checked root multiplicity recovery and the pruned DFS. High multiplicity at a root forces it into a base polynomial; applying this to the quotient family makes divisibility subspaces exactly spans of compatible power terms. Each recursive leaf discovers a previously unknown term, there are at most r leaves and depth at most Δ, so the apparent exponential factor-exponent tree is traversed in polynomially many nodes. The constant-term test and one-dimensional leaves return actual powers, not arbitrary kernel elements.
remaining: Scoped large-proof audit of a 78-page manuscript: the univariate reconstruction and basic curve-restriction PIT argument are checked conditional on the cited ABC interface. The claimed extension of that dependency to large positive characteristic has not been independently verified from its source. Robust multivariate lifting, hybrid reconstruction, all roABP/bounded-depth/bounded-read applications, and rational bit-complexity bounds remain unaudited. Finite-field deterministic factoring is polynomial in the characteristic p, not merely log p.

score_reasons.novelty: Truncated inclusion–exclusion handles incompatible representations instead of excluding all of them.
score_reasons.depth: Counting circuits, support-sensitive layouts and exact rational exponent certificates.

papers.title: Testing Fourier Sparsity Near Optimally

review.title: Testing Fourier Sparsity Near Optimally
review.authors: Arijit Ghosh; Manmatha Roy
review.summary: Nonadaptive Boolean Fourier-sparsity testing with O(s log³(2s)/ε) membership queries; distribution-free testing has the same query bound plus O(1/ε) samples from the unknown distribution. Guarantees concern query complexity.
review.prior_frontier: Narrows prior Õ(s^4/ε^4) upper bounds to nearly linear sparsity dependence, compared with Ω(s) and Ω(1/ε) lower bounds.

score_reasons.significance: Essentially closes a long polynomial query-complexity gap and extends to distribution-free access.
score_reasons.novelty: Fourier-domain self-correction enforces magnitude, character and additive consistency across affine restrictions.
score_reasons.depth: Must recover a globally sparse Boolean function from approximate spectral identities and shared samples.
score_reasons.exposition: A query-inefficient transparent tester precedes the compressed implementation.

checked: Checked the complete new proof, PDF pp8–23. The injective projection on S and S+S preserves both support and four-term identities. For an arbitrary fixed restriction space, the whole-vector majority vote has mass at least1−2ρ at every shift: two independent votes agree whenever two uniform consistency tests pass.

Checked exact character correction using four majority events and 8ρ<1, followed by Fourier reconstruction. The critical Boolean step is valid: a correct vote forces equality in Cauchy–Schwarz, hence exact common supports and coefficient magnitudes; additive consistency then makes every nonzero Fourier coefficient of the square vanish. This yields one globally Boolean s-sparse function, not merely sparse restrictions.

Checked shared-sample recovery and canonical coset representatives. They define a fixed Boolean surrogate even for a bad recovery sample. Uniform soundness follows from ε≤dist(f,surrogate)+8p_H(surrogate)≤9Pr[round rejects], and independent rounds remain independent conditional on that fixed surrogate. No union bound over exponentially many cosets is needed.

Checked distribution-free correction at every fixed target x. The single sparse corrected function is recovered with probability at least1−2ρ over a fresh uniform helper. Averaging this pointwise statement over arbitrary D gives rejection at least3ε/4 when ρ<1/8; otherwise structural rejection is at least1/8. Shared helper randomness requires containment, not independence, of the rejection events.

Verified the exact sparse-recovery dependency statements: Haviv–Regev Theorem1.1 applies to every flat unitary matrix, hence Walsh–Hadamard, with O(s log²s log N) independently sampled rows; Cai–Zhang arXiv1302.1236v1 Theorem3.1 gives exact ℓ1 recovery under δ_k<1/3 for k≥2. The manuscript pads the sparsity parameter to handle the small-k case. Query count and nonadaptivity, including D-samples chosen before answers, are correct.
remaining: The classical RIP and ℓ1-recovery theorems are used as verified external interfaces, not independently reproved. No implementation or numerical experiment was run; the claim is query complexity rather than a near-linear running-time algorithm.

sources.detail: Haviv–Regev Theorem1.1 and precise probability interface.
Cai–Zhang Theorem3.1; k≥2 and δ_k<1/3 checked.

review.prior_frontier: Unifies subexponential algorithms beyond ordinary minor-free classes. Uses a repaired external induced-minor separator theorem, explicitly distinguishing earlier flawed proofs; that repair was not independently verified.

score_reasons.significance: Provides a broad deletion and approximation framework covering several previously separate geometric graph problems.
score_reasons.novelty: A bounded-degeneracy small core replaces dense forbidden-subgraph branching and supports separator recursion.
score_reasons.depth: Interlocks core construction, induced-minor separators, torso edge control and logical dynamic programming.
score_reasons.exposition: States fixed-parameter and hereditary-target restrictions and identifies the repaired separator dependency.

checked: Traced connected-subtree decomposition, first-excess-neighborhood extraction and disjoint-region closure with two-bag boundaries.

Checked the central branching coverage: among |M|+k disjoint connected pieces, k deletions leave |M| intact; contracting them gives a treewidth-t graph on ≤2|M| vertices, hence some piece retains ≤2t core neighbors.
Verified this yields a solution-consistent branch deleting at least d−2t vertices, depth k/(d−2t)+1, and branching factor (k log t)^O(t).
Checked union-of-core invariants and LCA closure size.
remaining: External repaired separator, degeneracy branching subroutine, final torso-size analysis, MSO DP and QPTAS reduction remain unaudited.

review.title: Constant-Factor Approximation for Generalized Max–Min Degree Arborescence in Quasi-Polynomial Time
review.authors: Wenzheng Li
review.summary: Rounds a generalized weighted path LP of degree K to value at least K/2^17−δ, where δ is the largest edge weight. Gives a 2^19-approximation for unweighted MMDA/GMMDA in expected n^{O(log n)} time and a constant expected-polynomial approximation for restricted submodular Santa Claus.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the prior (log log n)^{O(1)} quasipolynomial MMDA ratio and O(log log n) restricted-submodular Santa Claus ratio to constants; does not settle general Santa Claus.

score_reasons.significance: Crosses constant-factor barriers in two recognized fair-allocation settings.
score_reasons.novelty: Potential-based single-source cost rounding plus directed-loss partial resampling handles dependent arborescences.
score_reasons.depth: Multiscale congestion and pruning require substantial additional analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Distinguishes weighted additive losses and graph-size versus LP-size running time.

checked: Checked available-child potential accounting and 8/(9d) selected-subtree cost bound. Checked weighted star selection: capped q/θ weights hit every bad event and inflation two gives activity at most four times expected two-way loss/θ.

Checked weighted configuration rounding (PDF pp21–23), conditional on the stated partial-resampling theorem. Weighted dependent rounding preserves marginals and loses at most one item; preliminary sampling rateα=1/16 makes two-way conflict loss at mostα²T while retained value isαT−δ. Assigning each resource to its highest-valued selected configuration yields T/32−δ.

Checked dyadic sparse-tree selection and the logarithmic-height rounding (pp24–27). The path-product potential bounds pruning loss at every retained parent. Competing occurrence probability γ^m combines with expected charge16^h on [m,2m), whose geometric sum is below1/15; weighted-star resampling therefore keeps each root potential below1. The final ordered-slot rounding loses at most one maximum edge weight, and source-reachable retention preserves assignments.
remaining: Scoped review of the 46-page manuscript: the new weighted configuration/star rounding and dyadic sparse-tree argument have substantial checked proofs, but the multiscale congestion reduction needed to remove the logarithmic height loss (pp35–43), weighted single-source construction (pp28–34), and height-reduction interface remain unaudited. The Harris–Srinivasan resampling theorem and Bamas–Garg–Rohwedder submodular reduction are used conditionally, not independently reverified. The full headline constant approximation is therefore not completely checked.

papers.title: Interior Point Methods Solve Random LPs in polylog(n) iterations

review.title: Interior Point Methods Solve Random LPs in polylog(n) iterations
review.authors: Daniel Dadush, Shunhua Jiang, Rasmus Kyng, Haoyuan Ma
review.summary: An interior-point method solves min{1^T x:Ax=A1,x≥0} for Gaussian d×n matrices with cn≤d≤(1−c)n in O(log^{6.5} n) linear-system iterations with high probability, returning exact primal/dual optima in the real-RAM model.
review.prior_frontier: Replaces polynomial-in-n rigorous bounds for this random-LP model by polylogarithmic iterations; does not improve worst-case LP or establish bit complexity.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves a longstanding random-IPM iteration question.
score_reasons.novelty: Conditions on central-path points, controls nonuniform conditional subspace density and Gaussian projections.
score_reasons.depth: Coarea formula, matrix resolvents and central-path rounding.
score_reasons.exposition: Random-instance and real-RAM restrictions are explicit.

checked: Checked derivative/divergence identities Lemma4.3 using d(M^-k)=−ΣM^-j(dM)M^{-(k+1−j)}; spectral-moment inequalities Lemma4.4 follow from normalized eigenvalues.
Checked independent-sign projection bound and inspected the essential distinction between actual conditional central-path measure and uniform constrained subspace measure.

Checked the full central-path conditional-law and determinant-tilt transfer calculation (PDF pp61–67). In Grassmann tangent coordinates the path-map derivative sees precisely the first row/column, and the hyperplane-volume correction cancels the apparent extra normal factor. Coarea therefore weights the reference fiber by det(VᵀD_xV), rather than treating the conditioned subspace as uniform.

Checked the second-moment bound for that density. Cauchy–Binet expresses the normalized determinant as a convex combination of squared Haar minors; Gaussian polar decomposition makes the frame independent of the Gram matrix, and chi-square product moments give the displayed (k+1)(k+2)(m−k+1)(m−k+2)/(2(m+1)(m+2)) bound. Cauchy–Schwarz then transfers a reference failure probability p to at most n√p under the actual conditioned law.
remaining: Scoped audit of an 86-page paper: the critical conditional-law correction and its probability transfer are checked, alongside the derivative identities recorded earlier. The long Gaussian projection narrow/wide-window analysis, quantitative uniform discretization of the entire central path, optimal-basis identification, and full smoothed-IPM iteration argument remain independently unchecked. Thus the advertised polylogarithmic iteration bound has not been completely verified.
resolved_notes: Several cross-references in the final transfer proof on p67 render as “??”; the intended statement and the proved density inequality are identifiable, but references should be repaired.

review.summary: For arbitrary edge arrivals forming a forest, achieves optimal 4/7 randomized matching against an oblivious adversary and deterministic 4/7 fractional matching with 7/4 fractional cover. The matching lower bound holds even for growing degree-four trees.
review.prior_frontier: Improves 5/9 matching and 11/6 fractional-cover guarantees and matches the matching impossibility bound.

score_reasons.significance: Settles a clean online-matching special case with exact constants.
score_reasons.novelty: A piecewise cover potential survives capping fractional weights by independent endpoint availability.
score_reasons.depth: Primal-dual component surplus and a tight adversarial tree construction.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit algorithms identify the rounding obstruction and the necessary cap.

checked: Verified Lemma 8: new edges join independent components, deterministic loads equal matching marginals, and accepting with x/((1−a)(1−b)) realizes each capped edge weight.
Checked Lemma 9’s two affine lower bounds on cψ and its a≤1/2 versus a≥1/2 algebra, conditional on the stated cover function.

review.title: Adaptive Data Analysis Beyond the Privacy Barrier
review.authors: Florian E. Dorner, Moritz Hardt
review.summary: A deterministic leaderboard mechanism achieves O((log m)^(3/2)√(log(2kn/β)/n)) error, m=min(k,n)+1. A shifted-model reduction answers Ω(√n/log²n) adaptive statistical queries with O(log²n/√n) population error, separating population accuracy from simultaneous empirical accuracy.
review.prior_frontier: Improves the privacy-based leaderboard accuracy frontier and contradicts a proposed √k/α² population-only sample lower bound in the k≈1/α regime; does not answer arbitrary numbers of queries at this precision. Prior lower-bound sources not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Changes the known attainable population-accuracy frontier and the role of privacy/sample accuracy in adaptive analysis.
score_reasons.novelty: A deterministic correction cascade combines sparse transcripts with an empirical kernel potential rather than privatizing answers.
score_reasons.depth: Requires coordinated correction-energy bounds, sample-dependent conditioning, exact transcript decoders and three simultaneous union bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: Algorithm and caps are explicit and the appendix gives decoders and numerical parameters, though the dependence structure requires careful reading.

checked: Traced the full central leaderboard proof: cascade telescoping, score quantization, correction caps and the quadratic energy increment >λ²/4 per recorded correction.
Verified reference-kernel matrix Chernoff domination, the fixed-list vector Bernstein/net bound and all matrix normalization inequalities.

Traced the conditional transcript decoder for hidden sample blocks, including hidden publication events and frozen processes; verified the global sample-independent transcript bound removes the reference-sample adaptivity issue.
Checked the three conditioning/union-bound stages, neighboring-process budget≤6Cᵢ, top-block budget one, λ²b=441log(60knh/β), and resulting h^(3/2)/√n accuracy.
Checked cap arithmetic, small-n trivial-answer branch and the stated 535 leading constant calculation. Inspected, but did not fully audit, the general-query reduction.
remaining: Appendix E shifted-model implementation, imported lower-bound hypotheses and the full population-versus-empirical impossibility corollary remain outside the main-proof audit. This is a human-readable proof audit, not formal verification.

papers.title: Tight bounds for fractional and randomized truthful scheduling
papers.authors: Georgios Anastasiadis, George Christodoulou, Elias Koutsoupias, Annamaria Kovacs, Conrad Schecker

review.title: Tight bounds for fractional and randomized truthful scheduling
review.authors: Georgios Anastasiadis, George Christodoulou, Elias Koutsoupias, Annamária Kovács, Conrad Schecker
review.summary: Every truthful fractional mechanism on n unrelated machines has ratio at least (n+1)/2 against integral makespan, hence so does every truthful-in-expectation mechanism. A universally truthful mechanism attains (n+1)/2+O(√(n log n)). Arbitrarily many finite tasks are allowed.
review.prior_frontier: The first superconstant general randomized lower bound, replacing 2−1/n; fractional ratio becomes exactly (n+1)/2 and universal leading constant improves from about 0.837 to 1/2.

score_reasons.significance: Settles the leading randomized approximation threshold in a foundational mechanism-design problem.
score_reasons.novelty: Symmetrized reservoir limits and within-parallel-class additivity replace task-independence assumptions.
score_reasons.depth: Two-task separation, discontinuity removal and finite-witness transfer carry the main burden.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise truthfulness classes and integral benchmark; technical limiting arguments require close audit.

checked: Traced fixed-star retention expansion with nonnegative binomial coefficients, root averaging, self-loop weak monotonicity and limit ratio. Checked selection of a common leaf value outside countably many monotone discontinuities and extension from rational own types by Lipschitz continuity.

Checked the complete new lower-bound argument and padding construction. Averaging over reservoir counts changes other-task allocations by at most4/(K+1), while many identical zero-type tasks force allocation to their zero-cost endpoint. Rational diagonal limits, then a Tychonoff subnet of coordinatewise rounding, preserve all incentive inequalities and give the real-domain limit; strict ratio violations transfer back to a finite positive-optimum input.

Checked two-task separation in full. Complementary truthful allocations give ∂_t A=−∂_s B; zero-type irrelevance makes boundary terms vanish. Two distinct Laplace-rate ratios force both transforms to zero, and the supplied polynomial-density proof establishes uniqueness. Without assumed measurability, monotonicity in opposing values supplies Borel versions agreeing for all own values outside one null set. A common diagonal continuity point avoids all countably many exceptional rational-input choices; Lipschitz extension then gives the full-class additivity used in the star proof.

Checked the universal upper bound. For fixed exponentials the bounded-square allocation is monotone even when lowering a bid changes eligibility. Its inverse-square probabilities give expected machine load≤(n+1)OPT/2; independently assigned bounded jobs satisfy Σ_j(t_j^min)^2≤n OPT², so Hoeffding and the deterministic2n OPT maximum yield the claimed O(√(n log n)) additive ratio. Zero processing times are handled explicitly.
remaining: The main new proofs and supplied technical appendices are checked. Standard incentive-envelope facts and Hoeffding concentration are used as standard mathematical dependencies, not rederived from first principles; no mechanism implementation was run.

papers.title: A Nearly Linear-Time FPRAS for Counting Knapsack
papers.authors: Ce Jin, Jaewoo Park, Barna Saha

review.title: A Nearly Linear-Time FPRAS for Counting Knapsack
review.authors: Ce Jin, Jaewoo Park, Barna Saha
review.summary: FPRAS for counting nonnegative-weight subsets below a threshold in soft-O(n/ε²) word-RAM time, with word length O(log(n/ε)+log T), success probability at least2/3.
review.prior_frontier: Improves soft-O(n^{3/2}/ε²) FPRAS; deterministic near-linear counting remains open.

score_reasons.significance: Achieves nearly input-linear randomized approximate knapsack counting.
score_reasons.novelty: Exponential tilting controls FFT precision and supports batched candidate sampling.
score_reasons.depth: Multi-scale rounded counting tables and numerical implementation.
score_reasons.exposition: Separates probabilistic table errors and numeric precision.

checked: Checked exponential-tilt transition argument: at feasibility probability1/2, independent product samples have an infeasible-to-feasible hybrid transition with probability1/4; ≤n|Ω| possible transitions each of mass≤1/C implies C≤4n|Ω|.
Checked derivative of log tilted partition function and its relation to expected selected weight.

Checked the random-shift rounding and normalized convolution core (PDF pp28–30,36–38). Each shift is conditionally unbiased even when its input depends on earlier shifts. The sum of squared spacings is O(S²log B), so the martingale MGF bound controls every fixed subset. Averaging exp(−λ error) over the tilted product distribution bounds total exact table mass; Markov plus a union bound makes the numerical mass assumptions simultaneous without a union bound over subsets.

Checked the candidate-family rounding-error and excess-layer arguments (pp42–44), conditional on the local table and popular-weight lemmas. Near-feasible subsets fail with exponentially small individual probability; Markov controls their total count. For excess layer d≥2, entry into the candidate set needs downward error Ω(dT/ℓ), whose exponentially small tail dominates the n^d growth of that layer.

Checked the batched sampling primitives (pp47–49). Independent affine F₂ seeds give pairwise-independent uniform subsets and a Walsh–Hadamard transform computes all weight sums. Uniform add/remove repair preserves the uniform fixed-cardinality law by symmetry, and negative-hypergeometric stopping time gives expected cost O~(√M+|k−M/2|+1), rather than scanning all items.
remaining: Scoped large-proof audit of the 63-page algorithm: substantial central rounding, table-mass and sampling primitives have been checked. The fine-stage local table construction, exact total table-size estimates, final light/heavy repair composition and variance/runtime accounting, and the numerical precision appendix remain independently unchecked. Consequently the full near-linear ε-dependent FPRAS running time is not certified by this review; no implementation was executed.

score_reasons.novelty: Compiles multipartite nonlocal separations against restricted quantum-resource players.

checked: Checked the round lower bound: with at most k rounds a prover permitted k calls can execute the entire honest quantum action once per round.

checked: Checked the local-query/no-Jump model and known-versus-unknown-n distinction.
Traced geometric decay of nonfrozen residual under pushing at least half the active mass.
Inspected the freezing charge and found that Eq(12) excludes the residue already held at the newly frozen vertex.

issues: PDF p18 Eq(12) bounds final r_f(u) by nonfrozen mass at time ℓ_u+L_f, although u is already frozen and its current residual is excluded. review.title: Optimal Semi-Honest Information-Theoretic Secure Multi-Party Computation with Servers and Erasures
review.authors: Wonseok Choi
review.summary: In the private point-to-point client/server model with prescribed erasures, implements ℓ oblivious transfers against passive rushing adaptive corruption of one client and αn servers, for fixed α<1/2, with Oα(ℓ+λ) communicated bits in expectation and with high probability and O(2^−λ) error/abort. A separate protocol bounds worst-case communication; a message lower bound is also claimed.
review.prior_frontier: Claims to refute the earlier 1−1/√2 erasure-model threshold by identifying servers omitted from a server–server-edge emulation. The old proof has not yet been independently compared.

score_reasons.significance: Would change the feasibility threshold and communication landscape for adaptive server-aided OT.
score_reasons.novelty: Uses hidden volunteer identities, erasures and weak-random-OT amplification rather than a revealed committee.
score_reasons.depth: Adaptive relabeling, complete-view simulation and signed reconstruction lower bounds are demanding.
score_reasons.exposition: Careful detailed simulators, but informal constant-MPC language requires circuit-size and communication-model qualification.

checked: Checked revelation-flag common/residual decomposition and its sequential conditional-independence requirement. Read Protocol 3 Alice leakage bound, current-state erasure simulation and Bob unmatched-bit masking argument.

Checked the adaptive-exposure simulator lemma (PDF pp18–21): a uniform fixed-size exposed set followed by random ordering of it and its complement is a uniform full ordering. The map from these orderings to adaptively assigned server labels is bijective even with overlapping pools, provided the stated conditional row-label exchangeability and erasure conditions hold. The hidden-half leakage calculation includes both direct exposure and imbalance among remaining candidates.

Checked Protocol3’s accepted-trial distribution and its fixed-corrupted-client simulation (pp33–40). Conditioning on exactly one volunteer outside the requested tuple and distinct tags leaves participant labels exchangeable; the two parity outputs stay independent of the unmatched position. For Alice, unseen request status is erased before tagged messages; for Bob, the unmatched bit is erased before selection/tags are announced. The conditional uniform-label hypotheses of the adaptive-exposure lemma therefore match the simulator at the stated phase boundaries. The uniform exposure bounds give the displayed p_A and p_B, and the accepted-trial Chernoff and communication calculations are consistent.
remaining: Scoped review of the 57-page security proof: Protocol3’s wROT core against either fixed corrupted client and the adaptive server-exposure reduction are checked in the prescribed private-channel, passive-corruption, phased-erasure model. Protocols1–2, amplification into full OT, adaptive client corruption, the UC-composition appendix, and the lower-bound reconstruction argument are not fully audited. Therefore the overall optimal MPC/UC claims remain only partially checked.
resolved_notes: Constant communication fixes the security parameter and OT/circuit size. Constant circuit depth alone does not bound circuit size; informal MPC corollary should not be read as a bound independent of circuit size. Communication counts protocol bits on addressed private channels.

review.summary: Tensor products of capacity-achieving classical code families retain erasure capacity under error-decay/minimum-distance conditions. checked: Checked the complete new classical nullity comparison and tensor-capacity argument (Lemmas6/13, Theorem7 and Corollary8), plus the dual-tensor rank-nullity transfer and sprinkling proof of Theorem15. For the union over small weights in Lemma14, use support sizes w/(kappa n) uniformly for w<=n^{2-nu/4}; their intersection is smaller than w and the number of choices is exp(o(n)), giving the required uniform bound.

Checked quantum rate algebra, local erasure Gaussian elimination, residual-weight threshold, and linear runtime for fixed local size. Identified and supplied a necessary conditioning repair to the displayed p29 argument: an ensemble-average local failure bound does not give independent block failures. Use Markov at rho+epsilon/24 and Theorem15 to choose, with probability tending to1 as Delta grows, fixed local codes whose two needed failure probabilities are <=1/2, simultaneously with distance/product-expansion properties. Then apply Theorem11 at the smaller target rho to each fixed code and use Chernoff only over independent erasures on disjoint views. The p29 display must use this smaller erasure rate.

The above fixed-code choice removes the shared-code dependence from the Chernoff step and preserves the asserted existential family statement. It does not certify the unexamined Tanner-decoder extension.

review.title: Sharp Limits of Graph-Based Nearest Neighbor Search on the Sphere
review.authors: Kejing Lu
review.summary: For iid uniform spherical data and exact greedy search from every entry for most independent queries, identifies a sharp degree exponent: β*(c)=(c/2)log(2−e^{−2/c}) when d=c log n, and degree 2^{d/2+o(d)} when √log n≪d≪log n. Extends to specified nonuniform local-density classes and quantifies fresh-start evaluation tradeoffs.
review.prior_frontier: Earlier work analyzed particular graph constructions and prescribed starts; here lower bounds allow graphs chosen after observing all data. These are distributional graph-navigation bounds, not unrestricted nearest-neighbor data-structure lower bounds.

score_reasons.significance: Sharp intrinsic limits for an important graph-search abstraction.
score_reasons.novelty: A rank-window trap argument handles arbitrary sample-dependent neighbor lists.
score_reasons.depth: Uniform geometric large deviations and restart exploration bounds are substantial.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit every-entry, query-measure and scan-cost conventions; nonuniform hypotheses are lengthy.

checked: Checked trap decomposition into atypical ranks, any near improving data point, and far stored edges. The far-edge direction bound holds for each fixed data set/list, avoiding a union bound over all constructed graphs.
remaining: Complete uniform progress and geometry estimates, simultaneous trap conclusion, nonuniform density construction and adaptive restart lower bounds.

papers.title: A Dichotomy for Constrained Eulerian Orientations
papers.authors: Jincheng Guan, Shuai Shao, Ke Shi

review.title: A Dichotomy for Constrained Eulerian Orientations
review.authors: Jincheng Guan, Shuai Shao, Ke Shi
review.summary: Classifies fixed finite Boolean constrained Eulerian-orientation languages into P or NP-complete; tractable branches include Δ-matroids, always-YES languages and one-sided minority/majority promise polymorphisms. General graph orientations with both pins retain unresolved Δ-matroid parity cases.
review.prior_frontier: Extends the counting-EO promise method to decision majority and supplies a complete EO decision classification, not a complete unrestricted graph-orientation classification.

score_reasons.significance: A complete tractability boundary for balanced local orientation constraints.
score_reasons.novelty: LP feasible supports recover ordinary affine/bijunctive closure from one-sided promises.
score_reasons.depth: Nonconstructive unsatisfiable-gadget reduction and algebraic obstruction analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly isolates the unresolved general-orientation branch.

checked: Checked full new LP tractability argument: edge signed marginals cancel, cubing preserves cancellation, one-sided imbalance forces zero mass on forbidden outputs, and majority/minority transformations preserve edge equations as odd marginal functions.
Averaging witness LPs proves support closure; bounded-arity affine equations or all valid binary clauses yield Gaussian elimination/2-SAT.
remaining: Hardness gadgets and reduction to Schaefer, always-YES characterization, Δ-matroid and general-orientation dependency interfaces.

review.title: Optimal (Randomized) Compact Routing Schemes
review.authors: Shiri Chechik; Avi Kadria; Gur Lifshitz; Liam Roditty
review.summary: Labeled compact routing achieves expected stretch 2k−1 with Õ(n^(1/k)) average local storage, Õ(k)-word labels and Õ(1)-word headers; only routing is randomized. Also improves deterministic, worst-case-storage and name-independent tradeoffs, including (8k/3+6,4k/9) expected stretch for unweighted worst-case storage.
review.prior_frontier: Claims optimal expected average-storage stretch under the girth-conjecture lower bound; improves deterministic average coefficient ≈2.64 to ≈2.47 and worst-case unweighted coefficients below previous ≈3.68.

score_reasons.significance: A simultaneous advance across the main compact-routing models, including an optimal leading tradeoff.
score_reasons.novelty: A source-level minimax LP randomizes hierarchical routing choices.
score_reasons.depth: Routing feasibility and storage must coexist with tight analytic level-selection bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: The table distinguishes expected stretch, additive errors and average versus worst-case space.

checked: Checked reduction of the worst distance to finitely many thresholds: piecewise-constant extra-cost numerators divided by d are maximal at interval left endpoints.
Verified how z*≤2τ in the level LP implies expected total stretch 2k−1, conditional on the routing/storage lemmas.

Checked the complete central average-storage expected-stretch argument (PDF 11–14, 35–37): bunch/cluster duality pays total table size; every walked vertex has its own tree label, so fallback and rerouting are implementable. Failure at level i gives d≥h_(i+1)(v)−h_i(u), reducing the worst-distance LP to O(k) thresholds.

Verified the LP dual analytically: reweight distance probabilities by 1/θ, express tail constraints through the quantile f, set φ=1−r+r f and Ψ(z)=∫1/φ. The two-step recurrence bounds Ψ(rH)≤τ; ∫φ≤rHm and Cauchy–Schwarz imply C≤2τm, hence z*≤2τ and expected stretch ≤2k−1.
remaining: Scoped exception for the 63-page multi-model paper: the central randomized average-storage theorem is checked conditional on the standard hierarchical bunch and tree-label interfaces. Their external constructions were not independently reconstructed.
The deterministic sharper constants, worst-case local storage, weighted and name-independent conversions remain unchecked; source computation is unrestricted.

review.authors: Shi Fu, Qixin Zhang, Dacheng Tao
review.summary: For monotone cardinality-constrained consistent maximization, proves the sharp polynomial-query/constant-worst-case-recourse threshold 2−√2: expected approximation β−ε at each fixed time with O(ε^−2) recourse; any improvement needs exponential pre-final queries or Ω(k) final changes. Coverage attains 1−1/e−ε with O(ε^−1) recourse, and bounded curvature has a matching interpolated threshold.
review.prior_frontier: Improves 0.51 to≈0.5858 for general functions, below offline1−1/e and unrestricted-query2/3. Stores the full arrival history and permits arbitrary subsets in current value queries; no streaming-memory claim.

score_reasons.significance: Identifies an exact computational-stability frontier and separates coverage from general submodularity.
score_reasons.novelty: Anchored sampling turns current greedy certificates into a future-uniform two-action LP; exact hiding forces costly repair.
score_reasons.depth: Combines finite-grid supporting-line geometry, checkpoint migration, hidden partitions and curvature-preserving augmentation.
score_reasons.exposition: The oracle, per-time expectation and worst-case random-outcome recourse quantifiers are explicit.

checked: Traced the full robust-core argument: submodular anchored interpolation, current value/residual certificates, LP duality and two-action support.
Verified a supporting line c+dt bounds greedy values and derivative from opposite directions, forcing (1−γ)²≤2cd≤γ²/2 and hence γ≥2−√2.
Checked the critical point lies in [0,2], and B=ceil(3/ε) converts the stated checkpoint factor into β−ε with O(ε^−2) recourse.
remaining: Checkpoint correctness, exact hidden-partition submodularity and adaptive query lower bound, coverage migration and bounded-curvature extensions remain unaudited.

sources.detail: Sharp theorem with precise query/recourse quantifiers
Sharp inequality and finite lower bound

review.authors: Ishan Chakraborty, Sobyasachi Chatterjee, Madhumita Kundu, Gopinath Mishra
review.summary: One insertion-only pass over distinct edges, with known n,Δ,k and an oblivious stream, finds a promised (Δ−k)-colouring using Õ(nk) bits throughout, for every 1≤k<Δ. Postprocessing is exhaustive and has no polynomial-time guarantee.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves the stated n poly(k,log n)-space question; matches known lower bounds up to logarithms for k<(Δ−1)/2. Repeated-edge streams require substantially more space.

score_reasons.significance: Optimal-space extension from saving one colour to arbitrary k.
score_reasons.novelty: Kernelization-inspired near-twin compression complements Molloy–Reed dense-piece structure.
score_reasons.depth: Two degree regimes, sparse recovery and palette preservation require lengthy analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: The promise, distinct-edge model and unrestricted time are stated conspicuously.

checked: Checked storage amortization and reconstruction of every edge incident to a removed vertex, including same-group pairs. Read the remainder dichotomy proof via nonedge counts and near-twin symmetric differences.
remaining: Streaming sketch recovery under adaptive removals, palette-extension probabilities, dense-piece transformations and complete workspace accounting.

review.title: Classical Verification of Quantum Sampling with Negligible Error
review.authors: Kai-Min Chung, Alexandru Cojocaru, Yi Lee, Han-Hsuan Lin
review.summary: Classical-verifier single-prover sampling verification with negligible computational error under subexponentially quantum-secure classical-client QFHE; information-theoretic precursor uses finite-set single-qubit preparation.
review.prior_frontier: Strengthens inverse-polynomial-error sampling verification, under a stronger stated encryption assumption; output security is abort-inclusive, not unqualified conditional-on-rare-acceptance closeness.

score_reasons.significance: Addresses negligible-error verification of full quantum output distributions.
score_reasons.novelty: Iterative partial Pauli twirling and authenticated resource distillation.
score_reasons.depth: 192-page coherent attack and remote-state-preparation composition.
score_reasons.exposition: Formal abort-inclusive guarantee is clearer than introductory conditional-on-acceptance wording.

checked: Checked the distinction between subnormalized accepted output and normalized conditional output: the formal guarantee compares L(Y) with pP_C+(1−p)δ_reject. It implies conditional error only after dividing by p.
Inspected round-by-round trap-copy invariant and retained subnormalized attack branches; checked the simple CNOT partial-twirling example and CSS low-weight accepted-error property.

Checked the coherent one-bad-input distillation reduction (PDF 73–76): two compatible stabilizer restrictions determine the surviving Pauli up to a stabilizer; every accepted Pauli summand has the same surviving ray. Its accepted Kraus maps have rank one, so the claim extends to coherent superpositions and arbitrary references without treating Pauli coefficients as probabilities.

Checked correlated-family closure (PDF 77–81): partial matrix elements of ∑Bα†Bα⊗Cα†Cα≤I preserve the full trace-nonincreasing family after accepted block maps. Refinement amplitudes can be absorbed into remaining bad factors; a bad parent requires ≥2 bad children, so potential ∑2^height implies at least 2^ℓ bad leaves. Key uniformity is used only in the reference representation, not after arbitrary ciphertext conditioning.
remaining: Scoped exception for a 192-page security proof. The checked local distillation theorem is conditional on the preceding twirled/factorizable invariant and Pauli-propagation interfaces, which were not fully independently verified.

The global MBQC invariant, CCZ distillation, computational RSP source interface, signed cross-term composition, all branch-weight budgets and final negligible-error parameterization remain unchecked. This is not a complete security certification.

review.title: Breaking the Graph-Size Barrier for Tree Vertex Sparsifiers in Near-Linear Time
review.authors: Daniel Agassy; Dani Dorfman; Haim Kaplan
review.summary: Randomized near-linear-time construction of an O(k)-vertex hierarchical tree preserving every terminal cut within O(log²k log log k), hence all terminal multicommodity congestion within O(log³k log log k), for arbitrary capacitated undirected graphs.
review.prior_frontier: Removes ambient n from the quality of near-linear-time tree vertex sparsifiers, answering the stated RST question.

score_reasons.significance: A major terminal-sensitive improvement in fast cut/flow sparsification.
score_reasons.novelty: Support-sensitive balanced cuts and routing between vertex measures replace ambient-size expansion losses.
score_reasons.depth: Hierarchical merging, boundary charging and fair-cut flows must preserve simultaneous terminal guarantees.
score_reasons.exposition: Precisely states graph-size versus terminal-size dependence and the extra flow-cut factor.

checked: Verified Theorem 3.5’s expansion-transfer formulas from |μ(S)−ν(S)|≤ρ cap(S): expansion changes α→α/(1+αρ), and sparse-cut loss is φ/(1−ρφ) when ρφ<1.
Checked the boundary-expansion corollary using unit-congestion routing along half-edges.

Checked terminal-charged merge Lemma 4.6 (PDF 20–22), conditional on balanced-cut/routing interface: balanced cuts remove Ω(1/log k) capacity; in the expanding-large-side case truncated flows reroute through cut-to-terminal routing, preserving O(1) charging and a dominated terminal measure. Recharging afresh prevents congestion accumulation.

Checked the final demand-state argument (PDF 40–43), conditional on merge/refinement interfaces: redistribution resets load to one, merge yields an absolute constant load, and the cut charges telescope along each endpoint's cluster chain. The logarithmic k_parent/k_child factors sum to O(log k), giving O(log²k log log k). Degree-two path contraction with minimum edge capacity preserves all terminal cuts.
remaining: Scoped exception for the 59-page paper: support-sensitive balanced cut Appendix A, refinement construction and boundary-routing interfaces were not fully verified; the central merge and final telescoping are checked conditional on them.
External fair-cut algorithm, capacity/bit-complexity dependence, and flow-cut-gap transfer were not independently reconstructed.

review.title: Elections, Fractional Dichromatic Number and Domination in Tournaments and Digraphs
review.authors: Paul Colinot, Alantha Newman
review.summary: Transfers undominated-election committee bounds to tournament domination, obtaining γ⁺(T)≤ceil(4.9109 χ_f(T)), improving an exponential dependence to linear. Also relates fractional dichromatic numbers of general digraphs to Condorcet-winning-set questions.
review.prior_frontier: The new main result is a reduction to existing committee bounds, not a new 4.9109 election bound. A secondary small-parameter theorem is false as written; the main linear transfer is unaffected.

score_reasons.significance: Resolves polynomial versus exponential dependence in a natural tournament structural question.
score_reasons.novelty: Weighted-prefix elections translate fractional acyclic covers into domination certificates.
score_reasons.depth: The central transfer is elegant and short; general-digraph equivalences add structural detail.
score_reasons.exposition: The main proof is transparent, but Theorem8 reverses a necessary inequality into a false sufficient condition.

checked: Traced the complete main transfer: any nondominated candidate belongs to fractional cover weight≥1 and thus beats the committee for election weight≥1/c; compare with the strict f/k guarantee.
Checked the committee theorem can use 4.9109 slightly above the stated 4.9108… constant.

Reproduced a counterexample to subsidiary Theorem8 using the Paley19 tournament: all 969 triples fail to dominate, and common out-neighborhoods have size4, so transitive sets have size≤6 and χ_f≥19/6.
remaining: General-digraph equivalence and other local-to-global extensions remain unaudited; Theorem8 needs a corrected hypothesis/conclusion.
issues: Theorem8 p5 asserts 1/c≤1−(k−1)k^(−k/(k−1)) implies γ⁺≤k+1. For k=2 this covers c≥2, but Paley19 has χ_f≥19/6 and γ⁺≥4, violating γ⁺≤3. The proof derives a necessary inequality for k=γ⁺−1, not the stated implication. Main Theorem3 remains valid under its cited election bound.

review.title: Pure privacy for structured problems in polynomial time
review.authors: Hongjie Chen, Deepak Narayanan Sridharan, David Steurer
review.summary: Gives polynomial-time pure-DP algorithms whose privacy cost reflects intrinsic structure: balanced SBM weak recovery at every fixed parameter above Kesten–Stigum and every fixed ε>0; low-threshold-rank MaxCut; sparse Gaussian mean estimation; and list-decodable means.
review.prior_frontier: Claims first pure-DP weak recovery throughout the above-KS regime and improved intrinsic-dimension privacy costs; prior comparisons have not been independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Several important statistical/computational privacy gaps are addressed in one framework.
score_reasons.novelty: Random sketches with public decoding plus correlation-preserving amplification and pure-privacy extension.
score_reasons.depth: Convex sampling, SoS certificates, finite precision and multiple applications form a very large technical development.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit per-application hypotheses; the 307-page scope requires a carefully bounded audit.

checked: Fully checked Lemma 5.1: the dominating-reference mixture has log-density derivative bounded by s, including the certified/noncertified boundary; its TV loss is at most R exp(−s depth). Read the exact SBM and MaxCut parameter statements.

Fully checked the generic smoothing/flattening amplification Lemmas 4.1–4.2 (PDF 24–28): q^θ changes privacy to 2θε0; Gaussian norm control follows from Jensen's normalization lower bound. Good directional mixtures stochastically dominate N(a,σ²/(θn)); the density ratio of bad to good components is bounded on the controlled ball. With θ=α/2 and σ=16/√θ·max(1,n/log(1/β)), this yields exactly c0=1/256 and c1=1/8192.
Checked the sketch-and-decode composition lemma (PDF 23), including the essential uniformity over witnesses that may depend on the public random sketch.
remaining: Scoped exception for a 307-page paper: two substantive generic analytic mechanisms (amplification and dominating-reference extension) are checked, but this does not verify the application theorems.
Efficient implementation of flattened sampling, finite precision, stable certification, uniform recovery interfaces, and the SBM/MaxCut/sparse-mean/list-decodable application proofs remain unchecked.

review.title: Demystifying Border of Structured Algebraic Circuits via Differential Equations

score_reasons.novelty: Wronskian differential equations replace repeated DiDIL differentiation.
score_reasons.depth: Coefficient-complexity control, division elimination and structured reconstruction.
score_reasons.exposition: Comparison tables separate newly proved bounds from informal adaptations.

checked: Checked border Waring partial-derivative dimension bound: rank minors remain zero under degeneration; each derivative order has dimension≤w even if approximant degrees exceed output degree, so total dimension≤w(Δ+1).
Checked conditional hitting-map degree O(nΔ³w²) and inspected normalized differential-equation recurrence/debordering route.

review.title: Online Graph Coloring: Competitive Ratios Separating Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms
review.authors: Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi; Hirotaka Yoneda; Masataka Yoneda
review.summary: Separates randomized and deterministic online vertex coloring: deterministic competitive ratio Ω(n/log n), randomized O(n(log log n)²/log²n) against oblivious inputs, and deterministic upper O(n/(log log n)^(2−ε)).
review.prior_frontier: Improves long-standing randomized upper and deterministic lower bounds and leaves only a (log log n)² gap in the randomized ratio.

score_reasons.significance: Establishes an asymptotic power-of-randomization separation in a central online problem.
score_reasons.novelty: A counting bound on possible final color pairings controls random reuse; a strengthened adversarial color strategy yields the lower bound.
score_reasons.depth: Combines transparent-model adversaries, probabilistic pairing analysis and clique-free coloring recurrences.
score_reasons.exposition: Clear distinction between oblivious randomized inputs and unlimited deterministic computation.

checked: Checked the fixed-pairing probability ≤θ^-m using conditional choice probabilities.
Checked the combinatorial bound k^m binom(n,m)^2: each first vertex can pair only with the last nonneighbor of one of k base colors, or a later vertex would promote its color out of level two.

Checked the complete deterministic Ω(n/log n) lower bound (PDF 15–16): distinct transversal admissible sets postpone base colors until pairing, rule out a third vertex of an online color, and still give a proper 2⌈log₂n⌉ coloring.

Checked the randomized multi-level analysis (PDF 17–23). For a fixed final B/profile, each target matching is determined before its vertex arrives; collisions invalidate the event, so adaptive conditional choice probabilities multiply to θ_(t−1)^−m. Backward ranks have total ≤(θ_t−1)m, giving the stars-and-bars count and geometric tail. Verified floor losses, choice of d, and resulting randomized ratio conditional on the small-k algorithm and unknown-parameter wrapper. Also checked the disjoint-set potential proof of the object-coloring lemma (PDF 25–26).
remaining: Scoped exception for the 45-page paper: deterministic lower bound and randomized central algorithm are checked. The full deterministic upper-bound framework in Section 6 remains unchecked.
External Halldórsson small-k coloring and Lemma 3.3's unknown-n/k combination were not independently verified here.

review.title: Fourier Entropy Bounds via Approximations
review.authors: Manaswi Paraashar, Nitin Saurabh
review.area: Analysis of Boolean functions; Fourier entropy
review.summary: Bounds Shannon Fourier entropy by O(log(1+approximate spectral norm)) for any fixed pointwise error<1, and consequently by randomized parity-query complexity. Adds one-sided average affine-certificate and exact nonnegative overlapping-representation bounds plus an XOR quantum-communication application.
review.prior_frontier: Strengthens earlier min-entropy and Rényi>1 approximation bounds to Shannon entropy; does not resolve Fourier Entropy–Influence or Mansour’s conjecture.

score_reasons.significance: Closes a genuine entropy-order gap in a central Boolean-complexity framework.
score_reasons.novelty: Groups coefficients by their first accurate low-spectral-norm approximant, making exponentially decaying error pay finite Shannon cost.
score_reasons.depth: Uses a multiscale entropy estimate, majority amplification and interpolation for exact representations.
score_reasons.exposition: The main analytic lemma and its application are concise and quantitatively explicit.

checked: Traced the full multiscale entropy lemma: first-good partition, tail mass≤2^−j, within-part ℓ1 bound and Jensen against geometric reference weights.
Verified all constants in the entropy decomposition, including subprobability massρ and ρlog(1/ρ)≤2(1−ρ).
Checked majority amplification of a scaled pointwise approximant gives exponentially small error and spectral norm≤(1+B²)^(t/2); t=4j+8 satisfies the lemma.
Verified randomized parity trees give a pointwise2/3 approximant with spectral norm≤2^R.
remaining: One-sided/conical representation moment inequalities and the quantum communication application remain unaudited. Theorem3.2 says ε>0 without ε<1, but the introduction and proof correctly require fixed error below1; at ε≥1 the unqualified wording is false.
issues: Local statement omission in Theorem3.2: ε must be fixed below1, as stated in the introduction; the proof is for ε=1/3 and amplification covers fixed ε<1.

review.title: Low-Error Extractors

review.summary: Constructs explicit two-source extractors for entropy C n^{1−c}, error 2^{−c n^c}, and output k, for universal constants; affine extractors reach entropy n^{4/5+α}. score_reasons.novelty: Spreadness growth and multi-regularity approximate duality provide a new route to two-source extraction.
score_reasons.depth: Entropic PFR, iterative spreadness and regularity transformations are deep.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise nonoptimal constants, entropy/error tradeoffs and intermediate statements are well organized.

checked: Checked Type I spreadness iteration and preservation under differencing, including the geometric sum in the rank threshold. Read the two cases of Type II growth and exact approximate-duality loss.

Checked the spreadness-PFR reduction and both growth regimes through rapid mixing (PDF 44–51), conditional on entropic H2-PFR and the stated spreadness closure facts. Quotienting a concentrated coset supplies the rank witness. In Type II, choosing the nearest remembered Type I scale supplies Ω(g′−g) spreadness and hence geometric gap contraction; checked the recurrence, stopping inequalities, O(log(n/k)+log(n/g)) bound and the n≈k endpoint handled by zero iterations.
remaining: Scoped exception for the 94-page paper: a central new rapid-mixing chain is checked conditionally, but the external entropic PFR theorem and closure interfaces were not fully reconstructed.

The multi-regularity approximate-duality construction, rank condensers, explicit final two-source/affine extractor composition and output/error accounting remain unchecked; no complete extractor correctness certification.

review.title: The Contraction Lemma Beyond ETH: Algorithms and Lower Bounds
review.authors: Karthik Gajulapalli
review.summary: Conditional on the stated, unaudited subexponential exact tensor-contraction lemma, develops new counting and simulation reductions; the checked fixed-algebraic-gate quantum simulation costs poly(input)·2^O((s+q)/sqrt(log(s+q))). The manuscript also claims search and hierarchy consequences and supplies a long contraction appendix. This review does not verify that appendix, an unconditional subexponential SAT algorithm, or an ETH refutation.
review.prior_frontier: The reviewed contribution is a collection of new reductions from a stated contraction speedup attributed to recent work. Their unconditional interpretation depends on the approximately 50-page contraction/precision argument, which this review has not certified. The existing partial-large-proof exception applies only to the explicitly checked reductions.

score_reasons.significance: A broad family of important exact-algorithm and uniform-separation consequences.
score_reasons.novelty: Tensor-preserving reductions account directly for shared bits, signs and algebraic amplitudes rather than forcing CNF encodings.
score_reasons.depth: The long contraction/precision appendix and succinct machine simulations are technically extensive.
score_reasons.exposition: Careful native gate-set, arithmetic and machine conventions accompany a very broad result list.

checked: Verified the doubled quantum network in Theorem 11 conditional on the contraction lemma: paired Hadamards rescale to signed integers, O(s+q) wires suffice, and postselection uses two exact contractions and a positive denominator.
Checked the fixed-field extension principle and Clifford+T example F(V)=2+V−V³, F(exp(iπ/4))/4=(2+sqrt(2))/4.
Inspected the classical block-schedule simulation: O(sqrt(T)log T) schedule bits and O(T) content/choice wires are subdominant to T/sqrt(log T).

Checked the local-constraint compiler and exact algebraic-entry reduction (PDF 19–22): variable-equality paths pay O(total incidence+variables) edges with unique extensions, including variables absent from constraints; fan-in-two circuit counting pays O(s+b), and recovering an accepting assignment uses b additional exact count queries. For fixed number field, cleared-denominator coefficient heights are 2^O(s), so ℓ=(d−1)m+1 and P=O(s) recover the integer polynomial before field reduction; the norm argument gives an exact polynomial-bit sign test.

Read the precise contraction interface and its claimed self-contained Appendix A architecture (PDF 52–54): maximum degree O(s^.9), P,ℓ=O(s), succinct entry evaluation 2^O(s^.9), polynomial space. These restrictions are needed by every downstream speedup.
remaining: Scoped exception only for the checked new reductions and quantum-simulation application, all CONDITIONAL on the contraction lemma. review.summary: Claims maliciously secure completely fair two-party protocols for comparison and a specified embedded-XOR function from quantum one-wayness, using Bell-state shares and input-consistency proofs. The real-world comparison protocol fails under a local phase flip.
review.prior_frontier: The comparison functionality already has classical fair protocols under stronger primitives; the claimed quantum-assumption improvement is not established by the supplied protocol.

score_reasons.significance: The stated goal is meaningful, but the delivered protocol does not achieve it.
score_reasons.novelty: Bell-state sharing is combined with existing OT and consistency tools.
score_reasons.depth: Security analysis does not cover a simple coherent modification of a retained share.
score_reasons.exposition: Hybrid and real protocols differ in authentication; the crucial gap is not acknowledged.

checked: Constructed a fixed-input attack on Algorithm 4: choose i=j=1, for which f=0. Malicious P1 prepares and proves inputs honestly, receives its own correct output first, applies Z to its half of E₂^(1), and sends it. This changes Φ+ to Φ−. P2 sets its target-round output to 1 without a check; later rounds may be honest. P1 has 0 and P2 has 1.
remaining: Other protocols and any redesigned authenticated reconstruction are not certified.
issues: Algorithm 4 (PDF p11) authenticates only garbage-round expected outputs; it has no target-round tag/authentication. Input-consistency ZK (pp11–12,35) constrains inputs, not the later local Z operation. Theorem 5/6 therefore fails as written. The hybrid AMD proof also analyzes replacement by an independent qubit rather than arbitrary coherent tampering.

review.desk_reject_reason: Concrete correctness/fairness attack on the claimed real-world protocol: a local Z flip in the first target round makes honest P2 accept the wrong comparison output while P1 receives the correct output (Algorithm 4, PDF p11; Theorems 5–6, pp11–12).

review.summary: Characterizes PAC learning when each target gives at most ℓ acceptable labels. For finite labels, full-set and bandit learnability are governed by generalized Natarajan dimension, while demonstrations are governed by intersections of at most ℓ+1 hypotheses and may require ε^{−ℓ} samples. A packed dimension handles countable labels; agnostic demonstrations require additional compatibility.
review.prior_frontier: Extends multiclass dimension theory to set-valued correctness and separates demonstrations from full-set/bandit feedback; no computational-efficiency guarantee is claimed.

score_reasons.significance: A broad characterization of a fundamental alternative supervision model.
score_reasons.novelty: The intersection-class criterion and packed dimension explain previously absent learnability separations.
score_reasons.depth: Transductive conversion, compactness, dimension comparisons and matching lower rates span a large development.
score_reasons.exposition: Feedback models and realizable versus agnostic distinctions are explicit; 157 pages require scoped audit.

checked: Traced the central prediction-family conversion through target retention, rare empty intersections, ν^ℓ lower bound and finite minimax. Checked compactness using subprobabilities and finite-coordinate constraints for countable labels.

Checked PDF pp71–77: the entire packed-dimension weak learner and its realizable/agnostic full-set compression conversion. Greedy minimal empty-intersection blocks have size at most ℓ+1; projecting d+1 coordinates with excessive packing would contradict packed dimension. Repetition, rational approximation, finite minimax and countable-label subprobability compactness give a symmetrized transductive rule with error γ+d/(m+1).

Checked boosting parameters η=Δ/[2(α+1)] and ζ=ητ−α(e^η−1)>0, the exponential-weight loss bound, and that an invalid most-probable label forces miss mass at least 1/(ℓ+1). O(log N) rounds eliminate all sample mistakes. Ordered repeated compression uses O((d+1)log N) indices; conditioning on these indices justifies the realizable union bound and the agnostic Hoeffding bound, including the removed-index r/n loss.
remaining: Large-proof exception: 157 pages. Checked the prediction-family conversion and packed-dimension/full-set learning core, not the whole characterization. The finite-label dimension comparisons, sharp ε^{−ℓ} demonstration lower bound, remaining demonstration conversions, agnostic local-compatibility/anchored-cube construction, and standard-Borel measurability extensions remain unverified.
