review.title: Breaking the $O(mn)$ Barrier for Minimum Bipartite Dijoin via Dynamic and Local Graph Algorithms
review.authors: Chaitanya Nalam, Thatchaphol Saranurak
review.summary: Minimum dijoin and maximum dicut packing in a bipartite digraph with all arcs L→R in m n^(21/22+o(1)) time, with corresponding maximum-join, cycle-code covering-radius and even-ear-decomposition improvements.
review.prior_frontier: Breaks Frank’s stated 33-year O(mn) barrier for this orientation-restricted class; not an arbitrary-digraph or general submodular-flow algorithm.

score_reasons.significance: A polynomial improvement for a longstanding canonical submodular-flow special case.
score_reasons.novelty: Relaxes maximum-matching maintenance and combines local-flow rematching with dynamic source contractions.
score_reasons.depth: The 61-page proof balances local search, dynamic matching, quotient maintenance and two global regimes.
score_reasons.exposition: Strong-end invariants and accounting are explicit, though several substantial implementation appendices are essential.

checked: Traced strong-end contraction optimality using a perfect matching and disjoint degree dicuts.
Checked local cleanup searches only recorded arcs, certifies extremal SCCs within σ² scans, and unmatched new representatives preserve the small-end invariant.
Verified potential |V|+unmatched decreases by2k−2 under a fitted2k-end contraction and by≥τ in each expensive phase, yielding O(n/τ) phases.
remaining: Local-flow implementation, dynamic contraction/augmentation path bound, quotient amortization and the21/22 parameter optimization remain unaudited.

papers.title: A Fast Algorithm for Subspace Convolution
papers.authors: Shlomo Perles, Omri Weinstein

review.title: A Fast Algorithm for Subspace Convolution
review.authors: Shlomo A. Perles, Omri Weinstein
review.summary: Computes subspace zeta/Möbius transforms, transposes and span convolution in O_q(N log N) ring operations for fixed q=p^m when p is invertible in the coefficient ring. Rank-restricted incidence transforms are quasi-linear in input/output table size; applications include Grassmann kernels and rank-decomposition graph colouring.
review.prior_frontier: Replaces covering-pair cost Θ_q(Nq^{n/2}) with quasi-linear arithmetic by permitting subtraction/scalar multiplication, avoiding addition-only lower bounds.

score_reasons.significance: A foundational transform speedup with several algorithmic applications.
score_reasons.novelty: Hyperplane cutting plus quotient Fourier transforms diagonalizes affine containment.
score_reasons.depth: A clean recursion must be extended to coefficient rings, rank truncation and graph states.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit ring assumptions and separate coordinate-construction costs prevent misleading operation counts.

checked: Checked the central transform construction and complexity in full (PDF pp12–16,22–25): crossing subspaces have a unique direction/coset representation; Fourier transformation turns affine containment into smaller linear containment; the cutoff recursion preserves total table length, and at least half its entries lose at least n units of the nk budget. Checked inverse and transposed circuits and the cyclotomic extension over any commutative ring with invertible p, including rings with zero divisors.

Checked the separate incidence recurrence and its repeated-input charge. With a≤c=n−b, the min(a,c)S budget drops by S−aJ or S−I−aJ; Gaussian-binomial ratios give at least S/4. Multiplication by n pays local FFT work and boundary calls, yielding O(S log S). Checked the subspace counts, integer-output magnitude bounds and coprime modular recovery.

Checked span/intersection convolution, exact-span counting with repeated/zero vectors, and the two-transform Grassmann kernel identity. Checked invariant inverse-kernel reconstruction from a stabilizer-orbit system; it does not assume a semisimple adjacency spectrum in finite characteristic. Checked the bounded-coefficient incidence lower bound via positive Gram decomposition and determinant growth.

Checked the full graph-coloring algorithm (PDF pp17–19): the cut bilinear form is well-defined, compatible partial matchings biject with parent color partitions, and processing concrete left classes in a canonical order justifies the available-right-multiplicity weights. Histograms need at most3L coordinates across outer and inner states, and O(N log N)-bit counts preserve N^{O(L)} runtime. Backtracking and falling-factorial conversion are valid.

Checked both graph-coloring reductions (PDF pp28–33). For unrestricted palettes, matrix-type register tests and common palettes enforce the desired monotone counter constraints; selector/anchor lists give both directions, and the supplied layout has cut-rank≤2d+12. Checked the r²/4−17r exponent calculation and the original Fomin et al. Lemma3.1 construction (author PDF pp8–9), including its constraint-count restrictions.

For fixed palettes, checked row/column agreement forces singleton consistent assignments once odd cycles enforce nonempty selection; the NAE gadgets encode a∨b∨c with exactly16 extensions. Counts 6·2^g·16^m and layout rank≤2k+19 give the claimed conditional decision/counting implications. These remain conditional ETH/#ETH consequences, not unconditional running-time exclusions.
remaining: The reported benchmarks and companion Lean artifacts were not rerun. The ancillary Grassmann spectral-projection formula uses the cited standard eigenvalue identity; its derivation from that external source was not independently reconstructed. Index construction has the stated additional table-size·poly(n) cost, separate from the O(S log S) ring-operation count.

sources.detail: Monotone min-CSP source lower bound and construction, Lemma3.1, PDF pp8–9.

papers.title: Vector Balancing in Polynomial Time
papers.authors: Shengtao Guo, Ethan X. Fang, Junwei Lu

review.title: Vector Balancing in Polynomial Time
review.authors: Shengtao Guo, Ethan X. Fang, Junwei Lu
review.summary: Deterministic real-RAM algorithm finds signs with infinity-norm discrepancy≤8272 for every matrix whose columns have Euclidean norm≤1, in O((mn^9+n^10)log(2+m+n)) arithmetic operations; implies constant·sqrt(t) Beck–Fiala rounding.
review.prior_frontier: Constructivizes the recently proved constant Komlós bound; this is a unit-cost real-arithmetic algorithm, not an established polynomial-bit-complexity algorithm.

score_reasons.significance: Polynomial-time constant Komlós discrepancy is a fundamental constructive advance.
score_reasons.novelty: Squared-entry Gram potential controls near-tight rows while concave barrier corrections supply negative curvature.
score_reasons.depth: Complete spectral, numerical derivative and finite-arithmetic direction-finding analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: All critical lemmas are proved, with explicit constants and runtime model.

checked: Checked entire new algorithm and proof pp5–20. Dominant-entry error telescopes below2K; tracked/true row error≤4K. Cleanup preserves row values, decreases barriers/weights and the largest eigenvalue via entrywise and PSD comparisons.

Checked spectral-gap≥η from positive rank-one perturbation; trace bounds give dimF≤4s/K+1/2. After all linear constraints, dimH>5s/K; diagonal-normalized restricted-trace lemma produces a direction with L′=0,L″≤0. Verified derivative matrices and bound ||W′h v||²≤L h^TUh.

Checked third-order remainder via reduced resolvent gap and H=2^24; full steps decrease potential, at most n short steps freeze coordinates, yielding O(n^7) updates and L<2 invariant. Final2K³+5K=8272 discrepancy.

Checked complete finite-arithmetic direction procedure: truncate negative exponentials with absolute accuracy, power iteration with gap, approximate inverse resolvent, exact constraint projection and Schur-complement negative direction. No exact exponential, square-root or spectral oracle is assumed.
Checked zero/completed rows, n≤K, arbitrary small retained entries through normalized zi, and Beck–Fiala scaling.
remaining: No formal verification or independent implementation was performed. Unit-cost real arithmetic does not establish polynomial bit complexity; prior literature priority claims were not independently audited.

papers.title: Testing isomorphism of finite groups in time polynomial in the group order
papers.authors: Youming Qiao, Chuanqi Zhang

review.title: Testing isomorphism of finite groups in time polynomial in the group order
review.authors: Youming Qiao, Chuanqi Zhang
review.summary: Claims polynomial time in group order N for finite-group isomorphism from Cayley tables, via q^{O(ℓ+m+n)} tensor isomorphism over every finite field and characteristic-two congruence machinery. This is not polynomial in a compact group presentation or in tensor dimension.
review.prior_frontier: Claims group-order N^{(1/4+o(1))log N} and tensor q^{Õ(n^{1.5})} as previous bounds; prior theorems not independently audited.

score_reasons.significance: Would resolve a central longstanding group-isomorphism frontier.
score_reasons.novelty: Integrates matrix-group structure and affine quotient transport beyond prior individualization.
score_reasons.depth: 282-page dependency chain involving characteristic-two obstruction modules, classical components and group extensions.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit models and supporting algebra, but unusually extensive technical machinery makes verification difficult.

checked: Checked affine quotient/fiber formulas in Lemma 3.5. Traced Lemma 4.4 normalized-error identity: inverse-conjugation linear map and defect cocycle compose correctly and transport the obstruction class. Read the reduction of obstruction-module action to conjugation in Lemma 4.6.

Checked Algorithm 7.6 and the complete conditional recursion-size proof, PDF pp63–70. Quotient transport followed by a fiber under the full stabilizer preserves the complete transporter coset. Invariant flags, split summands and active-module conversion have the claimed recursive roles, conditional on the stated local algebraic interfaces.

Checked Proposition 7.8 potential Φ=p^{k0(b+λv)}m: λ exceeds the active-conversion cost; quotient dimension weights add, and at a split the 2^b branches are offset by p^{−k0ηb}. Charging leaves and strict unary reductions to integer potential units bounds the recursion by p^{O(d)}poly(input size), conditional on D4/D6 and polynomial local costs. Root dimension is retained throughout; unsuccessful branches and unchanged unary chains are accounted for.
remaining: Large-proof exception: 282 pages. Checked affine/cocycle identities and the central recursive algorithm and cost accounting conditional on its local structural interfaces. The classical-group module and cohomology decompositions, local reduction and transporter algorithms (including the full Proposition 7.7 interfaces), degree-three tensor reduction, and general group-extension recursion remain unverified. This review does not certify a polynomial-time group-isomorphism algorithm.

papers.title: Sparsest Cut on Abelian Cayley Graphs
papers.authors: Jake Ruotolo

review.title: Sparsest Cut on Abelian Cayley Graphs
review.authors: Jake Ruotolo
review.summary: An exp(O(n^(2/3)))-time constant-factor sparsest-cut approximation for every finite undirected abelian Cayley graph, without requiring the group labeling as input.
review.prior_frontier: Extends degree-dependent sparse-Cayley PTAS results to all generator degrees. The theorem does not depend on the unverified OpenAI hardness/ETH claims mentioned in background.

score_reasons.significance: Answers a natural structured-instance approximation question beyond low-degree Cayley graphs.
score_reasons.novelty: Many small character eigenvalues force a sparse character threshold cut through an arithmetic-progression pigeonhole argument.
score_reasons.depth: Combines character multiplication inequalities, iterative threshold rounding and spectral-rank case splitting.
score_reasons.exposition: The algorithm handles unknown group presentations explicitly; several indexing/notation slips appear in the algebraic proof.

checked: Traced the collision argument: equal successive differences a_i−6a_(i−1) yield a nonzero character r with controlled eigenvalues at6^i r.
Checked the resulting geometric series(4/6)^i bounds threshold rounding by O(τ), conditional on its scalar rounding recurrence.
Verified the final three cases, including tr(A²)=n/d forcing dense high-threshold-rank graphs to be expanders, and sparse group-label recovery fitting exp(O(n^(2/3))) time.
remaining: Scalar threshold-rounding recurrence, exact character sweep bound and imported spectral cut-improvement theorem remain unaudited.

papers.title: Inapproximability of L1->L2 Subspace Distortion
papers.authors: Vijay Bhattiprolu

review.title: Inapproximability of ℓ1→ℓ2 Subspace Distortion
review.authors: Vijay Bhattiprolu
review.summary: Assuming NP has no randomized quasipolynomial-time algorithms, rules out polynomial-time 2^{(log n)^{1−ε}} approximation of normalized ℓ2/ℓ1 distortion of a real subspace, for every fixed ε>0. Uses a multiscale random affine tester of hypercube proximity followed by homogenization and tensor amplification.
review.prior_frontier: Previously only inverse-polynomial-gap NP-hardness, or near-polynomial hardness under Small-Set Expansion, was known according to the manuscript. Does not prove the analogous result for all fixed p<2.

score_reasons.significance: A major hardness advance for a central continuous sparsity parameter.
score_reasons.novelty: Nonlocal measurements at all dyadic scales overcome local sparse-vector obstructions.
score_reasons.depth: Sparsity inversion, uniform net estimates and homogenization carry substantial technical content.
score_reasons.exposition: Succinct argument, but several scaling/normalization displays in homogenization need reconciliation.

checked: Read the multiscale tester and checked the rounding inequality ||v||₁≥||v||₂²/||v||∞ used to recover a nearby cube point. Traced the small-homogenizing-coordinate versus near-one split and the intended tensor amplification.
remaining: Full sparsity inversion map, finite-precision randomized reduction, exact homogenization parameter choices and tensorization dependency.
issues: PDF p15 defines the first coordinate as z/m² but the following norm calculations use z/m; several preceding normalization inequalities omit small tolerances. These look repairable but require explicit consistent scaling before the central reduction is certified.

papers.title: How Many Votes Is a Lie Worth? Measuring Strategyproofness through Resource Augmentation
papers.authors: Ratip Emin Berker, Vincent Conitzer, Eden Hartman, Jiayuan Liu, Caspar Oesterheld

review.title: How Many Votes Is a Lie Worth? Measuring Strategyproofness through Resource Augmentation
review.authors: Ratip Emin Berker, Vincent Conitzer, Eden Hartman, Jiayuan Liu, Caspar Oesterheld
review.summary: Defines manipulation potential as truthful vote copies needed to match a strategic voter’s outcome; characterizes positional scoring frontier and proves universal m−2 lower bound for anonymous onto rules with electorate-size-independent bounded potential, attained by Borda.
review.prior_frontier: Introduces a prior-free ordinal resource-augmentation measure, not ordinary strategyproofness; plurality can be preferable for smaller electorates.

score_reasons.significance: A quantitative strategyproofness comparison and tight universal lower bound.
score_reasons.novelty: Truthful replication measures the benefit of manipulation without cardinal utilities.
score_reasons.depth: Positional-score optimization and a topological universal obstruction.
score_reasons.exposition: Interpretation and electorate/candidate regimes are explicit.

checked: Checked infinite-potential example for positional scores s1=s2: truthful copies cannot break the top-two tie, while demoting the second choice makes the first win.
Inspected precise finite-electorate versus uniform-over-electorates quantification and the rational-profile/Sperner route for the universal bound.
remaining: Full scoring-rule characterization and universal Lipschitz common-junction construction/linear-dependence proof.

papers.title: Path Decompositions of Sparse Graphs via Gaussian Sweeps and Faster Exponential Algorithms
papers.authors: Serge Gaspers

review.title: Path Decompositions of Sparse Graphs via Gaussian Sweeps and Faster Exponential Algorithms
review.authors: Serge Gaspers
review.summary: For all simple maximum-degree-three graphs, claims pathwidth, cutwidth and bisection width ≤(3/(4π))acos(5/6)n+o(n)≈.13982n; degree-four pathwidth≈.24577n and general per-edge 7m/48+o(n), with polynomial-time constructions and faster exact algorithms.
review.prior_frontier: Improves claimed cubic n/6, quartic n/3 and general 13m/75 bounds; numerical/formal certificates are supplied externally but were not run.

score_reasons.significance: Improves fundamental worst-case sparse-graph width constants and many exact-algorithm exponents.
score_reasons.novelty: Correlated Gaussian layouts and median switching replace recursive bisection.
score_reasons.depth: Star-comparison probabilities, concentration, deterministic construction and numerical certificates.
score_reasons.exposition: Explicit distinctions between unconditional cubic proof and conditional numerical/formal inputs.

checked: Checked path-decomposition construction from an ordering and the full two-Gaussian threshold lemma using independent sum and difference. Read local correlation setup and the median connector obstruction in the sharper bound.

Checked the full cubic median connector construction and its path-decomposition accounting, PDF pp48–56. Connector items can be ordered with at most one unit of excess; inner/outer bags plus the connector have size at most max(L0,L0′)+2 and satisfy every edge and vertex-interval condition.

Checked the ideal Gaussian-star probability f(0)=3 acos((3r²−1)/2)/(4π) and f(t)≤f(0). Checked the complete two-exceedance comparison: water-filling the correlation angles preserves positive semidefiniteness until the planar boundary, its Gaussian derivative has the required sign, and circular-arc overlap is minimized at the equilateral configuration. The median-switch identity ceil(N/2)=N−1[N≥2] then gives the sharper local bound. Comparison to arbitrary residual stars is conditional on Lemma 6.5.
remaining: Large-proof exception: 190 pages. The central cubic connector, star threshold and median-switch proofs are checked. The label-correlation construction (Lemma 5.4), full residual-simplex comparison (Lemma 6.5), uniform concentration and finite-precision derandomization, quartic/general coefficients, and downstream exponential-time applications remain unverified. External Lean and numerical certificates were not run; this is not a complete certification of all stated constants.

papers.title: Information Required to Preserve Past Learning
papers.authors: Pinang Xu

review.title: Information Required to Preserve Past Learning
review.authors: Pinang Xu
review.summary: A shared-response framework derives fine-accuracy memory laws for protective linear updates and sharp critical-window memorization tradeoffs. For k binary records of dimension d in a BSC capacity window, memory/(kd)=S/Φ(z)+o(1); claims the BBFST critical-signal conjecture and Gaussian near-Bayes cost(1/4+o(1))kd log₂ln k.
review.prior_frontier: The framework permits unrestricted computation/public history-independent codebooks; memory counts every retained history-dependent bit. Binary prediction is averaged over random databases/queries, whereas protective updates have per-instance guarantees.

score_reasons.significance: Targets precise information costs at a recognized memorization threshold and distinguishes query timing from raw parameter storage.
score_reasons.novelty: Common log-score compatibility is converted to finite-order source exponents, with affinity balls for lower bounds and KL covers for codes.
score_reasons.depth: The81-page analysis spans minimax geometry, channel concentration, information accounting and multiple operational models.
score_reasons.exposition: Exact regimes are stated, but many broad applications and nested appendices make the central dependence chain demanding.

checked: Traced the basic source-mass theorem and its data-processing conversion B≥slog(1/p)−h₂(s).

Verified the finite-affinity lemma: uniform-mixture mutual information bounds separated sets by2e^Δ; a maximal separated subtuple covers every compatible tuple, and a union bound gives the source exponent.
Checked the reverse finite-cell bound, original unconditioned source masses and the compactness/minimax limit qualification.
Inspected the binary critical-window specialization: affinity is proportional to Hamming distance, small balls have mass2^(−d(1−o(1))), and the stated BBFST parameter regime gives z→0.
remaining: Common-score concentration uniformly over arbitrary joint messages, sharp coverage accounting and endpoint coding, full protective-regression laws, Gaussian precision constant and population-learning reductions remain unaudited.

papers.title: B\"{u}chi Determinization with Optimal States and Square Root Index Improvement
papers.authors: Cong Tian, Runzhe Ma, Wensheng Wang, Zhenhua Duan

review.title: Büchi Determinization with Optimal States and Square Root Index Improvement
review.authors: Cong Tian, Runzhe Ma, Wensheng Wang, Zhenhua Duan
review.summary: On the state-optimal history-tree transition structure, reduces Rabin acceptance pairs from 2^{n−1} to 3·2^{n/2−1}−1 for even n and 2^{(n+1)/2}−1 for odd n, without increasing the approximately (1.65n)^n states. Proves matching exponential-order lower bounds for Rabin acceptance on that fixed structure.
review.prior_frontier: The state count was optimal, but its Rabin index was exponential with exponent n. The lower bound fixes this transition structure; it is not a lower bound for every state-optimal construction.

score_reasons.significance: Improves an important second resource in a standard determinization construction.
score_reasons.novelty: Coexistence coloring combines weight and reusable flag ranges to halve the exponential index.
score_reasons.depth: Closure-set combinatorics and cycle witnesses support nearly matching bounds.
score_reasons.exposition: Precise parity-sensitive formulas and an explicit scope restriction aid interpretation.

checked: Checked the color induction: within each recursive half the closure budget decreases by one, and low-weight cross-half ranges are disjoint while high-weight ranges may be reused. Checked summation of the per-weight minimum and parity formulas. Read the clique recurrence and the beginning of the letter-effect cycle construction.
remaining: Complete accepting/rejecting cycle witness construction, all letter-effect cases, and the pinching argument for arbitrary Rabin assignments on the fixed transition graph.

papers.title: One-point value of a combinatorial generating series as a complexity measure
papers.authors: Varsha Gupta

review.title: One-point value of a combinatorial generating series as a complexity measure
review.authors: Varsha Gupta
review.summary: At a sufficiently large encoded imaginary height, constant-factor evaluation of a positive-cost combinatorial generating series determines the exact minimum cost; variable-accuracy evaluation is equivalent to optimization plus approximate counting of optima. Studies hook-immanant tour truncations.
review.prior_frontier: Unifies standard low-temperature leading-term extraction with several counting/optimization examples; no new general optimization algorithm follows.

score_reasons.significance: Useful formal comparison of optimization and approximate optimal-solution counting.
score_reasons.novelty: One-point encoding and coefficient-sign characterization of low hook truncations.
score_reasons.depth: Mostly exponential-tail bounds with an additional immanant analysis.
score_reasons.exposition: Makes constant-factor versus approximation-scheme distinctions, though broad framing exceeds the modest extraction lemma.

checked: Checked logarithmic extraction error≤(|E|+1)ln2/(2πy)<1/2 at the stated threshold; integer rounding recovers OPT. Checked why a fixed factor-two black-box value cannot give arbitrarily accurate optimal-solution counts.
remaining: Formal floating-point encoding complexity, all reductions and hook-immanant truncation coefficients.

papers.title: Computational Complexity of Data-Driven Configuration for Integer Programming, Clustering, and Learning Algorithms
papers.authors: Dravyansh Sharma

review.title: Computational Complexity of Data-Driven Configuration for Integer Programming, Clustering, and Learning Algorithms
review.authors: Dravyansh Sharma
review.area: Learning theory and algorithm configuration complexity
review.summary: NP-complete shared-multiplier tuning of one root CG cut even with coefficients ≤8; hardness for scalar Lasso zero validation loss and power-mean linkage root split; statistical and smoothed-complexity results use explicitly different perturbation/oracle models.
review.prior_frontier: Moves beyond sample-complexity guarantees to computational ERM barriers; smoothing is not a uniform Turing-model polynomial-time claim.

score_reasons.significance: Broad computational limitations for concrete data-driven algorithm configuration.
score_reasons.novelty: Shared low-dimensional per-instance gadgets encode a growing global multiplier vector.
score_reasons.depth: Several independent reductions and smoothed path-complexity arguments.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly states solver restrictions, precision and real-root-isolation assumptions.

checked: Checked exact L/G gadget root-integrality conditions by floors and ceilings and all endpoint conventions for J0=[1/8,1/7], J1=(1/4,2/7]. Checked two-literal exclusive-or and three-literal-or interval sums and the fixed-dimension arrangement caveat.
remaining: Complete shared-vector reduction and constant additive loss bound; Lasso path gadget, linkage schedule/guards, smoothing and learning-rate constructions require separate audits.

papers.title: Decoding Expander Walk Codes up to the Johnson Bound in Near-Linear Time
papers.authors: Silas Richelson, Sourya Roy, Madhur Tulsiani

review.title: Decoding Expander Walk Codes up to the Johnson Bound in Near-Linear Time
review.authors: Silas Richelson, Sourya Roy, Madhur Tulsiani
review.summary: List-decodes Ta-Shma expander-walk binary linear codes of bias ε and rate Ω(ε^(2+β)) at correlationρ≥2√ε in soft-O(N)(1/ε)^cβ time, cβ=(1/β)^O(1/β), for fixed0<β≤1/2.
review.prior_frontier: Reaches the Johnson guarantee with near-linear blocklength time and polynomial inverse-bias dependence for fixedβ, replacing prior higher-degree SoS/global-correlation rounding costs. The exponent is not uniform asβ→0.

score_reasons.significance: Makes near-optimal-rate explicit codes efficiently decodable at their natural combinatorial radius.
score_reasons.novelty: Recovers parity operators from an SDP and rounds at the base-code correlation scale using operator amplification.
score_reasons.depth: Requires dimension-efficient matrix concentration, consistency penalties, wide replacement-product amplification and near-linear SDP optimization.
score_reasons.exposition: Parameter dependence and the role of the base code are clear; a local PSD-order typo does not affect the following valid inequality.

checked: Traced spectral operator recovery: threshold the Gram matrix of vector sums, bound discarded components byθ and retained differences byθ^−1 times consistency energy.
Checked involution telescoping yields the stated walk-level errorρ⁴/16 for the chosenθ,α.
Verified rounding enumerates sampled signs, uses one spectral eigenvector to produce a soft base-code word, and union-bounds both matrix approximation and base decoding over Johnson-list size≤2/ρ².
Checked final list verification prevents false positives and the two success stages yield probability≥1/4.
remaining: SDP potential optimization and near-linear solver implementation, wide-replacement operator amplification, exact base-code decoder and complete rate/runtime parameter substitution remain unaudited.

papers.title: The Movement Complexity of Sorting
papers.authors: Sichen Wang

review.title: The Movement Complexity of Sorting
review.authors: Sichen Wang
review.summary: For n keys on a fixed-dimensional grid with two moving comparison heads, determines the r-round movement exponent 1+(2d)^{r−1}/((2d)^r−(2d−1)^r), up to logarithms; obtains exact asymptotics in several boundary regimes and exponent 1+1/(2d) with unrestricted rounds.
review.prior_frontier: Introduces and sharply analyzes a movement-cost model; comparisons, memory and internal computation are free, and each round must commit its route before observing that round’s comparisons.

score_reasons.significance: A clean sharp tradeoff for a natural geometric access constraint.
score_reasons.novelty: Combines spatial pivot sampling with a route-uniform co-blocked rank argument.
score_reasons.depth: Matching multiscale exponents and adaptive lower bounds require substantive geometry and information accounting.
score_reasons.exposition: Model, regimes and residual logarithmic gaps are clearly separated.

checked: Checked the exponent recurrence and limiting exponent. Checked the product-box load proof: a large load gives either a large same-rank-block cluster or a large disjoint matching; their union bounds control all boxes and scales, and route segmentation then gives the logarithmic route bound.
remaining: Full forced-comparison/adaptive-round lower bound, logarithm removal on the line, and the complete constructive movement analysis.
issues: The lower bounds apply to algorithms correct on every input and every coin outcome; no bounded-error extension is established.

papers.title: Approximating the Euclidean Ball by Polytopes: Surprising Rates in High Dimensions
papers.authors: Yegor Gorodzha, Steven Hoehner, Gil Kur

review.title: Approximating the Euclidean Ball by Polytopes: Surprising Rates in High Dimensions
review.authors: Yegor Gorodzha, Steven Hoehner, Gil Kur
review.summary: Unrestricted-vertex approximation of the Euclidean ball in relative symmetric-difference volume has log vertex budget Θ(d log(1+1/(εsqrt(d)))) for sufficiently small ε; fixed-error budget exp(Θ(sqrt(d))), while cube and facet complexities remain exponential in d.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves a subexponential Gaussian vertex-approximation question and improves Laguerre–Delone dimensional coefficient to Θ(d^-1/2). Inscribed-polytope bounds differ fundamentally.

score_reasons.significance: Sharp high-dimensional approximation rates and failure of a natural extremality principle.
score_reasons.novelty: Radial/tangential cancellation and a median-sign simplex dual witness.
score_reasons.depth: Random polytope distribution, anti-concentration and uniform dimensional asymptotics.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly distinguishes unrestricted vertices, facets, volume and Gaussian errors.

checked: Checked interpolation-gap identities on a simplex and median-sign witness: permutation symmetry annihilates affine terms; off-diagonal Dirichlet moments give βm=(m+2)E|Q−median(Q)|/m, yielding the local L1 lower bound.

Checked the central small-error upper and lower arguments, PDF pp18–25 and 38–40. Conditional on the stated Blaschke–Petkantschin distribution identity, Y²=H+(1−H)Q separates independent radial and angular laws. Differentiation in logarithmic radial coordinates gives the stated mode curvature/tails; the small-H estimate controls the singular factor. The determinant-weighted angular Laplace estimate yields the required subgaussian lower tail conditional on the displayed Fourier/Andréief identity.

Checked that the integrated radial error retains the (1−t0)d^{−3/2} factor, and the choice t*=1/(1+ε√d/(2C1)) gives log N=O(d log(1+1/(ε√d))). For the matching lower bound, the simplex L1 witness and anti-concentration control bad facet weights, barycentric energy bounds cover a positive fraction of directions by caps of height r/√(1+2ζ), and both cap regimes yield log N=Ω(d log(1+1/(ε√d))).
remaining: Large-proof exception: 70 pages. Checked the small-error main theorem core conditional on the stated geometric change-of-variables, Fourier integration and anti-concentration interfaces, which were not independently checked in their primary sources. The extension to errors approaching one, cube approximation, exact Greenwood asymptotics and tiling/asymptotic-coefficient transfers remain unverified.

papers.title: Quantum Approximate Pattern Matching with Wildcards and Weighted Edits: Provable Baselines and Sparse-Defect Verification
papers.authors: Ziming Zhao, Junyu Chen, Zhaoxuan Li, Fanqi Kong, Yu Peng, Jiongchi Yu, Xiaofei Yue

review.title: Quantum Approximate Pattern Matching with Wildcards and Weighted Edits: Provable Baselines and Sparse-Defect Verification
review.authors: Ziming Zhao, Junyu Chen, Zhaoxuan Li, Fanqi Kong, Yu Peng, Jiongchi Yu, Xiaofei Yue
review.summary: Provides unrestricted weighted-wildcard edit matching baseline Õ(√(n+1)(m+floor(k/α)+1)) queries and promised sparse-periodic-background Õ(√((n+1)(q+1))) queries for comparable window/block lengths; does not claim comparable gate time or background discovery.
review.prior_frontier: Explicitly a baseline and a certified-input theorem, not unrestricted near-optimal weighted edit matching.

score_reasons.significance: Useful precisely limited query guarantees but not a general matching breakthrough.
score_reasons.novelty: Canonical coherent defect enumeration and a cost-row-variation event formulation.
score_reasons.depth: Uses standard search, reversible DP and careful cleanup accounting.
score_reasons.exposition: Unusually clear promises, nonclaims and query-versus-gate distinctions.

checked: Checked weighted-Hamming event bound: each defect enters/exits once and changes within a window only at a cost-row-variation offset. papers.title: The Margin Complexity of Maxima of Linear Functionals
papers.authors: Tianlang Chen

review.title: The Margin Complexity of Maxima of Linear Functionals
review.authors: Tianlang Chen
review.summary: The audited central fixed-margin theorem separates Θ(r log r) from O(r) fat-shattering growth for maxima of r homogeneous unit-norm linear functionals, at 1/(3√3) with witnesses and 1/7 at zero witnesses. The lower bound takes a supremum over ambient dimension. Critical-window refinements, unequal-radius entropy laws and multi-head retrieval results remain unchecked under the large-proof exception.
review.prior_frontier: Resolves the logarithmic-in-r lower-bound question for small margins while disproving an all-margin extrapolation; bounds at the critical margins retain a log log r gap.

score_reasons.significance: An exact phase transition in a basic aggregation class would substantially sharpen its known capacity theory.
score_reasons.novelty: Spectral block averaging and finite-field line gadgets identify the same critical constants.
score_reasons.depth: Combines margin geometry, polynomial agreement rigidity and random-label shattering transfer.
score_reasons.exposition: Clearly separates homogeneous from affine classes and determined regimes from remaining gaps.

checked: Checked the central spectral inequality: Π=2E Q is stochastic PSD, deviations of negative-label averages are independent of the current label, trace Π² controls errors, and witness contributions cancel at τ=1. Checked the line-isolation wedge-product reduction conditional on its polynomial-space lemmas and the q-dependent margin calculations.

Completed the new Reed–Solomon-type exponent-space construction, Lemmas5.3–5.6 (pp9–10). The separated support intervals T=R+I give the precise multiplier space: rho V subset E forces rho polynomial and every shifted support interval inside one T component. Degree sums remain below |K|, so equality as functions implies polynomial equality. Frobenius rotation of two-one base-q digit strings supplies u independent trace coefficients per disjoint orbit; the cyclic gaps at least k+1 place each orbit inside R. This proves the needed lower dimension of the F_q-valued multiplier code without invoking an unchecked subfield-subcode theorem.

Checked Frobenius rigidity: each exponent in R reduces under multiplication by q to degree at most D, including x^{N+qs}=x^{1+qs} for the last interval. More than D subfield-valued evaluations therefore force rho^q−rho=0. Together with spanning directions and the wedge-polynomial degree bound, off-line agreement is at most theta N. Two distinct direction classes cannot share a nonzero line displacement: their rational ratio preserves V, and both it and its inverse are polynomials, hence constants; a nonzero subfield multiplier evaluation forces that constant into F_q.

Checked all embedding normalizations and null-head compatibility (p11): q selected letters per coordinate give on-line score1/sqrt(q), off-line score at most theta/sqrt(q); adding the common negative coordinate gives zero-witness margin (1−theta)/(2sqrt(q)+1+theta). The witness margin is (1−theta)/(2sqrt(q)); q=3 and q=4 approach the stated critical constants from below.

Completed random-label-to-shattering transfer, Lemmas4.2–4.4 (pp8–9). Distinct direction blocks through a point intersect only there, so conditional selection events are independent. Verified the expected uncovered set, selected-block count, all four probability budgets, and fixed-sample averaging. A half-sample avoids the at-most1% uncovered set for enough labelings; dividing by extension multiplicity leaves more traces than the Sauer–Shelah bound at one-quarter size. The resulting subset realizes every labeling with full margin. Orthogonal copies with a shared offset preserve all cross-copy negative scores.

Checked all-r parameter selection and counting (pp11–12): the minimal u with q^{f(u)}>=M0 guarantees 4a²log2N<=M0; the binomial modal probability is at least1/(8sqrt(M0)); at least half of all e-tuples span V for e>=a+1. The chosen e gives (k+1)(M0−1)<=log2n<=2(k+2)M0 and enough direction classes. Choosing the largest admissible M0 requires no monotonicity of the jumps and gives M0>=ln r/(2(k+2)); disjoint copies yield the stated r ln r/[4826(k+2)] bound. The final span projection preserves scores and norms.

Checked Theorem5.8 fixed-deficit specialization: q=3 witness deficit is (sqrt3/2)3^{-k}; q=4 zero-witness deficit is32*4^{-k}/(49+28*4^{-k}). Minimal k yields k=O(log(1/Delta)) and onset log r=O(Delta^{-2}log²(1/Delta)). Together with the already checked spectral upper argument, this verifies the central fixed-margin phase transition, using the previously established O(r log r/gamma²) upper bound as a cited dependency.
remaining: SCOPED main-proof audit: checked the spectral O_gamma(r) obstruction and the finite-field/random-label Omega_gamma(r log r) construction for every fixed margin strictly below the critical constants. The critical-margin lower bounds, joint critical-window refinements, and their AppendixB estimates are not correctness-cleared by this audit.

The unequal-radius entropy law (Theorem1.2/AppendixC), retrieval results (Theorem1.3 and Sections7–8), and other appendices on dimensions, ceilings, aggregations and learning consequences remain unchecked. AppendixA was inspected for dependency placement only; its Hales–Jewett/box-barrier results are not needed for the audited Reed–Solomon construction and are not cleared.

The standard previously published Attias–Kontorovich fat-shattering upper bound is used as stated; its proof and all historical priority comparisons were not independently re-audited. No whole-paper verification is asserted.
resolved_notes: The lower bounds take a supremum over ambient dimension. The spectral O(r) bound concerns homogeneous heads; it must not be carried over unchanged to affine heads. Audit clearance is limited to the central fixed-margin phase transition, not every headline extension.
